entries.definition: The scheme is locally Noetherian. At every point $x$ one has $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{X,x}\geq\min(1,\dim\mathcal O_{X,x})$.
refs: Stacks 033Q · setting of the numbered statement

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Locally Noetherian scheme satisfying S₂
entries.definition: The scheme is locally Noetherian. At every point $x$ one has $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{X,x}\geq\min(2,\dim\mathcal O_{X,x})$.
refs: Stacks 033Q · setting of the numbered statement

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Scheme of dimension at most 1
entries.definition: All chains of distinct irreducible closed subsets have length at most 1.
refs: Stacks 0BX2 · setting of the numbered statement

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Scheme of dimension at most 2
entries.definition: All chains of distinct irreducible closed subsets have length at most 2.
refs: Stacks 0B3D · setting of the numbered statement

The target is locally Noetherian, so the morphism is locally of finite presentation. An fpqc covering family is flat and jointly surjective, hence fppf here.

theorems.subject: qcqs-cover
theorems.proof: The valuation test can be expressed as lifting the specialization from the generic point to the closed point after base change to a valuation spectrum. Over a rank-one valuation ring, lifting that pair of points yields an extension of rank one. Thus an arbitrary-rank cover satisfies the rank-at-most-one test. See Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.5 of Bhatt–Mathew.

theorems.proof: After shrinking affine charts about the same point, the smooth and unramified conditions give an étale algebra. The two converse implications hold at each étale point.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry II, Definition 18.34, étaleness on an open neighbourhood
theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point

theorems.name: An étale point is G-unramified
theorems.proof: An étale coordinate algebra on an affine chart about the point is finitely presented with vanishing relative differentials.
theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point

theorems.name: A smooth point is syntomic
theorems.proof: On a smooth affine chart the induced morphism is syntomic, giving the required chart at the original point.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry II, Definition 19.51 and Proposition 19.52, local factorizations and fibres
theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point

theorems.name: A syntomic point is flat
theorems.proof: The local stalk map at the point is flat by the local criterion for syntomicity.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry II, Definition 19.51 and Proposition 19.52, local factorizations and fibres
theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point

theorems.name: A syntomic point is a local complete intersection point
theorems.proof: A syntomic open neighbourhood is a local complete intersection over its target neighbourhood. Composing its smooth factor with the open immersion of the target neighbourhood preserves smoothness over the original target.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry II, Definitions 19.10 and 19.37, Koszul acyclicity and smooth factorization
theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
category-family-pair
theorems.name: Equal matching arrows are isomorphic over their target
theorems.proof: Use the same matching functions and equip each equality of arrows with the identity isomorphism of its domain.
refs: Stacks 00VV · (1) combinatorial equivalence implies tautological equivalence

theorems.name: Large cofinality gives a common stage
theorems.proof: Choose a representative at a stage for each value of $\varphi$. Those stages have an upper bound below $\beta$ by the strict inequality. Transport all representatives to such a stage.
refs: Stacks 05N2 · existence of a common stage and lift
theorems.subject: ordinal-colimit-map

theorems.name: A nonempty open cover bounds the size of its union
theorems.proof: Each affine open of the union is covered by finitely many affine opens lying in members of the cover. Count the finite lists of such opens and use the sheaf axiom to bound sections.
refs: Stacks 000Q · open-cover inequality for a nonempty index set
theorems.subject: indexed-open-cover

theorems.name: Locally finite type bounds the size of a quasi-compact source
theorems.proof: Cover the source by finitely many affine charts finite type over affine opens in the target. Bound the cardinal of a quotient of a polynomial algebra and apply the affine and open-cover bounds.
refs: Stacks 04T7 · locally finite type with quasi-compact source
theorems.subject: morphism

theorems.name: Size bound for a quasi-compact monomorphism
theorems.proof: Over an affine target each affine source chart gives a ring epimorphism, which bounds its cardinality. Quasi-compactness supplies a finite affine cover of the inverse image.
theorems.subject: morphism

theorems.name: Size bound for a locally finitely presented monomorphism
theorems.proof: Over an affine target count finite presentations of affine charts. A monomorphism admits at most one lift of a given affine target map.
theorems.subject: morphism
field
theorems.name: An algebraically closed field has trivial Brauer group
theorems.proof: For each element of a finite central division algebra over $k$, its generated commutative subalgebra is a finite field extension. Algebraic closedness makes every such element scalar.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Example 2.14(a)

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: The dimension of a central simple algebra is a positive square
theorems.proof: After extending scalars to an algebraic closure the algebra is a matrix ring, and the dimension is preserved.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.15 and Corollary 2.16

theorems.subject: brauer-embedded-subfield
theorems.name: Full-degree and self-centralizing subfields
theorems.proof: The algebra is finite central simple and $k\subseteq L\subseteq A$. The dimension identity $[L:k][C_A(L):k]=[A:k]$ and $L\subseteq C_A(L)$ give the equivalence.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Corollaries 3.4–3.6

theorems.subject: brauer-embedded-subfield
theorems.name: Self-centralization and maximal commutativity
theorems.proof: An element commuting with all of the field $L$ generates a commutative subring together with $L$. Conversely every commutative enlargement of $L$ lies in its centralizer.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Corollaries 3.4–3.6

theorems.subject: brauer-extension
theorems.name: Realizing a finite splitting field inside a representative
theorems.proof: If $A_L$ splits, choose a split simple module over $L$. The endomorphism construction in the proof yields a central simple representative of the class of $A$ (using the opposite algebra on the appropriate side), with $L$ embedded and dimension $[L:k]^2$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Corollaries 3.4–3.6

theorems.subject: brauer-extension
theorems.name: A full-degree embedding splits a representative
theorems.proof: For such a representative $B$, $L$ is self-centralizing. Inside $B\otimes_k B^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\operatorname{End}_k(B)$ its centralizer calculation identifies $B\otimes_k L$ with an endomorphism algebra over $L$. A matrix stabilization then splits $A$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Corollaries 3.4–3.6

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Defining conditions for a finite central simple algebra
theorems.proof: The scalar map from a field to a nonzero unital algebra is faithful; centrality then identifies its center with $k$. These are precisely the defining conditions.

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Central simplicity and algebraic closure
theorems.proof: A finite central simple algebra remains so after extending scalars and is a matrix algebra over an algebraically closed field. Faithful scalar extension detects dimension, centrality and two-sided simplicity.

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Central simplicity and separable closure
theorems.proof: A finite separable splitting extension embeds in a separable closure. Conversely a matrix presentation there persists over an algebraic closure.

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Central simplicity and finite Galois splitting
theorems.proof: Take the Galois closure of a finite separable splitting field. Conversely a matrix presentation over a finite Galois extension remains a matrix presentation over an algebraic closure.

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Central simplicity and matrix presentation over a central division algebra
theorems.proof: Wedderburn gives the matrix presentation and identifies the center of the division factor with $k$. Conversely the center, ideal correspondence and dimension of a positive-size matrix algebra give the defining conditions.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Hausdorffness and the closed diagonal
theorems.proof: An off-diagonal point lies in an open rectangle avoiding the diagonal exactly when its coordinates have disjoint open neighbourhoods.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definitions 1.8, 1.12 and Lemma 1.13

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closed graph with Hausdorff target
theorems.proof: The graph is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of the target under $(x,y)\mapsto(f(x),y)$.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definitions 1.8, 1.12 and Lemma 1.13

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Relative diagonal closedness test
theorems.proof: The diagonal is an embedding because a projection restricts to its inverse. An embedding is closed exactly when its image is closed.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Separation by neighbourhoods in the source
theorems.proof: The complement of the relative diagonal is open precisely when each unequal equal-image pair lies in a basic product neighbourhood missing the diagonal.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Hausdorff source implies a separated map
theorems.proof: Hausdorffness separates all unequal source points, including those having equal image.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definitions 1.8, 1.12 and Lemma 1.13

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Basis criterion
theorems.proof: The first condition ensures unions of basic sets are open. The second expresses each open as such a union.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.3 and Lemma 1.4

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Submersive maps as surjective strict maps
theorems.proof: For a surjection the subspace topology on the image is the original topology on the target.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.16 and Proposition 2.5

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Surjective open maps are submersive
theorems.proof: Openness of a target subset is detected by inverse image, which gives the quotient topology.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.16 and Proposition 2.5

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Surjective closed maps are submersive
theorems.proof: Openness of a target subset is detected by inverse image, which gives the quotient topology.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.16 and Proposition 2.5

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Connected fibres of a quotient map
theorems.proof: Fibre nonemptiness gives surjectivity, so the closed-set test is precisely the quotient condition. A separation of the inverse image of a closed component splits it into saturated closed sets and descends to a separation of the component.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Connected fibres of an open map
theorems.proof: Nonempty fibres give surjectivity. An open surjection has the quotient topology, so the connected-fibre quotient argument applies.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Locally connected spaces have open components
theorems.proof: At each point a connected neighbourhood lies in its component. Thus each component is a neighbourhood of all its points.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 4.8(i) and Proposition 4.9(i)
Pi-Base P000234 · Has open connected components

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Irreducibility and nonempty hyperconnectedness
theorems.proof: By taking complements, a cover by two proper closed sets is equivalent to two disjoint nonempty open sets. Nonemptiness is a separate hypothesis.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Sobriety from existence and uniqueness of generic points
theorems.proof: Point closures are nonempty irreducible closed sets. The point-closure map is surjective by quasi-sobriety, and injective exactly when distinct points are topologically distinguishable.
refs: Dickmann, Schwartz and Tressl, Spectral Spaces, §1.1.13 (point closures and uniqueness)
Pi-Base T000512 · quasi-sober and Kolmogorov imply sober

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Hausdorff spaces are sober
theorems.proof: Every irreducible closed subset is a singleton and its sole point is its unique generic point.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Closed point of a nonempty Kolmogorov Noetherian space
theorems.proof: Choose a minimal nonempty closed subset by the descending chain condition. Its points all have that set as closure, so the Kolmogorov condition makes it a singleton.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Catenarity by finite intervals and uniform lengths
theorems.proof: The finite codimension bounds all possible chain lengths and is attained. Every chain can then be extended to a maximal chain. Equality of maximal lengths forces their common length to be this bound.
refs: Stacks 02I1 · finite bound and equality of maximal lengths

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Catenarity is local on an open cover
theorems.proof: Choose a cover open meeting the smaller endpoint of any irreducible interval. Restriction identifies the entire interval, including its maximal chains, with the interval in that open by closure.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Catenarity by finite additive codimension
theorems.proof: In a catenary interval, concatenating maximal chains across the middle gives a maximal chain. Conversely finite codimension makes every maximal chain finite and additivity expresses its endpoint codimension as the sum of the unit codimensions of its adjacent steps.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Closed point in a nonempty quasi-compact Kolmogorov space
theorems.proof: A descending chain of point closures has a nonempty intersection by quasi-compactness, so some point closure is a lower bound. A minimal point closure exists by Zorn’s lemma and consists of one point by the Kolmogorov axiom.
refs: Stacks 005E · existence of a closed point

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Clopen intersection under quasi-compact basis hypotheses
theorems.proof: A separation of a quasicomponent would have quasi-compact closed sides. Cover them by quasi-compact opens whose traces are the sides. Compactness of the overlap and of the complement of their union produces one clopen neighbourhood on which they form a separation, contradicting the defining intersection.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Clopen intersection in a compact Hausdorff space
theorems.proof: Disjoint quasi-compact sides of a hypothetical separation of the quasicomponent have disjoint open neighbourhoods. Compactness of the complement of their union supplies a clopen neighbourhood already lying in their union, contradicting that separation.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Quasi-compact locally Noetherian spaces are Noetherian
theorems.proof: The interiors of Noetherian neighbourhoods have a finite subcover. The space is a finite union of Noetherian subspaces.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Baire theorem for locally quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces
theorems.proof: Inside any nonempty open, successively choose nonempty nested quasi-compact neighbourhoods lying in successive dense opens and in the interiors of the preceding neighbourhoods. They are closed in the first compact neighbourhood and have a common point.
refs: Stacks 0CQN · density of the countable intersection

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Inverse image criterion for constructibility
theorems.proof: Inverse image commutes with differences and finite unions. By continuity and the hypothesis, it sends each retrocompact open used in a presentation to a retrocompact open.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructible subsets are retrocompact
theorems.proof: Intersect a presentation by differences with a quasi-compact open. Each resulting piece is closed in the intersection of that quasi-compact open with a retrocompact open, hence quasi-compact. Take their finite union.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Corollary 2.3.4

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Topological properness and the relative diagonal
theorems.proof: This is the defining conjunction. Separation uses the relative diagonal in the fibre product.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness detected by product projections
theorems.proof: A tube about a compact fibre shows the projection is closed. Conversely take a family of closed subsets with the finite-intersection property and empty total intersection. Index their finite intersections by isolated finite subfamilies with a point at infinity having the tails as neighbourhoods. The closed subset with those finite intersections as fibres and empty fibre at infinity has nonclosed projection.
refs: Stacks 005Q · bibliographic identification of the projection criterion

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Bourbaki-proper versus closed quasi-proper
theorems.proof: Bourbaki-proper maps are closed by testing a singleton factor. Restrict any product to the inverse image of a quasi-compact subset, then compose with its closed product projection to test quasi-compactness upstairs. Conversely quasi-proper gives quasi-compact fibres and the closed-fibre criterion gives universal closedness.
refs: Stacks 005S · Bourbaki I, p. 77, Proposition 6 and p. 75, Theorem 1

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Bourbaki-proper versus universally closed
theorems.proof: Product tests are particular base changes. In the converse direction Bourbaki-proper maps are closed with quasi-compact fibres, so the tube argument after arbitrary base change applies.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closed maps with quasi-compact fibres
theorems.proof: For a closed map with quasi-compact fibres, use a tube around each fibre avoiding a relative closed set in a base change, then closedness of the original map to shrink on the base. Conversely test the identity base change for closedness and base change to each point, using the product projection criterion.
refs: Stacks 005S · Lang, Real and Functional Analysis, chapter II, Exercise 25

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Bourbaki closed-fibre criterion
theorems.proof: All products are base changes, and a closed map with quasi-compact fibres remains closed under base change. Conversely the product test implies quasi-compactness over compact subsets, in particular over any singleton.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Quasi-proper maps have quasi-compact fibres
theorems.proof: Each singleton of the target is quasi-compact; its inverse image is the corresponding fibre. The closed-map condition common to (1) and (4) is carried along.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Universally closed map from a quasi-compact space to a Hausdorff space
theorems.proof: A closed subset of the source is quasi-compact, so its image is quasi-compact and closed in the Hausdorff target. Fibres are closed in the source, hence quasi-compact. Apply the closed-fibre criterion.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Continuous bijection from a quasi-compact space to a Hausdorff space
theorems.proof: The map is closed since images of closed subspaces are quasi-compact and the target is Hausdorff. The inverse of a closed bijection is continuous.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Theorem 5.7

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Jacobson criterion on point closures
theorems.proof: Any nonempty relatively open part of a closed subset contains a point. Its point closure is contained in the subset, so density there supplies an ambient closed point in the same relatively open part.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Finite Jacobson spaces are discrete
theorems.proof: The finite set of closed points is dense and closed, so all points are closed. On a finite set this implies that each singleton is open.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Jacobson spaces with finitely many closed points are discrete
theorems.proof: The union of the finitely many closed singletons is closed and dense, hence equals the whole space. Its topology is therefore discrete.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closed sets are stable under specialization
theorems.proof: A closed set containing a point also contains its closure.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Open sets are stable under generalization
theorems.proof: If the open contains a specialization, its open neighbourhood must meet the singleton of the given generalization.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Directed closed unions and specialization stability
theorems.proof: For a specialization-stable subset take all finite unions of its point closures, including the empty union. These form a directed closed cover. Conversely every closed member is specialization-stable and unions preserve the condition.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closed maps lift specializations
theorems.proof: The image of the closure of the specified source point is closed and contains its image, so contains every specialization of that image.

theorems.subject: space-integer-function
theorems.name: Two conditions for a dimension function
theorems.proof: The first requirement covers all comparable distinct points, including intervals where no finite saturated chain is given. The second fixes the step on immediate intervals.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: A sober space with a dimension function is catenary
theorems.proof: All irreducible closed subsets have unique generic points. Strict integer decrease bounds chain length between two endpoints. Any maximal chain has immediate steps of size one, forcing its length to equal the endpoint difference.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Spectral space axioms
theorems.proof: Sobriety, quasi-compactness, the basis condition, and stability of quasi-compact opens under binary intersections are exactly the axioms.

theorems.subject: group-with-topology
theorems.name: Topological group operation axioms
theorems.proof: These two continuity conditions define topological group structures.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family

theorems.proof: The original family covers in degree zero. All positive matching maps of its relative zero-coskeleton are isomorphisms.
refs: Stacks 01G6 · numbered Stacks source and proof
Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, Definition 4.10 and Lemma 4.11, height-zero hypercovers
Stacks 01G6 · verification of the two covering conditions

theorems.subject: site-simplicial-family
theorems.name: Splitness via all degeneracy composites
theorems.proof: The image of the degeneracy maps supplies a disjoint union indexed by surjections of simplices; the remaining indices are exactly the nondegenerate ones. Every ordinal surjection factors into elementary degeneracy operators.
refs: Stacks 0DAU · numbered Stacks source and proof
Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, Definition 4.13, split simplicial objects

theorems.subject: site-simplicial-family

theorems.proof: The image of the degeneracy maps supplies a disjoint union indexed by surjections of simplices; the remaining indices are exactly the nondegenerate ones. Every ordinal surjection factors into elementary degeneracy operators.
refs: Stacks 0DAU · numbered Stacks source and proof
Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, Definition 4.13, split simplicial objects

theorems.subject: space-presheaf
theorems.name: Sheaves are separated
theorems.proof: Equal germs at each point give equality on an open cover, so the uniqueness part of gluing gives equality on the whole open.
refs: Stacks 0079 · injectivity on sections into the product of stalks

theorems.subject: concrete-category
theorems.name: Conditions characterizing a type of algebraic structure
theorems.proof: These are the four defining axioms with existence and preservation of the relevant limits and colimits recorded separately.

theorems.subject: space-sheaf-map
theorems.name: Sectionwise lifts give local lifts
theorems.proof: For any section on an open use its lift there and the singleton identity cover.

theorems.subject: space-sheaf-map
theorems.name: Stalk criterion for a monomorphism
theorems.proof: Equality of germs gives local equality and lifts of germs give local lifts. The sheaf gluing and uniqueness axioms turn these local tests into the categorical criterion.

theorems.subject: space-sheaf-map
theorems.name: Stalk criterion for a epimorphism
theorems.proof: Equality of germs gives local equality and lifts of germs give local lifts. The sheaf gluing and uniqueness axioms turn these local tests into the categorical criterion.

theorems.subject: space-sheaf-map
theorems.name: Stalk criterion for a isomorphism
theorems.proof: Equality of germs gives local equality and lifts of germs give local lifts. The sheaf gluing and uniqueness axioms turn these local tests into the categorical criterion.

theorems.subject: set-presheaf-morphism
theorems.name: Presheaf monomorphisms are sectionwise injective
theorems.proof: Limits and colimits of presheaves are computed pointwise. Apply the diagonal or codiagonal characterization.

theorems.subject: space-sheaf-map
theorems.name: Categorical criterion for injective sheaf morphisms
theorems.proof: Stalkwise injectivity is equivalent to injectivity on sections of sheaves. Stalkwise surjectivity is equivalent to lifting sections locally.

theorems.subject: set-presheaf-morphism
theorems.name: Presheaf epimorphisms are sectionwise surjective
theorems.proof: Limits and colimits of presheaves are computed pointwise. Apply the diagonal or codiagonal characterization.

theorems.subject: space-sheaf-map
theorems.name: Categorical criterion for surjective sheaf morphisms
theorems.proof: Stalkwise injectivity is equivalent to injectivity on sections of sheaves. Stalkwise surjectivity is equivalent to lifting sections locally.

theorems.subject: space-presheaf
theorems.name: Separated presheaves and the unit
theorems.proof: The unit identifies sections exactly when they have the same germs at every point of their common open.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Flat quasi-compact surjective monomorphisms are isomorphisms
theorems.proof: After fpqc base change by the morphism itself, its pullback is an isomorphism by the diagonal criterion for a monomorphism.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Universally injective étale morphisms are open immersions
theorems.proof: The étale map is open. Over its open image it is an étale surjection whose diagonal is an isomorphism, hence an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Faithful flatness gives a pure ring map
theorems.proof: The map $M\to M\otimes_R S$ becomes split injective after extension of scalars; faithful flatness reflects that injectivity.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Module descent implies effective module descent
theorems.proof: For a commutative ring map either condition is equivalent to purity of its underlying module map.
refs: B. Mesablishvili, Pure morphisms of commutative rings are effective descent morphisms for modules, Theorem 4

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Effective module descent is purity
theorems.proof: Character duality identifies purity with a split condition. Applying the descent comparison yields equivalence precisely in that case.
refs: B. Mesablishvili, Pure morphisms of commutative rings are effective descent morphisms for modules, Theorem 4

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Three conditions for étale locality on source and target
theorems.proof: The conjunction is the joint locality condition by definition.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Joint locality implies source locality
theorems.proof: Take the target vertical maps to be identity in the local comparison diagrams.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Joint locality implies target locality
theorems.proof: Base-change stable properties recognized by local étale squares descend along étale target covers.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Decomposing unramifiedness of a Noetherian local homomorphism
theorems.proof: In the Noetherian local domain of discourse, these are precisely the maximal-ideal, residue, and finiteness conditions.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat and unramified local maps
theorems.proof: Flatness is imposed in addition to all three local unramifiedness conditions.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.6.1 and 17.6.3, local and completed étale criteria

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Unramified monomorphisms and unramified radicial morphisms
theorems.proof: The unramified diagonal is open, and universal injectivity identifies it with the entire fibre square. The fibre criterion also detects residue-field equality and the required unramifiedness.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Unramified monomorphisms and locally finite type monomorphisms
theorems.proof: The unramified diagonal is open, and universal injectivity identifies it with the entire fibre square. The fibre criterion also detects residue-field equality and the required unramifiedness.

theorems.subject: morphism

theorems.proof: The unramified diagonal is open, and universal injectivity identifies it with the entire fibre square. The fibre criterion also detects residue-field equality and the required unramifiedness.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Closed immersions and proper monomorphisms
theorems.proof: The weakly stated clauses first imply unramified monomorphism by the fibre and diagonal criterion. Universal closedness and quasi-finiteness in this setting force finiteness; a finite monomorphism is a closed immersion.

theorems.subject: morphism

theorems.proof: The weakly stated clauses first imply unramified monomorphism by the fibre and diagonal criterion. Universal closedness and quasi-finiteness in this setting force finiteness; a finite monomorphism is a closed immersion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Open immersions and universally injective étale maps
theorems.proof: An étale radicial map identifies its source with its open image. Conversely an open immersion is étale, radicial, flat, locally of finite presentation and a monomorphism.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Open immersions and flat locally finitely presented monomorphisms
theorems.proof: An étale radicial map identifies its source with its open image. Conversely an open immersion is étale, radicial, flat, locally of finite presentation and a monomorphism.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: An fpqc morphism induces the quotient topology
theorems.proof: Fpqc descent for open subsets identifies subsets whose inverse images are open with opens of the target.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Finite presentation locally and unique infinitesimal lifting
theorems.proof: An étale morphism is locally finitely presented and formally étale. Conversely these two conditions imply étaleness on affine charts.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.6.1 and 17.6.3, local and completed étale criteria
Stacks 025K · (1) iff (2) for locally finitely presented morphisms

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme

theorems.proof: The local equation is required at every point of the divisor; the ambient scheme may have singularities away from it.

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme
theorems.name: Recognizing strict normal crossings from component intersections
theorems.proof: The proof works at points of $D$ and uses nonempty selections of components. Their local equations extend to regular parameters. For an empty selection the ambient intersection would be all of $X$, whose regularity away from $D$ is not required by Tag 0BI9.

Stacks 0BIA · (1) iff (2), nonempty intersections along D

theorems.subject: crystalline-frobenius
theorems.name: Forgetting nondegeneracy of an F-crystal
theorems.proof: The nondegeneracy condition is imposed on the Frobenius map of a finite locally free crystal.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-map
theorems.name: Three criteria for a locally ringed closed immersion
theorems.proof: These are precisely the three conditions in the definition.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Closed-image criterion for an immersion
theorems.proof: Within an open neighbourhood of its image the immersion is closed. The complementary open of its closed image completes a target cover on which it is a closed immersion.
refs: Stacks 01IQ · closed immersion ⇔ immersion with closed image

theorems.subject: scheme-chart-presheaf
theorems.name: Extending sheaves from the affine basis
theorems.proof: Sheaves on any topological basis extend uniquely up to unique compatible isomorphism.

theorems.subject: scheme-chart-presheaf
theorems.name: Binary principal-cover criterion
theorems.proof: Reduce an arbitrary affine cover to finite principal covers. A unit-ideal relation reduces a finite principal cover to a binary one and covers with fewer members.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Finite discrete schemes are affine
theorems.proof: Each open singleton is affine by the affine basis. A finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine, including the empty spectrum.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Section-ring test for reducedness
theorems.proof: A nilpotent section has nilpotent germs. Conversely a nilpotent germ is represented by a section whose chosen power vanishes after shrinking.
refs: Stacks 01J1 · reduced stalks ⇔ reduced section rings

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness on all affine opens
theorems.proof: A quasi-compact target open has a finite affine cover. The inverse image of a finite union of affines with quasi-compact inverse images is quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness on a single affine cover
theorems.proof: Over a member of the chosen target cover the source has a finite affine cover. Principal localizations and common finite refinements give quasi-compact inverse images of arbitrary affine opens.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Closed immersions are quasi-compact
theorems.proof: The inverse image of a quasi-compact open is a closed subspace thereof and is quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Closed images are stable under specialization
theorems.proof: Every closed subset contains all specializations of its points.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: A specialization-stable quasi-compact image is closed
theorems.proof: Over each target affine a finite affine cover of the source realizes the image as the image of one spectrum. That image is closed when stable under specialization.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Closed maps lift specializations
theorems.proof: The image of the closure of x′ is closed and contains f(x′), hence contains its specializations.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-compact maps that lift specializations are closed
theorems.proof: Restrict to each closed subset with its reduced structure. Its image is stable under specialization and the restricted map is quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Universal closedness lifts specializations universally
theorems.proof: Apply lifting for a closed continuous map to each base change.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Universal lifting and quasi-compactness imply universal closedness
theorems.proof: Quasi-compactness survives every base change, so the specialization-lifting criterion gives closedness for every projection.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Valuative existence and universal specialization lifting
theorems.proof: To construct a filler base change to the valuation spectrum and specialize the image of the generic point. A local overring of the valuation ring inside its fraction field that dominates it equals it. Conversely realize any base specialization using a valuation ring with prescribed generic field, then lift.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Universally closed morphisms satisfy valuative existence
theorems.proof: Universal closedness gives universal specialization lifting, which gives valuative existence. This direction does not need the quasi-compactness assumed in the proposition.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Valuative existence tests universal closedness for quasi-compact morphisms
theorems.proof: Existence gives lifting after every base change, and quasi-compactness gives closedness for each such morphism.
refs: Stacks 01KF · existence ⇒ universal closedness under quasi-compactness

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-separatedness by all compatible affine pairs
theorems.proof: Such a pair defines an affine chart of the relative square and its diagonal inverse image is the intersection. These charts cover the square.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-separatedness by one affine chart system
theorems.proof: The pairwise fibre products of the chosen charts affinely cover the relative square, so quasi-compactness of the diagonal can be checked there.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Separated morphisms satisfy valuative uniqueness
theorems.proof: Two lifts agree on the generic point. Their closed equalizer in the spectrum of the valuation domain is the entire scheme, since the domain embeds into its fraction field.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Valuative uniqueness tests separatedness for quasi-separated morphisms
theorems.proof: The quasi-compact diagonal is an immersion. Uniqueness of lifts for the morphism gives existence of lifts for its diagonal, so the diagonal is universally closed and hence a closed immersion.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA II, Proposition 7.2.3(b) ⇒ (a), with quasi-compact diagonal

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Diagonal criterion for a monomorphism
theorems.proof: The two projections from the relative square agree exactly when every pair of parallel test morphisms equalized by f already agrees. Then the diagonal is inverse to either projection.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Monomorphisms of schemes are separated
theorems.proof: An isomorphism is a closed immersion. Apply this to the diagonal.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Injectivity on points implies separatedness
theorems.proof: Over any point of the relative square both projections coincide as points. The square is therefore covered by affine chart squares U ×ᵥ U on which the diagonal is a closed immersion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Monomorphism from injective points and surjective stalks
theorems.proof: Two maps with equal composites have the same point map by injectivity. Their maps on each stalk agree after precomposition by a surjective ring map, hence agree.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Immersions of schemes are separated
theorems.proof: An immersion is a monomorphism and hence has isomorphic, in particular closed, diagonal.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Closed immersions from a topological embedding and a sheaf surjection
theorems.proof: The conditions make f quasi-compact and a monomorphism, hence separated. Its direct image of the structure sheaf is quasi-coherent, so the kernel ideal is quasi-coherent and locally generated by sections.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: The space of a qcqs scheme is spectral
theorems.proof: Affine opens form a quasi-compact basis, quasi-separatedness controls intersections, and schemes are sober.
refs: Stacks 094L · spectrality of the underlying space

theorems.subject: ring-predicate
theorems.name: Axioms of a local ring property
theorems.proof: This is the conjunction defining locality.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Nagata schemes are locally Noetherian
theorems.proof: A Nagata ring is Noetherian and Nagata affine charts cover the scheme.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Nagata schemes and universal Japanese finiteness
theorems.proof: On Noetherian affine charts, a ring is Nagata iff it is universally Japanese.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Normal schemes are geometrically unibranch
theorems.proof: A normal local domain is its own normalization and its residue field extension there is trivial.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: The two defining conditions of ampleness
theorems.proof: These are the two conjuncts of the definition.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-separated schemes admit common affine neighbourhoods of generic points
theorems.proof: The finite disjoint affine neighbourhoods supplied by the lemma have affine union.

theorems.proof: The forward direction needs local Noetherianity. Conversely both typed Serre predicates include local Noetherianity, and the affine Serre criterion recovers the asserted scheme property.
refs: Stacks 0344 · locally Noetherian equivalence, with both fixed indices

theorems.subject: scheme

refs: Stacks 0BX2 · conclusion under the dimension bound

theorems.subject: scheme

theorems.proof: Normality on a locally Noetherian scheme gives (R₁) and (S₂). The dimension bound makes the relevant local-ring condition exhaustive.
refs: Stacks 0B3D · conclusion under the dimension bound

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A nonzero ring has a nonempty spectrum. An idempotent and its complement specify a clopen partition of that spectrum.
theorems.name: Nonzero ring ∧ No nontrivial idempotents ⇔ Connected prime spectrum

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Multiplying by the inverse of a nonzero factor cancels it.
theorems.name: Field ⇒ Integral domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Nonzeroness is part of the definition of domain.
theorems.name: Integral domain ⇒ Nonzero ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The local ring has a proper maximal ideal. The zero ring has none.
theorems.name: Local ring ⇒ Nonzero ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The only maximal ideal of a field is the zero ideal.
theorems.name: Field ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The zero and unit ideals are principal.
theorems.name: Field ⇒ Every ideal is principal

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Division by each nonzero element has remainder zero.
theorems.name: Field ⇒ Euclidean domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Fields are included in the existence theorem for excellent rings.
theorems.name: Field ⇒ Excellent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A product of finitely many nonzero elements of a domain is nonzero.
theorems.name: Integral domain ⇒ Reduced ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A reduced ring equals its reduction. The nilradical of a domain is zero.
theorems.name: Reduced ring ∧ Reduction is a domain ⇔ Integral domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The zero ideal is prime and is contained in every prime ideal.
refs: Stacks 00BR · quotient criterion for a prime ideal
theorems.name: Integral domain ⇒ Finitely many minimal primes

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: If an idempotent e satisfies e(e−1)=0 in a domain, then e is zero or one.
theorems.name: Integral domain ⇒ Connected prime spectrum

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: One of e and 1−e is a unit in a local ring, and e(1−e)=0.
theorems.name: Local ring ⇒ Connected prime spectrum

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A singleton set of maximal ideals is finite.
theorems.name: Local ring ⇒ Semilocal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The maximal and minimal primes are subsets of the prime ideals.
theorems.name: Finitely many prime ideals ⇒ Semilocal ring ∧ Finitely many minimal primes

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The nilradical is locally nilpotent and is finitely generated by Noetherianity.
refs: Stacks 00IM · Noetherian locally nilpotent ideals are nilpotent
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ⇒ Nilpotent nilradical

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Apply the theorem on the Jacobson radical of an Artinian ring.
refs: Stacks 00J8 · Artinian rings have nilpotent Jacobson radical
theorems.name: Artinian ring ⇒ Nilpotent Jacobson radical

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The nilradical is contained in every maximal ideal and therefore in the Jacobson radical.
theorems.name: Nilpotent Jacobson radical ⇒ Nilpotent nilradical

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Every prime is maximal, so the two radical ideals are intersections of the same primes.
refs: Stacks 04MG · rings whose primes are all maximal
theorems.name: Krull dimension at most zero ∧ Nilpotent nilradical ⇒ Nilpotent Jacobson radical

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Every radical ideal is the intersection of the primes containing it, and each such prime is maximal.
refs: Stacks 00E0 · prime spectrum and radical ideals
theorems.name: Krull dimension at most zero ⇒ Jacobson ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Each prime is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it. In a local ring the only such maximal ideal is the unique maximal ideal, so it is the only prime.
refs: Stacks 00G2 · prime-ideal criterion for Jacobson rings
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Jacobson ring ⇒ Krull dimension at most zero

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The zero ideal of a domain is prime. In dimension at most zero it is maximal, which makes the domain a field. Every field has one prime.
refs: Stacks 00AR · prime and maximal ideal quotient criteria
theorems.name: Integral domain ∧ Krull dimension at most zero ⇔ Field

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The weak dimension zero criterion identifies absolute flatness with reducedness and maximality of all primes.
theorems.name: Reduced ring ∧ Krull dimension at most zero ⇔ Absolutely flat ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Flatness of all modules can be checked at primes. The resulting local rings of an absolutely flat ring are fields.
theorems.name: Absolutely flat ring ⇔ Field at every prime

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Use the ideal-flatness criterion and the classification of the local domains whose finitely generated ideals are principal.
refs: Stacks 092S · weak dimension at most one
theorems.name: Weak dimension at most one ⇔ Valuation ring at every prime

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Flat dimension zero is at most one.
theorems.name: Absolutely flat ring ⇒ Weak dimension at most one

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A local ring equals its localization at the maximal ideal. Localizations of valuation rings are valuation rings.
refs: Stacks 092S · weak dimension at most one
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Weak dimension at most one ⇔ Valuation ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Each prime localization is a field, and each field is an integrally closed domain.
theorems.name: Absolutely flat ring ⇒ Normal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Each prime localization is a valuation ring and every valuation ring is a normal domain.
refs: Stacks 092S · weak dimension and valuation localizations
theorems.name: Weak dimension at most one ⇒ Normal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: An ideal with flat quotient is pure. In an absolutely flat ring every quotient is flat, so any finitely generated ideal is generated by an idempotent and is a finitely presented direct summand of the ring.
theorems.name: Absolutely flat ring ⇒ Coherent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Finitely generated modules over a Noetherian ring are finitely presented, including finitely generated ideals.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ⇒ Coherent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The spectrum of a Noetherian ring is a Noetherian space. Its irreducible components correspond to minimal primes and are finite in number.
refs: Stacks 00FR · finite set of minimal primes
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ⇒ Finitely many minimal primes

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A Noetherian ring with every prime maximal is Artinian. Conversely an Artinian ring is Noetherian and every prime is maximal.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Krull dimension at most zero ⇔ Artinian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The Artinian finite-length criterion applies to the ring as a module over itself.
theorems.name: Artinian ring ⇔ Finite length over itself

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Every prime is maximal and the set of maximal ideals is finite.
theorems.name: Artinian ring ⇒ Finitely many prime ideals

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Artinian rings decompose as a finite product of their maximal localizations. If reduced, each localization is a field. A finite product of fields is Artinian and reduced.
theorems.name: Artinian ring ∧ Reduced ring ⇔ Finite product of fields

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A local Noetherian domain of dimension at least two has infinitely many prime ideals. The theorem extends the conclusion by passing to minimal-prime quotients and maximal localizations.
refs: Stacks 0ALV · finite prime spectrum of a Noetherian ring
theorems.name: Finitely many prime ideals ∧ Noetherian ring ⇒ Krull dimension at most one

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A chain with two strict inclusions would have a strict inclusion.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights
theorems.name: Krull dimension at most zero ⇒ Krull dimension at most one

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A nonzero ring has a prime ideal. A nonempty spectrum with no strict prime inclusions has dimension exactly zero.
refs: Stacks 00AQ · existence of primes for nonzero rings
Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights
theorems.name: Nonzero ring ∧ Krull dimension at most zero ⇔ Krull dimension zero with nonempty spectrum

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The definition bounds the length of any chain by one.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights
theorems.name: Krull dimension exactly one ⇒ Krull dimension at most one

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A prime exists if a strict inclusion of primes occurs.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights
theorems.name: Krull dimension exactly one ⇒ Nonzero ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The common finite bound is one.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights
theorems.name: Krull dimension at most one ⇒ Finite Krull dimension

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Equal endpoints give length zero. Distinct comparable endpoints admit only a chain of length one between them.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights
theorems.name: Krull dimension at most one ⇒ Catenary ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Noetherianity is part of the definition, and the ring is of finite type over itself.
theorems.name: Universally catenary ring ⇒ Noetherian ring ∧ Catenary ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Every nilpotent maps to zero in each prime localization, and prime localizations detect a zero element.
theorems.name: Normal ring ⇒ Reduced ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: An element integral over the ring lies in every prime localization. Local detection of membership in the ring then applies.
refs: Stacks 034M · normal rings are integrally closed in their total ring of fractions
theorems.name: Normal ring ⇒ Integrally closed in the total ring of fractions

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: For a domain, normality can be checked at the maximal ideals or at all primes.
refs: Stacks 030B · normality of a domain is local
theorems.name: Integral domain ∧ Normal ring ⇔ Normal domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The localization of a local ring at its maximal ideal is the original ring.
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Normal ring ⇒ Normal domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The total ring of fractions of a domain equals its fraction field.
theorems.name: Integral domain ∧ Integrally closed in the total ring of fractions ⇔ Normal domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Under the finite-minimal-primes and reducedness assumptions, the total ring of fractions is the product of the fraction fields of the minimal components.
refs: Stacks 030C · normality criterion with finitely many minimal primes
theorems.name: Reduced ring ∧ Finitely many minimal primes ∧ Integrally closed in the total ring of fractions ⇒ Normal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Normality supplies reducedness, so the finite-minimal-primes decomposition applies.
theorems.name: Normal ring ∧ Finitely many minimal primes ⇒ Finite product of normal domains

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Prime ideals of a finite product come from its factors, and localization selects one factor. Each domain factor has one minimal prime.
refs: Stacks 0CYA · finite products of normal rings
theorems.name: Finite product of normal domains ⇒ Normal ring ∧ Finitely many minimal primes

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: If a nonzero integral element lies outside a valuation ring, its inverse lies in the maximal ideal. Multiplying its monic equation by an inverse power contradicts reduction modulo the maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 00IC · valuation rings are normal domains
theorems.name: Valuation ring ⇒ Normal domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In a local domain with each two-generated ideal principal, a generating pair for a principal ideal contains a generator. Hence the two elements are comparable for divisibility. The valuation condition conversely orders principal ideals.
refs: Stacks 090Q · local domain with principal finitely generated ideals
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Integral domain ∧ Every finitely generated ideal is principal ⇔ Valuation ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A maximal nonprincipal ideal is prime. If all ideals are principal the implication in the other direction is immediate.
theorems.name: Every prime ideal is principal ⇔ Every ideal is principal

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A principal ideal has a finite generating set consisting of at most one element.
refs: Stacks 034U · principal ideals in a PID
theorems.name: Every ideal is principal ⇒ Every finitely generated ideal is principal ∧ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The height-one prime ideals form a subset of all prime ideals.
theorems.name: Every prime ideal is principal ⇒ Every height-one prime is principal

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: This is the definition of a principal ideal domain.
theorems.name: Integral domain ∧ Every ideal is principal ⇔ Principal ideal domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In a nonzero ideal choose a nonzero element of least Euclidean value. The remainder of any element of the ideal upon division by it lies in the ideal and must vanish.
theorems.name: Euclidean domain ⇒ Principal ideal domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A PID is Noetherian and has principal height-one primes, so the height-one criterion applies.
theorems.name: Principal ideal domain ⇒ Unique factorization domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A principal nonzero ideal factors uniquely because a generator factors uniquely into irreducibles, which generate nonzero prime ideals.
theorems.name: Principal ideal domain ⇒ Dedekind domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: For a fraction in lowest terms, any irreducible factor of its denominator would divide its numerator if the fraction satisfied a monic equation.
theorems.name: Unique factorization domain ⇒ Normal domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: For a nonzero element of a height-one prime, one irreducible factor belongs to that prime. Its principal prime ideal must equal the height-one prime.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Unique factorization domain ⇒ Every height-one prime is principal

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The ascending chain condition supplies factorization. Principal height-one primes force each irreducible to generate a prime ideal.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Integral domain ∧ Every height-one prime is principal ⇒ Unique factorization domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The Dedekind criterion gives this equivalence, including fields under the stated definition.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Normal domain ∧ Krull dimension at most one ⇔ Dedekind domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In dimension one a regular local ring is a domain and its maximal ideal is principal and nonzero. Conversely a discrete valuation ring has Krull dimension one and maximal ideal generated by a uniformizer.
refs: Stacks 00PD · equivalent conditions for a discrete valuation ring
theorems.name: Regular local ring ∧ Krull dimension exactly one ⇔ Discrete valuation ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A one-dimensional Noetherian local normal domain is a discrete valuation ring, and a DVR has all four conditions.
refs: Stacks 00PD · equivalent conditions for a discrete valuation ring
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Local ring ∧ Normal domain ∧ Krull dimension exactly one ⇔ Discrete valuation ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The valuation orders all ideals by their integer values. Each nonzero ideal has a generator of the least value that occurs in that ideal.
refs: Stacks 00PD · equivalent conditions for a discrete valuation ring
theorems.name: Discrete valuation ring ⇒ Valuation ring ∧ Principal ideal domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The ring is a Noetherian normal domain and the dimension-one DVR criterion applies.
refs: Stacks 00PD · equivalent conditions for a discrete valuation ring
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Dedekind domain ∧ Krull dimension exactly one ⇒ Discrete valuation ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Noetherianity is part of the definition of a regular ring.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A regular local ring remains regular after localization at every prime. Conversely use regularity at the unique maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 0AFS · localizations of regular local rings
theorems.name: Regular ring ∧ Local ring ⇔ Regular local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The associated graded ring of the maximal ideal is polynomial over the residue field, and the maximal ideal filtration is separated.
refs: Stacks 00NP · regular local rings are domains
theorems.name: Regular local ring ⇒ Integral domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In a Noetherian local ring the maximal ideal has finitely many generators, whose number bounds Krull dimension.
refs: Stacks 00KQ · dimension of a Noetherian local ring
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Local ring ⇒ Finite Krull dimension

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Apply the theorem that a regular local ring is factorial.
refs: Stacks 0AG0 · regular local rings are UFDs
theorems.name: Regular local ring ⇒ Unique factorization domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Regularity implies Serre (R₁), and the Cohen–Macaulay local rings imply (S₂). Apply the normality criterion.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Normal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In the Noetherian setting finite global dimension is equivalent to finite-dimensional regularity.
refs: Stacks 00OE · finite global dimension and finite dimensional regularity
theorems.name: Regular ring ∧ Finite Krull dimension ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Finite global dimension

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Each prime localization is regular local and its self-module in degree zero is a dualizing complex.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Gorenstein ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The completion is regular local and is its own quotient by the empty regular sequence.
theorems.name: Regular local ring ⇒ Complete intersection local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Every prime localization is regular local, so each is a complete intersection.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Local complete intersection ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Apply the definition at the maximal ideal. Conversely the complete-intersection property localizes to every prime.
refs: Stacks 09Q3 · local and global complete intersection conditions
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Local complete intersection ring ⇔ Complete intersection local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A regular local ring is Gorenstein. A quotient by a regular sequence remains Gorenstein. Apply flat local descent along the completion map.
refs: Stacks 0AWX · regular local rings are Gorenstein
theorems.name: Complete intersection local ring ⇒ Gorenstein local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Each prime localization is complete intersection and hence Gorenstein, by ascent along a regular-sequence quotient and descent from completion.
theorems.name: Local complete intersection ring ⇒ Gorenstein ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A Noetherian ring is Gorenstein of finite dimension exactly when it has finite injective dimension over itself.
refs: Stacks 0HB2 · finite injective dimension and Gorenstein rings
theorems.name: Gorenstein ring ∧ Finite Krull dimension ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Finite injective dimension over itself

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The local direction uses the unique maximal prime. The converse follows by localization of a dualizing complex.
refs: Stacks 0DW7 · global and local Gorenstein definitions
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Gorenstein ring ⇔ Gorenstein local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The dualizing complex of a Gorenstein local ring is concentrated in one degree, yielding the Cohen–Macaulay property.
theorems.name: Gorenstein ring ⇒ Cohen–Macaulay ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Localize a Cohen–Macaulay local ring at each prime for the global condition. The other direction uses the maximal ideal.
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇔ Cohen–Macaulay local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Polynomial algebras over the ring are Cohen–Macaulay and hence catenary. Catenarity descends to their quotients.
refs: Stacks 00NM · Cohen–Macaulay rings are universally catenary
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇒ Universally catenary ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Hensel lifting converges in the maximal ideal adic topology.
refs: Stacks 04GM · complete local rings are henselian
theorems.name: Complete local ring ⇒ Henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The maximal ideal is finitely generated if the ring is Noetherian. Conversely apply the Noetherianity criterion for complete local rings.
refs: Stacks 032B · finite maximal ideal in a complete local ring
theorems.name: Complete local ring ∧ Local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal ⇔ Complete local ring ∧ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The predicate specifies a unique maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 032B · finite maximal ideal in a complete local ring
theorems.name: Local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The definition requires a complete DVR with the stated uniformizer.
theorems.name: Cohen ring ⇒ Complete local ring ∧ Discrete valuation ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The henselian condition is imposed on a local ring.
refs: Stacks 04GF · henselian and strictly henselian local rings
theorems.name: Henselian local ring ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Finite algebras over the ring have only finitely many primes, all maximal. Their local-product decomposition is the finite-algebra criterion for henselianity.
refs: Stacks 06RS · dimension-zero local rings are henselian
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Krull dimension at most zero ⇒ Henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The maximal ideal is the Jacobson radical, which is nilpotent in an Artinian ring. The system of quotients by its powers is eventually constant.
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Artinian ring ⇒ Complete local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: This is the definition of strictly henselian.
refs: Stacks 04GF · henselian and strictly henselian local rings
theorems.name: Henselian local ring ∧ Separably closed residue field ⇔ Strictly henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The residue-field predicate is specified for the unique maximal ideal of a local ring.
theorems.name: Separably closed residue field ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A normal local ring is a normal domain. Its normalization is itself, and its residue field extension is the identity.
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Normal ring ⇒ Geometrically unibranch local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Geometric unibranchness adds a purely inseparable residue-field condition to unibranchness.
refs: Stacks 0BPZ · unibranch and geometrically unibranch local rings
theorems.name: Geometrically unibranch local ring ⇒ Unibranch local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Locality and a domain reduction are two of the defining conditions.
theorems.name: Unibranch local ring ⇒ Local ring ∧ Reduction is a domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The height-zero primes are included among primes of height at most one.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₁) ⇒ Serre condition (R₀)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The minimum of two and the local dimension is at least the minimum of one and that dimension.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₂) ⇒ Serre condition (S₁)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The stated Serre predicate includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₀) ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The stated Serre predicate includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₁) ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The regular ring condition covers every prime, including all primes of height at most one.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Serre condition (R₁)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Depth equal to dimension satisfies every finite Serre depth bound.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇒ Serre condition (S₂)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Use the associated-prime criterion for Serre (S₁) over a Noetherian ring.
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₁) ⇔ No embedded associated primes

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The two Serre conditions and the reducedness criterion are stated for Noetherian rings. The Noetherian premise appears explicitly on the reduced side.
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₀) ∧ Serre condition (S₁) ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Reduced ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Serre’s normality criterion applies to a Noetherian ring. The Noetherian premise appears explicitly on the normal side.
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₁) ∧ Serre condition (S₂) ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Normal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In dimension at most one the (R₁) condition covers every prime. For the converse, a regular ring is Noetherian and normal.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Normal ring ∧ Krull dimension at most one ⇔ Regular ring ∧ Krull dimension at most one

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The ring is a finite type algebra over itself.
theorems.name: Condition J-2 ⇒ Condition J-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The predicate is defined for Noetherian rings and its regular locus contains a prime.
theorems.name: Condition J-0 ⇒ Noetherian ring ∧ Nonzero ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The regular-locus predicate here uses the Noetherian setting.
theorems.name: Condition J-1 ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The definition of a G-ring includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
theorems.name: G-ring ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The entire prime spectrum is the regular locus.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Condition J-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The entire spectrum is regular and is nonempty for a nonzero ring.
theorems.name: Regular ring ∧ Nonzero ring ⇒ Condition J-0

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The three hypotheses are the defining conditions of quasi-excellence.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ G-ring ∧ Condition J-2 ⇔ Quasi-excellent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The two hypotheses are the defining conditions of excellence.
theorems.name: Quasi-excellent ring ∧ Universally catenary ring ⇔ Excellent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Apply the finiteness theorem for normalization over quasi-excellent rings.
theorems.name: Quasi-excellent ring ⇒ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A Noetherian universally Japanese ring is Nagata by the definitions, and the converse is the Nagata theorem.
refs: Stacks 0334 · Nagata rings are universally Japanese
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Universally Japanese ring ⇔ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The theorem on complete local Noetherian rings gives the requisite finiteness for every prime quotient and finite field extension.
refs: Stacks 032W · complete local Noetherian rings are Nagata
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Complete local ring ⇒ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Complete local Noetherian rings are among the standard classes of excellent rings.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Complete local ring ⇒ Excellent ring

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The presentation includes a surjection from a finite free module.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Definition 12.2 (the finite set of module generators in a presentation)
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Finite generators and relations are exactly the condition that the represented Hom functor preserve filtered colimits.
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ⇔ Maps from the module commute with filtered colimits

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A lift against a surjective map can be chosen on each basis vector.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, §12, following Definition 12.1 (arbitrary direct sums of copies of the ring)
theorems.name: Free module ⇒ Projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensoring with a free module gives a direct sum of copies of the input. Direct sums preserve exact sequences.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Example 11.3 (arbitrary free modules)
theorems.name: Free module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: If the base ring is nonzero, an infinite free basis cannot be generated by finitely many vectors with finite support. Over the zero ring the module is zero and admits the empty basis.
theorems.name: Finite module ∧ Free module ⇔ Finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A surjection from a free module onto a projective module splits, and a summand of a projective module is projective.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, §12, following Definition 12.1 (free summands of arbitrary rank characterize projectives)
theorems.name: Projective module ⇔ Direct summand of a free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The first Ext group vanishes for projective modules, and its vanishing against every module splits any short exact sequence ending in the module.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇔ Module with vanishing first Ext out of it

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Projectivity implies flatness by the characterization. Equivalently, a direct summand of a flat module is flat.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Theorem 12.6, proof of (a) ⇒ (d), using Example 11.3 for arbitrary direct summands
theorems.name: Projective module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: This is the finite-generation and projectivity condition together.
theorems.name: Finite module ∧ Projective module ⇔ Finite projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The finite-projective-module theorem identifies these two conditions.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Theorem 12.6(a),(d) (finite projectivity and flat finite presentation)
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ∧ Flat module ⇔ Finite projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Projectivity splits a finite free surjection, and a summand of a finite free module is finite projective.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, §12, immediately before Theorem 12.6 (summands of finite free modules)
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇔ Direct summand of a finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective module is finite locally free. Conversely, finite local freeness gives finite presentation and flatness.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Theorem 12.6(a),(c) (finite free trivializations on a principal open cover)
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇔ Finite locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use the same principal open covering and forget the fixed value of the rank.
theorems.name: Finite locally free module of a prescribed rank ⇒ Finite locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use the same principal open covering and forget the finiteness of the rank.
theorems.name: Finite locally free module ⇒ Locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Each localization at a maximal ideal is free, hence flat.
theorems.name: Locally free module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Lift a basis of the residue fibre. Nakayama gives a surjection, and flatness makes the lifted family a basis.
theorems.name: Module over a local ring ∧ Finite module ∧ Flat module ⇒ Finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Kaplansky’s theorem applies without finite-generation assumptions.
theorems.name: Module over a local ring ∧ Projective module ⇒ Free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The kernel of a finite free presentation is a submodule of a finite module over a Noetherian ring, hence finite.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Every submodule is finite. This is equivalent to the ascending chain condition.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Noetherian module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A module with the ascending chain condition has a maximal finitely generated submodule, which must be the whole module.
theorems.name: Noetherian module ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The module is a finite submodule of itself.
theorems.name: Coherent module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Every finite submodule is finitely presented over a Noetherian base.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Coherent module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The finite-ideal criterion for flatness is valid over any ring.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Tensor injectivity for finite ideals

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The ideal criterion for flatness is valid over any ring.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Tensor injectivity for all ideals

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Flatness gives vanishing of the derived functors of tensor. Conversely, the Tor exact sequence gives the injectivity of tensoring any inclusion.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Module with vanishing first Tor against every module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensor kernels are detected after localizing at maximal ideals.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Corollary 11.16 (testing at every maximal ideal)
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Flatness at every maximal ideal

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The fibre criterion for a flat module detects faithful flatness.
theorems.name: Flat module ∧ Nonzero fibres at all maximal ideals ⇔ Faithfully flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The support of a finite module is the vanishing set of its annihilator.
theorems.name: Finite module ⇒ Module with closed support

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use a prime filtration and the inclusion of the associated primes of an extension in the union of those of its terms.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Module with finitely many associated primes

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A simple module has the composition series consisting of a single factor.
theorems.name: Simple module ⇒ Module of finite length

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Lift finitely many generators of the quotient at each stage of the composition series.
theorems.name: Module of finite length ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Strict inclusions increase length, which is bounded by the length of the module.
theorems.name: Module of finite length ⇒ Noetherian module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensor multiplication by a nonzero scalar on the domain with the flat module.
theorems.name: Module over a domain ∧ Flat module ⇒ Torsion-free module over a domain

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Being a domain is part of the convention for valuation rings.
theorems.name: Module over a valuation ring ⇒ Module over a domain

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Over a valuation ring, the finite-ideal criterion reduces to injectivity of multiplication by nonzero scalars.
theorems.name: Module over a valuation ring ∧ Torsion-free module over a domain ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The characterization of projectivity yields both conditions.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇒ Mittag-Leffler module ∧ Sum of countably generated modules

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: All three conditions are hypotheses of the projectivity characterization.
theorems.name: Flat module ∧ Mittag-Leffler module ∧ Sum of countably generated modules ⇒ Projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective resolution is a finite projective-dimension witness. Its first two terms are finitely presented, so their cokernel is finitely presented.
theorems.name: Perfect module ⇒ Finitely presented module ∧ Module of finite projective dimension

theorems.subject: module
