theorems.proof: A finite projective resolution computes derived tensor and is bounded.
theorems.name: Module of finite projective dimension ⇒ Module of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The specified interval is one of the bounded intervals permitted in the definition.
theorems.name: Module of Tor dimension at most d ⇒ Module of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Apply the perfect complex criterion to the module placed in degree zero.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent module ∧ Module of finite Tor dimension ⇔ Perfect module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective module is its own resolution in degree zero.
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇒ Perfect module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A bounded complex of finite projective modules is pseudo-coherent. Apply this to a finite projective resolution.
theorems.name: Perfect module ⇒ Pseudo-coherent module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A pseudo-coherent module has a resolution by finite free modules. The first two terms give a finite presentation.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Successive syzygies over a Noetherian ring are finitely generated.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ⇒ Pseudo-coherent module

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A generator is a finite generating family.
theorems.name: Principal ideal ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient by a maximal ideal is a field, hence a domain.
theorems.name: Maximal ideal ⇒ Prime ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A domain has no nonzero nilpotent elements.
theorems.name: Prime ideal ⇒ Radical ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A single exponent killing the ideal also kills every element.
theorems.name: Nilpotent ideal ⇒ Locally nilpotent ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: If generators $x_i$ satisfy $x_i^{n_i}=0$, every monomial of total degree greater than the sum of the $n_i-1$ contains one of those powers.
theorems.name: Locally nilpotent ideal ∧ Finitely generated ideal ⇒ Nilpotent ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Every ideal in a Noetherian ring is finitely generated.
theorems.name: Ideal in a Noetherian ring ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient flatness criterion identifies these conditions.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal satisfying the intersection-product test

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient flatness criterion also gives the condition on individual elements.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal with local unit for each element

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The condition can also be imposed simultaneously on each finite family.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal with a common unit for each finite subset

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Apply the common-unit condition to a generating family. The chosen element is idempotent and generates the ideal.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ∧ Finitely generated ideal ⇔ Ideal generated by an idempotent

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: An idempotent splits the quotient map. Conversely, any section of the quotient splits the ambient module into ideals generated by complementary idempotents.
theorems.name: Ideal generated by an idempotent ⇔ Ideal with projective quotient

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: On every neighbourhood where regular generators exist, the Koszul complex is a resolution.
theorems.name: Regular ideal ⇒ Koszul-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The same generators satisfy the required vanishing in degree one on each neighbourhood.
theorems.name: Koszul-regular ideal ⇒ H₁-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The sequence implication from first Koszul homology to quasi-regularity applies on the same neighbourhoods.
theorems.name: H₁-regular ideal ⇒ Quasi-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Quasi-regular generators locally on the vanishing set, together with the unit generator on its complement, yield finite generation.
theorems.name: Quasi-regular ideal ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The degree-one graded piece is free on each principal neighbourhood from the definition. The conormal module is finite locally free over the quotient.
theorems.name: Quasi-regular ideal ⇒ Ideal with finite projective conormal module

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite presentation supplies a finite generating family of the algebra.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ⇒ Ring map of finite type

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite set of module generators also generates the target as an algebra.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite type

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite module presentation gives finite generation and a finite algebra presentation. Conversely, for a finite and finitely presented ring map apply the module restriction theorem to its target, a free module of rank one over itself.
theorems.name: Ring map with finitely presented target module ⇔ Finite ring map ∧ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite free module has a finite presentation and its tensor functor is exact.
theorems.name: Ring map with finite free target module ⇒ Ring map with finitely presented target module ∧ Flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The determinant trick yields a monic equation for each element of the target.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Integral ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Reduce powers of each finite algebra generator using its monic equation. Products of bounded powers then generate the target as a module.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ∧ Ring map of finite type ⇔ Finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Apply lying over to the inclusion of the source as a subring of the target.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ∧ Injective ring map ⇒ Ring map surjective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Quotient by the chosen prime over the smaller prime and apply lying over.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ⇒ Going up for prime ideals

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The fibre is integral over a field. Every prime in such an algebra is maximal.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ⇒ Incomparability of distinct primes in each fibre

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, so the kernel of its map onto the target is finitely generated.
theorems.name: Ring map with Noetherian source ∧ Ring map of finite type ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Apply the finite-presentation theorem for flat algebras of finite type over a valuation ring.
theorems.name: Ring map with valuation-ring source ∧ Flat ring map ∧ Ring map of finite type ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Being a field is part of the definition.
theorems.name: Algebra over a perfect field ⇒ Algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The geometric reducedness theorem over a perfect field supplies the assertion for all field extensions.
theorems.name: Algebra over a perfect field ∧ Ring map with reduced target ⇒ Geometrically reduced algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Use the trivial field extension to test the target.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced algebra over a field ⇒ Algebra over a field ∧ Ring map with reduced target

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Over each extension the ring is a domain exactly when it is reduced with a nonempty irreducible spectrum.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced algebra over a field ∧ Geometrically irreducible algebra over a field ⇔ Geometrically integral algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A nonempty irreducible space is connected. Apply this after every field extension.
theorems.name: Geometrically irreducible algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically connected algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Normality of a ring implies reducedness. Apply this after every field extension.
theorems.name: Geometrically normal algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically reduced algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Regular rings are normal. Test geometric normality after finitely generated field extensions by the equivalent criterion.
theorems.name: Geometrically regular Noetherian algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically normal algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: For a flat map, surjectivity on spectra is equivalent to faithful flatness.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Propositions 11.18–11.19 (surjectivity on spectra for a flat map)
theorems.name: Flat ring map ∧ Ring map surjective on spectra ⇔ Faithfully flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The spectrum-surjectivity criterion is preserved by every base change.
theorems.name: Ring map surjective on spectra ⇔ Ring map universally surjective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A faithfully flat map is universally injective as a module map. In particular, tensoring with the base ring shows ordinary injectivity.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Corollary 11.12 (injectivity and the equalizer for a faithfully flat map)
theorems.name: Faithfully flat ring map ⇒ Injective ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Localize at the given target prime. The induced flat local map is faithfully flat, hence has a surjective map on spectra.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Proposition 11.20 (lifting a specialization downwards along a flat homomorphism)
theorems.name: Flat ring map ⇒ Going down for prime ideals

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The faithfully flat equalizer criterion shows such an epimorphism is an isomorphism.
theorems.name: Faithfully flat ring map ∧ Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Ring isomorphism

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite epimorphism is surjective, and a quotient ring is generated by the image of the unit as a module.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ∧ Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Surjective ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The pushout of the two copies of the map is the tensor product of the target algebra with itself.
theorems.name: Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Tensor multiplication is an isomorphism

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A ring epimorphism has at most one prime over each source prime.
theorems.name: Epimorphism of rings ⇒ Ring map injective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A quotient ring is of finite type and has zero relative differentials.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map ⇒ Unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finitely many generators of the kernel give a finite presentation, and relative differentials of a quotient vanish. Conversely a G-unramified map is finitely presented. For a surjection, the polynomial presentation in zero variables then has finitely generated kernel.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map with finitely generated kernel ⇔ Surjective ring map ∧ G-unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Localization is an exact tensor functor.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Proposition 11.14 (flatness at an arbitrary multiplicative subset)
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: An element invertible modulo a nilpotent ideal already is invertible, and the universal property of localization gives the unique lift.
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Formally étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A map from a localization is uniquely determined by its restriction to the original ring.
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Epimorphism of rings

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A principal localization has a finite presentation and is étale by the stated permanence result.
theorems.name: Principal localization map ⇒ Localization map ∧ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finitely presented flat quotient has an idempotent-generated kernel. Conversely a localization at an idempotent is a quotient with a single relation and is flat.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map ∧ Flat ring map ∧ Ring map of finite presentation ⇔ Localization at an idempotent

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: An idempotent is one element, so its localization is principal.
theorems.name: Localization at an idempotent ⇒ Principal localization map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finite generators and relations detect factorization and equality at a finite stage of a directed system.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ⇔ Maps from the algebra commute with directed colimits

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Tensor a finite generating family with the residue field.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Ring map with finite-dimensional fibre algebras

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The finite-dimensional fibre criterion for a finite type map.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite type ∧ Ring map with finite-dimensional fibre algebras ⇔ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The unramified-at-a-prime criterion yields quasi-finiteness at every target prime.
theorems.name: Unramified ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The invertible Jacobian minor gives the splitting of the presentation defining the naive cotangent complex.
theorems.name: Standard smooth ring map ⇒ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Use the invertibility of the derivative and the Jacobian criterion for the localized one-variable presentation.
theorems.name: Standard étale ring map ⇒ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The naive cotangent complex is concentrated in degrees zero and one. The two homology conditions are the smoothness criterion.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Ring map with vanishing first naive cotangent homology ∧ Ring map with finite projective differentials ⇔ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The standard smooth presentation locally on the target is syntomic.
theorems.name: Smooth ring map ⇒ Syntomic ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A Koszul-regular ideal is quasi-regular, hence finitely generated. Thus a finite polynomial presentation of a local complete intersection map is finitely presented.
theorems.name: Local complete intersection ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The flat local-complete-intersection criterion is equivalent to the fibre definition.
theorems.name: Flat ring map ∧ Local complete intersection ring map ⇔ Syntomic ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finite presentation occurs in the definition of a syntomic map.
theorems.name: Syntomic ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The naive cotangent complex is quasi-isomorphic to zero precisely when both its homology modules vanish.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Ring map with vanishing first naive cotangent homology ∧ Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The zero module is finite projective. An étale map meets the smoothness criterion with zero differentials.
theorems.name: Étale ring map ⇒ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The criterion requires both flatness and G-unramifiedness, hence finite presentation.
theorems.name: Flat ring map ∧ G-unramified ring map ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Étale maps are quasi-finite.
theorems.name: Étale ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The condition is the conjunction of finiteness and étaleness.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ∧ Étale ring map ⇔ Finite étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: These are the two conditions defining unramifiedness.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite type ∧ Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: G-unramifiedness uses finite presentation together with vanishing relative differentials.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ G-unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: For a square-zero extension, the difference of two lifts is a derivation and conversely one may add any derivation to a lift.
theorems.name: Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Formally unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The finite presentation hypothesis is part of the equivalence between smoothness and formal smoothness.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Formally smooth ring map ⇔ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Existence and uniqueness of square-zero lifts are exactly the two lifting conditions together.
theorems.name: Formally smooth ring map ∧ Formally unramified ring map ⇔ Formally étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The formal lifting criterion for étaleness requires finite presentation.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ∧ Formally étale ring map ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: On a principal neighbourhood where the map is étale, it is smooth.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇒ Smooth at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: An étale presentation on the neighbourhood is G-unramified.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇒ G-unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Every étale map near the chosen point is standard étale after further principal localization. The converse follows from standard étale implying étale.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇔ Standard étale on a principal neighbourhood

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Intersect the two principal neighbourhoods. Vanishing of differentials localizes, and localizing a finitely presented algebra at one element preserves finite presentation.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime ∧ Finite presentation near a target prime ⇔ G-unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Unramifiedness at the chosen prime gives both residue conditions.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime ⇒ Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime ∧ Finite separable residue extension at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: The smooth neighbourhood is flat of finite presentation, and flatness passes to the induced map on local rings.
theorems.name: Smooth at a target prime ⇒ Flatness at a target prime ∧ Finite presentation near a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: These hypotheses give smoothness by the fibre criterion. Conversely, a smooth neighbourhood is flat and finitely presented, and its base change to the residue field is smooth.
theorems.name: Finite presentation near a target prime ∧ Flatness at a target prime ∧ Smooth fibre at a target prime ⇔ Smooth at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: First restrict to the finitely presented principal neighbourhood, then use the flatness and residue conditions there. Conversely, an étale neighbourhood supplies finite presentation, flatness, and the stated residue conditions.
theorems.name: Finite presentation near a target prime ∧ Flatness at a target prime ∧ Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime ∧ Finite separable residue extension at a target prime ⇔ Étale at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: The finite-type hypothesis allows the quasi-finiteness criterion for the fibre at the chosen prime.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime ∧ Chosen point of a finite type ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: For a finite-type map, the condition on the maximal ideal and separability of the residue extension give unramifiedness at the chosen point.
theorems.name: Chosen point of a finite type ring map ∧ Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime ∧ Finite separable residue extension at a target prime ⇒ Unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.proof: A finite Tor-amplitude bound lets one truncate the pseudo-coherent resolution to a bounded complex of finite projective modules.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent complex ∧ Complex of finite Tor dimension ⇔ Perfect complex

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.proof: The specified interval provides the required bound.
theorems.name: Complex with Tor-amplitude in a given interval ⇒ Complex of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A characteristic-zero field contains the infinite prime subfield $\mathbf Q$.
theorems.name: Finite field ⇒ Positive characteristic

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A number field is a finite extension of $\mathbf Q$, so its characteristic is zero.
theorems.name: Number field ⇒ Characteristic zero

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: The characteristic-zero case of the criterion for a perfect field.
refs: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10, Definition 2.23 and Proposition 2.24
theorems.name: Characteristic zero ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: The positive-characteristic case of the criterion for a perfect field.
refs: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10, Definition 2.23 and Proposition 2.24 in characteristic p
theorems.name: Positive characteristic with surjective Frobenius ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A finite field has positive characteristic. Frobenius is injective on a field and thus surjective on the finite underlying set.
refs: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10, Example 2.25(a), surjectivity of Frobenius by finiteness
theorems.name: Finite field ⇒ Positive characteristic with surjective Frobenius

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Every separable algebraic extension is algebraic and hence trivial.
theorems.name: Algebraically closed field ⇒ Separably closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: In positive characteristic, a root of $X^p-a$ lies in an algebraically closed field, for every element $a$. In characteristic zero every field is perfect.
refs: Stacks 09GR · polynomial criterion for algebraic closedness
theorems.name: Algebraically closed field ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Over a perfect field, every algebraic extension is separable. If the field is also separably closed, each algebraic extension is therefore trivial. An algebraically closed field is perfect and separably closed.
theorems.name: Perfect field ∧ Separably closed field ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Apply the minimal polynomial criterion to algebraic elements.
theorems.name: Every irreducible polynomial is linear ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: An irreducible polynomial with a root is linear, and algebraic closedness ensures every nonconstant polynomial has a root.
theorems.name: Every nonconstant polynomial has a root ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Factor a polynomial into irreducibles. Splitting implies that every irreducible is linear.
theorems.name: Every nonconstant polynomial splits ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field-polynomial-pair
theorems.proof: A nonconstant common irreducible factor gives a common root in an algebraic closure. A Bézout identity precludes a common root.
theorems.name: No common root in an algebraic closure ⇔ Relatively prime polynomials

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.proof: For an irreducible polynomial the derivative is relatively prime to the polynomial whenever it is nonzero, since it has smaller degree.
refs: Stacks 09H1 · definition of separable irreducible polynomial
theorems.name: Irreducible polynomial ∧ Nonzero formal derivative ⇔ Separable irreducible polynomial

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.proof: A repeated root in an algebraic closure is precisely a common root of the polynomial and its derivative.
theorems.name: Irreducible polynomial ∧ Only simple roots in an algebraic closure ⇔ Separable irreducible polynomial

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.proof: The separability condition is imposed on the minimal polynomial of an algebraic element.
refs: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10, §5, the algebraicity hypothesis of the separability definition preceding Theorem 5.1
theorems.name: Separable algebraic element ⇒ Algebraic element

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.proof: In characteristic $p>0$, $a$ is a root of $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}\in F[X]$. An element of the base field is algebraic in any characteristic.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable element ⇒ Algebraic element

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A single generator gives a finite generating set.
theorems.name: Simple field extension ⇒ Finitely generated field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Every finite set is at most countable.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension ⇒ Countably generated field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Adjoin a finite algebraic generating set successively and multiply its finite degrees. Conversely a finite extension is algebraic, and a finite vector space basis generates the field.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension ∧ Finitely generated field extension ⇔ Finite field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For an element $a$, the simple extension $F(a)$ is finite exactly when $a$ is algebraic over $F$.
theorems.name: Every simple subextension is finite ⇔ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: These are precisely the two defining conditions on $E/F$.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension ∧ Algebraically closed target field ⇔ Algebraic closure

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The adjective is used for an algebraic extension whose elements are separable.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Apply the polynomial $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}$ to each element in positive characteristic, with equality handled in any characteristic.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Once the base has positive characteristic, the general and review definitions of pure inseparability agree.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension ∧ Base field of positive characteristic ⇔ Purely inseparable extension in positive characteristic

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For $a^{p^r}\in F$, the polynomial $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}=(X-a)^{p^r}$ over $E$ is divisible by the minimal polynomial of $a$, which therefore splits over $E$.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension ⇒ Normal field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each minimal polynomial of an element of a separable purely inseparable extension has only one distinct root and is separable, hence has degree one. A trivial extension satisfies both conditions.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension ∧ Purely inseparable extension ⇔ Trivial extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: All elements of an algebraic extension lie in its relative algebraic closure; if this is the base field the extension is trivial.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension ∧ Base field algebraically closed in the target ⇔ Trivial extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The empty set is a transcendence basis of an algebraic extension.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A separably generated extension is separable in the general sense of Stacks 030O.
theorems.name: Separably generated extension ⇒ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Take the independent generators as transcendence basis. The resulting algebraic extension is trivial and hence separable.
theorems.name: Purely transcendental extension ⇒ Separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a simple subextension generated by an algebraic element, a transcendence basis is empty, so the general criterion forces this element to be separable.
theorems.name: Separable field extension ∧ Algebraic field extension ⇔ Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a finitely generated separable extension, apply the definition of general separability to the whole extension.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension ∧ Separable field extension ⇔ Finitely generated and separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The named condition is a conjunction of the two separately defined predicates.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension ∧ Separably generated extension ⇔ Finitely generated and separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Geometric reducedness characterizes separability of a field extension in either characteristic.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced field extension ⇔ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness is equivalent to the general notion of separability for field extensions.
theorems.name: Formally smooth field extension ⇔ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each separable minimal polynomial has invertible derivative at its root, forcing the differential of that root to vanish.
theorems.name: Finite field extension ∧ Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Vanishing relative differentials

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The finite-generation hypothesis is part of the criterion.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension ∧ Vanishing relative differentials ⇒ Finite field extension ∧ Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A nonconstant polynomial in characteristic zero has nonzero derivative. Apply the criterion to the minimal polynomial of each element.
theorems.name: Base field of characteristic zero ∧ Algebraic field extension ⇒ Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a finite extension the number of embeddings into an algebraic closure is at most the degree, with equality precisely in the separable case.
theorems.name: Finite field extension ∧ Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Finite extension with the maximal number of embeddings

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The primitive element theorem applies to finite separable extensions.
refs: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10, Theorem 5.1, the finite separable case
theorems.name: Finite field extension ∧ Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each intermediate field is generated over the base by the coefficients of the minimal polynomial of the primitive element over that intermediate field. This polynomial must be one of the finitely many monic factors over the target.
refs: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10, Proposition 5.3, simple algebraic extensions
theorems.name: Finite field extension ∧ Simple field extension ⇒ Finitely many intermediate fields

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Over an infinite base, finitely many proper intermediate fields cannot cover the target vector space. For a finite base the target is a finite field with cyclic multiplicative group.
refs: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10, Remark 5.4, finite extensions with finitely many intermediate fields
theorems.name: Finite field extension ∧ Finitely many intermediate fields ⇒ Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The Stacks definition of normal extension starts with an algebraic extension.
theorems.name: Normal field extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The image under an embedding contains every conjugate of every one of its elements precisely in the normal case.
theorems.name: Algebraic extension with a common image for all embeddings ⇔ Normal field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The automorphism group embeds into the set of embeddings into an algebraic closure, and normality means every such embedding has image the target field.
theorems.name: Finite field extension ∧ Normal field extension ⇔ Finite extension with as many automorphisms as its separable degree

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Both properties require algebraicity, and together they are the definition of a Galois extension.
theorems.name: Normal field extension ∧ Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The number of automorphisms is bounded by the separable degree, which in turn is bounded by the degree. Both equalities hold exactly for a finite Galois extension.
theorems.name: Finite field extension ∧ Galois extension ⇔ Finite extension with as many automorphisms as its degree

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The cyclicity condition is imposed on a finite Galois extension.
theorems.name: Finite cyclic Galois extension ⇒ Finite field extension ∧ Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a separable extension the sum of its distinct embeddings is nonzero by independence of characters. In a finite inseparable extension the trace is zero.
theorems.name: Finite field extension ∧ Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Finite extension with nonzero trace map

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: If the trace map is nonzero, choose $c$ of nonzero trace. Each nonzero $a$ pairs nontrivially with $a^{-1}c$. A zero trace map gives the zero pairing on the nonzero vector space.
theorems.name: Finite extension with nonzero trace map ⇔ Finite extension with nondegenerate trace pairing

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The matrix in a basis represents the linear map from the vector space to its dual. It is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero.
theorems.name: Finite extension with nondegenerate trace pairing ⇔ Finite extension with nonzero discriminant

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.proof: These are the two defining conditions on the family.
theorems.name: Algebraically independent family ∧ Target algebraic over the field generated by the family ⇔ Transcendence basis

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The empty family is algebraically independent and generates the base field. It is a transcendence basis precisely if the target is algebraic.
theorems.name: Transcendence degree zero ⇔ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A subfield of a finite field is finite, and a generator of the cyclic group of units of the target generates the extension.
refs: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10, Proposition 4.19 and its proof by a generator of the target multiplicative group
theorems.name: Finite target field ⇒ Finite base field ∧ Finite field extension ∧ Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Write $q=|F|$ and $[E:F]=n$. Every element of $E$ is a root of $X^{q^n}-X$, so $E$ is its splitting field, and the derivative is $-1$. The $q$-power Frobenius fixes $F$ and has order $n$: if its $i$th power were the identity for $0<i<n$, the degree-$q^i$ polynomial $X^{q^i}-X$ would have $q^n$ roots. The Galois group has order $n$, so this element generates it.
theorems.name: Finite target field ⇒ Finite cyclic Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A finite-dimensional vector space over a finite field has finitely many elements.
theorems.name: Finite base field ∧ Finite field extension ⇒ Finite target field

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The rational function field on an empty set of indeterminates is the base field.
theorems.name: Trivial extension ⇒ Purely transcendental extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A rational function involves only finitely many independent variables. In one variable any nonconstant rational function makes that variable algebraic over the subfield it generates. Induct on the number of variables by treating the last one over the rational function field on the others.
theorems.name: Purely transcendental extension ⇒ Base field algebraically closed in the target

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.proof: Every tensor has a representation using an $F$-linearly independent tuple on the $E$ side. Such tensors map to nonzero elements when any coefficient on the $L$ side is nonzero, precisely by preservation of independence.
theorems.name: Linear independence preserved in the compositum ⇔ Linearly disjoint subfields

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The two defining conditions of a henselian pair
theorems.proof: Both conditions are part of the definition. Neither individual condition is used by itself in this equivalence.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A locally nilpotent ideal gives a henselian pair
theorems.proof: Locally nilpotent thickenings have equivalent étale algebra categories and satisfy the henselian lifting criterion.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: An adically complete pair is henselian
theorems.proof: Successive nilpotent quotients lift comaximal factorizations compatibly. Pass to the inverse limit using completeness.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Finite-algebra idempotent criterion
theorems.proof: The finite-algebra idempotent criterion in the numbered result is equivalent to the defining lifting property.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Integral-algebra idempotent criterion
theorems.proof: The numbered result allows arbitrary integral algebras. Every finite algebra is integral.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Étale section criterion
theorems.proof: This criterion uses all étale algebras over the specified base, with section lifting along the specified quotient.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Gabber root criterion
theorems.proof: The root condition is coupled with the Jacobson radical hypothesis. Under those hypotheses the root in the residue class of one is unique.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The finite-algebra criterion tests the base pair
theorems.proof: Use the finite A-algebra A itself.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: An essentially finitely presented map is essentially finite type
theorems.proof: A finitely presented algebra has finitely many generators as an algebra. The same localization witnesses the conclusion.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A finite type map is essentially finite type
theorems.proof: Use the localization at the multiplicative set consisting of the unit.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A finitely presented map is essentially finitely presented
theorems.proof: Use the localization at the multiplicative set consisting of the unit.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: A module-regular sequence is quasi-regular
theorems.proof: The initial classes of the sequence freely generate the associated graded module over the quotient in the prescribed polynomial-module sense.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: A ring-regular sequence is quasi-regular
theorems.proof: Apply the regular sequence comparison to the module given by the ring itself.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Complete normality implies normality for a domain
theorems.proof: Powers of an integral element lie in the finite module generated by the powers below the degree of a monic equation. A common denominator of those generators gives almost integrality.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A Noetherian normal domain is completely normal
theorems.proof: For almost integral $g$, the algebra $R[g]$ is an $R$-submodule of $r^{-1}R$ for some nonzero $r\in R$. Noetherianity makes $R[g]$ a finite $R$-module. Thus $g$ is integral over $R$ and belongs to $R$ by normality.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: The directed colimit zero test
theorems.proof: In the directed colimit, equality of representatives occurs after passing to a common later index. Apply this to the zero representative.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Split sequences stay exact under tensor product
theorems.proof: The maps in a split short exact sequence identify with the inclusion and projection of a direct sum, which tensor product preserves.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Universal exactness with finitely presented quotient implies splitting
theorems.proof: The lifting test for finitely presented modules, applied to the quotient itself, lifts its identity map to a section.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: A flat quotient gives universal exactness
theorems.proof: Tensoring the sequence with a module gives no kernel at the left because the first Tor of the flat quotient vanishes.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Universal exactness with flat middle term forces flat end terms
theorems.proof: Use the Tor sequence and the injectivity after tensoring. First the quotient is flat, then the kernel is flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A faithfully flat ring map is universally injective on underlying modules
theorems.proof: After tensoring the test map with $S$, the multiplication $S\otimes_R S\to S$ supplies a retraction. Faithful flatness detects injectivity.
refs: J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Proposition 11.11 (injectivity of the unit on every module)

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Surjective transition maps give a Mittag-Leffler inverse system
theorems.proof: Each transition image is already the whole target term.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The canonical tensor comparison is the characterization of the Mittag–Leffler property. It must be tested on arbitrary families.
theorems.name: Mittag-Leffler module ⇔ Injective comparison with products under tensor

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.proof: The kernel of the canonical map to the completion is the intersection of all powers of the ideal applied to the module.
theorems.name: Adically complete module ⇒ Adically separated module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring remains Cohen–Macaulay after localization at each prime.
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay module ⇒ Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: For a finite Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring, each associated prime is minimal in the support.
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay module ⇒ Module without embedded associated primes

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: For a finite module over a Noetherian ring, depth zero at a support prime detects an associated prime. The S₁ bound excludes depth zero precisely at the nonminimal support primes.
theorems.name: Serre condition S₁ for a module ⇔ Module over a Noetherian ring ∧ Finite module ∧ Module without embedded associated primes

theorems.subject: algebra-element-pair
theorems.proof: An associate generates the same ideal. Conversely cancel a nonzero generator of the same ideal in a domain. If the ideal is zero both generators are zero.
theorems.name: Associate elements in a domain ⇔ Elements generating the same principal ideal

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Take the principal open given by the element one.
theorems.name: Global complete intersection over a field ⇒ Local complete intersection over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: An R-derivation on S vanishes on the image of R. For a surjection R → S this image is all of S.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map ⇒ Ring map with vanishing differentials

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The integral closure of a normal domain in its fraction field is the ring itself, hence is a finite module.
theorems.name: Normal domain ⇒ Domain satisfying N-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The identity extension of the fraction field is finite.
theorems.name: Japanese domain (N-2) ⇒ Domain satisfying N-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: All finite field extensions of the fraction field are separable in characteristic zero. Finiteness over a Noetherian normal domain in a finite separable extension and transitivity of finite maps give the result after first taking the finite normalization.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring ∧ Domain of characteristic zero ∧ Domain satisfying N-1 ⇔ Noetherian ring ∧ Domain of characteristic zero ∧ Japanese domain (N-2)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The local ring injects into its completion by the Krull intersection theorem, so it is reduced when its completion is.
theorems.name: Analytically unramified local ring ⇒ Reduced ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Analytical unramifiedness gives finiteness of the normalization in the total ring of fractions, which is the fraction field in the domain case.
theorems.name: Analytically unramified local ring ∧ Integral domain ⇒ Domain satisfying N-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A Noetherian local Nagata domain is analytically unramified by the numbered criterion.
theorems.name: Local ring ∧ Noetherian ring ∧ Integral domain ∧ Nagata ring ⇒ Analytically unramified local ring

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Koszul-regularity on a module implies H₁-regularity
theorems.proof: Take degree one in the vanishing condition.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Koszul-regularity in a ring implies H₁-regularity
theorems.proof: Take degree one in the vanishing condition.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Stably free modules are projective
theorems.proof: The module is a direct summand of a free module.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Free modules are stably free
theorems.proof: In the definition of stable isomorphism take both added free summands to be zero.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Root test for absolute integral closure
theorems.proof: A splitting supplies a root. Conversely divide by a monic linear factor at a chosen root and induct on the degree.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: An auto-associated ring is local
theorems.proof: Locality is part of the definition.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Auto-associated rings give nonzero annihilators
theorems.proof: The weak association of the maximal ideal gives a nonzero element killed by any chosen finitely generated proper ideal.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Universal injectivity criterion for projective modules
theorems.proof: The numbered result proves equivalence of the annihilator and universal-injectivity conditions.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Splitting criterion for finite projectives
theorems.proof: The universal-injectivity criterion yields a finite flat cokernel in this situation. The numbered result proves the converse by testing finite free modules.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexive modules over a domain are torsion free
theorems.proof: The dual of a module over a domain embeds in a product of copies of the domain and is torsion free. Apply this to the double dual.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexivity at all primes
theorems.proof: Finite modules over a Noetherian ring are finitely presented. Dualization then commutes with localization and localizations detect isomorphisms.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexivity at all maximal ideals
theorems.proof: The same localized evaluation maps at maximal ideals suffice to detect whether the evaluation map is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexivity via a finite free embedding
theorems.proof: The finite-module criterion over a Noetherian domain identifies reflexivity with this particular finite free embedding.

theorems.subject: topological-ring
theorems.name: Linearly topologized rings are topological rings
theorems.proof: Here the linear topology is the one on the specified topological ring.

theorems.subject: topological-module
theorems.name: Linearly topologized modules are topological modules
theorems.proof: The submodule neighbourhood condition is imposed on the specified topological module.

theorems.subject: topological-ring
theorems.name: A pre-adic ring is pre-admissible
theorems.proof: The ideal of definition of a pre-adic topology witnesses pre-admissibility.

theorems.subject: topological-ring
theorems.name: A pre-admissible ring is linearly topologized
theorems.proof: The definition starts with a linearly topologized ring.

theorems.subject: topological-ring
theorems.name: Admissibility is pre-admissibility and completeness
theorems.proof: Use the completeness convention in the definition.

theorems.subject: topological-ring
theorems.name: Adic rings are complete pre-adic rings
theorems.proof: The adic condition couples the pre-adic basis and completeness.

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.name: A p-basis is p-independent
theorems.proof: The monomials defining a basis are linearly independent.

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.name: Differential test for p-independence
theorems.proof: The numbered result identifies both independence conditions.

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.name: Differential test for a p-basis
theorems.proof: The same criterion identifies p-bases with bases of relative differentials.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: First Ext criterion for ideal-projectivity
theorems.proof: Multiplication factors through a projective module exactly when its pullback of every extension class vanishes.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A pseudo-coherent ring map has finite type
theorems.proof: Finite type is an explicit part of the definition.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Perfect maps are pseudo-coherent with finite Tor dimension
theorems.proof: This is the source definition of a perfect ring map.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Polynomial presentation criterion for perfect ring maps
theorems.proof: Use the criterion for finite resolutions over a finite polynomial presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat maps of finite presentation are perfect
theorems.proof: The source proves relative pseudo-coherence, and flatness gives Tor dimension zero.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type maps of Noetherian rings are pseudo-coherent
theorems.proof: A finite polynomial algebra over the source is Noetherian. The target is a finite module over it, hence pseudo-coherent.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Local complete intersection maps are perfect
theorems.proof: The Koszul-regular presentation gives the finite projective resolution required by the perfect map criterion.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Weak étaleness means flatness and a flat diagonal
theorems.proof: The two flatness conditions are precisely the definition.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat diagonal implies formal unramifiedness
theorems.proof: If the multiplication quotient is flat, the kernel has vanishing conormal module. The conormal module identifies with the differentials.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type maps with flat diagonal are unramified
theorems.proof: Formal unramifiedness and finite type give unramifiedness.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Weakly étale maps of finite presentation are étale
theorems.proof: The source applies flatness, finite presentation and the vanishing of differentials.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étale maps are weakly étale
theorems.proof: The étale map and its multiplication map are flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localizations are weakly étale
theorems.proof: A localization is flat and its tensor-square multiplication map is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Ratliff criterion for a Noetherian local ring
theorems.proof: Formal catenarity requires Noetherian locality. The source identifies it with universal catenarity in that setting.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: An extension of DVRs is injective and local
theorems.proof: The two map conditions are part of the definition.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: An extension of DVRs is an extension of valuation rings
theorems.proof: Each DVR is a valuation ring and the map is injective and local.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Ramification index one means a value-group isomorphism for DVRs
theorems.proof: After identifying both value groups with the integers via their uniformizers, the induced map is multiplication by the ramification index.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Adic formal smoothness criterion for extensions of DVRs
theorems.proof: The numbered result identifies adic formal smoothness with both conditions together.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Unramified finite separable extensions are tame
theorems.proof: Ramification index one is prime to every positive residue characteristic, and the residue extensions are already separable.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: A solution to eliminating ramification is weak
theorems.proof: Apply the adic formal smoothness criterion to each specified extension of discrete valuation rings.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: A separable solution is a solution
theorems.proof: The separable condition is additional.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Invertible modules are precisely line bundles
theorems.proof: The numbered result identifies invertibility under tensor product with finite local freeness of rank one.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: An invertible module has a tensor inverse
theorems.proof: An inverse to the tensor equivalence sends the unit module to an inverse object. Conversely a tensor inverse gives an inverse functor.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A trivial invertible module is invertible and free of rank one
theorems.proof: It is isomorphic to the tensor unit.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: An elementary divisor domain is Bézout
theorems.proof: Apply the diagonal form to a row vector of generators of an ideal.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A Bézout domain is a domain with finitely generated ideals principal
theorems.proof: These are exactly the conditions in the definition.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A local Bézout domain is a valuation ring
theorems.proof: In a local domain the principal generator of an ideal generated by two elements forces one of those elements to divide the other.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Finite generators reduce equality of maps to finitely many equalities, all valid at one sufficiently late index. Conversely, use quotients by the finitely generated submodules of the given module. The identity becomes zero in their colimit, so injectivity forces the whole module to occur as one of those submodules.
theorems.name: Finite module ⇔ Maps out of a module inject into maps to a filtered colimit

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The determinantal form of Nakayama applied to $I=I^2$ gives $e\in I$ with $(1-e)I=0$. Thus $e^2=e$ and $I=eR$. Conversely $eR$ is finitely generated and $(eR)^2=eR$.
theorems.name: Finitely generated ideal ∧ Idempotent ideal ⇔ Ideal generated by an idempotent

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The closure of the image is $V(\ker(R\to S))$. Thus density is equivalent to containment of the kernel in the nilradical.
theorems.name: Ring map with a locally nilpotent kernel ⇔ Ring map inducing a dense spectral image

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Every prime contracts over the kernel, so meeting every minimal prime forces the kernel into their intersection, the nilradical. Conversely factor through the quotient by the kernel, whose spectrum identifies with the spectrum of $R$ for a nil kernel, and apply the minimal-prime lifting result for the resulting injection.
theorems.name: Ring map with a locally nilpotent kernel ⇔ Ring map reaching every minimal prime of the base

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Localizing an injection at the complement of a minimal prime gives an injection over a nonzero ring with unique prime. Any prime of the localized target contracts to that unique prime.
theorems.name: Injective ring map ⇒ Ring map reaching every minimal prime of the base

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Regular local rings are unique factorization domains
theorems.proof: The factoriality theorem for regular local rings applies to the given ring. Its proof establishes that every height-one prime is principal.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Principal cyclic summands and the principal-ideal lifting condition
theorems.proof: The equality condition is exactly the surjectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/fR,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/fR,C)$ for each $f$. It extends to sums and summands. Conversely, map the direct sum over all maps from principal cyclic modules to $P$ onto $P$. This surjection satisfies the equality condition, so the lifting property splits it.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Total divisibility is equivalent to linearly ordered ideals
theorems.proof: One direction follows by checking principal ideals. For the other, if ideals $I,J$ are incomparable, choose $a\in I\setminus J$ and $b\in J\setminus I$; neither divides the other.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A nonzero chain ring is local with principal finitely generated ideals
theorems.proof: If $(a,b)=(c)$ in a local ring, write $a=cu$, $b=cv$. For $c\neq0$, the identity $c=ra+sb$ implies $1-ru-sv$ cannot be a unit, so at least one of $u,v$ is a unit. Thus $a,b$ are comparable. Conversely, linearly ordered ideals give a unique maximal ideal and any finite family of principal ideals has a largest member.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Perfect objects are exactly the dualizable objects
theorems.proof: A bounded complex of finite projectives has a dual by termwise dualizing with the Koszul signs. Conversely, factoring coevaluation through finite free subcomplexes shows that a dualizable object is a direct summand of a perfect object.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensor-invertible derived objects are exactly the locally shifted lines
theorems.proof: Invertibility implies perfectness. Over each residue field, the tensor inverse condition leaves one one-dimensional cohomology group in some degree. A perfect representative then gives a shifted rank-one free module near the prime. Conversely the evaluation with the perfect dual is an isomorphism, checked on these opens.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: A tensor-invertible object is perfect
theorems.proof: A tensor inverse determines a dual, and dualizability in the derived category of modules implies perfectness.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: A finite locally free module of rank r is characterized by two Fitting ideals
theorems.proof: Localize at each prime. The unit $r$th Fitting ideal allows $r$ generators in the local ring. With such a presentation, the preceding Fitting ideal is generated by the entries in the relation matrix, so its vanishing forces the module to be free on the generators. The converse follows from the Fitting ideals of a free module.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: Two adjacent Fitting ideals determine the entire rank-r step pattern
theorems.proof: The Fitting ideals are increasing in the index. The two boundary equalities recover every other equality. When $r=0$, the preceding Fitting ideal is zero by convention.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: An adically complete pair is henselian
theorems.proof: Write $(A,I)$ as the inverse limit of $(A/I^n,I/I^n)$. Each ideal in the limit system is nilpotent, and the henselian condition is preserved under inverse limits of pairs.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Reducedness ascends along smooth ring maps
theorems.proof: Over a Noetherian source the flat reduced-fibre criterion applies. In general, descend the smooth presentation and any nilpotent element to a finitely generated integer subalgebra of the reduced source.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Normality ascends along smooth ring maps
theorems.proof: The numbered lemma proves ascent for a normal source without a Noetherian hypothesis. It reduces to a normal domain locally and uses Noetherian approximation over that domain.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Regularity ascends along smooth ring maps
theorems.proof: The local criterion for regularity applies to the flat local maps, with geometrically regular fibres supplied by smoothness.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat Noetherian ascent of reducedness
theorems.proof: Apply ascent of the Noetherian Serre conditions R₀ and S₁ to the base and fibres.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat Noetherian ascent of normality
theorems.proof: Apply ascent of the Noetherian Serre conditions R₁ and S₂ to the base and fibres.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Noetherianity descends along faithfully flat maps
theorems.proof: Extend an ascending chain of ideals and contract it back using faithful flatness.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Reducedness descends along faithfully flat maps
theorems.proof: The source embeds in its target. A nilpotent element maps to zero and is therefore zero.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Normality descends along faithfully flat maps
theorems.proof: Localize at primes lying over each specified source prime, then use faithfully flat descent of integral closedness in the local domains.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Regularity descends along faithfully flat maps
theorems.proof: Noetherianity first descends. Choose a target prime above each source prime and use descent of regularity along the resulting flat local maps.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Nagata descends along smooth maps surjective on spectra
theorems.proof: Smoothness and surjectivity on spectra give faithful flatness. Use the Nagata descent statement for smooth surjections.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Two-sided Noetherianity for a ring map
theorems.proof: Both source and target being Noetherian are the defining conditions of the premise.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.proof: Induct on the length using the first nonzerodivisor to identify the first Koszul complex tensored with the module with its degree-zero homology.
theorems.name: Injective multiplication at every stage of a sequence ⇒ Koszul-regular sequence on a module

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.proof: Each injectivity condition is part of the definition of a regular sequence.
theorems.name: Regular sequence on a module ⇒ Injective multiplication at every stage of a sequence

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.proof: Apply the Koszul vanishing argument with the coefficient module equal to the ring.
theorems.name: Regular sequence in a ring ⇒ Koszul-regular sequence in a ring

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.proof: Vanishing of first Koszul homology identifies the relations on the sequence with Koszul relations. The numbered lemma passes this criterion to the associated graded module.
theorems.name: H₁-regular sequence on a module ⇒ Quasi-regular sequence on a module

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.proof: Specialize the result on modules to the coefficient module equal to the ring.
theorems.name: H₁-regular sequence in a ring ⇒ Quasi-regular sequence in a ring

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Affine universal homeomorphism criterion
theorems.proof: An integral map is universally closed. Surjectivity and universal injectivity give a bijection after every base change. Conversely a universal homeomorphism is integral, surjective and universally injective. Universal injectivity is equivalent to injectivity on points together with purely inseparable residue extensions.
refs: Stacks 0BRD · sufficient conditions for ring maps
Stacks 04DF · necessary and sufficient conditions for a universal homeomorphism
Stacks 01S4 · residue-field test for universal injectivity

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Separably algebraic constants characterize geometric irreducibility
theorems.proof: An extra finite separable constant splits after scalar extension to a separable closure and gives multiple minimal primes. Conversely, absence of extra separably algebraic constants makes the extension linearly disjoint from finite Galois extensions of the base, giving the finite separable field test.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Relative algebraic closure implies geometric irreducibility
theorems.proof: If the base field contains every algebraic element of the extension then it contains every separably algebraic element.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Prime-ideal test for Jacobson rings
theorems.proof: Every radical ideal is the intersection of the primes containing it. Conversely, each prime is radical.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type algebras over fields are Jacobson
theorems.proof: The Nullstellensatz expresses each radical ideal as an intersection of maximal ideals.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Closed points and Jacobson targets under finite type maps
theorems.proof: The finite type Jacobson theorem contracts each maximal ideal to a maximal ideal and gives a finite residue extension there. It also gives the Jacobson property of the target.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Principal ideal domains are normal domains
theorems.proof: Write an integral fraction in lowest terms. Its monic equation forces the denominator to divide a power of the relatively prime numerator, hence to be a unit.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Going down for integral extensions of a normal domain
theorems.proof: For each inclusion of primes of the source and each prime over the larger prime, the integral going-down theorem gives a smaller prime over the smaller one. Normality here concerns the source domain.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Empty support detects the zero module
theorems.proof: A nonzero element survives localization at a maximal ideal containing its proper annihilator. The zero module vanishes after every localization.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite presentation bounds the complement of the support
theorems.proof: In a finite presentation the relevant maximal minors provide finitely many principal opens on which the module vanishes. Their union is the complement of its closed support.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Open spectral maps lift generalizations
theorems.proof: After localizing at a chosen target prime, the image on spectra contains each generalization of its contraction.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Closed spectral maps and going up
theorems.proof: Closedness carries the closure of a point onto the closure of its image. Conversely going up makes the image of each closed affine subscheme stable under specialization, hence closed for such an affine image.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A finitely presented going-down map is open on spectra
theorems.proof: Each principal open has constructible image by finite presentation. Going down makes the image stable under generalization, so it is open.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Torsion freeness via the unique associated prime
theorems.proof: Each nonzero element of a torsion-free module over a domain has zero annihilator. For the converse use that the zero divisors on a finite module over a Noetherian ring form the union of its associated primes.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Torsion freeness via generic support and Serre S₁
theorems.proof: Generic support gives the full spectrum as support for a finite module. Under $(S_1)$ every associated prime is minimal in that support and hence is the generic point. The converse follows from the same associated-prime criterion.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Torsion freeness via generic support and absence of embedded primes
theorems.proof: With full support, the zero ideal is the only minimal prime. Absence of embedded primes then says precisely that every associated prime is zero.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexivity at low depth detects global reflexivity
theorems.proof: The forward direction is localization of reflexivity for finite modules over Noetherian domains. In the other direction apply the depth-two isomorphism criterion to evaluation into the torsion-free double dual.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A finite reflexive module over a Noetherian S₂ domain satisfies S₂
theorems.proof: Reflexivity gives torsion freeness. At primes of base depth at least two the module also has depth at least two. Together these bounds give the required Serre inequalities.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Torsion freeness at maximal ideals
theorems.proof: Localizing a torsion-free module over a domain preserves torsion freeness. Conversely, an element killed by a nonzero scalar has zero image at every maximal localization and hence is zero.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Torsion freeness of a finite module via a free embedding
theorems.proof: Embed the torsion-free module into its finite-dimensional generic fibre and clear the denominators of its finite generating set. A submodule of a free module over a domain is torsion free.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Flatness over a Dedekind domain via torsion freeness
theorems.proof: Flat modules over a domain are torsion free. For the converse test flatness locally at maximal ideals, whose local rings are fields or discrete valuation rings.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite torsion-free modules over a Dedekind domain are locally free
theorems.proof: The module is flat and finite over a Noetherian ring, hence finitely presented and locally free.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite torsion-free modules over a PID are free
theorems.proof: A finite torsion-free module embeds in a finite free module. Over a PID each submodule of a finite free module is finite free.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexivity via torsion freeness and Serre S₂
theorems.proof: A Noetherian normal domain is $(S_2)$. A finite reflexive module inherits the required depths. Conversely, the height-one intersection criterion and the depth-two extension criterion identify the module with its double dual.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexivity via reconstruction in codimension one
theorems.proof: Height-one local rings of a Noetherian normal domain are discrete valuation rings. Torsion-free finite modules there are free. In the generic fibre the height-one intersection identifies the module with its reflexive hull.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Serre’s splitting theorem
theorems.proof: The local summands imply $\dim V(x)>d=\dim\Omega$ at each closed point. Apply Serre’s selection proposition with $h=0$ and $k=d+1$. The exceptional closed locus is empty, giving a section which splits locally at every maximal ideal. Finite presentation gives a global splitting.
refs: Serre, Modules projectifs et espaces fibrés à fibre vectorielle, Exposé 23 (1958)

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Projectivity is equivalent to freeness after unrestricted free stabilization
theorems.proof: Write $M\oplus Q=F_0$ with $F_0$ free and reindex countably many copies of $F_0$ to absorb an extra $M$. Conversely a direct summand of a free module is projective.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite stably free summands capture all elements under Bass’s hypotheses
theorems.proof: Finite free stabilization places a given element in a finite free summand. Remove the stabilizing generators one at a time, using a unimodular element in the complementary projective module. This leaves a finite stably free summand containing the original element.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Bass’s freeness theorem for countably generated projectives
theorems.proof: A countable generating sequence gives a decomposition into finite stably free summands. The infinite local ranks then yield a countably infinite free summand. Eilenberg’s absorption isomorphism makes the entire module free.
refs: Bass, Big projective modules are free, Theorem 3.1 (1963)

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Tameness via a prime-to-characteristic root of a uniformizer
theorems.proof: A tame extension becomes unramified after adjoining a root whose index is divisible by all the ramification indices. Conversely the uniformizer-root extension is tame, and composition and passage to intermediate fields preserve tameness.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Universal catenarity of a Noetherian local ring implies formal catenarity
theorems.proof: In a Noetherian local ring, failure of formal catenarity produces a finite type algebra with saturated chains of distinct lengths. Apply the contrapositive.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Formal catenarity implies universal catenarity
theorems.proof: The formal equidimensionality condition on all minimal-prime quotients gives the dimension formula needed for universal catenarity of the Noetherian local ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Unibranchness via the henselization
theorems.proof: Normalization of the reduction and henselization identify the branch count with the number of minimal primes of $A^h$. A single branch gives precisely unibranchness.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Geometric unibranchness via the strict henselization
theorems.proof: Strict henselization detects the ordinary branch together with the possible residue embeddings of the normalization. A single resulting minimal prime is equivalent to geometric unibranchness.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Weak dimension at most zero is equivalent to absolute flatness
theorems.proof: A module of flat dimension at most zero is flat. The equivalence applies to all modules over the given ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Arbitrary products of fields are absolutely flat
theorems.proof: For $a=(a_i)$ choose $b_i=a_i^{-1}$ if $a_i\ne0$ and $b_i=0$ otherwise. Then $a^2b=a$, the von Neumann regularity criterion for commutative rings.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Absolute flatness ascends through a flat multiplication map
theorems.proof: Every module over the source is flat, so the ring map is flat. Apply the weak dimension ascent theorem at $d=0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Weakly étale algebras over reduced rings are reduced
theorems.proof: Embed the reduced base in the product of its residue fields. Flatness preserves that injection after tensoring with the target. The new target above the product of fields is absolutely flat by the flat diagonal criterion, hence reduced.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Weak dimension at most one via ideals
theorems.proof: Use the long exact Tor sequence for a quotient by an ideal and the ideal test for flatness.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Weak dimension at most one via finitely generated ideals
theorems.proof: Every ideal is the directed union of its finitely generated subideals. Flatness passes to that filtered colimit.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Weak dimension at most one via submodules
theorems.proof: A short exact sequence with flat middle term identifies the positive Tor groups of the submodule with the higher Tor groups of the quotient.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Simplicity and length one
theorems.proof: The unique possible strict chain in a simple module runs from zero to the whole nonzero module. A proper nonzero submodule would create a chain of length at least two.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Valuation rings are coherent
theorems.proof: Each nonzero finite ideal is principal and is free of rank one because the ring is a domain. The zero ideal is finitely presented as well.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Lazard’s characterization of flat modules
theorems.proof: A flat module is a directed colimit of finite free modules. Conversely tensor and exactness commute with directed colimits.
refs: D. Lazard, Autour de la platitude, Chapter I, Theorem 1.2(i)–(iii), pp. 84–85 (flat modules as filtered colimits of finite free modules)
J. S. Milne, A Primer of Commutative Algebra, v4.03, Example 11.6 (Lazard’s theorem)

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Tensor-product surjectivity characterizes finite generation
theorems.proof: Use finite generators to choose lifts uniformly. Conversely test the tuple of all module elements in a product of copies of the module.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Tensor-product bijectivity characterizes finite presentation
theorems.proof: A finite presentation commutes with products upon tensoring. Conversely surjectivity first gives finite generation and injectivity bounds the relations.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Chase’s criterion for coherent rings
theorems.proof: Finitely presented ideals test flatness of arbitrary products, and flatness of all products tests coherence.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Powers of the ring suffice in Chase’s criterion
theorems.proof: Testing all products of the regular module gives the converse direction in Chase’s theorem.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Adic formal smoothness via flatness and the closed fibre
theorems.proof: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)\to(B,\mathfrak n,K)$ be a local map of Noetherian local rings. Write $F=B/\mathfrak mB$ for its closed fibre. The following are equivalent. The map is flat and $F$ geometrically regular over $k$. The map is flat and $k\to F$ formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology on $F$. The map $A\to B$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: André criterion for regularity of a local ring map
theorems.proof: Regularity of the source completion lets regularity descend from the formally smooth map of complete local rings, using faithful flatness of target completion.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Adically formally smooth local maps of Noetherian local rings are flat
theorems.proof: Use the local flatness criterion after passage to the maximal-ideal-adic completions.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Regular ascent of the reduced property
