theorems.proof: For $f\in J$ there exists an $m\times n$ matrix $B$ with $BA=fI_m$. Apply the adjugate identity to each maximal square submatrix and form the corresponding linear combination. Conversely $BA=fI_m$ implies $f^m\in J$ by the Cauchy–Binet formula.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Multiplication by a square-block adjugate tracks maximal minors
theorems.hypotheses: Write an $n\times m$ matrix $A$ as the vertical concatenation of a square $m\times m$ matrix $A_1$ and the remaining block $A_2$, with $n\geq m$. Put $B=\operatorname{adj}(A_1)$ and $f=\det A_1$.
theorems.statement: The top block of $AB$ is $fI_m$. Its remaining entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the determinant of the matrix obtained from $A_1$ by replacing row $j$ with row $i$ of $A$, by expansion of that determinant along the replaced row.
theorems.proof: The top block of $AB$ is $fI_m$. Its remaining entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the determinant of the matrix obtained from $A_1$ by replacing row $j$ with row $i$ of $A$, by expansion of that determinant along the replaced row.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Too few generators obstruct an injection of a finite free module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\ne0$, $n\geq1$, and let $M$ be generated by fewer than $n$ elements.
theorems.statement: Every linear map $R^n\to M$ has a nonzero kernel. Such a map lifts through a surjection $R^m\to M$ with $m<n$. The determinantal argument for the resulting $m\times n$ matrix produces a nonzero vector in its kernel by choosing a maximal nonzero minor, adjoining an extra column, and using the signed minors of that submatrix.
theorems.proof: Every linear map $R^n\to M$ has a nonzero kernel. Such a map lifts through a surjection $R^m\to M$ with $m<n$. The determinantal argument for the resulting $m\times n$ matrix produces a nonzero vector in its kernel by choosing a maximal nonzero minor, adjoining an extra column, and using the signed minors of that submatrix.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: The rank of a finite free module is unique over a nonzero ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\ne0$ and suppose that $R^n\simeq R^m$ as $R$-modules for nonnegative integers $n,m$.
theorems.statement: Then $n=m$. After tensoring with the residue field at a maximal ideal, the two vector spaces have dimensions $n$ and $m$.
theorems.proof: Then $n=m$. After tensoring with the residue field at a maximal ideal, the two vector spaces have dimensions $n$ and $m$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Cayley–Hamilton for matrices over a commutative ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\in\operatorname{Mat}_n(R)$ and set $P(T)=\det(TI_n-A)\in R[T]$.
theorems.statement: Then $P(A)=0$. Use the adjugate identity for $TI_n-A$ and compare matrix coefficients.
theorems.proof: Then $P(A)=0$. Use the adjugate identity for $TI_n-A$ and compare matrix coefficients.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Every endomorphism of a finite module satisfies a monic polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over $R$ and let $\varphi:M\to M$ be $R$-linear.
theorems.statement: There is a monic $P(T)\in R[T]$ with $P(\varphi)=0$. Lift the endomorphism to a matrix on a finite free module surjecting onto $M$ and apply Cayley–Hamilton.
theorems.proof: There is a monic $P(T)\in R[T]$ with $P(\varphi)=0$. Lift the endomorphism to a matrix on a finite free module surjecting onto $M$ and apply Cayley–Hamilton.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Determinant trick with coefficients in successive ideal powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ and $M$ be a finite $R$-module. Assume $\varphi(M)\subseteq IM$ for an endomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$.
theorems.statement: A monic polynomial $T^n+a_1T^{n-1}+\cdots+a_n$ annihilates $\varphi$ with $a_j\in I^j$. A lift of $\varphi$ to a finite free module has matrix entries in $I$, so the characteristic coefficient of degree $n-j$ lies in $I^j$.
theorems.proof: A monic polynomial $T^n+a_1T^{n-1}+\cdots+a_n$ annihilates $\varphi$ with $a_j\in I^j$. A lift of $\varphi$ to a finite free module has matrix entries in $I$, so the characteristic coefficient of degree $n-j$ lies in $I^j$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: A surjective endomorphism of a finite module is an isomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over $R$ and let $\varphi:M\to M$ be surjective.
theorems.statement: Regard $M$ as a finite $R[T]$-module where $T$ acts by $\varphi$. Since $TM=M$, the determinantal trick gives $g(T)\in (T)$ acting as the identity. Thus multiplication by $T$ has inverse multiplication by $g(T)/T$.
theorems.proof: Regard $M$ as a finite $R[T]$-module where $T$ acts by $\varphi$. Since $TM=M$, the determinantal trick gives $g(T)\in (T)$ acting as the identity. Thus multiplication by $T$ has inverse multiplication by $g(T)/T$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Local maps between local rings reflect units
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of local rings.
theorems.statement: Locality is equivalent to $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, to $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$, and to reflection of invertibility. The nonunits in either ring form its maximal ideal, and homomorphisms preserve units.
theorems.proof: Locality is equivalent to $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, to $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$, and to reflection of invertibility. The nonunits in either ring form its maximal ideal, and homomorphisms preserve units.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Fibre and contraction tests for a point in the spectral image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map and let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$. Write $S_{\mathfrak p}=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}S$.
theorems.statement: The point $\mathfrak p$ lies in the image if and only if $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is nonzero. Equivalent conditions are $S_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, $(S/\mathfrak pS)_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p S)=\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: The point $\mathfrak p$ lies in the image if and only if $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is nonzero. Equivalent conditions are $S_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, $(S/\mathfrak pS)_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p S)=\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: An idempotent and its complement give a clopen partition
theorems.hypotheses: Let $e\in R$ satisfy $e^2=e$.
theorems.statement: There is a partition $\operatorname{Spec}R=D(e)\amalg D(1-e)$. Every prime contains precisely one of $e,1-e$ since their product is zero and their sum is one.
theorems.proof: There is a partition $\operatorname{Spec}R=D(e)\amalg D(1-e)$. Every prime contains precisely one of $e,1-e$ since their product is zero and their sum is one.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The spectrum of a finite product of two rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R=R_1\times R_2$.
theorems.statement: The two projections induce a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R_1\amalg\operatorname{Spec}R_2\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R$. The two summands are cut out by the complementary idempotents $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$.
theorems.proof: The two projections induce a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R_1\amalg\operatorname{Spec}R_2\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R$. The two summands are cut out by the complementary idempotents $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Finitely generated idempotent ideals cut out clopen subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be finitely generated and satisfy $I^2=I$.
theorems.statement: For an idempotent $e$ generating $I$, the quotient $R/I$ is canonically $R_{1-e}$, and $V(I)=D(1-e)$ is both open and closed.
theorems.proof: For an idempotent $e$ generating $I$, the quotient $R/I$ is canonically $R_{1-e}$, and $V(I)=D(1-e)$ is both open and closed.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Closed unions of components of a ring spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T$ be a subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: The following are equivalent. The set $T$ is closed and a union of connected components, or $T$ is an intersection of clopen subsets, or $T=V(I)$ for an ideal $I$ generated by idempotents. Such $I$ is unique. Each connected component of a ring spectrum is an intersection of clopen neighbourhoods of a point.
theorems.proof: The following are equivalent. The set $T$ is closed and a union of connected components, or $T$ is an intersection of clopen subsets, or $T=V(I)$ for an ideal $I$ generated by idempotents. Such $I$ is unique. Each connected component of a ring spectrum is an intersection of clopen neighbourhoods of a point.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The quotient attached to a connected component
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a connected component of $\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: There is an ideal $I$ generated by idempotents with $C=V(I)$ such that every idempotent of $R$ has image $0$ or $1$ in $R/I$. An idempotent cuts the full spectrum into two clopen subsets, and $C$ lies entirely in one side.
theorems.proof: There is an ideal $I$ generated by idempotents with $C=V(I)$ such that every idempotent of $R$ has image $0$ or $1$ in $R/I$. An idempotent cuts the full spectrum into two clopen subsets, and $C$ lies entirely in one side.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Local tests on a finite standard open cover of the base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)=R$, let $M,N,M',M''$ be $R$-modules, and let $S$ be an $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: If the condition holds after localizing at every $f_i$, it holds globally for each of the following: vanishing of $M$, finiteness or finite presentation of $M$, isomorphism of a specified map $M\to N$, exactness of a specified short complex $0\to M''\to M\to M'\to0$, Noetherianity of $R$, and finite type or finite presentation of $S$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: If the condition holds after localizing at every $f_i$, it holds globally for each of the following: vanishing of $M$, finiteness or finite presentation of $M$, isomorphism of a specified map $M\to N$, exactness of a specified short complex $0\to M''\to M\to M'\to0$, Noetherianity of $R$, and finite type or finite presentation of $S$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type and finite presentation are checked on a finite source cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and let $(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=S$.
theorems.statement: If all $S_{g_i}$ are finite type $R$-algebras, then $S$ is of finite type over $R$. If all are finitely presented $R$-algebras, then $S$ is finitely presented over $R$. The local algebras here come from localizing the target ring of the given map.
theorems.proof: If all $S_{g_i}$ are finite type $R$-algebras, then $S$ is of finite type over $R$. If all are finitely presented $R$-algebras, then $S$ is finitely presented over $R$. The local algebras here come from localizing the target ring of the given map.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Equalizer of localized sections on a finite standard cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)=R$ and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to M\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i,j}M_{f_if_j}$ is exact. The first map localizes into each component. The second map takes the difference of restrictions on each intersection.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to M\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i,j}M_{f_if_j}$ is exact. The first map localizes into each component. The second map takes the difference of restrictions on each intersection.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Equalizer of functions on a finite standard cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)=R$.
theorems.statement: The ring $R$ is the equalizer of the two restriction maps $\prod_i R_{f_i}\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}R_{f_if_j}$. As a sequence of $R$-modules, the diagonal followed by the difference is exact at $R$ and the first product.
theorems.proof: The ring $R$ is the equalizer of the two restriction maps $\prod_i R_{f_i}\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}R_{f_if_j}$. As a sequence of $R$-modules, the diagonal followed by the difference is exact at $R$ and the first product.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Disjoint open decomposition gives a product of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\operatorname{Spec}R=U\amalg V$ with $U,V$ open.
theorems.statement: There are complementary idempotents $e,1-e$ with $U=D(e)$ and $V=D(1-e)$. The natural map $R\to R_e\times R_{1-e}$ is an isomorphism. Both factors are also quotients of $R$.
theorems.proof: There are complementary idempotents $e,1-e$ with $U=D(e)$ and $V=D(1-e)$. The natural map $R\to R_e\times R_{1-e}$ is an isomorphism. Both factors are also quotients of $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Detecting injectivity of simultaneous localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module and let $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in R$ be any finite list.
theorems.statement: The localization map $M\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}$ is injective exactly when the common annihilator of $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ in $M$ is zero. If a nonzero element $m$ is killed by some power of every $f_i$, take the smallest $d\geq1$ such that $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^dm=0$. A nonzero element of $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^{d-1}m$ lies in the common annihilator.
theorems.proof: The localization map $M\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}$ is injective exactly when the common annihilator of $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ in $M$ is zero. If a nonzero element $m$ is killed by some power of every $f_i$, take the smallest $d\geq1$ such that $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^dm=0$. A nonzero element of $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^{d-1}m$ lies in the common annihilator.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Gluing module data from finitely many standard opens
theorems.hypotheses: Take $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in R$, modules $M_i$ over $R_{f_i}$, and isomorphisms $\psi_{ij}:(M_i)_{f_j}\simeq(M_j)_{f_i}$ with $\psi_{jk}\psi_{ij}=\psi_{ik}$ on every triple overlap.
theorems.statement: Let $M$ be the submodule of $\prod_iM_i$ of tuples compatible under the $\psi_{ij}$. Each projection induces an isomorphism $M_{f_i}\simeq M_i$, and the induced transition maps agree with the original isomorphisms. This construction works for an arbitrary finite list of $f_i$.
theorems.proof: Let $M$ be the submodule of $\prod_iM_i$ of tuples compatible under the $\psi_{ij}$. Each projection induces an isomorphism $M_{f_i}\simeq M_i$, and the induced transition maps agree with the original isomorphisms. This construction works for an arbitrary finite list of $f_i$.

theorems.subject: ring-subset
theorems.name: Total fractions are invariant under inverting nonzerodivisors
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be a multiplicative subset of nonzerodivisors.
theorems.statement: The induced map $Q(R)\to Q(S^{-1}R)$ is an isomorphism. The element $a/s$ is a nonzerodivisor in the localization exactly when $a$ is one in $R$, since every denominator acts injectively. Inverting all nonzerodivisors gives $Q(Q(R))\simeq Q(R)$.
theorems.proof: The induced map $Q(R)\to Q(S^{-1}R)$ is an isomorphism. The element $a/s$ is a nonzerodivisor in the localization exactly when $a$ is one in $R$, since every denominator acts injectively. Inverting all nonzerodivisors gives $Q(Q(R))\simeq Q(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Product formula for total fractions at finitely many minimal primes
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $R$ has finitely many minimal primes $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_t$ and its zero divisors are precisely $\bigcup_i\mathfrak q_i$.
theorems.statement: Then $Q(R)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^tR_{\mathfrak q_i}$. The primes of $Q(R)$ correspond to primes contained in the union of the minimal primes. Finite prime avoidance makes each equal to one of the minimal primes, so $Q(R)$ has finitely many primes, all maximal. Its clopen decomposition into singleton spectra yields the product formula.
theorems.proof: Then $Q(R)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^tR_{\mathfrak q_i}$. The primes of $Q(R)$ correspond to primes contained in the union of the minimal primes. Finite prime avoidance makes each equal to one of the minimal primes, so $Q(R)$ has finitely many primes, all maximal. Its clopen decomposition into singleton spectra yields the product formula.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Prime ideals identify irreducible closed subsets and components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring with its Zariski prime spectrum.
theorems.statement: The closure of $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$. Each irreducible closed subset is of this form, and inclusion is the reverse of inclusion of prime ideals. The irreducible components are the $V(\mathfrak p)$ indexed by minimal primes.
theorems.proof: The closure of $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$. Each irreducible closed subset is of this form, and inclusion is the reverse of inclusion of prime ideals. The irreducible components are the $V(\mathfrak p)$ indexed by minimal primes.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The Zariski spectrum of every commutative ring is spectral
theorems.hypotheses: Give $\operatorname{Spec}R$ its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: The space is quasi-compact and sober. Its principal opens are quasi-compact, form a basis, and satisfy $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$. These properties give spectrality, including for the zero ring.
theorems.proof: The space is quasi-compact and sober. Its principal opens are quasi-compact, form a basis, and satisfy $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$. These properties give spectrality, including for the zero ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Irreducible closed subsets through a point of a ring spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: Irreducible closed subsets containing $\mathfrak p$ correspond to prime ideals of $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Irreducible components through $\mathfrak p$ correspond to its minimal primes. Both correspondences send a localized prime to the vanishing set of its contraction to $R$.
theorems.proof: Irreducible closed subsets containing $\mathfrak p$ correspond to prime ideals of $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Irreducible components through $\mathfrak p$ correspond to its minimal primes. Both correspondences send a localized prime to the vanishing set of its contraction to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Separate a minimal prime from a quasi-compact open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ be quasi-compact open and let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime outside $W$.
theorems.statement: Some $f\notin\mathfrak p$ satisfies $D(f)\cap W=\varnothing$. Express $W$ as finitely many $D(g_j)$ with $g_j\in\mathfrak p$. Each $g_j$ becomes nilpotent in $R_{\mathfrak p}$, so a product of the finitely many denominators killing the relevant powers provides $f$.
theorems.proof: Some $f\notin\mathfrak p$ satisfies $D(f)\cap W=\varnothing$. Express $W$ as finitely many $D(g_j)$ with $g_j\in\mathfrak p$. Each $g_j$ becomes nilpotent in $R_{\mathfrak p}$, so a product of the finitely many denominators killing the relevant powers provides $f$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Recover an ideal inside a principal ideal from its colon
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq J$ be ideals in $R$ with $J=(a)$ principal. Write $(I:J)=\{r\in R:rJ\subseteq I\}$.
theorems.statement: Then $I=J(I:J)$. Every element of $I$ can be written $ra$ since it lies in $J$, and $ra\in I$ implies $r\in(I:J)$.
theorems.proof: Then $I=J(I:J)$. Every element of $I$ can be written $ra$ since it lies in $J$, and $ra\in I$ implies $r\in(I:J)$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: A maximal ideal outside an Oka family is prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal F$ be an Oka family of ideals of $R$ and let $I$ be maximal by inclusion among the ideals outside $\mathcal F$.
theorems.statement: Then $I$ is prime. If $a,b\notin I$ and $ab\in I$, then $I+(a)$ and $(I:a)$ strictly contain $I$. Maximality puts both in $\mathcal F$, so the Oka condition puts $I$ there, a contradiction. Also $I$ is proper since $R\in\mathcal F$.
theorems.proof: Then $I$ is prime. If $a,b\notin I$ and $ab\in I$, then $I+(a)$ and $(I:a)$ strictly contain $I$. Maximality puts both in $\mathcal F$, so the Oka condition puts $I$ there, a contradiction. Also $I$ is proper since $R\in\mathcal F$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Maximal ideals avoiding a multiplicative subset are prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative, and let $I$ be maximal among ideals disjoint from $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $I$ is prime. If $a,b\notin I$ and $ab\in I$, maximality produces $s\in (I+(a))\cap S$ and $t\in(I+(b))\cap S$. Expanding the product gives $st\in I\cap S$, which is impossible.
theorems.proof: Then $I$ is prime. If $a,b\notin I$ and $ab\in I$, maximality produces $s\in (I+(a))\cap S$ and $t\in(I+(b))\cap S$. Expanding the product gives $st\in I\cap S$, which is impossible.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Cohen’s criterion for Noetherianity from prime ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring.
theorems.statement: Every ideal maximal among the ideals that are not finitely generated is prime. Consequently if each prime ideal is finitely generated, $R$ is Noetherian. Apply the prime ideal principle for the Oka family of finitely generated ideals. The union of a chain of ideals outside the family stays outside it, because finitely many generators of a union would occur together in one member.
theorems.proof: Every ideal maximal among the ideals that are not finitely generated is prime. Consequently if each prime ideal is finitely generated, $R$ is Noetherian. Apply the prime ideal principle for the Oka family of finitely generated ideals. The union of a chain of ideals outside the family stays outside it, because finitely many generators of a union would occur together in one member.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A domain criterion using nonzerodivisors in nonzero primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring.
theorems.statement: An ideal maximal among ideals without a nonzerodivisor is prime, by applying multiplicative avoidance to the set of nonzerodivisors. If $R\ne0$ and every nonzero prime contains a nonzerodivisor, every ideal disjoint from that set lies in the zero prime. In particular a principal ideal generated by a zero divisor lies in the zero ideal, so all nonzero elements are nonzerodivisors.
theorems.proof: An ideal maximal among ideals without a nonzerodivisor is prime, by applying multiplicative avoidance to the set of nonzerodivisors. If $R\ne0$ and every nonzero prime contains a nonzerodivisor, every ideal disjoint from that set lies in the zero prime. In particular a principal ideal generated by a zero divisor lies in the zero ideal, so all nonzero elements are nonzerodivisors.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Quasi-compact opens in an affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $U$ be open in $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$. An open is retrocompact when its intersection with each quasi-compact open of $X$ is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The following conditions are equivalent. The open $U$ is retrocompact, $U$ is quasi-compact, $U$ is a finite union of principal opens, or $U=X\setminus V(I)$ for a finitely generated ideal $I$. Retrocompactness gives quasi-compactness by testing on $X$. The converse follows from the principal-open basis closed under finite intersection.
theorems.proof: The following conditions are equivalent. The open $U$ is retrocompact, $U$ is quasi-compact, $U$ is a finite union of principal opens, or $U=X\setminus V(I)$ for a finitely generated ideal $I$. Retrocompactness gives quasi-compactness by testing on $X$. The converse follows from the principal-open basis closed under finite intersection.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Affine spectral maps are quasi-compact and pull back constructible sets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be induced by any ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to S$.
theorems.statement: The inverse image of $D(r)$ is $D(\varphi(r))$. Thus the inverse image of a quasi-compact open is quasi-compact, and the inverse image of any constructible set is constructible by the Boolean description in terms of quasi-compact opens.
theorems.proof: The inverse image of $D(r)$ is $D(\varphi(r))$. Thus the inverse image of a quasi-compact open is quasi-compact, and the inverse image of any constructible set is constructible by the Boolean description in terms of quasi-compact opens.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite Boolean normal form for constructible subsets of an affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T$ be a subset of the Zariski spectrum of $R$.
theorems.statement: The set $T$ is constructible if and only if it is a finite union of subsets $D(f)\cap V(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ for ring elements $f,g_1,\ldots,g_m$. Reduce finite Boolean formulas in principal opens to disjunctive normal form. Products combine positive tests and finitely generated ideals combine negative tests.
theorems.proof: The set $T$ is constructible if and only if it is a finite union of subsets $D(f)\cap V(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ for ring elements $f,g_1,\ldots,g_m$. Reduce finite Boolean formulas in principal opens to disjunctive normal form. Products combine positive tests and finitely generated ideals combine negative tests.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A constructible subset is the image of a finitely presented algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ be constructible.
theorems.statement: There is a finitely presented $R$-algebra $S$ whose spectrum has image $T$. For a piece $D(f)\cap V(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ take $(R/(g_1,\ldots,g_m))_f$, and for the finite union use a finite product of these algebras.
theorems.proof: There is a finitely presented $R$-algebra $S$ whose spectrum has image $T$. For a piece $D(f)\cap V(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ take $(R/(g_1,\ldots,g_m))_f$, and for the finite union use a finite product of these algebras.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A principal localization preserves constructibility under direct image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f\in R$ and let $T$ be constructible in $\operatorname{Spec}R_f$.
theorems.statement: The image of $T$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is constructible. For any Boolean piece written with elements of $R_f$, clear the powers of $f$ in the denominators and intersect the resulting Boolean piece in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $D(f)$.
theorems.proof: The image of $T$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is constructible. For any Boolean piece written with elements of $R_f$, clear the powers of $f$ in the denominators and intersect the resulting Boolean piece in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $D(f)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A quotient by a finitely generated ideal preserves constructible images
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be finitely generated and let $T$ be constructible in $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$.
theorems.statement: The image of $T$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is constructible. Lift the elements used in a finite Boolean expression to $R$ and intersect with the constructible vanishing set $V(I)$.
theorems.proof: The image of $T$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is constructible. Lift the elements used in a finite Boolean expression to $R$ and intersect with the constructible vanishing set $V(I)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The affine-line projection is open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and consider the projection induced by $R\to R[x]$.
theorems.statement: For $F(x)=\sum_i a_i x^i$, the image of $D(F)$ is $\bigcup_iD(a_i)$, since a polynomial over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is contained in every prime exactly when it is zero. Thus standard opens have quasi-compact open images, and arbitrary opens have open images.
theorems.proof: For $F(x)=\sum_i a_i x^i$, the image of $D(F)$ is $\bigcup_iD(a_i)$, since a polynomial over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is contained in every prime exactly when it is zero. Thus standard opens have quasi-compact open images, and arbitrary opens have open images.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Fibrewise nilpotence is defined by characteristic coefficients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be free of finite rank $n$ as an $R$-module, let $u\in A$, and write $T^n+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a_jT^j$ for the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by $u$.
theorems.statement: The element $u$ acts nilpotently on $A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ exactly for $\mathfrak p\in V(a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})$. Characteristic polynomials commute with this base change. Over a field, a linear endomorphism is nilpotent precisely when its characteristic polynomial is a pure power of $T$.
theorems.proof: The element $u$ acts nilpotently on $A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ exactly for $\mathfrak p\in V(a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})$. Characteristic polynomials commute with this base change. Over a field, a linear endomorphism is nilpotent precisely when its characteristic polynomial is a pure power of $T$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Images of standard opens in a monic polynomial quotient are quasi-compact open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f,g\in R[x]$ and assume the leading coefficient of $g$ is a unit.
theorems.statement: The image of $D(f)\cap V(g)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a finite union of principal opens. The quotient $R[x]/(g)$ is finite free, and its fibre at a prime has a point with $f$ nonzero exactly when $f$ is not nilpotent in that fibre. Use the characteristic coefficients for multiplication by $f$ to express this complementary locus.
theorems.proof: The image of $D(f)\cap V(g)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a finite union of principal opens. The quotient $R[x]/(g)$ is finite free, and its fibre at a prime has a point with $f$ nonzero exactly when $f$ is not nilpotent in that fibre. Use the characteristic coefficients for multiplication by $f$ to express this complementary locus.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Chevalley’s theorem for finitely presented ring maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finitely presented and $T\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$ constructible.
theorems.statement: The image of $T$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is constructible. The finite-presentation hypothesis allows the computation to be reduced to the polynomial quotient projection with finitely many equations.
theorems.proof: The image of $T$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is constructible. The finite-presentation hypothesis allows the computation to be reduced to the polynomial quotient projection with finitely many equations.

theorems.subject: ring-inclusion
theorems.name: Finite type inclusions of domains become finitely presented on principal opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq S$ be an inclusion of domains such that $S$ is finite type over $R$.
theorems.statement: There exist nonzero $f\in R$ and $g\in S$ such that $R_f\to S_{fg}$ is finitely presented. The conclusion concerns a principal localization on each side, with the target localized also at the image of $f$.
theorems.proof: There exist nonzero $f\in R$ and $g\in S$ such that $R_f\to S_{fg}$ is finitely presented. The conclusion concerns a principal localization on each side, with the target localized also at the image of $f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Generic openness inside the closure of a point reached by a finite type image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, $E\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$ constructible and $\xi$ a point of its image.
theorems.statement: The intersection of the image with $\overline{\{\xi\}}$ contains a dense open subset of that closure. The theorem applies along each reached point, even when global constructibility of the image does not follow from the finite type assumption.
theorems.proof: The intersection of the image with $\overline{\{\xi\}}$ contains a dense open subset of that closure. The theorem applies along each reached point, even when global constructibility of the image does not follow from the finite type assumption.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Dense image, injectivity and reaching the generic point over a domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain and let $R\to S$ be any ring map.
theorems.statement: The map is injective if and only if its spectral image is dense, and these conditions hold if and only if some prime of $S$ contracts to $(0)$. The kernel of a dense-image map is contained in the nilradical, which is zero for the domain. An injection reaches the minimal prime $(0)$.
theorems.proof: The map is injective if and only if its spectral image is dense, and these conditions hold if and only if some prime of $S$ contracts to $(0)$. The kernel of a dense-image map is contained in the nilradical, which is zero for the domain. An injection reaches the minimal prime $(0)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A reached minimal prime lifts to a minimal prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime of $R$ that is in the spectral image.
theorems.statement: Choose a prime of $S$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$, and a minimal prime below it. The contraction of that minimal prime is contained in $\mathfrak p$, so it equals $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: Choose a prime of $S$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$, and a minimal prime below it. The contraction of that minimal prime is contained in $\mathfrak p$, so it equals $\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring-inclusion
theorems.name: Nonzero ideals contract nontrivially across algebraic fraction field extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subseteq B$ be domains with $\operatorname{Frac}(B)/\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ algebraic, and let $0\ne J\subseteq B$ be an ideal.
theorems.statement: The contraction $A\cap J$ is nonzero. For $0\ne x\in J$ clear denominators in an algebraic equation for $x$ with nonzero constant term. The constant term belongs to $A\cap xB$. Hence the image of a proper closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is not dense in $\operatorname{Spec}A$.
theorems.proof: The contraction $A\cap J$ is nonzero. For $0\ne x\in J$ clear denominators in an algebraic equation for $x$ with nonzero constant term. The constant term belongs to $A\cap xB$. Hence the image of a proper closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is not dense in $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

theorems.subject: ring-subset
theorems.name: A localization with closed spectral image is a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and suppose the image of $\operatorname{Spec}S^{-1}R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is closed.
theorems.statement: The localization map $R\to S^{-1}R$ is surjective, so its target is canonically the quotient by its kernel. Write its image as $V(J)$. For each $s\in S$, one has $(s)+J=R$, and $J$ maps into the nilradical of the localization. If $rs+j=1$, then $j/1$ is nilpotent. The finite geometric sum for $(1-j/1)^{-1}$ puts $s^{-1}$ in the image of $R$.
theorems.proof: The localization map $R\to S^{-1}R$ is surjective, so its target is canonically the quotient by its kernel. Write its image as $V(J)$. For each $s\in S$, one has $(s)+J=R$, and $J$ maps into the nilradical of the localization. If $rs+j=1$, then $j/1$ is nilpotent. The finite geometric sum for $(1-j/1)^{-1}$ puts $s^{-1}$ in the image of $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-subset
theorems.name: Closed localizations split under three alternative finiteness hypotheses
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative with closed spectral image. Assume that $R$ is Noetherian, that its spectrum is Noetherian as a topological space, or that $S$ is finitely generated as a monoid.
theorems.statement: The localization is a quotient and the image of its spectrum is open as well as closed. Consequently $R\simeq S^{-1}R\times R'$ for a complementary quotient $R'$.
theorems.proof: The localization is a quotient and the image of its spectrum is open as well as closed. Consequently $R\simeq S^{-1}R\times R'$ for a complementary quotient $R'$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz for finite type algebras over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite type $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ has residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ finite over $k$. Every radical ideal $I$ is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing $I$. The result applies to polynomial rings and their quotient algebras.
theorems.proof: Each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ has residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ finite over $k$. Every radical ideal $I$ is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing $I$. The result applies to polynomial rings and their quotient algebras.

theorems.subject: ring-inclusion
theorems.name: A field finite type over a domain is finite over a principal localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq K$ be a subring of a field and suppose $K$ is finite type over $R$.
theorems.statement: There exists $f\in R$ with $R_f$ a field and $K/R_f$ finite. In particular, $f\ne0$ and the field $R_f$ equals the fraction field of $R$.
theorems.proof: There exists $f\in R$ with $R_f$ a field and $K/R_f$ finite. In particular, $f\ne0$ and the field $R_f$ equals the fraction field of $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and fix a finite number of variables.
theorems.statement: The ring $R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ is Noetherian. Induct on $n$. In one variable use the $x$-adic filtration and choose generators of the initial ideal in the Noetherian associated graded ring $R[x]$. Successive correction by lifts converges in the formal power series topology and generates the original ideal.
theorems.proof: The ring $R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ is Noetherian. Induct on $n$. In one variable use the $x$-adic filtration and choose generators of the initial ideal in the Noetherian associated graded ring $R[x]$. Successive correction by lifts converges in the formal power series topology and generates the original ideal.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The spectrum of a Noetherian ring is a Noetherian space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, and equip its spectrum with the Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: The descending chain condition on closed sets follows because such chains correspond by vanishing sets to ascending chains of radical ideals.
theorems.proof: The descending chain condition on closed sets follows because such chains correspond by vanishing sets to ascending chains of radical ideals.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type change of base preserves Noetherianity of the target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $R\to R'$ be ring maps with $R\to R'$ of finite type and $S$ Noetherian.
theorems.statement: Then $R'\otimes_R S$ is Noetherian, as it is a finite type algebra over the Noetherian ring $S$. The finite type hypothesis is on $R\to R'$.
theorems.proof: Then $R'\otimes_R S$ is Noetherian, as it is a finite type algebra over the Noetherian ring $S$. The finite type hypothesis is on $R\to R'$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Base change of a Noetherian algebra to a finitely generated field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian algebra over a field $k$ and let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension.
theorems.statement: Then $K\otimes_k R$ is Noetherian. Express $K$ as the fraction field of a finitely generated $k$-subalgebra, then combine the finite type case with stability under localization.
theorems.proof: Then $K\otimes_k R$ is Noetherian. Express $K$ as the fraction field of a finitely generated $k$-subalgebra, then combine the finite type case with stability under localization.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: A principal neighbourhood embeds into a prescribed local ring under three alternative hypotheses
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$. Assume that $R$ is a domain, that $R$ is Noetherian, or that $R$ is reduced with finitely many minimal primes.
theorems.statement: There is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $R_f\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective. In the Noetherian case one denominator kills all generators of the kernel of $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$. In the reduced case with finitely many minimal primes, choose $f$ vanishing at the minimal primes outside $\mathfrak p$ and use the injective map to the product of the minimal-prime localizations.
theorems.proof: There is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $R_f\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective. In the Noetherian case one denominator kills all generators of the kernel of $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$. In the reduced case with finitely many minimal primes, choose $f$ vanishing at the minimal primes outside $\mathfrak p$ and use the injective map to the product of the minimal-prime localizations.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Surjective endomorphisms of Noetherian rings are automorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $\varphi:R\to R$ a surjective endomorphism.
theorems.statement: The ideals $\ker\varphi^n$ stabilize, say at $n$. For $a\in\ker\varphi$, lift $a=\varphi^n(b)$ by surjectivity. Then $b\in\ker\varphi^{n+1}=\ker\varphi^n$, so $a=0$ and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The ideals $\ker\varphi^n$ stabilize, say at $n$. For $a\in\ker\varphi$, lift $a=\varphi^n(b)$ by surjectivity. Then $b\in\ker\varphi^{n+1}=\ker\varphi^n$, so $a=0$ and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Extension of a locally nilpotent ideal remains locally nilpotent
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be a ring map and let $I\subseteq R$ consist of nilpotent elements.
theorems.statement: The extended ideal $IR'$ consists of nilpotent elements. Images of nilpotents are nilpotent, and in a commutative ring the nilpotents form an ideal.
theorems.proof: The extended ideal $IR'$ consists of nilpotent elements. Images of nilpotents are nilpotent, and in a commutative ring the nilpotents form an ideal.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Reduction modulo a locally nilpotent ideal reflects units
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be a locally nilpotent ideal and take $x\in R$.
theorems.statement: The element $x$ is invertible if and only if its image in $R/I$ is invertible. Lift an inverse to $y\in R$, so $xy=1+z$ for a nilpotent $z\in I$. A finite geometric sum inverts $1+z$.
theorems.proof: The element $x$ is invertible if and only if its image in $R/I$ is invertible. Lift an inverse to $y\in R$, so $xy=1+z$ for a nilpotent $z\in I$. A finite geometric sum inverts $1+z$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Idempotents lift uniquely modulo locally nilpotent ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ consist of nilpotent elements.
theorems.statement: Reduction $R\to R/I$ is a bijection on idempotents. A lift of an idempotent has nilpotent error $e^2-e$. Newton correction inside the subring generated by $e$ kills the error after finitely many steps. If idempotents $e,e'$ agree modulo $I$, then $e(1-e')$ and $e'(1-e)$ are nilpotent idempotents, hence zero.
theorems.proof: Reduction $R\to R/I$ is a bijection on idempotents. A lift of an idempotent has nilpotent error $e^2-e$. Newton correction inside the subring generated by $e$ kills the error after finitely many steps. If idempotents $e,e'$ agree modulo $I$, then $e(1-e')$ and $e'(1-e)$ are nilpotent idempotents, hence zero.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Polynomial correction for a nilpotent idempotent defect
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a possibly noncommutative algebra and suppose $x=e^2-e$ is nilpotent for an element $e\in A$.
theorems.statement: There is an idempotent $e'=e+xP(e,x)$ with $P\in\mathbf Z[U,V]$. The defect commutes with $e$, so the correction is performed in the commutative subring generated by $e$ and the identity.
theorems.proof: There is an idempotent $e'=e+xP(e,x)$ with $P\in\mathbf Z[U,V]$. The defect commutes with $e$, so the correction is performed in the commutative subring generated by $e$ and the identity.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Detecting powers of units modulo a locally nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be locally nilpotent and let $n\geq1$ be invertible in $R/I$.
theorems.statement: The $n$th-power map on $1+I$ is bijective. A unit of $R$ is an $n$th power if and only if its image in $R/I$ is one. Each individual lifting problem over $1+I$ can be solved by successive correction through the powers of a nilpotent principal ideal. For uniqueness, $(1+x)^n-1=x(n+xq(x))$ where the factor $n+xq(x)$ is a unit.
theorems.proof: The $n$th-power map on $1+I$ is bijective. A unit of $R$ is an $n$th power if and only if its image in $R/I$ is one. Each individual lifting problem over $1+I$ can be solved by successive correction through the powers of a nilpotent principal ideal. For uniqueness, $(1+x)^n-1=x(n+xq(x))$ where the factor $n+xq(x)$ is a unit.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: The determinant as the annihilator of degree-one elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite projective over $R$.
theorems.statement: The determinant identifies with the annihilator of the degree-one part $M$ in $\bigwedge^\ast_R M$. Locally choose a basis. The only basis monomials killed by multiplication by every basis element are in top exterior degree.
theorems.proof: The determinant identifies with the annihilator of the degree-one part $M$ in $\bigwedge^\ast_R M$. Locally choose a basis. The only basis monomials killed by multiplication by every basis element are in top exterior degree.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: The determinant of a short exact sequence of finite projectives
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of finite projective $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $\det(M')\otimes_R\det(M'')\xrightarrow{\sim}\det(M)$, in this order. Wedging a basis of $M'$ followed by lifted basis vectors of $M''$ is independent of the lifts.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical isomorphism $\det(M')\otimes_R\det(M'')\xrightarrow{\sim}\det(M)$, in this order. Wedging a basis of $M'$ followed by lifted basis vectors of $M''$ is independent of the lifts.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Naturality of the determinant of a short exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Take an isomorphism between short exact sequences of finite projective modules with components $u',u,u''$.
theorems.statement: If $\gamma$ and $\widetilde\gamma$ are the canonical determinant-product isomorphisms, then $\det(u)\circ\gamma=\widetilde\gamma\circ(\det(u')\otimes\det(u''))$.
theorems.proof: If $\gamma$ and $\widetilde\gamma$ are the canonical determinant-product isomorphisms, then $\det(u)\circ\gamma=\widetilde\gamma\circ(\det(u')\otimes\det(u''))$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Compatibility of determinant multiplication with a three-step filtration
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\subset L\subset M$ be a filtration with finite projective subquotients $K,L/K,M/L$.
theorems.statement: The two isomorphisms $\det(K)\otimes\det(L/K)\otimes\det(M/L)\to\det(M)$ obtained by first combining adjacent factors agree. Locally both wedge the bases in the same filtration order.
theorems.proof: The two isomorphisms $\det(K)\otimes\det(L/K)\otimes\det(M/L)\to\det(M)$ obtained by first combining adjacent factors agree. Locally both wedge the bases in the same filtration order.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: The sign on interchanging summands of determinant lines
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M',M''$ be finite projective. Use the ordered isomorphism $\det(M')\otimes\det(M'')\cong\det(M'\oplus M'')$.
theorems.statement: Swapping summands corresponds to swapping the tensor factors multiplied by $\det(-\mathrm{id}_{M'\otimes_RM''})$. On a component with ranks $r,s$ this scalar is $(-1)^{rs}$.
theorems.proof: Swapping summands corresponds to swapping the tensor factors multiplied by $\det(-\mathrm{id}_{M'\otimes_RM''})$. On a component with ranks $r,s$ this scalar is $(-1)^{rs}$.

theorems.subject: module-map-pair
theorems.name: Determinant identity for composites in opposite orders
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N$ be finite projective and let $a:M\to N$ and $b:N\to M$ be $R$-linear.
theorems.statement: The scalar determinants satisfy $\det(\mathrm{id}_N+ab)=\det(\mathrm{id}_M+ba)$ in $R$. Localize and compute the determinant of the block matrix with diagonal identity blocks and off-diagonal blocks $a$ and $-b$ by elimination in either order.
theorems.proof: The scalar determinants satisfy $\det(\mathrm{id}_N+ab)=\det(\mathrm{id}_M+ba)$ in $R$. Localize and compute the determinant of the block matrix with diagonal identity blocks and off-diagonal blocks $a$ and $-b$ by elimination in either order.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The determinant homomorphism from K-zero to the Picard group
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and give $\operatorname{Pic}(R)$ its tensor-product group law.
theorems.statement: The assignment $[P]\mapsto[\det(P)]$ defines a homomorphism $K_0(R)\to\operatorname{Pic}(R)$. If $P$ has constant rank $n$, the image is $[\bigwedge^n P]$. Direct sums give products by the determinant isomorphism for a split exact sequence.
theorems.proof: The assignment $[P]\mapsto[\det(P)]$ defines a homomorphism $K_0(R)\to\operatorname{Pic}(R)$. If $P$ has constant rank $n$, the image is $[\bigwedge^n P]$. Direct sums give products by the determinant isomorphism for a split exact sequence.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The Euler class of a perfect complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be an object of $D(R)$ represented by a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projectives.
theorems.statement: The class $c(K)=\sum_i(-1)^i[P^i]$ in $K_0(R)$ is independent of the representative. Shifting by $n$ multiplies it by $(-1)^n$, and a distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ gives $c(L)=c(K)+c(M)$.
theorems.proof: The class $c(K)=\sum_i(-1)^i[P^i]$ in $K_0(R)$ is independent of the representative. Shifting by $n$ multiplies it by $(-1)^n$, and a distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ gives $c(L)=c(K)+c(M)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The Grothendieck group of perfect complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Equip $K_0(D_{\mathrm{perf}}(R))$ with the relations of distinguished triangles.
theorems.statement: The Euler class gives an isomorphism $K_0(D_{\mathrm{perf}}(R))\xrightarrow{\sim}K_0(R)$, with inverse taking a finite projective module as a complex in degree zero. The filtration by terms gives the requisite alternating-sum relation.
theorems.proof: The Euler class gives an isomorphism $K_0(D_{\mathrm{perf}}(R))\xrightarrow{\sim}K_0(R)$, with inverse taking a finite projective module as a complex in degree zero. The filtration by terms gives the requisite alternating-sum relation.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Determinant, trace and characteristic polynomial in a finite length exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to(M,\varphi)\to(M',\varphi')\to(M'',\varphi'')\to0$ be a short exact sequence of finite length modules with compatible endomorphisms over $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$.
theorems.statement: The determinant of $\varphi'$ is the product of the end determinants, its trace is the sum of the end traces, and its characteristic polynomial is the product of the end polynomials, all over $\kappa$. Join filtrations from the two ends to compute the invariants in the middle.
theorems.proof: The determinant of $\varphi'$ is the product of the end determinants, its trace is the sum of the end traces, and its characteristic polynomial is the product of the end polynomials, all over $\kappa$. Join filtrations from the two ends to compute the invariants in the middle.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: The determinant of scalar multiplication is a residue field norm power
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be a local map with finite residue field extension $\kappa'/\kappa$. Fix $u\in R'$ and a finite length $R'$-module $M'$.
theorems.statement: The determinant over $\kappa$ of $u$ acting on $M'$ is $\operatorname{Norm}_{\kappa'/\kappa}(\bar u)^{\operatorname{length}_{R'}(M')}$. A composition series over $R'$ reduces it to the determinant on $\kappa'$.
theorems.proof: The determinant over $\kappa$ of $u$ acting on $M'$ is $\operatorname{Norm}_{\kappa'/\kappa}(\bar u)^{\operatorname{length}_{R'}(M')}$. A composition series over $R'$ reduces it to the determinant on $\kappa'$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Flat local base change of the determinant over the residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be flat local with residue fields $\kappa,\kappa'$. Assume $m=\operatorname{length}_{R'}(R'/\mathfrak mR')$ is finite. Let $\varphi$ be an endomorphism of a finite length $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: Under $\kappa\to\kappa'$, the element $\det_\kappa(\varphi)^m$ maps to $\det_{\kappa'}(\varphi\otimes1)$ on $M\otimes_RR'$. Flatness preserves the filtration and the closed fibre contributes the exponent $m$.
theorems.proof: Under $\kappa\to\kappa'$, the element $\det_\kappa(\varphi)^m$ maps to $\det_{\kappa'}(\varphi\otimes1)$ on $M\otimes_RR'$. Flatness preserves the filtration and the closed fibre contributes the exponent $m$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The Picard group of a principal localization of a regular local ring vanishes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a regular local ring and $f\in R$.
theorems.statement: The group $\operatorname{Pic}(R_f)$ is trivial.
theorems.proof: The group $\operatorname{Pic}(R_f)$ is trivial.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Trivial Picard group of a generic fibre over a valuation ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field $\kappa$. Let $R\to A$ be a flat local map to a local ring, essentially of finite type, and suppose $A\otimes_R\kappa$ is regular.
theorems.statement: The Picard group of $A\otimes_R K$ is trivial.
theorems.proof: The Picard group of $A\otimes_R K$ is trivial.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: A surjective quasi-isomorphism preserves the determinant element
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a^\bullet:K^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ be a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism of finite projective complexes in degrees $-1,0$. Require that $L^{-1}$ and $L^0$ have the same rank at every prime.
theorems.statement: Then both complexes have Euler rank zero. The induced $\det(K^\bullet)\to\det(L^\bullet)$ maps $\det(d_K)$ to $\det(d_L)$.
theorems.proof: Then both complexes have Euler rank zero. The induced $\det(K^\bullet)\to\det(L^\bullet)$ maps $\det(d_K)$ to $\det(d_L)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Homotopic termwise surjective quasi-isomorphisms give the same determinant map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a^\bullet:K^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ be a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism between complexes of finite projectives concentrated in degrees $-1,0$. Fix $h:K^0\to L^{-1}$ such that $a^0+d_Lh$ and $a^{-1}+hd_K$ are again surjective.
theorems.statement: Writing $b^\bullet$ for the resulting homotopic map, the two isomorphisms $\det(a^\bullet),\det(b^\bullet):\det(K^\bullet)\to\det(L^\bullet)$ agree.
theorems.proof: Writing $b^\bullet$ for the resulting homotopic map, the two isomorphisms $\det(a^\bullet),\det(b^\bullet):\det(K^\bullet)\to\det(L^\bullet)$ agree.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Compatibility of determinant maps with composition
theorems.hypotheses: Take degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms $a^\bullet:K^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ and $b^\bullet:L^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ of finite projective complexes in degrees $-1,0$.
theorems.statement: The two covariant maps from $\det(K^\bullet)$ to $\det(M^\bullet)$ agree: $\det(b^\bullet)\circ\det(a^\bullet)=\det(b^\bullet\circ a^\bullet)$. The direction follows the definition of the determinant map preceding 0FJJ.
theorems.proof: The two covariant maps from $\det(K^\bullet)$ to $\det(M^\bullet)$ agree: $\det(b^\bullet)\circ\det(a^\bullet)=\det(b^\bullet\circ a^\bullet)$. The direction follows the definition of the determinant map preceding 0FJJ.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Determinant functor and canonical elements for two-term perfect complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and consider perfect objects with Tor-amplitude contained in $[-1,0]$, with isomorphisms as morphisms.
theorems.statement: The determinant is a functor to the groupoid of invertible $R$-modules. A rank-zero object has a canonical element in its determinant line, given by the determinant of the differential in a two-term projective model and preserved by isomorphisms.
theorems.proof: The determinant is a functor to the groupoid of invertible $R$-modules. A rank-zero object has a canonical element in its determinant line, given by the determinant of the differential in a two-term projective model and preserved by isomorphisms.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Extending a valuation across a purely inseparable field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ of characteristic $p>0$, let $L/K$ be purely inseparable, and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$.
theorems.statement: The ring $B$ is a valuation ring of $L$ and $A\subseteq B$ is a local extension. If $x\in L^\times$ and $x^{p^n}\in K$, then $x^{p^n}$ or its inverse belongs to $A$, making $x$ or its inverse integral over $A$.
theorems.proof: The ring $B$ is a valuation ring of $L$ and $A\subseteq B$ is a local extension. If $x\in L^\times$ and $x^{p^n}\in K$, then $x^{p^n}$ or its inverse belongs to $A$, making $x$ or its inverse integral over $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Descent of a power up to a unit through weakly unramified height-one extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be flat local between Noetherian local normal domains and suppose $f=wh^n$ for $f\in A$, $h\in B$, $w\in B^\times$ and $n>1$. For each height-one $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ assume that some height-one $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$ makes $A_{\mathfrak p}\subset B_{\mathfrak q}$ weakly unramified.
theorems.statement: There are $u\in A^\times$ and $g\in A$ with $f=ug^n$.
theorems.proof: There are $u\in A^\times$ and $g\in A$ with $f=ug^n$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finitely presented modules over a nonzero chain ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be nonzero with linearly ordered ideals, and let $M$ be finitely presented over $R$.
theorems.statement: There is an isomorphism $M\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^nR/f_iR$ for some $f_i\in R$. Total divisibility permits a pivot dividing all matrix entries at each presentation reduction step.
theorems.proof: There is an isomorphism $M\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^nR/f_iR$ for some $f_i\in R$. Total divisibility permits a pivot dividing all matrix entries at each presentation reduction step.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Local chain-ring conditions imply a global cyclic-summand presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let each $R_{\mathfrak m}$ for a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ be a chain ring, and let $M$ be finitely presented over $R$.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of modules $R/f_iR$. The local cyclic decompositions are used with finite presentation to obtain a finite global splitting.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of modules $R/f_iR$. The local cyclic decompositions are used with finite presentation to obtain a finite global splitting.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finitely presented modules over a Bézout domain split into free and torsion parts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Bézout domain.
theorems.statement: A finitely generated submodule of a free module is finite free. A finitely presented $M$ is a direct sum of a finite free module and its torsion submodule; that submodule is a summand of a finite direct sum of $R/f_iR$ with $f_i\ne0$.
theorems.proof: A finitely generated submodule of a free module is finite free. A finitely presented $M$ is a direct sum of a finite free module and its torsion submodule; that submodule is a summand of a finite direct sum of $R/f_iR$ with $f_i\ne0$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Structure of finitely generated modules over a principal ideal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a principal ideal domain and $M$ a finitely generated $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The module is isomorphic to $R^r\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^n R/f_iR$ for $r,n\geq0$ and nonzero elements $f_i\in R$.
theorems.proof: The module is isomorphic to $R^r\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^n R/f_iR$ for $r,n\geq0$ and nonzero elements $f_i\in R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Completing a unimodular row over a Bézout domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ generate the unit ideal of a Bézout domain $R$, with $n\geq1$.
theorems.statement: Some matrix in $\operatorname{GL}_n(R)$ has first row $(f_1,\dots,f_n)$. The kernel of this split surjection $R^n\to R$ is a finite free module, so choose a basis of the kernel and a lift of $1$.
theorems.proof: Some matrix in $\operatorname{GL}_n(R)$ has first row $(f_1,\dots,f_n)$. The kernel of this split surjection $R^n\to R$ is a finite free module, so choose a basis of the kernel and a lift of $1$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Dimension-one growth of the lengths of powers of a parameter
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local of dimension one. Take $x\in\mathfrak m$ outside every minimal prime and put $P(n)=\operatorname{length}_R(R/x^nR)$.
theorems.statement: Then $P(n)\leq nP(1)$ for $n\geq0$, with equality if $x$ is a nonzerodivisor. Multiplication by $x^i$ gives surjections $R/xR\to x^iR/x^{i+1}R$, which are isomorphisms in the nonzerodivisor case.
theorems.proof: Then $P(n)\leq nP(1)$ for $n\geq0$, with equality if $x$ is a nonzerodivisor. Multiplication by $x^i$ gives surjections $R/xR\to x^iR/x^{i+1}R$, which are isomorphisms in the nonzerodivisor case.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A colength bound on minimal primes in dimension one
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local of dimension one and $x\in\mathfrak m$ lie outside all minimal primes.
theorems.statement: The number of minimal primes of $R$ is at most $\operatorname{length}_R(R/xR)$.
theorems.proof: The number of minimal primes of $R$ is at most $\operatorname{length}_R(R/xR)$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Extend a parameter to a parameter system using prescribed deep elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local of dimension $d>1$, and take $f\in\mathfrak m$ outside every minimal prime and an integer $k\geq0$.
theorems.statement: There exist $g_1,\dots,g_{d-1}\in\mathfrak m^k$ such that $f,g_1,\dots,g_{d-1}$ is a system of parameters. One can choose powers of parameters for $R/fR$.
theorems.proof: There exist $g_1,\dots,g_{d-1}\in\mathfrak m^k$ such that $f,g_1,\dots,g_{d-1}$ is a system of parameters. One can choose powers of parameters for $R/fR$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Stability of a parameter colength under deep perturbation in dimension two
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local of dimension two, and let $f\in\mathfrak m$ avoid every minimal prime.
theorems.statement: There are $g\in\mathfrak m$ and $N\geq0$ such that both $(f,g)$ and $(f+h,g)$ are systems of parameters for each $h\in\mathfrak m^N$, with the same quotient lengths.
theorems.proof: There are $g\in\mathfrak m$ and $N\geq0$ such that both $(f,g)$ and $(f+h,g)$ are systems of parameters for each $h\in\mathfrak m^N$, with the same quotient lengths.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A reduced principal divisor through prescribed height-one primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local normal domain of dimension two and let $\mathfrak p_1,\dots,\mathfrak p_r$ be distinct height-one primes.
theorems.statement: There is a nonzero $f$ in their intersection such that $R/fR$ is reduced.
theorems.proof: There is a nonzero $f$ in their intersection such that $R/fR$ is reduced.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A power of a reduced principal divisor is divisible by a prescribed element
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a Noetherian local normal domain of dimension two, and let $a$ be nonzero in its maximal ideal.
theorems.statement: There is $c\in A$ with $A/cA$ reduced such that $a\mid c^n$ for some $n\geq1$. Choose a reduced principal divisor through the height-one primes over $a$ and bound their finitely many valuation multiplicities.
theorems.proof: There is $c\in A$ with $A/cA$ reduced such that $a\mid c^n$ for some $n\geq1$. Choose a reduced principal divisor through the height-one primes over $a$ and bound their finitely many valuation multiplicities.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Parameter-ideal multiplicity is bounded by colength
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local of dimension $d$ and $I$ generated by a system of parameters. Let $e_I$ be $d!$ times the leading coefficient of the eventual polynomial of $\operatorname{length}_R(R/I^{n+1})$.
theorems.statement: Then $e_I\leq\operatorname{length}_R(R/I)$. The degree-$n$ monomials in the $d$ generators span $I^n/I^{n+1}$ over $R/I$, which bounds its length and leading coefficient.
theorems.proof: Then $e_I\leq\operatorname{length}_R(R/I)$. The degree-$n$ monomials in the $d$ generators span $I^n/I^{n+1}$ over $R/I$, which bounds its length and leading coefficient.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: A colength bound on maximal-dimensional minimal primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local of dimension $d$ and let $I=(g_1,\ldots,g_d)$ be generated by a system of parameters.
theorems.statement: The number of minimal primes $\mathfrak p$ with $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)=d$ is at most $\operatorname{length}_R(R/I)$. Each such component contributes at least one to the multiplicity.
theorems.proof: The number of minimal primes $\mathfrak p$ with $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)=d$ is at most $\operatorname{length}_R(R/I)$. Each such component contributes at least one to the multiplicity.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Stability of parameter colength under deep perturbation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local of dimension $d\geq1$, with $f\in\mathfrak m$ outside every minimal prime.
theorems.statement: There are $g_1,\ldots,g_{d-1}\in\mathfrak m$ and $N\geq0$ for which $(f,g_1,\ldots,g_{d-1})$ and $(f+h,g_1,\ldots,g_{d-1})$ are parameter systems of equal quotient length whenever $h\in\mathfrak m^N$.
theorems.proof: There are $g_1,\ldots,g_{d-1}\in\mathfrak m$ and $N\geq0$ for which $(f,g_1,\ldots,g_{d-1})$ and $(f+h,g_1,\ldots,g_{d-1})$ are parameter systems of equal quotient length whenever $h\in\mathfrak m^N$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A nonzero radical ideal contains a reduced principal divisor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a catenary Noetherian local normal domain and $0\ne J\subseteq R$ a radical ideal.
theorems.statement: There is a nonzero $f\in J$ for which $R/fR$ is reduced. The nonzero condition on $J$ is required by the initial choice in the source proof and by the nonzero conclusion.
theorems.proof: There is a nonzero $f\in J$ for which $R/fR$ is reduced. The nonzero condition on $J$ is required by the initial choice in the source proof and by the nonzero conclusion.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The derived category of modules is symmetric monoidal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and use the ordinary cohomological sign conventions.
theorems.statement: The category $D(R)$ is symmetric monoidal with product $\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}$ and tensor unit $R$. The associativity constraint comes from total tensors and the symmetry uses the sign $(-1)^{ij}$ on degrees $i,j$.
theorems.proof: The category $D(R)$ is symmetric monoidal with product $\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}$ and tensor unit $R$. The associativity constraint comes from total tensors and the symmetry uses the sign $(-1)^{ij}$ on degrees $i,j$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Finite free subcomplexes contain any specified finitely many elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded above cochain complex of free $R$-modules and choose finitely many elements in specified degrees.
theorems.statement: There is a bounded subcomplex of finite free modules containing the elements. Fix bases and successively include the finitely many basis vectors needed to support the elements and their differentials, proceeding through the finitely many degrees up to the upper bound.
theorems.proof: There is a bounded subcomplex of finite free modules containing the elements. Fix bases and successively include the finitely many basis vectors needed to support the elements and their differentials, proceeding through the finitely many degrees up to the upper bound.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Cohomology decomposition of a derived-invertible object
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be tensor-invertible in $D(R)$.
theorems.statement: The object is perfect and is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_n H^n(M)[-n]$. Each cohomology module is finite projective over $R$. There is a finite ring-product decomposition indexed by the degrees that occur, such that $H^n(M)$ corresponds to an invertible module over the factor indexed by $n$.
theorems.proof: The object is perfect and is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_n H^n(M)[-n]$. Each cohomology module is finite projective over $R$. There is a finite ring-product decomposition indexed by the degrees that occur, such that $H^n(M)$ corresponds to an invertible module over the factor indexed by $n$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Artin–Rees stability of exactness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and let $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$. Let $L\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}N$ and $L\xrightarrow{f'}M\xrightarrow{g'}N$ be complexes of finite $A$-modules. Assume the first is exact at $M$, the same Artin–Rees index $c$ works for $f$ and $g$, and $f'-f$ and $g'-g$ take values in $I^{c+1}M$ and $I^{c+1}N$, respectively.
theorems.statement: The second complex is exact at its middle term, and the same index works for its outgoing map.
theorems.proof: The second complex is exact at its middle term, and the same index works for its outgoing map.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Associated graded cokernels under an Artin–Rees perturbation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and let $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$. Let $L\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}N$ and $L\xrightarrow{f'}M\xrightarrow{g'}N$ be complexes of finite $A$-modules. Assume the first is exact at $M$, the same Artin–Rees index $c$ works for $f$ and $g$, and $f'-f$ and $g'-g$ take values in $I^{c+1}M$ and $I^{c+1}N$, respectively.
theorems.statement: The associated graded modules of $\operatorname{coker}(g)$ and $\operatorname{coker}(g')$ are isomorphic over the graded ring $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)$.
theorems.proof: The associated graded modules of $\operatorname{coker}(g)$ and $\operatorname{coker}(g')$ are isomorphic over the graded ring $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: An Artin–Rees index survives flat base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be flat between Noetherian rings, let $I\subset A$, and let $f:M\to N$ be an $A$-linear map of finite modules for which $c$ works.
theorems.statement: The same index works for $M\otimes_A B\to N\otimes_A B$ and the ideal $IB$. Flatness commutes with the intersection of the two submodules used in the test.
theorems.proof: The same index works for $M\otimes_A B\to N\otimes_A B$ and the ideal $IB$. Flatness commutes with the intersection of the two submodules used in the test.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type of a pullback of finite type algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian. Let $A,B,C$ be finite type $R$-algebras, with $R$-algebra maps $A\to B$ and $C\to B$. Suppose $A\to B$ is surjective and $B$ is finite as a $C$-module.
theorems.statement: The pullback $A\times_B C$ is of finite type over $R$.
theorems.proof: The pullback $A\times_B C$ is of finite type over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type of a pullback along a finite product of surjections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $J$ a finite set. For $i\in J$, let $A_i\to B_i$ and $Q\to B_i$ be surjective $R$-algebra maps with $A_i,B_i,Q$ of finite type over $R$.
theorems.statement: The pullback $Q\times_{\prod_i B_i}\prod_i A_i$ is of finite type over $R$.
theorems.proof: The pullback $Q\times_{\prod_i B_i}\prod_i A_i$ is of finite type over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Principal localization of a ring pullback
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B'=B\times_R R'$ and $h=(g,f)\in B'$, with $g\in B$, $f\in R'$ and their common image $s\in R$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $(B')_h\to B_g\times_{R_s}(R')_f$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $(B')_h\to B_g\times_{R_s}(R')_f$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Taking a module pullback is right adjoint to restriction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B'\to B$, $B'\to R'$, $B\to R$ and $R'\to R$ form a commutative ring square. Let $(N,M',\varphi)$ consist of a $B$-module and an $R'$-module with $\varphi:N\otimes_B R\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{R'}R$.
theorems.statement: The functor sending a $B'$-module to its two scalar extensions and canonical overlap identification has right adjoint $(N,M',\varphi)\mapsto N\times_{M'\otimes_{R'}R}M'$, where the map from $N$ to the overlap uses $\varphi$.
theorems.proof: The functor sending a $B'$-module to its two scalar extensions and canonical overlap identification has right adjoint $(N,M',\varphi)\mapsto N\times_{M'\otimes_{R'}R}M'$, where the map from $N$ to the overlap uses $\varphi$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The spectrum of a one-sided-surjective ring pullback
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map from the topological pushout $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\amalg_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is a homeomorphism.
theorems.proof: The canonical map from the topological pushout $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\amalg_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is a homeomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integrality of the projection to the surjective side of a pullback
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Assume $B\to A$ is integral.
theorems.statement: The induced homomorphism $B'\to A'$ is integral.
theorems.proof: The induced homomorphism $B'\to A'$ is integral.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Restriction recovers the prescribed module gluing data
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Let $(N,M',\varphi)$ consist of a $B$-module, an $A'$-module and an isomorphism $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim} M'/IM'$. Put $M=M'/IM'$.
theorems.statement: Taking $N'=N\times_M M'$ is right adjoint to restriction, and extending $N'$ to $B$ and $A'$ recovers the given triple, including its overlap isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Taking $N'=N\times_M M'$ is right adjoint to restriction, and extending $N'$ to $B$ and $A'$ recovers the given triple, including its overlap isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Every module maps surjectively to the pullback of its restrictions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Let $L'$ be any $B'$-module.
theorems.statement: The unit $L'\to (L'\otimes_{B'}B)\times_{L'\otimes_{B'}A}(L'\otimes_{B'}A')$ is surjective. Injectivity can fail for unrestricted modules.
theorems.proof: The unit $L'\to (L'\otimes_{B'}B)\times_{L'\otimes_{B'}A}(L'\otimes_{B'}A')$ is surjective. Injectivity can fail for unrestricted modules.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Componentwise surjections induce a surjection on glued modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Take a morphism of compatible triples $(N_i,M_i',\varphi_i)$ whose maps on the $B$-modules and $A'$-modules are both surjective.
theorems.statement: The induced map $N_1\times_{M_1'/IM_1'}M_1'\to N_2\times_{M_2'/IM_2'}M_2'$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: The induced map $N_1\times_{M_1'/IM_1'}M_1'\to N_2\times_{M_2'/IM_2'}M_2'$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finiteness of a glued module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Let $(N,M',\varphi)$ consist of a $B$-module, an $A'$-module and an isomorphism $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim} M'/IM'$. Put $M=M'/IM'$. Suppose $N$ is finite over $B$ and $M'$ is finite over $A'$.
theorems.statement: The glued module $N\times_M M'$ is finite over $B'$.
theorems.proof: The glued module $N\times_M M'$ is finite over $B'$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Flat modules satisfy descent across the pullback square
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
theorems.statement: The category of flat $B'$-modules is equivalent by restriction to the full subcategory of compatible triples with $N$ flat over $B$ and $M'$ flat over $A'$. The inverse is $N\times_M M'$. In particular a flat $B'$-module is isomorphic to the pullback of its restrictions.
theorems.proof: The category of flat $B'$-modules is equivalent by restriction to the full subcategory of compatible triples with $N$ flat over $B$ and $M'$ flat over $A'$. The inverse is $N\times_M M'$. In particular a flat $B'$-module is isomorphic to the pullback of its restrictions.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite projective modules descend across the pullback square
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
theorems.statement: The category of finite projective $B'$-modules is equivalent by restriction to the full subcategory of compatible triples with both components finite projective over their respective rings.
theorems.proof: The category of finite projective $B'$-modules is equivalent by restriction to the full subcategory of compatible triples with both components finite projective over their respective rings.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Adjunction and restriction for relative module gluing
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Fix a map $B'\to D'$ and set $D=D'\otimes_{B'} B$, $C'=D'\otimes_{B'} A'$, and $C=D'\otimes_{B'} A$. Let $(N,M',\varphi)$ consist of a $D$-module, a $C'$-module and an identification $\varphi:N\otimes_D C\xrightarrow{\sim}M'/IM'$. Put $M=M'/IM'$.
theorems.statement: Gluing by $N'=N\times_M M'$ is right adjoint to extension to $D$ and $C'$. Extending $N'$ to $D$ and $C'$ recovers the prescribed triple.
theorems.proof: Gluing by $N'=N\times_M M'$ is right adjoint to extension to $D$ and $C'$. Extending $N'$ to $D$ and $C'$ recovers the prescribed triple.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The ideal of the relative overlap is generated by the base kernel
