theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Fix a map $B'\to D'$ and set $D=D'\otimes_{B'} B$, $C'=D'\otimes_{B'} A'$, and $C=D'\otimes_{B'} A$.
theorems.statement: With $J=\ker(B'\to B)$, the natural map $JD'\to IC'$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: With $J=\ker(B'\to B)$, the natural map $JD'\to IC'$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finiteness of a relatively glued module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Fix a map $B'\to D'$ and set $D=D'\otimes_{B'} B$, $C'=D'\otimes_{B'} A'$, and $C=D'\otimes_{B'} A$. Let $(N,M',\varphi)$ consist of a $D$-module, a $C'$-module and an identification $\varphi:N\otimes_D C\xrightarrow{\sim}M'/IM'$. Put $M=M'/IM'$. Suppose $N$ is finite over $D$ and $M'$ is finite over $C'$.
theorems.statement: The glued module $N\times_M M'$ is finite over $D'$.
theorems.proof: The glued module $N\times_M M'$ is finite over $D'$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Gluing of modules flat over the respective base rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Fix a map $B'\to D'$ and set $D=D'\otimes_{B'} B$, $C'=D'\otimes_{B'} A'$, and $C=D'\otimes_{B'} A$.
theorems.statement: Restriction identifies $D'$-modules flat over $B'$ with compatible triples whose $D$-module is flat over $B$ and whose $C'$-module is flat over $A'$. The inverse is the module pullback.
theorems.proof: Restriction identifies $D'$-modules flat over $B'$ with compatible triples whose $D$-module is flat over $B$ and whose $C'$-module is flat over $A'$. The inverse is the module pullback.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite presentation under relative module gluing
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Fix a map $B'\to D'$ and set $D=D'\otimes_{B'} B$, $C'=D'\otimes_{B'} A'$, and $C=D'\otimes_{B'} A$. Let $(N,M',\varphi)$ consist of a $D$-module, a $C'$-module and an identification $\varphi:N\otimes_D C\xrightarrow{\sim}M'/IM'$. Put $M=M'/IM'$. Assume $N$ is finitely presented over $D$ and flat over $B$, and $M'$ is finitely presented over $C'$ and flat over $A'$. Assume $B'\to D'$ factors as a flat map $B'\to D''$ followed by a finitely presented map $D''\to D'$.
theorems.statement: Then $N\times_M M'$ is finitely presented over $D'$.
theorems.proof: Then $N\times_M M'$ is finitely presented over $D'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Algebra properties over a pullback from its two restrictions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Let $D$ be a $B$-algebra and $C'$ an $A'$-algebra with a chosen identification $D\otimes_B A\cong C'/IC'=C$. Put $D'=D\times_C C'$.
theorems.statement: For each of finite type, flat, flat and finitely presented, smooth, and étale, the map $B'\to D'$ has the property precisely when both $B\to D$ and $A'\to C'$ have it. Restriction and this gluing functor give inverse equivalences on the flat algebras.
theorems.proof: For each of finite type, flat, flat and finitely presented, smooth, and étale, the map $B'\to D'$ has the property precisely when both $B\to D$ and $A'\to C'$ have it. Restriction and this gluing functor give inverse equivalences on the flat algebras.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Flat finitely presented quotients over a relative ring square
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to A$ be a surjection with kernel $I$, let $B\to A$ be any map, and put $B'=B\times_A A'$. Fix a map $B'\to D'$ and set $D=D'\otimes_{B'} B$, $C'=D'\otimes_{B'} A'$, and $C=D'\otimes_{B'} A$. Assume $B'\to D'$ is finitely presented and fix a $D'$-module $L'$.
theorems.statement: Base change gives a bijection between quotients of $L'$ that are finitely presented over $D'$ and flat over $B'$ and pairs of such quotients of its restrictions (over $D$ and flat over $B$, and over $C'$ and flat over $A'$). Their further restrictions to $C$ must be equal as quotients of $L'\otimes_{D'}C$. The inverse takes their pullback over that common quotient.
theorems.proof: Base change gives a bijection between quotients of $L'$ that are finitely presented over $D'$ and flat over $B'$ and pairs of such quotients of its restrictions (over $D$ and flat over $B$, and over $C'$ and flat over $A'$). Their further restrictions to $C$ must be equal as quotients of $L'\otimes_{D'}C$. The inverse takes their pullback over that common quotient.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Identities for determinantal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an $n\times m$ matrix over $R$ and let $I_r(A)$ be the ideal of its $r$ by $r$ minors, with $I_0(A)=R$ and $I_r(A)=0$ above the smaller matrix dimension.
theorems.statement: The ideals decrease with $r$. Appending $n'$ rows yields a matrix $B$ with $I_{r+n'}(B)\subseteq I_r(A)$. For an $n\times n$ matrix $C$, $I_r(CA)\subseteq I_r(A)$. For a block diagonal matrix with blocks $A_1,A_2$, $I_r(A)=\sum_{i+j=r}I_i(A_1)I_j(A_2)$.
theorems.proof: The ideals decrease with $r$. Appending $n'$ rows yields a matrix $B$ with $I_{r+n'}(B)\subseteq I_r(A)$. For an $n\times n$ matrix $C$, $I_r(CA)\subseteq I_r(A)$. For a block diagonal matrix with blocks $A_1,A_2$, $I_r(A)=\sum_{i+j=r}I_i(A_1)I_j(A_2)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: The ideal of minors does not depend on the presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ a finite $R$-module. Present $M$ as the cokernel of a map from a possibly infinite rank free module to $R^n$. Fix $k\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The ideal of the $(n-k)$ by $(n-k)$ minors, using the unit ideal when $k\geq n$, depends only on $M$ and $k$.
theorems.proof: The ideal of the $(n-k)$ by $(n-k)$ minors, using the unit ideal when $k\geq n$, depends only on $M$ and $k$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Operations, annihilator and support for Fitting ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ a finite $R$-module.
theorems.statement: An $n$-element generating set forces $\operatorname{Fit}_n(M)=R$. Direct sums obey $\operatorname{Fit}_l(M\oplus N)=\sum_{i+j=l}\operatorname{Fit}_i(M)\operatorname{Fit}_j(N)$ for finite $N$. Arbitrary scalar extension extends the ideals. Finite presentation makes every Fitting ideal finitely generated. Surjections enlarge the ideals. Also $\operatorname{Fit}_0(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)$, its vanishing set is the support of $M$, and $\operatorname{Fit}_0(R/I)=I$ for every ideal $I$.
theorems.proof: An $n$-element generating set forces $\operatorname{Fit}_n(M)=R$. Direct sums obey $\operatorname{Fit}_l(M\oplus N)=\sum_{i+j=l}\operatorname{Fit}_i(M)\operatorname{Fit}_j(N)$ for finite $N$. Arbitrary scalar extension extends the ideals. Finite presentation makes every Fitting ideal finitely generated. Surjections enlarge the ideals. Also $\operatorname{Fit}_0(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)$, its vanishing set is the support of $M$, and $\operatorname{Fit}_0(R/I)=I$ for every ideal $I$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: All Fitting ideals of a finite free module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M=R^n$ with $n\geq0$.
theorems.statement: For $k\geq0$, the Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)$ is zero if $k<n$ and is $R$ if $k\geq n$.
theorems.proof: For $k\geq0$, the Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)$ is zero if $k<n$ and is $R$ if $k\geq n$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: First Fitting ideals for a sum of cyclic modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I,J$ be ideals of an arbitrary ring $R$.
theorems.statement: The zeroth Fitting ideal of $R/I$ is $I$. For $R/I\oplus R/J$, the zeroth is $IJ$ and the first is $I+J$.
theorems.proof: The zeroth Fitting ideal of $R/I$ is $I$. For $R/I\oplus R/J$, the zeroth is $IJ$ and the first is $I+J$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Fitting ideals and local generator bounds
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ a finite $R$-module. Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $k\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The following conditions are equivalent. The $k$th Fitting ideal is not contained in $\mathfrak p$. The fibre has dimension at most $k$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ can be generated by $k$ elements. The module $M_f$ can be generated by $k$ elements for some $f\notin\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: The following conditions are equivalent. The $k$th Fitting ideal is not contained in $\mathfrak p$. The fibre has dimension at most $k$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ can be generated by $k$ elements. The module $M_f$ can be generated by $k$ elements for some $f\notin\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A principal Fitting ideal bounds generators after removing f-annihilated elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local, let $M$ be finite and suppose $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)=(f)$ for $k\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The quotient $M/\ker(f:M\to M)$ can be generated by $k$ elements.
theorems.proof: The quotient $M/\ker(f:M\to M)$ can be generated by $k$ elements.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Splitting and projective dimension with two adjacent Fitting ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finitely presented over $R$ and suppose $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)=(f)$ where $f$ is a nonzerodivisor and $\operatorname{Fit}_{k-1}(M)=0$, with $k\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The modules $M$ and $M'=\ker(f:M\to M)$ have projective dimension at most one. The submodule $M'$ is the $f$-power torsion. The quotient is finite locally free of rank $k$ and the sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M/M'\to0$ splits.
theorems.proof: The modules $M$ and $M'=\ker(f:M\to M)$ have projective dimension at most one. The submodule $M'$ is the $f$-power torsion. The quotient is finite locally free of rank $k$ and the sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M/M'\to0$ splits.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting a unit after étale extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Let $\bar u$ be a unit of $A/I$.
theorems.statement: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. There is a unit $u'\in A'$ lifting $\bar u$. One may localize $A$ at a lift of $\bar u$.
theorems.proof: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. There is a unit $u'\in A'$ lifting $\bar u$. One may localize $A$ at a lift of $\bar u$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting an idempotent after étale extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Fix an idempotent $\bar e\in A/I$.
theorems.statement: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. There is an idempotent $e'\in A'$ lifting $\bar e$. A product of suitable principal localizations separates the two factors determined by $\bar e$.
theorems.proof: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. There is an idempotent $e'\in A'$ lifting $\bar e$. A product of suitable principal localizations separates the two factors determined by $\bar e$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting a finite disjoint open cover after étale extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Give $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ a finite disjoint open cover indexed by a fixed finite set.
theorems.statement: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. The given cover lifts to a disjoint open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ with the same index set.
theorems.proof: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. The given cover lifts to a disjoint open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ with the same index set.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Principal étale neighbourhood of the closed locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be any ring map and $J\subset B$ an ideal. Assume the map is étale at every prime of $V(J)$.
theorems.statement: Some $g\in B$ maps to a unit in $B/J$ and makes $A\to B_g$ étale.
theorems.proof: Some $g\in B$ maps to a unit in $B/J$ and makes $A\to B_g$ étale.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting comaximal monic factors after étale extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Let $f\in A[T]$ be monic and factor its image in $(A/I)[T]$ into two comaximal monic factors.
theorems.statement: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. The specified factorization lifts to a monic factorization over $A'$.
theorems.proof: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. The specified factorization lifts to a monic factorization over $A'$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Étale lifting of a factorization with a unit leading coefficient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Let $f\in A[T]$ be monic and factor its reduction as $\bar g\bar h$. Assume $\bar g,\bar h$ generate the unit ideal and the leading coefficient of $\bar g$ is invertible in $A/I$.
theorems.statement: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. There are lifts $g',h'\in A'[T]$ with $f=g'h'$.
theorems.proof: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. There are lifts $g',h'\in A'[T]$ with $f=g'h'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A ring element separating two disjoint closed loci
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $I\subset R$, $J\subset S$ ideals. Suppose the closure of the image of $V(J)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is disjoint from $V(I)$.
theorems.statement: There is $f\in R$ with $f$ congruent to $1$ modulo $I$ and with image in $J$. In fact the closure in the hypothesis is $V(J\cap R)$, where $J\cap R$ denotes the inverse image, hence the two ideals are comaximal.
theorems.proof: There is $f\in R$ with $f$ congruent to $1$ modulo $I$ and with image in $J$. In fact the closure in the hypothesis is $V(J\cap R)$, where $J\cap R$ denotes the inverse image, hence the two ideals are comaximal.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Monic annihilator of an element idempotent modulo an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Let $A\to B$ be integral and let $b\in B$ map to an idempotent in $B/IB$.
theorems.statement: There is a monic $f\in A[T]$ annihilating $b$ and reducing to $T^d(T-1)^d$ modulo $I$ for some $d\geq1$.
theorems.proof: There is a monic $f\in A[T]$ annihilating $b$ and reducing to $T^d(T-1)^d$ modulo $I$ for some $d\geq1$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étale base change lifts an idempotent in an integral algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Let $A\to B$ be integral and $\bar e\in B/IB$ be idempotent.
theorems.statement: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. There is an idempotent $e'\in B\otimes_A A'$ lifting $\bar e$.
theorems.proof: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. There is an idempotent $e'\in B\otimes_A A'$ lifting $\bar e$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Étale lifting of a finite projective module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Let $\bar P$ be finite projective over $A/I$.
theorems.statement: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. A finite projective $A'$-module $P'$ exists whose reduction is isomorphic to $\bar P$.
theorems.proof: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. A finite projective $A'$-module $P'$ exists whose reduction is isomorphic to $\bar P$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The naive cotangent complex of a symmetric algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to K\to A^m\to M\to0$ be exact over $A$ and $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A^*(M)$. Use the induced polynomial presentation $\alpha:A[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to C$.
theorems.statement: The resulting complex $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ is $K\otimes_A C\to\bigoplus_{j=1}^m C\,\mathrm d y_j$ in homological degrees one and zero. Its cokernel is $\Omega_{C/A}=M\otimes_A C$.
theorems.proof: The resulting complex $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ is $K\otimes_A C\to\bigoplus_{j=1}^m C\,\mathrm d y_j$ in homological degrees one and zero. Its cokernel is $\Omega_{C/A}=M\otimes_A C$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Smoothness of a symmetric algebra characterizes finite projectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring, $M$ an $A$-module, and $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A^*(M)$.
theorems.statement: The structural map $A\to C$ is smooth exactly when $M$ is finite projective over $A$.
theorems.proof: The structural map $A\to C$ is smooth exactly when $M$ is finite projective over $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étale neighbourhoods lift sections of a smooth algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in a ring $A$. Let $B$ be a smooth $A$-algebra with an $A$-algebra map $B\to A/I$.
theorems.statement: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. The map $B\to A/I$ lifts to an $A$-algebra map $B\to A'$.
theorems.proof: There is an étale map $A\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$. The map $B\to A/I$ lifts to an $A$-algebra map $B\to A'$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Reduction modulo a locally nilpotent ideal preserves étale algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a pair with $I$ locally nilpotent.
theorems.statement: The pair is henselian, and $B\mapsto B/IB$ is an equivalence between the categories of étale algebras over $A$ and $A/I$.
theorems.proof: The pair is henselian, and $B\mapsto B/IB$ is an equivalence between the categories of étale algebras over $A$ and $A/I$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Kernels of projections from a nilpotent-transition inverse limit are henselian
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$ for an inverse sequence of rings whose transition maps are surjections with locally nilpotent kernels.
theorems.statement: For each index $n$, with $I_n=\ker(A\to A_n)$, the pair $(A,I_n)$ is henselian.
theorems.proof: For each index $n$, with $I_n=\ker(A\to A_n)$, the pair $(A,I_n)$ is henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: An integral closure captures a finite factor modulo an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a pair, $A\to B$ finite type, and $B/IB=C_1\times C_2$, where $C_1$ is finite over $A/I$. Write $B'$ for the integral closure of the image of $A$ in $B$.
theorems.statement: There is a factorization $B'/IB'=C_1\times C'_2$ compatible with that of $B/IB$. For some $g\in B'$ mapping to $(1,0)$ in this decomposition, $B'_g\to B_g$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: There is a factorization $B'/IB'=C_1\times C'_2$ compatible with that of $B/IB$. For some $g\in B'$ mapping to $(1,0)$ in this decomposition, $B'_g\to B_g$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Equivalent criteria for henselian pairs and unique Gabber roots
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a ring–ideal pair.
theorems.statement: Henselianity, lifting sections of every étale algebra, and bijectivity on idempotents in every finite algebra or in every integral algebra are equivalent. They are also equivalent to $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$ together with Gabber's root condition. Under this last criterion each specified root in $1+I$ is unique.
theorems.proof: Henselianity, lifting sections of every étale algebra, and bijectivity on idempotents in every finite algebra or in every integral algebra are equivalent. They are also equivalent to $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$ together with Gabber's root condition. Under this last criterion each specified root in $1+I$ is unique.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselianity depends on the radical of the ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I,J\subset A$ be ideals with $\sqrt I=\sqrt J$.
theorems.statement: The pair $(A,I)$ is henselian if and only if $(A,J)$ is henselian.
theorems.proof: The pair $(A,I)$ is henselian if and only if $(A,J)$ is henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral base change of a henselian pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be henselian and $A\to B$ an integral map.
theorems.statement: The target pair $(B,IB)$ is henselian.
theorems.proof: The target pair $(B,IB)$ is henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselianity along a nested pair of ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq J\subseteq A$ be ideals.
theorems.statement: The pair $(A,J)$ is henselian exactly when both $(A,I)$ and $(A/I,J/I)$ are henselian.
theorems.proof: The pair $(A,J)$ is henselian exactly when both $(A,I)$ and $(A/I,J/I)$ are henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The sum of two henselian ideals is henselian
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $(A,I)$ and $(A,I')$ are henselian pairs in the same ring.
theorems.statement: Then $(A,I+I')$ is a henselian pair.
theorems.proof: Then $(A,I+I')$ is a henselian pair.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Products of henselian pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Take a set-indexed family of pairs $(A_j,I_j)$.
theorems.statement: The pair $(\prod_j A_j,\prod_j I_j)$ is henselian if and only if each $(A_j,I_j)$ is henselian.
theorems.proof: The pair $(\prod_j A_j,\prod_j I_j)$ is henselian if and only if each $(A_j,I_j)$ is henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Inverse limits of henselian pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Let $J$ be a preordered set and let $(A_j,I_j)_{j\in J}$ be an inverse system of henselian pairs.
theorems.statement: The pair $(\varprojlim_j A_j,\varprojlim_j I_j)$ is henselian.
theorems.proof: The pair $(\varprojlim_j A_j,\varprojlim_j I_j)$ is henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Filtered colimits of henselian pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A_j,I_j)$ be a directed system of henselian pairs.
theorems.statement: The colimit pair $(\operatorname{colim}_j A_j,\operatorname{colim}_j I_j)$ is henselian.
theorems.proof: The colimit pair $(\operatorname{colim}_j A_j,\operatorname{colim}_j I_j)$ is henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Existence of a largest henselian ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be any ring.
theorems.statement: There is a largest ideal $I$ such that $(A,I)$ is henselian. Sums and filtered unions of henselian ideals stay henselian, so one takes the sum of all of them.
theorems.proof: There is a largest ideal $I$ such that $(A,I)$ is henselian. Sums and filtered unions of henselian ideals stay henselian, so one takes the sum of all of them.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A henselian pair cuts a connected locus from each prime subscheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be henselian and let $\mathfrak p$ be any prime of $A$.
theorems.statement: The closed subset $V(\mathfrak p+I)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is connected. The quotient $A/\mathfrak p$ is a domain, and the descended henselian pair gives a bijection on idempotents.
theorems.proof: The closed subset $V(\mathfrak p+I)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is connected. The quotient $A/\mathfrak p$ is a domain, and the descended henselian pair gives a bijection on idempotents.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Flatness and preservation of finite adic quotients under henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a pair and $(A^h,I^h)$ its henselization.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to A^h$ is flat, $I^h=IA^h$, and $A/I^n\to A^h/I^nA^h$ is an isomorphism for each $n\geq1$.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to A^h$ is flat, $I^h=IA^h$, and $A/I^n\to A^h/I^nA^h$ is an isomorphism for each $n\geq1$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Compatibility with henselization of local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be local.
theorems.statement: The ring of the henselization of the pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is the local henselization of $A$, with ideal $\mathfrak mA^h$.
theorems.proof: The ring of the henselization of the pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is the local henselization of $A$, with ideal $\mathfrak mA^h$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselization and completion of a Noetherian pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subset A$ an ideal.
theorems.statement: The henselization $A^h$ is Noetherian and its $IA^h$-adic completion is canonically the $I$-adic completion $\widehat A$ of $A$. Both maps in $A\to A^h\to\widehat A$ are flat, and the second is faithfully flat.
theorems.proof: The henselization $A^h$ is Noetherian and its $IA^h$-adic completion is canonically the $I$-adic completion $\widehat A$ of $A$. Both maps in $A\to A^h\to\widehat A$ are flat, and the second is faithfully flat.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselization commutes with filtered colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)=\operatorname{colim}_j(A_j,I_j)$ be a filtered colimit of pairs.
theorems.statement: The natural map from the colimit of $(A_j^h,I_j^h)$ to $(A^h,I^h)$ is an isomorphism of pairs.
theorems.proof: The natural map from the colimit of $(A_j^h,I_j^h)$ to $(A^h,I^h)$ is an isomorphism of pairs.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The henselized ring depends only on the radical
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I,J$ be ideals in $A$ with $\sqrt I=\sqrt J$.
theorems.statement: The two henselized rings for $(A,I)$ and $(A,J)$ are canonically isomorphic over $A$. Their distinguished ideals are the respective extensions of $I$ and $J$.
theorems.proof: The two henselized rings for $(A,I)$ and $(A,J)$ are canonically isomorphic over $A$. Their distinguished ideals are the respective extensions of $I$ and $J$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselization commutes with integral base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)\to(B,J)$ be a map of pairs with $A\to B$ integral and $\sqrt J=\sqrt{IB}$.
theorems.statement: The natural map $A^h\otimes_A B\to B^h$ is an isomorphism of rings.
theorems.proof: The natural map $A^h\otimes_A B\to B^h$ is an isomorphism of rings.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselization along pairwise comaximal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I_1,\dots,I_n$ be pairwise comaximal ideals of $A$, with $n\geq1$. Let $A^h$ henselize the pair with ideal $\bigcap_i I_i$, and let $A_i^h$ henselize the pair with ideal $I_i$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $A^h\to\prod_{i=1}^n A_i^h$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $A^h\to\prod_{i=1}^n A_i^h$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Finite projectives over a henselian pair and its reduction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,I)$ be henselian.
theorems.statement: Reduction $P\mapsto P/IP$ induces a bijection on isomorphism classes of finite projective modules over $R$ and $R/I$.
theorems.proof: Reduction $P\mapsto P/IP$ induces a bijection on isomorphism classes of finite projective modules over $R$ and $R/I$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Finite étale algebras are invariant under henselian reduction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair.
theorems.statement: Reduction $B\mapsto B/IB$ gives an equivalence of the categories of finite étale algebras over $A$ and $A/I$.
theorems.proof: Reduction $B\mapsto B/IB$ gives an equivalence of the categories of finite étale algebras over $A$ and $A/I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smooth algebras lift against henselian reductions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be smooth, let $A$ be an $R$-algebra, and let $(A,I)$ be henselian.
theorems.statement: Every $R$-algebra map $S\to A/I$ lifts to an $R$-algebra map $S\to A$.
theorems.proof: Every $R$-algebra map $S\to A/I$ lifts to an $R$-algebra map $S\to A$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Finite projectives from a compatible inverse system
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$ along surjective transition maps with locally nilpotent kernels. Suppose $M_1$ is finite projective over $A_1$, the modules $M_n$ are finite flat over $A_n$, and the transition maps identify $M_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n$ with $M_n$.
theorems.statement: The inverse limit $M=\varprojlim_n M_n$ is finite projective over $A$ and its scalar extensions to $A_n$ recover $M_n$.
theorems.proof: The inverse limit $M=\varprojlim_n M_n$ is finite projective over $A$ and its scalar extensions to $A_n$ recover $M_n$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Depth formula for a tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module and $N$ a finite $S$-module flat over $R$. Set $F=S/\mathfrak m_RS$.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{depth}_S(M\otimes_R N)=\operatorname{depth}_R(M)+\operatorname{depth}_F(N/\mathfrak m_RN)$, with $+\infty$ for the depth of a zero module.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{depth}_S(M\otimes_R N)=\operatorname{depth}_R(M)+\operatorname{depth}_F(N/\mathfrak m_RN)$, with $+\infty$ for the depth of a zero module.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Depth formula for flat local maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, with closed fibre $F=S/\mathfrak m_RS$.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{depth}(S)=\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(F)$. Apply the module formula with $M=R$ and $N=S$.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{depth}(S)=\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(F)$. Apply the module formula with $M=R$ and $N=S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay criterion for a flat local homomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, with closed fibre $F=S/\mathfrak m_RS$.
theorems.statement: The target $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when both $R$ and $F$ are Cohen–Macaulay. The local depth and dimension formulas add the respective invariants, and depth is bounded above by dimension.
theorems.proof: The target $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when both $R$ and $F$ are Cohen–Macaulay. The local depth and dimension formulas add the respective invariants, and depth is bounded above by dimension.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Serre S ascends with Serre S fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat with $R$ and $S$ Noetherian. Fix an integer $k\geq 0$.
theorems.statement: If $R$ and each $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ satisfy $(S_k)$, then $S$ satisfies $(S_k)$. Apply the local depth and dimension formulas at each prime of $S$.
theorems.proof: If $R$ and each $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ satisfy $(S_k)$, then $S$ satisfies $(S_k)$. Apply the local depth and dimension formulas at each prime of $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Serre R ascends with Serre R fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat with $R$ and $S$ Noetherian. Fix an integer $k\geq 0$.
theorems.statement: If $R$ and each $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ satisfy $(R_k)$, then $S$ satisfies $(R_k)$. At primes of height at most $k$, the flat local dimension formula bounds both local dimensions by $k$.
theorems.proof: If $R$ and each $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ satisfy $(R_k)$, then $S$ satisfies $(R_k)$. At primes of height at most $k$, the flat local dimension formula bounds both local dimensions by $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Serre S descends along faithfully flat maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be faithfully flat with $S$ Noetherian. Fix an integer $k\geq 0$.
theorems.statement: If $S$ satisfies $(S_k)$, then $R$ does as well. For each source prime, take a prime minimal over its extension in the corresponding localized fibre, where the fibre local ring has dimension and depth zero.
theorems.proof: If $S$ satisfies $(S_k)$, then $R$ does as well. For each source prime, take a prime minimal over its extension in the corresponding localized fibre, where the fibre local ring has dimension and depth zero.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Serre R descends along faithfully flat maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be faithfully flat with $S$ Noetherian. Fix an integer $k\geq 0$.
theorems.statement: If $S$ satisfies $(R_k)$, then $R$ does as well. Lift each source prime to a prime minimal in its fibre, preserving the local dimension by the flat local dimension formula, and use descent of regularity.
theorems.proof: If $S$ satisfies $(R_k)$, then $R$ does as well. Lift each source prime to a prime minimal in its fibre, preserving the local dimension by the flat local dimension formula, and use descent of regularity.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Field-extension tests for geometric normality
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an algebra over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: Geometric normality is equivalent to normality after every finitely generated extension, after every finite purely inseparable extension, and after base change to $k^{\mathrm{perf}}$. Each test is an alternative criterion.
theorems.proof: Geometric normality is equivalent to normality after every finitely generated extension, after every finite purely inseparable extension, and after base change to $k^{\mathrm{perf}}$. Each test is an alternative criterion.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localization preserves geometric normality
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an algebra over a field $k$. Fix a multiplicative subset of $A$.
theorems.statement: Localizing after a field base change is the same as base-changing the localization. Normality is checked at prime localizations.
theorems.proof: Localizing after a field base change is the same as base-changing the localization. Normality is checked at prime localizations.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Separable field extensions are geometrically normal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be a separable extension of fields in the sense of Stacks 030I.
theorems.statement: For every field extension $k'/k$, the algebra $K\otimes_k k'$ is a normal ring.
theorems.proof: For every field extension $k'/k$, the algebra $K\otimes_k k'$ is a normal ring.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Tensor product with a geometrically normal algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A,B$ be $k$-algebras for a field $k$. Assume $A$ is geometrically normal over $k$ and $B$ is a normal ring.
theorems.statement: The ring $A\otimes_k B$ is normal.
theorems.proof: The ring $A\otimes_k B$ is normal.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Geometric normality over a separable algebraic base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k'/k$ be separable algebraic and $A$ a $k'$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The algebra $A$ is geometrically normal over $k$ if and only if it is geometrically normal over $k'.$
theorems.proof: The algebra $A$ is geometrically normal over $k$ if and only if it is geometrically normal over $k'.$

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Field-extension tests for geometric regularity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an algebra over a field $k$. Assume $A$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: Testing regularity of $k'\otimes_k A$ for every finitely generated field extension $k'/k$ is equivalent to testing every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$.
theorems.proof: Testing regularity of $k'\otimes_k A$ for every finitely generated field extension $k'/k$ is equivalent to testing every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Geometric regularity descends by faithful flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a faithfully flat map of algebras over a field $k$ and suppose $B$ is geometrically regular over $k$.
theorems.statement: Then $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$. After any finite purely inseparable base extension, faithful flatness persists and regularity descends.
theorems.proof: Then $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$. After any finite purely inseparable base extension, faithful flatness persists and regularity descends.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Geometric regularity ascends by smoothness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a smooth map of algebras over a field $k$ and suppose $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$.
theorems.statement: Then $B$ is geometrically regular over $k$. Base change preserves smoothness, so ordinary smooth ascent applies after each finite purely inseparable extension.
theorems.proof: Then $B$ is geometrically regular over $k$. Base change preserves smoothness, so ordinary smooth ascent applies after each finite purely inseparable extension.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Geometric regularity over a directed union of subfields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a $k$-algebra with $k$ a directed union of subfields $k_i$. Suppose $A$ is geometrically regular over every $k_i$.
theorems.statement: Then $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$.
theorems.proof: Then $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Geometric regularity over a separable algebraic base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k'/k$ be separable algebraic and $A$ a $k'$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The algebra $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$ if and only if it is geometrically regular over $k'.$
theorems.proof: The algebra $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$ if and only if it is geometrically regular over $k'.$

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.name: Tensor product of field extensions is Cohen–Macaulay
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ and $L/k$ be extensions of a field, with at least one finitely generated as a field extension.
theorems.statement: The ring $K\otimes_k L$ is Noetherian and Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.proof: The ring $K\otimes_k L$ is Noetherian and Cohen–Macaulay.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local Cohen–Macaulayness under a field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a Noetherian $k$-algebra and $K/k$ a finitely generated field extension. Set $S_K=K\otimes_k S$. Fix primes $\mathfrak q_K$ of $S_K$ and $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ with $\mathfrak q_K\cap S=\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: The local ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when $(S_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is. Apply the flat local Cohen–Macaulay criterion and the Cohen–Macaulayness of the localized field tensor product in the fibre.
theorems.proof: The local ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when $(S_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is. Apply the flat local Cohen–Macaulay criterion and the Cohen–Macaulayness of the localized field tensor product in the fibre.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flat modules of finite presentation at a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be of finite presentation, $M$ a finitely presented $S$-module flat over $R$, and $R=\varinjlim R_i$ a directed colimit.
theorems.statement: There is a stage with a finitely presented algebra $S_i$ over $R_i$ and a finitely presented $S_i$-module $M_i$ flat over $R_i$ that base-change to $S$ and $M$. In any compatible presentation by finitely presented data and scalar extension along the transitions, the modules become flat over the respective base rings at all sufficiently large stages. One can also choose a finite type model over a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra, with the module finite and flat over that base.
theorems.proof: There is a stage with a finitely presented algebra $S_i$ over $R_i$ and a finitely presented $S_i$-module $M_i$ flat over $R_i$ that base-change to $S$ and $M$. In any compatible presentation by finitely presented data and scalar extension along the transitions, the modules become flat over the respective base rings at all sufficiently large stages. One can also choose a finite type model over a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra, with the module finite and flat over that base.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A finitely presented faithfully flat map descends
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A\to B$ be ring homomorphisms and assume $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and of finite presentation.
theorems.statement: There is a finitely presented $R$-algebra $A_0$ with a map to $A$, and a faithfully flat finitely presented $A_0$-algebra $B_0$ such that $A\otimes_{A_0}B_0\cong B$ as $A$-algebras.
theorems.proof: There is a finitely presented $R$-algebra $A_0$ with a map to $A$, and a faithfully flat finitely presented $A_0$-algebra $B_0$ such that $A\otimes_{A_0}B_0\cong B$ as $A$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite maps descend to a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be a directed colimit of rings. Fix an index $0$ and a homomorphism $B_0\to C_0$ of $A_0$-algebras. Suppose $B_0\to C_0$ is of finite type and its base change to $A$ satisfies the named property.
theorems.statement: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.
theorems.proof: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.

theorems.name: Surjective maps descend to a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be a directed colimit of rings. Fix an index $0$ and a homomorphism $B_0\to C_0$ of $A_0$-algebras. Suppose $B_0\to C_0$ is of finite type and its base change to $A$ satisfies the named property.
theorems.statement: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.
theorems.proof: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.

theorems.statement: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.

theorems.name: Isomorphisms descend to a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be a directed colimit of rings. Fix an index $0$ and a homomorphism $B_0\to C_0$ of $A_0$-algebras. Suppose $B_0\to C_0$ is of finite presentation and its base change to $A$ satisfies the named property.
theorems.statement: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.
theorems.proof: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.

theorems.name: Étale maps descend to a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be a directed colimit of rings. Fix an index $0$ and a homomorphism $B_0\to C_0$ of $A_0$-algebras. Suppose $B_0\to C_0$ is of finite presentation and its base change to $A$ satisfies the named property.
theorems.statement: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.
theorems.proof: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smooth maps descend to a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be a directed colimit of rings. Fix an index $0$ and a homomorphism $B_0\to C_0$ of $A_0$-algebras. Suppose $B_0\to C_0$ is of finite presentation and its base change to $A$ satisfies the named property.
theorems.statement: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.
theorems.proof: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Syntomic maps descend to a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be a directed colimit of rings. Fix an index $0$ and a homomorphism $B_0\to C_0$ of $A_0$-algebras. Suppose $B_0\to C_0$ is of finite presentation and its base change to $A$ satisfies the named property.
theorems.statement: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.
theorems.proof: For some $i\geq0$, the base change $A_i\otimes_{A_0} B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0} C_0$ has the same property.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Relative global complete intersection descends to a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be a directed colimit of rings. Fix an index $0$ and a homomorphism $B_0\to C_0$ of $A_0$-algebras. Suppose $C_0$ is finitely presented over $B_0$ and the base change over $A$ is a relative global complete intersection.
theorems.statement: The map $A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ is a relative global complete intersection for some $i\geq 0$.
theorems.proof: The map $A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ is a relative global complete intersection for some $i\geq 0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A quasi-finite faithfully flat refinement of a finitely presented faithfully flat map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be faithfully flat and of finite presentation.
theorems.statement: There is an $R$-algebra map $S\to S'$ with $R\to S'$ quasi-finite, faithfully flat and of finite presentation. The three properties are assertions about $R\to S'.$
theorems.proof: There is an $R$-algebra map $S\to S'$ with $R\to S'$ quasi-finite, faithfully flat and of finite presentation. The three properties are assertions about $R\to S'.$

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Multiplying the last terms of two regularities
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module, $\mathbf f$ a common initial sequence and $g,h\in R$.
theorems.statement: If $(\mathbf f,g)$ and $(\mathbf f,h)$ are both $M$-$H_1$-regular, then $(\mathbf f,gh)$ is $M$-$H_1$-regular. The same implication holds for $M$-Koszul-regularity.
theorems.proof: If $(\mathbf f,g)$ and $(\mathbf f,h)$ are both $M$-$H_1$-regular, then $(\mathbf f,gh)$ is $M$-$H_1$-regular. The same implication holds for $M$-Koszul-regularity.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Flat base change preserves Koszul and H₁ regularity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $M$ an $R$-module, $N=M\otimes_R S$ and $\mathbf f$ a finite sequence in $R$.
theorems.statement: The image sequence on N satisfies each of the two regularity conditions that the original sequence satisfies on M. Koszul homology commutes with the flat extension of scalars.
theorems.proof: The image sequence on N satisfies each of the two regularity conditions that the original sequence satisfies on M. Koszul homology commutes with the flat extension of scalars.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Four equivalent regularity tests in the Noetherian local setting
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local, $M$ a nonzero finite $R$-module and $\mathbf f$ a finite sequence in $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: Regularity, Koszul regularity, $H_1$-regularity and quasi-regularity on $M$ are equivalent. Taking $M=R$ gives the equivalence for sequences in $R$.
theorems.proof: Regularity, Koszul regularity, $H_1$-regularity and quasi-regularity on $M$ are equivalent. Taking $M=R$ gives the equivalence for sequences in $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Intersection with an ideal from regularity in a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subset A$ be an ideal, and $\mathbf g$ a sequence whose image is $H_1$-regular in $A/I$.
theorems.statement: If $J=(\mathbf g)$, then $I\cap J=IJ$. The vanishing of first Koszul homology in the quotient gives the needed injection on degree-zero homology.
theorems.proof: If $J=(\mathbf g)$, then $I\cap J=IJ$. The vanishing of first Koszul homology in the quotient gives the needed injection on degree-zero homology.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Conormal intersection for nested ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subset J\subset A$ and assume $J/I$ is generated by an $H_1$-regular sequence over $A/I$.
theorems.statement: Then $I\cap J^2=IJ$.
theorems.proof: Then $I\cap J^2=IJ$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Concatenating a quasi-regular prefix and an H₁-regular quotient sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring, with sequences $\mathbf f$ and $\mathbf g$ in $A$. Write $I=(\mathbf f)$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ for the image of the second sequence in $A/I$.
theorems.statement: If $\mathbf f$ is quasi-regular and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ is $H_1$-regular, then $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ is quasi-regular.
theorems.proof: If $\mathbf f$ is quasi-regular and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ is $H_1$-regular, then $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ is quasi-regular.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Concatenation of H₁-regular sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring, with sequences $\mathbf f$ and $\mathbf g$ in $A$. Write $I=(\mathbf f)$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ for the image of the second sequence in $A/I$.
theorems.statement: If $\mathbf f$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ are $H_1$-regular over their respective rings, then $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ is $H_1$-regular in $A$.
theorems.proof: If $\mathbf f$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ are $H_1$-regular over their respective rings, then $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ is $H_1$-regular in $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Truncating an H₁-regular sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring, with sequences $\mathbf f$ and $\mathbf g$ in $A$. Write $I=(\mathbf f)$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ for the image of the second sequence in $A/I$.
theorems.statement: If $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ is $H_1$-regular over $A$, its tail $\bar{\mathbf g}$ is $H_1$-regular over $A/I$.
theorems.proof: If $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ is $H_1$-regular over $A$, its tail $\bar{\mathbf g}$ is $H_1$-regular over $A/I$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Concatenation of Koszul-regular sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring, with sequences $\mathbf f$ and $\mathbf g$ in $A$. Write $I=(\mathbf f)$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ for the image of the second sequence in $A/I$.
theorems.statement: If $\mathbf f$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ are Koszul-regular over their respective rings, then $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ is Koszul-regular in $A$.
theorems.proof: If $\mathbf f$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ are Koszul-regular over their respective rings, then $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ is Koszul-regular in $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Truncating a Koszul-regular sequence with a Koszul-regular prefix
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring, with sequences $\mathbf f$ and $\mathbf g$ in $A$. Write $I=(\mathbf f)$ and $\bar{\mathbf g}$ for the image of the second sequence in $A/I$.
theorems.statement: If both $\mathbf f$ and $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ are Koszul-regular over $A$, then $\bar{\mathbf g}$ is Koszul-regular over $A/I$.
theorems.proof: If both $\mathbf f$ and $(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)$ are Koszul-regular over $A$, then $\bar{\mathbf g}$ is Koszul-regular over $A/I$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Regularity is independent of generators at a fixed length
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ generate $I\subset R$. Assume $I$ has another generating sequence of length $r$.
theorems.statement: If that sequence is quasi-regular, $H_1$-regular or Koszul-regular, then $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ satisfies the same condition.
theorems.proof: If that sequence is quasi-regular, $H_1$-regular or Koszul-regular, then $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ satisfies the same condition.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A generic linear combination is a nonzerodivisor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in R$. Assume the map $R\to R^n$, $x\mapsto(xa_1,\ldots,xa_n)$, is injective.
theorems.statement: Then $\sum_i a_iT_i$ is a nonzerodivisor in $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$.
theorems.proof: Then $\sum_i a_iT_i$ is a nonzerodivisor in $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Changing Koszul-regular generators to a regular sequence after smooth extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathbf f=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ be Koszul-regular in $R$ and generate a proper ideal. Let $S$ be the polynomial algebra on $t_{ij}$ for $i\leq j$ with all diagonal variables inverted.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to S$ is smooth and faithfully flat. The elements $g_i=\sum_{j\geq i}t_{ij}f_j$ form a regular sequence and generate $(\mathbf f)S$.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to S$ is smooth and faithfully flat. The elements $g_i=\sum_{j\geq i}t_{ij}f_j$ form a regular sequence and generate $(\mathbf f)S$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Jacobson rings and density of closed points
theorems.hypotheses: Give $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: The ring is Jacobson precisely when $X$ is a Jacobson space. In each closed subset $Z$, the points of $Z$ closed in $X$ are dense in $Z$. For $Z=V(I)$ this identifies the radical of $I$ with the intersection of the maximal ideals containing $I$.
theorems.proof: The ring is Jacobson precisely when $X$ is a Jacobson space. In each closed subset $Z$, the points of $Z$ closed in $X$ are dense in $Z$. For $Z=V(I)$ this identifies the radical of $I$ with the intersection of the maximal ideals containing $I$.
refs: Stacks 01P3 · Jacobson ring iff its spectrum is Jacobson

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Isolated nonclosed points detect failure of the Jacobson property
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a ring $R$ and use $D(f)$ for the principal open defined by $f$.
theorems.statement: If $R$ fails to be Jacobson, there are a nonmaximal prime $\mathfrak p$ and $f\notin\mathfrak p$ with $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\}$ and $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ a field. For a Jacobson ring every such pair with $\mathfrak p$ nonmaximal and $f\notin\mathfrak p$ gives an infinite intersection $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)$.
theorems.proof: If $R$ fails to be Jacobson, there are a nonmaximal prime $\mathfrak p$ and $f\notin\mathfrak p$ with $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\}$ and $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ a field. For a Jacobson ring every such pair with $\mathfrak p$ nonmaximal and $f\notin\mathfrak p$ gives an infinite intersection $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A Jacobson criterion for one-dimensional Noetherian domains
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a Noetherian domain has infinitely many maximal ideals and each nonzero prime is maximal.
theorems.statement: Every prime is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it. For the zero prime, each nonzero element belongs to only finitely many maximal ideals since these are minimal over its principal ideal. In particular $\mathbf Z$ is Jacobson.
theorems.proof: Every prime is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it. For the zero prime, each nonzero element belongs to only finitely many maximal ideals since these are minimal over its principal ideal. In particular $\mathbf Z$ is Jacobson.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Algebraic residue extension over a closed point
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to S$ take a prime $\mathfrak q$ with maximal contraction $\mathfrak m$ and algebraic residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak m)$.
theorems.statement: Then $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. The domain $S/\mathfrak q$ lies between the field $R/\mathfrak m$ and an algebraic extension of that field, so each nonzero element has an inverse in the domain.
theorems.proof: Then $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. The domain $S/\mathfrak q$ lies between the field $R/\mathfrak m$ and an algebraic extension of that field, so each nonzero element has an inverse in the domain.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Cardinality bound on invertible polynomial operators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T$ be an endomorphism of a nonzero $k$-vector space $V$, with $\dim_k V<|k|$.
theorems.statement: Some monic $P\in k[t]$ has $P(T)$ noninvertible. Otherwise the polynomial action would extend to a $k(t)$-vector space structure, whereas the fractions $1/(t-a)$ for $a\in k$ are linearly independent over $k$.
theorems.proof: Some monic $P\in k[t]$ has $P(T)$ noninvertible. Otherwise the polynomial action would extend to a $k(t)$-vector space structure, whereas the fractions $1/(t-a)$ for $a\in k$ are linearly independent over $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Nullstellensatz with a cardinal bound
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a $k$-algebra $S$ admits a set of algebra generators indexed by $I$, where $k$ is a field and $|I|<|k|$.
theorems.statement: The ring $S$ is Jacobson and $\kappa(\mathfrak m)/k$ is algebraic for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset S$. Finite generating families are covered by the ordinary Nullstellensatz even over finite fields.
theorems.proof: The ring $S$ is Jacobson and $\kappa(\mathfrak m)/k$ is algebraic for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset S$. Finite generating families are covered by the ordinary Nullstellensatz even over finite fields.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Countably many generators over a countable field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a countable field. Adjoin $x$ and one variable $u_f$ for each nonzero $f\in k[x]$.
theorems.statement: The quotient by all $fu_f-1$ is the field $k(x)$. Its kernel is maximal with transcendental residue extension over $k$. Equality of the two infinite cardinalities does not suffice for the algebraic-residue conclusion.
theorems.proof: The quotient by all $fu_f-1$ is the field $k(x)$. Its kernel is maximal with transcendental residue extension over $k$. Equality of the two infinite cardinalities does not suffice for the algebraic-residue conclusion.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Jacobson property after passing to a sufficiently large field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a $k$-algebra and $K/k$ a field extension with $|K|>|S|$.
theorems.statement: Then $S\otimes_kK$ is Jacobson and each maximal residue field is algebraic over $K$. The elements of $S$ supply a generating set of size strictly smaller than $|K|$.
theorems.proof: Then $S\otimes_kK$ is Jacobson and each maximal residue field is algebraic over $K$. The elements of $S$ supply a generating set of size strictly smaller than $|K|$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Jacobson rings on principal opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Jacobson and $f\in R$.
theorems.statement: The localization $R_f$ is Jacobson. Contraction identifies its maximal ideals with the maximal ideals of $R$ avoiding $f$.
theorems.proof: The localization $R_f$ is Jacobson. Contraction identifies its maximal ideals with the maximal ideals of $R$ avoiding $f$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Jacobson rings on closed subschemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of a Jacobson ring $R$.
theorems.statement: The quotient $R/I$ is Jacobson. Its maximal ideals correspond by inverse image to the maximal ideals of $R$ containing $I$.
theorems.proof: The quotient $R/I$ is Jacobson. Its maximal ideals correspond by inverse image to the maximal ideals of $R$ containing $I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A Jacobson subring of a finite type field algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a field $K$ contains a Jacobson ring $R$ and is finitely generated as an $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The subring $R$ is itself a field and $[K:R]$ is finite.
theorems.proof: The subring $R$ is itself a field and $[K:R]$ is finite.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite type algebras over the integers are Jacobson
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R$ is generated by finitely many elements as a $\mathbf Z$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Then $R$ is Jacobson, by permanence for finite type algebras applied to $\mathbf Z$.
theorems.proof: Then $R$ is Jacobson, by permanence for finite type algebras applied to $\mathbf Z$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Closed points and constructible images over Jacobson rings
theorems.hypotheses: Write $f:Y=\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ for a finite type map of Jacobson rings. Let $E\subset Y$ be constructible and use $A_0$ for the closed points of a subspace $A$.
theorems.statement: Then $f(E)_0=f(E_0)=X_0\cap f(E)$. Moreover $x\in f(E)$ precisely when $f(E_0)\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ is dense in $\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.proof: Then $f(E)_0=f(E_0)=X_0\cap f(E)$. Moreover $x\in f(E)$ precisely when $f(E_0)\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ is dense in $\overline{\{x\}}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Closed-point restriction commutes with constructible direct image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and Jacobson, $S$ finite type over $R$, and $f:Y=\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Give the closed-point sets $X_0,Y_0$ the subspace topology.
theorems.statement: Intersecting with closed points gives bijections between constructible subsets of $X$ and of $X_0$, and likewise for $Y$. These bijections commute with taking the image under $f$ and under the induced map $Y_0\to X_0$.
theorems.proof: Intersecting with closed points gives bijections between constructible subsets of $X$ and of $X_0$, and likewise for $Y$. These bijections commute with taking the image under $f$ and under the induced map $Y_0\to X_0$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Irreducible components of pairs of two-by-two matrices with zero product
theorems.hypotheses: Over an algebraically closed field $k$, let $X,Y$ be two $2\times2$ matrices of variables and impose the four entries of $XY=0$.
theorems.statement: The underlying algebraic set has three irreducible components. Two are $X=0$ and $Y=0$. The third consists of pairs satisfying $XY=0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(X),\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le1$. Its dense stratum has both ranks one and is one orbit under independent changes of bases in the three copies of $k^2$. Degenerating one or both rank-one maps to zero gives all boundary pairs with both ranks at most one.
theorems.proof: The underlying algebraic set has three irreducible components. Two are $X=0$ and $Y=0$. The third consists of pairs satisfying $XY=0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(X),\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le1$. Its dense stratum has both ranks one and is one orbit under independent changes of bases in the three copies of $k^2$. Degenerating one or both rank-one maps to zero gives all boundary pairs with both ranks at most one.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Rank components of the space of idempotent matrices
theorems.hypotheses: Over an algebraically closed field $k$, consider matrices $T$ of size $n$ cut out by $T^2=T$.
theorems.statement: For each $0\le r\le n$ the rank-$r$ locus is the conjugacy orbit of $\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0)$, hence irreducible. It is open and closed since its characteristic polynomial $t^{n-r}(t-1)^r$ separates it from the finitely many other orbits in every characteristic. These are exactly the irreducible components.
theorems.proof: For each $0\le r\le n$ the rank-$r$ locus is the conjugacy orbit of $\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0)$, hence irreducible. It is open and closed since its characteristic polynomial $t^{n-r}(t-1)^r$ separates it from the finitely many other orbits in every characteristic. These are exactly the irreducible components.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: A finite stable module certifies integrality
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $y\in S$. Suppose a finite $R$-submodule $M\subset S$ contains $1$ and satisfies $yM\subseteq M$.
theorems.statement: Multiplication by $y$ on $M$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $R$ by the determinant trick. Evaluation on $1$ proves that $y$ is integral over $R$.
theorems.proof: Multiplication by $y$ on $M$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $R$ by the determinant trick. Evaluation on $1$ proves that $y$ is integral over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A common finite subalgebra for finitely many integral elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ belong to an $R$-algebra $S$.
theorems.statement: All $s_i$ are integral over $R$ exactly when some $R$-subalgebra finite as an $R$-module contains them. For monic equations of degrees $d_i$, the monomials with exponents below the respective $d_i$ span the algebra they generate.
theorems.proof: All $s_i$ are integral over $R$ exactly when some $R$-subalgebra finite as an $R$-module contains them. For monic equations of degrees $d_i$, the monomials with exponents below the respective $d_i$ span the algebra they generate.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral elements form a subalgebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be any commutative $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The elements of $S$ integral over $R$ form an $R$-subalgebra. Any two integral elements lie in a common finite subalgebra, so their sum, difference and product are integral.
theorems.proof: The elements of $S$ integral over $R$ form an $R$-subalgebra. Any two integral elements lie in a common finite subalgebra, so their sum, difference and product are integral.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Integrality of an element in a finite product
theorems.hypotheses: Take finitely many ring maps $R_i\to S_i$ and $s=(s_i)\in\prod_i S_i$.
theorems.statement: The element $s$ is integral over $\prod_iR_i$ exactly when every $s_i$ is integral over $R_i$. Monic equations can be made of the same degree by multiplying by powers of the indeterminate.
theorems.proof: The element $s$ is integral over $\prod_iR_i$ exactly when every $s_i$ is integral over $R_i$. Monic equations can be made of the same degree by multiplying by powers of the indeterminate.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral closure in finite products
theorems.hypotheses: For finitely many ring maps $R_i\to S_i$, write $C_i$ for the integral closure of $R_i$ in $S_i$.
theorems.statement: The integral closure for $\prod_i R_i\to\prod_i S_i$ is $\prod_i C_i$. In particular the product map is an integrally closed inclusion precisely when all the component maps are integrally closed inclusions.
theorems.proof: The integral closure for $\prod_i R_i\to\prod_i S_i$ is $\prod_i C_i$. In particular the product map is an integrally closed inclusion precisely when all the component maps are integrally closed inclusions.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localization of integral closure
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ have integral closure $C$ in $B$. Take a multiplicative subset $U\subset A$.
theorems.statement: Inside $U^{-1}B$, the integral closure of $U^{-1}A$ equals $U^{-1}C$. Clear the finitely many denominators in a monic equation after rescaling its root by an element of $U$.
theorems.proof: Inside $U^{-1}B$, the integral closure of $U^{-1}A$ equals $U^{-1}C$. Clear the finitely many denominators in a monic equation after rescaling its root by an element of $U$.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Integrality tested in all source stalks
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $x$ in an $R$-algebra $S$. Here $S_{\mathfrak p}$ denotes localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Then $x$ is integral over $R$ exactly when $x/1$ is integral over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ in $S_{\mathfrak p}$ for each source prime $\mathfrak p$. Apply localization to the integral closure and test membership in a submodule at all primes.
theorems.proof: Then $x$ is integral over $R$ exactly when $x/1$ is integral over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ in $S_{\mathfrak p}$ for each source prime $\mathfrak p$. Apply localization to the integral closure and test membership in a submodule at all primes.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change for finite and integral algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Given $R\to S$ and any $R\to A$, set $B=A\otimes_R S$.
theorems.statement: Integrality of $R\to S$ implies integrality of $A\to B$. Finiteness of the original map implies finiteness of the new map. Integral generators remain integral after changing coefficients, and module generators remain generators after tensoring.
theorems.proof: Integrality of $R\to S$ implies integrality of $A\to B$. Finiteness of the original map implies finiteness of the new map. Integral generators remain integral after changing coefficients, and module generators remain generators after tensoring.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Gluing integrality and finiteness on a principal cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ generate the unit ideal of $R$, and let $S$ be an $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: If every $R_{f_i}\to S_{f_i}$ is integral, then $R\to S$ is integral. If each localized map is finite, the original map is finite.
theorems.proof: If every $R_{f_i}\to S_{f_i}$ is integral, then $R\to S$ is integral. If each localized map is finite, the original map is finite.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Enlarging the intermediate ring for integral or finite maps
theorems.hypotheses: Take a diagram $A\to B\to C$ of commutative rings.
theorems.statement: Integrality of $C$ over $A$ gives integrality over $B$ by mapping coefficients. Finiteness of $C$ as an $A$-module gives finiteness as a $B$-module using the same generators.
theorems.proof: Integrality of $C$ over $A$ gives integrality over $B$ by mapping coefficients. Finiteness of $C$ as an $A$-module gives finiteness as a $B$-module using the same generators.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral closure in a tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be ring maps. Write $B'$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $B$.
theorems.statement: The integral closures of $A$ and of $B'$ in $C$ agree. Transitivity of integrality proves the inclusion from coefficients in $B'$ to coefficients in $A$.
theorems.proof: The integral closures of $A$ and of $B'$ in $C$ agree. Transitivity of integrality proves the inclusion from coefficients in $B'$ to coefficients in $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-inclusion
theorems.name: Descent of the field property along integral inclusions
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R$ is a subring of a field $K$ and $K$ is integral over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $R$ is a field and $K/R$ is algebraic. Apply integrality to $1/r$ for each nonzero $r\in R$. If $K$ is finite as an $R$-module, the resulting field extension is finite.
theorems.proof: Then $R$ is a field and $K/R$ is algebraic. Apply integrality to $1/r$ for each nonzero $r\in R$. If $K$ is finite as an $R$-module, the resulting field extension is finite.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral algebras over a field have only maximal primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be integral over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: Every prime of $S$ is maximal. Indeed any integral domain algebraic over a field is a field, by solving a minimal equation for the inverse of each nonzero element. In particular a finite-dimensional domain over $k$ is a field.
theorems.proof: Every prime of $S$ is maximal. Indeed any integral domain algebraic over a field is a field, by solving a minimal equation for the inverse of each nonzero element. In particular a finite-dimensional domain over $k$ is a field.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Finite presentation of modules under restriction of scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite and finitely presented as a ring map, and let $M$ be an $S$-module.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is finitely presented over $R$ exactly when it is finitely presented over $S$. Here finiteness is module finiteness of $S$ and presentation of the map is algebra presentation.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is finitely presented over $R$ exactly when it is finitely presented over $S$. Here finiteness is module finiteness of $S$ and presentation of the map is algebra presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-inclusion
theorems.name: An exact sequence from two inverse fractions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $x,y$ be nonzerodivisors of $R$ and assume $R$ is integrally closed in $R_x$ or in $R_y$. Work in $R_{xy}$ and set $u=x/y$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to R\to R[u]\oplus R[u^{-1}]\to R[u,u^{-1}]\to0$ is exact, with maps $r\mapsto(-r,r)$ and $(a,b)\mapsto a+b$. In particular the two subalgebras intersect in $R$.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to R\to R[u]\oplus R[u^{-1}]\to R[u,u^{-1}]\to0$ is exact, with maps $r\mapsto(-r,r)$ and $(a,b)\mapsto a+b$. In particular the two subalgebras intersect in $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral closure inside a normal domain
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to S$ let $S$ be a normal domain and $C$ the integral closure of $R$ in $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $C$ is a normal domain. An element of $\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ integral over $C$ is integral over $S$, hence lies in $S$, and transitivity puts it in $C$.
theorems.proof: Then $C$ is a normal domain. An element of $\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ integral over $C$ is integral over $S$, hence lies in $S$, and transitivity puts it in $C$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Localizations of normal domains
theorems.hypotheses: Take a multiplicative subset $U$ of a normal domain $R$.
theorems.statement: The localization $U^{-1}R$ is normal. If $0\notin U$ it is a normal domain, since integral closure commutes with localization in the fraction field. If $0\in U$, it is the zero ring, whose normality is vacuous.
theorems.proof: The localization $U^{-1}R$ is normal. If $0\notin U$ it is a normal domain, since integral closure commutes with localization in the fraction field. If $0\in U$, it is the zero ring, whose normality is vacuous.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Integrality of coefficients of a polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain with fraction field $K$ and $f=\sum_i a_i x^i\in K[x]$.
theorems.statement: If $f$ is integral over $R[x]$, each $a_i$ is integral over $R$. If $f$ is almost integral over $R[x]$, each $a_i$ is almost integral over $R$.
theorems.proof: If $f$ is integral over $R[x]$, each $a_i$ is integral over $R$. If $f$ is almost integral over $R[x]$, each $a_i$ is almost integral over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The polynomial ring over a normal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a normal domain.
theorems.statement: Then $R[x]$ is a normal domain. An integral fraction first belongs to $\operatorname{Frac}(R)[x]$ by normality over a field. Its coefficients are integral and therefore belong to $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $R[x]$ is a normal domain. An integral fraction first belongs to $\operatorname{Frac}(R)[x]$ by normality over a field. Its coefficients are integral and therefore belong to $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Formal power series over a Noetherian normal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R$ is both Noetherian and a normal domain.
theorems.statement: The formal power series ring $R[[x]]$ is again a Noetherian normal domain.
theorems.proof: The formal power series ring $R[[x]]$ is again a Noetherian normal domain.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Normality of a polynomial ring in one variable
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a normal ring, allowing zero divisors.
theorems.statement: Then $R[x]$ is normal. At a prime over $\mathfrak p$, its stalk is a localization of the polynomial ring over the normal domain $R_{\mathfrak p}$.
theorems.proof: Then $R[x]$ is normal. At a prime over $\mathfrak p$, its stalk is a localization of the polynomial ring over the normal domain $R_{\mathfrak p}$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite products preserve normality
theorems.hypotheses: Take a finite family of normal rings.
theorems.statement: Their product is normal. A prime of the product comes from one factor and its local ring agrees with the local ring of that factor at the corresponding prime.
theorems.proof: Their product is normal. A prime of the product comes from one factor and its local ring agrees with the local ring of that factor at the corresponding prime.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Normal rings under directed colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a directed system $(R_i)$ of normal rings with arbitrary transition homomorphisms.
theorems.statement: Then $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$ is normal. At a prime of $R$ one obtains a directed system of normal local domains with local maps, whose colimit is the required normal local domain.
theorems.proof: Then $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$ is normal. At a prime of $R$ one obtains a directed system of normal local domains with local maps, whose colimit is the required normal local domain.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Rees algebra criterion for integrality over an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to S$ and $I\subset R$, let $A=R[It]=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^nt^n\subset R[t]$. Fix $s\in S$.
theorems.statement: The element $s$ is integral over $I$ exactly when $st\in S[t]$ is integral over $A$. Homogenizing a monic equation gives one direction, and taking its component of total degree equal to its monic degree gives the other.
theorems.proof: The element $s$ is integral over $I$ exactly when $st\in S[t]$ is integral over $A$. Homogenizing a monic equation gives one direction, and taking its component of total degree equal to its monic degree gives the other.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Elements integral over an ideal form a module
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R\to S$ and an ideal $I\subset R$.
theorems.statement: The elements of $S$ integral over $I$ form an $R$-submodule. Multiplication by any element of $S$ integral over $R$ preserves this submodule.
theorems.proof: The elements of $S$ integral over $I$ form an $R$-submodule. Multiplication by any element of $S$ integral over $R$ preserves this submodule.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Elements of an extended ideal under an integral map
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $S$ is integral over $R$ and $I$ is an ideal of $R$.
theorems.statement: Every element of $IS$ satisfies a monic equation of degree $d$ whose coefficient of degree $j<d$ belongs to the image of $I^{d-j}$.
theorems.proof: Every element of $IS$ satisfies a monic equation of degree $d$ whose coefficient of degree $j<d$ belongs to the image of $I^{d-j}$.

theorems.subject: field-polynomial-pair
theorems.name: Integrality and radicals of coefficients of monic factors
theorems.hypotheses: Take monic $F,G\in K[x]$ over a field, of respective degrees $n,m$, with $F$ dividing $G$. Let $a_i,b_j$ be their nonleading coefficients.
theorems.statement: Every $a_i$ is integral over any subring of $K$ containing all $b_j$. In any subring $A$ containing all $a_i,b_j$, one has $a_i\in\sqrt{(b_0,\ldots,b_{m-1})A}$.
theorems.proof: Every $a_i$ is integral over any subring of $K$ containing all $b_j$. In any subring $A$ containing all $a_i,b_j$, one has $a_i\in\sqrt{(b_0,\ldots,b_{m-1})A}$.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Coefficients of a minimal polynomial over a normal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subset S$ be domains with $R$ normal. Take $s\in S$ integral over $R$.
theorems.statement: The monic minimal polynomial of $s$ over $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ lies in $R[x]$. It divides a monic integral equation, so its coefficients are integral over $R$ and belong to the fraction field.
theorems.proof: The monic minimal polynomial of $s$ over $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ lies in $R[x]$. It divides a monic integral equation, so its coefficients are integral over $R$ and belong to the fraction field.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Flat modules preserve binary intersections of extended ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be flat over $R$ and let $I,J$ be arbitrary ideals of $R$.
theorems.statement: One has $IM\cap JM=(I\cap J)M$ in $M$. Flatness preserves the kernel computing the intersection inside $I\oplus J$.
theorems.proof: One has $IM\cap JM=(I\cap J)M$ in $M$. Flatness preserves the kernel computing the intersection inside $I\oplus J$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Directed colimits of flat modules
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $(M_i)$ is a directed system of flat modules over one fixed ring $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{colim}_iM_i$ is flat. Tensor product commutes with colimits and directed colimits are exact in modules.
