theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{colim}_iM_i$ is flat. Tensor product commutes with colimits and directed colimits are exact in modules.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Composition and restriction of scalars for flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Take maps $R\to S\to T$ or an $S$-module $N$ together with $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: If both maps are flat, their composite is flat. If both are faithfully flat, the composite is faithfully flat. Likewise $N$ is flat over $R$ if $S$ is flat over $R$ and $N$ flat over $S$, with the same assertion when both hypotheses are faithful flatness.
theorems.proof: If both maps are flat, their composite is flat. If both are faithfully flat, the composite is faithfully flat. Likewise $N$ is flat over $R$ if $S$ is flat over $R$ and $N$ flat over $S$, with the same assertion when both hypotheses are faithful flatness.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Flatness over a directed colimit of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$ for a directed system of rings.
theorems.statement: An $R$-module flat over every $R_i$ is flat over $R$. More generally, if $M_i$ is flat over $R_i$ and the transition maps of modules are compatible and linear over the ring transitions, then $\operatorname{colim}_i M_i$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: An $R$-module flat over every $R_i$ is flat over $R$. More generally, if $M_i$ is flat over $R_i$ and the transition maps of modules are compatible and linear over the ring transitions, then $\operatorname{colim}_i M_i$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Changing an intermediate scalar ring while testing flatness over a fixed base
theorems.hypotheses: For $R$-algebras take a flat map $S\to S'$ and an $S$-module $M$. Write $M'=S'\otimes_S M$.
theorems.statement: Flatness of $M$ over $R$ implies flatness of $M'$ over $R$. If $S\to S'$ is faithfully flat, flatness over $R$ of $M'$ also implies that of $M$.
theorems.proof: Flatness of $M$ over $R$ implies flatness of $M'$ over $R$. If $S\to S'$ is faithfully flat, flatness over $R$ of $M'$ also implies that of $M$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Testing flatness of a ring map with a faithfully flat module
theorems.hypotheses: Given $R\to S$, suppose the $S$-module $M$ is faithfully flat over $S$ and flat over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is flat over $R$. Tensor an injection first with $S$ and then with $M$ over $S$. The composite preserves injectivity by $R$-flatness, and faithful flatness over $S$ detects it after the first tensor product.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is flat over $R$. Tensor an injection first with $S$ and then with $M$ over $S$. The composite preserves injectivity by $R$-flatness, and faithful flatness over $S$ detects it after the first tensor product.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: The equational criterion for flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module. A finite relation is an equality $\sum_i f_i x_i=0$ in $M$.
theorems.statement: The module is flat exactly when, for each such relation, there exist finitely many $y_j\in M$ and $a_{ij}\in R$ with $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}y_j$ and $\sum_i f_i a_{ij}=0$ for every $j$. Thus each relation is induced by scalar relations on a finite free module.
theorems.proof: The module is flat exactly when, for each such relation, there exist finitely many $y_j\in M$ and $a_{ij}\in R$ with $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}y_j$ and $\sum_i f_i a_{ij}=0$ for every $j$. Thus each relation is induced by scalar relations on a finite free module.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: An exact sequence with flat quotient stays exact under tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ be exact with $N$ flat over $R$, and take any $R$-module $P$.
theorems.statement: Tensoring all three terms with $P$ preserves short exactness. In particular $P\otimes_RL\to P\otimes_RM$ is injective.
theorems.proof: Tensoring all three terms with $P$ preserves short exactness. In particular $P\otimes_RL\to P\otimes_RM$ is injective.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Flatness of kernels and extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Given an exact sequence $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ of $R$-modules, assume that $N$ is flat.
theorems.statement: Then $L$ is flat if and only if $M$ is flat. Use tensor exactness for a flat quotient and the injectivity test for flatness.
theorems.proof: Then $L$ is flat if and only if $M$ is flat. Use tensor exactness for a flat quotient and the injectivity test for flatness.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Faithfully flat modules detect the zero morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Faithful flatness is equivalent to flatness together with the following detection property. For every linear map $u:P\to Q$, the map $u\otimes_R M$ vanishes exactly when $u$ vanishes. Flatness identifies the tensor of the image with the image of the tensor map.
theorems.proof: Faithful flatness is equivalent to flatness together with the following detection property. For every linear map $u:P\to Q$, the map $u\otimes_R M$ vanishes exactly when $u$ vanishes. Flatness identifies the tensor of the image with the image of the tensor map.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Nonvanishing tests for faithful flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $M$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.statement: The following are equivalent. The module $M$ is faithfully flat. Every nonzero $N$ has $N\otimes_RM\ne0$. All fibres $M\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are nonzero. All maximal fibres $M/\mathfrak mM$ are nonzero.
theorems.proof: The following are equivalent. The module $M$ is faithfully flat. Every nonzero $N$ has $N\otimes_RM\ne0$. All fibres $M\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are nonzero. All maximal fibres $M/\mathfrak mM$ are nonzero.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Closed fibres suffice for faithful flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat.
theorems.statement: Faithful flatness is equivalent both to surjectivity on spectra and to its image containing every closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Surjectivity at maximal ideals tests nonvanishing of the maximal fibres of the $R$-module $S$.
theorems.proof: Faithful flatness is equivalent both to surjectivity on spectra and to its image containing every closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Surjectivity at maximal ideals tests nonvanishing of the maximal fibres of the $R$-module $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Locality of module flatness on the source and target rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an $R$-algebra and $M$ an $A$-module.
theorems.statement: Flatness over $R$ can be tested by flatness of $M_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R_{\mathfrak q\cap R}$ for all primes, or just all maximal ideals, of $A$. On a finite principal cover $D(g_i)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ it is also equivalent to $R$-flatness of every $M_{g_i}$. For $A=U^{-1}R$ each $A$-module is $R$-flat exactly when it is $A$-flat, and $A$ itself is $R$-flat.
theorems.proof: Flatness over $R$ can be tested by flatness of $M_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R_{\mathfrak q\cap R}$ for all primes, or just all maximal ideals, of $A$. On a finite principal cover $D(g_i)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ it is also equivalent to $R$-flatness of every $M_{g_i}$. For $A=U^{-1}R$ each $A$-module is $R$-flat exactly when it is $A$-flat, and $A$ itself is $R$-flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Directed colimits of faithfully flat algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(S_i)$ be a directed system of faithfully flat $R$-algebras, with transition homomorphisms over $R$.
theorems.statement: The colimit $S$ is faithfully flat over $R$. It is flat by exactness of directed colimits. Each residue-field fibre is a directed colimit of nonzero unital algebras over that field and is therefore nonzero.
theorems.proof: The colimit $S$ is faithfully flat over $R$. It is flat by exactness of directed colimits. Each residue-field fibre is a directed colimit of nonzero unital algebras over that field and is therefore nonzero.

theorems.subject: module-element
theorems.name: Annihilators under flat base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $M$ an $R$-module, and $x\in M$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Ann}_S(x\otimes1)=\operatorname{Ann}_R(x)S$. If $M$ is finite, also $\operatorname{Ann}_S(M\otimes_RS)=\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)S$. Use flatness on the kernel of $R\to M$ for the element, then take the finite intersection for a generating family.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Ann}_S(x\otimes1)=\operatorname{Ann}_R(x)S$. If $M$ is finite, also $\operatorname{Ann}_S(M\otimes_RS)=\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)S$. Use flatness on the kernel of $R\to M$ for the element, then take the finite intersection for a generating family.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Support after arbitrary base change for a finite module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module, $R\to S$ arbitrary, and $f:\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Supp}(S\otimes_RM)=f^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(M))$. At each point of the target ring, use Nakayama and extend the residue field of its contraction.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Supp}(S\otimes_RM)=f^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(M))$. At each point of the target ring, use Nakayama and extend the residue field of its contraction.

theorems.subject: module-element
theorems.name: Nonvanishing locus of a fixed element
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $m\in M$ and $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: The image of $m$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is nonzero precisely when $\operatorname{Ann}_R(m)\subseteq\mathfrak p$. A localized element vanishes if some denominator kills it.
theorems.proof: The image of $m$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is nonzero precisely when $\operatorname{Ann}_R(m)\subseteq\mathfrak p$. A localized element vanishes if some denominator kills it.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Support of submodules, quotients and exact sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module, $N\subseteq M$, $Q=M/N$, and let $I$ be an ideal of $R$.
theorems.statement: Localizing the short exact sequence yields $\operatorname{Supp}(M)=\operatorname{Supp}(N)\cup\operatorname{Supp}(Q)$, in particular both supports are contained in that of $M$. For finite $M$, Nakayama gives $\operatorname{Supp}(M/IM)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(I)$.
theorems.proof: Localizing the short exact sequence yields $\operatorname{Supp}(M)=\operatorname{Supp}(N)\cup\operatorname{Supp}(Q)$, in particular both supports are contained in that of $M$. For finite $M$, Nakayama gives $\operatorname{Supp}(M/IM)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(I)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Topological lifting interpretations of going up and going down
theorems.hypotheses: Consider the spectral map of an arbitrary ring homomorphism $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: Going up is equivalent to lifting all specializations of the image of a given point. Going down is equivalent to lifting all generalizations of the image of a given point. In a spectrum the specialization order is inclusion of primes.
theorems.proof: Going up is equivalent to lifting all specializations of the image of a given point. Going down is equivalent to lifting all generalizations of the image of a given point. In a spectrum the specialization order is inclusion of primes.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition preserves going up and going down
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S\to T$ be a composable pair.
theorems.statement: If both maps have going up then the composite has going up. If both maps have going down then the composite has going down. Lift a chosen prime inclusion in two successive steps.
theorems.proof: If both maps have going up then the composite has going up. If both maps have going down then the composite has going down. Lift a chosen prime inclusion in two successive steps.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: An affine spectral image stable under specialization is closed
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to S$ suppose its image in $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is stable under specialization.
theorems.statement: The image equals its closure $V(\ker(R\to S))$. After quotienting by the kernel every minimal prime of the source ring is reached. Stability then supplies every specialization of those minimal primes.
theorems.proof: The image equals its closure $V(\ker(R\to S))$. After quotienting by the kernel every minimal prime of the source ring is reached. Stability then supplies every specialization of those minimal primes.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Specialization stability for constructible subsets of an affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Take a constructible subset $E\subset\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: If $E$ is stable under specialization it is closed. If $E$ is stable under generalization it is open. Apply the first assertion to the complement to obtain the second.
theorems.proof: If $E$ is stable under specialization it is closed. If $E$ is stable under generalization it is open. Apply the first assertion to the complement to obtain the second.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Images of principal tensor-product opens under extension of a factor
theorems.hypotheses: For $k$-algebras $R,S$ over a field, a subalgebra $S'\subseteq S$, and $f\in S'\otimes_k R$, compare the two projections to $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: The principal opens cut out by $f$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(S'\otimes_k R)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_k R)$ have the same image. Over each residue field the inclusion stays injective, so $f$ is nilpotent in one fibre exactly when it is nilpotent in the other.
theorems.proof: The principal opens cut out by $f$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(S'\otimes_k R)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_k R)$ have the same image. Over each residue field the inclusion stays injective, so $f$ is nilpotent in one fibre exactly when it is nilpotent in the other.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Every algebra over a field gives universally open projections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R,S$ be arbitrary algebras over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: The projection $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_kR)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is open. For a principal open descend its defining element to a finitely generated subalgebra of $S$, where flatness and finite presentation give openness.
theorems.proof: The projection $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_kR)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is open. For a principal open descend its defining element to a finitely generated subalgebra of $S$, where flatness and finite presentation give openness.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Comparison of localizations at a prime and its contraction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak q$ be the unique prime of $S$ over $\mathfrak p$ for $R\to S$. Suppose either going up holds, or going down holds and at most one prime lies over each source prime.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}S\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is an isomorphism. Under the stated hypotheses the localization on the left is local with maximal ideal induced by $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}S\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is an isomorphism. Under the stated hypotheses the localization on the left is local with maximal ideal induced by $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Lifting generalizations on the support of a relatively flat module
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to S$ let $N$ be finite over $S$ and flat over $R$. Give its support in $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ the induced topology.
theorems.statement: Each generalization of the image of a point of $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ lifts to a generalization in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$.
theorems.proof: Each generalization of the image of a point of $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ lifts to a generalization in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Separability descends to intermediate subfields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$ be fields and suppose $K/k$ is separable in the general, possibly transcendental sense.
theorems.statement: Then $F/k$ is separable. Every finitely generated subextension of $F/k$ is a finitely generated subextension of $K/k$.
theorems.proof: Then $F/k$ is separable. Every finitely generated subextension of $F/k$ is a finitely generated subextension of $K/k$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Separating transcendence basis with a single algebraic generator
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be finitely generated and separably generated, with $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_kK$.
theorems.statement: There are $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y$ with $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ a transcendence basis and $K=k(x_1,\ldots,x_r,y)$, where $y$ is separable algebraic over $k(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. Use a primitive element for the finite separable remainder.
theorems.proof: There are $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y$ with $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ a transcendence basis and $K=k(x_1,\ldots,x_r,y)$, where $y$ is separable algebraic over $k(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. Use a primitive element for the finite separable remainder.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: A separating model after finite purely inseparable extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $K/k$ is a finitely generated extension of fields.
theorems.statement: There exist a finite purely inseparable $k'/k$ and a finite purely inseparable $K'/K$ in a commuting square with $k'\subseteq K'$ such that $K'/k'$ is separably generated.
theorems.proof: There exist a finite purely inseparable $k'/k$ and a finite purely inseparable $K'/K$ in a commuting square with $k'\subseteq K'$ such that $K'/k'$ is separably generated.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Subalgebras, localizations and directed colimits for geometric reducedness
theorems.hypotheses: Take algebras over a fixed field $k$.
theorems.statement: Subalgebras and localizations of geometrically reduced algebras are geometrically reduced. Directed colimits of geometrically reduced algebras are geometrically reduced. Thus geometric reducedness can be tested on all finitely generated $k$-subalgebras.
theorems.proof: Subalgebras and localizations of geometrically reduced algebras are geometrically reduced. Directed colimits of geometrically reduced algebras are geometrically reduced. Thus geometric reducedness can be tested on all finitely generated $k$-subalgebras.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Polynomial and localized geometrically reduced algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be geometrically reduced over a field $k$ and $U$ any multiplicative subset of $R$.
theorems.statement: Both $U^{-1}R$ and $R[x]$ are geometrically reduced over $k$. Field extension commutes with either construction, each of which preserves reducedness.
theorems.proof: Both $U^{-1}R$ and $R[x]$ are geometrically reduced over $k$. Field extension commutes with either construction, each of which preserves reducedness.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Finite detection of algebraic defects in a tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R,S$ be algebras over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: If $R\otimes_kS$ contains a nonzero nilpotent, a nonzero zero divisor, or an idempotent other than $0,1$, there are finite type subalgebras $R'\subseteq R$, $S'\subseteq S$ whose tensor product has the corresponding defect. Include all coefficients from representatives of the elements witnessing it and use injectivity over the field.
theorems.proof: If $R\otimes_kS$ contains a nonzero nilpotent, a nonzero zero divisor, or an idempotent other than $0,1$, there are finite type subalgebras $R'\subseteq R$, $S'\subseteq S$ whose tensor product has the corresponding defect. Include all coefficients from representatives of the elements witnessing it and use injectivity over the field.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Tensor product with a reduced algebra over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $S$ is geometrically reduced over $k$ and $R$ is any reduced $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The ring $R\otimes_kS$ is reduced. Any proposed nilpotent is detected using a finite type reduced subalgebra of $R$ and its generic residue fields.
theorems.proof: The ring $R\otimes_kS$ is reduced. Any proposed nilpotent is detected using a finite type reduced subalgebra of $R$ and its generic residue fields.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Separable extension of the base preserves reducedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a reduced $k$-algebra and $K/k$ a separable or a separably generated field extension.
theorems.statement: The ring $K\otimes_kS$ is reduced. One reduces to finite type data and uses a separating transcendence basis followed by a separable algebraic extension.
theorems.proof: The ring $K\otimes_kS$ is reduced. One reduces to finite type data and uses a separating transcendence basis followed by a separable algebraic extension.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Testing geometric reducedness at generic points
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a reduced $k$-algebra and assume $S_{\mathfrak p}$ is geometrically reduced over $k$ for every minimal prime of $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is geometrically reduced over $k$. The local rings at the minimal primes detect elements because $S$ is reduced.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is geometrically reduced over $k$. The local rings at the minimal primes detect elements because $S$ is reduced.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: The diagonal of a separable algebraic extension is a localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be separable algebraic, with no finiteness assumption.
theorems.statement: The multiplication homomorphism $K\otimes_kK\to K$ identifies with localization at a multiplicative subset of the tensor square.
theorems.proof: The multiplication homomorphism $K\otimes_kK\to K$ identifies with localization at a multiplicative subset of the tensor square.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Changing a separable algebraic field of definition
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be separable algebraic and $A$ a $K$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Geometric reducedness of $A$ over $k$ is equivalent to geometric reducedness over $K$. This compares the same algebra under restriction of scalars.
theorems.proof: Geometric reducedness of $A$ over $k$ is equivalent to geometric reducedness over $K$. This compares the same algebra under restriction of scalars.

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.name: Selecting a separating basis from a generating tuple
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ have characteristic $p>0$ and be generated by $x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1}$. Assume the first $n$ form a transcendence basis and for every finite $k$-linearly independent tuple $(a_i)$ of $K$ the tuple $(a_i^p)$ is $k$-linearly independent.
theorems.statement: There is an index $j$ such that deleting $x_j$ leaves a separating transcendence basis of $K/k$.
theorems.proof: There is an index $j$ such that deleting $x_j$ leaves a separating transcendence basis of $K/k$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Four tests for separability in positive characteristic
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be an arbitrary extension in characteristic $p>0$. Put $k^{1/p}=\{a\in\overline{k}:a^p\in k\}$.
theorems.statement: Separability of $K/k$, preservation of $k$-linear independence of finite tuples in $K$ under taking $p$th powers, reducedness of $K\otimes_k k^{1/p}$, and geometric reducedness of $K$ over $k$ are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Separability of $K/k$, preservation of $k$-linear independence of finite tuples in $K$ under taking $p$th powers, reducedness of $K\otimes_k k^{1/p}$, and geometric reducedness of $K$ over $k$ are equivalent.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Field tests for geometric reducedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a $k$-algebra. In characteristic $p>0$ use $k^{1/p}$ for adjoining all $p$th roots and $k^{\mathrm{perf}}$ for the perfect closure. In characteristic zero both denote $k$ in these tests.
theorems.statement: Geometric reducedness is equivalent to reducedness after each finite purely inseparable extension. Equivalently one can test over $k^{1/p}$, over $k^{\mathrm{perf}}$, or over an algebraic closure, with a single base change for each test.
theorems.proof: Geometric reducedness is equivalent to reducedness after each finite purely inseparable extension. Equivalently one can test over $k^{1/p}$, over $k^{\mathrm{perf}}$, or over an algebraic closure, with a single base change for each test.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: A separable model given by a reduced tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $K/k$ is finitely generated.
theorems.statement: A finite purely inseparable $k'/k$ may be chosen so that $K'=(k'\otimes_kK)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a field separable over $k'$. It identifies with the compositum $k'K$ and is finite purely inseparable over $K$.
theorems.proof: A finite purely inseparable $k'/k$ may be chosen so that $K'=(k'\otimes_kK)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a field separable over $k'$. It identifies with the compositum $k'K$ and is finite purely inseparable over $K$.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Existence and rigidity of the perfect closure
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a field $k$.
theorems.statement: There is a purely inseparable field extension of $k$ that is perfect, unique up to unique $k$-isomorphism. In characteristic $p>0$ take the union of the fields $k^{1/p^n}$ in an algebraic closure. In characteristic zero $k$ already suffices.
theorems.proof: There is a purely inseparable field extension of $k$ that is perfect, unique up to unique $k$-isomorphism. In characteristic $p>0$ take the union of the fields $k^{1/p^n}$ in an algebraic closure. In characteristic zero $k$ already suffices.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Tensor products of reduced algebras over a perfect field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R,S$ be reduced algebras over a perfect field $k$.
theorems.statement: Each reduced $k$-algebra is geometrically reduced over $k$, and $R\otimes_kS$ is reduced. Perfection removes the purely inseparable field extension obstruction.
theorems.proof: Each reduced $k$-algebra is geometrically reduced over $k$, and $R\otimes_kS$ is reduced. Perfection removes the purely inseparable field extension obstruction.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Nil quotients preserve spectra and residue fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be surjective with nil kernel, meaning each kernel element is nilpotent.
theorems.statement: Its map of spectra is a homeomorphism with isomorphic residue fields. After every base change the map is again surjective with nil kernel, since an ideal generated by nilpotent elements is nil.
theorems.proof: Its map of spectra is a homeomorphism with isomorphic residue fields. After every base change the map is again surjective with nil kernel, since an ideal generated by nilpotent elements is nil.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Classification of field extensions with powers in the base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be an extension of fields.
theorems.statement: Every element of $K$ has some positive power in $k$ precisely in these cases. Either $K=k$, or in positive characteristic $p$ the extension is purely inseparable or the two fields are algebraic over $\mathbf F_p$. The exponent can depend on the element.
theorems.proof: Every element of $K$ has some positive power in $k$ precisely in these cases. Either $K=k$, or in positive characteristic $p$ the extension is purely inseparable or the two fields are algebraic over $\mathbf F_p$. The exponent can depend on the element.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A homeomorphism on spectra from powers in the image
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:R\to S$, suppose $\ker f$ is nil and every $x\in S$ has some positive power in $f(R)$.
theorems.statement: The induced spectral map is a homeomorphism. In every residue extension each element has some positive power in the smaller residue field. This allows nontrivial separable residue extensions between algebraic extensions of a finite field.
theorems.proof: The induced spectral map is a homeomorphism. In every residue extension each element has some positive power in the smaller residue field. This allows nontrivial separable residue extensions between algebraic extensions of a finite field.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Square-and-cube generators preserve residue fields universally
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $f:R\to S$ has nil kernel and $S$ is generated over $R$ by elements $x$ with $x^2,x^3\in f(R)$.
theorems.statement: Then $f$ induces a homeomorphism of spectra and isomorphisms on residue fields. Every base change again satisfies the same two algebraic hypotheses.
theorems.proof: Then $f$ induces a homeomorphism of spectra and isomorphisms on residue fields. Every base change again satisfies the same two algebraic hypotheses.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A uniform binomial estimate for a fixed prime
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime number $p$ and positive integers $n,m$. Use indeterminates $x,y$ over $\mathbf Z$.
theorems.statement: For some nonnegative integer $a$ both $(x+y)^{p^a}$ and $p^a(x+y)$ belong to the subring $\mathbf Z[x^{p^n},p^n x,y^{p^m},p^m y]$ of $\mathbf Z[x,y]$.
theorems.proof: For some nonnegative integer $a$ both $(x+y)^{p^a}$ and $p^a(x+y)$ belong to the subring $\mathbf Z[x^{p^n},p^n x,y^{p^m},p^m y]$ of $\mathbf Z[x,y]$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Field extensions detected by two fixed-prime power conditions
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime number $p$ and a field extension $K/k$.
theorems.statement: The field $K$ is generated over $k$ by elements $x$ for which $x^{p^n}$ and $p^n x$ lie in $k$ for some $n>0$ depending on $x$, exactly when $K=k$ or the characteristic is $p$ and $K/k$ is purely inseparable.
theorems.proof: The field $K$ is generated over $k$ by elements $x$ for which $x^{p^n}$ and $p^n x$ lie in $k$ for some $n>0$ depending on $x$, exactly when $K=k$ or the characteristic is $p$ and $K/k$ is purely inseparable.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A fixed-prime power criterion for universal homeomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:R\to S$ have nil kernel. For a fixed prime number $p$, suppose the algebra is generated by elements $x$ with $x^{p^n},p^n x\in f(R)$ for some $n>0$ depending on $x$.
theorems.statement: The induced map is a homeomorphism of spectra. Each residue extension is trivial or purely inseparable in characteristic $p$. After any base change the two algebraic hypotheses still hold.
theorems.proof: The induced map is a homeomorphism of spectra. Each residue extension is trivial or purely inseparable in characteristic $p$. After any base change the two algebraic hypotheses still hold.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Stability of spectral injectivity with purely inseparable residue fields
theorems.hypotheses: Assume that $R\to S$ induces an injection of spectra and all residue extensions are purely inseparable.
theorems.statement: For every $R$-algebra $A$, the map $A\to A\otimes_R S$ has both properties. In particular this pair of hypotheses gives universal injectivity on spectra.
theorems.proof: For every $R$-algebra $A$, the map $A\to A\otimes_R S$ has both properties. In particular this pair of hypotheses gives universal injectivity on spectra.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral radicial affine maps are homeomorphisms onto closed images
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be integral, injective on spectra, and purely inseparable at all residue extensions.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ maps homeomorphically onto a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. All three hypotheses hold after arbitrary base change. Surjectivity on spectra is not assumed.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ maps homeomorphically onto a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. All three hypotheses hold after arbitrary base change. Surjectivity on spectra is not assumed.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A universal homeomorphism criterion using translated powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:R\to S$ have nil kernel. Assume $S$ is generated by elements $x$ for each of which $(T-x)^n$ lies in the image of $R[T]\to S[T]$ for some positive $n$.
theorems.statement: Then the spectral map is a homeomorphism and the residue extensions are purely inseparable. Both assumptions persist after arbitrary base change.
theorems.proof: Then the spectral map is a homeomorphism and the residue extensions are purely inseparable. Both assumptions persist after arbitrary base change.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Irreducibility from an open spectral map and dense irreducible fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is irreducible, $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is open and the fibres over a dense set of base primes have nonempty irreducible spectra. A flat finitely presented map supplies openness.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ is irreducible. The images of two nonempty opens meet over a good fibre, where their inverse images must intersect.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ is irreducible. The images of two nonempty opens meet over a good fibre, where their inverse images must intersect.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: A unique minimal prime after tensoring over a separably closed field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be separably closed and let $R,S$ be $k$-algebras, each having exactly one minimal prime.
theorems.statement: Their tensor product over $k$ has exactly one minimal prime. Equivalently its spectrum is nonempty and irreducible.
theorems.proof: Their tensor product over $k$ has exactly one minimal prime. Equivalently its spectrum is nonempty and irreducible.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Field tests for geometric irreducibility
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be any $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Geometric irreducibility over $k$ is equivalent to irreducibility after all finite separable field extensions, after one separable algebraic closure, or after one algebraic closure. In every test irreducibility requires nonemptiness.
theorems.proof: Geometric irreducibility over $k$ is equivalent to irreducibility after all finite separable field extensions, after one separable algebraic closure, or after one algebraic closure. In every test irreducibility requires nonemptiness.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Geometric irreducibility over a separably closed field
theorems.hypotheses: Assume the base field $k$ is separably closed and $R$ is a $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The spectrum of $R$ is irreducible exactly when $R$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. Finite separable extensions are trivial here.
theorems.proof: The spectrum of $R$ is irreducible exactly when $R$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. Finite separable extensions are trivial here.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Subalgebras and directed colimits of geometrically irreducible algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Take algebras over a fixed field $k$.
theorems.statement: A $k$-subalgebra of a geometrically irreducible algebra is geometrically irreducible. Directed colimits preserve this property. In particular it suffices to check all finitely generated subalgebras.
theorems.proof: A $k$-subalgebra of a geometrically irreducible algebra is geometrically irreducible. Directed colimits preserve this property. In particular it suffices to check all finitely generated subalgebras.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: A geometrically irreducible factor preserves irreducible components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be geometrically irreducible over $k$, and $R$ any $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The projection $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kS)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ induces a bijection on irreducible components, via their generic points.
theorems.proof: The projection $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kS)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ induces a bijection on irreducible components, via their generic points.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Transitivity of geometric irreducibility along a field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be geometrically irreducible and let $S$ be geometrically irreducible as a $K$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is geometrically irreducible as a $k$-algebra. Apply the component bijection after a field extension of $k$.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is geometrically irreducible as a $k$-algebra. Apply the component bijection after a field extension of $k$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Geometric irreducibility after adjoining one rational variable
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be a field extension and $t$ an indeterminate.
theorems.statement: Then $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible precisely when $K(t)/k(t)$ is geometrically irreducible.
theorems.proof: Then $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible precisely when $K(t)/k(t)$ is geometrically irreducible.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: An internal transcendental element preserves geometric irreducibility of subfields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M\subseteq L\subseteq K$ be fields. Suppose $L/M$ is geometrically irreducible and $x\in K$ is transcendental over $L$.
theorems.statement: Then $L(x)/M(x)$ is geometrically irreducible, by identifying $x$ with a rational variable over $L$.
theorems.proof: Then $L(x)/M(x)$ is geometrically irreducible, by identifying $x$ with a rational variable over $L$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Passing to separably algebraic constants gives geometric irreducibility
theorems.hypotheses: Given any field extension $K/k$, let $k'$ be the elements of $K$ separably algebraic over $k$.
theorems.statement: The extension $K/k'$ is geometrically irreducible. If $K/k$ is finitely generated, then $k'/k$ is finite.
theorems.proof: The extension $K/k'$ is geometrically irreducible. If $K/k$ is finitely generated, then $k'/k$ is finite.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Transitivity of the absolute Galois group on a geometric field fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Take a field extension $K/k$ and a separable algebraic closure $k^s$ of $k$.
theorems.statement: The action of $\operatorname{Gal}(k^s/k)$ on the first tensor factor acts transitively on the prime ideals of $k^s\otimes_kK$.
theorems.proof: The action of $\operatorname{Gal}(k^s/k)$ on the first tensor factor acts transitively on the prime ideals of $k^s\otimes_kK$.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Connected tensor products over a separably closed field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be separably closed and assume the spectra of both $k$-algebras $R,S$ are nonempty and connected.
theorems.statement: The spectrum of $R\otimes_k S$ is nonempty and connected.
theorems.proof: The spectrum of $R\otimes_k S$ is nonempty and connected.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite separable field tests for geometric connectedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a $k$-algebra and use the Stacks convention that a connected space is nonempty.
theorems.statement: Geometric connectedness is equivalent to connectedness of the spectrum after every finite separable extension of $k$.
theorems.proof: Geometric connectedness is equivalent to connectedness of the spectrum after every finite separable extension of $k$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Geometric connectedness over a separably closed field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be separably closed and let $R$ be a $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Then $R$ is geometrically connected precisely when $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is nonempty and connected.
theorems.proof: Then $R$ is geometrically connected precisely when $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is nonempty and connected.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Subalgebras and directed colimits for geometric connectedness
theorems.hypotheses: Work over a field $k$ and require connected spectra to be nonempty.
theorems.statement: Subalgebras of geometrically connected algebras and directed colimits of geometrically connected algebras are geometrically connected. Thus it suffices to test every finite type subalgebra.
theorems.proof: Subalgebras of geometrically connected algebras and directed colimits of geometrically connected algebras are geometrically connected. Thus it suffices to test every finite type subalgebra.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: A geometrically connected factor preserves idempotents and components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be geometrically connected over $k$ in the nonempty Stacks convention, and $R$ any $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to R\otimes_k S$ is bijective on idempotents. Its spectral projection induces a bijection on connected components.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to R\otimes_k S$ is bijective on idempotents. Its spectral projection induces a bijection on connected components.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite extensions and algebraic closure detect geometric integrality
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Geometric integrality is equivalent to $R\otimes_k E$ being a domain for every finite extension $E/k$, or to $R\otimes_k\overline{k}$ being a domain for an algebraic closure $\overline{k}$. A domain is required to be nonzero.
theorems.proof: Geometric integrality is equivalent to $R\otimes_k E$ being a domain for every finite extension $E/k$, or to $R\otimes_k\overline{k}$ being a domain for an algebraic closure $\overline{k}$. A domain is required to be nonzero.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: A domain stays a domain after tensoring with a geometrically integral factor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be geometrically integral over $k$ and let $R$ be a $k$-algebra which is a domain.
theorems.statement: Then $R\otimes_kS$ is a domain. It embeds into $\operatorname{Frac}(R)\otimes_kS$ by flatness over $k$, and the latter ring is a domain by hypothesis.
theorems.proof: Then $R\otimes_kS$ is a domain. It embeds into $\operatorname{Frac}(R)\otimes_kS$ by flatness over $k$, and the latter ring is a domain by hypothesis.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Determinantal test for injectivity over a local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local and $u:R^m\to R^n$. Write $r$ for its exterior rank and $I$ for the ideal of $r$-minors.
theorems.statement: The map is injective exactly when $r=m$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_R(I)=0$. For Noetherian $R$, the latter annihilator test at full rank is equivalent to $I=R$ or $I$ containing a nonzerodivisor.
theorems.proof: The map is injective exactly when $r=m$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_R(I)=0$. For Noetherian $R$, the latter annihilator test at full rank is equivalent to $I=R$ or $I$ containing a nonzerodivisor.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Vanishing dual of the cokernel of a square injection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:R^n\to R^n$ be injective, with $n$ finite.
theorems.statement: Every $R$-linear functional on $\operatorname{coker}(u)$ vanishes. Locally the determinant of $u$ is a nonzerodivisor and annihilates its cokernel.
theorems.proof: Every $R$-linear functional on $\operatorname{coker}(u)$ vanishes. Locally the determinant of $u$ is a nonzerodivisor and annihilates its cokernel.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Intersection of two flattening ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module and $I,J$ ideals. Assume $M/IM$ is $R/I$-flat and $M/JM$ is $R/J$-flat.
theorems.statement: Then $M/(I\cap J)M$ is flat over $R/(I\cap J)$.
theorems.proof: Then $M/(I\cap J)M$ is flat over $R/(I\cap J)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Universal property of the Artinian flattening ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Artinian, $M$ any $R$-module, $I$ its least flattening ideal, and $R\to B$ any ring map.
theorems.statement: The $B$-module $M\otimes_R B$ is flat if and only if $R\to B$ factors through $R/I$.
theorems.proof: The $B$-module $M\otimes_R B$ is flat if and only if $R\to B$ factors through $R/I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Base change of relative flatness above a closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R\to S$ and an $S$-module $M$. Let $R\to B$ carry $I\subseteq R$ into $H\subseteq B$. Set $T=S\otimes_R B$ and $N=M\otimes_R B$.
theorems.statement: If $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat at all primes over $V(I)$, then $N_{\mathfrak Q}$ is $B$-flat at all primes over $V(H)$.
theorems.proof: If $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat at all primes over $V(I)$, then $N_{\mathfrak Q}$ is $B$-flat at all primes over $V(H)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Descent of relative flatness above a closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R\to S$ and an $S$-module $M$. Let $R\to B$ carry $I\subseteq R$ into $H\subseteq B$. Set $T=S\otimes_R B$ and $N=M\otimes_R B$. The map $V(H)\to V(I)$ is surjective and $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $R$ for every $\mathfrak p\in V(H)$.
theorems.statement: If $N_{\mathfrak Q}$ is $B$-flat at all primes over $V(H)$, then $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat at all primes over $V(I)$.
theorems.proof: If $N_{\mathfrak Q}$ is $B$-flat at all primes over $V(H)$, then $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat at all primes over $V(I)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Detection of flatness above a closed subset at a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be finitely presented over $R$, and $M$ finitely presented over $S$. Let $B=\operatorname{colim}_i B_i$ be a directed colimit of $R$-algebras with $I_iB_j\subseteq I_j$ for $j\geq i$ and $I=\operatorname{colim}_i I_i$.
theorems.statement: If the base change to $B$ is flat above $V(I)$, then the base change to some $B_i$ is flat above $V(I_i)$.
theorems.proof: If the base change to $B$ is flat above $V(I)$, then the base change to some $B_i$ is flat above $V(I_i)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Base change of flatness on a prescribed source locus
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R\to S$ and an $S$-module $M$. Let $R\to B$ carry $I\subseteq R$ into $H\subseteq B$. Set $T=S\otimes_R B$ and $N=M\otimes_R B$. Fix $J\subseteq S$.
theorems.statement: Flatness of $M$ over $R$ at all primes of $V(IS+J)$ implies flatness of $N$ over $B$ at every prime of $V(HT+JT)$.
theorems.proof: Flatness of $M$ over $R$ at all primes of $V(IS+J)$ implies flatness of $N$ over $B$ at every prime of $V(HT+JT)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Descent of flatness on a prescribed source locus
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R\to S$ and an $S$-module $M$. Let $R\to B$ carry $I\subseteq R$ into $H\subseteq B$. Set $T=S\otimes_R B$ and $N=M\otimes_R B$. The map $V(H)\to V(I)$ is surjective and $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $R$ for every $\mathfrak p\in V(H)$. Fix $J\subseteq S$.
theorems.statement: Flatness of $N$ over $B$ at all primes of $V(HT+JT)$ implies flatness of $M$ over $R$ at every prime of $V(IS+J)$.
theorems.proof: Flatness of $N$ over $B$ at all primes of $V(HT+JT)$ implies flatness of $M$ over $R$ at every prime of $V(IS+J)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Limit criterion with a prescribed source locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be essentially of finite presentation over $R$, $M$ finitely presented over $S$, and $J\subseteq S$. Let $B=\operatorname{colim}_i B_i$ be a directed colimit of $R$-algebras with $I_iB_j\subseteq I_j$ for $j\geq i$ and $I=\operatorname{colim}_i I_i$.
theorems.statement: Flatness over $B$ at all primes containing the extended ideals $I$ and $J$ descends to flatness over some $B_i$ at every prime containing the extended ideals $I_i$ and $J$.
theorems.proof: Flatness over $B$ at all primes containing the extended ideals $I$ and $J$ descends to flatness over some $B_i$ at every prime containing the extended ideals $I_i$ and $J$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Adic flatness test along a source and base locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map of Noetherian rings, $M$ finite over $S$, and $I\subseteq R$, $J\subseteq S$ ideals. For every $n\geq1$ and every $\mathfrak q\supseteq J+IS$, assume $(M/I^nM)_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R/I^n$.
theorems.statement: At each such prime the module $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: At each such prime the module $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Universal flattening test for Noetherian local targets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be complete Noetherian local, $S$ a Noetherian $R$-algebra, $M$ a finite $S$-module, and $I$ the flattening ideal along the closed fibre. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(B,\mathfrak n)$ be local. Suppose $B$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The base change $M\otimes_R B$ is flat over $B$ at every prime of $S\otimes_R B$ over $\mathfrak n$ exactly when $IB=0$.
theorems.proof: The base change $M\otimes_R B$ is flat over $B$ at every prime of $S\otimes_R B$ over $\mathfrak n$ exactly when $IB=0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Universal flattening test for arbitrary local targets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be complete Noetherian local, $S$ a Noetherian $R$-algebra, $M$ a finite $S$-module, and $I$ the flattening ideal along the closed fibre. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(B,\mathfrak n)$ be local. Suppose $S$ is of finite type over $R$.
theorems.statement: The base change $M\otimes_R B$ is flat over $B$ at every prime of $S\otimes_R B$ over $\mathfrak n$ exactly when $IB=0$.
theorems.proof: The base change $M\otimes_R B$ is flat over $B$ at every prime of $S\otimes_R B$ over $\mathfrak n$ exactly when $IB=0$.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Division of a monic polynomial by a root factor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\in R[T]$ be monic of positive degree with $P(a)=0$ for $a\in R$.
theorems.statement: Division by $T-a$ gives $P=(T-a)Q$ with $Q$ monic.
theorems.proof: Division by $T-a$ gives $P=(T-a)Q$ with $Q$ monic.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: One root after finite free base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\in R[T]$ be monic of positive degree.
theorems.statement: Over $B=R[T]/(P)$ the tautological root splits off a linear factor of $P$. The powers of that root of degrees below $\deg P$ form a finite free basis of $B$.
theorems.proof: Over $B=R[T]/(P)$ the tautological root splits off a linear factor of $P$. The powers of that root of degrees below $\deg P$ form a finite free basis of $B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Split polynomial presentation after finite free extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite free extension $R\hookrightarrow B$ such that $S\otimes_R B$ is a quotient of $B[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(P_i(T_i))$, with each $P_i$ a product of monic linear factors in $B[T_i]$.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite free extension $R\hookrightarrow B$ such that $S\otimes_R B$ is a quotient of $B[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(P_i(T_i))$, with each $P_i$ a product of monic linear factors in $B[T_i]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Image on spectra of a split finite algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Write $S=R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/J$ with $\prod_j(T_i-a_{ij})\in J$ for every $i$. For each choice $\mathbf k$ of one root index per variable let $J_{\mathbf k}$ be the image of $J$ under evaluation at $(a_{i k_i})_i$.
theorems.statement: The image of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $V(\bigcap_{\mathbf k}J_{\mathbf k})$.
theorems.proof: The image of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $V(\bigcap_{\mathbf k}J_{\mathbf k})$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flat descent along a finite injection of Noetherian rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\hookrightarrow S$ be finite with both rings Noetherian. Let $M$ be any $R$-module.
theorems.statement: If $M\otimes_R S$ is $S$-flat, then $M$ is $R$-flat.
theorems.proof: If $M\otimes_R S$ is $S$-flat, then $M$ is $R$-flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flat descent for polynomial modules along integral injections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\hookrightarrow S$ be integral and let $M$ be finitely presented over $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.
theorems.statement: Flatness of $M\otimes_R S$ over $S$ implies flatness of $M$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: Flatness of $M\otimes_R S$ over $S$ implies flatness of $M$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Projectivity descends along a finite Noetherian injection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\hookrightarrow S$ be finite with both rings Noetherian. Let $P$ be any $R$-module.
theorems.statement: If $P\otimes_R S$ is projective over $S$, then $P$ is projective over $R$.
theorems.proof: If $P\otimes_R S$ is projective over $S$, then $P$ is projective over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Canonical torsion-free quotient via the generic fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be the fraction field of a domain $R$ and $M$ any $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The quotient by $\ker(M\to M\otimes_R K)$ embeds into $M\otimes_R K$. In particular $M/M_{\mathrm{tors}}$ is torsion free.
theorems.proof: The quotient by $\ker(M\to M\otimes_R K)$ embeds into $M\otimes_R K$. In particular $M/M_{\mathrm{tors}}$ is torsion free.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localization preserves torsion freeness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be torsion free over a domain $R$ and let $U$ be a multiplicative subset with $0\notin U$.
theorems.statement: The module $U^{-1}M$ is torsion free over $U^{-1}R$. If $0\in U$ the localization is the zero module over the zero ring.
theorems.proof: The module $U^{-1}M$ is torsion free over $U^{-1}R$. If $0\in U$ the localization is the zero module over the zero ring.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flat pullback of torsion-free modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a flat map between domains. Let $M$ be a torsion-free $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Then $M\otimes_R S$ is torsion free as an $S$-module.
theorems.proof: Then $M\otimes_R S$ is torsion free as an $S$-module.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Extension closure of torsion-free modules
theorems.hypotheses: In a short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ over a domain, assume $A$ and $C$ are torsion free.
theorems.statement: The middle module $B$ is torsion free. A torsion element maps to zero in $C$, and therefore comes from a torsion element in $A$.
theorems.proof: The middle module $B$ is torsion free. A torsion element maps to zero in $C$, and therefore comes from a torsion element in $A$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated-prime and Serre tests for torsion freeness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M\ne0$ be finite over a Noetherian domain $R$ with generic point $\eta=(0)$.
theorems.statement: The following conditions are equivalent. The module is torsion free. It embeds in a finite free module. Its associated-prime set is $\{\eta\}$. Its support contains $\eta$ and it satisfies $(S_1)$. Its support contains $\eta$ and it has no embedded associated primes.
theorems.proof: The following conditions are equivalent. The module is torsion free. It embeds in a finite free module. Its associated-prime set is $\{\eta\}$. Its support contains $\eta$ and it satisfies $(S_1)$. Its support contains $\eta$ and it has no embedded associated primes.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Hom into a torsion-free module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L,N$ be modules over a domain $R$ and suppose $N$ is torsion free.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,N)$ is torsion free, since each function value of a torsion homomorphism is a torsion element of $N$.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,N)$ is torsion free, since each function value of a torsion homomorphism is a torsion element of $N$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Surjectivity of bidual evaluation over a DVR
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over a discrete valuation ring $R$.
theorems.statement: The canonical evaluation $M\to M^{**}$ is surjective. It factors through the finite free quotient by torsion.
theorems.proof: The canonical evaluation $M\to M^{**}$ is surjective. It factors through the finite free quotient by torsion.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Kernel in a reflexive module with torsion-free quotient image
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $0\to L\to M\to N$ is exact over a Noetherian domain and all three modules are finite. Assume $M$ is reflexive and $N$ torsion free.
theorems.statement: Then $L$ is reflexive. The map to $N$ may have proper image.
theorems.proof: Then $L$ is reflexive. The map to $N$ may have proper image.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flat pullback of a finite reflexive module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a flat map of Noetherian domains and $M$ a finite reflexive $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The finite $S$-module $M\otimes_R S$ is reflexive.
theorems.proof: The finite $S$-module $M\otimes_R S$ is reflexive.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Depth at least one or two passes to an internal Hom
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and $L,N$ finite $R$-modules. Choose $d\in\{1,2\}$.
theorems.statement: If $\operatorname{depth}N\geq d$, then $\operatorname{depth}\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,N)\geq d$.
theorems.proof: If $\operatorname{depth}N\geq d$, then $\operatorname{depth}\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,N)\geq d$.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Preservation of low Serre conditions by Hom
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $L,N$ finite $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: For $i=1,2$, if $N$ satisfies $(S_i)$ then $\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,N)$ satisfies $(S_i)$. Over a domain, when $N$ is also torsion free, the Hom module is torsion free as well.
theorems.proof: For $i=1,2$, if $N$ satisfies $(S_i)$ then $\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,N)$ satisfies $(S_i)$. Over a domain, when $N$ is also torsion free, the Hom module is torsion free as well.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Testing injectivity at associated primes of the source
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:M\to N$ be any module map over a Noetherian ring. Suppose $u_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$.
theorems.statement: Then $u$ is injective. A nonzero kernel would have an associated prime among those of $M$.
theorems.proof: Then $u$ is injective. A nonzero kernel would have an associated prime among those of $M$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Extending an isomorphism across the depth-two locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:M\to N$ be a module map over a Noetherian ring, with $M$ finite. At each prime where $u_{\mathfrak p}$ is not an isomorphism, assume $\operatorname{depth}M_{\mathfrak p}\geq2$ and $\mathfrak p\notin\operatorname{Ass}(N)$.
theorems.statement: Then $u$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Then $u$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Depth-two extension into a torsion-free target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:M\to N$ be a map over a Noetherian domain with $M$ finite and $N$ torsion free. At every prime where $u_{\mathfrak p}$ fails to be an isomorphism, assume $\operatorname{depth}M_{\mathfrak p}\geq2$.
theorems.statement: The map $u$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The map $u$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexivity tested away from depth at least two
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over a Noetherian domain $R$.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is reflexive exactly when $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is reflexive at every prime with $\operatorname{depth}M_{\mathfrak p}<2$.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is reflexive exactly when $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is reflexive at every prime with $\operatorname{depth}M_{\mathfrak p}<2$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth bounds inherited by a reflexive module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite reflexive over a Noetherian domain $R$.
theorems.statement: At every $\mathfrak p$ where $\operatorname{depth}R_{\mathfrak p}\geq2$ one has $\operatorname{depth}M_{\mathfrak p}\geq2$. In particular, if $R$ satisfies $(S_2)$ then $M$ does too.
theorems.proof: At every $\mathfrak p$ where $\operatorname{depth}R_{\mathfrak p}\geq2$ one has $\operatorname{depth}M_{\mathfrak p}\geq2$. In particular, if $R$ satisfies $(S_2)$ then $M$ does too.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Reflexivity of a finite integral closure
theorems.hypotheses: Take a Noetherian normal domain $R$ with fraction field $K$, a finite field extension $L/K$, and the integral closure $B$ of $R$ in $L$. Suppose $B$ is a finite $R$-module.
theorems.statement: As an $R$-module, $B$ is reflexive.
theorems.proof: As an $R$-module, $B$ is reflexive.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Finite presentation from prime-local presentations
theorems.hypotheses: There is a finite set of primes $\mathfrak p_i$ of $R$ with $R\hookrightarrow\prod_iR_{\mathfrak p_i}$. Let $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and let $M$ be finite over $P$ and flat over $R$. For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, assume $M_{\mathfrak p}$ finitely presented over $P_{\mathfrak p}$, using localization on the base.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is finitely presented over $P$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is finitely presented over $P$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite presentation of a flat finite type algebra from all base localizations
theorems.hypotheses: There is a finite set of primes $\mathfrak p_i$ of $R$ with $R\hookrightarrow\prod_iR_{\mathfrak p_i}$. Suppose $R\to S$ is flat and of finite type and $S\otimes_R R_{\mathfrak p}$ is finitely presented over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime of $R$.
theorems.statement: The $R$-algebra $S$ is finitely presented.
theorems.proof: The $R$-algebra $S$ is finitely presented.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Finite presentation over a graded polynomial algebra over a local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local and $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ graded with $\deg x_i>0$. Suppose $M$ is a finite graded $P$-module and is flat over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is finitely presented over $P$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is finitely presented over $P$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flatness and finite presentation for a graded algebra and its modules
theorems.hypotheses: There is a finite set of primes $\mathfrak p_i$ of $R$ with $R\hookrightarrow\prod_iR_{\mathfrak p_i}$. Suppose $S$ is a nonnegatively graded finitely generated $R$-algebra with $S_0$ finite over $R$. Let $M$ be a $\mathbf Z$-graded $S$-module.
theorems.statement: If $S$ is $R$-flat, it is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra. If $M$ is $R$-flat and finite over $S$, it is finitely presented over $S$.
theorems.proof: If $S$ is $R$-flat, it is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra. If $M$ is $R$-flat and finite over $S$, it is finitely presented over $S$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Sufficient conditions for detection by finitely many localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring.
theorems.statement: The finite localization test holds for local rings, Noetherian rings, domains, reduced rings with finitely many minimal primes, and rings with finitely many weakly associated primes.
theorems.proof: The finite localization test holds for local rings, Noetherian rings, domains, reduced rings with finitely many minimal primes, and rings with finitely many weakly associated primes.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flat finite modules over a finite type algebra over a valuation ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, $B$ a finite type $A$-algebra and $M$ a finite $B$-module.
theorems.statement: If $M$ is flat over $A$, it is finitely presented over $B$. If $B$ is flat over $A$, the algebra $B$ is finitely presented over $A$.
theorems.proof: If $M$ is flat over $A$, it is finitely presented over $B$. If $B$ is flat over $A$, the algebra $B$ is finitely presented over $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Essential finite presentation over a valuation base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism essentially of finite type and let $M$ be finite over $B$.
theorems.statement: If $B$ is $A$-flat then $B$ is essentially of finite presentation over $A$. If $M$ is $A$-flat then $M$ is finitely presented over $B$.
theorems.proof: If $B$ is $A$-flat then $B$ is essentially of finite presentation over $A$. If $M$ is $A$-flat then $M$ is finitely presented over $B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Flattening strict transforms on a chart chosen by a valuation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local domain with $\mathfrak m\ne0$, let a valuation ring $V$ in its fraction field dominate $R$, and take a finite type $R$-algebra $S$ with a finite $S$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: There exist a finitely generated $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and nonzero $a\in I$ such that $V$ has centre on $B=R[I/a]$ and $B/\mathfrak m B\ne0$. On this chart the strict transform of $S$ is flat and finitely presented over $B$, and that of $M$ is flat over $B$ and finitely presented over the transformed algebra. The proof descends a presentation from the valuation ring to the chart. For a field base the identity chart suffices.
theorems.proof: There exist a finitely generated $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and nonzero $a\in I$ such that $V$ has centre on $B=R[I/a]$ and $B/\mathfrak m B\ne0$. On this chart the strict transform of $S$ is flat and finitely presented over $B$, and that of $M$ is flat over $B$ and finitely presented over the transformed algebra. The proof descends a presentation from the valuation ring to the chart. For a field base the identity chart suffices.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: The transformed Fitting ideal is the unit ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module, $k\geq0$, $I=\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)$, and $a\in I$. Set $B=R[I/a]$ and let $M'$ be the quotient of $M\otimes_R B$ by its $a$-power torsion.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M')=B$.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M')=B$.

theorems.subject: module-index
theorems.name: A Fitting blowup giving a locally free strict transform
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over $R$, $k\geq0$, $I=\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)$, and assume $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is free of rank $k$ for every $\mathfrak p\notin V(I)$.
theorems.statement: For every $a\in I$ the strict transform of $M$ over $R[I/a]$ is locally free of rank $k$.
theorems.proof: For every $a\in I$ the strict transform of $M$ over $R[I/a]$ is locally free of rank $k$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Making a module locally free by blowing up a prescribed locus
theorems.hypotheses: Take a finite $R$-module $M$ and $f\in R$ such that $M_f$ is finite locally free of constant rank $r$.
theorems.statement: There is a finitely generated ideal $I$ with $V(I)=V(f)$ such that the strict transform on every chart $R[I/a]$, $a\in I$, is locally free of rank $r$.
theorems.proof: There is a finitely generated ideal $I$ with $V(I)=V(f)$ such that the strict transform on every chart $R[I/a]$, $a\in I$, is locally free of rank $r$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Universal injectivity from a completed free sum to a product
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R$ is Noetherian and complete for an ideal $I$. Let $E$ be any set.
theorems.statement: The natural map from the $I$-adic completion of $R^{(E)}$ to $R^E$ remains injective after tensoring with every $R$-module.
theorems.proof: The natural map from the $I$-adic completion of $R^{(E)}$ to $R^E$ remains injective after tensoring with every $R$-module.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Flatness of a completed free module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $I$ any ideal and $E$ any set.
theorems.statement: The $I$-adic completion of the free module $R^{(E)}$ is flat over $R$.
theorems.proof: The $I$-adic completion of the free module $R^{(E)}$ is flat over $R$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Strict pro-vanishing of positive Tor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian, $I$ any ideal, and $M$ finite over $A$. Fix an integer $p>0$.
theorems.statement: There is a shift $c>0$ such that for every $n\geq c$ the transition $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^n)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^{n-c})$ vanishes.
theorems.proof: There is a shift $c>0$ such that for every $n\geq c$ the transition $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^n)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^{n-c})$ vanishes.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Flat inverse limits along surjections modulo powers of an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I$ any ideal. Let $(M_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system of $A$-modules with $M_n$ flat over $A/I^n$ and each transition $M_{n+1}\to M_n$ surjective.
theorems.statement: Its inverse limit $M$ is flat over $A$. For every finite $A$-module $Q$ the canonical map $Q\otimes_A M\to\varprojlim_n(Q\otimes_A M_n)$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Its inverse limit $M$ is flat over $A$. For every finite $A$-module $Q$ the canonical map $Q\otimes_A M\to\varprojlim_n(Q\otimes_A M_n)$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Flatness over the completed base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be finitely generated in $R$, $R/I$ Noetherian, $M/IM$ flat over $R/I$, and $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(M,R/I)=0$.
theorems.statement: The $I$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is Noetherian and $\widehat M$ is flat over $\widehat R$.
theorems.proof: The $I$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is Noetherian and $\widehat M$ is flat over $\widehat R$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Functoriality of the Koszul differential graded algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:E\to R$, $\varphi':E'\to R$ be linear with $\varphi'\psi=\varphi$ for a linear $\psi:E\to E'$.
theorems.statement: The exterior algebra map induced by $\psi$ is a morphism $K_\bullet(\varphi)\to K_\bullet(\varphi')$ of differential graded algebras.
theorems.proof: The exterior algebra map induced by $\psi$ is a morphism $K_\bullet(\varphi)\to K_\bullet(\varphi')$ of differential graded algebras.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Invariance of a Koszul complex under an invertible matrix
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a tuple of $r$ elements of $R$ and let $U\in\operatorname{GL}_r(R)$.
theorems.statement: The Koszul complexes of $f$ and $Uf$ are isomorphic by change of basis.
theorems.proof: The Koszul complexes of $f$ and $Uf$ are isomorphic by change of basis.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Exterior multiplication gives a Koszul homotopy
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:E\to R$ be linear, $e\in E$, and $h$ exterior multiplication on the left by $e$ on $K_\bullet(\varphi)$.
theorems.statement: Then $dh+hd=\varphi(e)\operatorname{id}$.
theorems.proof: Then $dh+hd=\varphi(e)\operatorname{id}$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The defining ideal annihilates Koszul homology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ be elements of $R$.
theorems.statement: Multiplication by each $f_i$ is null homotopic on $K_\bullet(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Thus $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ annihilates every homology module.
theorems.proof: Multiplication by each $f_i$ is null homotopic on $K_\bullet(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Thus $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ annihilates every homology module.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Mapping cone after adjoining a free summand to a Koszul map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:E\to R$ be linear and $f\in R$. Enlarge it to $\psi:E\oplus R\to R$ by $\psi(e,t)=\varphi(e)+ft$.
theorems.statement: The complex $K_\bullet(\psi)$ is isomorphic to the mapping cone of $f:K_\bullet(\varphi)\to K_\bullet(\varphi)$.
theorems.proof: The complex $K_\bullet(\psi)$ is isomorphic to the mapping cone of $f:K_\bullet(\varphi)\to K_\bullet(\varphi)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Appending an element to a finite Koszul sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ with $r\geq1$ and let $K$ be the Koszul complex of its first $r-1$ entries.
theorems.statement: The full Koszul complex is isomorphic to the cone of multiplication by $f_r$ on $K$.
theorems.proof: The full Koszul complex is isomorphic to the cone of multiplication by $f_r$ on $K$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Cone of a product of scalar maps
theorems.hypotheses: For a homological complex $A$ and $f,g\in R$, write $C(s)$ for the cone of $s:A\to A$. Use the source shift in which a degree-zero copy of $R$ moves to degree $-1$ under $[1]$.
theorems.statement: There exists a chain map $C(f)[1]\to C(g)$ whose cone is homotopy equivalent to $C(fg)$.
theorems.proof: There exists a chain map $C(f)[1]\to C(g)$ whose cone is homotopy equivalent to $C(fg)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Product of two appended Koszul scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $\varphi:E\to R$ and let $K(s)$ be the Koszul complex of the extension $E\oplus R\to R$ given by $(e,t)\mapsto\varphi(e)+st$. Use the homological shift convention of the source.
theorems.statement: The complex $K(fg)$ is homotopy equivalent to the cone of a chain map $K(f)[1]\to K(g)$.
theorems.proof: The complex $K(fg)$ is homotopy equivalent to the cone of a chain map $K(f)[1]\to K(g)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Koszul cone for a product at the end of a sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a tuple over $R$ and let $K(s)$ denote the Koszul complex after appending $s$. Use the homological shift convention of the source.
theorems.statement: For $f,g\in R$ there is a map $K(f)[1]\to K(g)$ whose cone has the homotopy type of $K(fg)$.
theorems.proof: For $f,g\in R$ there is a map $K(f)[1]\to K(g)$ whose cone has the homotopy type of $K(fg)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Concatenation of tuples gives a total tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ and $g$ be finite sequences in $R$.
theorems.statement: The Koszul complex of their concatenation is isomorphic to the total complex of $K_\bullet(f)\otimes_R K_\bullet(g)$ with the usual signed tensor differential.
theorems.proof: The Koszul complex of their concatenation is isomorphic to the total complex of $K_\bullet(f)\otimes_R K_\bullet(g)$ with the usual signed tensor differential.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensoring the ring Čech complex with coefficients
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $R$ and an $R$-module $M$. Let $C^\bullet(f;M)$ denote the extended alternating Čech complex.
theorems.statement: Degreewise localization identifies $C^\bullet(f;M)$ with $C^\bullet(f;R)\otimes_R M$, including the alternating restriction differentials.
theorems.proof: Degreewise localization identifies $C^\bullet(f;M)$ with $C^\bullet(f;R)\otimes_R M$, including the alternating restriction differentials.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Arbitrary base change of the extended Čech complex
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $R$ and an $R$-module $M$. Let $C^\bullet(f;M)$ denote the extended alternating Čech complex. Let $R\to S$ send $f$ to $g$ and put $N=M\otimes_R S$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $C^\bullet(f;M)\otimes_R S\cong C^\bullet(g;N)$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical isomorphism $C^\bullet(f;M)\otimes_R S\cong C^\bullet(g;N)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Contractibility in the presence of a unit
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $R$ and an $R$-module $M$. Let $C^\bullet(f;M)$ denote the extended alternating Čech complex. Assume at least one $f_i$ is a unit in $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $C^\bullet(f;M)$ is chain homotopy equivalent to zero.
theorems.proof: Then $C^\bullet(f;M)$ is chain homotopy equivalent to zero.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Support and torsion of extended Čech cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $R$ and an $R$-module $M$. Let $C^\bullet(f;M)$ denote the extended alternating Čech complex.
theorems.statement: Cohomology vanishes outside degrees $0,\ldots,r$. Each class in each degree is killed by some power of every $f_i$, and its support lies in $V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. If an element of $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ acts invertibly on $M$, all cohomology vanishes.
theorems.proof: Cohomology vanishes outside degrees $0,\ldots,r$. Each class in each degree is killed by some power of every $f_i$, and its support lies in $V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. If an element of $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ acts invertibly on $M$, all cohomology vanishes.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The extended Čech complex as a filtered Koszul colimit
theorems.hypotheses: For a tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ use the Koszul complexes of the tuples $(f_1^n,\ldots,f_r^n)$, reindexed so the top exterior power is in cochain degree zero. On the exterior basis indexed by $J$, the transition to $n+1$ multiplies by $\prod_{i\notin J} f_i$.
theorems.statement: The colimit complex is isomorphic to $C^\bullet(f;R)$, with the complementary index sets identifying the localized summands after the sign adjustment in the source.
theorems.proof: The colimit complex is isomorphic to $C^\bullet(f;R)$, with the complementary index sets identifying the localized summands after the sign adjustment in the source.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Čech vanishing below the length of a Koszul-regular sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ is a Koszul-regular sequence in $R$.
theorems.statement: The complex $C^\bullet(f;R)$ has vanishing cohomology in every degree different from $r$.
theorems.proof: The complex $C^\bullet(f;R)$ has vanishing cohomology in every degree different from $r$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Presentation of the blowup chart for an H₁-regular tuple
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $a,a_2,\ldots,a_r$ is $H_1$-regular in $R$, and put $I=(a,a_2,\ldots,a_r)$.
theorems.statement: The map $R[y_2,\ldots,y_r]/(ay_i-a_i)\to R[I/a]$ sending $y_i$ to $a_i/a$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The map $R[y_2,\ldots,y_r]/(ay_i-a_i)\to R[I/a]$ sending $y_i$ to $a_i/a$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: First Koszul homology under base change with flat quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with $B/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ flat over $A$, and let $A\to A'$ be arbitrary. Write $B'=B\otimes_A A'$ and $f'$ for the image tuple.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $H_1(K_\bullet(B,f))\otimes_A A'\to H_1(K_\bullet(B',f'))$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $H_1(K_\bullet(B,f))\otimes_A A'\to H_1(K_\bullet(B',f'))$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Two regularity conditions under base change with flat quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with $B/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ flat over $A$. Base change by any $A\to A'$.
theorems.statement: If the tuple is quasi-regular in $B$ its image is quasi-regular in $B\otimes_A A'$. If the tuple is $H_1$-regular, its image is $H_1$-regular.
theorems.proof: If the tuple is quasi-regular in $B$ its image is quasi-regular in $B\otimes_A A'$. If the tuple is $H_1$-regular, its image is $H_1$-regular.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flatness of a lifted quasi-regular quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to B'$ be flat and finitely presented with a locally nilpotent ideal $I\subseteq A'$. Put $A=A'/I$, $B=B'/IB'$. Fix $f'_1,\ldots,f'_r$ in $B'$ with quasi-regular reductions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $B$. Assume $B/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is flat over $A$.
theorems.statement: Then $B'/(f'_1,\ldots,f'_r)$ is flat over $A'$.
theorems.proof: Then $B'/(f'_1,\ldots,f'_r)$ is flat over $A'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
