theorems.name: Smoothness of a lifted quasi-regular quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\to B'$ be flat and finitely presented with a locally nilpotent ideal $I\subseteq A'$. Put $A=A'/I$, $B=B'/IB'$. Fix $f'_1,\ldots,f'_r$ in $B'$ with quasi-regular reductions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $B$. Assume $B/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is smooth over $A$.
theorems.statement: Then $B'/(f'_1,\ldots,f'_r)$ is smooth over $A'$.
theorems.proof: Then $B'/(f'_1,\ldots,f'_r)$ is smooth over $A'$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of three ideal regularity conditions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be faithfully flat and let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal.
theorems.statement: For each of Koszul-regularity, $H_1$-regularity, and quasi-regularity of ideals, if $IB$ has the property then $I$ has it.
theorems.proof: For each of Koszul-regularity, $H_1$-regularity, and quasi-regularity of ideals, if $IB$ has the property then $I$ has it.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: An intersection identity from relative H₁-regularity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq J$ be ideals of $A$ with $J/I$ an $H_1$-regular ideal in $A/I$.
theorems.statement: Then $I\cap J^2=IJ$.
theorems.proof: Then $I\cap J^2=IJ$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Independence of the Koszul-regular presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B$ be a finite type $A$-algebra with one finite polynomial presentation having a Koszul-regular kernel.
theorems.statement: The kernel of every finite polynomial presentation of $B$ over $A$ is Koszul-regular.
theorems.proof: The kernel of every finite polynomial presentation of $B$ over $A$ is Koszul-regular.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Gluing local complete intersection maps on the target spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ generate the unit ideal of $S$. Assume $R\to S_{g_i}$ is a local complete intersection for every $i$.
theorems.statement: Then $R\to S$ is a local complete intersection.
theorems.proof: Then $R\to S$ is a local complete intersection.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Koszul regularity of the equations of a relative global complete intersection
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose the given presentation $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection.
theorems.statement: The specified tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is Koszul-regular in the polynomial ring.
theorems.proof: The specified tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is Koszul-regular in the polynomial ring.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Cotangent transitivity with a terminal local complete intersection
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A\to B\to C$ with $B\to C$ a local complete intersection. For compatible polynomial presentations let $I,J,K$ be the kernels for $B/A$, $C/B$, and $C/A$, respectively.
theorems.statement: The conormal sequence $0\to(I/I^2)\otimes_B C\to K/K^2\to J/J^2\to0$ is exact and maps to the exact sequence of the polynomial differential modules tensored up to $C$. Writing $\mathrm{NL}$ for the naive cotangent complex, the sequence $0\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C)\to H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$ is exact.
theorems.proof: The conormal sequence $0\to(I/I^2)\otimes_B C\to K/K^2\to J/J^2\to0$ is exact and maps to the exact sequence of the polynomial differential modules tensored up to $C$. Writing $\mathrm{NL}$ for the naive cotangent complex, the sequence $0\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C)\to H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$ is exact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Cotangent transitivity with a terminal filtered colimit of local complete intersections
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A\to B\to C$ with $C$ a filtered colimit of local complete intersection $B$-algebras.
theorems.statement: Writing $\mathrm{NL}$ for the naive cotangent complex, the sequence $0\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C)\to H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$ is exact.
theorems.proof: Writing $\mathrm{NL}$ for the naive cotangent complex, the sequence $0\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C)\to H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B C\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$ is exact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The naive cotangent complex after henselizing a local homomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take a local homomorphism $A\to B$. For strict henselizations choose compatible separable closures of the residue fields.
theorems.statement: The comparison $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B^h\to\mathrm{NL}_{B^h/A^h}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Replacing both henselizations by the chosen strict henselizations gives another quasi-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The comparison $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B^h\to\mathrm{NL}_{B^h/A^h}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Replacing both henselizations by the chosen strict henselizations gives another quasi-isomorphism.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Cartier equality for a finitely generated extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension.
theorems.statement: Both $\Omega_{K/k}$ and $H_1(L_{K/k})$ have finite dimension over $K$, and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k K=\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}-\dim_K H_1(L_{K/k})$.
theorems.proof: Both $\Omega_{K/k}$ and $H_1(L_{K/k})$ have finite dimension over $K$, and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k K=\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}-\dim_K H_1(L_{K/k})$.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Jacobi–Zariski exact sequence for a tower of fields
theorems.hypotheses: Consider any field tower $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_L M\to H_1(L_{M/K})\to H_1(L_{M/L})\to \Omega_{L/K}\otimes_L M\to\Omega_{M/K}\to\Omega_{M/L}\to0$ is exact.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_L M\to H_1(L_{M/K})\to H_1(L_{M/L})\to \Omega_{L/K}\otimes_L M\to\Omega_{M/K}\to\Omega_{M/L}\to0$ is exact.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Defect formula for differentials and cotangent homology in a field square
theorems.hypotheses: Consider compatible embeddings $k\to k'$, $K\to K'$ over extensions $K/k$ and $K'/k'$, where $k'/k$ and $K'/K$ are finitely generated. Write $\alpha$ and $\beta$ for the induced maps on differentials and first cotangent homology after extending scalars from $K$ to $K'$.
theorems.statement: Both kernels and cokernels are finite dimensional. Writing $e(u)=\dim_{K'}\ker u-\dim_{K'}\operatorname{coker}u$, one has $e(\alpha)-e(\beta)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k k'-\operatorname{trdeg}_K K'$.
theorems.proof: Both kernels and cokernels are finite dimensional. Writing $e(u)=\dim_{K'}\ker u-\dim_{K'}\operatorname{coker}u$, one has $e(\alpha)-e(\beta)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k k'-\operatorname{trdeg}_K K'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Four tests for geometric regularity in positive characteristic
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ be a Noetherian local algebra over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$.
theorems.statement: Geometric regularity is equivalent to regularity of $A\otimes_k k'$ for each finite $k'/k$ in $k^{1/p}$. It is also equivalent to regularity of $A$ together with injectivity of $H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, or to regularity of $A$ together with injectivity of $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_k K\to\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_A K$.
theorems.proof: Geometric regularity is equivalent to regularity of $A\otimes_k k'$ for each finite $k'/k$ in $k^{1/p}$. It is also equivalent to regularity of $A$ together with injectivity of $H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, or to regularity of $A$ together with injectivity of $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_k K\to\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_A K$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat polynomial coordinates with regular quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ be a geometrically regular Noetherian local algebra over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$ with $F/k$ finitely generated. Choose $k[y_1,\ldots,y_s]\to A$ with residues in $F$ whose differentials form a basis for $\Omega_{F/k}$. Let $\mathfrak p$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: The induced map $k[y_1,\ldots,y_s]_{\mathfrak p}\to A$ is flat and $A/\mathfrak p A$ is regular.
theorems.proof: The induced map $k[y_1,\ldots,y_s]_{\mathfrak p}\to A$ is flat and $A/\mathfrak p A$ is regular.

theorems.subject: topological-module
theorems.name: Baire category for complete linearly topologized groups
theorems.hypotheses: Let $G$ be a complete separated linearly topologized abelian group with a countable neighbourhood basis at zero.
theorems.statement: For every sequence of open dense subsets of $G$ their intersection is dense. Here an abelian group can be regarded as a module over discrete $\mathbf Z$.
theorems.proof: For every sequence of open dense subsets of $G$ their intersection is dense. Here an abelian group can be regarded as a module over discrete $\mathbf Z$.

theorems.subject: topological-module
theorems.name: A closed subgroup in a countable cover is open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $G$ be a complete separated linearly topologized abelian group with a countable neighbourhood basis at zero. Suppose countably many closed subgroups cover $G$.
theorems.statement: At least one of the subgroups is open.
theorems.proof: At least one of the subgroups is open.

theorems.subject: topological-module-map
theorems.name: Open mapping alternative for topological abelian groups
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:N\to M$ be a continuous group homomorphism, $M$ separated, and $N$ complete, linearly topologized, with a countable neighbourhood basis at zero.
theorems.statement: Exactly one alternative holds. The map is open, or there exists an open subgroup $N'$ whose image has closure with empty interior in $M$.
theorems.proof: Exactly one alternative holds. The map is open, or there exists an open subgroup $N'$ whose image has closure with empty interior in $M$.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Formal smoothness lifts a continuous map through an adic quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology on $S$. Let $T$ be adic and $J\subseteq T$ closed with some $J^t$ contained in an ideal of definition. Take a compatible continuous square from $R\to S$ to $T\to T/J$, with quotient topology on $T/J$.
theorems.statement: There is a continuous $R$-algebra lift $S\to T$.
theorems.proof: There is a continuous $R$-algebra lift $S\to T$.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Formal smoothness after enlarging the adic ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to S$ and ideals $\mathfrak n\subseteq\mathfrak n'$ in $S$. Suppose the map is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.
theorems.statement: It is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak n'$-adic topology.
theorems.proof: It is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak n'$-adic topology.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of formally smooth continuous ring maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be continuous formally smooth maps of linearly topologized rings.
theorems.statement: The composite $A\to C$ is formally smooth.
theorems.proof: The composite $A\to C$ is formally smooth.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Arbitrary base change of adic formal smoothness
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology. For any $R\to B$ set $T=S\otimes_R B$.
theorems.statement: The map $B\to T$ is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak n T$-adic topology.
theorems.proof: The map $B\to T$ is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak n T$-adic topology.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Descent of adic formal smoothness along a module splitting
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to B$ admits an $R$-linear retraction. For $R\to S$ and $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$, put $T=S\otimes_R B$ and assume $B\to T$ formally smooth in the $\mathfrak nT$-adic topology.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to S$ is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to S$ is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Infinitesimal local test for adic formal smoothness
theorems.hypotheses: Take a local map $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ and give $S$ its $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness is equivalent to lifting every local square from this map to $A\to A/J$ with $J^2=0$, nilpotent maximal ideal of the local ring $A$, and $S\to A/J$ inducing a residue-field isomorphism. If $S$ is Noetherian, testing only such small extensions suffices.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness is equivalent to lifting every local square from this map to $A\to A/J$ with $J^2=0$, nilpotent maximal ideal of the local ring $A$, and $S\to A/J$ inducing a residue-field isomorphism. If $S$ is Noetherian, testing only such small extensions suffices.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Adic formal smoothness of a local algebra over a field implies regularity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $(A,\mathfrak m)$ a Noetherian local $k$-algebra. Suppose $k\to A$ is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology.
theorems.statement: Then $A$ is regular local.
theorems.proof: Then $A$ is regular local.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Lifting a separable residue field into a complete local algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a complete local $k$-algebra with $\kappa/k$ separable.
theorems.statement: The residue map admits a $k$-algebra section $\kappa\to A$.
theorems.proof: The residue map admits a $k$-algebra section $\kappa\to A$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Complete regular local algebra over a field with separable residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Take a complete regular local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ with $\kappa/k$ separable and $d=\dim A$.
theorems.statement: As a $k$-algebra, $A$ is isomorphic to $\kappa[[t_1,\ldots,t_d]]$.
theorems.proof: As a $k$-algebra, $A$ is isomorphic to $\kappa[[t_1,\ldots,t_d]]$.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Regular local algebra with separable residue field is adically formally smooth
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a regular local $k$-algebra with $\kappa/k$ separable.
theorems.statement: The map $k\to A$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology.
theorems.proof: The map $k\to A$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Detecting smoothness of finite type maps by adic formal smoothness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be of finite type, $A$ Noetherian, and let $\mathfrak q$ lie over $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: The map is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ exactly when $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology on $B_{\mathfrak q}$.
theorems.proof: The map is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ exactly when $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology on $B_{\mathfrak q}$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Splitting a specified tuple near a maximal ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finitely presented over $R$ and give the space $\Omega$ of maximal ideals the subspace topology from $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. For $x\in\Omega$ write $M(x)=M/xM$. Let $V(x)$ be the quotient of $M(x)$ by the common kernel of the reductions of all maps $M\to R$. Fix $x\in\Omega$ and $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in M$.
theorems.statement: The map $R^r\to M$ with columns $s_i$ is split injective over some $R_f$ with $f\notin x$ exactly when the classes of the $s_i$ in $V(x)$ are linearly independent. A nonvanishing determinant of the functional evaluations produces the retraction.
theorems.proof: The map $R^r\to M$ with columns $s_i$ is split injective over some $R_f$ with $f\notin x$ exactly when the classes of the $s_i$ in $V(x)$ are linearly independent. A nonvanishing determinant of the functional evaluations produces the retraction.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Simultaneous interpolation in finitely many splitting quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finitely presented over $R$ and give the space $\Omega$ of maximal ideals the subspace topology from $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. For $x\in\Omega$ write $M(x)=M/xM$. Let $V(x)$ be the quotient of $M(x)$ by the common kernel of the reductions of all maps $M\to R$. Choose distinct $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\Omega$ and arbitrary $v_i\in V(x_i)$.
theorems.statement: One element of $M$ induces all $v_i$. The Chinese remainder theorem surjects $M$ onto the direct sum of the residue fibres, and these fibres surject onto the indicated quotients.
theorems.proof: One element of $M$ induces all $v_i$. The Chinese remainder theorem surjects $M$ onto the direct sum of the residue fibres, and these fibres surject onto the indicated quotients.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Serre’s codimension bound for the dependence locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finitely presented over $R$ and give the space $\Omega$ of maximal ideals the subspace topology from $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. For $x\in\Omega$ write $M(x)=M/xM$. Let $V(x)$ be the quotient of $M(x)$ by the common kernel of the reductions of all maps $M\to R$. Assume $\Omega$ is Noetherian. Fix $s_1,\ldots,s_h\in M$. Let $Z(\mathbf s)$ consist of points where their images in $V(x)$ are dependent. Choose a closed $F\supseteq Z(\mathbf s)$, finitely many distinct $x_i\in F$ with prescribed $v_i\in V(x_i)$, and $k\ge0$ such that $h+k\le\dim V(x)$ for every $x\in\Omega$.
theorems.statement: There exist $s\in M$ attaining all $v_i$ and a closed $F'\subseteq\Omega$ with $Z(\mathbf s,s)\subseteq F\cup F'$. Every irreducible component of $F'$ has codimension at least $k$ in $\Omega$.
theorems.proof: There exist $s\in M$ attaining all $v_i$ and a closed $F'\subseteq\Omega$ with $Z(\mathbf s,s)\subseteq F\cup F'$. Every irreducible component of $F'$ has codimension at least $k$ in $\Omega$.
refs: Serre, Modules projectifs et espaces fibrés à fibre vectorielle, Exposé 23 (1958)

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Eilenberg absorption for an infinite free module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a free module which is not finitely generated. Suppose $P\oplus Q\cong F$.
theorems.statement: There is an isomorphism $P\oplus F\cong F$. A countable direct sum of copies of $F$ is isomorphic to $F$, and regrouping the copies of $P$ and $Q$ absorbs one extra $P$.
theorems.proof: There is an isomorphism $P\oplus F\cong F$. A countable direct sum of copies of $F$ is isomorphic to $F$, and regrouping the copies of $P$ and $Q$ absorbs one extra $P$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite free stabilization around a single element
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be projective over any ring $R$ and choose $s\in P$.
theorems.statement: There are a finite free module $F$ and a finite free direct summand $K$ of $F\oplus P$ containing $(0,s)$. Stabilize first by a possibly infinite free module, then use that $s$ and the generators of its containing summand have finite support.
theorems.proof: There are a finite free module $F$ and a finite free direct summand $K$ of $F\oplus P$ containing $(0,s)$. Stabilize first by a possibly infinite free module, then use that $s$ and the generators of its containing summand have finite support.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A unimodular representative of a specified coset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be a projective $R$-module, assume $R/\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ is Noetherian, and assume $P_{\mathfrak m}$ has infinite rank at each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Fix $s\in P$ and a submodule $N\subseteq P$ with $Rs+N=P$.
theorems.statement: Some $n\in N$ and $R$-linear functional $\lambda:P\to R$ satisfy $\lambda(s+n)=1$. In particular $R(s+n)$ is a copy of $R$ splitting off $P$.
theorems.proof: Some $n\in N$ and $R$-linear functional $\lambda:P\to R$ satisfy $\lambda(s+n)=1$. In particular $R(s+n)$ is a copy of $R$ splitting off $P$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Persistence of a solution after further finite extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Take finite $K_2/K_1/K$ such that $K_1/K$ is a solution for $A\subset B$.
theorems.statement: Then $K_2/K$ is also a solution. Formal smoothness for the local maximal-ideal topologies persists in the normalized base change.
theorems.proof: Then $K_2/K$ is also a solution. Formal smoothness for the local maximal-ideal topologies persists in the normalized base change.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Nagata descent for a separable extension of DVR fraction fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Suppose $B$ is Nagata and $L/K$ is separable.
theorems.statement: The DVR $A$ is Nagata. The separability condition concerns the fraction fields.
theorems.proof: The DVR $A$ is Nagata. The separability condition concerns the fraction fields.

theorems.subject: ring-inclusion
theorems.name: Transporting a finite modification along a high-order congruence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A'\subset A$ be finite, let $f\in A'$ be regular on $A$, and assume $A'_f=A_f$.
theorems.statement: There exists $n_0>0$ such that, for $n\ge n_0$, every isomorphism $A'/f^nA'\cong B'/g^nB'$ matching $f$ with $g$ for $g$ regular in $B'$ gives a finite extension $B'\subset B$ and a compatible isomorphism $A/fA\cong B/gB$.
theorems.proof: There exists $n_0>0$ such that, for $n\ge n_0$, every isomorphism $A'/f^nA'\cong B'/g^nB'$ matching $f$ with $g$ for $g$ regular in $B'$ gives a finite extension $B'\subset B$ and a compatible isomorphism $A/fA\cong B/gB$.

theorems.subject: ring-inclusion
theorems.name: Functoriality of the finite modification under congruences
theorems.hypotheses: Take a map of finite inclusions $A'_i\subset A_i$ for $i=1,2$, with compatible elements $f$ regular on each $A_i$ and $(A'_i)_f=(A_i)_f$. Use a map $B'_1\to B'_2$ with compatible regular elements $g$ and compatible isomorphisms $A'_i/f^n\cong B'_i/g^n$ matching $f,g$. Take $n$ at least both bounds in Tag 0GLT.
theorems.statement: The explicit finite extensions $B'_i\subset B_i$ from the construction admit a compatible map $B_1\to B_2$. Modulo $g$, this map intertwines the map $A_1/f\to A_2/f$ via the constructed isomorphisms.
theorems.proof: The explicit finite extensions $B'_i\subset B_i$ from the construction admit a compatible map $B_1\to B_2$. Modulo $g$, this map intertwines the map $A_1/f\to A_2/f$ via the constructed isomorphisms.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Replacing one purely inseparable step of a solution
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Assume $\operatorname{char}K=p$, $L/K$ separable and $B$ Nagata. Let $K_2/K_1/K$ be finite, $K_2/K_1$ purely inseparable of degree $p$, with $K_2$ a solution.
theorems.statement: There is a finite separable extension $K_3/K_1$ such that $K_3/K$ is a solution. Separability here is relative to $K_1$.
theorems.proof: There is a finite separable extension $K_3/K_1$ such that $K_3/K$ is a solution. Separability here is relative to $K_1$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Separabilizing a solution for a Nagata target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Assume that $L/K$ is separable, $B$ is Nagata, and a solution exists.
theorems.statement: There is a finite separable extension of $K$ which is a solution.
theorems.proof: There is a finite separable extension of $K$ which is a solution.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Noetherian normalization after an algebraic field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Assume $B$ essentially of finite type over $A$. Let $K'/K$ be algebraic with Noetherian integral closure $A'$ of $A$ in $K'$. Let $B'$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_K K')_{\mathrm{red}}$.
theorems.statement: The ring $B'$ is Noetherian. Its spectrum surjects onto that of $A'$, and at corresponding primes all residue extensions are finitely generated as field extensions.
theorems.proof: The ring $B'$ is Noetherian. Its spectrum surjects onto that of $A'$, and at corresponding primes all residue extensions are finitely generated as field extensions.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Elimination of ramification in the essentially finite type case
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Suppose $B$ is essentially of finite type over $A$.
theorems.statement: Some finite extension $K_1/K$ is a solution for $A\subset B$, giving formal smoothness at every corresponding local extension in the normalized base change.
theorems.proof: Some finite extension $K_1/K$ is a solution for $A\subset B$, giving formal smoothness at every corresponding local extension in the normalized base change.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Separable elimination of ramification in the essentially finite type case
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Suppose $B$ is essentially of finite type over $A$, $L/K$ is separable, and at least one of $A,B$ is Nagata.
theorems.statement: A finite separable extension $K_1/K$ solves the ramification problem for $A\subset B$.
theorems.proof: A finite separable extension $K_1/K$ solves the ramification problem for $A\subset B$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Totally ramified separable base change of an index-one extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Given a finite extension $K_1/K$, write $A_1$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, $L_1=(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $B_1$ for the integral closure of $B$ in $L_1$. Suppose $A\subset B$ has index one and $K_1/K$ is finite separable and totally ramified at $A$.
theorems.statement: The tensor product $L\otimes_K K_1$ is a field. Both $A_1$ and $B_1=B\otimes_A A_1$ are DVRs, and $A_1\subset B_1$ has index one.
theorems.proof: The tensor product $L\otimes_K K_1$ is a field. Both $A_1$ and $B_1=B\otimes_A A_1$ are DVRs, and $A_1\subset B_1$ has index one.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Composition and restriction of ramification solutions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B\subset C$ be a tower of extensions of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L\subset M$. Fix finite $K_1/K$ and use either the solution condition throughout or the weak-solution condition throughout.
theorems.statement: A solution for $A\subset C$ solves $A\subset B$. Conversely, if $K_1$ solves $A\subset B$ and each field factor of $(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$ solves $B\subset C$, then $K_1$ solves $A\subset C$.
theorems.proof: A solution for $A\subset C$ solves $A\subset B$. Conversely, if $K_1$ solves $A\subset B$ and each field factor of $(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$ solves $B\subset C$, then $K_1$ solves $A\subset C$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Reduction to separably closed residue fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$.
theorems.statement: There is a compatible extension to DVRs $A'\subset B'$ with fraction fields separable algebraic over $K,L$ and residue fields separable closures of $\kappa_A,\kappa_B$. Existence of a solution over $A'\subset B'$ implies existence over $A\subset B$, separately for ordinary, weak and separable solutions.
theorems.proof: There is a compatible extension to DVRs $A'\subset B'$ with fraction fields separable algebraic over $K,L$ and residue fields separable closures of $\kappa_A,\kappa_B$. Existence of a solution over $A'\subset B'$ implies existence over $A\subset B$, separately for ordinary, weak and separable solutions.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Transitivity on normalized base-change primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Given a finite extension $K_1/K$, write $A_1$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, $L_1=(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $B_1$ for the integral closure of $B$ in $L_1$. Assume $K_1/K$ is normal.
theorems.statement: The group $\operatorname{Aut}(K_1/K)$ acts compatibly on $K_1,L_1,A_1,B_1$ and transitively on the maximal ideals of $B_1$.
theorems.proof: The group $\operatorname{Aut}(K_1/K)$ acts compatibly on $K_1,L_1,A_1,B_1$ and transitively on the maximal ideals of $B_1$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Separable totally ramified extensions approximating a uniformizer root
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$, residue characteristic $p>0$ and fraction field $K$. Fix an integer $n>1$ and a power $q$ of $p$.
theorems.statement: There exists a separable totally ramified extension of degree $q$ and index $q$ whose integral closure $B$ has a uniformizer $u$ with $u^q-\pi\in\pi^nB=u^{nq}B$.
theorems.proof: There exists a separable totally ramified extension of degree $q$ and index $q$ whose integral closure $B$ has a uniformizer $u$ with $u^q-\pi\in\pi^nB=u^{nq}B$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Adjoining a root of a residue non-pth-power
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR of residue characteristic $p>0$, fraction field $K$, and choose $a\in A$ whose residue is not a $p$th power.
theorems.statement: Then $a$ is not a $p$th power in $K$. The ring $A[a^{1/p}]$ is the integral closure in $K(a^{1/p})$ and is a DVR with ramification index one.
theorems.proof: Then $a$ is not a $p$th power in $K$. The ring $A[a^{1/p}]$ is the integral closure in $K(a^{1/p})$ and is a DVR with ramification index one.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Three alternatives for a purely inseparable degree-p step
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B\subset C$ be a tower of extensions of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L\subset M$. Suppose $B$ is Nagata, $A\subset B$ has index one, $M/L$ is purely inseparable of degree $p$, and $\pi$ is a uniformizer of $A$.
theorems.statement: Either $A\subset C$ has index one, or $C=B[\pi^{1/p}]$, or a separable degree-$p$ extension $K_1/K$ totally ramified at $A$ makes the tensor products $L\otimes_K K_1,M\otimes_K K_1$ fields and both normalized tower maps extensions of DVRs of index one.
theorems.proof: Either $A\subset C$ has index one, or $C=B[\pi^{1/p}]$, or a separable degree-$p$ extension $K_1/K$ totally ramified at $A$ makes the tensor products $L\otimes_K K_1,M\otimes_K K_1$ fields and both normalized tower maps extensions of DVRs of index one.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Compatible residue-field sections for nilpotent thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be local of characteristic $p>0$ with nilpotent maximal ideal.
theorems.statement: The residue homomorphism admits a ring section. For a local map to a second such ring $A'$ with separable residue extension, a section for $A'$ can be chosen compatible with the chosen section for $A$.
theorems.proof: The residue homomorphism admits a ring section. For a local map to a second such ring $A'$ with separable residue extension, a section for $A'$ can be chosen compatible with the chosen section for $A$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Artin–Schreier ramification and the pole of the parameter
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$ of characteristic $p>0$. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$, let $\xi\in K$, and adjoin a root of $z^p-z=\xi$.
theorems.statement: The extension is Galois. It is either trivial, unramified of degree $p$, totally ramified of index $p$, or has a unique prolongation with index one and purely inseparable residue degree $p$. If $\xi\in A$ only the first two possibilities occur. For $\xi=\pi^{-n}a$ with $a$ a unit and $n>0$, the third occurs when $p\nmid n$, and the fourth when $p\mid n$ and $\bar a\notin\kappa_A^p$.
theorems.proof: The extension is Galois. It is either trivial, unramified of degree $p$, totally ramified of index $p$, or has a unique prolongation with index one and purely inseparable residue degree $p$. If $\xi\in A$ only the first two possibilities occur. For $\xi=\pi^{-n}a$ with $a$ a unit and $n>0$, the third occurs when $p\nmid n$, and the fourth when $p\mid n$ and $\bar a\notin\kappa_A^p$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: A weak solution for an equal-characteristic Galois step
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B\subset C$ be a tower of extensions of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L\subset M$. Suppose $A\subset B$ has index one, $\operatorname{char}K=p>0$, $M/L$ is Galois of degree $p$, and $\kappa_A=\bigcap_{n\ge1}\kappa_B^{p^n}$.
theorems.statement: A finite Galois extension of $K$ totally ramified at $A$ is a weak solution for $A\subset C$.
theorems.proof: A finite Galois extension of $K$ totally ramified at $A$ is a weak solution for $A\subset C$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The composition law of the normalized cyclotomic polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Use the polynomial $P$ over $\mathbf Z[\zeta_p]$ and its specializations, with $w=1-\zeta_p$.
theorems.statement: One has $P(z)\equiv z^p-z\bmod w$ and $P(s+t+wst)=P(s)+P(t)+w^pP(s)P(t)$. The latter follows from $(1+ws)(1+wt)=1+w(s+t+wst)$.
theorems.proof: One has $P(z)\equiv z^p-z\bmod w$ and $P(s+t+wst)=P(s)+P(t)+w^pP(s)P(t)$. The latter follows from $(1+ws)(1+wt)=1+w(s+t+wst)$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Ramification of the cyclotomic deformation in mixed characteristic
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a mixed-characteristic $(0,p)$ DVR containing $\zeta_p$, with uniformizer $\pi$. Over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ take $\xi\in K$ and adjoin a root of $P(z)=\xi$, so $(1+wz)^p=1+w^p\xi$.
theorems.statement: The extension is Galois. It is either trivial, unramified of degree $p$, totally ramified of index $p$, or has a unique prolongation with index one and purely inseparable residue degree $p$. If $\xi\in A$ only the first two possibilities occur. For $\xi=\pi^{-n}a$ with $a$ a unit and $n>0$, the third occurs when $p\nmid n$, and the fourth when $p\mid n$ and $\bar a\notin\kappa_A^p$.
theorems.proof: The extension is Galois. It is either trivial, unramified of degree $p$, totally ramified of index $p$, or has a unique prolongation with index one and purely inseparable residue degree $p$. If $\xi\in A$ only the first two possibilities occur. For $\xi=\pi^{-n}a$ with $a$ a unit and $n>0$, the third occurs when $p\nmid n$, and the fourth when $p\mid n$ and $\bar a\notin\kappa_A^p$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Reaching a finite level in mixed characteristic
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B\subset C$ be a tower of extensions of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L\subset M$. Assume $A$ has mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, $A\subset B$ has index one, $B$ contains $\zeta_p$ primitive, and $M/L$ is Galois of degree $p$.
theorems.statement: A finite Galois extension $K_1/K$ totally ramified at $A$ either gives a weak solution for $A\subset C$ or makes the base-changed extension $M_1/L_1$ a degree-$p$ extension of finite level.
theorems.proof: A finite Galois extension $K_1/K$ totally ramified at $A$ either gives a weak solution for $A\subset C$ or makes the base-changed extension $M_1/L_1$ a degree-$p$ extension of finite level.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Lowering a positive ramification level
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B\subset C$ be a tower of extensions of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L\subset M$. Assume $A$ has mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, $A\subset B$ has index one, $B$ contains $\zeta_p$ primitive, $M/L$ has degree $p$ and finite level $\ell>0$, and $\kappa_A=\bigcap_{n\ge1}\kappa_B^{p^n}$.
theorems.statement: After a finite separable extension of $K$ totally ramified at $A$, one either has a weak solution for $A\subset C$ or a degree-$p$ extension of level at most $\max(0,\ell-1,2\ell-p)$.
theorems.proof: After a finite separable extension of $K$ totally ramified at $A$, one either has a weak solution for $A\subset C$ or a degree-$p$ extension of level at most $\max(0,\ell-1,2\ell-p)$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Weak elimination with algebraically closed common perfect residue subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B\subset C$ be a tower of extensions of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L\subset M$. Assume $A,B$ complete, $A\subset B$ of index one and $M/L$ finite. Suppose $\kappa_A$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$ and equals $\bigcap_{n\ge1}\kappa_B^{p^n}$.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite extension of $K$ which is a weak solution for $A\subset C$.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite extension of $K$ which is a weak solution for $A\subset C$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Normalized finite field base change for an extension of DVRs
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Given a finite extension $K_1/K$, write $A_1$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, $L_1=(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $B_1$ for the integral closure of $B$ in $L_1$.
theorems.statement: The algebra $L_1$ is a nonempty finite product of fields. The rings $A_1,B_1$ are respectively a Dedekind domain and a product of Dedekind domains. The map $B\otimes_A A_1\to B_1$ is integral with nil kernel, and $\operatorname{Spec}(B_1)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_1)$ is surjective. Pairs of lying-over maximal ideals give local DVR extensions. If $A$ is henselian, $A_1$ is local. If $B$ is henselian, each field factor gives a local normalization. Pure inseparability gives a single DVR on each side. Separability of $K_1/K$ gives finite normalizations on both sides and $L_1=L\otimes_K K_1$. Each Nagata base ring also guarantees finiteness of its own normalization.
theorems.proof: The algebra $L_1$ is a nonempty finite product of fields. The rings $A_1,B_1$ are respectively a Dedekind domain and a product of Dedekind domains. The map $B\otimes_A A_1\to B_1$ is integral with nil kernel, and $\operatorname{Spec}(B_1)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_1)$ is surjective. Pairs of lying-over maximal ideals give local DVR extensions. If $A$ is henselian, $A_1$ is local. If $B$ is henselian, each field factor gives a local normalization. Pure inseparability gives a single DVR on each side. Separability of $K_1/K$ gives finite normalizations on both sides and $L_1=L\otimes_K K_1$. Each Nagata base ring also guarantees finiteness of its own normalization.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: A root of a uniformizer and its intermediate fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$ and uniformizer $\pi$. Choose $u$ with $u^n=\pi$, $n\ge2$.
theorems.statement: The extension $K(u)/K$ has degree $n$. Its normalization is the DVR $A[u]$ with index $n$ and unchanged residue field. When $n$ is invertible in the residue field the extension is separable and tame, and every intermediate field has the form $K(u^{n/d})$ for a divisor $d$ of $n$.
theorems.proof: The extension $K(u)/K$ has degree $n$. Its normalization is the DVR $A[u]$ with index $n$ and unchanged residue field. When $n$ is invertible in the residue field the extension is separable and tame, and every intermediate field has the form $K(u^{n/d})$ for a divisor $d$ of $n$.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Formally smooth DVR extensions after normalized finite base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Given a finite extension $K_1/K$, write $A_1$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, $L_1=(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $B_1$ for the integral closure of $B$ in $L_1$. Suppose $A\to B$ is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal topology of $B$.
theorems.statement: The tensor product $L\otimes_K K_1$ is reduced, $B_1=B\otimes_A A_1$, and for each pair of corresponding maximal ideals $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ the map $(A_1)_{\mathfrak p}\to(B_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal topology on the target.
theorems.proof: The tensor product $L\otimes_K K_1$ is reduced, $B_1=B\otimes_A A_1$, and for each pair of corresponding maximal ideals $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ the map $(A_1)_{\mathfrak p}\to(B_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal topology on the target.

theorems.subject: ramification-solution
theorems.name: Abhyankar’s lemma at a chosen prime after base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Given a finite extension $K_1/K$, write $A_1$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, $L_1=(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $B_1$ for the integral closure of $B$ in $L_1$. Let $e=e(B/A)$. Assume residue characteristic zero, or positive residue characteristic $p$ with $p\nmid e$ and $\kappa_B/\kappa_A$ separable. At a chosen maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A_1$ suppose $e$ divides $e((A_1)_{\mathfrak p}/A)$.
theorems.statement: For every maximal $\mathfrak q$ of $B_1$ over $\mathfrak p$, the map $(A_1)_{\mathfrak p}\to(B_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ is formally smooth in the maximal-ideal topology of the target.
theorems.proof: For every maximal $\mathfrak q$ of $B_1$ over $\mathfrak p$, the map $(A_1)_{\mathfrak p}\to(B_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ is formally smooth in the maximal-ideal topology of the target.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Composition of tamely ramified extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$, let $M/L/K$ be finite separable, and let $B$ normalize $A$ in $L$. Assume $L/K$ is tame at $A$ and $M/L$ tame at $B_{\mathfrak m}$ for every maximal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$.
theorems.statement: Then $M/K$ is tamely ramified at $A$.
theorems.proof: Then $M/K$ is tamely ramified at $A$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Tameness of intermediate fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M/L/K$ be finite separable with $M/K$ tame at a DVR $A$ of fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: The intermediate field $L$ is tame over $K$ at $A$.
theorems.proof: The intermediate field $L$ is tame over $K$ at $A$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Uniformity of the root criterion for tameness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of a DVR $A$ with fraction field $K$, and let $L/K$ be finite separable.
theorems.statement: Tameness is equivalent to the existence of one admissible root exponent $e$ as in the embedding criterion with this $\pi$. Equivalently, there is one $e_0$ invertible in $\kappa_A$ such that every $de_0$ works when $d\ge1$ is invertible in $\kappa_A$.
theorems.proof: Tameness is equivalent to the existence of one admissible root exponent $e$ as in the embedding criterion with this $\pi$. Equivalently, there is one $e_0$ invertible in $\kappa_A$ such that every $de_0$ works when $d\ge1$ is invertible in $\kappa_A$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Tame Galois envelopes and joint tame extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a DVR $A$ with fraction field $K$ and finite separable extensions tame with respect to $A$.
theorems.statement: Each embeds into a finite Galois extension of $K$ tame at $A$. Any two embed simultaneously into a finite separable extension tame at $A$.
theorems.proof: Each embeds into a finite Galois extension of $K$ tame at $A$. Any two embed simultaneously into a finite separable extension tame at $A$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Tameness and unramifiedness in every base-change field factor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subset B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $K\subset L$. Let $K'/K$ be finite separable and decompose $L\otimes_K K'$ into its finite product of fields.
theorems.statement: If $K'/K$ is unramified at $A$, each field factor is unramified over $L$ at $B$. The same conclusion with “tamely ramified” holds when $K'/K$ is tame at $A$.
theorems.proof: If $K'/K$ is unramified at $A$, each field factor is unramified over $L$ at $B$. The same conclusion with “tamely ramified” holds when $K'/K$ is tame at $A$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Stability of a simple root in a complete one-dimensional local domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a complete local domain of dimension one with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Suppose $P\in A[T]$, $P(\alpha)=0$ and $P'(\alpha)\ne0$ for $\alpha\in A$.
theorems.statement: For each $c\ge0$ there is $n$ such that every polynomial perturbation $Q\in\mathfrak m^n A[T]$ gives a root $\beta\in A$ of $P+Q$ with $\beta-\alpha\in\mathfrak m^c$. The derivative may be a nonunit.
theorems.proof: For each $c\ge0$ there is $n$ such that every polynomial perturbation $Q\in\mathfrak m^n A[T]$ gives a root $\beta\in A$ of $P+Q$ with $\beta-\alpha\in\mathfrak m^c$. The derivative may be a nonunit.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Realizing finite separable extensions of the completed fraction field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$ and let $\widehat K=\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat A)$. Suppose $M/\widehat K$ is finite separable.
theorems.statement: There is a finite separable extension $L/K$ and a $\widehat K$-isomorphism $\widehat K\otimes_K L\cong M$.
theorems.proof: There is a finite separable extension $L/K$ and a $\widehat K$-isomorphism $\widehat K\otimes_K L\cong M$.

theorems.subject: valued-field-extension
theorems.name: Degree as the sum of local ramification and residue degrees
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$ and $L/K$ finite separable. Let $B$ be its normalization in $L$.
theorems.statement: The ring $B$ is a finite semilocal Dedekind domain. For its maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_i$ take local ramification indices $e_i$ and residue degrees $f_i$. Then $[L:K]=\sum_i e_i f_i$. If $A$ is henselian there is just one maximal ideal.
theorems.proof: The ring $B$ is a finite semilocal Dedekind domain. For its maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_i$ take local ramification indices $e_i$ and residue degrees $f_i$. Then $[L:K]=\sum_i e_i f_i$. If $A$ is henselian there is just one maximal ideal.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: Transitivity of the Galois group on extensions of a DVR
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be finite Galois, let $B$ normalize $A$ in $L$, and fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$. Write $D,I,P$ for the decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at this prime.
theorems.statement: Every $K$-automorphism of $L$ preserves $B$. The resulting action on maximal ideals of $B$ has a single orbit.
theorems.proof: Every $K$-automorphism of $L$ preserves $B$. The resulting action on maximal ideals of $B$ has a single orbit.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: Degree formula in a finite Galois extension of a DVR
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be finite Galois, let $B$ normalize $A$ in $L$, and fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$. Write $D,I,P$ for the decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at this prime.
theorems.statement: All maximal ideals of $B$ have the same ramification index $e$ and residue degree $f$. If $g$ is their number, $[L:K]=gef$.
theorems.proof: All maximal ideals of $B$ have the same ramification index $e$ and residue degree $f$. If $g$ is their number, $[L:K]=gef$.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: The residue automorphism quotient of a decomposition group
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be finite Galois, let $B$ normalize $A$ in $L$, and fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$. Write $D,I,P$ for the decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at this prime.
theorems.statement: The residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak m)/\kappa_A$ is normal. Its entire automorphism group is the image of $D$, with kernel $I$. If it is separable at one maximal ideal it is separable at all, hence Galois.
theorems.proof: The residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak m)/\kappa_A$ is normal. Its entire automorphism group is the image of $D$, with kernel $I$. If it is separable at one maximal ideal it is separable at all, hence Galois.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: Equivariance of the inertia character
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be finite Galois, let $B$ normalize $A$ in $L$, and fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$. Write $D,I,P$ for the decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at this prime.
theorems.statement: Let $\theta:I\to\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$ be the character on $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Then $\theta(\tau\sigma\tau^{-1})=\tau(\theta(\sigma))$ for $\sigma\in I$ and $\tau\in D$.
theorems.proof: Let $\theta:I\to\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$ be the character on $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Then $\theta(\tau\sigma\tau^{-1})=\tau(\theta(\sigma))$ for $\sigma\in I$ and $\tau\in D$.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: Étale localization of the inertia fixed ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be finite Galois, let $B$ normalize $A$ in $L$, and fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$. Write $D,I,P$ for the decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at this prime.
theorems.statement: The fixed ring $B^I$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $L^I$. Localized at $\mathfrak m\cap B^I$, it is étale over $A$.
theorems.proof: The fixed ring $B^I$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $L^I$. Localized at $\mathfrak m\cap B^I$, it is étale over $A$.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: The tower of fixed local rings and the tame layer
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be finite Galois, let $B$ normalize $A$ in $L$, and fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$. Write $D,I,P$ for the decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at this prime.
theorems.statement: The fixed rings $B^H$ normalize $A$ in $L^H$ for $H=D,I,P$. The extensions $L^I/L^D$, $L^P/L^I$, $L^P/L^D$ have groups $D/I,I/P,D/P$. The selected prime of $B^D$ has a unique prime above it at every higher stage, as do its successors. Localizing the tower, the steps from $A$ to $B^D$ and from $B^D$ to $B^I$ are étale, with respective residue extensions trivial and Galois of group $D/I$. From $B^I$ to $B^P$ the residue extension is trivial and the index is $|I/P|$, invertible in the residue field. Over $A$ and $B^D$, the local $B^P$ thus has that same index and separable residue field.
theorems.proof: The fixed rings $B^H$ normalize $A$ in $L^H$ for $H=D,I,P$. The extensions $L^I/L^D$, $L^P/L^I$, $L^P/L^D$ have groups $D/I,I/P,D/P$. The selected prime of $B^D$ has a unique prime above it at every higher stage, as do its successors. Localizing the tower, the steps from $A$ to $B^D$ and from $B^D$ to $B^I$ are étale, with respective residue extensions trivial and Galois of group $D/I$. From $B^I$ to $B^P$ the residue extension is trivial and the index is $|I/P|$, invertible in the residue field. Over $A$ and $B^D$, the local $B^P$ thus has that same index and separable residue field.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: Functoriality of the ramification groups in a Galois tower
theorems.hypotheses: Take finite Galois $M/K,L/K$ with $L\subset M$ over a DVR of fraction field $K$. Choose compatible primes in the normalizations. Use primes on notation for the upper extension, and $e',e$ for indices over $K$.
theorems.statement: Restriction surjects $D'\to D$, $I'\to I$ and $P'\to P$, compatibly with residue actions. For $\sigma'\in I'$ mapping to $\sigma\in I$, the image of $\theta(\sigma)$ in the upper residue field is $\theta'(\sigma')^{e'/e}$.
theorems.proof: Restriction surjects $D'\to D$, $I'\to I$ and $P'\to P$, compatibly with residue actions. For $\sigma'\in I'$ mapping to $\sigma\in I$, the image of $\theta(\sigma)$ in the upper residue field is $\theta'(\sigma')^{e'/e}$.

theorems.subject: galois-prime
theorems.name: Canonical scaling of the tame inertia character
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be finite Galois, let $B$ normalize $A$ in $L$, and fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$. Write $D,I,P$ for the decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups at this prime.
theorems.statement: Put $t=|I/P|$ and $q=e/t$. Then $\sigma\mapsto\theta(\sigma)^q$ induces a $D$-equivariant isomorphism $I/P\to\mu_t(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$. In a finite Galois tower, restriction on inertia corresponds to the power $t'/t$ on the groups of roots of unity, where $t'$ is the upper tame order.
theorems.proof: Put $t=|I/P|$ and $q=e/t$. Then $\sigma\mapsto\theta(\sigma)^q$ induces a $D$-equivariant isomorphism $I/P\to\mu_t(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$. In a finite Galois tower, restriction on inertia corresponds to the power $t'/t$ on the groups of roots of unity, where $t'$ is the upper tame order.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting an orbit polynomial over an equivariant surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a $G$-equivariant surjection with $G$ finite of order $n$, and let $b\in B^G$.
theorems.statement: There is a monic $P\in A^G[T]$ mapping to $(T-b)^n$. One may take the product of $T-\sigma(a)$ over the group for any lift $a$ of $b$.
theorems.proof: There is a monic $P\in A^G[T]$ mapping to $(T-b)^n$. One may take the product of $T-\sigma(a)$ over the group for any lift $a$ of $b$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Invariants modulo a group-stable ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ of order $n$ act by automorphisms on $R$. Suppose $I\subseteq R$ is a $G$-stable ideal.
theorems.statement: The injection $R^G/(I\cap R^G)\to(R/I)^G$ is integral, induces a homeomorphism of spectra and has purely inseparable residue extensions.
theorems.proof: The injection $R^G/(I\cap R^G)\to(R/I)^G$ is integral, induces a homeomorphism of spectra and has purely inseparable residue extensions.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Orbit-polynomial coefficients in an invariant ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ of order $n$ act by automorphisms on $R$. Take an ideal $J\subseteq R^G$ and $x\in JR$.
theorems.statement: Each nonleading coefficient of $\prod_{\sigma\in G}(T-\sigma x)$ lies in $J$ as an ideal of $R^G$.
theorems.proof: Each nonleading coefficient of $\prod_{\sigma\in G}(T-\sigma x)$ lies in $J$ as an ideal of $R^G$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Invariants of a quotient by an extended ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ of order $n$ act by automorphisms on $R$. Let $J\subseteq R^G$ be an ideal and $\varphi:R^G/J\to(R/JR)^G$ the natural map.
theorems.statement: For every $b$ in the target, $(T-b)^n$ lifts to a monic polynomial over $R^G/J$. Each $a\in\ker\varphi$ satisfies $(T-a)^n=T^n$. The map is integral, induces a homeomorphism on spectra and purely inseparable residue extensions.
theorems.proof: For every $b$ in the target, $(T-b)^n$ lifts to a monic polynomial over $R^G/J$. Each $a\in\ker\varphi$ satisfies $(T-a)^n=T^n$. The map is integral, induces a homeomorphism on spectra and purely inseparable residue extensions.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Invariants of a quotient when group order is invertible
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ of order $n$ act by automorphisms on $R$. Assume $n$ is a unit in $R$ and take an ideal $J\subseteq R^G$.
theorems.statement: The natural map $R^G/J\to(R/JR)^G$ is an isomorphism. Averaging over the group gives invariant lifts, and averaging the coefficients of elements of $JR$ recovers $J$ on invariants.
theorems.proof: The natural map $R^G/J\to(R/JR)^G$ is an isomorphism. Averaging over the group gives invariant lifts, and averaging the coefficients of elements of $JR$ recovers $J$ on invariants.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Orbit-polynomial descent after arbitrary scalar extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ of order $n$ act by automorphisms on $R$. Let $A$ be an $R^G$-algebra and $\varphi:A\to(A\otimes_{R^G}R)^G$ the canonical map.
theorems.statement: For every invariant $b$ in the target, $(T-b)^n$ is the image of a monic $P\in A[T]$. For each $a\in\ker\varphi$, the identity $(T-a)^n=T^n$ holds in $A[T]$.
theorems.proof: For every invariant $b$ in the target, $(T-b)^n$ is the image of a monic $P\in A[T]$. For each $a\in\ker\varphi$, the identity $(T-a)^n=T^n$ holds in $A[T]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change for invariant rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ of order $n$ act by automorphisms on $R$. Let $R^G\to A$ be any ring map and act on $A\otimes_{R^G}R$ through $R$.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to(A\otimes_{R^G}R)^G$ is integral, gives a homeomorphism on spectra and induces purely inseparable residue extensions. It is an isomorphism when $R^G\to A$ is flat.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to(A\otimes_{R^G}R)^G$ is integral, gives a homeomorphism on spectra and induces purely inseparable residue extensions. It is an isomorphism when $R^G\to A$ is flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Primes above one invariant prime form a single orbit
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ of order $n$ act by automorphisms on $R$. Suppose $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak q'\subset R$ have the same contraction to $R^G$.
theorems.statement: There is a $\sigma\in G$ with $\sigma(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q'$.
theorems.proof: There is a $\sigma\in G$ with $\sigma(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Stabilizers and residue automorphisms of a finite quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ of order $n$ act by automorphisms on $R$. Choose $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R^G)$.
theorems.statement: The residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is normal algebraic. The stabilizer of $\mathfrak q$ in $G$ surjects onto its automorphism group, including when the residue extension is inseparable.
theorems.proof: The residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is normal algebraic. The stabilizer of $\mathfrak q$ in $G$ surjects onto its automorphism group, including when the residue extension is inseparable.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Transitivity on primes in an infinite Galois normalization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a normal domain of fraction field $K$, $L/K$ any Galois extension, and $B$ the integral closure of $A$ in $L$.
theorems.statement: The primes of $B$ over each prime of $A$ form a single Galois orbit. At a prime of $B$ its residue extension is algebraic normal, and its stabilizer surjects onto the group of residue automorphisms.
theorems.proof: The primes of $B$ over each prime of $A$ form a single Galois orbit. At a prime of $B$ its residue extension is algebraic normal, and its stabilizer surjects onto the group of residue automorphisms.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Restriction of decomposition and inertia in possibly infinite towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a normal domain of fraction field $K$. Suppose $M/K$ and $L/K$ are Galois, possibly infinite, with $K\subset L\subset M$. Take compatible primes in the integral closures of $A$ in $M$ and $L$.
theorems.statement: Restriction $\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ sends the upper decomposition group onto the lower one and the kernel of the upper residue action onto the kernel of the lower residue action.
theorems.proof: Restriction $\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ sends the upper decomposition group onto the lower one and the kernel of the upper residue action onto the kernel of the lower residue action.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Equidimensionality over a flat local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be flat local between Noetherian local rings. Assume $B$ catenary and its spectrum equidimensional.
theorems.statement: For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak pB)$ is equidimensional. The base $A$ is catenary with equidimensional spectrum.
theorems.proof: For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak pB)$ is equidimensional. The base $A$ is catenary with equidimensional spectrum.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Geometrically normal formal fibres and universal catenarity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat A$ its maximal-ideal completion and $A^h$ its henselization. Suppose all formal fibres of $A$ are geometrically normal.
theorems.statement: The henselization $A^h$ is universally catenary. If $A$ is unibranch, in particular if $A$ is normal, then $A$ itself is universally catenary.
theorems.proof: The henselization $A^h$ is universally catenary. If $A$ is unibranch, in particular if $A$ is normal, then $A$ itself is universally catenary.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Ordinary and geometric branch counts increase under completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat A$ its maximal-ideal completion and $A^h$ its henselization.
theorems.statement: Contraction from the minimal primes of $\widehat A$ onto those of $A^h$ is surjective. The number of branches of $A$ is bounded above by that of $\widehat A$, and the inequality also holds for geometric branch counts.
theorems.proof: Contraction from the minimal primes of $\widehat A$ onto those of $A^h$ is surjective. The number of branches of $A$ is bounded above by that of $\widehat A$, and the inequality also holds for geometric branch counts.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Criterion for equality of branch counts after completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat A$ its maximal-ideal completion and $A^h$ its henselization.
theorems.statement: The branch counts agree exactly when $\sqrt{\mathfrak q\widehat A}$ is prime for every minimal prime $\mathfrak q\subset A^h$.
theorems.proof: The branch counts agree exactly when $\sqrt{\mathfrak q\widehat A}$ is prime for every minimal prime $\mathfrak q\subset A^h$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Complementing an open-and-closed factor away from an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finitely generated ideal $I$ of a ring $A$ and a map $A\to C$. Suppose $A_f\to C_f$ is localization at an idempotent for every $f\in I$.
theorems.statement: There is a quotient $A\twoheadrightarrow C'$ such that $A_f\to(C\times C')_f$ is an isomorphism for all $f\in I$.
theorems.proof: There is a quotient $A\twoheadrightarrow C'$ such that $A_f\to(C\times C')_f$ is an isomorphism for all $f\in I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Algebraizing a quotient of a completed finite type algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian, $I\subset A$ an ideal and $B$ a finite type $A$-algebra. Let $\widehat B\twoheadrightarrow C$ have kernel $J$, with completion taken for $I$. Assume $I^c(J/J^2)=0$ for some $c\ge0$.
theorems.statement: The ring $C$ is isomorphic as an $A$-algebra to the $I$-adic completion of a finite type $A$-algebra.
theorems.proof: The ring $C$ is isomorphic as an $A$-algebra to the $I$-adic completion of a finite type $A$-algebra.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: A one-dimensional formal branch comes from the henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat A$ its maximal-ideal completion and $A^h$ its henselization. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a minimal prime of $\widehat A$ with $\dim(\widehat A/\mathfrak q)=1$.
theorems.statement: Some minimal prime $\mathfrak q^h$ of $A^h$ satisfies $\mathfrak q=\sqrt{\mathfrak q^h\widehat A}$.
theorems.proof: Some minimal prime $\mathfrak q^h$ of $A^h$ satisfies $\mathfrak q=\sqrt{\mathfrak q^h\widehat A}$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Connectedness of the punctured spectrum under completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat A$ its maximal-ideal completion and $A^h$ its henselization.
theorems.statement: The complement of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A)$ is disconnected exactly when the complement of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A^h)$ is disconnected.
theorems.proof: The complement of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A)$ is disconnected exactly when the complement of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A^h)$ is disconnected.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: One-dimensional rings have the same branch counts after completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat A$ its maximal-ideal completion and $A^h$ its henselization. Assume $\dim A=1$.
theorems.statement: Both the ordinary and geometric branch counts agree between $A$ and $\widehat A$.
theorems.proof: Both the ordinary and geometric branch counts agree between $A$ and $\widehat A$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Geometrically normal formal fibres preserve branch counts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat A$ its maximal-ideal completion and $A^h$ its henselization. Assume every formal fibre is geometrically normal. This holds for quasi-excellent rings.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is Nagata, and both its ordinary and its geometric branch counts agree with those of $\widehat A$.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is Nagata, and both its ordinary and its geometric branch counts agree with those of $\widehat A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Nonzero contraction of ideals along maps of domains
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a map of domains. Assume one of these conditions. The map is a localization of an étale map. It is flat and a localization of an unramified, quasi-finite, or integral map. It is flat and its fibres have no proper specializations. The generic point maps to the generic point and the fibres have no proper specializations. Or the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ has exactly one preimage.
theorems.statement: The preimage of every nonzero ideal of $B$ is a nonzero ideal of $A$.
theorems.proof: The preimage of every nonzero ideal of $B$ is a nonzero ideal of $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Étaleness near an injective unramified local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be unramified at $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$. Assume $A$ is a domain, $A_{\mathfrak p}$ geometrically unibranch, and $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ injective.
theorems.statement: Some $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ makes $B_g$ étale over $A$.
theorems.proof: Some $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ makes $B_g$ étale over $A$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: An essentially étale criterion over a geometrically unibranch domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)\to B$ be an injective local map, essentially of finite type, from a geometrically unibranch local domain. Assume $\mathfrak mB$ is the maximal ideal of $B$ and the residue extension is separable.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to B$ is a localization of an étale ring map.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to B$ is a localization of an étale ring map.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Minimal primes in a strictly henselian tensor-product neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, and $A,B$ strictly henselian local $k$-algebras with residue field $k$. Strictly henselize $A\otimes_k B$ at the kernel of the residue map to $k$, calling the result $C$.
theorems.statement: Contraction gives a bijection between minimal primes of $C$ and pairs of minimal primes of $A$ and $B$.
theorems.proof: Contraction gives a bijection between minimal primes of $C$ and pairs of minimal primes of $A$ and $B$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Henselization and the maximal ideals of the normalization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be local with finitely many minimal primes and let $A'$ normalize $A_{\mathrm{red}}$ in its total ring of fractions. Put $C=A'\otimes_A A^h$.
theorems.statement: Contraction from $C$ to $A'$ bijects maximal ideals, and contraction to $A^h$ bijects minimal primes. Each minimal prime of $C$ lies in one maximal ideal and each maximal ideal contains one minimal prime.
theorems.proof: Contraction from $C$ to $A'$ bijects maximal ideals, and contraction to $A^h$ bijects minimal primes. Each minimal prime of $C$ lies in one maximal ideal and each maximal ideal contains one minimal prime.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Strict henselization and the residue embeddings of a normalized branch
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be local with finitely many minimal primes and let $A'$ normalize $A_{\mathrm{red}}$ in its total ring of fractions. Fix an algebraic closure of $\kappa=\kappa_A$, form $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ using its separable part, and put $C=A'\otimes_A A^{\mathrm{sh}}$.
theorems.statement: For maximal $\mathfrak m'\subset A'$ the residue field is algebraic over $\kappa$, and primes of $C$ above $\mathfrak m'$ correspond canonically to $\kappa$-embeddings of $\kappa(\mathfrak m')$ in the chosen algebraic closure. Contraction bijects minimal primes of $C$ and $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$. In $C$ the containment of a minimal prime in a maximal ideal pairs them bijectively.
theorems.proof: For maximal $\mathfrak m'\subset A'$ the residue field is algebraic over $\kappa$, and primes of $C$ above $\mathfrak m'$ correspond canonically to $\kappa$-embeddings of $\kappa(\mathfrak m')$ in the chosen algebraic closure. Contraction bijects minimal primes of $C$ and $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$. In $C$ the containment of a minimal prime in a maximal ideal pairs them bijectively.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Structure of weakly étale algebras over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be a field and $B$ a weakly étale $K$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The algebra is reduced and integral over $K$. Each finitely generated $K$-subalgebra is a finite product of finite separable fields over $K$. For nonzero $B$, it is a field precisely when it has no nontrivial idempotents, and then it is algebraic separable over $K$. Subalgebras, quotients, and tensor products with other weakly étale $K$-algebras remain weakly étale.
theorems.proof: The algebra is reduced and integral over $K$. Each finitely generated $K$-subalgebra is a finite product of finite separable fields over $K$. For nonzero $B$, it is a field precisely when it has no nontrivial idempotents, and then it is algebraic separable over $K$. Subalgebras, quotients, and tensor products with other weakly étale $K$-algebras remain weakly étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Functoriality of the maximal weakly étale subalgebra
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a field $K$ and write $B_{\max}$ for the maximal weakly étale subalgebra functor on $K$-algebras.
theorems.statement: A map carries the maximal subalgebra into the maximal subalgebra. For $A'\subset A$, $B_{\max}(A')=A'\cap B_{\max}(A)$. The construction commutes with filtered colimits and finite products, and is invariant under reduction. If $A\ne0$ has no nontrivial idempotents, $B_{\max}(A)$ is a separable algebraic field extension of $K$.
theorems.proof: A map carries the maximal subalgebra into the maximal subalgebra. For $A'\subset A$, $B_{\max}(A')=A'\cap B_{\max}(A)$. The construction commutes with filtered colimits and finite products, and is invariant under reduction. If $A\ne0$ has no nontrivial idempotents, $B_{\max}(A)$ is a separable algebraic field extension of $K$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Maximal weakly étale subalgebra after extending the ground field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be any field extension and let $A$ be a $K$-algebra.
theorems.statement: The inclusion $B_{\max}(A)\otimes_K L\subseteq A\otimes_K L$ identifies its source with the maximal weakly étale $L$-subalgebra of the target.
theorems.proof: The inclusion $B_{\max}(A)\otimes_K L\subseteq A\otimes_K L$ identifies its source with the maximal weakly étale $L$-subalgebra of the target.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Weak dimension bounds ascend under weakly étale maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be weakly étale and fix $d\ge0$ such that all $A$-modules have flat dimension at most $d$.
theorems.statement: All $B$-modules have flat dimension at most $d$ over $B$.
theorems.proof: All $B$-modules have flat dimension at most $d$ over $B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change for weak étaleness and flatness of the diagonal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ and $A\to A'$ be ring maps, and set $B'=A'\otimes_A B$.
theorems.statement: Flatness of $B\otimes_A B\to B$ implies flatness of $B'\otimes_{A'}B'\to B'$. If $A\to B$ is weakly étale, $A'\to B'$ is weakly étale.
theorems.proof: Flatness of $B\otimes_A B\to B$ implies flatness of $B'\otimes_{A'}B'\to B'$. If $A\to B$ is weakly étale, $A'\to B'$ is weakly étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of weakly étale maps and of maps with flat diagonal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be composable ring maps.
theorems.statement: If both multiplication maps for the steps are flat, then $C\otimes_A C\to C$ is flat. If both steps are weakly étale, so is the composite.
theorems.proof: If both multiplication maps for the steps are flat, then $C\otimes_A C\to C$ is flat. If both steps are weakly étale, so is the composite.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Faithfully flat target descent for weak étaleness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be ring maps with $B\to C$ faithfully flat.
theorems.statement: Flatness of $C\otimes_A C\to C$ implies flatness of $B\otimes_A B\to B$. If $A\to C$ is weakly étale, so is $A\to B$.
theorems.proof: Flatness of $C\otimes_A C\to C$ implies flatness of $B\otimes_A B\to B$. If $A\to C$ is weakly étale, so is $A\to B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Field extensions with flat multiplication map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be a field extension for which $L\otimes_K L\to L$ is flat.
theorems.statement: Then $L/K$ is algebraic and separable, allowing infinite algebraic degree.
theorems.proof: Then $L/K$ is algebraic and separable, allowing infinite algebraic degree.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Residue field extensions of weakly étale maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be weakly étale. At any $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$.
theorems.statement: The residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is separable algebraic.
theorems.proof: The residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is separable algebraic.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A product of valuation rings and the localization at regular elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A_j)_{j\in J}$ be valuation rings with fraction fields $K_j$, with arbitrary index set $J$.
theorems.statement: The ring $\prod_j A_j$ has weak dimension at most one. Inverting the elements with every coordinate nonzero gives $\prod_j K_j$.
theorems.proof: The ring $\prod_j A_j$ has weak dimension at most one. Inverting the elements with every coordinate nonzero gives $\prod_j K_j$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A valuation-ring pullback presentation of a normal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a normal domain with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: There is a pullback $A\cong K\times_L V$ in rings, where $V$ has weak dimension at most one and $V\to L$ is an injective flat epimorphism. One can take products of valuation rings and of their fraction fields.
theorems.proof: There is a pullback $A\cong K\times_L V$ in rings, where $V$ has weak dimension at most one and $V\to L$ is an injective flat epimorphism. One can take products of valuation rings and of their fraction fields.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Integral closedness in a flat epimorphic extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ have weak dimension at most one and let $A\to B$ be injective, flat and an epimorphism in rings.
theorems.statement: Every element of $B$ integral over $A$ belongs to $A$.
theorems.proof: Every element of $B$ integral over $A$ belongs to $A$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Vanishing in degree zero for a product total complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A_0^\bullet\to A_1^\bullet\to\cdots$ be a complex of complexes of abelian groups. For every $p\ge0$ suppose $H^{-p}(A_p^\bullet)=0$.
theorems.statement: Its product total complex has zero cohomology in degree zero. The right half-plane convention permits one to construct the primitive successively in increasing column degree.
theorems.proof: Its product total complex has zero cohomology in degree zero. The right half-plane convention permits one to construct the primitive successively in increasing column degree.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Columnwise quasi-isomorphisms of product totalizations
theorems.hypotheses: A map of complexes of complexes of abelian groups, indexed by columns $p\ge0$, induces quasi-isomorphisms on each column.
theorems.statement: The map of product total complexes is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the diagonal vanishing lemma in all shifts to the mapping cone.
theorems.proof: The map of product total complexes is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the diagonal vanishing lemma in all shifts to the mapping cone.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Eventual constancy of Ext into adic quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Let $K\in D(A)$ be pseudo-coherent, $a\in\mathbf Z$, and assume $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(K,M)$ is $I$-power torsion for every finite $M$ and every $i\ge a$.
theorems.statement: For such $M,i$, the tower $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(K,M/I^nM)$ is essentially constant with value $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(K,M)$, canonically its inverse limit. Essential constancy refers to the pro-object and allows individual terms to vary.
theorems.proof: For such $M,i$, the tower $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(K,M/I^nM)$ is essentially constant with value $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(K,M)$, canonically its inverse limit. Essential constancy refers to the pro-object and allows individual terms to vary.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Uniform vanishing of Tor maps out of a high power
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Let $M$ be finite and let $N$ be any $A$-module with $IN=0$.
theorems.statement: A single $n>0$ makes $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(I^nM,N)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,N)$ zero for every $p\ge0$.
theorems.proof: A single $n>0$ makes $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(I^nM,N)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,N)$ zero for every $p\ge0$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent tensor factors commute with derived inverse limits of modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be pseudo-coherent in $D(R)$ for any ring $R$, and let $(M_n)$ be a tower of $R$-modules in degree zero.
theorems.statement: The natural morphism $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\mathbf R\lim_n M_n\to\mathbf R\lim_n(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M_n)$ is an isomorphism.
