theorems.proof: The natural morphism $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\mathbf R\lim_n M_n\to\mathbf R\lim_n(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M_n)$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Additivity of finite projective dimensions for a local quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local, $I$ an ideal, and $E$ a nonzero finite $R/I$-module. Assume $\operatorname{pd}_R(R/I)$ and $\operatorname{pd}_{R/I}(E)$ finite.
theorems.statement: The projective dimension over $R$ is finite and $\operatorname{pd}_R E=\operatorname{pd}_R(R/I)+\operatorname{pd}_{R/I} E$.
theorems.proof: The projective dimension over $R$ is finite and $\operatorname{pd}_R E=\operatorname{pd}_R(R/I)+\operatorname{pd}_{R/I} E$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: A cardinal bound for enlarging compatible subcomplexes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $A\to B$. Let an $A$-linear cochain map $M\to N$, with $N$ a $B$-complex, induce $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\simeq N$. Choose subcomplexes $M_1,N_1$ over their respective rings compatible under that map, and put $T_j=M_j\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$.
theorems.statement: There exist compatible enlargements $M_2,N_2$ inside $M,N$. In every degree $i$ the kernel of $H^i(T_1)\to H^i(N_1)$ vanishes in $H^i(T_2)$, and the image of $H^i(N_1)$ in $H^i(N_2)$ lifts to $H^i(T_2)$. The combined cardinality of the underlying terms is bounded by $\max(|A|,|B|,\aleph_0,|M_1|,|N_1|)$, where each complex is counted across all degrees.
theorems.proof: There exist compatible enlargements $M_2,N_2$ inside $M,N$. In every degree $i$ the kernel of $H^i(T_1)\to H^i(N_1)$ vanishes in $H^i(T_2)$, and the image of $H^i(N_1)$ in $H^i(N_2)$ lifts to $H^i(T_2)$. The combined cardinality of the underlying terms is bounded by $\max(|A|,|B|,\aleph_0,|M_1|,|N_1|)$, where each complex is counted across all degrees.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Detecting negative cohomology by localization and a cone
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M\in D(R)$, $f\in R$, and $C=\operatorname{Cone}(f:M\to M)$. Assume $H^i(M)_f=0$ for $i<0$ and $H^i(C)=0$ for $i<-1$.
theorems.statement: Then $H^i(M)=0$ for all $i<0$. In those degrees multiplication by $f$ is injective by the cone sequence, while each class vanishes after localization.
theorems.proof: Then $H^i(M)=0$ for all $i<0$. In those degrees multiplication by $f$ is injective by the cone sequence, while each class vanishes after localization.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Detecting a flat module in degree zero from two derived restrictions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M\in D(R)$ have no positive cohomology and let $f\in R$. Assume its derived restrictions to $R_f$ and $R/fR$ are flat modules over the respective rings, placed in degree zero.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ itself is isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a flat $R$-module in degree zero.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ itself is isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a flat $R$-module in degree zero.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Artin–Rees comparison for cohomology of powered subcomplexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Take a complex of finite modules $K\to L\to M$ with middle cohomology $H$. Let $H_n$ be the middle cohomology of $I^nK\to I^nL\to I^nM$.
theorems.statement: There exists $c>0$ such that $H_n\to H$ has image in $I^{n-c}H$ for $n\ge c$, and canonical maps $I^nH\to H_{n-c}$ exist. For $n\ge2c$, composing these shifted maps in either order gives the transition through $2c$ places in the respective tower. Thus $(H_n)$ and $(I^nH)$ are pro-isomorphic.
theorems.proof: There exists $c>0$ such that $H_n\to H$ has image in $I^{n-c}H$ for $n\ge c$, and canonical maps $I^nH\to H_{n-c}$ exist. For $n\ge2c$, composing these shifted maps in either order gives the transition through $2c$ places in the respective tower. Thus $(H_n)$ and $(I^nH)$ are pro-isomorphic.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Factoring restriction on Ext through a power in the target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Let $M$ be finite, $N$ an arbitrary module, and $p>0$.
theorems.statement: There is $c\ge0$ such that, for each $n\ge c$, restriction $\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(M,N)\to\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(I^nM,N)$ factors through the map from $\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(I^nM,I^{n-c}N)$ induced by inclusion in $N$.
theorems.proof: There is $c\ge0$ such that, for each $n\ge c$, restriction $\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(M,N)\to\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(I^nM,N)$ factors through the map from $\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(I^nM,I^{n-c}N)$ induced by inclusion in $N$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Restriction on positive Ext vanishes for bounded-power torsion targets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Suppose $M$ finite, $I^bN=0$ for some $b\ge0$, and fix $p>0$.
theorems.statement: For some $n$, the inclusion $I^nM\subset M$ induces the zero map $\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(M,N)\to\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(I^nM,N)$.
theorems.proof: For some $n$, the inclusion $I^nM\subset M$ induces the zero map $\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(M,N)\to\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(I^nM,N)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The induced adic topology on Ext of a pseudo-coherent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Fix pseudo-coherent $K\in D(A)$ and a finite $A$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: For every $p\in\mathbf Z$ there exists $c\ge0$ such that for all $n\ge c$ the image of $\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(K,I^nM)\to\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(K,M)$ is contained in $I^{n-c}\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(K,M)$.
theorems.proof: For every $p\in\mathbf Z$ there exists $c\ge0$ such that for all $n\ge c$ the image of $\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(K,I^nM)\to\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(K,M)$ is contained in $I^{n-c}\operatorname{Ext}^p_A(K,M)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Truncated Koszul complexes give the pro-system of ideal powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Choose finite generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $I$. Write $K_n$ for the cohomologically indexed Koszul complex on the $n$th powers. Form $T_n=(K_n/A)[-1]$, quotienting by the degree-zero copy of $A$.
theorems.statement: The natural augmentations to $(f_1^n,\ldots,f_r^n)$ identify $(T_n)$ and $(I^n)$ as pro-objects in $D(A)$. The ideals generated by the powers of individual generators form a cofinal filtration with the ordinary powers.
theorems.proof: The natural augmentations to $(f_1^n,\ldots,f_r^n)$ identify $(T_n)$ and $(I^n)$ as pro-objects in $D(A)$. The ideals generated by the powers of individual generators form a cofinal filtration with the ordinary powers.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Termwise ideal powers agree with derived multiplication as pro-objects
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Let $M^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of finite $A$-modules.
theorems.statement: The canonical tower of morphisms $I^n\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M^\bullet\to I^nM^\bullet$ induces an isomorphism of pro-objects of $D(A)$. The right-hand complex takes the power in each cochain term.
theorems.proof: The canonical tower of morphisms $I^n\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M^\bullet\to I^nM^\bullet$ induces an isomorphism of pro-objects of $D(A)$. The right-hand complex takes the power in each cochain term.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: A high ideal power factors through the derived tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Suppose $M$ is a finite $A$-module.
theorems.statement: Some $n>0$ makes the inclusion $I^nM\to M$ factor through $I\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M\to M$ in $D(A)$.
theorems.proof: Some $n>0$ makes the inclusion $I^nM\to M$ factor through $I\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M\to M$ in $D(A)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Existence of a dominating valuation ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a local subring of a field $K$.
theorems.statement: There is a valuation ring $V$ of $K$ containing $A$ whose maximal ideal contracts to the maximal ideal of $A$. The fraction field of $V$ is all of $K$.
theorems.proof: There is a valuation ring $V$ of $K$ containing $A$ whose maximal ideal contracts to the maximal ideal of $A$. The fraction field of $V$ is all of $K$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The fraction-or-inverse condition
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a valuation ring and $x$ a nonzero element of its fraction field.
theorems.statement: At least one of $x,x^{-1}$ belongs to $A$. Both belong precisely when $x$ is a unit of $A$.
theorems.proof: At least one of $x,x^{-1}$ belongs to $A$. Both belong precisely when $x$ is a unit of $A$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Recognizing a valuation subring of a specified field
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $A\subseteq K$ and for each $x\in K^\times$ at least one of $x,x^{-1}$ belongs to $A$.
theorems.statement: Then $A$ is a valuation ring with fraction field $K$.
theorems.proof: Then $A$ is a valuation ring with fraction field $K$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Directed colimits of valuation rings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a directed system of valuation rings and unital transition homomorphisms.
theorems.statement: Its colimit is a valuation ring. The divisibility relation remains total and the colimit is a domain.
theorems.proof: Its colimit is a valuation ring. The divisibility relation remains total and the colimit is a domain.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Restriction of a valuation ring to a subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields and $B\subseteq L$ a valuation ring.
theorems.statement: Then $A=B\cap K$ is a valuation ring. If $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=L$, the fraction-or-inverse test gives $\operatorname{Frac}(A)=K$.
theorems.proof: Then $A=B\cap K$ is a valuation ring. If $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=L$, the fraction-or-inverse test gives $\operatorname{Frac}(A)=K$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Nontriviality under restriction across an algebraic extension
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $L/K$ is algebraic, $B$ has fraction field $L$ and is a valuation ring which is not a field.
theorems.statement: The valuation ring $K\cap B$ is not a field. Otherwise $K\subseteq B$ and integrality of all elements of $L$ over $K$ would force $L=B$.
theorems.proof: The valuation ring $K\cap B$ is not a field. Otherwise $K\subseteq B$ and integrality of all elements of $L$ over $K$ would force $L=B$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Prime quotients and localizations of a valuation ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a valuation ring and $\mathfrak p$ a prime of $A$.
theorems.statement: Both $A/\mathfrak p$ and $A_{\mathfrak p}$ are valuation rings. Localization at any multiplicative set avoiding zero also gives a valuation ring. Inverting zero yields the zero ring and is excluded by the domain convention.
theorems.proof: Both $A/\mathfrak p$ and $A_{\mathfrak p}$ are valuation rings. Localization at any multiplicative set avoiding zero also gives a valuation ring. Inverting zero yields the zero ring and is excluded by the domain convention.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Composition of two valuation rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $V$ be a valuation ring with residue field $K$ and $W$ a valuation ring of $K$.
theorems.statement: The inverse image of $W$ under $V\to K$ is a valuation ring. Apply the fraction-or-inverse test in $V$ and, for units, to their classes in $K$.
theorems.proof: The inverse image of $W$ under $V\to K$ is a valuation ring. Apply the fraction-or-inverse test in $V$ and, for units, to their classes in $K$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Normal domains as intersections of valuation overrings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a normal domain with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: For each $x\in K\setminus A$ there is a valuation ring $A\subseteq V\subseteq K$ excluding $x$. If $A$ is local, $V$ may be chosen to dominate $A$. Thus the relevant intersection is $A$.
theorems.proof: For each $x\in K\setminus A$ there is a valuation ring $A\subseteq V\subseteq K$ excluding $x$. If $A$ is local, $V$ may be chosen to dominate $A$. Thus the relevant intersection is $A$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Ordered value group
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ have fraction field $K$ and be a valuation ring.
theorems.statement: In $\Gamma=K^\times/A^\times$ written additively, the image of $A\setminus\{0\}$ is the positive cone including zero. Its induced order makes $\Gamma$ a totally ordered abelian group.
theorems.proof: In $\Gamma=K^\times/A^\times$ written additively, the image of $A\setminus\{0\}$ is the positive cone including zero. Its induced order makes $\Gamma$ a totally ordered abelian group.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Basic identities of the valuation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $v$ be the quotient map from the nonzero elements of the valuation ring $A$ into its ordered value group.
theorems.statement: One has $v(a)=0$ precisely for units, $v(ab)=v(a)+v(b)$ and $v(a+b)\ge\min(v(a),v(b))$ whenever the three values are defined.
theorems.proof: One has $v(a)=0$ precisely for units, $v(ab)=v(a)+v(b)$ and $v(a+b)\ge\min(v(a),v(b))$ whenever the three values are defined.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Recovering a valuation ring from a group-valued valuation
theorems.hypotheses: For a field $K$ take a homomorphism $v:K^\times\to\Gamma$ to a totally ordered abelian group satisfying the valuation inequality for nonzero sums.
theorems.statement: The nonnegative elements together with zero form a valuation ring of $K$. Its value group is $\operatorname{im}(v)$, its units have value zero, and its maximal ideal consists of zero and the elements of strictly positive value.
theorems.proof: The nonnegative elements together with zero form a valuation ring of $K$. Its value group is $\operatorname{im}(v)$, its units have value zero, and its maximal ideal consists of zero and the elements of strictly positive value.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Value sets classify ideals of a valuation ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take a valuation ring $A$ with value group $\Gamma$.
theorems.statement: Sending $I$ to $v(I\setminus\{0\})$ bijects ideals with upward closed subsets of $\Gamma_{\ge0}$, preserving inclusion. Prime ideals correspond to sets $E$ with $0\notin E$ such that $\alpha+\beta\in E$ forces $\alpha\in E$ or $\beta\in E$ for nonnegative $\alpha,\beta$.
theorems.proof: Sending $I$ to $v(I\setminus\{0\})$ bijects ideals with upward closed subsets of $\Gamma_{\ge0}$, preserving inclusion. Prime ideals correspond to sets $E$ with $0\notin E$ such that $\alpha+\beta\in E$ forces $\alpha\in E$ or $\beta\in E$ for nonnegative $\alpha,\beta$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Noetherian valuation rings
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $A$ is a valuation ring, including the field case.
theorems.statement: Then $A$ is Noetherian exactly when it is either a field or a discrete valuation ring.
theorems.proof: Then $A$ is Noetherian exactly when it is either a field or a discrete valuation ring.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Finite modules over a Noetherian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $M$ a finite $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Every submodule of $M$ is finite, ascending chains of submodules stabilize, and $M$ is finitely presented. Apply finiteness to the kernel of a finite free presentation.
theorems.proof: Every submodule of $M$ is finite, ascending chains of submodules stabilize, and $M$ is finitely presented. Apply finiteness to the kernel of a finite free presentation.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Artin–Rees lemma
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $I$ an ideal, and $N\subseteq M$ finite $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: For some $c>0$, all $n\ge c$ satisfy $I^nM\cap N=I^{n-c}(I^cM\cap N)$.
theorems.proof: For some $c>0$, all $n\ge c$ satisfy $I^nM\cap N=I^{n-c}(I^cM\cap N)$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Artin–Rees for maps
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:M\to N$ between finite modules over Noetherian $R$, put $K=\ker(f)$ and fix an ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: Some $c$ works for all $n\ge c$ in both $f^{-1}(I^nN)=K+I^{n-c}f^{-1}(I^cN)$ and $f(M)\cap I^nN\subseteq f(I^{n-c}M)$.
theorems.proof: Some $c$ works for all $n\ge c$ in both $f^{-1}(I^nN)=K+I^{n-c}f^{-1}(I^cN)$ and $f(M)\cap I^nN\subseteq f(I^{n-c}M)$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Krull intersection in a Noetherian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a proper ideal of a Noetherian local ring $R$ and $M$ finite over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $\bigcap_{n\ge0}I^nM=0$. Artin–Rees and Nakayama apply to the finite intersection submodule.
theorems.proof: Then $\bigcap_{n\ge0}I^nM=0$. Artin–Rees and Nakayama apply to the finite intersection submodule.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Krull intersection near the vanishing locus
theorems.hypotheses: For Noetherian $R$, finite $M$ and ideal $I$, put $N=\bigcap_{n\ge0}I^nM$.
theorems.statement: Every prime containing $I$ has a principal neighbourhood $D(f)$ on which $N_f=0$. If $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical, this implies $N=0$.
theorems.proof: Every prime containing $I$ has a principal neighbourhood $D(f)$ on which $N_f=0$. If $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical, this implies $N=0$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Artin–Tate lemma
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $S$ a finite type $R$-algebra and $T\subseteq S$ an $R$-subalgebra over which $S$ is module-finite.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is of finite type over $R$. Finitely many structure coefficients give a finite type intermediate algebra over which $S$, and then $T$, is finite.
theorems.proof: Then $T$ is of finite type over $R$. Finitely many structure coefficients give a finite type intermediate algebra over which $S$, and then $T$, is finite.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Additivity of length
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: Then $\ell_R(M)=\ell_R(L)+\ell_R(N)$ in the nonnegative integers with infinity.
theorems.proof: Then $\ell_R(M)=\ell_R(L)+\ell_R(N)$ in the nonnegative integers with infinity.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A power of the maximal ideal kills every finite length module
theorems.hypotheses: Take a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and an $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: If $M$ has finite length then $\mathfrak m^nM=0$ for some $n$. Otherwise the length is infinite.
theorems.proof: If $M$ has finite length then $\mathfrak m^nM=0$ for some $n$. Otherwise the length is infinite.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Length on restriction of scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Take an $S$-module $M$ for a ring map $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: Every chain of $S$-submodules is a chain of $R$-submodules, so $\ell_S(M)\le\ell_R(M)$. Surjectivity of $R\to S$ gives equality.
theorems.proof: Every chain of $S$-submodules is a chain of $R$-submodules, so $\ell_S(M)\le\ell_R(M)$. Surjectivity of $R\to S$ gives equality.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Length over the residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ annihilates $M$.
theorems.statement: Then $\ell_R(M)$ is the vector-space dimension over $R/\mathfrak m$, interpreted as infinity for infinite dimension. Finiteness of this length is equivalent to finite generation.
theorems.proof: Then $\ell_R(M)$ is the vector-space dimension over $R/\mathfrak m$, interpreted as infinity for infinite dimension. Finiteness of this length is equivalent to finite generation.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Length decreases under localization
theorems.hypotheses: Localize the $R$-module $M$ at any multiplicative subset $U$.
theorems.statement: Then $\ell_{U^{-1}R}(U^{-1}M)\le\ell_R(M)$. Contract a strict chain to $M$ and use the correspondence between localized submodules and their contractions.
theorems.proof: Then $\ell_{U^{-1}R}(U^{-1}M)\le\ell_R(M)$. Contract a strict chain to $M$ and use the correspondence between localized submodules and their contractions.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite length from nilpotent maximal-ideal action
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak m$ be a finitely generated maximal ideal and $M$ a finite module killed by a power of $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ has finite length. Its filtration by powers of $\mathfrak m$ has finitely many factors of finite dimension over the residue field.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ has finite length. Its filtration by powers of $\mathfrak m$ has finitely many factors of finite dimension over the residue field.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Simple modules are residue fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Simplicity, length one, and $M\simeq R/\mathfrak m$ for some maximal $\mathfrak m$ are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Simplicity, length one, and $M\simeq R/\mathfrak m$ for some maximal $\mathfrak m$ are equivalent.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Composition factors by localization
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a maximal strict submodule chain in a module $M$ of finite length.
theorems.statement: Its length is $\ell_R(M)$ and each factor is a residue field. The number of factors isomorphic to $R/\mathfrak m$ equals $\ell_{R_{\mathfrak m}}(M_{\mathfrak m})$.
theorems.proof: Its length is $\ell_R(M)$ and each factor is a residue field. The number of factors isomorphic to $R/\mathfrak m$ equals $\ell_{R_{\mathfrak m}}(M_{\mathfrak m})$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Restriction of finite length modules from a semilocal ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)\to B$ with $B$ semilocal. Its maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_i$ contract to $\mathfrak m$ and their residue degrees $f_i$ are finite. Let $M$ have finite $B$-length.
theorems.statement: Then $\ell_A(M)=\sum_i f_i\ell_{B_{\mathfrak n_i}}(M_{\mathfrak n_i})$, in particular it is finite.
theorems.proof: Then $\ell_A(M)=\sum_i f_i\ell_{B_{\mathfrak n_i}}(M_{\mathfrak n_i})$, in particular it is finite.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Flat local extension multiplies module length
theorems.hypotheses: Take a flat local map $(A,\mathfrak m)\to B$ and any $A$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: Then $\ell_B(B\otimes_A M)=\ell_A(M)\ell_B(B/\mathfrak m B)$, with $0\cdot\infty=0$. If the closed fibre has finite length, finiteness of length is equivalent on the two sides.
theorems.proof: Then $\ell_B(B\otimes_A M)=\ell_A(M)\ell_B(B/\mathfrak m B)$, with $0\cdot\infty=0$. If the closed fibre has finite length, finiteness of length is equivalent on the two sides.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Multiplication of closed-fibre lengths in a tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be flat local homomorphisms.
theorems.statement: The fibre length $\ell_C(C/\mathfrak m_A C)$ equals $\ell_B(B/\mathfrak m_A B)\ell_C(C/\mathfrak m_B C)$.
theorems.proof: The fibre length $\ell_C(C/\mathfrak m_A C)$ equals $\ell_B(B/\mathfrak m_A B)\ell_C(C/\mathfrak m_B C)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite-dimensional algebras are Artinian
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be finite-dimensional as an algebra over a field.
theorems.statement: Descending chains of ideals are descending chains of finite-dimensional vector subspaces and stabilize.
theorems.proof: Descending chains of ideals are descending chains of finite-dimensional vector subspaces and stabilize.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finitely many maximal ideals in an Artinian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose the ring is Artinian.
theorems.statement: Its set of maximal ideals is finite. Otherwise finite intersections of distinct maximal ideals would yield a strictly descending chain.
theorems.proof: Its set of maximal ideals is finite. Otherwise finite intersections of distinct maximal ideals would yield a strictly descending chain.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Local product decomposition from a nil Jacobson radical
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R$ has finitely many maximal ideals and each element of its Jacobson radical is nilpotent.
theorems.statement: Every prime is maximal and $R$ is the product of the localizations at its maximal ideals. The zero ring corresponds to the empty product.
theorems.proof: Every prime is maximal and $R$ is the product of the localizations at its maximal ideals. The zero ring corresponds to the empty product.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Length homomorphism for an Artinian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local Artinian.
theorems.statement: The assignment $[M]\mapsto\ell_R(M)$ defines a group map $K'_0(R)\to\mathbf Z$ since finite modules have finite length and length is additive.
theorems.proof: The assignment $[M]\mapsto\ell_R(M)$ defines a group map $K'_0(R)\to\mathbf Z$ since finite modules have finite length and length is additive.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Grothendieck groups of a product
theorems.hypotheses: Take a product $R=A\times B$.
theorems.statement: The groups $K_0(R)$ and $K'_0(R)$ decompose into the products of the corresponding groups of $A,B$. The two coordinate idempotents split each module functorially.
theorems.proof: The groups $K_0(R)$ and $K'_0(R)$ decompose into the products of the corresponding groups of $A,B$. The two coordinate idempotents split each module functorially.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Length identifies the Grothendieck group of finite modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local Artinian.
theorems.statement: Length gives an isomorphism $K'_0(R)\simeq\mathbf Z$. The inverse sends one to the class of the residue field, the unique simple module up to isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Length gives an isomorphism $K'_0(R)\simeq\mathbf Z$. The inverse sends one to the class of the residue field, the unique simple module up to isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Rank identifies the projective Grothendieck group of a local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local.
theorems.statement: Finite projectives are finite free. Taking rank induces $K_0(R)\simeq\mathbf Z$ with inverse sending one to $[R]$.
theorems.proof: Finite projectives are finite free. Taking rank induces $K_0(R)\simeq\mathbf Z$ with inverse sending one to $[R]$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Cartan map for a local Artinian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local Artinian and identify its two Grothendieck groups with the integers via rank and length.
theorems.statement: The map $K_0(R)\to K'_0(R)$ forgetting projectivity is multiplication by $\ell_R(R)$.
theorems.proof: The map $K_0(R)\to K'_0(R)$ forgetting projectivity is multiplication by $\ell_R(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Graded Nakayama lemma
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be nonnegatively graded, $S_+$ its positive-degree ideal, and consider graded $S$-modules and homogeneous maps.
theorems.statement: A finite $M=S_+M$ vanishes. If $M=N+S_+N'$ for graded submodules with $N'$ finite then $M=N$. A map to finite $M$ surjective modulo $S_+$ is surjective. Homogeneous elements generating finite $M$ modulo $S_+$ generate $M$.
theorems.proof: A finite $M=S_+M$ vanishes. If $M=N+S_+N'$ for graded submodules with $N'$ finite then $M=N$. A map to finite $M$ surjective modulo $S_+$ is surjective. Homogeneous elements generating finite $M$ modulo $S_+$ generate $M$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Standard grading of high Veronese subalgebras
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose the nonnegatively graded $S$ is finite type over $S_0$.
theorems.statement: For every sufficiently divisible positive $d$, the Veronese algebra $\bigoplus_{n\ge0} S_{nd}$ is generated by its new degree-one part $S_d$.
theorems.proof: For every sufficiently divisible positive $d$, the Veronese algebra $\bigoplus_{n\ge0} S_{nd}$ is generated by its new degree-one part $S_d$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Integral closure inherits the grading
theorems.hypotheses: For a degree-preserving homomorphism $R\to S$ of nonnegatively graded rings, let $C$ be the integral closure inside $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $C=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}(C\cap S_d)$, so all homogeneous components of an integral element are integral.
theorems.proof: Then $C=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}(C\cap S_d)$, so all homogeneous components of an integral element are integral.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Graded primes and degree-zero spectra
theorems.hypotheses: Let the $\mathbf Z$-graded ring $S$ contain a homogeneous unit of positive degree.
theorems.statement: Contraction gives a homeomorphism from the subspace of homogeneous prime ideals of $S$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(S_0)$.
theorems.proof: Contraction gives a homeomorphism from the subspace of homogeneous prime ideals of $S$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(S_0)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Principal charts and closed subsets of Proj
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}S_d$. For homogeneous $f$ of positive degree write $D_+(f)$ for the primes of $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ avoiding $f$.
theorems.statement: These form a basis and $D_+(fg)=D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)$. The chart is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}((S_f)_0)$ via homogeneous primes of $S_f$. For $g=\sum_i g_i$, $D(g)$ on Proj is the union of the opens for its components. For $g_0\in S_0$ its open is the union of $D_+(g_0 f)$ over positive-degree homogeneous $f$. The closed sets are exactly $V_+(I)$ for homogeneous $I$, empty exactly if $S_+\subseteq\sqrt I$. Proj need not be quasi-compact for arbitrary $S$.
theorems.proof: These form a basis and $D_+(fg)=D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)$. The chart is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}((S_f)_0)$ via homogeneous primes of $S_f$. For $g=\sum_i g_i$, $D(g)$ on Proj is the union of the opens for its components. For $g_0\in S_0$ its open is the union of $D_+(g_0 f)$ over positive-degree homogeneous $f$. The closed sets are exactly $V_+(I)$ for homogeneous $I$, empty exactly if $S_+\subseteq\sqrt I$. Proj need not be quasi-compact for arbitrary $S$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Homogeneous localizations on a Proj chart
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be graded and let $\mathfrak p\in D_+(f)$ correspond to $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}((S_f)_0)$.
theorems.statement: Localizing the degree-zero chart ring at $\mathfrak q$ gives $S_{(\mathfrak p)}$. Compatibly $((M_f)_0)_{\mathfrak q}=M_{(\mathfrak p)}$.
theorems.proof: Localizing the degree-zero chart ring at $\mathfrak q$ gives $S_{(\mathfrak p)}$. Compatibly $((M_f)_0)_{\mathfrak q}=M_{(\mathfrak p)}$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Homogeneous prime avoidance
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a graded ideal $I\subseteq S_+$ is contained in none of finitely many homogeneous primes $\mathfrak p_i$.
theorems.statement: A single homogeneous element of positive degree in $I$ lies outside every $\mathfrak p_i$.
theorems.proof: A single homogeneous element of positive degree in $I$ lies outside every $\mathfrak p_i$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Homogeneous core of a prime
theorems.hypotheses: Given a prime $\mathfrak p$ of a graded ring, form the ideal generated by the homogeneous elements of $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: The resulting homogeneous ideal is prime.
theorems.proof: The resulting homogeneous ideal is prime.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Homogeneity of minimal primes
theorems.hypotheses: Take a graded ring and a homogeneous ideal.
theorems.statement: Every prime minimal over this ideal is homogeneous. In particular every minimal prime of the ring is homogeneous.
theorems.proof: Every prime minimal over this ideal is homogeneous. In particular every minimal prime of the ring is homogeneous.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finiteness after dehomogenization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type graded $R$-algebra and $f$ homogeneous of positive degree.
theorems.statement: The degree-zero localization $(S_f)_0$ is finite type over $R$. For finite graded $M$, the module $(M_f)_0$ is finite over $(S_f)_0$.
theorems.proof: The degree-zero localization $(S_f)_0$ is finite type over $R$. For finite graded $M$, the module $(M_f)_0$ is finite over $(S_f)_0$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Homogenizing a finite algebra presentation and module
theorems.hypotheses: Take a finite type $R$-algebra $A$ and finite $A$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: There exist a standard graded $R$-algebra $S$ generated in degree one by finitely many elements, a finite graded $S$-module $N$, and $f\in S_1$ with $S_0=R$, $(S_f)_0\simeq A$ and $(N_f)_0\simeq M$.
theorems.proof: There exist a standard graded $R$-algebra $S$ generated in degree one by finitely many elements, a finite graded $S$-module $N$, and $f\in S_1$ with $S_0=R$, $(S_f)_0\simeq A$ and $(N_f)_0\simeq M$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Homogeneous generators of the irrelevant ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a family of positive-degree homogeneous elements of $S$.
theorems.statement: It generates $S$ over $S_0$ as an algebra exactly when it generates $S_+$ as an ideal, by induction on degree.
theorems.proof: It generates $S$ over $S_0$ as an algebra exactly when it generates $S_+$ as an ideal, by induction on degree.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Noetherian graded ring test
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be nonnegatively graded.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is Noetherian precisely when $S_0$ is Noetherian and the ideal $S_+$ is finite. Use homogeneous generators and the Hilbert basis theorem.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is Noetherian precisely when $S_0$ is Noetherian and the ideal $S_+$ is finite. Use homogeneous generators and the Hilbert basis theorem.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Numerical polynomials under homomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f(n)$ be a numerical polynomial in an abelian group $A$ and let $u:A\to B$ be additive.
theorems.statement: Then $u(f(n))$ is numerical polynomial with coefficients the images under $u$ of the binomial-basis coefficients.
theorems.proof: Then $u(f(n))$ is numerical polynomial with coefficients the images under $u$ of the binomial-basis coefficients.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Discrete antiderivatives of numerical polynomials
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $f(n)$ is defined in an abelian group for all sufficiently large integers and $f(n)-f(n-1)$ is numerical polynomial.
theorems.statement: Then $f(n)$ is itself numerical polynomial, by summing the binomial coefficient identities and choosing its constant term.
theorems.proof: Then $f(n)$ is itself numerical polynomial, by summing the binomial coefficient identities and choosing its constant term.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finiteness of graded pieces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite graded $S$-module, where $S$ is a nonnegatively graded finite type $S_0$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Every $M_n$ is finite as an $S_0$-module. Only finitely many monomials in positive-degree generators contribute at a fixed degree for each module generator.
theorems.proof: Every $M_n$ is finite as an $S_0$-module. Only finitely many monomials in positive-degree generators contribute at a fixed degree for each module generator.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Graded Hilbert polynomial in the Grothendieck group
theorems.hypotheses: Take a Noetherian graded $S$ with $S_+$ generated in degree one and a finite graded $S$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: The function $n\mapsto[M_n]$ with values in $K'_0(S_0)$ is a numerical polynomial for large $n$.
theorems.proof: The function $n\mapsto[M_n]$ with values in $K'_0(S_0)$ is a numerical polynomial for large $n$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Hilbert polynomial after a nonzero homogeneous relation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\ne0$ be homogeneous in the standard graded $k[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$ over a field, with $d\ge1$.
theorems.statement: For the quotient, the eventual dimension polynomial of the degree-$n$ part has degree less than $d-1$, or vanishes identically. For $d=1$ it vanishes.
theorems.proof: For the quotient, the eventual dimension polynomial of the degree-$n$ part has degree less than $d-1$, or vanishes identically. For $d=1$ it vanishes.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Bounds after removing a finite length quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Over a Noetherian local ring with ideal of definition $I$, put $\chi_M(n)=\ell(M/I^{n+1}M)$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\ell(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)$. Take $M'\subseteq M$ finite with quotient of finite length.
theorems.statement: Some constants $c_1,c_2$ give $c_1+\chi_{M'}(n-c_2)\le\chi_M(n)\le c_1+\chi_{M'}(n)$ for $n\ge c_2$.
theorems.proof: Some constants $c_1,c_2$ give $c_1+\chi_{M'}(n-c_2)\le\chi_M(n)\le c_1+\chi_{M'}(n)$ for $n\ge c_2$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Shifted Hilbert functions in an exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Over a Noetherian local ring with ideal of definition $I$, put $\chi_M(n)=\ell(M/I^{n+1}M)$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\ell(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)$. Suppose $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ is exact with all terms finite.
theorems.statement: There exist $L'\subseteq L$ of finite colength $a$ and $c\ge0$ with $\chi_M(n)=\chi_N(n)+\chi_{L'}(n-c)+a$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\varphi_N(n)+\varphi_{L'}(n-c)$ for $n\ge c$.
theorems.proof: There exist $L'\subseteq L$ of finite colength $a$ and $c\ge0$ with $\chi_M(n)=\chi_N(n)+\chi_{L'}(n-c)+a$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\varphi_N(n)+\varphi_{L'}(n-c)$ for $n\ge c$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Comparison between two ideals of definition
theorems.hypotheses: Over a Noetherian local ring with ideal of definition $I$, put $\chi_M(n)=\ell(M/I^{n+1}M)$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\ell(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)$. Let $I,J$ be ideals of definition and $M$ finite.
theorems.statement: For some integer $a>0$, $\chi_{I,M}(n)\le\chi_{J,M}(an)$ for $n\ge1$. Cofinality of powers of the two ideals gives the bound.
theorems.proof: For some integer $a>0$, $\chi_{I,M}(n)\le\chi_{J,M}(an)$ for $n\ge1$. Cofinality of powers of the two ideals gives the bound.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Eventual polynomiality of Hilbert functions
theorems.hypotheses: Over a Noetherian local ring with ideal of definition $I$, put $\chi_M(n)=\ell(M/I^{n+1}M)$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\ell(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)$. Take a finite module $M$.
theorems.statement: Both $\varphi_M$ and $\chi_M$ are numerical polynomials for all sufficiently large arguments.
theorems.proof: Both $\varphi_M$ and $\chi_M$ are numerical polynomials for all sufficiently large arguments.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Independence of Hilbert degrees
theorems.hypotheses: Over a Noetherian local ring with ideal of definition $I$, put $\chi_M(n)=\ell(M/I^{n+1}M)$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\ell(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)$. Take a finite module $M$.
theorems.statement: The eventual polynomial degrees of $\chi_M$ and of $\varphi_M$ are separately independent of the chosen ideal of definition.
theorems.proof: The eventual polynomial degrees of $\chi_M$ and of $\varphi_M$ are separately independent of the chosen ideal of definition.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Lower-degree difference after finite colength
theorems.hypotheses: Over a Noetherian local ring with ideal of definition $I$, put $\chi_M(n)=\ell(M/I^{n+1}M)$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\ell(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)$. Suppose $M$ is finite of infinite length and $L\subset M$ has finite colength.
theorems.statement: The eventual polynomial $\chi_M-\chi_L$ has degree strictly less than the common degree of $\chi_M$ and $\chi_L$.
theorems.proof: The eventual polynomial $\chi_M-\chi_L$ has degree strictly less than the common degree of $\chi_M$ and $\chi_L$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: The maximal degree in an exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Over a Noetherian local ring with ideal of definition $I$, put $\chi_M(n)=\ell(M/I^{n+1}M)$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\ell(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)$. Let $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ be exact with all terms finite.
theorems.statement: The degree of $\chi_M$ is the maximum of those of $\chi_L,\chi_N$, and $d(M)=\max(d(L),d(N))$. If $L$ has infinite length, $\chi_M-\chi_N-\chi_L$ has degree strictly below that of $\chi_L$.
theorems.proof: The degree of $\chi_M$ is the maximum of those of $\chi_L,\chi_N$, and $d(M)=\max(d(L),d(N))$. If $L$ has infinite length, $\chi_M-\chi_N-\chi_L$ has degree strictly below that of $\chi_L$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Dimension from the heights of maximal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring.
theorems.statement: The dimension equals the supremum of heights of all primes, and equally the supremum over maximal ideals. Every chain ends in a prime contained in some maximal ideal.
theorems.proof: The dimension equals the supremum of heights of all primes, and equally the supremum over maximal ideals. Every chain ends in a prime contained in some maximal ideal.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Artinian and zero-dimensional Noetherian rings
theorems.hypotheses: Assume the ring is nonzero for the equality of its dimension to zero.
theorems.statement: It is Artinian precisely when it is Noetherian of dimension zero. The zero ring is Artinian and has no strict inclusions of primes.
theorems.proof: It is Artinian precisely when it is Noetherian of dimension zero. The zero ring is Artinian and has no strict inclusions of primes.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Zero-dimensional local Hilbert criterion
theorems.hypotheses: Over a Noetherian local ring with ideal of definition $I$, put $\chi_M(n)=\ell(M/I^{n+1}M)$ and $\varphi_M(n)=\ell(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)$. Take the module $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim R=0$ exactly when $d(R)=0$, where $d(R)$ is the degree of the cumulative Hilbert polynomial.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim R=0$ exactly when $d(R)=0$, where $d(R)$ is the degree of the cumulative Hilbert polynomial.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Artinian decomposition and the zero-dimensional criteria
theorems.hypotheses: For an arbitrary ring use “no strict prime inclusions” for dimension at most zero, including the empty spectrum.
theorems.statement: Artinianness, finite length as a self-module, and Noetherianness with no strict prime inclusions are equivalent. Equivalently the ring is Noetherian with finite discrete spectrum, or Noetherian semilocal with nilpotent Jacobson radical. Equivalently it is a finite product of Artinian local rings, which can themselves be described as Noetherian local rings with dimension zero, Hilbert degree zero, or nilpotent maximal ideal.
theorems.proof: Artinianness, finite length as a self-module, and Noetherianness with no strict prime inclusions are equivalent. Equivalently the ring is Noetherian with finite discrete spectrum, or Noetherian semilocal with nilpotent Jacobson radical. Equivalently it is a finite product of Artinian local rings, which can themselves be described as Noetherian local rings with dimension zero, Hilbert degree zero, or nilpotent maximal ideal.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Dimension one via a parameter
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local.
theorems.statement: Dimension one, $d(R)=1$, and minimum number of generators one among ideals of definition are equivalent. Equivalently there exists a nonnilpotent $x\in\mathfrak m$ with $\sqrt{(x)}=\mathfrak m$, or $V(x)=\{\mathfrak m\}$.
theorems.proof: Dimension one, $d(R)=1$, and minimum number of generators one among ideals of definition are equivalent. Equivalently there exists a nonnilpotent $x\in\mathfrak m$ with $\sqrt{(x)}=\mathfrak m$, or $V(x)=\{\mathfrak m\}$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Dimension equals the number of parameters
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local and $d\ge0$.
theorems.statement: The equality $\dim R=d$ is equivalent both to $d(R)=d$ and to $d$ being the minimal number of generators of an ideal of definition. Here $d(R)$ is the degree of the cumulative Hilbert polynomial.
theorems.proof: The equality $\dim R=d$ is equivalent both to $d(R)=d$ and to $d$ being the minimal number of generators of an ideal of definition. Here $d(R)$ is the degree of the cumulative Hilbert polynomial.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Principal ideal theorem
theorems.hypotheses: For Noetherian $R$ and $x\in R$, choose a prime minimal over $(x)$.
theorems.statement: Its height is at most one. More generally if $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $(\mathfrak p,x)$ for prime $\mathfrak p$, no prime lies strictly between $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: Its height is at most one. More generally if $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $(\mathfrak p,x)$ for prime $\mathfrak p$, no prime lies strictly between $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Generalized principal ideal theorem
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ be elements of a Noetherian ring.
theorems.statement: Every minimal prime over their ideal has height at most $r$. If $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $(\mathfrak p,f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, every strict chain from the prime $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak q$ has length at most $r$.
theorems.proof: Every minimal prime over their ideal has height at most $r$. If $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $(\mathfrak p,f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, every strict chain from the prime $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak q$ has length at most $r$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Dimension after quotient by one element
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local and $x$ in its maximal ideal.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim R\le1+\dim(R/xR)$. Equality holds when $x$ avoids all minimal primes, in particular if it is a nonzerodivisor.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim R\le1+\dim(R/xR)$. Equality holds when $x$ avoids all minimal primes, in particular if it is a nonzerodivisor.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Initial segments of a system of parameters
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $d=\dim R$ for a Noetherian local ring and $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ generate an ideal of definition.
theorems.statement: Each quotient by the first $i$ parameters has dimension $d-i$ for $1\le i\le d$.
theorems.proof: Each quotient by the first $i$ parameters has dimension $d-i$ for $1\le i\le d$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Infinite open subsets of a higher-dimensional local domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local domain of dimension at least two.
theorems.statement: Every nonempty open subset of its prime spectrum has infinitely many points.
theorems.proof: Every nonempty open subset of its prime spectrum has infinitely many points.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Jacobson tests from infinite prime incidence
theorems.hypotheses: Take a Noetherian ring $R$.
theorems.statement: If each prime is maximal or contained in infinitely many primes, then $R$ is Jacobson. In particular a one-dimensional Noetherian domain with infinitely many primes is Jacobson.
theorems.proof: If each prime is maximal or contained in infinitely many primes, then $R$ is Jacobson. In particular a one-dimensional Noetherian domain with infinitely many primes is Jacobson.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Prime filtration of a finite module
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $M$ is finite over a Noetherian ring $R$.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite filtration whose nonzero successive factors have the form $R/\mathfrak p_i$ with $\mathfrak p_i$ prime.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite filtration whose nonzero successive factors have the form $R/\mathfrak p_i$ with $\mathfrak p_i$ prime.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Support from a prime filtration
theorems.hypotheses: For finite $M$ over Noetherian $R$ take a filtration with factors $R/\mathfrak p_i$.
theorems.statement: The union of $V(\mathfrak p_i)$ is the support of $M$. In particular each $\mathfrak p_i$ lies in the support.
theorems.proof: The union of $V(\mathfrak p_i)$ is the support of $M$. In particular each $\mathfrak p_i$ lies in the support.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite length and singleton support
theorems.hypotheses: Take a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$.
theorems.statement: It has finite length exactly when its support consists solely of $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.proof: It has finite length exactly when its support consists solely of $\mathfrak m$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Support inside a vanishing locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $M$ finite and $I$ an ideal.
theorems.statement: Some power of $I$ annihilates $M$ exactly when $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subseteq V(I)$. Use the radical of the annihilator and finite generation of $I$.
theorems.proof: Some power of $I$ annihilates $M$ exactly when $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subseteq V(I)$. Use the radical of the annihilator and finite generation of $I$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Multiplicities of minimal primes in a filtration
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime filtration of finite $M$ over Noetherian $R$ with factors $R/\mathfrak p_i$.
theorems.statement: The minimal primes among the $\mathfrak p_i$ are the minimal points of the support. Each such $\mathfrak p$ occurs $\ell_{R_{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p})$ times.
theorems.proof: The minimal primes among the $\mathfrak p_i$ are the minimal points of the support. Each such $\mathfrak p$ occurs $\ell_{R_{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p})$ times.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Dimension of support from the cumulative Hilbert function
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over Noetherian local $R$.
theorems.statement: The numerical invariant $d(M)$ defined from the cumulative Hilbert polynomial equals the dimension of $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, with the source convention for the zero module.
theorems.proof: The numerical invariant $d(M)$ defined from the cumulative Hilbert polynomial equals the dimension of $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, with the source convention for the zero module.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Support dimensions in an exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ be exact with finite terms over a Noetherian ring.
theorems.statement: The dimension of the support of $M$ is the maximum of the dimensions for $L$ and $N$, since it is the union of those closed supports.
theorems.proof: The dimension of the support of $M$ is the maximum of the dimensions for $L$ and $N$, since it is the union of those closed supports.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated primes belong to the support
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathfrak p$ be the annihilator of an element $x$ of the $R$-module $M$. Assume $\mathfrak p$ is prime.
theorems.statement: Then $M_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$ because no element outside $\mathfrak p$ kills $x$. Thus $\operatorname{Ass}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(M)$.
theorems.proof: Then $M_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$ because no element outside $\mathfrak p$ kills $x$. Thus $\operatorname{Ass}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(M)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated primes in extensions and direct sums
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ be exact.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Ass}(L)\subseteq\operatorname{Ass}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Ass}(L)\cup\operatorname{Ass}(N)$. For $L\oplus N$ the outer union is the exact associated-prime set.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Ass}(L)\subseteq\operatorname{Ass}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Ass}(L)\cup\operatorname{Ass}(N)$. For $L\oplus N$ the outer union is the exact associated-prime set.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated primes bounded by the primes in a filtration
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose an $R$-module $M$ has a finite filtration with factors $R/\mathfrak p_i$ for primes $\mathfrak p_i$.
theorems.statement: Every associated prime is one of the $\mathfrak p_i$. This follows by applying the inclusion for short exact sequences at each step.
theorems.proof: Every associated prime is one of the $\mathfrak p_i$. This follows by applying the inclusion for short exact sequences at each step.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Three descriptions of the minimal associated primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over Noetherian $R$ and choose any prime filtration.
theorems.statement: The minimal elements of its support, the minimal associated primes, and the minimal elements among the primes of the filtration coincide.
theorems.proof: The minimal elements of its support, the minimal associated primes, and the minimal elements among the primes of the filtration coincide.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Nonzero modules have associated primes over Noetherian rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $M$ any $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The module is zero exactly when $\operatorname{Ass}(M)$ is empty. A maximal annihilator of a nonzero element is prime.
theorems.proof: The module is zero exactly when $\operatorname{Ass}(M)$ is empty. A maximal annihilator of a nonzero element is prime.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Minimal support points are associated
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $M$ any $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Every minimal element of $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}(M)$. No finite generation of $M$ is required.
theorems.proof: Every minimal element of $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}(M)$. No finite generation of $M$ is required.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Zero divisors from associated primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an arbitrary module over a Noetherian ring $R$.
theorems.statement: The scalars which kill a nonzero element of $M$ form exactly the union of the associated primes of $M$.
theorems.proof: The scalars which kill a nonzero element of $M$ form exactly the union of the associated primes of $M$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Dimension of a module after one equation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite and nonzero over a Noetherian local ring, and $f$ in its maximal ideal. Write $d(N)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)$.
theorems.statement: Then $d(M/fM)\le d(M)\le d(M/fM)+1$. If $f$ avoids the minimal primes of the support, the right inequality is equality.
theorems.proof: Then $d(M/fM)\le d(M)\le d(M/fM)+1$. If $f$ avoids the minimal primes of the support, the right inequality is equality.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Contraction of associated primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $S$-module for a ring map $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: Contraction sends $\operatorname{Ass}_S(M)$ into $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ since annihilators contract.
theorems.proof: Contraction sends $\operatorname{Ass}_S(M)$ into $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ since annihilators contract.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated primes under restriction from a Noetherian target
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to S$ with $S$ Noetherian and $M$ any $S$-module.
theorems.statement: The contractions of the associated primes over $S$ exhaust $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$.
theorems.proof: The contractions of the associated primes over $S$ exhaust $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated primes of a quotient-ring module
theorems.hypotheses: Take an $R/I$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: Under the closed inclusion of spectra one has $\operatorname{Ass}_{R/I}(M)=\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$.
theorems.proof: Under the closed inclusion of spectra one has $\operatorname{Ass}_{R/I}(M)=\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Testing a single associated prime in its stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Take an $R$-module $M$ and a prime $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: If $\mathfrak p$ is associated to $M$, its localization is associated to $M_{\mathfrak p}$. Conversely the local assertion implies the global one when $\mathfrak p$ is finitely generated.
theorems.proof: If $\mathfrak p$ is associated to $M$, its localization is associated to $M_{\mathfrak p}$. Conversely the local assertion implies the global one when $\mathfrak p$ is finitely generated.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated primes after localization
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $U$ multiplicative and identify $\operatorname{Spec}(U^{-1}R)$ with the primes avoiding $U$.
theorems.statement: For $U^{-1}M$ its associated primes over $R$ equal its associated primes over $U^{-1}R$ under this identification. They contain every associated prime of $M$ avoiding $U$, with equality if $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: For $U^{-1}M$ its associated primes over $R$ equal its associated primes over $U^{-1}R$ under this identification. They contain every associated prime of $M$ avoiding $U$, with equality if $R$ is Noetherian.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localization at module nonzerodivisors
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose all elements of the multiplicative set $U$ act injectively on $M$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)=\operatorname{Ass}_R(U^{-1}M)$. Localization does not change the annihilator of a numerator under this hypothesis.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)=\operatorname{Ass}_R(U^{-1}M)$. Localization does not change the annihilator of a numerator under this hypothesis.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Prime avoidance for a module nonzerodivisor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over Noetherian local $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: Some element of $I$ acts injectively on $M$ exactly when $I$ is contained in no associated prime of $M$. Use finiteness of associated primes and prime avoidance.
theorems.proof: Some element of $I$ acts injectively on $M$ exactly when $I$ is contained in no associated prime of $M$. Use finiteness of associated primes and prime avoidance.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated localizations detect elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $M$ an arbitrary $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The natural map $M\to\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)}M_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective. A nonzero kernel would have an associated prime.
theorems.proof: The natural map $M\to\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)}M_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective. A nonzero kernel would have an associated prime.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A nonunit nonzerodivisor in positive dimension
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $S$ is finite type over a field $k$ and has positive dimension.
theorems.statement: There exists an element of $S$ which acts injectively on $S$ and is not a unit.
theorems.proof: There exists an element of $S$ which acts injectively on $S$ and is not a unit.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Six relative associated-prime tests
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to S$ and $S$-module $N$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$ when testing a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$. Let $A,A'$ test association of $\mathfrak q$ in $N\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ over $S$ or the fibre ring respectively. Let $C,D$ test association in $N/\mathfrak pN$ or $N/\mathfrak p'N$ for some prime $\mathfrak p'$. Let $B,F$ test association in $N\otimes_R M$ for some module $M$ or some finite $M$, respectively.
theorems.statement: Always $A=A'$, $C\subseteq A\subseteq B$ and $C\subseteq D\subseteq F\subseteq B$. For Noetherian $S$, $A=C$ and $B=F$. For $R$-flat $N$, $A=C=D$ and $B=F$. If also $R$ is Noetherian then all six sets coincide.
theorems.proof: Always $A=A'$, $C\subseteq A\subseteq B$ and $C\subseteq D\subseteq F\subseteq B$. For Noetherian $S$, $A=C$ and $B=F$. For $R$-flat $N$, $A=C=D$ and $B=F$. If also $R$ is Noetherian then all six sets coincide.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Bourbaki formula for associated primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$, let $M$ be an $R$-module and let $N$ be an $S$-module flat over $R$.
theorems.statement: The associated primes over $S$ of $M\otimes_RN$ contain the union of $\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak pN)$ over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$. If $R$ is Noetherian there is equality.
theorems.proof: The associated primes over $S$ of $M\otimes_RN$ contain the union of $\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak pN)$ over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$. If $R$ is Noetherian there is equality.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Associated primes over the generic fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose the domain $R$ has fraction field $K$, $R\to S$ is a ring map and $N$ is an $S$-module flat over $R$.
theorems.statement: The associated primes of $N$ over $S$ agree with those of $N\otimes_R K$ computed over $S$ or over the fibre ring $S\otimes_R K$, after contraction.
theorems.proof: The associated primes of $N$ over $S$ agree with those of $N\otimes_R K$ computed over $S$ or over the fibre ring $S\otimes_R K$, after contraction.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Bourbaki formula with fibre rings
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to S$, fix an $R$-module $M$ and an $S$-module $N$ flat over $R$. Identify fibre prime spectra with subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$.
theorems.statement: The associated primes of $M\otimes_RN$ contain the union, over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$, of the associated primes of $N\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ over the fibre ring. When $R$ is Noetherian the inclusion is equality.
theorems.proof: The associated primes of $M\otimes_RN$ contain the union, over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$, of the associated primes of $N\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ over the fibre ring. When $R$ is Noetherian the inclusion is equality.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Lifting a weakly associated prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $S$-module under a ring homomorphism $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: Every weakly associated prime of $M$ over $R$ is the contraction of a weakly associated prime over $S$.
theorems.proof: Every weakly associated prime of $M$ over $R$ is the contraction of a weakly associated prime over $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Weakly associated primes under finite maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite and let $M$ be an $S$-module.
theorems.statement: Contraction takes the weakly associated primes over $S$ onto precisely those over $R$.
theorems.proof: Contraction takes the weakly associated primes over $S$ onto precisely those over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Weakly associated primes of the generic fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $N$ be an $S$-module flat over a domain $R$ via $R\to S$, and let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$.
theorems.statement: The weakly associated primes of $N$ coincide with those of $N\otimes_R K$ over $S\otimes_R K$ under the injection of spectra.
theorems.proof: The weakly associated primes of $N$ coincide with those of $N\otimes_R K$ over $S\otimes_R K$ under the injection of spectra.

theorems.subject: ring-map-module
theorems.name: Contraction after extending a ground field
theorems.hypotheses: For $K/k$ a field extension, $R$ a $k$-algebra and $M$ an $R$-module, take a weakly associated prime of $M\otimes_kK$ over $R\otimes_kK$.
theorems.statement: Its contraction is weakly associated to $M$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: Its contraction is weakly associated to $M$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Removing embedded associated primes
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $M$ is finite over Noetherian $R$. Consider submodules with nowhere dense support in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$.
theorems.statement: They have a largest member $K$. The quotient $M'=M/K$ has the same support and no embedded associated primes. For every $f$ in all the embedded associated primes of $M$, localization identifies $M_f$ and $M'_f$.
theorems.proof: They have a largest member $K$. The quotient $M'=M/K$ has the same support and no embedded associated primes. For every $f$ in all the embedded associated primes of $M$, localization identifies $M_f$ and $M'_f$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Removing embedded primes commutes with principal localization
theorems.hypotheses: Take finite $M$ over Noetherian $R$ and $f\in R$. Write $M'$ for the quotient by the largest submodule with nowhere dense support.
theorems.statement: The canonical quotient localized at $f$ identifies $(M')_f$ with $(M_f)'$.
theorems.proof: The canonical quotient localized at $f$ identifies $(M')_f$ with $(M_f)'$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Annihilator quotient without embedded primes
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $M$ is finite over Noetherian $R$ and has no embedded associated primes.
theorems.statement: The ring $R/\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)$ has no embedded associated primes as a module over itself.
theorems.proof: The ring $R/\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)$ has no embedded associated primes as a module over itself.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth using only successive injectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Take a finite $R$-module $M$ and ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: The $I$-depth equals the supremum of lengths of sequences of elements in $I$ acting injectively on successive quotients of $M$. No nonzero final quotient is required for this formulation, including when $IM=M$.
theorems.proof: The $I$-depth equals the supremum of lengths of sequences of elements in $I$ acting injectively on successive quotients of $M$. No nonzero final quotient is required for this formulation, including when $IM=M$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth is bounded by support dimension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite nonzero module over a Noetherian local ring.
theorems.statement: Its depth at the maximal ideal is at most $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$.
theorems.proof: Its depth at the maximal ideal is at most $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finiteness of ideal-depth
theorems.hypotheses: Take finite nonzero $M$ over Noetherian $R$ and an ideal $I$ with $IM\ne M$.
theorems.statement: The supremum defining $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ is finite.
theorems.proof: The supremum defining $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ is finite.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth lemma for short exact sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $0\to L\to M\to N\to0$ is exact with all three terms nonzero and finite over a Noetherian local ring. Write $a,b,c$ for their respective depths.
theorems.statement: Then $b\ge\min(a,c)$, $c\ge\min(b,a-1)$ and $a\ge\min(b,c+1)$, by the long exact Ext sequence with the residue field.
theorems.proof: Then $b\ge\min(a,c)$, $c\ge\min(b,a-1)$ and $a\ge\min(b,c+1)$, by the long exact Ext sequence with the residue field.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth after dividing by a regular element
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite and nonzero over Noetherian local $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and $x\in\mathfrak m$ act injectively on $M$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{depth}(M/xM)=\operatorname{depth}(M)-1$. Each $M$-regular sequence in the maximal ideal extends to one of length $\operatorname{depth}(M)$.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{depth}(M/xM)=\operatorname{depth}(M)-1$. Each $M$-regular sequence in the maximal ideal extends to one of length $\operatorname{depth}(M)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated primes after a power of a parameter
theorems.hypotheses: Over Noetherian local $(R,\mathfrak m)$ take finite $M$, $x\in\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$ and $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $\mathfrak p+(x)$.
theorems.statement: Then $\mathfrak q$ is associated to $M/x^nM$ for at least one $n\ge1$.
theorems.proof: Then $\mathfrak q$ is associated to $M/x^nM$ for at least one $n\ge1$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth bound from each associated prime
theorems.hypotheses: For finite $M$ over a Noetherian local ring choose $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{depth}(M)\le\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{depth}(M)\le\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth inequality after localization
theorems.hypotheses: Take finite $M$ over Noetherian local $R$ and a prime $\mathfrak p$. Use infinite depth for the zero module.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{depth}(M)\le\operatorname{depth}(M_{\mathfrak p})+\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{depth}(M)\le\operatorname{depth}(M_{\mathfrak p})+\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Depth under finite restriction of scalars
theorems.hypotheses: For Noetherian local $(R,\mathfrak m)$ let $S$ be a finite $R$-algebra and $N$ finite over $S$.
theorems.statement: The $\mathfrak m$-depth of $N$ as an $R$-module is the minimum of the local depths at all maximal ideals of $S$. If $S=0$, use the empty infimum $+\infty$.
theorems.proof: The $\mathfrak m$-depth of $N$ as an $R$-module is the minimum of the local depths at all maximal ideals of $S$. If $S=0$, use the empty infimum $+\infty$.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Flat change of scalars in the first Ext variable
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be flat, $M$ an $R$-module, and $N$ an $A$-module.
theorems.statement: For $i\ge0$, restriction and adjunction give $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(A\otimes_R M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M,N)$. Extend a free resolution along the flat map.
theorems.proof: For $i\ge0$, restriction and adjunction give $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(A\otimes_R M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M,N)$. Extend a free resolution along the flat map.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Split injections detected modulo arbitrarily high powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $I$ contained in its Jacobson radical, and $u:N\to M$ a map of finite modules.
theorems.statement: If the reduction of $u$ modulo $I^n$ is split injective for arbitrarily large $n$, then $u$ is split injective over $R$. The splittings at different exponents need not be chosen compatibly.
theorems.proof: If the reduction of $u$ modulo $I^n$ is split injective for arbitrarily large $n$, then $u$ is split injective over $R$. The splittings at different exponents need not be chosen compatibly.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Independence of the lift defining Tor
theorems.hypotheses: Let a map $M_1\to M_2$ be lifted to a chain map between free resolutions, then tensor with $N$.
theorems.statement: The homology map is independent of the lift, sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms, and for the identity on the same resolution it is the identity. Chain-homotopic lifts induce identical homology maps.
theorems.proof: The homology map is independent of the lift, sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms, and for the identity on the same resolution it is the identity. Chain-homotopic lifts induce identical homology maps.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Long exact Tor sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $M$ and an exact sequence $0\to L\to N\to P\to0$ over $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural long exact sequence with maps from $\operatorname{Tor}_i(M,L)$ through $\operatorname{Tor}_i(M,N)$ to $\operatorname{Tor}_i(M,P)$, then to $\operatorname{Tor}_{i-1}(M,L)$. In degree zero the terms are tensor products and the sequence ends in $M\otimes_RP\to0$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural long exact sequence with maps from $\operatorname{Tor}_i(M,L)$ through $\operatorname{Tor}_i(M,N)$ to $\operatorname{Tor}_i(M,P)$, then to $\operatorname{Tor}_{i-1}(M,L)$. In degree zero the terms are tensor products and the sequence ends in $M\otimes_RP\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Comparing homology through a resolving double complex
theorems.hypotheses: Take a first-quadrant homological double complex whose rows resolve their degree-zero cokernels and whose columns do likewise. The induced row and column cokernel complexes are denoted $R(A)$ and $U(A)$.
theorems.statement: There are natural isomorphisms $H_i(R(A))\simeq H_i(U(A))$, functorial for maps of such double complexes.
theorems.proof: There are natural isomorphisms $H_i(R(A))\simeq H_i(U(A))$, functorial for maps of such double complexes.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Symmetry of Tor over a commutative ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be commutative, $M,N$ modules and $i\ge0$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical bifunctorial isomorphism $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(N,M)$. Resolve both variables and compare the two directions.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical bifunctorial isomorphism $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(N,M)$. Resolve both variables and compare the two directions.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Finiteness of Tor modules
theorems.hypotheses: Take finite $M,N$ over a Noetherian ring $R$.
theorems.statement: For every $i\ge0$, $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)$ is finite. A resolution of $M$ can be taken degreewise finite free.
theorems.proof: For every $i\ge0$, $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)$ is finite. A resolution of $M$ can be taken degreewise finite free.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Tor tests for flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Take an arbitrary $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: Flatness is equivalent to vanishing of all higher $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(M,-)$, or only of $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(M,-)$. It is also equivalent to testing this first Tor on the quotients $R/I$ for all ideals, or only the finitely generated ideals.
theorems.proof: Flatness is equivalent to vanishing of all higher $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(M,-)$, or only of $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(M,-)$. It is also equivalent to testing this first Tor on the quotients $R/I$ for all ideals, or only the finitely generated ideals.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Flat base change of Tor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be flat over $R$ and $M,N$ any $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: For each $i\ge0$, the canonical map $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)\otimes_R A\to\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(M\otimes_R A,N\otimes_R A)$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: For each $i\ge0$, the canonical map $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)\otimes_R A\to\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(M\otimes_R A,N\otimes_R A)$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Tor commutes with filtered colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M=\operatorname{colim}_jM_j$ be a filtered colimit over $R$ and fix $N$.
theorems.statement: For each $i\ge0$ the natural map $\operatorname{colim}_j\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M_j,N)\to\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)$ is an isomorphism. Resolve $N$ and use exactness of filtered colimits.
theorems.proof: For each $i\ge0$ the natural map $\operatorname{colim}_j\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M_j,N)\to\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)$ is an isomorphism. Resolve $N$ and use exactness of filtered colimits.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Testing projectivity against finite modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $P$ finite over $R$.
theorems.statement: If $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(P,N)=0$ for each finite $N$, then $P$ is projective. Apply the hypothesis to the finite kernel of a surjection from a finite free module.
theorems.proof: If $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(P,N)=0$ for each finite $N$, then $P$ is projective. Apply the hypothesis to the finite kernel of a surjection from a finite free module.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Direct sums of projectives
theorems.hypotheses: Take any family $(P_i)$ of projective $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: Their direct sum is projective. A direct sum of splittings exhibits it as a summand of a free module.
theorems.proof: Their direct sum is projective. A direct sum of splittings exhibits it as a summand of a free module.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Lifting projectives across a nilpotent ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $I\subset R$ is nilpotent and $Q$ is projective over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: There exists a projective $R$-module $P$ with $P/IP\simeq Q$, with no finite generation requirement on $Q$.
theorems.proof: There exists a projective $R$-module $P$ with $P/IP\simeq Q$, with no finite generation requirement on $Q$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Lifting finite projectives across a nil ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let each element of $I\subset R$ be nilpotent, and let $Q$ be finite projective over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: There is a finite projective $R$-module $P$ whose reduction is $Q$. Lifting a finite idempotent matrix involves only finitely many elements of the nil ideal.
theorems.proof: There is a finite projective $R$-module $P$ whose reduction is $Q$. Lifting a finite idempotent matrix involves only finitely many elements of the nil ideal.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Flat module with projective nilpotent reduction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be nilpotent, $M$ be flat over $R$ and $M/IM$ projective over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is projective over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is projective over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Projectivity detected by two quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $I\cap J=0$ for ideals of $R$ and both $P/IP$ and $P/JP$ are projective over the respective quotient rings.
theorems.statement: Then $P$ is projective over $R$. No finite generation is required.
theorems.proof: Then $P$ is projective over $R$. No finite generation is required.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Local and global criteria for finite projectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be any module, with fibre dimension $\rho(\mathfrak p)=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}(M\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$.
theorems.statement: Finite projectivity is equivalent to finite presentation and flatness, or being a summand of a finite free module. It is equivalent to finite presentation and freeness of all prime stalks or of all maximal stalks, to finite local freeness, and to finite generation with free prime stalks and locally constant $\rho$.
theorems.proof: Finite projectivity is equivalent to finite presentation and flatness, or being a summand of a finite free module. It is equivalent to finite presentation and freeness of all prime stalks or of all maximal stalks, to finite local freeness, and to finite generation with free prime stalks and locally constant $\rho$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Fibre dimensions detect finite projectivity over reduced rings
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $R$ reduced and $M$ finite over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is finite projective exactly when $\mathfrak p\mapsto\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}(M\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ is locally constant.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is finite projective exactly when $\mathfrak p\mapsto\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}(M\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ is locally constant.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite projectivity tested by a flat local homomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take a flat local homomorphism $R\to S$ of local rings and a finite $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: Finite projectivity of $M$ over $R$ is equivalent to finite projectivity of $M\otimes_RS$ over $S$.
theorems.proof: Finite projectivity of $M$ over $R$ is equivalent to finite projectivity of $M\otimes_RS$ over $S$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Constant rank over a semilocal ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite locally free over semilocal $R$.
theorems.statement: A constant rank makes $M$ free. In particular this applies when $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is connected.
theorems.proof: A constant rank makes $M$ free. In particular this applies when $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is connected.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A basis inside a specified generating submodule
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is local with infinite residue field, $S$ is a semilocal $R$-algebra with $\mathfrak mS$ in its Jacobson radical, and $M$ is finite free over $S$.
theorems.statement: Every $R$-submodule $N\subseteq M$ generating $M$ over $S$ contains an $S$-basis of $M$.
theorems.proof: Every $R$-submodule $N\subseteq M$ generating $M$ over $S$ contains an $S$-basis of $M$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Evaluation for finite projective source
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite projective over $R$, and $N,L$ arbitrary modules.
