theorems.statement: The canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\otimes_R L\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N\otimes_R L)$ is an isomorphism. Reduce to finite free modules and direct summands.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\otimes_R L\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N\otimes_R L)$ is an isomorphism. Reduce to finite free modules and direct summands.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Surjectivity locus for a finite target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:M\to N$ be linear with $N$ finite.
theorems.statement: The stalk-surjective locus equals the fibre-surjective locus and is open. On every principal open contained in this locus the localized map is surjective, by vanishing of the localized cokernel.
theorems.proof: The stalk-surjective locus equals the fibre-surjective locus and is open. On every principal open contained in this locus the localized map is surjective, by vanishing of the localized cokernel.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Isomorphism locus for a finitely presented target
theorems.hypotheses: For $u:M\to N$ assume $M$ finite and $N$ finitely presented.
theorems.statement: The set of primes where $u_{\mathfrak p}$ is an isomorphism is open.
theorems.proof: The set of primes where $u_{\mathfrak p}$ is an isomorphism is open.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Freeness of a stalk spreads to a principal open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finitely presented and suppose $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is free.
theorems.statement: There exists $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $M_f$ is free over $R_f$.
theorems.proof: There exists $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $M_f$ is free over $R_f$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Fibre-rank loci for a map between finite projectives
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:P\to Q$ be a map of finite projective modules.
theorems.statement: The fibre-injective, fibre-surjective and fibre-isomorphism loci are open. On a principal open in the first locus the map is injective with finite projective cokernel. In the second it is surjective with finite projective kernel. In the third it is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The fibre-injective, fibre-surjective and fibre-isomorphism loci are open. On a principal open in the first locus the map is injective with finite projective cokernel. In the second it is surjective with finite projective kernel. In the third it is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Flatness by killing relations through finite free modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module and vary the maps $f:R^n\to M$ with $n$ finite.
theorems.statement: Flatness is equivalent to factoring each $f$ via a finite free module so the first map kills any prescribed $x\in\ker f$, or any finite subset of the kernel. Equivalently, if a given factorization already kills a submodule $N$, another can be found killing $N+Rx$ for each $x\in\ker f$.
theorems.proof: Flatness is equivalent to factoring each $f$ via a finite free module so the first map kills any prescribed $x\in\ker f$, or any finite subset of the kernel. Equivalently, if a given factorization already kills a submodule $N$, another can be found killing $N+Rx$ for each $x\in\ker f$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Factorization from finitely presented modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: It is flat exactly when every map $P\to M$ from a finitely presented module factors through a finite free module.
theorems.proof: It is flat exactly when every map $P\to M$ from a finitely presented module factors through a finite free module.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Lifting maps to a flat module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: It is flat exactly when for every finitely presented $P$ and surjection $N\to M$, each map $P\to M$ lifts to $P\to N$.
theorems.proof: It is flat exactly when for every finitely presented $P$ and surjection $N\to M$, each map $P\to M$ lifts to $P\to N$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Lazard’s theorem
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an arbitrary $R$-module.
theorems.statement: It is flat precisely when it is isomorphic to a directed colimit of finite free $R$-modules.
theorems.proof: It is flat precisely when it is isomorphic to a directed colimit of finite free $R$-modules.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite presentation plus flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an arbitrary $R$-module.
theorems.statement: It is finite projective exactly when it is flat and finitely presented. A finite presentation and the factorization criterion yield a splitting through a finite free module.
theorems.proof: It is finite projective exactly when it is flat and finitely presented. A finite presentation and the factorization criterion yield a splitting through a finite free module.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of finiteness, presentation and flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be faithfully flat and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: If $M\otimes_R S$ is finite, finitely presented or flat over $S$, the corresponding property holds for $M$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: If $M\otimes_R S$ is finite, finitely presented or flat over $S$, the corresponding property holds for $M$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of finite projectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Take a faithfully flat $R$-algebra $S$ and an arbitrary $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: If $M\otimes_RS$ is finite projective, then $M$ is finite projective. Descend finite presentation and flatness separately.
theorems.proof: If $M\otimes_RS$ is finite projective, then $M$ is finite projective. Descend finite presentation and flatness separately.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A countable test for projective-freeness of a ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take a ring $R$.
theorems.statement: Every projective $R$-module is free exactly when every countably generated projective $R$-module is free.
theorems.proof: Every projective $R$-module is free exactly when every countably generated projective $R$-module is free.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A free-summand criterion for countably generated modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be countably generated. In each decomposition $M=N\oplus P$ with $P$ finite free assume each element of $N$ lies in a free direct summand of $N$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is free. Use successive free summands to capture an enumeration of generators.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is free. Use successive free summands to capture an enumeration of generators.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Elements in free summands of local projectives
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be projective over local $R$.
theorems.statement: Every element of $P$ lies in a free direct summand. This assertion allows projectives of arbitrary cardinality.
theorems.proof: Every element of $P$ lies in a free direct summand. This assertion allows projectives of arbitrary cardinality.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Tensor products of Mittag-Leffler modules
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose both $M$ and $N$ are Mittag-Leffler over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $M\otimes_R N$ is Mittag-Leffler over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M\otimes_R N$ is Mittag-Leffler over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Mittag-Leffler test with finite free sources
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: It is Mittag-Leffler precisely when, for every $f:F\to M$ with $F$ finite free, there is $g:F\to Q$ with $Q$ finitely presented such that $\ker(f\otimes_R N)=\ker(g\otimes_R N)$ for every $R$-module $N$. The kernel equality is inside $F\otimes_RN$.
theorems.proof: It is Mittag-Leffler precisely when, for every $f:F\to M$ with $F$ finite free, there is $g:F\to Q$ with $Q$ finitely presented such that $\ker(f\otimes_R N)=\ker(g\otimes_R N)$ for every $R$-module $N$. The kernel equality is inside $F\otimes_RN$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Restriction of Mittag-Leffler modules along finite and finitely presented maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be both a finite $R$-module and a finitely presented $R$-algebra. Suppose the $S$-module $M$ is Mittag-Leffler over $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is Mittag-Leffler as an $R$-module.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is Mittag-Leffler as an $R$-module.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Mittag-Leffler modules over a finitely generated ideal quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal, $S=R/I$ and $M$ an $S$-module.
theorems.statement: The Mittag-Leffler property over $R$ is equivalent to the Mittag-Leffler property over $S$.
theorems.proof: The Mittag-Leffler property over $R$ is equivalent to the Mittag-Leffler property over $S$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Surjectivity of tensor with products detects finite generation
theorems.hypotheses: For each family $(Q_i)$ compare $M\otimes_R\prod_i Q_i$ with $\prod_i(M\otimes_R Q_i)$ by the natural map.
theorems.statement: Finite generation of $M$ is equivalent to surjectivity for all families, for all constant families, or for products of copies of $R$ indexed by arbitrary sets.
theorems.proof: Finite generation of $M$ is equivalent to surjectivity for all families, for all constant families, or for products of copies of $R$ indexed by arbitrary sets.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Bijection of tensor with products detects finite presentation
theorems.hypotheses: For each family $(Q_i)$ compare $M\otimes_R\prod_i Q_i$ with $\prod_i(M\otimes_R Q_i)$ by the natural map.
theorems.statement: Finite presentation of $M$ is equivalent to bijectivity for all families, for every constant family, or just for products of copies of $R$ indexed by arbitrary sets.
theorems.proof: Finite presentation of $M$ is equivalent to bijectivity for all families, for every constant family, or just for products of copies of $R$ indexed by arbitrary sets.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A finitely presented intermediate module killing a tensor relation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be finitely presented, $f:P\to M$, $Q$ any module and $x\in\ker(P\otimes_R Q\to M\otimes_R Q)$.
theorems.statement: There is a factorization $P\to P'\to M$ with $P'$ finitely presented and $x$ already zero in $P'\otimes_R Q$.
theorems.proof: There is a factorization $P\to P'\to M$ with $P'$ finitely presented and $x$ already zero in $P'\otimes_R Q$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Smallest coefficient submodule for a flat Mittag-Leffler module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be flat and Mittag-Leffler, $F$ any module, and $x\in F\otimes_R M$. Flatness identifies $F'\otimes_R M$ with its image for each $F'\subseteq F$.
theorems.statement: There is a smallest submodule $F'\subseteq F$ with $x\in F'\otimes_R M$, and this $F'$ is finitely generated.
theorems.proof: There is a smallest submodule $F'\subseteq F$ with $x\in F'\otimes_R M$, and this $F'$ is finitely generated.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Quotient by a finitely generated image preserves Mittag-Leffler
theorems.hypotheses: Take an exact sequence $M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ with $M_1$ finite and $M_2$ Mittag-Leffler.
theorems.statement: Then $M_3$ is Mittag-Leffler.
theorems.proof: Then $M_3$ is Mittag-Leffler.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Directed colimits with universally injective transition maps
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose each $M_i$ is Mittag-Leffler and every transition map in the directed system stays injective after tensor product with any module.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{colim}_iM_i$ is Mittag-Leffler.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{colim}_iM_i$ is Mittag-Leffler.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Restriction for a relatively flat Mittag-Leffler module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a Mittag-Leffler $R$-module under $R\to S$, and $M$ an $S$-module that is flat and Mittag-Leffler over $S$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is Mittag-Leffler over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is Mittag-Leffler over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Closure properties of coherent modules
theorems.hypotheses: Work with modules over any commutative ring.
theorems.statement: A finite submodule of a coherent module is coherent. A map from a finite module to a coherent one has finite kernel and coherent image and cokernel. For maps between coherent modules both kernel and cokernel are coherent. In a short exact sequence coherence of any two terms implies that of the third.
theorems.proof: A finite submodule of a coherent module is coherent. A map from a finite module to a coherent one has finite kernel and coherent image and cokernel. For maps between coherent modules both kernel and cokernel are coherent. In a short exact sequence coherence of any two terms implies that of the third.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Finite presentation over a coherent ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be coherent.
theorems.statement: An $R$-module is coherent precisely when it is finitely presented. Finite free modules are coherent, and coherent modules are closed under cokernels of maps between such modules.
theorems.proof: An $R$-module is coherent precisely when it is finitely presented. Finite free modules are coherent, and coherent modules are closed under cokernels of maps between such modules.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Dimension computes both Grothendieck groups of a field
theorems.hypotheses: Take a field $k$.
theorems.statement: Both $K_0(k)$ and $K'_0(k)$ are canonically $\mathbf Z$ by vector-space dimension.
theorems.proof: Both $K_0(k)$ and $K'_0(k)$ are canonically $\mathbf Z$ by vector-space dimension.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Grothendieck groups of a principal ideal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Take a principal ideal domain $R$.
theorems.statement: Rank identifies both $K_0(R)$ and $K'_0(R)$ with $\mathbf Z$. The cyclic torsion summands of a finite module contribute zero in $K'_0(R)$ by a length-one free resolution.
theorems.proof: Rank identifies both $K_0(R)$ and $K'_0(R)$ with $\mathbf Z$. The cyclic torsion summands of a finite module contribute zero in $K'_0(R)$ by a length-one free resolution.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Grothendieck groups of a one-variable polynomial ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take a field $k$.
theorems.statement: Both Grothendieck groups of $k[x]$ identify with $\mathbf Z$ by rank since $k[x]$ is a PID.
theorems.proof: Both Grothendieck groups of $k[x]$ identify with $\mathbf Z$ by rank since $k[x]$ is a PID.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Different Grothendieck groups for an affine node
theorems.hypotheses: Write $R=\{f\in k[x]: f(0)=f(1)\}$ over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: For this nodal algebra $K_0(R)\simeq k^\times\oplus\mathbf Z$ and $K'_0(R)\simeq\mathbf Z$.
theorems.proof: For this nodal algebra $K_0(R)\simeq k^\times\oplus\mathbf Z$ and $K'_0(R)\simeq\mathbf Z$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Proj of a polynomial ring in one variable
theorems.hypotheses: Give $R[X]$ the grading $\deg X=1$.
theorems.statement: The unique standard chart $D_+(X)$ covers its Proj, which is canonically homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.proof: The unique standard chart $D_+(X)$ covers its Proj, which is canonically homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Hilbert function of a graded polynomial module
theorems.hypotheses: For a field $k$, take a finite graded module over $k[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$ with its standard grading.
theorems.statement: The dimensions of its homogeneous pieces agree eventually with a numerical polynomial. Here dimension identifies $K'_0(k)$ with $\mathbf Z$.
theorems.proof: The dimensions of its homogeneous pieces agree eventually with a numerical polynomial. Here dimension identifies $K'_0(k)$ with $\mathbf Z$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Rees algebra of the polynomial origin
theorems.hypotheses: For any ring $R$, put $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$.
theorems.statement: The Rees algebra of $I$ in $P$ is $P[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(t_iT_j-t_jT_i)_{i,j}$, with $T_i$ mapping to $t_i$ in degree one.
theorems.proof: The Rees algebra of $I$ in $P$ is $P[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(t_iT_j-t_jT_i)_{i,j}$, with $T_i$ mapping to $t_i$ in degree one.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: An affine chart of the blowup of the polynomial origin
theorems.hypotheses: In $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ take $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ with $n\ge1$.
theorems.statement: The chart $P[I/t_1]$ is $P[x_2,\ldots,x_n]/(t_1x_i-t_i)_{2\le i\le n}$, sending $x_i$ to $t_i/t_1$.
theorems.proof: The chart $P[I/t_1]$ is $P[x_2,\ldots,x_n]/(t_1x_i-t_i)_{2\le i\le n}$, sending $x_i$ to $t_i/t_1$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Adic formal smoothness of formal power series algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Take finitely many formal variables. The coefficient ring is a characteristic-zero field $K$, a field $L$ of characteristic $p>0$, or a Cohen ring $\Lambda$.
theorems.statement: The power series algebra is adically formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$, $\mathbf F_p$, or $\mathbf Z$, respectively, using its maximal ideal.
theorems.proof: The power series algebra is adically formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$, $\mathbf F_p$, or $\mathbf Z$, respectively, using its maximal ideal.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Changing formal coordinates and quotienting by parameters
theorems.hypotheses: Let $D$ be a field or a Cohen ring and $T=D[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$. A list $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ extends to a regular parameter system, together with the initial uniformizer $p$ in the Cohen-ring case.
theorems.statement: One has $r\le n$ and $T/(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ is a power series algebra over $D$ in $n-r$ variables. For $r=n$ the substitution map $D[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]\to T$ itself is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: One has $r\le n$ and $T/(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ is a power series algebra over $D$ in $n-r$ variables. For $r=n$ the substitution map $D[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]\to T$ itself is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Compatible regular presentations of a local map of complete rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be local between complete Noetherian local rings.
theorems.statement: There is a commutative square with surjections $P\to A$, $Q\to B$ and $P\to Q$ carrying a regular parameter system into one. Both presenting rings are formal power series rings over fields in residue characteristic zero and over Cohen rings in positive residue characteristic. The presenting map is flat with regular closed fibre.
theorems.proof: There is a commutative square with surjections $P\to A$, $Q\to B$ and $P\to Q$ carrying a regular parameter system into one. Both presenting rings are formal power series rings over fields in residue characteristic zero and over Cohen rings in positive residue characteristic. The presenting map is flat with regular closed fibre.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: A pullback of complete local surjections
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $S\to R$ and $T\to R$ are surjections of complete Noetherian local rings.
theorems.statement: The pullback $S\times_R T$ is a complete Noetherian local ring.
theorems.proof: The pullback $S\times_R T$ is a complete Noetherian local ring.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Equicharacteristic criteria for adic formal smoothness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ be a Noetherian local algebra over a field $k$.
theorems.statement: In characteristic zero adic formal smoothness of $k\to A$ is equivalent to regularity of $A$. In characteristic $p>0$ it is equivalent to geometric regularity, or regularity of all $A\otimes_k k'$ for finite $k'/k$ inside $k^{1/p}$. Two further equivalent tests are regularity plus injectivity of $H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, and regularity plus injectivity of $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_k K\to\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_A K$.
theorems.proof: In characteristic zero adic formal smoothness of $k\to A$ is equivalent to regularity of $A$. In characteristic $p>0$ it is equivalent to geometric regularity, or regularity of all $A\otimes_k k'$ for finite $k'/k$ inside $k^{1/p}$. Two further equivalent tests are regularity plus injectivity of $H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, and regularity plus injectivity of $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_k K\to\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_A K$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Jacobi–Zariski sequence at an adically formally smooth local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)\to(B,\mathfrak n,K)$ be a local map of Noetherian local rings. Write $F=B/\mathfrak mB$ for its closed fibre. Assume maximal-ideal-adic formal smoothness.
theorems.statement: One has $0\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{K/A})\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B K\to\Omega_{K/A}\to0$.
theorems.proof: One has $0\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{K/A})\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\to\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B K\to\Omega_{K/A}\to0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting an adically formally smooth closed fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be complete Noetherian local and let $B$ be a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra formally smooth for its maximal-ideal-adic topology.
theorems.statement: There exists an adically formally smooth local map $A\to C$ with $C$ complete Noetherian local and $C\otimes_A k\cong B$.
theorems.proof: There exists an adically formally smooth local map $A\to C$ with $C$ complete Noetherian local and $C\otimes_A k\cong B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Compatibility of a smooth closed-fibre lift with a second base
theorems.hypotheses: Take local maps $A\to A'\to B$ of complete Noetherian local rings, with the first inducing an isomorphism on residue fields $k$ and $B\otimes_{A'} k$ adically formally smooth over $k$.
theorems.statement: There is a compatible adically formally smooth local $A\to C$ lifting the same fibre and mapping to $B$. The $\mathfrak m_{A'}$-adic completed tensor $C\widehat\otimes_A A'$ is flat over $A'$ and surjects onto $B$, isomorphically if $B$ is $A'$-flat. Surjectivity or finiteness of $A\to A'$ implies the corresponding property of $C\to B$.
theorems.proof: There is a compatible adically formally smooth local $A\to C$ lifting the same fibre and mapping to $B$. The $\mathfrak m_{A'}$-adic completed tensor $C\widehat\otimes_A A'$ is flat over $A'$ and surjects onto $B$, isomorphically if $B$ is $A'$-flat. Surjectivity or finiteness of $A\to A'$ implies the corresponding property of $C\to B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Testing regular ring maps at target primes or maximal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to B$ have Noetherian target. For $\mathfrak q\subset B$ denote its contraction by $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Regularity is equivalent to regularity of each $R_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$. It suffices to test maximal ideals of $B$, keeping their actual contractions in $R$.
theorems.proof: Regularity is equivalent to regularity of each $R_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$. It suffices to test maximal ideals of $B$, keeping their actual contractions in $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type base change of a regular homomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to B$ be regular and $R\to S$ of finite type.
theorems.statement: The map $S\to B\otimes_R S$ is regular.
theorems.proof: The map $S\to B\otimes_R S$ is regular.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of regular maps with Noetherian composite fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be regular and suppose every fibre of $A\to C$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: Then $A\to C$ is regular.
theorems.proof: Then $A\to C$ is regular.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Regularity for a directed colimit of smooth algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B$ be a directed colimit of smooth $R$-algebras, with $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ Noetherian at every base prime.
theorems.statement: Then $R\to B$ is regular.
theorems.proof: Then $R\to B$ is regular.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Regular homomorphisms between fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be any field extension.
theorems.statement: The ring map $k\to K$ is regular precisely when $K/k$ is separable in the general field-extension sense.
theorems.proof: The ring map $k\to K$ is regular precisely when $K/k$ is separable in the general field-extension sense.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Descent of regularity through the target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be ring maps, with $A\to C$ regular and $B\to C$ faithfully flat.
theorems.statement: Then $A\to B$ is regular.
theorems.proof: Then $A\to B$ is regular.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Krull dimension under local completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: One has $\dim A=\dim\widehat A$.
theorems.proof: One has $\dim A=\dim\widehat A$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Depth under local completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{depth}A=\operatorname{depth}\widehat A$.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{depth}A=\operatorname{depth}\widehat A$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulayness under local completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $\widehat A$ is Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $\widehat A$ is Cohen–Macaulay.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Regularity under local completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is regular if and only if $\widehat A$ is regular.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is regular if and only if $\widehat A$ is regular.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Discrete valuation under local completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is a DVR if and only if $\widehat A$ is a DVR.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is a DVR if and only if $\widehat A$ is a DVR.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Reducedness under local completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: Reducedness descends from $\widehat A$ to $A$. The converse holds when $A$ is Nagata and fails for some reduced Noetherian local rings.
theorems.proof: Reducedness descends from $\widehat A$ to $A$. The converse holds when $A$ is Nagata and fails for some reduced Noetherian local rings.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Normality under local completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: Normality of $\widehat A$ implies normality of $A$.
theorems.proof: Normality of $\widehat A$ implies normality of $A$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Flatness detected on local completions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)\to(B,\mathfrak n,K)$ be a local map of Noetherian local rings. Write $F=B/\mathfrak mB$ for its closed fibre.
theorems.statement: The induced map $\widehat A\to\widehat B$ is flat if and only if $A\to B$ is flat.
theorems.proof: The induced map $\widehat A\to\widehat B$ is flat if and only if $A\to B$ is flat.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: An isomorphism of completions from a flat local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)\to(B,\mathfrak n,K)$ be a local map of Noetherian local rings. Write $F=B/\mathfrak mB$ for its closed fibre. Suppose $A\to B$ is flat, $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak n$, and $k\to K$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: Then $\widehat A\to\widehat B$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Then $\widehat A\to\widehat B$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Noetherianness at an étale point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be étale, let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be prime, and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$.
theorems.statement: The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian exactly when $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is.
theorems.proof: The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian exactly when $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Dimension at an étale point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be étale, let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be prime, and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$.
theorems.statement: The two local rings $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B_{\mathfrak q}$ have equal Krull dimension.
theorems.proof: The two local rings $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B_{\mathfrak q}$ have equal Krull dimension.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Regularity at an étale point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be étale, let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be prime, and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$.
theorems.statement: The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular exactly when $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is.
theorems.proof: The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular exactly when $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Étale algebras over a Dedekind domain
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $A\to B$ is étale and $A$ is a Dedekind domain, allowing fields.
theorems.statement: The algebra $B$ is a finite product of Dedekind domains. Its localizations at maximal ideals are fields in dimension zero and DVRs in dimension one. For a DVR $A$ with uniformizer $\pi$, the étale algebra $A[1/\pi]$ exhibits the field case.
theorems.proof: The algebra $B$ is a finite product of Dedekind domains. Its localizations at maximal ideals are fields in dimension zero and DVRs in dimension one. For a DVR $A$ with uniformizer $\pi$, the étale algebra $A[1/\pi]$ exhibits the field case.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Flatness, maximal ideals and infinitesimal neighbourhoods of henselizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field.
theorems.statement: Both legs of $R\to R^h\to R^{sh}$ are faithfully flat and extend the maximal ideals. Modulo each $\mathfrak m^n$, ordinary henselization induces an isomorphism. The strict henselization quotients have a free basis over $R/\mathfrak m^n$ lifted from one fixed family of elements of $R^{sh}$.
theorems.proof: Both legs of $R\to R^h\to R^{sh}$ are faithfully flat and extend the maximal ideals. Modulo each $\mathfrak m^n$, ordinary henselization induces an isomorphism. The strict henselization quotients have a free basis over $R/\mathfrak m^n$ lifted from one fixed family of elements of $R^{sh}$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Formal étaleness and adic formal smoothness of henselizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field.
theorems.statement: The maps $R\to R^h$, $R^h\to R^{sh}$ and $R\to R^{sh}$ are formally étale and each is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology of its target.
theorems.proof: The maps $R\to R^h$, $R^h\to R^{sh}$ and $R\to R^{sh}$ are formally étale and each is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology of its target.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Noetherianness of henselizations and their completions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field.
theorems.statement: Noetherianness of any of $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ implies it for all three. Their completions are Noetherian local and the completion maps are flat. One has $\widehat R\cong\widehat{R^h}$ and $\widehat R\to\widehat{R^{sh}}$ is adically formally smooth. Also $(\widehat R)^{sh}\cong\widehat R\otimes_{R^h}R^{sh}$ and its completion is $\widehat{R^{sh}}$.
theorems.proof: Noetherianness of any of $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ implies it for all three. Their completions are Noetherian local and the completion maps are flat. One has $\widehat R\cong\widehat{R^h}$ and $\widehat R\to\widehat{R^{sh}}$ is adically formally smooth. Also $(\widehat R)^{sh}\cong\widehat R\otimes_{R^h}R^{sh}$ and its completion is $\widehat{R^{sh}}$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Reducedness detected by either henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field.
theorems.statement: Reducedness of any one of $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ is equivalent to reducedness of the other two.
theorems.proof: Reducedness of any one of $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ is equivalent to reducedness of the other two.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Nilradicals under henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field.
theorems.statement: The nilradical of either henselization is the extension of the nilradical of $R$.
theorems.proof: The nilradical of either henselization is the extension of the nilradical of $R$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Normal domains and henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field.
theorems.statement: The rings $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ are simultaneously normal domains whenever one of them is.
theorems.proof: The rings $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ are simultaneously normal domains whenever one of them is.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Krull dimension of the two henselizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field.
theorems.statement: One has $\dim R=\dim R^h=\dim R^{sh}$.
theorems.proof: One has $\dim R=\dim R^h=\dim R^{sh}$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Depth and henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field. Suppose $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: All three rings have the same depth.
theorems.proof: All three rings have the same depth.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulayness and henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field. Suppose $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The three Cohen–Macaulay conditions on $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ are equivalent.
theorems.proof: The three Cohen–Macaulay conditions on $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ are equivalent.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Regularity and henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field. Suppose $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: Regularity of any one of the three local rings is equivalent to regularity of all three.
theorems.proof: Regularity of any one of the three local rings is equivalent to regularity of all three.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Discrete valuation and henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field. Suppose $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The three DVR conditions on $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ are equivalent.
theorems.proof: The three DVR conditions on $R,R^h,R^{sh}$ are equivalent.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Noetherian ind-étale fibres are products of separable algebraic fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B$ be a filtered colimit of étale $A$-algebras and suppose $B$ is Noetherian. Fix $\mathfrak p\subset A$.
theorems.statement: There are finitely many primes $\mathfrak q$ above $\mathfrak p$, and $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the product of their residue fields. Each is separable algebraic over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.
theorems.proof: There are finitely many primes $\mathfrak q$ above $\mathfrak p$, and $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the product of their residue fields. Each is separable algebraic over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Fibres of a Noetherian local henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field. Suppose $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: Above each base prime the fibre of either henselization is a finite product of the residue fields of the primes above it, each separable algebraic over the base residue field.
theorems.proof: Above each base prime the fibre of either henselization is a finite product of the residue fields of the primes above it, each separable algebraic over the base residue field.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Detecting a rational vector over an intersection of fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be the intersection of a nonempty downward directed family of intermediate subfields $K_i\subseteq K$. Let $V\subseteq K^n$ be a $K$-subspace with $n\geq1$.
theorems.statement: The intersection $V\cap k^n$ is nonzero exactly when every $V\cap K_i^n$ is nonzero.
theorems.proof: The intersection $V\cap k^n$ is nonzero exactly when every $V\cap K_i^n$ is nonzero.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Intersections down to the p-th powers
theorems.hypotheses: In characteristic $p>0$, let the subfields $K_i$ of $K$ form a downward directed family with intersection $K^p$.
theorems.statement: The maps $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K/K_i}$ have zero common kernel. For every finite $L/K$ one has $L^p=\bigcap_i L^pK_i$.
theorems.proof: The maps $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K/K_i}$ have zero common kernel. For every finite $L/K$ one has $L^p=\bigcap_i L^pK_i$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Finite subalgebras associated to a p-basis of coefficients
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A=k[[u_1,\ldots,u_n]][v_1,\ldots,v_m]$ over a field of characteristic $p$. For a finite subset $J$ of a fixed $p$-basis, generate $k_J$ over $k^p$ by the complementary basis elements. Set $A_J=k_J[[u_1^p,\ldots,u_n^p]][v_1^p,\ldots,v_m^p]$.
theorems.statement: Each $A_J\subseteq A$ is finite. Their fraction fields form a downward directed family with intersection $\operatorname{Frac}(A)^p$.
theorems.proof: Each $A_J\subseteq A$ is finite. Their fraction fields form a downward directed family with intersection $\operatorname{Frac}(A)^p$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Open regular locus via closed irreducible subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for Noetherian $R$.
theorems.statement: The ring is J-1 exactly when for each regular point $\mathfrak p$ its closure has a nonempty relatively open subset of regular points of $X$.
theorems.proof: The ring is J-1 exactly when for each regular point $\mathfrak p$ its closure has a nonempty relatively open subset of regular points of $X$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: J-0 for prime quotients implies J-1
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian with $R/\mathfrak p$ J-0 at every prime $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Then $R$ is J-1.
theorems.proof: Then $R$ is J-1.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Dominant finite type descent of J-0
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\hookrightarrow S$ be of finite type between domains with $R$ Noetherian and $S$ J-0.
theorems.statement: Then $R$ is J-0.
theorems.proof: Then $R$ is J-0.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Separable finite type ascent of J-0
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\hookrightarrow S$ be finite type between domains with separable fraction field extension. Suppose $R$ is Noetherian and J-0.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is J-0.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is J-0.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Characterizations of J-2
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian.
theorems.statement: J-2 is equivalent to J-0 for all finite type domain algebras, and to J-1 for all finite algebras. It is also equivalent to existence, for every prime $\mathfrak p$ and finite purely inseparable $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, of a finite domain algebra over $R/\mathfrak p$ with fraction field $L$ and J-0.
theorems.proof: J-2 is equivalent to J-0 for all finite type domain algebras, and to J-1 for all finite algebras. It is also equivalent to existence, for every prime $\mathfrak p$ and finite purely inseparable $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, of a finite domain algebra over $R/\mathfrak p$ with fraction field $L$ and J-0.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Extension of derivations to completions, localizations and birational algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $D:R\to R$ be a derivation.
theorems.statement: It extends canonically to each adic completion and uniquely to each localization. For a finite type inclusion $R\subseteq S$ with $R_g=S_g$ and $g$ a nonzerodivisor in $S$, some $g^ND$ extends to $S$.
theorems.proof: It extends canonically to each adic completion and uniquely to each localization. For a finite type inclusion $R\subseteq S$ with $R_g=S_g$ and $g$ a nonzerodivisor in $S$, some $g^ND$ extends to $S$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Derivation criterion for a regular hypersurface
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be regular, $f\in R$, and suppose a derivation $D:R\to R$ has $D(f)$ invertible modulo $f$.
theorems.statement: Then $R/(f)$ is regular.
theorems.proof: Then $R/(f)$ is regular.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Invertible Jacobian matrix in a regular local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take $r\geq1$ elements $f_j$ in the maximal ideal of a regular local ring and derivations $D_i$ with $\det(D_i f_j)$ a unit.
theorems.statement: The quotient by these elements is regular and the tuple is a regular sequence.
theorems.proof: The quotient by these elements is regular and the tuple is a regular sequence.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Regularity of polynomial covers detected by a derivation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be regular and assume that $D(f)$ is a unit of $R$ for some derivation $D$.
theorems.statement: For each polynomial $P\in\mathbf Z[z]$ the ring $R[z]/(P(z)-f)$ is regular, including the case $P=z^n$ with $n\geq1$.
theorems.proof: For each polynomial $P\in\mathbf Z[z]$ the ring $R[z]/(P(z)-f)$ is regular, including the case $P=z^n$ with $n\geq1$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Detecting a non-p-th power by a derivation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B$ be a domain of characteristic $p>0$, of finite type over a complete Noetherian local ring. Suppose $f\in B$ is not a $p$-th power in its fraction field.
theorems.statement: There is a derivation $D:B\to B$ with $D(f)\ne0$.
theorems.proof: There is a derivation $D:B\to B$ with $D(f)\ne0$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: An open regular piece of a complete local domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a complete Noetherian local domain.
theorems.statement: The domain is J-0.
theorems.proof: The domain is J-0.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Standard classes of J-2 rings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a field, a complete Noetherian local ring, $\mathbf Z$, a one-dimensional Noetherian local or Nagata ring, or a Dedekind domain whose fraction field has characteristic zero.
theorems.statement: Each ring listed is J-2, as is every finite type algebra over it.
theorems.proof: Each ring listed is J-2, as is every finite type algebra over it.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting a derivation into a complete formally smooth target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)\to(B,\mathfrak n,K)$ be a local map of Noetherian local rings. Write $F=B/\mathfrak mB$ for its closed fibre. Suppose $B$ is complete and $A\to B$ adically formally smooth.
theorems.statement: Every derivation $A\to A$ extends to a derivation $B\to B$.
theorems.proof: Every derivation $A\to A$ extends to a derivation $B\to B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Four regularity tests for a map of complete local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)\to(B,\mathfrak n,K)$ be a local map of Noetherian local rings. Write $F=B/\mathfrak mB$ for its closed fibre. Assume both rings complete.
theorems.statement: Regularity of the map is equivalent to each of the three closed-fibre or formal lifting tests. The following are equivalent. The map is flat and $F$ geometrically regular over $k$. The map is flat and $k\to F$ formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology on $F$. The map $A\to B$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.
theorems.proof: Regularity of the map is equivalent to each of the three closed-fibre or formal lifting tests. The following are equivalent. The map is flat and $F$ geometrically regular over $k$. The map is flat and $k\to F$ formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology on $F$. The map $A\to B$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Testing the G-ring condition on pairs of primes
theorems.hypotheses: Take Noetherian $R$. For primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $R$, put $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)=\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.
theorems.statement: The G-ring condition is equivalent to geometric regularity over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ of each $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)$, equivalently of $\widehat{(R/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_{R/\mathfrak q}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.
theorems.proof: The G-ring condition is equivalent to geometric regularity over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ of each $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)$, equivalently of $\widehat{(R/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_{R/\mathfrak q}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Quasi-finite ascent for individual regular formal fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type between Noetherian rings, and $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak p'$ primes of $S$ with contractions $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p$. Suppose the map is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak p'$. For primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $R$, put $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)=\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Use the same construction for $S$.
theorems.statement: Geometric regularity of $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)$ gives geometric regularity of $F_S(\mathfrak p',\mathfrak q')$ over its own residue field. This gives ascent for all formal fibres of the two stated local rings and, for a quasi-finite map, ascent of the G-ring property.
theorems.proof: Geometric regularity of $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)$ gives geometric regularity of $F_S(\mathfrak p',\mathfrak q')$ over its own residue field. This gives ascent for all formal fibres of the two stated local rings and, for a quasi-finite map, ascent of the G-ring property.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Testing G-rings by finite free extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian.
theorems.statement: It is a G-ring exactly when all formal fibres at all prime localizations of every finite free $R$-algebra are regular rings.
theorems.proof: It is a G-ring exactly when all formal fibres at all prime localizations of every finite free $R$-algebra are regular rings.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Generic formal fibres of mixed polynomial and power series algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ with $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$.
theorems.statement: For each $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, the algebra $\widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_A K$ is geometrically regular over $K$.
theorems.proof: For each $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, the algebra $\widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_A K$ is geometrically regular over $K$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Complete Noetherian local rings are G-rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: If $A$ is complete, then it is a G-ring.
theorems.proof: If $A$ is complete, then it is a G-ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: G-rings detected at maximal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Take Noetherian $R$.
theorems.statement: It is a G-ring if and only if $R_{\mathfrak m}$ has geometrically regular formal fibres for each maximal $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.proof: It is a G-ring if and only if $R_{\mathfrak m}$ has geometrically regular formal fibres for each maximal $\mathfrak m$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: The two henselizations of a local G-ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local. Fix an ordinary henselization $R^h$ and a strict henselization $R^{sh}$ using a separable closure of its residue field. Suppose $R$ is Noetherian. Assume $R$ a G-ring.
theorems.statement: The rings $R^h$ and $R^{sh}$ are G-rings.
theorems.proof: The rings $R^h$ and $R^{sh}$ are G-rings.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A formal fibre of a polynomial over a complete local domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a complete Noetherian local domain of fraction characteristic $p>0$. In $A[x]$ choose a maximal $\mathfrak q$ above the closed point and $0\ne\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$ prime above $(0)$.
theorems.statement: The fibre $\widehat{A[x]_{\mathfrak q}}\otimes_{A[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$.
theorems.proof: The fibre $\widehat{A[x]_{\mathfrak q}}\otimes_{A[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Essentially finite type algebras over a G-ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a G-ring and $S$ an essentially finite type $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Then $S$ is a G-ring.
theorems.proof: Then $S$ is a G-ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Failure of the G-ring condition after general adic completion
theorems.hypotheses: Consider completion of a G-ring at an arbitrary ideal, as distinguished from completion of a local ring at its maximal ideal.
theorems.statement: Nishimura’s example gives a G-ring with an ideal whose adic completion fails the G-ring condition. The source cites the example and Dumitrescu’s extension.
theorems.proof: Nishimura’s example gives a G-ring with an ideal whose adic completion fails the G-ring condition. The source cites the example and Dumitrescu’s extension.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Basic families of G-rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a field, a complete Noetherian local ring, $\mathbf Z$, or a Dedekind domain of fraction characteristic zero.
theorems.statement: Both $R$ and every finite type $R$-algebra are G-rings.
theorems.proof: Both $R$ and every finite type $R$-algebra are G-rings.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Henselian local rings as colimits of henselian local G-rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a henselian local ring.
theorems.statement: There is a filtered system of henselian local G-rings with local transition maps and colimit $A$.
theorems.proof: There is a filtered system of henselian local G-rings with local transition maps and colimit $A$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Regularity of adic completion maps for G-rings
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $A$ is a G-ring and $I\subseteq A$ any ideal.
theorems.statement: Then $A\to\widehat A_I$ is regular.
theorems.proof: Then $A\to\widehat A_I$ is regular.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Henselization of an arbitrary pair over a G-ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a G-ring and $(A^h,I^h)$ the henselization along an ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: Then $A^h$ is a G-ring.
theorems.proof: Then $A^h$ is a G-ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Prime-pair criterion for a P-ring
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a fibre property $P$ of Noetherian algebras over fields and a Noetherian $R$. For primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $R$, put $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)=\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.
theorems.statement: The ring is a $P$-ring precisely if all $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\widehat{(R/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_{R/\mathfrak q}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ have $P$.
theorems.proof: The ring is a $P$-ring precisely if all $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\widehat{(R/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_{R/\mathfrak q}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ have $P$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Local testing of fibre properties
theorems.hypotheses: Assume the indicated axioms for the property P of Noetherian algebras over fields. (B) $P(k\to T)$ holds exactly when $P(k\to T_{\mathfrak p})$ holds for every prime of $T$.
theorems.statement: For any map of Noetherian rings, having $P$ on all fibres can be tested on the induced maps of local rings at every target prime and its contraction, or at every target maximal ideal and its contraction.
theorems.proof: For any map of Noetherian rings, having $P$ on all fibres can be tested on the induced maps of local rings at every target prime and its contraction, or at every target maximal ideal and its contraction.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Quasi-finite ascent for a specified fibre property
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type between Noetherian rings, and $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak p'$ primes of $S$ with contractions $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p$. Suppose the map is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak p'$. For primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $R$, put $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)=\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Use the same construction for $S$. Assume the indicated axioms for the property P of Noetherian algebras over fields. (A) $P$ ascends under every finitely generated field extension of the base. (B) $P(k\to T)$ holds exactly when $P(k\to T_{\mathfrak p})$ holds for every prime of $T$.
theorems.statement: If $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)$ has $P$, then $F_S(\mathfrak p',\mathfrak q')$ has $P$. The implication applies to all formal fibres of the local rings, and a quasi-finite $S$ over a $P$-ring $R$ is a $P$-ring.
theorems.proof: If $F_R(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)$ has $P$, then $F_S(\mathfrak p',\mathfrak q')$ has $P$. The implication applies to all formal fibres of the local rings, and a quasi-finite $S$ over a $P$-ring $R$ is a $P$-ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Maximal-ideal test for P-rings
theorems.hypotheses: Assume the indicated axioms for the property P of Noetherian algebras over fields. (C) For flat maps $A\to B\to C$ of Noetherian rings, $P$ on the first map’s fibres and regularity of the second imply $P$ on the composite fibres. theorems.statement: A Noetherian ring $R$ is a $P$-ring exactly when $P$ holds for every formal fibre of each $R_{\mathfrak m}$ at maximal ideals.
theorems.proof: A Noetherian ring $R$ is a $P$-ring exactly when $P$ holds for every formal fibre of each $R_{\mathfrak m}$ at maximal ideals.

theorems.subject: ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Essentially finite type permanence of excellence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a localization of a finite type algebra over $R$.
theorems.statement: If $R$ is quasi-excellent then so is $S$. If $R$ is excellent then so is $S$.
theorems.proof: If $R$ is quasi-excellent then so is $S$. If $R$ is excellent then so is $S$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Standard classes of excellent rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a field, a complete Noetherian local ring, $\mathbf Z$, or a Dedekind domain of fraction characteristic zero.
theorems.statement: The ring $R$ and all its finite type algebras are excellent.
theorems.proof: The ring $R$ and all its finite type algebras are excellent.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Nagata local rings via geometrically reduced formal fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is Nagata if and only if all its formal fibres are geometrically reduced over the corresponding residue fields.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is Nagata if and only if all its formal fibres are geometrically reduced over the corresponding residue fields.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Normal completion with normal formal fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local and let $\widehat A$ denote its maximal-ideal-adic completion. Assume $A$ normal and all formal fibres normal. The fibre hypothesis holds for a quasi-excellent ring.
theorems.statement: The completed ring is normal.
theorems.proof: The completed ring is normal.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Yoneda extensions of modules and the first derived Ext
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N$ be $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: The group of Yoneda extension classes in the abelian module category identifies naturally with $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(M,N)$, compatibly with the connecting maps in both arguments.
theorems.proof: The group of Yoneda extension classes in the abelian module category identifies naturally with $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(M,N)$, compatibly with the connecting maps in both arguments.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Exactness of the character dual
theorems.hypotheses: Take $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$ with its natural $R$-action.
theorems.statement: The character dual functor carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences with arrows reversed, since $\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$ is injective as an abelian group.
theorems.proof: The character dual functor carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences with arrows reversed, since $\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$ is injective as an abelian group.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Character bidual evaluation is a monomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be any $R$-module and use the character dual.
theorems.statement: Evaluation $M\to M^{\vee\vee}$ is injective because characters separate elements.
theorems.proof: Evaluation $M\to M^{\vee\vee}$ is injective because characters separate elements.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A canonical injective module built from characters
theorems.hypotheses: For an $R$-module $M$ let $F(N)$ denote the free $R$-module on the underlying set of $N$. Put $J(M)=F(M^\vee)^\vee$ for the character dual.
theorems.statement: The module $J(M)$ is injective. It identifies with a product of copies of $R^\vee$.
theorems.proof: The module $J(M)$ is injective. It identifies with a product of copies of $R^\vee$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Functorial embedding in an injective module
theorems.hypotheses: Use $J(M)=F(M^\vee)^\vee$, where $F$ is free on the underlying set and $\vee$ denotes the character dual.
theorems.statement: Evaluation followed by the dual of the free surjection gives a natural injection $M\hookrightarrow J(M)$ into an injective module, defining a functor to the arrow category.
theorems.proof: Evaluation followed by the dual of the free surjection gives a natural injection $M\hookrightarrow J(M)$ into an injective module, defining a functor to the arrow category.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Flat restriction of scalars preserves K-injectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to S$ is flat and $I$ K-injective over $S$.
theorems.statement: Restriction makes $I$ K-injective over $R$.
theorems.proof: Restriction makes $I$ K-injective over $R$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: K-injectivity along ring epimorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be an epimorphism of rings and $I$ a complex of $S$-modules whose restriction is K-injective over $R$.
theorems.statement: Then $I$ is K-injective over $S$.
theorems.proof: Then $I$ is K-injective over $S$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Coinduction preserves K-injectivity
theorems.hypotheses: For $A\to B$ suppose $I$ is a K-injective complex of $A$-modules.
theorems.statement: The coinduced complex $\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,I)$ is K-injective over $B$.
theorems.proof: The coinduced complex $\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,I)$ is K-injective over $B$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Derived tensor with a module on bounded-above complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: The functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} M$ takes $D^-(R)$ to $D^-(R)$ and computes Tor in negative cohomological degrees for module inputs.
theorems.proof: The functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} M$ takes $D^-(R)$ to $D^-(R)$ and computes Tor in negative cohomological degrees for module inputs.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Derived tensor with an algebra on bounded-above complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a ring map $R\to A$.
theorems.statement: The functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} A$ takes $D^-(R)$ to $D^-(A)$ with the target algebra action.
theorems.proof: The functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} A$ takes $D^-(R)$ to $D^-(A)$ with the target algebra action.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Signed symmetric monoidal structure on complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Use cochain complexes over a commutative ring $R$ with the direct-sum total tensor product.
theorems.statement: The unit is $R[0]$, associativity is the total tensor rebracketing and the symmetry on bidegree $(p,q)$ is the flip multiplied by $(-1)^{pq}$. These make the category symmetric monoidal.
theorems.proof: The unit is $R[0]$, associativity is the total tensor rebracketing and the symmetry on bidegree $(p,q)$ is the flip multiplied by $(-1)^{pq}$. These make the category symmetric monoidal.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensoring a chain homotopy
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f,g:L\to M$ be homotopic chain maps and take any complex $P$.
theorems.statement: The induced maps on total tensor products with $P$ are homotopic. Thus total tensoring descends to the homotopy category.
theorems.proof: The induced maps on total tensor products with $P$ are homotopic. Thus total tensoring descends to the homotopy category.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Signed symmetric monoidal structure on the homotopy category
theorems.hypotheses: Use the homotopy category $K(R)$ of complexes over a commutative ring.
theorems.statement: The total tensor, its graded symmetry and its usual associativity constraints define a symmetric monoidal structure.
theorems.proof: The total tensor, its graded symmetry and its usual associativity constraints define a symmetric monoidal structure.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Total tensor is triangulated on the homotopy category
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any complex $P$ over $R$.
theorems.statement: Left and right total tensor product with $P$ both define exact functors $K(R)\to K(R)$.
theorems.proof: Left and right total tensor product with $P$ both define exact functors $K(R)\to K(R)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Semifree resolutions and generation of the derived category
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be any complex over $R$.
theorems.statement: It has a quasi-isomorphic filtered resolution whose filtration is exhaustive, starts at zero, is termwise split, and has graded pieces direct sums of shifts of $R$. Its telescope triangle shows that a property stable under arbitrary direct sums and two-out-of-three in triangles and holding for every $R[k]$ holds throughout $D(R)$.
theorems.proof: It has a quasi-isomorphic filtered resolution whose filtration is exhaustive, starts at zero, is termwise split, and has graded pieces direct sums of shifts of $R$. Its telescope triangle shows that a property stable under arbitrary direct sums and two-out-of-three in triangles and holding for every $R[k]$ holds throughout $D(R)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensoring a quasi-isomorphism of K-flat complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\to Q$ be a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes.
theorems.statement: Total tensor with any complex $L$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes_R P)\to\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes_R Q)$.
theorems.proof: Total tensor with any complex $L$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes_R P)\to\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes_R Q)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Canonical symmetry of derived tensor products
theorems.hypotheses: Take $K,L\in D(R)$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural symmetry $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L\cong L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$, given on K-flat models by the graded sign $(-1)^{pq}$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural symmetry $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L\cong L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$, given on K-flat models by the graded sign $(-1)^{pq}$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Associativity of the derived tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Take $K,L,M\in D(R)$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural associator $(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural associator $(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: A homotopy factorization out of a K-flat complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a:K\to L$ be a chain map with $K$ K-flat.
theorems.statement: It is homotopic to $K\to N\to L$ with $N$ K-flat and the second arrow a quasi-isomorphism. If each term of $K$ is flat, all terms of $N$ can also be chosen flat.
theorems.proof: It is homotopic to $K\to N\to L$ with $N$ K-flat and the second arrow a quasi-isomorphism. If each term of $K$ is flat, all terms of $N$ can also be chosen flat.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Derived change of rings with coefficients in a complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ and $N\in D(A)$.
theorems.statement: The resulting functor $D(R)\to D(A)$ is exact and identifies $E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ with $(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$.
theorems.proof: The resulting functor $D(R)\to D(A)$ is exact and identifies $E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ with $(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Functoriality of derived extension with complex coefficients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:L\to N$ be a map of complexes of $A$-modules and $R\to A$ a ring map.
theorems.statement: It induces a transformation between the corresponding derived tensor functors, and a quasi-isomorphism induces a natural isomorphism.
theorems.proof: It induces a transformation between the corresponding derived tensor functors, and a quasi-isomorphism induces a natural isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Derived extension and restriction are adjoints
theorems.hypotheses: Take any ring homomorphism $R\to A$.
theorems.statement: Derived extension $D(R)\to D(A)$ is left adjoint to restriction of scalars.
theorems.proof: Derived extension $D(R)\to D(A)$ is left adjoint to restriction of scalars.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Two distinct target actions on derived tensor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R=k[x,y]$, $A=R/(xy)$ and $N=R/(x)$. Compare $N\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} A$ with the $A$-action obtained from either factor.
theorems.statement: Using the action on $N$ gives $N[1]\oplus N$ in $D(A)$, whereas using the action on $A$ gives the two-term perfect complex $[A\xrightarrow{x}A]$. These objects have different perfection behaviour.
theorems.proof: Using the action on $N$ gives $N[1]\oplus N$ in $D(A)$, whereas using the action on $A$ gives the two-term perfect complex $[A\xrightarrow{x}A]$. These objects have different perfection behaviour.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Composition of derived tensor change of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ and take $M\in D(A)$, $N\in D(B)$, $K\in D(C)$.
theorems.statement: In $D(C)$, $(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}K$ identifies with $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}K)$, equivalently $(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C)\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}(N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}K)$. By symmetry it also identifies with $(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K)\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}(N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)$.
theorems.proof: In $D(C)$, $(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}K$ identifies with $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}K)$, equivalently $(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C)\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}(N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}K)$. By symmetry it also identifies with $(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K)\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}(N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)$.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Comparison map for a commutative base-change square
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$, $R\to S$, $A\to B$, $S\to B$ form a commutative square, and take $K\in D(A)$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural comparison $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\to K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ in $D(S)$, using restriction on the right.
theorems.proof: There is a natural comparison $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\to K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ in $D(S)$, using restriction on the right.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Tor independence makes derived base change an isomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A,R\to S$ have $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(A,S)=0$ for $i>0$, and set $B=A\otimes_R S$.
theorems.statement: For every $K\in D(A)$ the canonical comparison $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\to K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$.
theorems.proof: For every $K\in D(A)$ the canonical comparison $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\to K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Flat change of a pair of algebras in Tor
theorems.hypotheses: Take a compatible morphism of diagrams $(A\leftarrow R\to B)\to(A'\leftarrow R'\to B')$. Assume $R'$ flat over $R$, $A'$ flat over $A\otimes_R R'$, and $B'$ flat over $R'\otimes_R B$.
theorems.statement: For each $i$, $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(A,B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}(A'\otimes_{R'}B')\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{R'}_i(A',B')$.
theorems.proof: For each $i$, $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(A,B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}(A'\otimes_{R'}B')\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{R'}_i(A',B')$.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Cohomological base change for a complex on a pair of algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Take a compatible morphism of diagrams $(A\leftarrow R\to B)\to(A'\leftarrow R'\to B')$. Assume $R'$ flat over $R$, $A'$ flat over $A\otimes_R R'$, and $B'$ flat over $R'\otimes_R B$.
theorems.statement: For $M\in D(A)$, the cohomology of $(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')\otimes_{R'}^{\mathbf L}B'$ equals $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}(A'\otimes_{R'}B')$ in degree $i$, canonically as modules over $A'\otimes_{R'}B'$.
theorems.proof: For $M\in D(A)$, the cohomology of $(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')\otimes_{R'}^{\mathbf L}B'$ equals $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}(A'\otimes_{R'}B')$ in degree $i$, canonically as modules over $A'\otimes_{R'}B'$.

theorems.subject: algebra-pair
theorems.name: Tor independence detected at matching primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A,B$ be $R$-algebras.
theorems.statement: Vanishing of all positive $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(A,B)$ is equivalent to Tor independence of $A_{\mathfrak p},B_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R_{\mathfrak r}$ for all primes over the same $\mathfrak r$. Equivalently all positive Tor groups vanish after localization at each prime of $A\otimes_R B$.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of all positive $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(A,B)$ is equivalent to Tor independence of $A_{\mathfrak p},B_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R_{\mathfrak r}$ for all primes over the same $\mathfrak r$. Equivalently all positive Tor groups vanish after localization at each prime of $A\otimes_R B$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Two hyper-Tor spectral sequences for a chain complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K_\bullet$ be a bounded-below chain complex and $M$ a module over $R$.
theorems.statement: Both $E^2_{i,j}=\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(H_iK,M)$ and $E^1_{i,j}=\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(K_i,M)$ abut to $H_{i+j}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)$. The first $d_2$ changes $(i,j)$ by $(1,-2)$ and the second $d_1$ by $(-1,0)$.
theorems.proof: Both $E^2_{i,j}=\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(H_iK,M)$ and $E^1_{i,j}=\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(K_i,M)$ abut to $H_{i+j}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)$. The first $d_2$ changes $(i,j)$ by $(1,-2)$ and the second $d_1$ by $(-1,0)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Change-of-rings spectral sequence for Tor
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R\to S$, an $R$-module $M$ and an $S$-module $N$.
theorems.statement: The spectral sequence has $\operatorname{Tor}^S_n(\operatorname{Tor}^R_m(M,S),N)$ on page two and abuts to $\operatorname{Tor}^R_{n+m}(M,N)$.
theorems.proof: The spectral sequence has $\operatorname{Tor}^S_n(\operatorname{Tor}^R_m(M,S),N)$ on page two and abuts to $\operatorname{Tor}^R_{n+m}(M,N)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Base change spectral sequence for a flat family of modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be flat, $A\to A'$ any map, and $M,N$ be $B$-modules both flat over $A$. Write primes for ordinary base change to $A'$.
theorems.statement: There is a spectral sequence $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(\operatorname{Tor}^B_j(M,N),A')\Rightarrow\operatorname{Tor}^{B'}_{i+j}(M',N')$.
theorems.proof: There is a spectral sequence $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(\operatorname{Tor}^B_j(M,N),A')\Rightarrow\operatorname{Tor}^{B'}_{i+j}(M',N')$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Two cohomological hyper-Tor spectral sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Take $K,L\in D^-(R)$.
theorems.statement: Either $H^p(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H^q(L))$ or $H^p(H^q(K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} L)$ gives a second page abutting to $H^{p+q}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} L)$, with $d_2$ of bidegree $(2,-1)$.
theorems.proof: Either $H^p(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H^q(L))$ or $H^p(H^q(K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} L)$ gives a second page abutting to $H^{p+q}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} L)$, with $d_2$ of bidegree $(2,-1)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Product of cohomology classes into derived tensor cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Take $K,L\in D(R)$ and integers $i,j$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural map $H^i(K)\otimes_R H^j(L)\to H^{i+j}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural map $H^i(K)\otimes_R H^j(L)\to H^{i+j}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Derived extension of scalars is monoidal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ and $K,L\in D(R)$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A)\cong(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical isomorphism $(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A)\cong(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: External product for Tor groups
theorems.hypotheses: Take two $R$-modules $M,N$, an $R$-algebra $A$, and $n,m\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The external product has source $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)\otimes_A\operatorname{Tor}^R_m(N,A)$ and target $\operatorname{Tor}^R_{n+m}(M\otimes_R N,A)$, using the map from the derived to the ordinary tensor of $M,N$.
theorems.proof: The external product has source $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)\otimes_A\operatorname{Tor}^R_m(N,A)$ and target $\operatorname{Tor}^R_{n+m}(M\otimes_R N,A)$, using the map from the derived to the ordinary tensor of $M,N$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Functoriality of the algebra structure on Tor
theorems.hypotheses: Take $R$-algebras $A,B,C$ and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $B\to C$.
theorems.statement: The induced map $\operatorname{Tor}^R_*(B,A)\to\operatorname{Tor}^R_*(C,A)$ preserves the graded $A$-algebra structure.
theorems.proof: The induced map $\operatorname{Tor}^R_*(B,A)\to\operatorname{Tor}^R_*(C,A)$ preserves the graded $A$-algebra structure.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Convergence for the tensor filtration on flat filtered models
theorems.hypotheses: Use decreasingly filtered complexes $K,L$ over $R$. Assume they, every filtration step, and every associated graded complex are K-flat with flat terms. For each complex the large positive steps are acyclic and the large negative steps map quasi-isomorphically to the whole complex.
theorems.statement: The tensor filtration gives a bounded spectral sequence with $E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{i+j=p}H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^i K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^j L)$ converging to $H^{p+q}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$ with a finite filtration in each total degree. Finite filtrations meet the tail requirements.
theorems.proof: The tensor filtration gives a bounded spectral sequence with $E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{i+j=p}H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^i K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^j L)$ converging to $H^{p+q}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$ with a finite filtration in each total degree. Finite filtrations meet the tail requirements.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Compatible K-flat resolutions of a filtered complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be a decreasingly filtered complex of modules over $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a map of filtered complexes $P\to K$ inducing quasi-isomorphisms on the underlying complex, each filtration step, and each associated graded. All corresponding complexes for $P$ are K-flat with free terms.
theorems.proof: There is a map of filtered complexes $P\to K$ inducing quasi-isomorphisms on the underlying complex, each filtration step, and each associated graded. All corresponding complexes for $P$ are K-flat with free terms.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Filtered Künneth spectral sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Take any decreasingly filtered complexes $K,L$.
theorems.statement: Their derived tensor has a filtered representative with first page $\bigoplus_{i+j=p}H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^i K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^j L)$. If for both filtrations sufficiently positive steps are acyclic and sufficiently negative steps include quasi-isomorphically, it converges with a finite filtration on each cohomology module.
theorems.proof: Their derived tensor has a filtered representative with first page $\bigoplus_{i+j=p}H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^i K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^j L)$. If for both filtrations sufficiently positive steps are acyclic and sufficiently negative steps include quasi-isomorphically, it converges with a finite filtration on each cohomology module.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Künneth spectral sequence for bounded cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Take $K,L\in D^b(R)$.
theorems.statement: The second page $E_2^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{i+j=q}\operatorname{Tor}^R_{-p}(H^iK,H^jL)$ converges to $H^{p+q}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$. Its $d_r$ has bidegree $(r,1-r)$.
theorems.proof: The second page $E_2^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{i+j=q}\operatorname{Tor}^R_{-p}(H^iK,H^jL)$ converges to $H^{p+q}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$. Its $d_r$ has bidegree $(r,1-r)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Künneth short exact sequence over a Dedekind domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain and $K,L\in D^b(R)$.
theorems.statement: The Künneth spectral sequence degenerates at page two. In degree $n$ one obtains a short exact sequence with middle $H^n(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$, submodule $\bigoplus_{i+j=n}H^iK\otimes_R H^jL$, and quotient $\bigoplus_{i+j=n+1}\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(H^iK,H^jL)$.
