theorems.hypotheses: Take $K\to K'$ between objects supported in degrees $-1,0$, inducing an isomorphism on $H^0$ and surjection on $H^{-1}$.
theorems.statement: If $I$ kills $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ for every $N$, then it kills $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K',N)$ for every $N$.
theorems.proof: If $I$ kills $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ for every $N$, then it kills $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K',N)$ for every $N$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Power annihilation of first Ext and projectivity off a closed set
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$. Fix an ideal $I\subset R$.
theorems.statement: Some power of $I$ kills all $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ precisely when some power $I^c$ kills $H^{-1}(K)$ and $H^0(K)$ is $I^c$-projective. Exponents may change between these conditions. Under Noetherianity and finite cohomology it suffices to test finite $N$. Equivalently $H^{-1}(K)$ is $I$-power torsion and $H^0(K)$ is projective after localization at each member of a finite generating family up to radical for $I$. One can use any such family, or a finite principal cover of $D(I)$ by opens on which those localizations are projective, allowing their union to contain $D(I)$.
theorems.proof: Some power of $I$ kills all $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(K,N)$ precisely when some power $I^c$ kills $H^{-1}(K)$ and $H^0(K)$ is $I^c$-projective. Exponents may change between these conditions. Under Noetherianity and finite cohomology it suffices to test finite $N$. Equivalently $H^{-1}(K)$ is $I$-power torsion and $H^0(K)$ is projective after localization at each member of a finite generating family up to radical for $I$. One can use any such family, or a finite principal cover of $D(I)$ by opens on which those localizations are projective, allowing their union to contain $D(I)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Vanishing of a two-term composite
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K_1\xrightarrow{f}K_2\xrightarrow{g}K_3$ have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$. Assume $H^0(f)=0$ and $H^{-1}(g)=0$.
theorems.statement: The composable product $g\circ f$ is zero in $D(R)$.
theorems.proof: The composable product $g\circ f$ is zero in $D(R)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: The determinant kills a square two-term complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be $R^n\xrightarrow{A}R^n$ in degrees $-1,0$.
theorems.statement: Multiplication by $\det A$ is null-homotopic using the adjugate matrix.
theorems.proof: Multiplication by $\det A$ is null-homotopic using the adjugate matrix.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Formal smoothness and smoothness via first Ext of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a ring map $A\to B$.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness is equivalent to $\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A},N)=0$ for every $B$-module $N$. Smoothness is equivalent to that vanishing plus finite presentation.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness is equivalent to $\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A},N)=0$ for every $B$-module $N$. Smoothness is equivalent to that vanishing plus finite presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Truncated derived tensor of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S\to S'$ be ring maps.
theorems.statement: The ordinary base change of the standard naive cotangent complex over $S$ represents its derived base change truncated in degrees $\ge-1$. The same statement holds for the model attached to any polynomial presentation.
theorems.proof: The ordinary base change of the standard naive cotangent complex over $S$ represents its derived base change truncated in degrees $\ge-1$. The same statement holds for the model attached to any polynomial presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Naive cotangent base change in degrees zero and minus one
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S'=S\otimes_R R'$ and base change a polynomial presentation of $S/R$.
theorems.statement: The natural map $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\mathrm{NL}_{S'/R'}$ is an isomorphism on $H^0$ and a surjection on $H^{-1}$. The corresponding statement holds for the presentation models.
theorems.proof: The natural map $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\mathrm{NL}_{S'/R'}$ is an isomorphism on $H^0$ and a surjection on $H^{-1}$. The corresponding statement holds for the presentation models.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Flat source algebra and naive cotangent base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B$ be flat over $A$ and put $B'=B\otimes_A A'$.
theorems.statement: The ordinary base-change map $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B'\to\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This also holds with derived tensor when $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ has Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$.
theorems.proof: The ordinary base-change map $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B'\to\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This also holds with derived tensor when $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ has Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: The naive cotangent complex of an lci map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local complete intersection ring map.
theorems.statement: Its naive cotangent complex is perfect over $B$ of Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$.
theorems.proof: Its naive cotangent complex is perfect over $B$ of Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-complex
theorems.name: Excess conormal kernel in an lci base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B'=B\otimes_A A'$ with both $A\to B$ and $A'\to B'$ local complete intersections.
theorems.statement: The kernel of $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B')\to H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'})$ is finite projective over $B'$.
theorems.proof: The kernel of $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B B')\to H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'})$ is finite projective over $B'$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived inverse limit of an abelian tower
theorems.hypotheses: Take a countable inverse tower of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: The derived limit is the two-term difference map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product, in degrees $0,1$, giving zero in higher degrees. A Mittag–Leffler tower has vanishing first derived limit. Every complex of towers admits a termwise limit-acyclic replacement, and on such a replacement taking the ordinary limit in each degree computes the derived limit.
theorems.proof: The derived limit is the two-term difference map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product, in degrees $0,1$, giving zero in higher degrees. A Mittag–Leffler tower has vanishing first derived limit. Every complex of towers admits a termwise limit-acyclic replacement, and on such a replacement taking the ordinary limit in each degree computes the derived limit.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived inverse limit over a tower of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction.
theorems.statement: The derived limit is the two-term difference map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product, in degrees $0,1$, giving zero in higher degrees. A Mittag–Leffler tower has vanishing first derived limit. Every complex of towers admits a termwise limit-acyclic replacement, and on such a replacement taking the ordinary limit in each degree computes the derived limit.
theorems.proof: The derived limit is the two-term difference map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product, in degrees $0,1$, giving zero in higher degrees. A Mittag–Leffler tower has vanishing first derived limit. Every complex of towers admits a termwise limit-acyclic replacement, and on such a replacement taking the ordinary limit in each degree computes the derived limit.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Six-term limit sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian towers.
theorems.statement: There is an exact sequence $0\to\lim A\to\lim B\to\lim C\to R^1\lim A\to R^1\lim B\to R^1\lim C\to0$.
theorems.proof: There is an exact sequence $0\to\lim A\to\lim B\to\lim C\to R^1\lim A\to R^1\lim B\to R^1\lim C\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Commuting degree-zero cohomology with inverse limit
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of complexes of abelian groups from degrees $-2$ through $1$. Assume $R^1\lim$ vanishes on the term towers in degrees $-2,-1$ and on the tower of $H^{-1}$.
theorems.statement: The degree-zero cohomology of the ordinary termwise limit is the limit of the degree-zero cohomologies.
theorems.proof: The degree-zero cohomology of the ordinary termwise limit is the limit of the degree-zero cohomologies.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Invariance of limit and first derived limit under pro-isomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take a countable inverse tower of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: A pro-morphism induces maps on $\lim$ and $R^1\lim$, which are isomorphisms for a pro-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: A pro-morphism induces maps on $\lim$ and $R^1\lim$, which are isomorphisms for a pro-isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Maps into a triangulated derived limit
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $K$ is a derived limit of a sequence $K_n$ in a triangulated category, and fix an object $L$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural short exact sequence from $R^1\lim\operatorname{Hom}(L,K_n[-1])$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(L,K)$ onto $\lim\operatorname{Hom}(L,K_n)$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural short exact sequence from $R^1\lim\operatorname{Hom}(L,K_n[-1])$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(L,K)$ onto $\lim\operatorname{Hom}(L,K_n)$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Pro-isomorphic towers in a triangulated category
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose two towers in a triangulated category are pro-isomorphic and both have derived limits.
theorems.statement: The chosen derived limits are isomorphic. The resulting identification can depend on choices.
theorems.proof: The chosen derived limits are isomorphic. The resulting identification can depend on choices.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Maps from a sequential homotopy colimit
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K$ be a derived colimit of $K_n$ in a triangulated category and fix $L$.
theorems.statement: There is a short exact sequence from $R^1\lim\operatorname{Hom}(K_n,L[-1])$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$ onto $\lim\operatorname{Hom}(K_n,L)$.
theorems.proof: There is a short exact sequence from $R^1\lim\operatorname{Hom}(K_n,L[-1])$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$ onto $\lim\operatorname{Hom}(K_n,L)$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Tower cohomology as sheaf cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Give the poset $\mathbf N$ the topology in which only maximal sieves cover. A presheaf of abelian groups is then an abelian tower and a sheaf.
theorems.statement: Global sections are the limit and $H^p(\mathbf N,\mathcal F)=R^p\lim\mathcal F_n$.
theorems.proof: Global sections are the limit and $H^p(\mathbf N,\mathcal F)=R^p\lim\mathcal F_n$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived global sections over a ringed tower
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction.
theorems.statement: On the poset site with only maximal covering sieves, $(A_n)$ is a structure sheaf. Sheaves of modules are compatible towers of $A_n$-modules. The derived limit is the derived global sections functor with values in $D(A)$.
theorems.proof: On the poset site with only maximal covering sieves, $(A_n)$ is a structure sheaf. Sheaves of modules are compatible towers of $A_n$-modules. The derived limit is the derived global sections functor with values in $D(A)$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Canonical difference triangle for abelian towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take an object of the derived category of towers of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical triangle $\mathbf R\lim K_n\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod K_n\to(\mathbf R\lim K_n)[1]$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical triangle $\mathbf R\lim K_n\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod K_n\to(\mathbf R\lim K_n)[1]$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Canonical difference triangle for module towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical triangle $\mathbf R\lim K_n\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod K_n\to(\mathbf R\lim K_n)[1]$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical triangle $\mathbf R\lim K_n\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod K_n\to(\mathbf R\lim K_n)[1]$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Milnor exact sequence for abelian towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take an object of the derived category of towers of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.
theorems.proof: In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Milnor exact sequence for module towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.
theorems.proof: In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Lifting a tower in the derived category of abelian groups
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a tower in $D(\mathrm{Ab})$.
theorems.statement: It can be represented by a complex of towers with compatible degreewise-derived identifications at every index.
theorems.proof: It can be represented by a complex of towers with compatible degreewise-derived identifications at every index.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Lifting derived systems over a sequence of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Give $K_n\in D(A_n)$ and maps $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ in $D(A_{n+1})$.
theorems.statement: One can represent the entire tower by a complex of compatible module systems with levelwise isomorphisms commuting with the given arrows in the respective derived categories.
theorems.proof: One can represent the entire tower by a complex of compatible module systems with levelwise isomorphisms commuting with the given arrows in the respective derived categories.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Independence of an abelian tower lift
theorems.hypotheses: A tower in $D(\mathrm{Ab})$ is represented by a lifted complex of towers.
theorems.statement: The isomorphism class of its derived inverse limit is independent of the lift, since each lift realizes the product-difference triangle. In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.
theorems.proof: The isomorphism class of its derived inverse limit is independent of the lift, since each lift realizes the product-difference triangle. In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Independence of a module tower lift
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: For any lift of a fixed tower of derived objects the resulting derived limit in $D(A)$ has the same isomorphism class. In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.
theorems.proof: For any lift of a fixed tower of derived objects the resulting derived limit in $D(A)$ has the same isomorphism class. In each degree $p$ there is a natural exact sequence $0\to R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)\to H^p(\mathbf R\lim K_n)\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to0$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived inverse limit of a pro-isomorphic morphism
theorems.hypotheses: A morphism in the derived category of abelian towers induces a pro-isomorphism between the levelwise derived objects.
theorems.statement: Its induced map on derived inverse limits is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Its induced map on derived inverse limits is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Extensions of Mittag–Leffler towers
theorems.hypotheses: In a short exact sequence of abelian towers suppose the outer terms are Mittag–Leffler.
theorems.statement: The middle tower is Mittag–Leffler.
theorems.proof: The middle tower is Mittag–Leffler.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Zero pro-objects via repeated sums
theorems.hypotheses: Take a countable inverse tower of abelian groups.
theorems.statement: The tower is pro-zero precisely when its limit and first derived limit both vanish and both also vanish for the termwise countable direct sum of copies of the tower.
theorems.proof: The tower is pro-zero precisely when its limit and first derived limit both vanish and both also vanish for the termwise countable direct sum of copies of the tower.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Degreewise surjective representatives of derived towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: There exists a representative by complexes with surjective transition maps in each degree.
theorems.proof: There exists a representative by complexes with surjective transition maps in each degree.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Levelwise K-flat representatives of derived towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: There exists a representative by a tower whose complex at every level is K-flat.
theorems.proof: There exists a representative by a tower whose complex at every level is K-flat.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Derived tensor products for module towers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower of rings $(A_n)$ and its limit $A$. A tower of modules has $M_n$ over $A_n$ with transitions linear over $A_{n+1}$ by restriction. Take an object of the derived category of compatible module towers.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical symmetric derived tensor on the derived category of towers, exact in each argument and computed at each level by the corresponding derived tensor.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical symmetric derived tensor on the derived category of towers, exact in each argument and computed at each level by the corresponding derived tensor.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Functorial tensor followed by derived inverse limit
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a tower $E_n$ in $D(A)$ and choose a lift to the derived category of towers.
theorems.statement: The construction $K\mapsto\mathbf R\lim(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}E_n)$ is exact and functorial in $K$ for this chosen lift, using the constant tower of $K$.
theorems.proof: The construction $K\mapsto\mathbf R\lim(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}E_n)$ is exact and functorial in $K$ for this chosen lift, using the constant tower of $K$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Tensor-limit functors preserve tower triangles
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $K\in D(A)$ and a triangle of complexes of towers over $A$.
theorems.statement: Levelwise derived tensor with the constant tower of the fixed object, followed by derived inverse limit, yields a distinguished triangle.
theorems.proof: Levelwise derived tensor with the constant tower of the fixed object, followed by derived inverse limit, yields a distinguished triangle.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Tensor-limit comparison for pro-isomorphic towers
theorems.hypotheses: A morphism in $D(\mathbf N,A)$ gives a pro-isomorphism on levelwise derived objects. Fix any $K\in D(A)$.
theorems.statement: After tensoring levelwise with the fixed object and taking derived inverse limits, the induced morphism is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: After tensoring levelwise with the fixed object and taking derived inverse limits, the induced morphism is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Cyclic quotient resolution of an ideal-power-torsion module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subset R$ be any ideal and $M$ an $I$-power-torsion module.
theorems.statement: It has a resolution by direct sums of modules $R/I^n$, with exponents allowed to vary across summands.
theorems.proof: It has a resolution by direct sums of modules $R/I^n$, with exponents allowed to vary across summands.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Vanishing of ideal torsion by a localization test
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $M$ is any module.
theorems.statement: The annihilator $M[I]$ vanishes exactly when every $M[I^n]$ vanishes for $n>0$, equivalently when $M\to\bigoplus_j M_{f_j}$ is injective.
theorems.proof: The annihilator $M[I]$ vanishes exactly when every $M[I^n]$ vanishes for $n>0$, equivalently when $M\to\bigoplus_j M_{f_j}$ is injective.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Removing ideal-power torsion and closure under extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be finitely generated.
theorems.statement: The quotient $M/M[I^\infty]$ has no nonzero elements killed by $I$. Extensions of two $I$-power-torsion modules are $I$-power torsion.
theorems.proof: The quotient $M/M[I^\infty]$ has no nonzero elements killed by $I$. Extensions of two $I$-power-torsion modules are $I$-power torsion.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Power-torsion modules form a Serre subcategory
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal.
theorems.statement: The $I$-power-torsion modules are closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions in all $R$-modules.
theorems.proof: The $I$-power-torsion modules are closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions in all $R$-modules.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Support criterion for ideal-power torsion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be finitely generated and $M$ any module.
theorems.statement: The module is $I$-power torsion exactly when $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subset V(I)$. Thus this subcategory depends only on the closed subset.
theorems.proof: The module is $I$-power torsion exactly when $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subset V(I)$. Thus this subcategory depends only on the closed subset.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensor nonpositivity on torsion modules and complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$ has no positive cohomology for an arbitrary ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: The same holds with $R/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, every $I$-power-torsion module, and every bounded nonpositive-cohomology complex whose cohomologies are $I$-power torsion.
theorems.proof: The same holds with $R/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, every $I$-power-torsion module, and every bounded nonpositive-cohomology complex whose cohomologies are $I$-power torsion.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Vanishing on torsion complexes tested by the quotient ring
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I=0$.
theorems.statement: The derived tensor with $K$ vanishes on all $R/I^n$, $n\ge1$, on all $I$-power-torsion modules, and on bounded complexes with $I$-power-torsion cohomology.
theorems.proof: The derived tensor with $K$ vanishes on all $R/I^n$, $n\ge1$, on all $I$-power-torsion modules, and on bounded complexes with $I$-power-torsion cohomology.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Scalar extension on power torsion under adic congruences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ induce isomorphisms $R/I^n\cong R'/I^nR'$ for all $n>0$.
theorems.statement: For every $I$-power-torsion $M$, the map $M\to M\otimes_R R'$ is an isomorphism. Adic completion supplies an example for finitely generated $I$.
theorems.proof: For every $I$-power-torsion $M$, the map $M\to M\otimes_R R'$ is an isomorphism. Adic completion supplies an example for finitely generated $I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Faithfulness over a closed fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat and $I\subset R$ an ideal.
theorems.statement: Faithful flatness of $R/I\to S/IS$, surjectivity of its spectrum map, faithfulness of scalar extension on modules killed by $I$, and faithfulness on all $I$-power-torsion modules are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Faithful flatness of $R/I\to S/IS$, surjectivity of its spectrum map, faithfulness of scalar extension on modules killed by $I$, and faithfulness on all $I$-power-torsion modules are equivalent.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Closed fibre isomorphism tested on ideal-power torsion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat and $R/I\to S/IS$ faithfully flat.
theorems.statement: This quotient map is an isomorphism precisely when $M\to M\otimes_R S$ is an isomorphism for every $I$-power-torsion module.
theorems.proof: This quotient map is an isomorphism precisely when $M\to M\otimes_R S$ is an isomorphism for every $I$-power-torsion module.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Equivalence of torsion module categories
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: Extension of scalars identifies $M[I^\infty]$ with $(M\otimes_R S)[(IS)^\infty]$ for all $M$. It gives an isomorphism on Hom groups whenever the source or target module is power torsion, and induces an equivalence of the two power-torsion categories.
theorems.proof: Extension of scalars identifies $M[I^\infty]$ with $(M\otimes_R S)[(IS)^\infty]$ for all $M$. It gives an isomorphism on Hom groups whenever the source or target module is power torsion, and induces an equivalence of the two power-torsion categories.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Koszul and extended Čech comparisons over the neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism. Choose another finite list $g_i$ defining $V(I)$ set-theoretically.
theorems.statement: Both the Koszul complexes on the $g_i$ and their augmented alternating localization Čech complexes map by quasi-isomorphisms from the versions over $R$ to the versions over $S$.
theorems.proof: Both the Koszul complexes on the $g_i$ and their augmented alternating localization Čech complexes map by quasi-isomorphisms from the versions over $R$ to the versions over $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The first Koszul relations give an approximation to the ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Take $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$. Let $U$ have generators $e_i$ and relations $f_ie_j=f_je_i$.
theorems.statement: The map $U\to I$ given by $e_i\mapsto f_i$ is onto and its kernel $J$ is annihilated by $I$.
theorems.proof: The map $U\to I$ given by $e_i\mapsto f_i$ is onto and its kernel $J$ is annihilated by $I$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: First Ext inside the module of Koszul cocycles
theorems.hypotheses: Use $U\to I$ and its kernel $J$ from Tag 05ED. Let $N$ be any module. Put $H=\{(x_i)\in N^t:f_ix_j=f_jx_i\}/\{(f_i x):x\in N\}$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(R/I,N)\to H\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(J,N)$ is exact at the first two nonzero terms. The last map is induced by restriction from $U$ to $J$.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(R/I,N)\to H\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(J,N)$ is exact at the first two nonzero terms. The last map is induced by restriction from $U$ to $J$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Annihilation of first Koszul cocycles modulo boundaries
theorems.hypotheses: Take $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$, any module $N$, and the cocycle quotient $H$ in Tag 05EE.
theorems.statement: Every $a\in I$ annihilates $H$: multiplying a cocycle by $f_j$ gives the boundary determined by $x_j$.
theorems.proof: Every $a\in I$ annihilates $H$: multiplying a cocycle by $f_j$ gives the boundary determined by $x_j$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Descent of extensions with torsion quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism. Let $M,N$ be $R$-modules with $M$ power torsion for $I$.
theorems.statement: Every extension of $M\otimes_R S$ by $N\otimes_R S$ is the scalar extension of an extension of $M$ by $N$, compatibly with the identity identifications of the end terms.
theorems.proof: Every extension of $M\otimes_R S$ by $N\otimes_R S$ is the scalar extension of an extension of $M$ by $N$, compatibly with the identity identifications of the end terms.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The equalizer for global module gluing
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: For every $M$, its restriction map identifies $M$ with the kernel of the overlap difference maps on $(M\otimes_R S)\times\prod_i M_{f_i}$, comparing against $(M\otimes_R S)_{f_i}$ and $M_{f_i f_j}$.
theorems.proof: For every $M$, its restriction map identifies $M$ with the kernel of the overlap difference maps on $(M\otimes_R S)\times\prod_i M_{f_i}$, comparing against $(M\otimes_R S)_{f_i}$ and $M_{f_i f_j}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Adjunction for compatible gluing sections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map and fix $f_1,\ldots,f_t$ with ideal $I$. Write $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ for the scalar extension to $S$ and localizations at the $f_i$, with their canonical identifications.
theorems.statement: Taking compatible sections $H^0$ is right adjoint to $\mathrm{Can}$.
theorems.proof: Taking compatible sections $H^0$ is right adjoint to $\mathrm{Can}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Recovering the module from its canonical data
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: The natural unit $M\to H^0(\mathrm{Can}(M))$ is an isomorphism for every $R$-module.
theorems.proof: The natural unit $M\to H^0(\mathrm{Can}(M))$ is an isomorphism for every $R$-module.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Exactness and colimits of ordinary gluing
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map and fix $f_1,\ldots,f_t$ with ideal $I$. Write $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ for the scalar extension to $S$ and localizations at the $f_i$, with their canonical identifications. Suppose $R\to S$ flat.
theorems.statement: The category of data is abelian and $\mathrm{Can}$ is exact and preserves all colimits.
theorems.proof: The category of data is abelian and $\mathrm{Can}$ is exact and preserves all colimits.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Gluing when the principal opens already cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map and fix $f_1,\ldots,f_t$ with ideal $I$. Write $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ for the scalar extension to $S$ and localizations at the $f_i$, with their canonical identifications. Suppose $R\to S$ flat and $I=R$.
theorems.statement: The functors $\mathrm{Can}$ and $H^0$ are quasi-inverse equivalences.
theorems.proof: The functors $\mathrm{Can}$ and $H^0$ are quasi-inverse equivalences.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Flat base change of gluing data
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map and fix $f_1,\ldots,f_t$ with ideal $I$. Write $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ for the scalar extension to $S$ and localizations at the $f_i$, with their canonical identifications. Assume $R\to S$ flat and base change along a flat $R\to R'$.
theorems.statement: With $S'=S\otimes_R R'$, extension on all terms of the data commutes both with $\mathrm{Can}$ and with taking compatible sections $H^0$.
theorems.proof: With $S'=S\otimes_R R'$, extension on all terms of the data commutes both with $\mathrm{Can}$ and with taking compatible sections $H^0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Formal gluing along a finitely generated ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: The category of all $R$-modules is equivalent to the category of compatible gluing data for $R\to S$ and the $f_i$, with inverse given by compatible sections.
theorems.proof: The category of all $R$-modules is equivalent to the category of compatible gluing data for $R\to S$ and the $f_i$, with inverse given by compatible sections.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting a modification with power-torsion kernel and cokernel
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: An $S$-linear map $M'\to N\otimes_R S$ with $I$-power-torsion kernel and cokernel descends to an $R$-linear map $M\to N$ with compatible identification $M\otimes_R S\simeq M'$. The dual situation with prescribed source also descends. The kernels and cokernels downstairs identify with those upstairs as $R$-modules.
theorems.proof: An $S$-linear map $M'\to N\otimes_R S$ with $I$-power-torsion kernel and cokernel descends to an $R$-linear map $M\to N$ with compatible identification $M\otimes_R S\simeq M'$. The dual situation with prescribed source also descends. The kernels and cokernels downstairs identify with those upstairs as $R$-modules.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Principal formal gluing for arbitrary modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism. Suppose $I=(f)$.
theorems.statement: Restriction gives $\mathrm{Mod}_R\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_S\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_{S_f}}\mathrm{Mod}_{R_f}$, with overlap identification part of the fibre-product data.
theorems.proof: Restriction gives $\mathrm{Mod}_R\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_S\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_{S_f}}\mathrm{Mod}_{R_f}$, with overlap identification part of the fibre-product data.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Noetherian completion gluing for finite modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $f\in R$, and $\widehat R$ its $f$-adic completion.
theorems.statement: A finite $R$-module is equivalently a finite $\widehat R$-module and a finite $R_f$-module identified over $\widehat R_f$. Restriction of a finite module gives its completion and its localization.
theorems.proof: A finite $R$-module is equivalently a finite $\widehat R$-module and a finite $R_f$-module identified over $\widehat R_f$. Restriction of a finite module gives its completion and its localization.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Tensor structures and properties under formal gluing
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ and $R/I\to S/IS$ an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: Finite generation, finite presentation, flatness and projectivity are each detected on $S$ and all $R_{f_i}$. The gluing equivalence respects tensor structures and therefore also identifies the corresponding algebra objects.
theorems.proof: Finite generation, finite presentation, flatness and projectivity are each detected on $S$ and all $R_{f_i}$. The gluing equivalence respects tensor structures and therefore also identifies the corresponding algebra objects.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Sheaf gluing near a closed submanifold
theorems.hypotheses: Let a smooth manifold have a compact closed submanifold, choose a tubular neighbourhood of it, and take the open complement.
theorems.statement: A sheaf is equivalently its restrictions to these two opens with an isomorphism on their intersection. The algebraic gluing theorem supplies a formal neighbourhood in the module setting.
theorems.proof: A sheaf is equivalently its restrictions to these two opens with an isomorphism on their intersection. The algebraic gluing theorem supplies a formal neighbourhood in the module setting.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: All principal-power quotients of the completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\widehat R$ be the $f$-adic completion of any ring $R$.
theorems.statement: For every $n>0$, the canonical map $R/f^nR\to\widehat R/f^n\widehat R$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: For every $n>0$, the canonical map $R/f^nR\to\widehat R/f^n\widehat R$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Joint tensor detection by a neighbourhood and its complement
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $f\in R$ induce $R/f^nR\simeq S/f^nS$ for every $n>0$.
theorems.statement: For every nonzero module $M$, $M\otimes_R(S\oplus R_f)$ is nonzero. This includes $S=\widehat R$.
theorems.proof: For every nonzero module $M$, $M\otimes_R(S\oplus R_f)$ is nonzero. This includes $S=\widehat R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Joint surjectivity on spectra for the two pieces
theorems.hypotheses: Assume only $R/fR\simeq S/fS$.
theorems.statement: The images of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R_f$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.proof: The images of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R_f$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Detecting finite generation on the two pieces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $f\in R$ induce $R/f^nR\simeq S/f^nS$ for every $n>0$.
theorems.statement: An $R$-module is finite precisely when its scalar extensions to $S$ and $R_f$ are finite over the respective rings.
theorems.proof: An $R$-module is finite precisely when its scalar extensions to $S$ and $R_f$ are finite over the respective rings.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completion and the limits of faithfully flat descent
theorems.hypotheses: Take $S=\widehat R$ for completion at a principal ideal, over an arbitrary ring.
theorems.statement: Although localization is flat, completion can fail to be flat. Even when flatness holds, a full descent datum on $S\times R_f$ also involves $S\otimes_R S$. The gluing theorem uses only the overlap $S_f$.
theorems.proof: Although localization is flat, completion can fail to be flat. Even when flatness holds, a full descent datum on $S\times R_f$ also involves $S\otimes_R S$. The gluing theorem uses only the overlap $S_f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Torsion criterion for a principal gluing pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $f\in R$ induce $R/f^nR\simeq S/f^nS$ for every $n>0$.
theorems.statement: The difference map $S\oplus R_f\to S_f$ is onto. Exactness of $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f$ at $R$ and at the middle term is respectively injectivity and surjectivity of $R[f^\infty]\to S[f^\infty]$. Thus the pair condition is equivalent to bijectivity on power torsion.
theorems.proof: The difference map $S\oplus R_f\to S_f$ is onto. Exactness of $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f$ at $R$ and at the middle term is respectively injectivity and surjectivity of $R[f^\infty]\to S[f^\infty]$. Thus the pair condition is equivalent to bijectivity on power torsion.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Principal completion at a regular element gives a gluing pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ act injectively on $R$.
theorems.statement: It acts injectively on $\widehat R$ as well, so the completion map and $f$ are a gluing pair.
theorems.proof: It acts injectively on $\widehat R$ as well, so the completion map and $f$ are a gluing pair.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Flat principal completion gives a gluing pair
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose the $f$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is flat over $R$, as for Noetherian $R$.
theorems.statement: The map identifies $R[f^n]$ with $\widehat R[f^n]$ for each $n$, hence gives a gluing pair.
theorems.proof: The map identifies $R[f^n]$ with $\widehat R[f^n]$ for each $n$, hence gives a gluing pair.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Power torsion criterion for a gluable module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $f\in R$ induce $R/f^nR\simeq S/f^nS$ for every $n>0$. Put $M'=M\otimes_R S$ and use the difference sequence $0\to M\to M'\oplus M_f\to M'_f\to0$.
theorems.statement: This sequence is right exact at the last term. Left injectivity and exactness at the middle are equivalent, respectively, to injectivity and surjectivity of $M[f^\infty]\to M'[f^\infty]$. For a gluing pair surjectivity is automatic, so injectivity suffices.
theorems.proof: This sequence is right exact at the last term. Left injectivity and exactness at the middle are equivalent, respectively, to injectivity and surjectivity of $M[f^\infty]\to M'[f^\infty]$. For a gluing pair surjectivity is automatic, so injectivity suffices.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Sufficient tests for module gluability
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R\to S,f)$ be a gluing pair, so the integral congruences hold and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ is exact.
theorems.statement: Vanishing of $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,S_f)$ suffices, equivalently $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,S)$ is $f$-power torsion. Thus flat $M$ are gluable, as are all $M$ if $S$ is flat. For $S=\widehat R$, the condition $M[f]\cap\bigcap_n f^nM=0$ also suffices.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,S_f)$ suffices, equivalently $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,S)$ is $f$-power torsion. Thus flat $M$ are gluable, as are all $M$ if $S$ is flat. For $S=\widehat R$, the condition $M[f]\cap\bigcap_n f^nM=0$ also suffices.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Tor vanishing for principal powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R\to S,f)$ be a gluing pair, so the integral congruences hold and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ is exact.
theorems.statement: For every $n>0$, $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(S,f^nR)=0$.
theorems.proof: For every $n>0$, $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(S,f^nR)=0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Tor vanishing after dividing by scalar power torsion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R\to S,f)$ be a gluing pair, so the integral congruences hold and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ is exact.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(S,R/R[f^\infty])=0$.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(S,R/R[f^\infty])=0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Tor vanishing for the localization cokernel
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R\to S,f)$ be a gluing pair, so the integral congruences hold and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ is exact.
theorems.statement: For any module $M$, $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(S,\operatorname{coker}(M\to M_f))=0$.
theorems.proof: For any module $M$, $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(S,\operatorname{coker}(M\to M_f))=0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Beauville–Laszlo equivalence on gluable modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R\to S,f)$ be a gluing pair, so the integral congruences hold and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ is exact.
theorems.statement: The restriction functor on gluable $R$-modules is an equivalence with pairs of an $S$-module and an $R_f$-module identified after extending to $S_f$.
theorems.proof: The restriction functor on gluable $R$-modules is an equivalence with pairs of an $S$-module and an $R_f$-module identified after extending to $S_f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Canonical gluable quotient of an arbitrary module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R\to S,f)$ be a gluing pair, so the integral congruences hold and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ is exact.
theorems.statement: Taking compatible sections of the restrictions of $M$ gives a gluable module $\widetilde M$. The canonical map $M\to\widetilde M$ is onto, an isomorphism after extending to $S$, and an isomorphism after inverting $f$.
theorems.proof: Taking compatible sections of the restrictions of $M$ gives a gluable module $\widetilde M$. The canonical map $M\to\widetilde M$ is onto, an isomorphism after extending to $S$, and an isomorphism after inverting $f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Flatness tested on both gluing pieces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R\to S,f)$ be a gluing pair, so the integral congruences hold and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ is exact.
theorems.statement: For any $M$, flatness over $R$ is equivalent to flatness of $M\otimes_R S$ over $S$ and $M_f$ over $R_f$.
theorems.proof: For any $M$, flatness over $R$ is equivalent to flatness of $M\otimes_R S$ over $S$ and $M_f$ over $R_f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Finite projectivity tested on both gluing pieces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R\to S,f)$ be a gluing pair, so the integral congruences hold and $0\to R\to S\oplus R_f\to S_f\to0$ is exact.
theorems.statement: For any $M$, finite projectivity is equivalent to finite projectivity after extension to each of $S,R_f$.
theorems.proof: For any $M$, finite projectivity is equivalent to finite projectivity after extension to each of $S,R_f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Extension of the nonzerodivisor setting of Beauville and Laszlo
theorems.hypotheses: In the original principal-completion setting $S=\widehat R$ and $f$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$.
theorems.statement: Modules on which $f$ acts injectively are gluable. The general equivalence applies to every gluable module, and the finite-projectivity test applies to every module.
theorems.proof: Modules on which $f$ acts injectively are gluable. The general equivalence applies to every gluable module, and the finite-projectivity test applies to every module.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Equivalent localization tests for derived completeness at one element
theorems.hypotheses: For $K\in D(A)$ and $f\in A$, let $T(K,f)$ be the derived inverse limit of the tower with transition $f:K\to K$.
theorems.statement: Vanishing of $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,K)$, of all $\operatorname{Ext}^n_A(A_f,K)$, of $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(E,K)$ for every restricted $E\in D(A_f)$, and of $T(K,f)$ are equivalent. Equivalently $1-f\cdot\mathrm{shift}$ on $\prod_{n\ge0}K$ is invertible. Cohomologywise each $T(H^p(K),f)$ vanishes, equivalently both $\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,H^pK)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(A_f,H^pK)$ vanish for all $p$.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,K)$, of all $\operatorname{Ext}^n_A(A_f,K)$, of $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(E,K)$ for every restricted $E\in D(A_f)$, and of $T(K,f)$ are equivalent. Equivalently $1-f\cdot\mathrm{shift}$ on $\prod_{n\ge0}K$ is invertible. Cohomologywise each $T(H^p(K),f)$ vanishes, equivalently both $\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,H^pK)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(A_f,H^pK)$ vanish for all $p$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The ideal of scalars along which a complex is derived complete
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $K\in D(A)$.
theorems.statement: The elements $f$ for which $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,K)=0$ form a radical ideal of $A$.
theorems.proof: The elements $f$ for which $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,K)=0$ form a radical ideal of $A$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Surjectivity of the map from a derived complete module to completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion. Suppose $M$ is derived complete for $I$.
theorems.statement: Then $M\to\lim_n M/I^nM$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: Then $M\to\lim_n M/I^nM$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Weak Serre property of derived-complete modules
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any ideal $I\subset A$.
theorems.statement: Derived-complete modules form a weak Serre subcategory. An object of $D(A)$ is derived complete exactly when every cohomology module is in this subcategory.
theorems.proof: Derived-complete modules form a weak Serre subcategory. An object of $D(A)$ is derived complete exactly when every cohomology module is in this subcategory.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Nakayama for derived-complete modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion. Suppose $M$ is derived complete and $M/IM=0$.
theorems.statement: Then $M=0$, with no finite generation condition on $M$.
theorems.proof: Then $M=0$, with no finite generation condition on $M$.
refs: B. Bhatt, Prismatic cohomology, Lecture III, §2, property (2), module case (ordinary quotient by a finitely generated ideal)

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent complexes over a derived-complete base
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $A$ as a module over itself is derived complete for $I$.
theorems.statement: Any pseudo-coherent $K\in D(A)$ is derived complete for $I$. Ordinary $I$-adic completeness of $A$ suffices.
theorems.proof: Any pseudo-coherent $K\in D(A)$ is derived complete for $I$. Ordinary $I$-adic completeness of $A$ suffices.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Successive derived Hom from localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f,g\in A$ and $K\in D(A)$.
theorems.statement: One has $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_g,K))\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_{fg},K)$ by derived adjunction and flatness.
theorems.proof: One has $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_g,K))\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_{fg},K)$ by derived adjunction and flatness.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Čech formula and universal property for derived completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion.
theorems.statement: With $C^\bullet$ the augmented alternating localization complex for any finite generating list of $I$, $\Lambda_I K\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C^\bullet,K)$. Precomposition with its unit identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_I K,E)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(K,E)$ for every complete $E$.
theorems.proof: With $C^\bullet$ the augmented alternating localization complex for any finite generating list of $I$, $\Lambda_I K\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C^\bullet,K)$. Precomposition with its unit identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_I K,E)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(K,E)$ for every complete $E$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completion of a localized complex vanishes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion. Some $f\in I$ acts invertibly on the complex, for example it comes by restriction from $A_f$.
theorems.statement: Its derived $I$-completion is zero.
theorems.proof: Its derived $I$-completion is zero.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Compatibility of completion with derived Hom
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion.
theorems.statement: For $K,L\in D(A)$, $\Lambda_I\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(K,\Lambda_I L)\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_I K,\Lambda_I L)$.
theorems.proof: For $K,L\in D(A)$, $\Lambda_I\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(K,\Lambda_I L)\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_I K,\Lambda_I L)$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Limits of systems killed levelwise by powers of ideal elements
theorems.hypotheses: In a tower $E_n$ assume each $f\in I$ acts nilpotently as a derived endomorphism of each $E_n$. Exponents may depend on $n$ and $f$.
theorems.statement: For any $K$, $\mathbf R\lim_n(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}E_n)$ is derived $I$-complete.
theorems.proof: For any $K$, $\mathbf R\lim_n(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}E_n)$ is derived $I$-complete.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The inverse limit of Koszul reductions is derived complete
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and let $K_n$ be the Koszul complex on the list of $n$th powers, in degrees $[-r,0]$.
theorems.statement: For any $M\in D(A)$ the object $\mathbf R\lim_n(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n)$ is derived complete.
theorems.proof: For any $M\in D(A)$ the object $\mathbf R\lim_n(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n)$ is derived complete.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Koszul fixed-point test for completeness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and let $K_n$ be the Koszul complex on the list of $n$th powers, in degrees $[-r,0]$.
theorems.statement: An object $M$ is derived complete exactly when $M\to\mathbf R\lim_n(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n)$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: An object $M$ is derived complete exactly when $M\to\mathbf R\lim_n(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n)$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Koszul formula for derived completion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and let $K_n$ be the Koszul complex on the list of $n$th powers, in degrees $[-r,0]$.
theorems.statement: The functor $M\mapsto\mathbf R\lim_n(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n)$ realizes the left adjoint $\Lambda_I$ with its natural unit.
theorems.proof: The functor $M\mapsto\mathbf R\lim_n(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n)$ realizes the left adjoint $\Lambda_I$ with its natural unit.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Detecting nonpositive degrees on a complete complex
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and let $K_n$ be the Koszul complex on the list of $n$th powers, in degrees $[-r,0]$. Suppose $M$ derived complete.
theorems.statement: The three conditions that $M$, $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I$, and $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_1$ have no positive cohomology are equivalent.
theorems.proof: The three conditions that $M$, $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I$, and $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_1$ have no positive cohomology are equivalent.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Derived Nakayama lemma
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion. Suppose $K$ is derived complete and $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I=0$.
theorems.statement: Then $K=0$ in $D(A)$.
theorems.proof: Then $K=0$ in $D(A)$.
refs: B. Bhatt, Prismatic cohomology, Lecture III, §2, property (2) (derived Nakayama for complexes at a finitely generated ideal)

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Cohomological bounds for completion at an ideal with r generators
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $I$ has $r$ generators. Let $u:K\to L$ in $D(A)$.
theorems.statement: If $H^i(u)$ is an isomorphism for $i\ge1$ and surjective at zero, the same holds for $\Lambda_Iu$. If $H^i(u)$ is an isomorphism for $i\le-1$ and injective at zero, then $H^i(\Lambda_Iu)$ is an isomorphism for $i\le-r-1$ and injective at $-r$.
theorems.proof: If $H^i(u)$ is an isomorphism for $i\ge1$ and surjective at zero, the same holds for $\Lambda_Iu$. If $H^i(u)$ is an isomorphism for $i\le-1$ and injective at zero, then $H^i(\Lambda_Iu)$ is an isomorphism for $i\le-r-1$ and injective at $-r$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Filtered spectral sequence for derived completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion. Let $K$ be a filtered cochain complex.
theorems.statement: There is a spectral sequence of derived-complete modules with $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\Lambda_I\operatorname{gr}^pK)$ and differentials of degree $(r,1-r)$. Finite filtration in each cochain degree yields bounded convergence to $H^*(\Lambda_I K)$.
theorems.proof: There is a spectral sequence of derived-complete modules with $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\Lambda_I\operatorname{gr}^pK)$ and differentials of degree $(r,1-r)$. Finite filtration in each cochain degree yields bounded convergence to $H^*(\Lambda_I K)$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completion spectral sequence from cohomological truncations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion.
theorems.statement: For every $K$ there is a bounded convergent spectral sequence $E_2^{i,j}=H^i(\Lambda_I H^j(K))\Rightarrow H^{i+j}(\Lambda_I K)$ with differentials of degree $(r,1-r)$.
theorems.proof: For every $K$ there is a bounded convergent spectral sequence $E_2^{i,j}=H^i(\Lambda_I H^j(K))\Rightarrow H^{i+j}(\Lambda_I K)$ with differentials of degree $(r,1-r)$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Restriction detects derived completeness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, $I\subset A$ any ideal, and $K\in D(B)$.
theorems.statement: The complex is derived complete over $B$ for $IB$ precisely when its restriction to $A$ is derived complete for $I$.
theorems.proof: The complex is derived complete over $B$ for $IB$ precisely when its restriction to $A$ is derived complete for $I$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Equivalence of complete subcategories over flat neighbourhoods
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion. Let $A\to B$ be flat and induce an isomorphism modulo $I$.
theorems.statement: Restriction gives an equivalence from derived $IB$-complete complexes over $B$ to derived $I$-complete complexes over $A$.
theorems.proof: Restriction gives an equivalence from derived $IB$-complete complexes over $B$ to derived $I$-complete complexes over $A$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Limits and colimits of derived-complete modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subset A$ be an ideal.
theorems.statement: The category of derived-complete modules is abelian and complete under all small limits. The inclusion into modules is exact and preserves limits. If $I$ is finitely generated there are all small colimits and the inclusion has a left adjoint $M\mapsto H^0(\Lambda_I M)$.
theorems.proof: The category of derived-complete modules is abelian and complete under all small limits. The inclusion into modules is exact and preserves limits. If $I$ is finitely generated there are all small colimits and the inclusion has a left adjoint $M\mapsto H^0(\Lambda_I M)$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Bounded torsion compares quotient and principal Koszul towers
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f\in A$, $I=(f)$ and use $\Lambda_f$ for derived completion. Suppose $A[f^n]$ stabilizes for $n\ge c$, as over a Noetherian ring.
theorems.statement: The natural augmentation from $[A\xrightarrow{f^n}A]$ to $A/f^n$ admits shifted reverse maps from $A/f^{n+c}$ which exhibit a pro-isomorphism in $D(A)$.
theorems.proof: The natural augmentation from $[A\xrightarrow{f^n}A]$ to $A/f^n$ admits shifted reverse maps from $A/f^{n+c}$ which exhibit a pro-isomorphism in $D(A)$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Criterion for computing principal completion by ordinary quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f\in A$, $I=(f)$ and use $\Lambda_f$ for derived completion.
theorems.statement: The comparison $\Lambda_f K\to\mathbf R\lim_n(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/f^n)$ is an isomorphism for every $K$ exactly when the $f$-power torsion in $A$ is bounded.
theorems.proof: The comparison $\Lambda_f K\to\mathbf R\lim_n(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/f^n)$ is an isomorphism for every $K$ exactly when the $f$-power torsion in $A$ is bounded.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Presenting a derived-complete module by torsion-free complete modules
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f\in A$, $I=(f)$ and use $\Lambda_f$ for derived completion. Suppose $f$ is a nonzerodivisor in $A$.
theorems.statement: An $A$-module $M$ is derived complete exactly when $0\to N\to L\to M\to0$ exists with $N,L$ classically $f$-adically complete and multiplication by $f$ injective on both.
theorems.proof: An $A$-module $M$ is derived complete exactly when $0\to N\to L\to M\to0$ exists with $N,L$ classically $f$-adically complete and multiplication by $f$ injective on both.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Principal completion of a module and its Tate module
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f\in A$, $I=(f)$ and use $\Lambda_f$ for derived completion.
theorems.statement: For a module $M$, the only possibly nonzero cohomologies are $H^{-1}=T_f(M)$ and $H^0$, fitting into $0\to R^1\lim M[f^n]\to H^0(\Lambda_f M)\to\lim M/f^nM\to0$. For any $K$, $0\to H^0(\Lambda_f H^pK)\to H^p(\Lambda_f K)\to T_f(H^{p+1}K)\to0$ is exact.
theorems.proof: For a module $M$, the only possibly nonzero cohomologies are $H^{-1}=T_f(M)$ and $H^0$, fitting into $0\to R^1\lim M[f^n]\to H^0(\Lambda_f M)\to\lim M/f^nM\to0$. For any $K$, $0\to H^0(\Lambda_f H^pK)\to H^p(\Lambda_f K)\to T_f(H^{p+1}K)\to0$ is exact.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Comparison diagram for ordinary and derived principal completion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f\in A$, $I=(f)$ and use $\Lambda_f$ for derived completion. Set $K_n=K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}[A\xrightarrow{f^n}A]$.
theorems.statement: The exact sequence $0\to H^0(\Lambda_f H^pK)\to H^p(\Lambda_f K)\to T_f(H^{p+1}K)\to0$ maps onto $0\to\widehat{H^pK}\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to T_f(H^{p+1}K)\to0$. The Tate map is the identity and the first two kernels identify canonically as $R^1\lim H^p(K)[f^n]\simeq R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)$.
theorems.proof: The exact sequence $0\to H^0(\Lambda_f H^pK)\to H^p(\Lambda_f K)\to T_f(H^{p+1}K)\to0$ maps onto $0\to\widehat{H^pK}\to\lim H^p(K_n)\to T_f(H^{p+1}K)\to0$. The Tate map is the identity and the first two kernels identify canonically as $R^1\lim H^p(K)[f^n]\simeq R^1\lim H^{p-1}(K_n)$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Mittag–Leffler test for principal Koszul fibre cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f\in A$, $I=(f)$ and use $\Lambda_f$ for derived completion. Set $K_n=K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}[A\xrightarrow{f^n}A]$.
theorems.statement: The tower $H^p(K_n)$ is Mittag–Leffler exactly when the torsion tower $H^{p+1}(K)[f^n]$ is, with transition multiplication by $f$.
theorems.proof: The tower $H^p(K_n)$ is Mittag–Leffler exactly when the torsion tower $H^{p+1}(K)[f^n]$ is, with transition multiplication by $f$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Uniform exponent for a derived-complete power-torsion module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion. Suppose the module $M$ is both derived complete and $I$-power torsion.
theorems.statement: There exists a single $n$ with $I^nM=0$.
theorems.proof: There exists a single $n$ with $I^nM=0$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Square-zero obstruction to principal adic separatedness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f\in A$, $I=(f)$ and use $\Lambda_f$ for derived completion. Let $J=\bigcap_n f^nA$ and suppose $M$ derived complete.
theorems.statement: The ideal $J$ annihilates the kernel of $M\to\lim_n M/f^nM$. In particular $J^2=0$ if $A$ itself is derived complete.
theorems.proof: The ideal $J$ annihilates the kernel of $M\to\lim_n M/f^nM$. In particular $J^2=0$ if $A$ itself is derived complete.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Nilpotence of the completion kernel
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $A$ is derived complete for $I$ generated by $r$ elements. Put $J=\bigcap_{n\ge1}I^n$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Adic completeness of a reduced derived-complete ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$. Write $\Lambda_I$ for derived completion. Let $A$ be reduced and derived complete for $I$.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to\lim A/I^n$ is an isomorphism, since its kernel is nilpotent and hence zero.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to\lim A/I^n$ is an isomorphism, since its kernel is nilpotent and hence zero.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Pro-isomorphism of Noetherian Koszul and quotient towers
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and let $K_n$ be the Koszul complex on the list of $n$th powers, in degrees $[-r,0]$. Assume $A$ Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The augmentations give an isomorphism of pro-objects from $(K_n)$ to $(A/(f_1^n,\ldots,f_r^n))$ in $D(A)$.
theorems.proof: The augmentations give an isomorphism of pro-objects from $(K_n)$ to $(A/(f_1^n,\ldots,f_r^n))$ in $D(A)$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Noetherian derived completion by the ordinary quotient tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian with ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: For any $K$, the derived limit $\mathbf R\lim_n(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I^n)$ realizes the derived completion functor with its adjunction.
theorems.proof: For any $K$, the derived limit $\mathbf R\lim_n(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I^n)$ realizes the derived completion functor with its adjunction.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Tor exact sequence for Noetherian derived completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian with ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: For any module $M$, $0\to R^1\lim_n\operatorname{Tor}_{i+1}^A(M,A/I^n)\to H^{-i}(\Lambda_I M)\to\lim_n\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(M,A/I^n)\to0$ is exact. The same sequence for $D^-(A)$ uses the cohomology groups of the derived tensor reductions.
theorems.proof: For any module $M$, $0\to R^1\lim_n\operatorname{Tor}_{i+1}^A(M,A/I^n)\to H^{-i}(\Lambda_I M)\to\lim_n\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(M,A/I^n)\to0$ is exact. The same sequence for $D^-(A)$ uses the cohomology groups of the derived tensor reductions.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completion of complexes with finite cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian with ideal $I$. Let $K\in D(A)$ have finite $H^i(K)$ in every degree.
theorems.statement: The cohomology $H^i(\Lambda_I K)$ is the ordinary $I$-adic completion of $H^i(K)$ for every $i$.
theorems.proof: The cohomology $H^i(\Lambda_I K)$ is the ordinary $I$-adic completion of $H^i(K)$ for every $i$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Derived completeness and finiteness of reduction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian with ideal $I$. Suppose $M$ is derived complete and $M/IM$ finite over $A/I$.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is classically complete and finite over $\widehat A$.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is classically complete and finite over $\widehat A$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: When derived completion of a module is ordinary completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian with ideal $I$. Let $M$ be finite and $N$ flat over $A$.
theorems.statement: The derived completion of $M\otimes_A N$ is its ordinary completion in degree zero. This includes $M_f$ for any $f\in A$.
theorems.proof: The derived completion of $M\otimes_A N$ is its ordinary completion in degree zero. This includes $M_f$ for any $f\in A$.

theorems.subject: complex-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Derived completion commutes with tensor by a pseudo-coherent object
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian with ideal $I$. Fix $K\in D^-(A)$ and pseudo-coherent $L\in D(A)$.
theorems.statement: There is an isomorphism $\Lambda_I(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L)\simeq(\Lambda_I K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L$. In particular $L$ may be any finite module in degree zero.
theorems.proof: There is an isomorphism $\Lambda_I(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L)\simeq(\Lambda_I K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L$. In particular $L$ may be any finite module in degree zero.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Décalage can fail to preserve a cone triangle
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a nonunit nonzerodivisor $f\in A$. Use the triangle of the map multiplying by $f$ between copies of $A$ in cohomological degree one.
theorems.statement: Décalage sends its cone to the contractible complex $A\xrightarrow f fA$. On the first two terms the induced map is multiplication by the nonunit $f$ on $fA$, which is not invertible. Thus the image triangle is not distinguished, although the construction commutes with shift up to the standard $f$ factor.
theorems.proof: Décalage sends its cone to the contractible complex $A\xrightarrow f fA$. On the first two terms the induced map is multiplication by the nonunit $f$ on $fA$, which is not invertible. Thus the image triangle is not distinguished, although the construction commutes with shift up to the standard $f$ factor.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Cohomology of décalage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor of $A$, and let $M$ be a cochain complex of $f$-torsion-free $A$-modules.
theorems.statement: Multiplication by $f^i$ identifies $H^i(M)/H^i(M)[f]$ with $H^i(\eta_f M)$.
theorems.proof: Multiplication by $f^i$ identifies $H^i(M)/H^i(M)[f]$ with $H^i(\eta_f M)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Quasi-isomorphism invariance on torsion-free complexes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor of $A$, and let $M$ be a cochain complex of $f$-torsion-free $A$-modules.
theorems.statement: Applying $\eta_f$ to a quasi-isomorphism between such complexes gives a quasi-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Applying $\eta_f$ to a quasi-isomorphism between such complexes gives a quasi-isomorphism.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Existence of derived décalage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$.
theorems.statement: There exists an additive endofunctor $L\eta_f$ of $D(A)$ computed on objects and maps by $\eta_f$ on torsion-free representatives.
theorems.proof: There exists an additive endofunctor $L\eta_f$ of $D(A)$ computed on objects and maps by $\eta_f$ on torsion-free representatives.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Cycle and boundary description of décalage modulo f
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor of $A$, and let $M$ be a cochain complex of $f$-torsion-free $A$-modules.
theorems.statement: Write $Z^i,B^i$ for the cycles and boundaries of $M/f$. There is an exact sequence $0\to B^{i+1}\to(\eta_f M)^i/f\to Z^i\to0$ using $f^i$ to identify the twists. Over $B^i\subset Z^i$ it splits. The resulting terms $B^{i+1}\oplus B^i$ form an acyclic subcomplex and the quotient has terms $H^i(M/f)$.
theorems.proof: Write $Z^i,B^i$ for the cycles and boundaries of $M/f$. There is an exact sequence $0\to B^{i+1}\to(\eta_f M)^i/f\to Z^i\to0$ using $f^i$ to identify the twists. Over $B^i\subset Z^i$ it splits. The resulting terms $B^{i+1}\oplus B^i$ form an acyclic subcomplex and the quotient has terms $H^i(M/f)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Bockstein description of derived décalage modulo f
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor of $A$, and let $M$ be a cochain complex of $f$-torsion-free $A$-modules.
theorems.statement: The canonical map from $\eta_f M\otimes_A A/f$ to the cohomology of the reduction with Bockstein differential is a quasi-isomorphism. The degree-$i$ term on the right is $H^i(M\otimes_A f^iA/f^{i+1}A)$.
theorems.proof: The canonical map from $\eta_f M\otimes_A A/f$ to the cohomology of the reduction with Bockstein differential is a quasi-isomorphism. The degree-$i$ term on the right is $H^i(M\otimes_A f^iA/f^{i+1}A)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Lifting cycles modulo f squared
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor of $A$, and let $M$ be a cochain complex of $f$-torsion-free $A$-modules.
theorems.statement: The reduction from degree-$i$ cycles modulo $f^2$ onto those modulo $f$ is surjective precisely when the degree-$i$ Bockstein is zero. Vanishing of $H^{i+1}(M)[f]$ suffices.
theorems.proof: The reduction from degree-$i$ cycles modulo $f^2$ onto those modulo $f$ is surjective precisely when the degree-$i$ Bockstein is zero. Vanishing of $H^{i+1}(M)[f]$ suffices.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Split coordinate image when cycles lift modulo f squared
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor of $A$, and let $M$ be a cochain complex of $f$-torsion-free $A$-modules. Suppose cycles in degree $i$ lift from modulo $f$ to modulo $f^2$.
theorems.statement: The map $(1,d^i)$ identifies $(\eta_fM)^i/f$ with the direct sum of its two coordinate images in $f^iM^i/f^{i+1}M^i\oplus f^{i+1}M^{i+1}/f^{i+2}M^{i+1}$.
theorems.proof: The map $(1,d^i)$ identifies $(\eta_fM)^i/f$ with the direct sum of its two coordinate images in $f^iM^i/f^{i+1}M^i\oplus f^{i+1}M^{i+1}/f^{i+2}M^{i+1}$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Composition of two décalage operators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f,g$ be nonzerodivisors in $A$ and suppose multiplication by $fg$ is injective on all $M^i$.
theorems.statement: Then $\eta_f\eta_gM=\eta_{fg}M$ as subcomplexes of the localization.
theorems.proof: Then $\eta_f\eta_gM=\eta_{fg}M$ as subcomplexes of the localization.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Flat base change for décalage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor of $A$, and let $M$ be a cochain complex of $f$-torsion-free $A$-modules. Let $A\to B$ be flat and call the image of $f$ in $B$ by $g$.
theorems.statement: The element $g$ acts injectively on $B$ and on every term of $M\otimes_A B$, and $(\eta_f M)\otimes_A B=\eta_g(M\otimes_A B)$.
theorems.proof: The element $g$ acts injectively on $B$ and on every term of $M\otimes_A B$, and $(\eta_f M)\otimes_A B=\eta_g(M\otimes_A B)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Determinantal ideals of equivalent finite free models
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$ and $M$ a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules. Write $I_i$ for the ideal of maximal minors of $(f,d^i)$. Let $N$ be another such model of the same derived object.
theorems.statement: Write $s_i(M)=\sum_{j\ge i}(-1)^{j-i}\operatorname{rk}M^j$. For $m,n\ge0$ satisfying $m+s_i(M)=n+s_i(N)$ one has $f^m I_i(M,f)=f^n I_i(N,f)$.
theorems.proof: Write $s_i(M)=\sum_{j\ge i}(-1)^{j-i}\operatorname{rk}M^j$. For $m,n\ge0$ satisfying $m+s_i(M)=n+s_i(N)$ one has $f^m I_i(M,f)=f^n I_i(N,f)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Unit invariance of the determinantal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$ and $M$ a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules. Write $I_i$ for the ideal of maximal minors of $(f,d^i)$.
theorems.statement: For $u$ a unit, $I_i(M,uf)=I_i(M,f)$ for every $i$.
theorems.proof: For $u$ a unit, $I_i(M,uf)=I_i(M,f)$ for every $i$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Determinantal ideals commute with scalar extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$ and $M$ a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules. Write $I_i$ for the ideal of maximal minors of $(f,d^i)$. Let $A\to B$ carry $f$ to a nonzerodivisor $g$.
theorems.statement: Then $I_i(M,f)B=I_i(M\otimes_A B,g)$.
theorems.proof: Then $I_i(M,f)B=I_i(M\otimes_A B,g)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Principal determinantal ideal at a point of free cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$ and $M$ a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules. Write $I_i$ for the ideal of maximal minors of $(f,d^i)$. Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ where every $H^j(M)_{\mathfrak p}$ is free.
theorems.statement: For each $i$, the localized ideal $(I_i)_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by a power of $f$.
theorems.proof: For each $i$, the localized ideal $(I_i)_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by a power of $f$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Local freeness of décalage from a principal determinantal ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$ and $M$ a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules. Write $I_i$ for the ideal of maximal minors of $(f,d^i)$. Assume $I_i$ principal at the specified degree.
theorems.statement: The module $(\eta_f M)^i$ is locally free of rank $r_i$ and $(1,d^i)$ includes it as a direct summand of $f^iM^i\oplus f^{i+1}M^{i+1}$.
theorems.proof: The module $(\eta_f M)^i$ is locally free of rank $r_i$ and $(1,d^i)$ includes it as a direct summand of $f^iM^i\oplus f^{i+1}M^{i+1}$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Nonflat base change with principal determinantal ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$ and $M$ a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules. Write $I_i$ for the ideal of maximal minors of $(f,d^i)$. Assume every $I_i$ principal and $A\to B$ carries $f$ to a nonzerodivisor $g$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $\eta_f(M)\otimes_A B\cong\eta_g(M\otimes_A B)$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical isomorphism $\eta_f(M)\otimes_A B\cong\eta_g(M\otimes_A B)$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Universal quotient for a split graph to split by coordinates
theorems.hypotheses: Take finite projective modules $M,N_1,N_2$ with split injection $s:M\to N_1\oplus N_2$.
theorems.statement: A finitely generated ideal $J\subset A$ represents the condition that the base-changed image of $s$ be a sum of submodules of the individual target factors. A map $A\to B$ has this property exactly when it factors through $A/J$.
theorems.proof: A finitely generated ideal $J\subset A$ represents the condition that the base-changed image of $s$ be a sum of submodules of the individual target factors. A map $A\to B$ has this property exactly when it factors through $A/J$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Derived invariance of the splitting ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$ and $M$ a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules. Write $I_i$ for the ideal of maximal minors of $(f,d^i)$. Assume all $I_i(M,f)$ principal and let $N$ be a bounded finite free complex representing the same derived object.
theorems.statement: The splitting ideals agree $J_i(M,f)=J_i(N,f)$ in $A/f$ for every $i$.
theorems.proof: The splitting ideals agree $J_i(M,f)=J_i(N,f)$ in $A/f$ for every $i$.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Universal quotient with finite locally free décalage cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a nonzerodivisor in $A$ and $M$ a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules. Write $I_i$ for the ideal of maximal minors of $(f,d^i)$. Assume all $I_i$ principal and set $J=\sum_iJ_i(M,f)$, $C=(A/f)/J$.
theorems.statement: The ideal $J$ is finitely generated and $C$ finitely presented over $A/f$. Its ideal vanishes locally at all primes over $f$ where all Bocksteins vanish, equivalently where all cycles lift modulo $f^2$. This includes such primes with free localized cohomologies of $M$. Every cohomology module of $(\eta_fM)\otimes_A C$ is finite locally free over $C$.
theorems.proof: The ideal $J$ is finitely generated and $C$ finitely presented over $A/f$. Its ideal vanishes locally at all primes over $f$ where all Bocksteins vanish, equivalently where all cycles lift modulo $f^2$. This includes such primes with free localized cohomologies of $M$. Every cohomology module of $(\eta_fM)\otimes_A C$ is finite locally free over $C$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Reconstructing a pseudo-coherent complex over a nilpotent tower
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a tower of rings $A_n$ with limit $A$, and complexes $K_n$ with transition maps identifying $K_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}^{\mathbf L}A_n$ and $K_n$. Assume all ring transitions are onto with locally nilpotent kernels.
