theorems.statement: One has $a^d=-c_d^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}c_i a^i$ in $F[T]/(P)$.
theorems.proof: Evaluate the displayed source equation at the residue class $a$ and divide by the nonzero leading coefficient.
refs: Stacks 09G7 · power basis for an irreducible quotient

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: A real annihilating polynomial for every complex number
theorems.hypotheses: Take $z=a+bi\in\mathbf C$, with $a,b\in\mathbf R$.
theorems.statement: The polynomial $T^2-2aT+a^2+b^2$ vanishes at $z$. Thus $\mathbf C/\mathbf R$ is algebraic.
theorems.proof: The polynomial factors over $\mathbf C$ as $(T-z)(T-\bar z)$.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Transitivity of algebraicity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower with $E/F$ and $L/E$ algebraic.
theorems.statement: The extension $L/F$ is algebraic.
theorems.proof: For $a\in L$ the coefficients of its minimal polynomial over $E$ generate a finite extension $F'$ of $F$. Then $F'(a)/F'$ and $F'(a)/F$ are finite.

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.name: Uniqueness of algebraic closure up to base-field isomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ and $L$ be algebraic closures of the same field $F$.
theorems.statement: There exists an $F$-isomorphism $E\to L$.
theorems.proof: Embed $E$ into $L$ over $F$. Its image is algebraically closed, and $L$ is algebraic over that image, so the embedding is surjective.
refs: Stacks 09GU · embedding in an algebraic closure

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Frobenius preserves the number of distinct roots
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ have characteristic $p>0$, fix an algebraic closure $\overline F$, and let $P\in F[T]$.
theorems.statement: The sets of roots of $P(T^p)$ and $P(T)$ in $\overline F$ are in bijection.
theorems.proof: Frobenius $u\mapsto u^p$ is a bijection on $\overline F$. Its restriction maps the first root set onto the second.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Embeddings correspond to compatible successive roots
theorems.hypotheses: Take the generating tower $K_i=F(a_1,\ldots,a_i)$ of a finite extension with $K_0=F$, $K_n=K$. Let $P_i$ be the minimal polynomial of $a_i$ over $K_{i-1}$, and fix $\overline F$.
theorems.statement: An $F$-embedding $K\to\overline F$ is uniquely determined by successive choices of roots $b_i$ of the coefficientwise images of $P_i$ under the previously chosen embedding of $K_{i-1}$. Each compatible tuple occurs.
theorems.proof: The presentation $K_i\cong K_{i-1}[T]/(P_i)$ extends the preceding embedding uniquely after specifying the image of $T$.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Separability detected at every generator in a finite tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K_i=F(a_1,\ldots,a_i)$ be a generating tower for a finite extension $K/F$ ending at $K$, with $K_0=F$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline F$.
theorems.statement: If every $a_i$ is separable over $K_{i-1}$, the number of $F$-embeddings of $K$ into $\overline F$ equals $[K:F]$ and $K/F$ is separable. If some $a_i$ is inseparable over $K_{i-1}$, that number is strictly smaller.
theorems.proof: Compare the product of the numbers of distinct roots of the successive minimal polynomials with the product of their degrees. Equality characterizes separability of a finite extension.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Transitivity of algebraic separability
theorems.hypotheses: For a tower $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$, assume that $E/F$ and $L/E$ are separable algebraic.
theorems.statement: The extension $L/F$ is separable algebraic.
theorems.proof: Given $a\in L$, the coefficients of its separable minimal polynomial over $E$ lie in a finite separable extension $F'$ of $F$ inside $E$. The minimal polynomial of $a$ over $F'$ divides this separable polynomial. The finite tower criterion applies to $F'(a)/F$.

theorems.subject: field-map
theorems.name: Distinct field embeddings are linearly independent
theorems.hypotheses: Given extensions $K/F$ and $L/F$, let $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n:K\to L$ be distinct $F$-embeddings.
theorems.statement: As functions on $K$, the $\sigma_i$ are linearly independent over $L$.
theorems.proof: Apply independence of distinct multiplicative characters to the underlying multiplicative monoid of $K$ and the field $L$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Separable degree counts embeddings of a finite extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/F$ be finite with a fixed algebraic closure $\overline F$.
theorems.statement: The number of $F$-embeddings $K\to\overline F$ equals $[K:F]_s$.
theorems.proof: The maximal separable subextension has this many embeddings. Each extends uniquely across the purely inseparable remaining extension, since each required root is unique.
refs: Stacks 030K · separable and purely inseparable tower

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Cyclicity from bounds on every torsion subgroup
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an abelian group, viewed as a $\mathbf Z$-module. Suppose $nA=0$ for $n\ge1$ and $|\ker(d:A\to A)|\le d$ for every positive divisor $d$ of $n$.
theorems.statement: The group $A$ is cyclic of order dividing $n$. For a finite subgroup of a field's multiplicative group the required bounds follow from the polynomials $T^d-1$.
theorems.proof: The bound with $d=n$ gives finiteness. If two or more nontrivial invariant factors occur, the torsion killed by the smallest factor $e$ has at least $e^2$ elements.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Trace and norm from two coefficients of the minimal polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be finite and $a\in L$ have monic minimal polynomial $P(T)=T^d+c_1T^{d-1}+\cdots+c_d$. Put $e=[L:K(a)]$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(a)=-ec_1$ and $\operatorname{N}_{L/K}(a)=(-1)^{[L:K]}c_d^e$.
theorems.proof: The characteristic polynomial of multiplication by $a$ is $P^e$. Compare the coefficient of degree $[L:K]-1$ and the constant coefficient.
refs: Stacks 0BIG · characteristic polynomial as a power

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Galois extension over an intermediate field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq K$ be a tower of algebraic extensions with $K/F$ Galois.
theorems.statement: The extension $K/E$ is Galois.
theorems.proof: Both separability and normality pass from $K/F$ to $K/E$.
refs: Stacks 09H2 · separability over an intermediate field
Stacks 09HN · normality over an intermediate field

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: The normal closure of a finite separable extension is Galois
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be finite separable and let $M$ be its normal closure over $K$ inside a fixed algebraic closure.
theorems.statement: The extension $M/K$ is finite Galois.
theorems.proof: The normal closure is generated by conjugates of finitely many separable generators of $L/K$. They remain separable over $K$, and normality holds by construction.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: The restriction sequence of finite Galois groups
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$, with $L/K$ and $M/K$ both finite Galois.
theorems.statement: Restriction gives the exact sequence $1\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/M)\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\to\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)\to1$ of finite groups.
theorems.proof: Normality preserves $M$ and gives extensions of its $K$-automorphisms to $L$. The automorphisms fixing $M$ give the kernel.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Universal property of the Krull topology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be Galois, give $L$ the discrete topology, and give $G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ the coarsest topology making evaluation $G\times L\to L$ continuous. Let $X$ be a topological space.
theorems.statement: A function $u:X\to G$ is continuous exactly when $(x,a)\mapsto u(x)(a)$ is continuous on $X\times L$. In this topology $G$ is a profinite group.
theorems.proof: Continuity on the discrete slices is continuity of every coordinate evaluation. These coordinates generate the Krull topology, which is the inverse limit topology from finite Galois subextensions.
refs: Stacks 0BU2 · inverse system of finite Galois groups

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Continuous surjection onto the group of a Galois subextension
theorems.hypotheses: Take a tower $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$ with $L/K$ and $M/K$ Galois. Give the Galois groups their Krull topologies.
theorems.statement: Restriction $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\to\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)$ is a continuous surjective homomorphism.
theorems.proof: Normality allows lifting every $K$-automorphism of $M$. The inverse image of a pointwise stabilizer of a finite subset of $M$ is the pointwise stabilizer of that subset in the larger group.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Galois extensions as unions and Galois groups as inverse limits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be Galois. Order its finite Galois subextensions $L_\lambda/K$ by inclusion and set $G_\lambda=\operatorname{Gal}(L_\lambda/K)$.
theorems.statement: These subextensions form a directed system whose union is $L$. Restriction gives an inverse system of finite groups with surjective transitions and a topological group isomorphism $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\cong\varprojlim_\lambda G_\lambda$. Every projection is continuous and surjective.
theorems.proof: Each finite subset of $L$ lies in a finite Galois subextension. Compatible finite restrictions glue to an automorphism of the union. Stabilizers of the finite subextensions give a neighbourhood basis at the identity.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Transcendence degree of the field generated by e and π
theorems.hypotheses: Consider $\mathbf Q(e,\pi)\subset\mathbf R$. Both generators are transcendental over $\mathbf Q$.
theorems.statement: Its transcendence degree is $1$ or $2$. It is $2$ exactly when the two generators are algebraically independent. The source records their algebraic independence as an open question.
theorems.proof: Either generator alone gives a transcendence-degree-one subfield. The two-element generating set bounds the transcendence degree above by two.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Compact Riemann surfaces and one-variable function fields
theorems.hypotheses: Use compact connected Riemann surfaces with nonconstant holomorphic maps, and finitely generated field extensions of $\mathbf C$ of transcendence degree one with $\mathbf C$-embeddings.
theorems.statement: The assignment $X\mapsto\mathbf C(X)$ on objects and pullback on functions is a contravariant equivalence of these categories. Over an algebraically closed field $k$, smooth projective integral curves and nonconstant morphisms have the analogous correspondence with one-variable function fields over $k$.
theorems.proof: The source cites Forster for compact Riemann surfaces. In the algebraic statement, a one-variable function field has a smooth projective model, and field embeddings correspond to dominant rational maps, which extend to morphisms on the smooth proper models.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: A Jacobian witness at a smooth prime
theorems.hypotheses: Write $A=P/I$ for a finite polynomial presentation with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Suppose $R\to A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: After reordering generators and variables, some $a\notin\mathfrak q$ is a multiple of a $c$-minor on the first $c$ equations and $aI\subseteq(f_1,\ldots,f_c)+I^2$ using any lift of $a$ to $P$.
theorems.proof: After reordering generators and variables, some $a\notin\mathfrak q$ is a multiple of a $c$-minor on the first $c$ equations and $aI\subseteq(f_1,\ldots,f_c)+I^2$ using any lift of $a$ to $P$.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Jacobian minors and a scalar splitting up to a power
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $A=P/I$, $c$ chosen equations and a scalar $a\in A$. Let $D:A^c\to I/I^2\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_PA$ send basis vectors to the differentials of the chosen equations.
theorems.statement: Membership of $a$ in the ideal of $c$-minors of $D$ gives an $A$-linear $v$ with $vD=a\,\mathrm{id}$. Conversely such a $v$ gives membership of $a^c$ in the minors ideal by taking determinants.
theorems.proof: Membership of $a$ in the ideal of $c$-minors of $D$ gives an $A$-linear $v$ with $vD=a\,\mathrm{id}$. Conversely such a $v$ gives membership of $a^c$ in the minors ideal by taking determinants.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Elkik’s description of the singular ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Take $A$ finitely presented over $R$.
theorems.statement: The radical of the ideal generated by the elementary standard elements equals $H_{A/R}$. The strictly standard elements generate an ideal with the same radical.
theorems.proof: The radical of the ideal generated by the elementary standard elements equals $H_{A/R}$. The strictly standard elements generate an ideal with the same radical.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Standard elements persist after arbitrary base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be finitely presented over $R$, and take a homomorphism $R\to T$.
theorems.statement: If $a$ is elementary standard, its image in $A\otimes_R T$ is elementary standard over $T$. The corresponding assertion holds separately for strictly standard elements.
theorems.proof: If $a$ is elementary standard, its image in $A\otimes_R T$ is elementary standard over $T$. The corresponding assertion holds separately for strictly standard elements.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smooth factorization when the singular ideal becomes the unit ideal
theorems.hypotheses: For $R\to A\to L$ let $A$ be finitely presented over $R$ and $H_{A/R}L=L$.
theorems.statement: The map to $L$ factors as $A\to B\to L$ with $B$ smooth over $R$.
theorems.proof: The map to $L$ factors as $A\to B\to L$ with $B$ smooth over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: A retract with improved conormal and differential modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finitely presented $R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: There is a finite type map $A\to C$ with an $A$-algebra retraction. Whenever $R\to A_a$ is lci, $C_a$ is smooth over $A_a$ and has a finite-variable polynomial presentation over $R$ with free conormal module. Wherever $R\to A_a$ is smooth, $\Omega_{C_a/R}$ is free over $C_a$.
theorems.proof: There is a finite type map $A\to C$ with an $A$-algebra retraction. Whenever $R\to A_a$ is lci, $C_a$ is smooth over $A_a$ and has a finite-variable polynomial presentation over $R$ with free conormal module. Wherever $R\to A_a$ is smooth, $\Omega_{C_a/R}$ is free over $C_a$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting smooth and syntomic algebras across any surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Take a surjection $R\to R_0$ with kernel $I$ and an $R_0$-algebra $A_0$.
theorems.statement: If $A_0$ is smooth over $R_0$ there exists a smooth $R$-algebra $A$ with $A/IA\simeq A_0$. The same assertion holds with syntomicity in both places.
theorems.proof: If $A_0$ is smooth over $R_0$ there exists a smooth $R$-algebra $A$ with $A/IA\simeq A_0$. The same assertion holds with syntomicity in both places.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Syntomic algebras as retracts of relative complete intersections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be syntomic over $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a smooth split $A$-algebra $C$ that is a global relative complete intersection over $R$. It admits a presentation on $n$ variables with $c$ equations, flat over $R$, with nonempty fibres of pure dimension $n-c$.
theorems.proof: There is a smooth split $A$-algebra $C$ that is a global relative complete intersection over $R$. It admits a presentation on $n$ variables with $c$ equations, flat over $R$, with nonempty fibres of pure dimension $n-c$.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Smooth algebras as retracts of standard smooth algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Take a smooth $R$-algebra $A$.
theorems.statement: There is a smooth $A$-algebra $B$ with an $A$-algebra retraction such that $B$ admits a standard smooth presentation over $R$. In that presentation a square Jacobian minor of size the number of equations is a unit.
theorems.proof: There is a smooth $A$-algebra $B$ with an $A$-algebra retraction such that $B$ admits a standard smooth presentation over $R$. In that presentation a square Jacobian minor of size the number of equations is a unit.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Prescribing variables in a standard smooth presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be standard smooth over $R$ and fix $n$ distinct elements of $A$.
theorems.statement: A standard smooth presentation can include these elements as the first $n$ coordinate classes, with $c\ge n$ equations and the Jacobian minor for the first $c$ variables invertible.
theorems.proof: A standard smooth presentation can include these elements as the first $n$ coordinate classes, with $c\ge n$ equations and the Jacobian minor for the first $c$ variables invertible.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Power converses for standard-element tests
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $a$ in a finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$.
theorems.statement: When $A_a$ is smooth with stably free $\Omega_{A_a/R}$, all sufficiently high powers of $a$ are strictly standard in $A$. When $A_a$ is standard smooth, all sufficiently high powers are elementary standard.
theorems.proof: When $A_a$ is smooth with stably free $\Omega_{A_a/R}$, all sufficiently high powers of $a$ are strictly standard in $A$. When $A_a$ is standard smooth, all sufficiently high powers are elementary standard.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Functoriality of the affine Néron blowup
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$.
theorems.statement: For $a\notin\mathfrak p$, the blowup of $A_a$ is $(A')_a$. For a surjection $B\to A$ of flat finite type $R$-algebras with kernel $I$, the blowup of $A$ is the quotient of $B'/IB'$ by its $\pi$-power torsion, using the centre induced on $B$.
theorems.proof: For $a\notin\mathfrak p$, the blowup of $A_a$ is $(A')_a$. For a surjection $B\to A$ of flat finite type $R$-algebras with kernel $I$, the blowup of $A$ is the quotient of $B'/IB'$ by its $\pi$-power torsion, using the centre induced on $B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Differentials after blowing up a smooth valuation centre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$. Assume smoothness at $\mathfrak p$ and separability of the residue extension of the DVRs. Put $c=\dim((A/\pi A)_{\mathfrak p})$.
theorems.statement: Then $A'$ is smooth over $R$ at $\mathfrak p'$. There is an exact sequence $0\to\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_AA'_{\mathfrak p'}\to(\Omega_{A'/R})_{\mathfrak p'}\to((A'/\pi A')_{\mathfrak p'})^c\to0$.
theorems.proof: Then $A'$ is smooth over $R$ at $\mathfrak p'$. There is an exact sequence $0\to\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_AA'_{\mathfrak p'}\to(\Omega_{A'/R})_{\mathfrak p'}\to((A'/\pi A')_{\mathfrak p'})^c\to0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Néron smoothness test via a free differential cokernel
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$. Assume $A$ smooth at $\mathfrak q$, and choose a surjection $B\to A$ of $R$-algebras with kernel $I$, with $B$ smooth over $R$ at the preimage of $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: If the cokernel of $(I/I^2)\otimes_A V\to\Omega_{B/R}\otimes_BV$ is free over $V$, then $A$ is smooth over $R$ at $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: If the cokernel of $(I/I^2)\otimes_A V\to\Omega_{B/R}\otimes_BV$ is free over $V$, then $A$ is smooth over $R$ at $\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Finite iteration of affine Néron blowups
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq V$ be DVRs of ramification index one with common uniformizer $\pi$. Factor $R\to A\to V$ with $A$ flat of finite type. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker(A\to V)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the preimage of the maximal ideal of $V$. Let $A'=A[\mathfrak p/\pi]$ with the induced primes $\mathfrak q',\mathfrak p'$. Assume $A$ smooth at $\mathfrak q$ and the residue extension of the DVRs separable.
theorems.statement: After finitely many blowups at the successive valuation centres the resulting algebra is smooth over $R$ at its centre.
theorems.proof: After finitely many blowups at the successive valuation centres the resulting algebra is smooth over $R$ at its centre.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Ind-smoothness for an extension of DVRs
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\subseteq V$ are DVRs of ramification index one and both their residue-field extension and their fraction-field extension are separable.
theorems.statement: Then $V$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras. The field separability assumptions allow extensions of positive transcendence degree.
theorems.proof: Then $V$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras. The field separability assumptions allow extensions of positive transcendence degree.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A first lift across a square-zero ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I^2=0$ in $R$, assume $L/IL$ is ind-smooth over $R/I$, and fix a finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$ mapping to $L$.
theorems.statement: The map factors over $R$ as $A\to B/J\to L$ with $B$ smooth over $R$ and $J$ a finitely generated ideal contained in $IB$.
theorems.proof: The map factors over $R$ as $A\to B/J\to L$ with $B$ smooth over $R$ and $J$ a finitely generated ideal contained in $IB$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Eliminating the remaining square-zero relations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I^2=0$ in $R$, let $L$ be flat over $R$ with $L/IL$ ind-smooth over $R/I$, and let $B\to L$ be an $R$-algebra map from a smooth algebra. Suppose $J\subseteq IB$ is a finitely generated ideal killed in $L$.
theorems.statement: There is a factorization $B\to B'\to L$ with $B'$ smooth over $R$ such that $J$ already maps to zero in $B'$.
theorems.proof: There is a factorization $B\to B'\to L$ with $B'$ smooth over $R$ such that $J$ already maps to zero in $B'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Ind-smoothness lifts across a nilpotent base ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $R\to L$ is flat, $I\subseteq R$ is nilpotent and $L/IL$ is ind-smooth over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: Then $L$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.
theorems.proof: Then $L$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Lifting a finite presentation and its smooth locus from a thickening
theorems.hypotheses: Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Let $R$ be Noetherian, $R\to L$ a map satisfying $E_R(\pi)$ and $E_L(\pi)$, and $R/\pi^2R\to \bar C\to L/\pi^2L$ a diagram with $\bar C$ finitely presented over $R/\pi^2R$.
theorems.statement: There are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $D\to L$ and a map $\bar C\to D/\pi D$ compatible modulo $\pi$. The map $R\to D$ is smooth off $V(\pi)$ and at each prime in $V(\pi)$ mapping to the smooth locus of $\bar C$ over $R/\pi^2R$. The map $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to D/\pi D$ is smooth at every prime over that same locus.
theorems.proof: There are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $D\to L$ and a map $\bar C\to D/\pi D$ compatible modulo $\pi$. The map $R\to D$ is smooth off $V(\pi)$ and at each prime in $V(\pi)$ mapping to the smooth locus of $\bar C$ over $R/\pi^2R$. The map $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to D/\pi D$ is smooth at every prime over that same locus.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Improving the singular ideal from a fourth-order retraction
theorems.hypotheses: Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Let $R$ be Noetherian, $A$ finitely presented over $R$ and $A\to L$ given. Assume $E_L(\pi)$, with $\pi\in R$ strictly standard in $A$, and an $R/\pi^4R$-algebra retraction $A/\pi^4A\to R/\pi^4R$ compatible with the map to $L/\pi^4L$.
theorems.statement: There is a factorization $A\to B\to L$ over $R$ with $B$ finitely presented and $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi^2)/\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi))B\subseteq H_{B/R}$.
theorems.proof: There is a factorization $A\to B\to L$ over $R$ with $B$ finitely presented and $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi^2)/\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi))B\subseteq H_{B/R}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Simultaneous factorization preserving two smooth loci
theorems.hypotheses: Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Let $R$ be Noetherian with $E_R(\pi)$ and $E_L(\pi)$, and let $A,D$ be finitely presented $R$-algebras mapping to $L$. Assume $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ and a map $A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$ over $R$ commutes with the maps to $L/\pi^4L$.
theorems.statement: There is a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ mapping to $L$ through which both original maps factor, with $H_{D/R}B\subseteq H_{B/D}$ and $H_{D/R}B\subseteq H_{B/R}$.
theorems.proof: There is a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ mapping to $L$ through which both original maps factor, with $H_{D/R}B\subseteq H_{B/D}$ and $H_{D/R}B\subseteq H_{B/R}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Controlling the singular ideal from an eighth-order factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Let $R$ be Noetherian with $E_R(\pi)$ and $E_L(\pi)$. Let $A$ be finitely presented over $R$, mapping to $L$, with $\pi$ strictly standard in $A$. Factor $A/\pi^8A\to\bar C\to L/\pi^8L$ over $R/\pi^8R$ with $\bar C$ finitely presented over that ring.
theorems.statement: The given map factors as $A\to B\to L$ with $B$ finitely presented over $R$, $R_\pi\to B_\pi$ smooth, and the extension of $H_{\bar C/(R/\pi^8R)}$ to $L/\pi^8L$ contained in the image of $\sqrt{H_{B/R}L}$ in that quotient.
theorems.proof: The given map factors as $A\to B\to L$ with $B$ finitely presented over $R$, $R_\pi\to B_\pi$ smooth, and the extension of $H_{\bar C/(R/\pi^8R)}$ to $L/\pi^8L$ contained in the image of $\sqrt{H_{B/R}L}$ in that quotient.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: The global desingularization problem
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a regular homomorphism $R\to L$ of Noetherian rings.
theorems.statement: In this situation the condition called PT asks that $L$ be a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras. The assertion that this condition holds is Popescu's theorem, Tag 07GC.
theorems.proof: In this situation the condition called PT asks that $L$ be a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras. The assertion that this condition holds is Popescu's theorem, Tag 07GC.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Products of two desingularization problems
theorems.hypotheses: For $i=1,2$ let $R_i\to L_i$ be regular homomorphisms of Noetherian rings and suppose each $L_i$ is ind-smooth over $R_i$.
theorems.statement: The product $L_1\times L_2$ is ind-smooth over $R_1\times R_2$.
theorems.proof: The product $L_1\times L_2$ is ind-smooth over $R_1\times R_2$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Descending a smooth factorization from a localized base
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R\to A\to L$ with $A$ finitely presented over $R$ and a multiplicative subset $S$ of $R$. Assume $S^{-1}A\to S^{-1}L$ factors through a smooth $S^{-1}R$-algebra.
theorems.statement: Then $A\to L$ factors through a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ in which some $s\in S$ becomes elementary standard over $R$.
theorems.proof: Then $A\to L$ factors through a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ in which some $s\in S$ becomes elementary standard over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Reduction of global desingularization to field bases
theorems.hypotheses: Assume every geometrically regular Noetherian algebra over every field is a filtered colimit of smooth algebras over that field.
theorems.statement: Every regular homomorphism $R\to L$ between Noetherian rings then exhibits $L$ as a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.
theorems.proof: Every regular homomorphism $R\to L$ between Noetherian rings then exhibits $L$ as a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Lifting a resolution through successive eighth powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $A$ finitely presented over $R$, and $A\to L$ an $R$-algebra map with a specified prime $\mathfrak q$ of $L$. For every such algebra $B$ over $R$ mapping to $L$, put $h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}L}$. A resolution at $\mathfrak q$ is a factorization through finitely presented $B$ with $h_A\subseteq h_B$ and $h_B\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Fix elements $\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_r$ of $R$, $r\ge1$, landing in $\mathfrak q$ and strictly standard in $A$ over $R$. Put $J_i=(\pi_1^8,\ldots,\pi_i^8)$ and $J_0=0$. Assume $E_{R/J_{i-1}}(\pi_i)$ and $E_{L/J_{i-1}L}(\pi_i)$ for every $i$.
theorems.statement: A resolution of the induced problem over $R/J_r$ at $\mathfrak q/J_rL$ implies a resolution of the original problem at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: A resolution of the induced problem over $R/J_r$ at $\mathfrak q/J_rL$ implies a resolution of the original problem at $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Descending a smooth neighbourhood from a localized resolution
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $A$ finitely presented over $R$, and $A\to L$ an $R$-algebra map with a specified prime $\mathfrak q$ of $L$. For every such algebra $B$ over $R$ mapping to $L$, put $h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}L}$. A resolution at $\mathfrak q$ is a factorization through finitely presented $B$ with $h_A\subseteq h_B$ and $h_B\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be minimal over $h_A$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$, and assume the localized problem $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to L_{\mathfrak q}$ at its specified prime $\mathfrak q L_{\mathfrak q}$ admits a resolution.
theorems.statement: One obtains a factorization through a finitely presented $R$-algebra $C$ with $H_{C/R}L\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: One obtains a factorization through a finitely presented $R$-algebra $C$ with $H_{C/R}L\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Descending a resolution at a prime of height zero
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $A$ finitely presented over $R$, and $A\to L$ an $R$-algebra map with a specified prime $\mathfrak q$ of $L$. For every such algebra $B$ over $R$ mapping to $L$, put $h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}L}$. A resolution at $\mathfrak q$ is a factorization through finitely presented $B$ with $h_A\subseteq h_B$ and $h_B\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be minimal over $h_A$ with $\dim L_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Assume the localized problem $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to L_{\mathfrak q}$ at $\mathfrak q L_{\mathfrak q}$ is resolvable.
theorems.statement: There is a resolution over $R$ at $\mathfrak q$, including the containment $h_A\subseteq h_B$.
theorems.proof: There is a resolution over $R$ at $\mathfrak q$, including the containment $h_A\subseteq h_B$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Ogoma’s simultaneous kernel stabilization after clearing a denominator
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be finite over a Noetherian ring $A$, $S\subseteq A$ multiplicative, and $\pi\in A$. Assume the kernels of multiplication by $\pi$ and by $\pi^2$ agree on $S^{-1}M$.
theorems.statement: There exists $s\in S$ such that, for every $n>0$, the kernels of multiplication by $s^n\pi$ and by $(s^n\pi)^2$ already agree on $M$.
theorems.proof: There exists $s\in S$ such that, for every $n>0$, the kernels of multiplication by $s^n\pi$ and by $(s^n\pi)^2$ already agree on $M$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Local parameters with stabilized annihilators
theorems.hypotheses: Write $E_T(\pi)$ for the equality $\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_T(\pi^2)$. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak q$ in a Noetherian ring $L$, with $\mathfrak q$ prime, $L_{\mathfrak q}$ regular local of dimension $d$, and $\mathfrak q^nL_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq IL_{\mathfrak q}$ for some $n>0$. Prescribe $e>0$.
theorems.statement: There are $\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_d\in L$ generating $\mathfrak q L_{\mathfrak q}$ after localization, and a common $N>0$ with $\pi_i^N\in I$ for all $i$. For each $i$, $E_{L/(\pi_1^e,\ldots,\pi_{i-1}^e)}(\pi_i)$ holds.
theorems.proof: There are $\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_d\in L$ generating $\mathfrak q L_{\mathfrak q}$ after localization, and a common $N>0$ with $\pi_i^N\in I$ for all $i$. For each $i$, $E_{L/(\pi_1^e,\ldots,\pi_{i-1}^e)}(\pi_i)$ holds.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local desingularization with separable residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $A$ finitely presented over $R$, and $A\to L$ an $R$-algebra map with a specified prime $\mathfrak q$ of $L$. For every such algebra $B$ over $R$ mapping to $L$, put $h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}L}$. A resolution at $\mathfrak q$ is a factorization through finitely presented $B$ with $h_A\subseteq h_B$ and $h_B\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Take $R=k$ a field and $L$ Noetherian. Suppose $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $h_A$, $L_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is separable over $k$.
theorems.statement: The specified problem admits a resolution at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: The specified problem admits a resolution at $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Artinian approximation in positive characteristic
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ have characteristic $p>0$ and $(L,\mathfrak m,K)$ be a local Artinian $k$-algebra. Suppose the first homology of the cotangent complex of the residue field satisfies $\dim_K H_1(L_{K/k})<\infty$.
theorems.statement: The algebra $L$ is a filtered colimit of local Artinian $k$-algebras $B$ essentially of finite type over $k$ for which $B\to L$ is flat and $\mathfrak m_B L=\mathfrak m$.
theorems.proof: The algebra $L$ is a filtered colimit of local Artinian $k$-algebras $B$ essentially of finite type over $k$ for which $B\to L$ is flat and $\mathfrak m_B L=\mathfrak m$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: An essentially smooth model of a prescribed finite set of jets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $L$ a Noetherian geometrically regular $k$-algebra, $\mathfrak q$ a prime, $n\ge1$, and $E$ a finite subset of $T=L_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n L_{\mathfrak q}$.
theorems.statement: There is a map from a finite polynomial algebra $P$ over $k$ to $L$ such that, for $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap P$, the map $P_{\mathfrak p}\to L_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat and $\mathfrak p L_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q L_{\mathfrak q}$. The induced map $P_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nP_{\mathfrak p}\to T$ factors through a local Artinian ring $D$ by an essentially smooth local map followed by a flat local map whose image contains $E$.
theorems.proof: There is a map from a finite polynomial algebra $P$ over $k$ to $L$ such that, for $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap P$, the map $P_{\mathfrak p}\to L_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat and $\mathfrak p L_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q L_{\mathfrak q}$. The induced map $P_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nP_{\mathfrak p}\to T$ factors through a local Artinian ring $D$ by an essentially smooth local map followed by a flat local map whose image contains $E$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Adjoining a power of a unit to a jet model
theorems.hypotheses: Take a field $k$ in positive characteristic, a geometrically regular Noetherian $k$-algebra $L$, a prime $\mathfrak q$, $n\ge1$ and $T=L_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n L_{\mathfrak q}$. Let $P\to L$ be a polynomial model in finitely many variables as in Tag 07FH, with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap P$, flat $P_{\mathfrak p}\to L_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak p L_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q L_{\mathfrak q}$. Fix its local Artinian factorization $P_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nP_{\mathfrak p}\to D\to T$, first essentially smooth and then flat.
theorems.statement: For each $\lambda\in L\setminus\mathfrak q$ there exists a further factorization $D\to D'\to T$ by an essentially smooth map of local Artinian rings followed by a flat map whose image contains the residue of $\lambda^a$ for some integer $a>0$.
theorems.proof: For each $\lambda\in L\setminus\mathfrak q$ there exists a further factorization $D\to D'\to T$ by an essentially smooth map of local Artinian rings followed by a flat map whose image contains the residue of $\lambda^a$ for some integer $a>0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local desingularization over a field in positive characteristic
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $A$ finitely presented over $R$, and $A\to L$ an $R$-algebra map with a specified prime $\mathfrak q$ of $L$. For every such algebra $B$ over $R$ mapping to $L$, put $h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}L}$. A resolution at $\mathfrak q$ is a factorization through finitely presented $B$ with $h_A\subseteq h_B$ and $h_B\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Take $R=k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$ and $L$ Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$. Suppose $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $h_A$.
theorems.statement: The specified problem admits a resolution at $\mathfrak q$.
theorems.proof: The specified problem admits a resolution at $\mathfrak q$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Approximation of a formal solution in a pointed étale neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local G-ring. Fix finitely many polynomial equations in finitely many variables over $R$, a solution in $\widehat R$, and an integer $N\ge1$.
theorems.statement: There is an étale $R$-algebra $R'$ with a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ over $\mathfrak m$ inducing an isomorphism on residue fields, and a solution in $R'$ agreeing with the chosen one modulo $(\mathfrak m')^N$ in the canonically identified local completions.
theorems.proof: There is an étale $R$-algebra $R'$ with a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ over $\mathfrak m$ inducing an isomorphism on residue fields, and a solution in $R'$ agreeing with the chosen one modulo $(\mathfrak m')^N$ in the canonically identified local completions.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Elements of the completion lying in the henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. For the algebraicity criterion assume further that $R$ is a domain and a G-ring, and write $K$ for its fraction field.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $R^h\to\widehat R$ is injective. Under the additional hypotheses its image consists exactly of the elements satisfying a nonzero polynomial equation with coefficients in $R$, equivalently algebraic over $K$ after extending scalars to $K$.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $R^h\to\widehat R$ is injective. Under the additional hypotheses its image consists exactly of the elements satisfying a nonzero polynomial equation with coefficients in $R$, equivalently algebraic over $K$ after extending scalars to $K$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Algebraic approximation at a nonclosed prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $\mathfrak p$ a prime for which $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a G-ring. Fix a solution of a finite system of polynomials over $R$ in the completion of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $N\ge1$.
theorems.statement: There are an étale $R$-algebra $R'$, a prime $\mathfrak p'$ above $\mathfrak p$ with unchanged residue field, and a solution in $R'$ agreeing with the original modulo $(\mathfrak p')^N$ in the identified completed local rings.
theorems.proof: There are an étale $R$-algebra $R'$, a prime $\mathfrak p'$ above $\mathfrak p$ with unchanged residue field, and a solution in $R'$ agreeing with the original modulo $(\mathfrak p')^N$ in the identified completed local rings.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Approximation for a Noetherian henselian pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be henselian with $A$ Noetherian and $\widehat A$ its $I$-adic completion. Assume either that $A\to\widehat A$ is regular, that $A$ is a G-ring, or that $(A,I)$ is the henselization of a pair $(B,J)$ with $B$ a Noetherian G-ring.
theorems.statement: For any finite system of polynomial equations over $A$, every solution in $\widehat A$ and every $N\ge1$, some solution in $A$ agrees with the specified one modulo $I^N\widehat A$.
theorems.proof: For any finite system of polynomial equations over $A$, every solution in $\widehat A$ and every $N\ge1$, some solution in $A$ agrees with the specified one modulo $I^N\widehat A$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Reduced ring and its affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: The ring $R$ is reduced if and only if the scheme $X$ is reduced. One direction uses that localizations of reduced rings are reduced; the other tests global sections.
theorems.proof: The ring $R$ is reduced if and only if the scheme $X$ is reduced. One direction uses that localizations of reduced rings are reduced; the other tests global sections.
refs: Stacks 01J2 · reducedness of an affine scheme

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Integral domain and its affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: $R$ is a domain if and only if $X$ is integral. The nonzero requirement on $R$ corresponds to the nonempty requirement for an irreducible scheme.
theorems.proof: $R$ is a domain if and only if $X$ is integral. The nonzero requirement on $R$ corresponds to the nonempty requirement for an irreducible scheme.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Noetherian ring and its affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: $R$ is Noetherian if and only if $X$ is a Noetherian scheme. This tests the ringed space and does not follow from the topology alone.
theorems.proof: $R$ is Noetherian if and only if $X$ is a Noetherian scheme. This tests the ringed space and does not follow from the topology alone.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Zero dimensionality and a profinite affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: The Zariski space of $X$ is profinite exactly when every prime of $R$ is maximal. Indeed the affine scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so its underlying space is spectral; closed points correspond to maximal ideals.
theorems.proof: The Zariski space of $X$ is profinite exactly when every prime of $R$ is maximal. Indeed the affine scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so its underlying space is spectral; closed points correspond to maximal ideals.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Absolute flatness, reducedness and a profinite spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: $R$ is absolutely flat exactly when $R$ is reduced and the Zariski space of $X$ is profinite. Profinite topology alone cannot detect nilpotent elements of the coordinate ring.
theorems.proof: $R$ is absolutely flat exactly when $R$ is reduced and the Zariski space of $X$ is profinite. Profinite topology alone cannot detect nilpotent elements of the coordinate ring.
refs: Stacks 01J3 · reduced closed subscheme on a given closed subset

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Regular ring and its affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Assume that $R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: Regularity of $R$ (each $R_{\mathfrak p}$ regular local) is equivalent to regularity of $X$.
theorems.proof: Regularity of $R$ (each $R_{\mathfrak p}$ regular local) is equivalent to regularity of $X$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite ring map and its affine morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with identity and put $f=\operatorname{Spec}(A\leftarrow R):\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: $A$ is finite as an $R$-module if and only if $f$ is finite.
theorems.proof: $A$ is finite as an $R$-module if and only if $f$ is finite.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite type ring map and its affine morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with identity and put $f=\operatorname{Spec}(A\leftarrow R):\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra if and only if $f$ is of finite type; the morphism of affine schemes is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra if and only if $f$ is of finite type; the morphism of affine schemes is quasi-compact.
refs: Stacks 01T1 · definition of finite type morphism

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat ring map and its affine morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with identity and put $f=\operatorname{Spec}(A\leftarrow R):\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: $A$ is flat as an $R$-module if and only if $f$ is flat. Flatness of the morphism is checked on local rings, or equivalently on affine charts.
theorems.proof: $A$ is flat as an $R$-module if and only if $f$ is flat. Flatness of the morphism is checked on local rings, or equivalently on affine charts.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étale ring map and its affine morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with identity and put $f=\operatorname{Spec}(A\leftarrow R):\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.statement: $R\to A$ is étale if and only if $f$ is étale. The algebraic property is local on the source and target, and local finite presentation is part of the geometric definition.
theorems.proof: $R\to A$ is étale if and only if $f$ is étale. The algebraic property is local on the source and target, and local finite presentation is part of the geometric definition.

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Every set occurs in the hierarchy
theorems.hypotheses: Work in ZFC and fix a set $x$.
theorems.statement: There exists an ordinal $\alpha$ with $x\in V_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Well-founded recursion defines the rank of $x$ from the ranks of its elements. Transfinite induction gives $x\in V_{\operatorname{rank}(x)+1}$.
refs: William Weiss, An Introduction to Set Theory, Theorem 40 (exhaustion by ranks)
Stacks 000C · existence of a rank stage

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Ordinals of arbitrarily large cofinality
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\kappa$ be a cardinal in ZFC.
theorems.statement: Some ordinal $\beta$ satisfies $\operatorname{cf}(\beta)>\kappa$.
theorems.proof: Use $\omega$ when $\kappa$ is finite. For infinite $\kappa$, a cofinal subset of $\kappa^+$ of size at most $\kappa$ would express $\kappa^+$ as a union of at most $\kappa$ sets of size at most $\kappa$.
refs: Stacks 05N3 · ordinal of cofinality greater than a given cardinal

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Simultaneous reflection of a finite list
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite list of first-order formulas $\phi_i$ of set theory and a set $M_0$. The assertion is a theorem scheme for each fixed list.
theorems.statement: Some $M\supseteq M_0$ satisfies $\phi_i(\bar x)\leftrightarrow\phi_i^M(\bar x)$ for all tuples in $M$ and each listed formula.
theorems.proof: Close the finite collection under subformulas and take a rank segment closed under witnesses to its existential subformulas. Induction on formulas gives absoluteness.
refs: William Weiss, An Introduction to Set Theory, Theorem 49 and its proof (Lévy reflection)
Stacks 000G · simultaneous reflection over a set containing the parameters

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Reflection at a limit level
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite list of first-order formulas $\phi_i$ of set theory and a set $M_0$. The assertion is a theorem scheme for each fixed list.
theorems.statement: The reflecting $M$ may be chosen to be $V_\alpha$ for a nonzero limit ordinal $\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Starting above the ranks of all prescribed parameters, iterate the bounds on witness ranks and take the supremum of the resulting increasing sequence.
refs: William Weiss, An Introduction to Set Theory, Theorem 49 and its proof (Lévy reflection)
Stacks 000G · choice of a reflecting limit rank

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Set of representatives for schemes of bounded size
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a cardinal $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: There is a set of schemes containing a representative of every isomorphism class of schemes of size at most $\kappa$.
theorems.proof: Encode affine charts, their coordinate rings and gluing data on sets of bounded cardinality.
refs: Stacks 000I · set of isomorphic representatives for bounded-size schemes

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Inclusion of a prescribed set of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Given a set $S_0$ of schemes, there exists one limit ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 000J simultaneously. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ for the full rank subcategory.
theorems.statement: Every member of $S_0$ is an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Iterate rank bounds for representatives and countable diagrams, then take a limit at a stage of uncountable cofinality.
refs: Stacks 000J · (1) inclusion of the prescribed set

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Size closure of a rank subcategory of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Given a set $S_0$ of schemes, there exists one limit ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 000J simultaneously. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ for the full rank subcategory.
theorems.statement: If $S$ belongs to $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ and $\operatorname{size}(T)\le B_{\rm Sch}(\operatorname{size}(S))$, then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Iterate rank bounds for representatives and countable diagrams, then take a limit at a stage of uncountable cofinality.

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Limit comparison for schemes · ambient existence implies internal existence
theorems.hypotheses: Given a set $S_0$ of schemes, there exists one limit ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 000J simultaneously. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ for the full rank subcategory. The diagram takes values in that subcategory. Its indexing category has at most countably many objects and at most countable hom-sets.
theorems.statement: Existence of the ambient limit implies existence of the limit in the full rank subcategory.
theorems.proof: Apply Stacks 000J to the chosen rank subcategory and countable diagram. The choice of the rank segment is essential.
refs: Stacks 000J · (3) ambient existence implies internal existence

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Limit comparison for schemes · internal existence implies ambient existence
theorems.hypotheses: Given a set $S_0$ of schemes, there exists one limit ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 000J simultaneously. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ for the full rank subcategory. The diagram takes values in that subcategory. Its indexing category has at most countably many objects and at most countable hom-sets.
theorems.statement: Existence of the limit in the chosen rank subcategory implies existence of the ambient limit.
theorems.proof: Apply Stacks 000J to the chosen rank subcategory and countable diagram. The choice of the rank segment is essential.
refs: Stacks 000J · (3) internal existence implies ambient existence

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Limit comparison for schemes · canonical comparison is invertible
theorems.hypotheses: Given a set $S_0$ of schemes, there exists one limit ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 000J simultaneously. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ for the full rank subcategory. The diagram takes values in that subcategory. Its indexing category has at most countably many objects and at most countable hom-sets.
theorems.statement: When the limit exists, the canonical comparison between the internal and ambient limit is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Apply Stacks 000J to the chosen rank subcategory and countable diagram. The choice of the rank segment is essential.

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Colimit comparison for schemes · ambient existence implies internal existence
theorems.hypotheses: Given a set $S_0$ of schemes, there exists one limit ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 000J simultaneously. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ for the full rank subcategory. The diagram takes values in that subcategory. Its indexing category has at most countably many objects and at most countable hom-sets.
theorems.statement: Existence of the ambient colimit implies existence of the colimit in the full rank subcategory.
theorems.proof: Apply Stacks 000J to the chosen rank subcategory and countable diagram. The choice of the rank segment is essential.
refs: Stacks 000J · (4) ambient existence implies internal existence

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Colimit comparison for schemes · internal existence implies ambient existence
theorems.hypotheses: Given a set $S_0$ of schemes, there exists one limit ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 000J simultaneously. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ for the full rank subcategory. The diagram takes values in that subcategory. Its indexing category has at most countably many objects and at most countable hom-sets.
theorems.statement: Existence of the colimit in the chosen rank subcategory implies existence of the ambient colimit.
theorems.proof: Apply Stacks 000J to the chosen rank subcategory and countable diagram. The choice of the rank segment is essential.
refs: Stacks 000J · (4) internal existence implies ambient existence

theorems.subject: set-theory
theorems.name: Colimit comparison for schemes · canonical comparison is invertible
theorems.hypotheses: Given a set $S_0$ of schemes, there exists one limit ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 000J simultaneously. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ for the full rank subcategory. The diagram takes values in that subcategory. Its indexing category has at most countably many objects and at most countable hom-sets.
theorems.statement: When the colimit exists, the canonical comparison between the internal and ambient colimit is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Apply Stacks 000J to the chosen rank subcategory and countable diagram. The choice of the rank segment is essential.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Size of an affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{size}(S)=\max(\aleph_0,|R|)$.
theorems.proof: Each affine open admits a finite cover by principal opens. Its sections inject into the corresponding finite product of localizations. The whole affine scheme supplies the lower bound.

theorems.subject: indexed-open-cover
theorems.name: Size bound including the empty cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be any indexed open covering of a scheme $X$, allowing $I=\varnothing$.
theorems.statement: One always has $\operatorname{size}(X)\le\max(\aleph_0,|I|,\sup_i\operatorname{size}(U_i))$. With an empty index set $X$ is empty and has size $\aleph_0$, so the uncorrected right side in 000Q is zero.
theorems.proof: For a nonempty family the extra cardinal is already bounded by the size of a member. For the empty family evaluate the defining maximum in 000H.
refs: Stacks 000Q · empty cover with the cardinal floor restored

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Size of a fibre product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be any morphisms of schemes.
theorems.statement: The inequality $\operatorname{size}(X\times_S Y)\le\max(\operatorname{size}(X),\operatorname{size}(Y))$ holds.
theorems.proof: Pass to affine charts. The tensor product of two algebras has cardinality at most the maximum of their cardinalities and the first infinite cardinal. Apply the open-cover estimate.
refs: Stacks 04T6 · size estimate for the fibre product

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Fibre products in a small category of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $X\to S\leftarrow Y$ be a cospan in $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.statement: Its fibre product exists in $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ and its cone is a fibre product of schemes.
theorems.proof: The ambient fibre product exists. Apply the countable-limit comparison in 000J.
refs: Stacks 000R · (1) fibre product in the subcategory and ambient universal property

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Countable coproducts in a small category of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Take an at most countable family in $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.statement: Its coproduct exists in $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ and its cocone is a coproduct of schemes.
theorems.proof: The disjoint union is an ambient coproduct. Apply the countable-colimit comparison in 000J.
refs: Stacks 000R · (2) at most countable coproduct with its ambient universal property

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Open subschemes in a small category of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S\in\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ and suppose $T\to S$ is an open immersion.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Each affine open of the source is already an affine open of the target. Then apply the bounded representative property in 000J.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed subschemes in a small category of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S\in\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ and suppose $T\to S$ is a closed immersion.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Apply the size estimate for a quasi-compact monomorphism. Then apply the bounded representative property in 000J.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Finite type schemes over a chosen object in a small category of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S\in\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ and suppose $T\to S$ is of finite type.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Over each affine target chart apply the size estimate to its quasi-compact inverse image. Then apply the bounded representative property in 000J.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Locally finitely presented monomorphisms in a small category of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S\in\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ and suppose $T\to S$ is a locally finitely presented monomorphism.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Apply the locally finitely presented case of 04VA. Then apply the bounded representative property in 000J.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-compact monomorphisms in a small category of schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S\in\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ and suppose $T\to S$ is a quasi-compact monomorphism.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Apply the quasi-compact case of 04VA. Then apply the bounded representative property in 000J.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Representatives from bounded open covers
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Suppose $T=\bigcup_{i\in I}T_i$ is an open cover and there is a single $S\in\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$ such that both $|I|$ and every $\operatorname{size}(T_i)$ are at most $\operatorname{size}(S)^{\aleph_0}$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Apply the open-cover bound, including the empty case, then the bounded representative property.
refs: Stacks 000R · (6) simultaneous bounds on cover arity and member size

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Locally finite type with a size-bounded affine cover
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $T\to S$ be locally of finite type with $S\in\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$. Suppose $T$ has an affine open cover of cardinality at most $\operatorname{size}(S)^{\aleph_0}$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Each affine chart is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over the base. Apply 04T7 and the bounded-cover conclusion of 000R(6).

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Locally finite type with at most continuum many affine charts
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $T\to S$ be locally of finite type with $S\in\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$. Suppose $T$ has an affine open cover of cardinality at most $2^{\aleph_0}$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Each affine chart is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over the base. Apply 04T7 and the bounded-cover conclusion of 000R(6).
refs: Stacks 000R · (7) example with continuum many charts

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Spectra of adic completions
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be affine and belong to $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$. Choose an ideal $I\subseteq R$ and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}(\varprojlim_n R/I^n)$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: The inverse limit injects into a countable product of quotients. Apply the affine size bound and 000J(2).

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Spectra of finite type algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be affine and belong to $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$. Take $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for any finite type $R$-algebra $A$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Bound the size by that of a polynomial algebra on finitely many generators. Apply the affine size bound and 000J(2).

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Spectra of localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be affine and belong to $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$. For any multiplicative subset $D\subseteq R$, take $T=\operatorname{Spec}(D^{-1}R)$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: A fraction has a representative in the product of the ring and the multiplicative subset. Apply the affine size bound and 000J(2).

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Spectra of algebraic closures of residue fields
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be affine and belong to $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$. Choose a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Count fractions and then roots of nonzero polynomials over the residue field. Apply the affine size bound and 000J(2).

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Spectra of subrings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be affine and belong to $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$. Take $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for any subring $A\subseteq R$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: The underlying subset bounds the cardinality of the subring. Apply the affine size bound and 000J(2).

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Finite type schemes over cardinal-bounded rings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a limit ordinal $\alpha$ furnished by Stacks 000J. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be affine and belong to $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$. Let $T$ be of finite type over a ring $A$ with $|A|\le |R|^{\aleph_0}$.
theorems.statement: Then $T$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathrm{Sch}_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: The affine base has bounded size and the source is quasi-compact, so apply 04T7. Apply the affine size bound and 000J(2).

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: An fpqc cover factoring through a morphism bounds its target
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to Y$ suppose there is an fpqc covering $(Y_j\to Y)_j$ in which every arrow factors through $f$.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{size}(Y)\le\operatorname{size}(X)$.
theorems.proof: Over each affine target open the fpqc condition gives a finite witnessing cover by images of affine opens. The factorization bounds the number of affine opens and the cardinalities of their section rings as in the source proof.
refs: Stacks 0AHK · target size bounded by the intermediate scheme

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Fppf character of the bounded refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Given an fppf covering $(X_i\to X)_{i\in I}$, one family $(W_j\to X)_{j\in J}$ can be chosen with all the properties of Stacks 0AHL.
theorems.statement: The chosen family is fppf covering.
theorems.proof: Cover the base by at most its size in affine opens. Over each choose finitely many quasi-compact open pieces in the given sources whose images cover that affine. Use 04T7 and the open-cover bound.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Factorization of arrows of the bounded refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Given an fppf covering $(X_i\to X)_{i\in I}$, one family $(W_j\to X)_{j\in J}$ can be chosen with all the properties of Stacks 0AHL.
theorems.statement: For every $j$ there is an $i$ and a factorization $W_j\to X_i\to X$.
theorems.proof: Cover the base by at most its size in affine opens. Over each choose finitely many quasi-compact open pieces in the given sources whose images cover that affine. Use 04T7 and the open-cover bound.
refs: Stacks 0AHL · new cover refines the given cover

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Total size of the fppf refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Given an fppf covering $(X_i\to X)_{i\in I}$, one family $(W_j\to X)_{j\in J}$ can be chosen with all the properties of Stacks 0AHL.
theorems.statement: The chosen family satisfies $\operatorname{size}(\coprod_j W_j)\le\operatorname{size}(X)$.
theorems.proof: Cover the base by at most its size in affine opens. Over each choose finitely many quasi-compact open pieces in the given sources whose images cover that affine. Use 04T7 and the open-cover bound.
refs: Stacks 0AHL · bound on the size of the coproduct

theorems.subject: group-action
theorems.name: Prescribed group actions in a rank segment
theorems.hypotheses: For a group $G$ and a set $S_0$ of left $G$-sets there is one limit ordinal $\alpha$ with all the properties in Stacks 000U. Write $\mathcal G_\alpha$ for the full subcategory coded in $V_\alpha$.
theorems.statement: Every member of $S_0$ is an object of $\mathcal G_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Use the rank construction for group actions in 000U. Its size bound and the countable diagram comparison hold at the same chosen stage.

theorems.subject: group-action
theorems.name: Inclusion of the regular left action
theorems.hypotheses: For a group $G$ and a set $S_0$ of left $G$-sets there is one limit ordinal $\alpha$ with all the properties in Stacks 000U. Write $\mathcal G_\alpha$ for the full subcategory coded in $V_\alpha$.
theorems.statement: The regular left action of $G$ on itself is an object of $\mathcal G_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Use the rank construction for group actions in 000U. Its size bound and the countable diagram comparison hold at the same chosen stage.

theorems.subject: group-action
theorems.name: Group actions of bounded size admit representatives
theorems.hypotheses: For a group $G$ and a set $S_0$ of left $G$-sets there is one limit ordinal $\alpha$ with all the properties in Stacks 000U. Write $\mathcal G_\alpha$ for the full subcategory coded in $V_\alpha$.
theorems.statement: For $S\in\mathcal G_\alpha$, every $G$-set $T$ satisfying $\operatorname{size}_G(T)\le\operatorname{size}_G(S)^{\aleph_0}$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathcal G_\alpha$.
theorems.proof: Use the rank construction for group actions in 000U. Its size bound and the countable diagram comparison hold at the same chosen stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Inclusion of prescribed covering families
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category. Its given proper class of covering families contains singleton isomorphisms, is closed under composition of covers, and admits and includes their base changes along every arrow. Given any set $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ of these covers, one cardinal $\kappa$ and one limit ordinal $\alpha$ work simultaneously. Write $D$ for the original covering families in $V_\alpha$ of arity at most $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: Every member of $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ belongs to $D$.
theorems.proof: Choose the cardinal and the initial rank to dominate the given set of families and their index sets.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Singleton isomorphisms in the small coverage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category. Its given proper class of covering families contains singleton isomorphisms, is closed under composition of covers, and admits and includes their base changes along every arrow. Given any set $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ of these covers, one cardinal $\kappa$ and one limit ordinal $\alpha$ work simultaneously. Write $D$ for the original covering families in $V_\alpha$ of arity at most $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: For every isomorphism $V\to U$ its singleton covering family belongs to $D$.
theorems.proof: There is a set of singleton isomorphism covers, which fits in an initial rank level.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composites in the small coverage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category. Its given proper class of covering families contains singleton isomorphisms, is closed under composition of covers, and admits and includes their base changes along every arrow. Given any set $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ of these covers, one cardinal $\kappa$ and one limit ordinal $\alpha$ work simultaneously. Write $D$ for the original covering families in $V_\alpha$ of arity at most $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: If $(U_i\to U)_i\in D$ and $(W_{ij}\to U_i)_j\in D$ for each $i$, the composite covering family belongs to $D$.
theorems.proof: The final ordinal has sufficiently large cofinality and a sum of at most the bounded number of index sets still has bounded cardinality.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Existence of the fibre products for a base-changed cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category. Its given proper class of covering families contains singleton isomorphisms, is closed under composition of covers, and admits and includes their base changes along every arrow. Given any set $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ of these covers, one cardinal $\kappa$ and one limit ordinal $\alpha$ work simultaneously. Write $D$ for the original covering families in $V_\alpha$ of arity at most $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: For any $(U_i\to U)_i\in D$ and any $V\to U$, each $U_i\times_U V$ exists in $\mathcal C$.
theorems.proof: Each retained family is an original cover, so the original base-change axiom applies.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Base-changed families in the small coverage
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category. Its given proper class of covering families contains singleton isomorphisms, is closed under composition of covers, and admits and includes their base changes along every arrow. Given any set $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ of these covers, one cardinal $\kappa$ and one limit ordinal $\alpha$ work simultaneously. Write $D$ for the original covering families in $V_\alpha$ of arity at most $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: For each such family and $V\to U$, the base-changed covering family $(U_i\times_U V\to V)_i$ belongs to $D$ using the chosen fibre products.
theorems.proof: Include the chosen base changes when iterating the ordinal bound. The index set remains bounded.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A site presented by a set of coverings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category. Its given proper class of covering families contains singleton isomorphisms, is closed under composition of covers, and admits and includes their base changes along every arrow. Given any set $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ of these covers, one cardinal $\kappa$ and one limit ordinal $\alpha$ work simultaneously. Write $D$ for the original covering families in $V_\alpha$ of arity at most $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: The pair $(\mathcal C,D)$ is a site in the covering-family convention of Stacks 00VH.
theorems.proof: The three covering axioms hold for the same set of families on the given category.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Combinatorial representatives for every original cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category. Its given proper class of covering families contains singleton isomorphisms, is closed under composition of covers, and admits and includes their base changes along every arrow. Given any set $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ of these covers, one cardinal $\kappa$ and one limit ordinal $\alpha$ work simultaneously. Write $D$ for the original covering families in $V_\alpha$ of arity at most $\kappa$.
theorems.statement: Each original covering family is combinatorially equivalent to some member of $D$.
theorems.proof: The sets of distinct arrows in the original families form a set. Include one original representative for each support and choose the bounds to cover them.

theorems.subject: abelian-category
theorems.name: Existence of an abelian subcategory
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be a big locally small abelian category with enough injectives. Given a set of objects $(A_s)_{s\in S}$, there exists one abelian subcategory $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal A$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 0010.
theorems.statement: The witness $\mathcal A'$ is an abelian category with the indicated inclusion functor.
theorems.proof: This is a component of the existence assertion in Stacks 0010, whose proof is omitted there. All clauses concern the same subcategory and inclusion.

theorems.subject: abelian-category
theorems.name: Exact inclusion of the chosen subcategory
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be a big locally small abelian category with enough injectives. Given a set of objects $(A_s)_{s\in S}$, there exists one abelian subcategory $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal A$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 0010.
theorems.statement: The inclusion preserves short exact sequences.
theorems.proof: This is a component of the existence assertion in Stacks 0010, whose proof is omitted there. All clauses concern the same subcategory and inclusion.

theorems.subject: abelian-category
theorems.name: Smallness of the chosen abelian subcategory
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be a big locally small abelian category with enough injectives. Given a set of objects $(A_s)_{s\in S}$, there exists one abelian subcategory $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal A$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 0010.
theorems.statement: The objects of $\mathcal A'$ form a set.
theorems.proof: This is a component of the existence assertion in Stacks 0010, whose proof is omitted there. All clauses concern the same subcategory and inclusion.

theorems.subject: abelian-category
theorems.name: Inclusion of prescribed objects
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be a big locally small abelian category with enough injectives. Given a set of objects $(A_s)_{s\in S}$, there exists one abelian subcategory $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal A$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 0010.
theorems.statement: Every $A_s$ belongs to $\mathcal A'$.
theorems.proof: This is a component of the existence assertion in Stacks 0010, whose proof is omitted there. All clauses concern the same subcategory and inclusion.

theorems.name: Enough injectives in the chosen subcategory
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be a big locally small abelian category with enough injectives. Given a set of objects $(A_s)_{s\in S}$, there exists one abelian subcategory $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal A$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 0010.
theorems.statement: Every object of $\mathcal A'$ embeds into an injective object of $\mathcal A'$.

theorems.statement: Its image is injective in $\mathcal A$.
theorems.proof: This is a component of the existence assertion in Stacks 0010, whose proof is omitted there. All clauses concern the same subcategory and inclusion.

Given a set of objects $(A_s)_{s\in S}$, there exists one abelian subcategory $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal A$ satisfying all conclusions of Stacks 0010. Suppose $I$ belongs to $\mathcal A'$ and its image is injective in $\mathcal A$.
theorems.statement: Then $I$ is injective in $\mathcal A'$.
theorems.proof: This is a component of the existence assertion in Stacks 0010, whose proof is omitted there. All clauses concern the same subcategory and inclusion.

theorems.subject: associative-ring
theorems.name: Bicommutant of a nonzero right ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a unital ring with no nontrivial two-sided ideal and let $0\ne I\subseteq R$ be a right ideal. Set $E=\operatorname{End}_R(I)$.
theorems.statement: Right multiplication identifies $R^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\operatorname{End}_E(I)$ under ordinary composition. The source writes the latter on the right with the opposite multiplication.
theorems.proof: The right action is faithful by simplicity. In the right-acting convention its image contains the identity and is a right ideal of the bicommutant, since $RI=R$ and left multiplications by elements of $I$ lie in $E$.
refs: Stacks 0745 · right action identifies the bicommutant

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Existence of a simple module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ an associative unital $k$-algebra, with scalars central. Assume $0<\dim_k A<\infty$.
theorems.statement: There exists a simple right $A$-module.
theorems.proof: Apply the minimal-dimension argument to the nonzero regular module.

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: A simple submodule in a nonzero module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ an associative unital $k$-algebra, with scalars central. Assume $\dim_k A<\infty$ and let $N$ be a nonzero unital right module of arbitrary dimension.
theorems.statement: The module $N$ contains a simple submodule.
