theorems.proof: Take a nonzero cyclic submodule and then a nonzero submodule of least positive vector-space dimension.

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Finite dimension of a simple module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ an associative unital $k$-algebra, with scalars central. Assume $\dim_k A<\infty$ and let $M$ be a simple right module.
theorems.statement: One has $\dim_k M\le\dim_k A$.
theorems.proof: For $m\ne0$, the map $A\to M$, $a\mapsto ma$, surjects.

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Endomorphisms of a simple right module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ an associative unital $k$-algebra, with scalars central. Let $M$ be a simple right module. The source assumes $A$ finite; the proof of this clause also applies in arbitrary dimension.
theorems.statement: The ring $\operatorname{End}_A(M)$ is a division ring.
theorems.proof: A nonzero endomorphism has zero kernel and image $M$, and its inverse is $A$-linear.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Lemma 1.16 and Theorem 1.17

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Wedderburn structure theorem
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules.
theorems.statement: There exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a division algebra $D$ finite-dimensional over $k$ with $A\simeq M_n(D)$ over $k$. The center of $D$ can strictly contain $k$.
theorems.proof: Use the bicommutant of a minimal right ideal and a basis over its division endomorphism ring.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Lemma 1.16 and Theorem 1.17

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Centralizers of tensor products
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field, $A,A^{\prime}$ associative unital $k$-algebras and $B\subseteq A$, $B^{\prime}\subseteq A^{\prime}$ unital $k$-subalgebras of any dimension.
theorems.statement: Inside $A\otimes_k A^{\prime}$, the centralizer of $B\otimes_k B^{\prime}$ equals $C_A(B)\otimes_k C_{A^{\prime}}(B^{\prime})$.
theorems.proof: Expand a tensor using independent coefficients, first imposing commutation with $B\otimes1$, then with $1\otimes B^{\prime}$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.3 and Corollary 2.4
Stacks 0749 · centralizer of a tensor product

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Center of a finite simple algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules.
theorems.statement: The center $Z(A)$ is a finite field extension of $k$.
theorems.proof: A nonzero central element generates a nonzero two-sided ideal and hence has an inverse, which is central. The center is a vector subspace of $A$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.3 and Corollary 2.4
Stacks 074A · center a finite field extension

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Descent of scalar-stable vector subspaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $V$ be any $k$-vector space and $D$ a division algebra with center $k$. Let $W\subseteq V\otimes_k D$ be stable under both left and right multiplication by $D$ on its second factor.
theorems.statement: Put $V_0=\{v\in V:v\otimes1\in W\}$. Then $W=V_0\otimes_k D$; the vectors $v\otimes1$ for $v\in V_0$ generate $W$ over $D$ on the left.
theorems.proof: Pass to $V/V_0$. A nonzero tensor with minimal support can be normalized to have one coefficient equal to one. Commutators have smaller support, forcing every coefficient to be central.

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Two-sided ideals after tensoring with a central division algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ an associative unital $k$-algebra, with scalars central. Let $D$ be a division algebra with center exactly $k$.
theorems.statement: Each two-sided ideal $I$ of $A\otimes_k D$ equals $J\otimes_k D$ for the uniquely determined ideal $J=\{a\in A:a\otimes1\in I\}$.
theorems.proof: Apply scalar-stable subspace descent to $V=A$; contraction preserves the two-sided ideal condition.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.6, Lemma 2.7 and Corollary 2.8
Stacks 074C · descent of each two-sided ideal

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Preservation of simplicity by a central division factor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ an associative unital $k$-algebra, with scalars central. Let $D$ be a division algebra with center exactly $k$. Suppose $A$ is nonzero and simple.
theorems.statement: The tensor product $A\otimes_k D$ is nonzero and simple.
theorems.proof: Its ideals are extensions of the two ideals of $A$ and tensoring nonzero vector spaces over $k$ gives a nonzero space.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.6, Lemma 2.7 and Corollary 2.8

theorems.subject: associative-ring
theorems.name: Matrix Morita equivalence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a unital ring, possibly noncommutative, let $n\ge1$, and write $S=M_n(R)$ with matrix units $e_{ij}$.
theorems.statement: The functors $M\mapsto M^{\oplus n}$ with row-vector action and $N\mapsto Ne_{11}$ are quasi-inverse between unital right $R$- and $S$-modules.
theorems.proof: The matrix units transport the first summand of $N$ into each $Ne_{ii}$; the diagonal idempotents resolve the identity.

theorems.subject: associative-ring
theorems.name: Two-sided ideals of a full matrix ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a unital ring, possibly noncommutative, let $n\ge1$, and write $S=M_n(R)$ with matrix units $e_{ij}$.
theorems.statement: Every two-sided ideal of $S$ is $M_n(I)$ for a unique two-sided ideal $I\subseteq R$.
theorems.proof: The corners selected by the matrix units identify all component ideals with the first diagonal corner.

theorems.subject: associative-ring
theorems.name: Center of a full matrix ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a unital ring, possibly noncommutative, let $n\ge1$, and write $S=M_n(R)$ with matrix units $e_{ij}$.
theorems.statement: The center of $M_n(R)$ consists of $zI_n$ for $z\in Z(R)$.
theorems.proof: Commutation with matrix units forces a scalar diagonal. Commutation with individual entries forces the scalar to be central.

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Unique simple module of a finite simple algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules.
theorems.statement: There is exactly one isomorphism class of simple right $A$-modules.
theorems.proof: Under matrix Morita equivalence simple modules correspond to dimension-one vector spaces over the division algebra.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 1.18, Theorem 1.19 and Corollary 1.21 (left modules; apply to the opposite algebra)

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Decomposition into copies of the simple module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules. Fix a simple right $A$-module $M$ and set $E=\operatorname{End}_A(M)$, acting on the left. Let $N$ be a finite-dimensional right $A$-module.
theorems.statement: For some integer $r\ge0$ there is an $A$-linear isomorphism $N\simeq M^{\oplus r}$.
theorems.proof: Matrix Morita equivalence reduces decomposition to choosing a basis over a division ring.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 1.18, Theorem 1.19 and Corollary 1.21 (left modules; apply to the opposite algebra)

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Dimension classifies finite modules over a simple algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules. Let $N,N^{\prime}$ be finite-dimensional right modules over the same $A$.
theorems.statement: They are isomorphic exactly when their $k$-dimensions agree.
theorems.proof: Their dimensions equal the multiplicities of the unique simple module times its positive dimension.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 1.18, Theorem 1.19 and Corollary 1.21 (left modules; apply to the opposite algebra)

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Simplicity of the row module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $D$ be a division algebra finite-dimensional over $k$, $n\ge1$, $A=M_n(D)$, and $M=D^{1\times n}$ with its natural right matrix action.
theorems.statement: The row module $M$ is simple.
theorems.proof: A nonzero entry can be inverted. Matrix units and scalar matrices then let a nonzero row generate every row.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 1.18, Theorem 1.19 and Corollary 1.21 (left modules; apply to the opposite algebra)
H. Bass, Lectures on Topics in Algebraic K-Theory, Chapter 2, §6, Theorem 6.1, converse (simplicity of the right module and its endomorphisms by left multiplication)
Stacks 074E · (4) simplicity of the matrix row

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Endomorphism algebra of the row module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $D$ be a division algebra finite-dimensional over $k$, $n\ge1$, $A=M_n(D)$, and $M=D^{1\times n}$ with its natural right matrix action.
theorems.statement: With ordinary composition, $\operatorname{End}_A(M)\simeq D$ by coordinatewise left multiplication. The opposite ring of these endomorphisms is $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, the orientation printed in clause (4).
theorems.proof: Commutation with each matrix unit forces one coefficient on the left of every entry. Left multiplications compose by $L_a\circ L_b=L_{ab}$.
refs: H. Bass, Lectures on Topics in Algebraic K-Theory, Chapter 2, §6, Theorem 6.1, converse (simplicity of the right module and its endomorphisms by left multiplication)
Stacks 074E · (4) endomorphisms of the matrix row, with multiplication convention

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Finite division algebra acting on a simple module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules. Fix a simple right $A$-module $M$ and set $E=\operatorname{End}_A(M)$, acting on the left.
theorems.statement: The evaluation action makes $M$ a left $E$-module, and $E$ is a finite-dimensional division $k$-algebra.
theorems.proof: Schur gives invertibility. The endomorphism algebra embeds in the finite-dimensional vector space of $k$-linear endomorphisms.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Lemma 1.16 and Theorem 1.17
H. Bass, Lectures on Topics in Algebraic K-Theory, Chapter 2, §6, Theorem 6.1(1), division endomorphism algebra

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Bicommutant of a simple right module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules. Fix a simple right $A$-module $M$ and set $E=\operatorname{End}_A(M)$, acting on the left.
theorems.statement: Right multiplication gives an isomorphism $A^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\operatorname{End}_E(M)$ with ordinary composition.
theorems.proof: The simple module is isomorphic to a minimal right ideal. Apply the nonzero right ideal bicommutant theorem.
refs: H. Bass, Lectures on Topics in Algebraic K-Theory, Chapter 2, §6, Theorem 6.1(3), opposite endomorphism algebra acting by right multiplication
Stacks 074E · (5) recovery of the acting algebra

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Centers on the two sides of a simple module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules. Fix a simple right $A$-module $M$ and set $E=\operatorname{End}_A(M)$, acting on the left.
theorems.statement: Right scalar action identifies $Z(A)$ with $Z(E)$.
theorems.proof: For a matrix algebra over $D$, the centers on both sides act as scalars from $Z(D)$.
refs: H. Bass, Lectures on Topics in Algebraic K-Theory, Chapter 2, §6, Theorem 6.1(5), centres identified by their actions

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Dimension product for a simple module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules. Fix a simple right $A$-module $M$ and set $E=\operatorname{End}_A(M)$, acting on the left.
theorems.proof: In a matrix presentation the three quantities have dimensions $n^2[D:k]$, $[D:k]$, and $n[D:k]$, respectively.

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Endomorphisms of several copies of a simple module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules. Fix a simple right $A$-module $M$ and set $E=\operatorname{End}_A(M)$, acting on the left. Write a finite right module as $N\simeq M^{\oplus r}$.
theorems.statement: For $r>0$, $\operatorname{End}_A(N)\simeq M_r(E)$. For $r=0$ the endomorphism ring is the zero ring.
theorems.proof: The inclusions and projections of the summands give the matrix entries. Composition is matrix multiplication.
refs: H. Bass, Lectures on Topics in Algebraic K-Theory, Chapter 2, §6, opening formula for endomorphisms of a finite direct sum
Stacks 074E · (6) endomorphism ring of a finite module

theorems.subject: associative-right-module
theorems.name: Bicommutant of a nonzero finite module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital algebra over a field $k$ with no nontrivial two-sided ideal. All modules are unital right modules. Fix a simple right $A$-module $M$ and set $E=\operatorname{End}_A(M)$, acting on the left. Let $N$ be finite-dimensional and nonzero and put $B=\operatorname{End}_A(N)$.
theorems.statement: Right multiplication identifies $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\operatorname{End}_B(N)$ under ordinary composition. For $N=0$ the bicommutant is zero, so recovery requires the displayed nonzero hypothesis.
theorems.proof: For $N=M^{\oplus r}$ with $r>0$, commuting with all matrix units reduces the bicommutant to the diagonal copy of $\operatorname{End}_E(M)$.
refs: Stacks 074E · (6) bicommutant for nonzero finite modules

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Tensoring simple algebras with one finite central factor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ an associative unital $k$-algebra, with scalars central. Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero simple $k$-algebras. At least one factor is finite-dimensional and central over $k$.
theorems.statement: The algebra $A\otimes_k B$ is simple. The second factor may have infinite dimension if the first meets both additional hypotheses.
theorems.proof: Write the finite central factor as a matrix algebra over a central division algebra and use ideal descent and the matrix ideal correspondence.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.6, Lemma 2.7 and Corollary 2.8
Stacks 074F · simplicity of a tensor product

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Finite dimension of the tensor product of central simple algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A,B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional central simple algebras over the same field $k$.
theorems.statement: $[A\otimes_k B:k]=[A:k][B:k]<\infty$.
theorems.proof: Tensoring bases gives a basis of the product.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.6, Lemma 2.7 and Corollary 2.8

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Centrality of the tensor product of central simple algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A,B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional central simple algebras over the same field $k$.
theorems.statement: $Z(A\otimes_k B)=k$.
theorems.proof: The tensor centralizer identity applies to the full subalgebras.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.6, Lemma 2.7 and Corollary 2.8

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Simplicity of the tensor product of central simple algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A,B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional central simple algebras over the same field $k$.
theorems.statement: $A\otimes_k B$ is simple.
theorems.proof: Tensor simplicity applies because each factor is finite and central.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.6, Lemma 2.7 and Corollary 2.8

theorems.subject: brauer-extension
theorems.name: Finite dimension after extending scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $L/k$ be any field extension and write $A_L=A\otimes_k L$.
theorems.proof: A basis of $A$ over $k$ remains a basis over $L$ after scalar extension.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.15 and Corollary 2.16

theorems.subject: brauer-extension
theorems.name: Centrality after extending scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $L/k$ be any field extension and write $A_L=A\otimes_k L$.
theorems.proof: The centralizer tensor formula computes the center after extending scalars.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.15 and Corollary 2.16

theorems.subject: brauer-extension
theorems.name: Simplicity after extending scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $L/k$ be any field extension and write $A_L=A\otimes_k L$.
theorems.statement: $A_L$ is simple.
theorems.proof: Apply tensor simplicity to $A$ and the simple $k$-algebra $L$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 2.15 and Corollary 2.16

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Enveloping algebra of a central simple algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$.
theorems.statement: The map $A\otimes_k A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{End}_k(A)$ taking $a\otimes b$ to $x\mapsto axb$ is a $k$-algebra isomorphism. A choice of basis identifies its target with $M_{[A:k]}(k)$.
theorems.proof: The source is simple and the map preserves the nonzero unit. The dimensions on the two sides agree.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Corollary 2.9

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Similarity is an equivalence relation
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a field $k$. Similarity is considered on isomorphism classes of finite central simple $k$-algebras, using positive-size matrix stabilizations.
theorems.statement: Similarity is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
theorems.proof: For transitivity, stabilize the two given matrix isomorphisms until the middle matrix sizes agree.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, definition of the Brauer group and Remark 2.13(a)

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Existence of a division representative
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a field $k$. Similarity is considered on isomorphism classes of finite central simple $k$-algebras, using positive-size matrix stabilizations.
theorems.statement: Every similarity class has a representative which is a finite division algebra with center $k$.
theorems.proof: Wedderburn supplies a matrix presentation over a division algebra; the matrix center identifies its center with $k$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, definition of the Brauer group and Remark 2.13(a)

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Uniqueness of the division representative
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a field $k$. Similarity is considered on isomorphism classes of finite central simple $k$-algebras, using positive-size matrix stabilizations.
theorems.statement: Any two division representatives in one class are isomorphic as $k$-algebras.
theorems.proof: The endomorphism algebra of the unique simple right module recovers the coefficient division algebra from each stabilization.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, definition of the Brauer group and Remark 2.13(a)

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Similarity of matrix algebras over division rings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a field $k$. Similarity is considered on isomorphism classes of finite central simple $k$-algebras, using positive-size matrix stabilizations. Let $D,E$ be finite division algebras with center $k$ and $n,m\ge1$.
theorems.statement: $M_n(D)$ and $M_m(E)$ are similar if and only if $D$ and $E$ are isomorphic as $k$-algebras.
theorems.proof: Stabilization preserves the division representative; conversely isomorphic division factors give isomorphic stabilizations.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, definition of the Brauer group and Remark 2.13(a)

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Addition of Brauer classes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A,B$ be finite central simple $k$-algebras.
theorems.statement: The sum of their classes is $[A\otimes_k B]$. This operation is well defined and gives a commutative and associative law.
theorems.proof: Matrix stabilization commutes with tensor products, and the tensor associator and symmetry give the two laws.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, definition of the Brauer group and Remark 2.13(a)

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Identity in the Brauer group
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field.
theorems.statement: The identity is the class of $k$; it is also represented by every $M_n(k)$ for $n\ge1$.
theorems.proof: Tensoring with $k$ uses the scalar unit, and each matrix algebra is stably isomorphic to $k$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, definition of the Brauer group and Remark 2.13(a)

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Inversion of Brauer classes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$.
theorems.statement: The inverse of $[A]$ is $[A^{\mathrm{op}}]$.
theorems.proof: The enveloping algebra is a full matrix algebra over $k$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, definition of the Brauer group and Remark 2.13(a)
J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Corollary 2.9

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Skolem–Noether conjugacy
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $B$ be a simple unital $k$-algebra and $f,g:B\to A$ unital $k$-algebra maps.
theorems.statement: There exists $u\in A^\times$ such that $f(b)=ug(b)u^{-1}$ for every $b\in B$.
theorems.proof: Both maps are faithful. Their two actions on a simple module of $A$ give isomorphic modules over the auxiliary finite simple algebra in the proof; an intertwiner yields the required unit.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Theorem 2.10 and Corollary 2.12
Stacks 074Q · conjugacy of the two specified maps

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Automorphisms of a central simple algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $f$ be a $k$-algebra automorphism.
theorems.statement: There is $u\in A^\times$ such that $f(a)=uau^{-1}$ for all $a\in A$.
theorems.proof: Apply Skolem–Noether to $f$ and the identity map.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Theorem 2.10 and Corollary 2.12

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Automorphisms of a full matrix algebra over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $n\ge1$, $k$ be a field and $f$ a $k$-algebra automorphism of $M_n(k)$.
theorems.statement: There exists $U\in\mathrm{GL}_n(k)$ such that $f(X)=UXU^{-1}$ for all $X$.
theorems.proof: The matrix algebra is finite central simple, so the innerness conclusion applies.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Theorem 2.10 and Corollary 2.12

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Simplicity of the centralizer
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a simple unital $k$-subalgebra, and write $C=C_A(B)$.
theorems.statement: The centralizer $C$ is a simple algebra.
theorems.proof: In the module proof its algebra, up to opposite, is a matrix algebra over a division algebra.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.3

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Dimension formula for a centralizer
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a simple unital $k$-subalgebra, and write $C=C_A(B)$.
theorems.proof: Compute dimensions after decomposing the simple module of $A$ over the auxiliary simple algebra attached to $B$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.3

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Double centralizer inside a central simple algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a simple unital $k$-subalgebra, and write $C=C_A(B)$.
theorems.statement: One has $C_A(C)=B$ as subalgebras of $A$.
theorems.proof: The inclusion of $B$ is immediate. Applying the dimension formula to $C$ yields equality.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.3

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Centralizer of a central simple subalgebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a simple unital $k$-subalgebra, and write $C=C_A(B)$. Suppose $Z(B)=k$.
theorems.statement: The centralizer $C$ is a finite central simple $k$-algebra.
theorems.proof: It is finite-dimensional and simple. The double centralizer identity gives $Z(C)=C\cap B=Z(B)=k$.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.3

theorems.subject: associative-field-algebra
theorems.name: Tensor factorization by a centralizer
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a field $k$, with $1\ne0$. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a simple unital $k$-subalgebra, and write $C=C_A(B)$. Suppose $Z(B)=k$.
theorems.statement: Multiplication $B\otimes_k C\to A$, $b\otimes c\mapsto bc$, is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras.
theorems.proof: The factors commute. The source is simple and has the dimension of $A$, so this unital map is bijective.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.3

theorems.subject: brauer-embedded-subfield
theorems.name: Degree of a maximal subfield of a division algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $D$ be a finite-dimensional division algebra with center $k$. Let $L$ be any maximal subfield containing $k$.
theorems.statement: One has $[D:k]=[L:k]^2$. No separability of $L/k$ is required.
theorems.proof: Inside a division algebra, a finite-dimensional commutative domain over $k$ is a field. Hence a maximal subfield is maximal as a commutative subring, and the centralizer criterion applies.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Corollaries 3.4–3.6
Stacks 074W · square of each maximal-subfield degree

theorems.subject: brauer-extension
theorems.name: A maximal subfield splits a central division algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $D$ be a finite-dimensional division algebra with center $k$. Let $L\subseteq D$ be a maximal subfield containing $k$.
theorems.statement: One has $D\otimes_k L\simeq M_{[L:k]}(L)$.
theorems.proof: The degree formula supplies the full-degree embedding in the splitting criterion.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Corollaries 3.4–3.6
Stacks 0750 · splitting by any maximal subfield

theorems.subject: brauer-extension
theorems.name: The index divides every finite splitting degree
theorems.hypotheses: Let $D$ be a finite-dimensional division algebra with center $k$. Put $d^2=[D:k]$ and suppose $L/k$ is finite and splits $D$.
theorems.statement: The integer $d$ divides $[L:k]$.
theorems.proof: A representative with a full-degree embedding of $L$ is $M_r(D)$ for some $r\ge1$. Comparing dimensions gives $[L:k]=rd$.
refs: Stacks 0751 · divisibility of the finite splitting degree

theorems.subject: brauer-embedded-subfield
theorems.name: Existence of a separable maximal subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $D$ be a finite-dimensional division algebra with center $k$.
theorems.statement: There exists a maximal subfield $k\subseteq L\subseteq D$ separable over $k$.
theorems.proof: The source enlarges a separable intermediate field inside its centralizer. A nontrivial finite central division algebra has a noncentral element separable over its center; finite dimension makes the process terminate.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 3.8 and proof of Corollary 3.10

theorems.subject: brauer-extension
theorems.name: Finite separable splitting of a Brauer class
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any field $k$ and any class $\alpha\in\operatorname{Br}(k)$.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite separable extension $L/k$ such that the image of $\alpha$ in $\operatorname{Br}(L)$ is zero.
theorems.proof: Choose the division representative of the class and a separable maximal subfield. This subfield splits the representative.
refs: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, IV, Proposition 3.8 and proof of Corollary 3.10
Stacks 0752 · finite separable splitting extension for each Brauer class

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closed image of a continuous section
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $s:Y\to X$ be continuous, with $fs=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $X$ Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: The subset $s(Y)$ is closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: It is the inverse image of the diagonal in $X\times X$ under $x\mapsto(x,s(f(x)))$.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definitions 1.8, 1.12 and Lemma 1.13

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closed fibre product over a Hausdorff space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Z$ and $Y\to Z$ be continuous with $Z$ Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: $X\times_ZY$ is closed in $X\times Y$.
theorems.proof: It is the inverse image of the diagonal of $Z$ under the product of the two given maps.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definitions 1.8, 1.12 and Lemma 1.13
Stacks 08ZH · closedness in the ordinary product

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Base change of a separated continuous map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and $Y^{\prime}\to Y$ continuous.
theorems.statement: The projection $Y^{\prime}\times_Y X\to Y^{\prime}$ is separated.
theorems.proof: Its relative diagonal image is the inverse image of the closed relative diagonal image for $f$.

theorems.subject: set-with-subset-family
theorems.name: Existence of a topology with prescribed basis
theorems.hypotheses: Let a family of subsets cover a set $X$. Require every point of an intersection of two members to lie in a third member contained in the intersection.
theorems.statement: There is a topology with the prescribed family as a basis.
theorems.proof: Arbitrary unions of members are closed under finite intersection by the pointwise refinement condition.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.3 and Lemma 1.4

theorems.subject: set-with-subset-family
theorems.name: Uniqueness of the topology with prescribed basis
theorems.hypotheses: Let a family of subsets cover a set $X$. Require every point of an intersection of two members to lie in a third member contained in the intersection.
theorems.statement: The topology with this basis is uniquely determined.
theorems.proof: The open sets must be exactly the unions of members.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.3 and Lemma 1.4

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Refinement of an open cover by basic open sets
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis for $X$ and an open cover of an open subspace $U$.
theorems.statement: The given cover admits an open refinement by members of the basis.
theorems.proof: Take all basic opens contained in at least one member of the cover; each point lies in one.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.3 and Lemma 1.4

theorems.subject: set-with-subset-family
theorems.name: Existence of the topology with prescribed subbasis
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any family of subsets of a set $X$, allowing the empty family.
theorems.statement: There exists a topology on $X$ in which the family is a subbasis.
theorems.proof: Its finite intersections include $X$ and are stable under binary intersection, so their unions define a topology.

theorems.subject: set-with-subset-family
theorems.name: Uniqueness of the topology with prescribed subbasis
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of subsets of $X$.
theorems.statement: At most one topology has this family as subbasis.
theorems.proof: A basis determines its topology, and the finite intersections are prescribed.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Continuity of the membership quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let a family of opens cover $X$ and express the intersection of any two members as a union of members contained in both. Form the one common quotient $f:X\to Y$ by membership in this family.
theorems.statement: The indicated quotient map is continuous.
theorems.proof: Membership is constant on equivalence classes. The image family covers and refines pairwise intersections, so it determines a topology. Preimages of its basic opens are the original open members.
refs: Stacks 0D5Q · existence of the common continuous map

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Open image of each member
theorems.hypotheses: Let a family of opens cover $X$ and express the intersection of any two members as a union of members contained in both. Form the one common quotient $f:X\to Y$ by membership in this family.
theorems.statement: Every member has open image under $f$.
theorems.proof: Membership is constant on equivalence classes. The image family covers and refines pairwise intersections, so it determines a topology. Preimages of its basic opens are the original open members.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Saturation of each member
theorems.hypotheses: Let a family of opens cover $X$ and express the intersection of any two members as a union of members contained in both. Form the one common quotient $f:X\to Y$ by membership in this family.
theorems.statement: Every member $U$ satisfies $f^{-1}(f(U))=U$.
theorems.proof: Membership is constant on equivalence classes. The image family covers and refines pairwise intersections, so it determines a topology. Preimages of its basic opens are the original open members.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Basis formed by images
theorems.hypotheses: Let a family of opens cover $X$ and express the intersection of any two members as a union of members contained in both. Form the one common quotient $f:X\to Y$ by membership in this family.
theorems.statement: The images of the family constitute a basis of $Y$.
theorems.proof: Membership is constant on equivalence classes. The image family covers and refines pairwise intersections, so it determines a topology. Preimages of its basic opens are the original open members.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Coarsest topology making an injection continuous
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a topological space $X$ and a set injection $f:Y\to X$.
theorems.statement: The induced topology on $Y$ is the coarsest one making $f$ continuous.
theorems.proof: Inverse image preserves arbitrary unions, finite intersections and complements. These operations give the topology and the corresponding closed-set criterion.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.14 and Proposition 2.4

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Open-set test for the induced topology
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a topological space $X$ and a set injection $f:Y\to X$.
theorems.statement: Its open sets are exactly inverse images of open subsets of $X$.
theorems.proof: Inverse image preserves arbitrary unions, finite intersections and complements. These operations give the topology and the corresponding closed-set criterion.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.14 and Proposition 2.4

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closed-set test for the induced topology
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a topological space $X$ and a set injection $f:Y\to X$.
theorems.statement: Its closed sets are exactly inverse images of closed subsets of $X$.
theorems.proof: Inverse image preserves arbitrary unions, finite intersections and complements. These operations give the topology and the corresponding closed-set criterion.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.14 and Proposition 2.4

theorems.subject: set-surjection-from-space
theorems.name: Finest topology making a surjection continuous
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a topological space $X$ and a set surjection $f:X\to Y$.
theorems.statement: The quotient topology on $Y$ is the finest one making $f$ continuous.
theorems.proof: Inverse image preserves arbitrary unions, finite intersections and complements. These operations give the topology and the corresponding closed-set criterion.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.16 and Proposition 2.5

theorems.subject: set-surjection-from-space
theorems.name: Open-set test for the quotient topology
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a topological space $X$ and a set surjection $f:X\to Y$.
theorems.statement: A subset of $Y$ is open exactly when its inverse image is open in $X$.
theorems.proof: Inverse image preserves arbitrary unions, finite intersections and complements. These operations give the topology and the corresponding closed-set criterion.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.16 and Proposition 2.5

theorems.subject: set-surjection-from-space
theorems.name: Closed-set test for the quotient topology
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a topological space $X$ and a set surjection $f:X\to Y$.
theorems.statement: A subset of $Y$ is closed exactly when its inverse image is closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Inverse image preserves arbitrary unions, finite intersections and complements. These operations give the topology and the corresponding closed-set criterion.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 1.16 and Proposition 2.5

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closure formula for a surjective open map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective open continuous map, and let $T\subseteq Y$.
theorems.statement: $f^{-1}(\overline T)=\overline{f^{-1}(T)}$.
theorems.proof: The image of any open neighbourhood disjoint from the inverse image is open and misses the subset. Continuity supplies the reverse inclusion.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Surjective open maps detect closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective open continuous map, and let $T\subseteq Y$.
theorems.statement: $T$ is closed exactly when $f^{-1}(T)$ is closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Surjectivity identifies a subset with the image of its inverse image. Apply the image condition and continuity, taking complements for the other kind of subset.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Surjective open maps detect open subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective open continuous map, and let $T\subseteq Y$.
theorems.statement: $T$ is open exactly when $f^{-1}(T)$ is open in $X$.
theorems.proof: Surjectivity identifies a subset with the image of its inverse image. Apply the image condition and continuity, taking complements for the other kind of subset.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Surjective open maps detect locally closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective open continuous map, and let $T\subseteq Y$.
theorems.statement: $T$ is locally closed exactly when $f^{-1}(T)$ is locally closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Apply descent of openness on the closure, using the closure formula. In the closed-map case restrict the closed map to the closure of the preimage.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closure formula for a surjective closed map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective closed continuous map, and let $T\subseteq Y$.
theorems.statement: $\overline T=f(\overline{f^{-1}(T)})$.
theorems.proof: The image of the closed preimage-closure is closed, contains the original subset, and lies in its closure by continuity.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Surjective closed maps detect closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective closed continuous map, and let $T\subseteq Y$.
theorems.statement: $T$ is closed exactly when $f^{-1}(T)$ is closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Surjectivity identifies a subset with the image of its inverse image. Apply the image condition and continuity, taking complements for the other kind of subset.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Surjective closed maps detect open subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective closed continuous map, and let $T\subseteq Y$.
theorems.statement: $T$ is open exactly when $f^{-1}(T)$ is open in $X$.
theorems.proof: Surjectivity identifies a subset with the image of its inverse image. Apply the image condition and continuity, taking complements for the other kind of subset.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Surjective closed maps detect locally closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective closed continuous map, and let $T\subseteq Y$.
theorems.statement: $T$ is locally closed exactly when $f^{-1}(T)$ is locally closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Apply descent of openness on the closure, using the closure formula. In the closed-map case restrict the closed map to the closure of the preimage.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Continuous image of a connected subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be a nonempty connected subspace of the domain of a continuous map $f$.
theorems.statement: $f(E)$ is connected in its subspace topology.
theorems.proof: Restrict to the surjection from $E$ to its image. A separation of the image pulls back to a separation of $E$.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 4.5

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closure of a connected subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space. Connected subsets are nonempty.
theorems.statement: If $T$ is connected, its closure is connected.
theorems.proof: Each nonempty relatively open side of a separation of the closure meets its dense subset $T$.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 4.4 and Definition 4.7(i)

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Connected components are closed
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space. Connected subsets are nonempty.
theorems.statement: Each component is closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Its closure is connected, so maximality gives equality.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 4.4 and Definition 4.7(i)

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Unique component containing a connected subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space. Connected subsets are nonempty.
theorems.statement: Each connected subset is contained in exactly one component.
theorems.proof: All connected supersets of the given subset meet at a point. Their union is connected and contains every such superset.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 4.4 and Definition 4.7(i)

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Partition into connected components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space. Connected subsets are nonempty.
theorems.statement: Every point lies in a unique component.
theorems.proof: Apply the preceding union construction to the singleton.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 4.4 and Definition 4.7(i)

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Finite-fibre bound for connected components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be open, closed and continuous between nonempty spaces. Assume $Y$ is connected and fix $y\in Y$ whose fibre has finite cardinality $m$.
theorems.statement: $X$ has at most $m$ connected components.
theorems.proof: If there are at least $k$ components one can split clopen pieces inductively into $k$ nonempty clopen pieces. Every piece maps onto $Y$ and therefore meets the chosen fibre.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Openness of source components over a finite fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be open, closed and continuous between nonempty spaces. Assume $Y$ is connected and fix $y\in Y$ whose fibre has finite cardinality $m$.
theorems.statement: Every component of $X$ is open.
theorems.proof: There are finitely many closed components. The union of the others is closed.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closedness of source components over a finite fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be open, closed and continuous between nonempty spaces. Assume $Y$ is connected and fix $y\in Y$ whose fibre has finite cardinality $m$.
theorems.statement: Every component of $X$ is closed.
theorems.proof: A component is maximal among connected subspaces and its closure is connected.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Nonempty component images
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be open, closed and continuous between nonempty spaces. Assume $Y$ is connected and fix $y\in Y$ whose fibre has finite cardinality $m$.
theorems.statement: The image of each component is nonempty.
theorems.proof: Every component is nonempty.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Open component images
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be open, closed and continuous between nonempty spaces. Assume $Y$ is connected and fix $y\in Y$ whose fibre has finite cardinality $m$.
theorems.statement: The image of each component is open in $Y$.
theorems.proof: The map is open and the component is open.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closed component images
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be open, closed and continuous between nonempty spaces. Assume $Y$ is connected and fix $y\in Y$ whose fibre has finite cardinality $m$.
theorems.statement: The image of each component is closed in $Y$.
theorems.proof: The map is closed and the component is closed.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Each source component covers the target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be open, closed and continuous between nonempty spaces. Assume $Y$ is connected and fix $y\in Y$ whose fibre has finite cardinality $m$.
theorems.statement: Each component maps onto $Y$.
theorems.proof: A nonempty clopen subset of a connected target must be the whole target.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Total disconnectedness of the component space
theorems.hypotheses: Give the component set of $X$ the quotient topology and write $q$ for the component projection.
theorems.statement: The component space is totally disconnected.
theorems.proof: The quotient has connected fibres and induces a bijection of components. Each source component maps to one point.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Factorization through the component space
theorems.hypotheses: Give the component set of $X$ the quotient topology and write $q$ for the component projection.
theorems.statement: Every continuous map from $X$ to a totally disconnected space factors uniquely and continuously through $q$.
theorems.proof: Its restriction to a component has connected image and therefore is constant. Surjectivity gives uniqueness and the quotient topology gives continuity.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Open subspaces inherit local connectedness
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally connected.
theorems.statement: Every open subspace is locally connected.
theorems.proof: A neighbourhood basis restricts to the connected neighbourhoods contained in the chosen open.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 4.8(i) and Proposition 4.9(i)

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Components of opens in a locally connected space
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally connected.
theorems.statement: Each component of any open subset is open in $X$.
theorems.proof: The open subspace is locally connected, so the component is open in it and in $X$.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 4.8(i) and Proposition 4.9(i)

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Basis of open connected neighbourhoods
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally connected.
theorems.statement: Every point has a neighbourhood basis of open connected sets.
theorems.proof: In each open neighbourhood choose the component of that point.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 4.8(i) and Proposition 4.9(i)

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Continuous image of an irreducible subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be an irreducible subset of the domain of a continuous map.
theorems.statement: Its image is an irreducible subspace.
theorems.proof: The image is nonempty. A cover of the image by two proper relatively closed subsets pulls back to such a cover of $E$.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closure of an irreducible subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a space, with subspaces carrying the induced topology.
theorems.statement: The closure of any irreducible subset $T$ is irreducible.
theorems.proof: In a binary closed cover of the closure, one member contains $T$ and thus its closure.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Irreducible components are closed
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a space, with subspaces carrying the induced topology.
theorems.statement: Each irreducible component is closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Taking the closure preserves irreducibility, so maximality forces equality.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Extending an irreducible subset to a component
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a space, with subspaces carrying the induced topology.
theorems.statement: An irreducible subset lies in at least one irreducible component.
theorems.proof: A nonempty chain of irreducible supersets has irreducible union: two opens meeting its union already meet a common chain member. Apply Zorn’s lemma.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Cover by irreducible components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a space, with subspaces carrying the induced topology.
theorems.statement: Every point of $X$ belongs to an irreducible component.
theorems.proof: Every singleton is irreducible and hence extends to a maximal irreducible subset.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Irredundant members are components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be covered by finitely many irreducible closed subsets, none contained in the union of the others.
theorems.statement: Each member of the cover is an irreducible component.
theorems.proof: A component containing the member is itself one of the members, so irredundancy forces equality.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Irredundant covers exhaust the components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be covered by finitely many irreducible closed subsets, none contained in the union of the others.
theorems.statement: Each irreducible component occurs in the cover.
theorems.proof: A component has a finite closed cover by its intersections with the members. By irreducibility one contains the component, and maximality gives equality.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Bound on target irreducible components
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous and surjective with exactly $n<\infty$ irreducible components in $X$.
theorems.statement: $Y$ has at most $n$ irreducible components.
theorems.proof: The closures of the images of the components form a finite irreducible closed cover. Remove redundant members to obtain precisely the components of $Y$.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Inheritance of the Kolmogorov property
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ is Kolmogorov and $Y$ is any subspace of $X$.
theorems.statement: $Y$ is Kolmogorov.
theorems.proof: Restrict a distinguishing open to the subspace.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Cover criterion for the Kolmogorov property
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ is covered by locally closed subsets carrying their subspace topologies.
theorems.statement: $X$ is Kolmogorov exactly when every member is Kolmogorov.
theorems.proof: Points with the same ambient closure have identical membership in every locally closed set. A chosen cover member containing one contains both and distinguishes them if they differ.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Inheritance of the quasi-sober property
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ is quasi-sober and $Y$ is a locally closed subspace of $X$.
theorems.statement: $Y$ is quasi-sober.
theorems.proof: The closure in $X$ of an irreducible closed subset of the subspace is irreducible. Its generic point belongs to the subspace since the latter is the intersection of an open set meeting that closure with a closed set containing it.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Cover criterion for the quasi-sober property
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ is covered by open subsets carrying their subspace topologies.
theorems.statement: $X$ is quasi-sober exactly when every member is quasi-sober.
theorems.proof: Intersect an irreducible closed subset with a cover member that meets it. This intersection is nonempty open dense in the closed subset, so a generic point of the intersection remains generic for the original closed subset.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Inheritance of the sober property
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ is sober and $Y$ is a locally closed subspace of $X$.
theorems.statement: $Y$ is sober.
theorems.proof: Apply inheritance of quasi-sobriety and of the Kolmogorov axiom.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Cover criterion for the sober property
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ is covered by open subsets carrying their subspace topologies.
theorems.statement: $X$ is sober exactly when every member is sober.
theorems.proof: Apply the local criteria for quasi-sobriety and for the Kolmogorov axiom.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Irreducibility from a dense family of irreducible fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous and open, with irreducible $Y$. Suppose the points with nonempty irreducible fibre are dense in $Y$.
theorems.statement: $X$ is irreducible.
theorems.proof: There is a nonempty fibre. The images of any two nonempty source opens intersect in a nonempty open of $Y$. Choose a point there with irreducible fibre. Its intersections with both source opens must meet.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Bijection on irreducible components for an open map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be open and continuous, with a nonempty irreducible fibre over every point.
theorems.statement: Inverse image gives a bijection from target components to source components. Its inverse takes the closure of the image.
theorems.proof: The map is onto, and its restriction over a target component is open with irreducible fibres and irreducible base. Conversely the closure of each irreducible image is irreducible. Maximality identifies the two assignments.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.1.14, applied over each component

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Continuous point-closure map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space and $X^{s}$ its space of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, topologized by meeting open subsets of $X$. Put $c(x)=\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: The point-closure map $c$ is continuous.
theorems.proof: The inverse image of the open defined by $U$ is exactly $U$.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.9.2 and (2.9.2.2–5), pp. 68–69

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Sobriety of the point-closure construction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space and $X^{s}$ its space of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, topologized by meeting open subsets of $X$. Put $c(x)=\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: $X^{s}$ is sober.
theorems.proof: An irreducible closed family consists of the irreducible closed sets contained in a closed subset $Z$ of $X$. That $Z$ is irreducible by the correspondence of opens, and is its family’s unique generic point.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.9.2 and (2.9.2.2–5), pp. 68–69

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Universal mapping property of sobrification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space and $X^{s}$ its space of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, topologized by meeting open subsets of $X$. Put $c(x)=\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: Every continuous map from $X$ into a sober space factors uniquely and continuously through $c$.
theorems.proof: Send an irreducible closed subset to the unique generic point of the closure of its image. Inverse images of opens verify continuity and force uniqueness in the Kolmogorov target.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.9.2 and (2.9.2.2–5), pp. 68–69
Stacks 0A2N · universal property for sober targets

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Bijection of opens under sobrification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space and $X^{s}$ its space of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, topologized by meeting open subsets of $X$. Put $c(x)=\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: Inverse image along $c$ bijects the opens of $X^{s}$ and $X$.
theorems.proof: The inverse sends each open to the family of irreducible closed subsets meeting it.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.9.2 and (2.9.2.2–5), pp. 68–69

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Finite intersections under sobrification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space and $X^{s}$ its space of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, topologized by meeting open subsets of $X$. Put $c(x)=\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: The bijection on opens preserves finite intersections.
theorems.proof: The inverse image of a finite intersection is the intersection of the preimages.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.9.2 and (2.9.2.2–5), pp. 68–69

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Arbitrary unions under sobrification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space and $X^{s}$ its space of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, topologized by meeting open subsets of $X$. Put $c(x)=\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: The bijection on opens preserves arbitrary unions.
theorems.proof: Inverse image commutes with arbitrary union.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.9.2 and (2.9.2.2–5), pp. 68–69

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: The image of the point-closure map is Kolmogorov
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space and $X^{s}$ its space of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, topologized by meeting open subsets of $X$. Put $c(x)=\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: The subspace $c(X)$ is Kolmogorov.
theorems.proof: The ambient sobrification is sober, hence Kolmogorov, and this property is hereditary.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Kolmogorov reflection in the sobrification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space and $X^{s}$ its space of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, topologized by meeting open subsets of $X$. Put $c(x)=\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: Every continuous map from $X$ to a Kolmogorov space factors uniquely and continuously through the surjection to $c(X)$.
theorems.proof: Points with the same closure have the same image in a Kolmogorov target. Each open of $X$ is the pullback of an open in $c(X)$, which gives continuity of the factorization.
refs: Stacks 0A2N · universal property for Kolmogorov targets

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Removing an irreducible component while retaining connectedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be connected, with finitely many irreducible components and at least two.
theorems.statement: One component can be omitted so that the union of all the others is still connected.
theorems.proof: The finite component-intersection graph is connected: a disconnected graph would split the space into two disjoint closed unions. Remove a leaf of a spanning tree. The remaining components have connected union by the connected intersections along the remaining edges.
refs: Stacks 0GM3 · existence of a removable index

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: A component is contained in its quasicomponent
theorems.hypotheses: Take any point of a space.
theorems.statement: Its connected component is contained in its quasicomponent.
theorems.proof: A clopen neighbourhood separates its complement from every connected subset through the chosen point.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Singleton cover of an indiscrete space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be indiscrete with at least two points.
theorems.statement: Its singleton subspaces give a cover by discrete Kolmogorov spaces.
theorems.proof: Each singleton has the unique one-point topology.
refs: Pi-Base S000004 · Two-point indiscrete space, a finite instance
Stacks 0B32 · cover by discrete Kolmogorov subspaces

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Singleton cover of an infinite cofinite space
theorems.hypotheses: Give an infinite set the cofinite topology.
theorems.statement: The singleton subspaces form a cover by discrete sober spaces.
theorems.proof: Each singleton is its own unique generic point.
refs: Pi-Base S000015 · Countable cofinite space, a countable instance
Stacks 0B33 · cover by discrete sober subspaces

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Hausdorff irreducible spaces are singletons
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: $X$ is irreducible exactly when it consists of one point.
theorems.proof: Irreducibility requires a point. Two distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods, whereas any singleton is irreducible.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Irreducible subsets of a Hausdorff space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be any subset of a Hausdorff space.
theorems.statement: $E$ is irreducible exactly when it consists of one point.
theorems.proof: The subspace is Hausdorff, so the whole-space criterion applies to it.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Subspaces of a Noetherian space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be any subset of a Noetherian space.
theorems.statement: $E$ with its induced topology is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: Represent each closed term of a descending chain by an ambient closed set. Replace each representative by its intersection with all preceding representatives to produce a descending ambient chain. Stabilization descends to $E$.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Noetherian continuous image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous and give the image its subspace topology.
theorems.statement: If $X$ is Noetherian, its image is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: Pull a descending closed chain back to $X$. Surjectivity onto the image detects stabilization.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Locally Noetherian open image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous and give the image its subspace topology.
theorems.statement: If $X$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ is open, its image is locally Noetherian.
theorems.proof: At each image point choose a preimage and a Noetherian neighbourhood there. Its image is Noetherian by the first assertion and contains an open neighbourhood by openness.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Finite union of Noetherian subspaces
theorems.hypotheses: Take finitely many Noetherian subspaces of a space.
theorems.statement: Their union in its subspace topology is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: A descending closed chain restricts to an eventually constant chain on each member. A common index works because there are only finitely many members.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: An obstruction to being a locally Noetherian scheme space
theorems.hypotheses: Give the positive integers the topology of finite initial segments, together with the whole set and the empty set.
theorems.statement: It cannot be homeomorphic to the underlying space of a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.proof: The space is nonempty without a closed point. Every nonempty locally Noetherian scheme has a closed point.
refs: Stacks 02IL · existence of a closed point in a nonempty locally Noetherian scheme

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Dimension of the empty space
theorems.hypotheses: Use the extended order of dimensions with the empty supremum equal to negative infinity.
theorems.statement: Dimension equals negative infinity exactly on the empty space.
theorems.proof: In a nonempty space the closure of any point is an irreducible closed subset and gives a chain of length zero.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Dimension as a supremum of local dimensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be any space, including the empty one.
theorems.statement: $\dim X=\sup_{x\in X}\dim_x X$.
theorems.proof: The dimension at each point is bounded by the global dimension. Given a chain, take a point in its smallest member. Intersecting with any neighbourhood of the point preserves every strict inclusion, since each intersection is dense in the corresponding irreducible member.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Krull dimension of Euclidean space
theorems.hypotheses: Equip $\mathbb R^n$ with its usual topology for an integer $n\geq0$.
theorems.statement: Its topological Krull dimension is zero.
theorems.proof: The space is nonempty Hausdorff. The only irreducible closed subsets are singletons, so every chain has length zero.
refs: Pi-Base S000025 · Euclidean real line, the case n = 1

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Krull dimension of the Sierpiński space
theorems.hypotheses: Use a finite linearly ordered set with all terminal segments open.
theorems.statement: For two elements the dimension is one.
theorems.proof: The closed sets other than the empty set are the lower singleton and the whole space, giving exactly one strict inclusion.
refs: Pi-Base S000010 · Sierpiński space, the two-point case

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Finite spaces of every nonnegative Krull dimension
theorems.hypotheses: Use a finite linearly ordered set with all terminal segments open.
theorems.statement: For each integer $n\geq0$ the chain of $n+1$ points has Krull dimension $n$.
theorems.proof: The nonempty closed initial segments form one chain of $n+1$ members. Each has a generic point at its maximum.
refs: Pi-Base S000010 · Sierpiński space, the two-point case

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Codimension after meeting an open subspace
theorems.hypotheses: Take an irreducible closed $Y\subseteq X$ and an open $U$ meeting $Y$.
theorems.statement: The codimension of $Y$ in $X$ equals the codimension of $Y\cap U$ in $U$.
theorems.proof: Intersection with $U$ and ambient closure identify the posets of irreducible closed sets above the two given subsets, preserving chain lengths.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Locally closed subspace of a catenary space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be catenary and $E$ a locally closed subset.
theorems.statement: $E$ is catenary.
theorems.proof: An open restriction preserves each interval meeting both endpoints by closure. A closed restriction retains every intermediate subset between two endpoints lying inside the closed set.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Composition of quasi-compact continuous maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let two composable continuous maps be quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: Their composite is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: The second inverse image of a quasi-compact open is open and quasi-compact. The first map thus has quasi-compact inverse image of that set.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closed subspace of a quasi-compact space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be a closed subset of a quasi-compact space $X$.
theorems.statement: $Z$ is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Extend a relative open cover to ambient opens and add the complement of $Z$. A finite subcover restricts to $Z$.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 5.4
Stacks 005C · quasi-compactness of the closed subspace

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Quasi-compact subsets of Hausdorff spaces are closed
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: Any quasi-compact subset $E$ of $X$ is closed.
theorems.proof: For a point outside the subset, separate it from each point of the subset. Finitely many of the latter neighbourhoods cover the subset, so intersect the corresponding neighbourhoods of the outside point.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Separating two disjoint quasi-compact subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: Any two disjoint quasi-compact subsets admit disjoint open neighbourhoods.
theorems.proof: First separate each point of the first subset from the whole second subset by a finite covering argument. Apply quasi-compactness of the first subset once more.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closedness versus quasi-compactness inside a compact Hausdorff space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be a subset of a quasi-compact Hausdorff space.
theorems.statement: $E$ is closed precisely when it is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Closed subspaces inherit quasi-compactness. Conversely finite Hausdorff separation supplies an exterior neighbourhood at every point outside a quasi-compact subset.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Propositions 5.4–5.5

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Finite-intersection property for closed sets
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ is quasi-compact and a family of closed subsets has nonempty intersection for each finite subfamily, including the empty one.
theorems.statement: The whole family has nonempty intersection.
theorems.proof: Otherwise their open complements cover the space. A finite subcover contradicts the finite-intersection hypothesis.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 5.1 and Proposition 5.2

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Quasi-compact continuous image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous. Give every image its induced topology.
theorems.statement: If $X$ is quasi-compact, its image is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Pull an open cover back and choose a finite subcover in the source. Its image covers the original image.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 5.6, quasi-compactness of continuous images

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Retrocompact image of a quasi-compact map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous. Give every image its induced topology.
theorems.statement: If $f$ is quasi-compact, its image is retrocompact in $Y$.
theorems.proof: For each quasi-compact open of $Y$, its intersection with the image is the image of a quasi-compact inverse image.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 5.6, quasi-compactness of continuous images

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of the locus of closed points
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be quasi-compact and Kolmogorov.
theorems.statement: Its set of closed points is quasi-compact in the induced topology.
theorems.proof: Lift a cover of the closed points to ambient opens. Their closed complement, if inhabited, would be quasi-compact and Kolmogorov and contain a point closed also in $X$. Thus the lifted cover covers $X$.
refs: Stacks 08ZM · quasi-compactness of the closed-point subspace

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closed unions of components as intersections of clopens
theorems.hypotheses: Assume the ambient space is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact opens, and the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: A subset is an intersection of clopens precisely when it is closed and is a union of connected components.
theorems.proof: Each clopen preserves entire components. Conversely the component of an exterior point is an intersection of clopens disjoint in total from the given closed quasi-compact union. A finite subintersection already misses it, and the complementary clopen separates the point from the subset.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Retrocompactness of subsets of a Noetherian space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be any subset of a Noetherian space.
theorems.statement: $E$ is retrocompact.
theorems.proof: Its intersection with every quasi-compact ambient open is again a subspace of a Noetherian space, hence Noetherian and quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Alexander subbase theorem
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a subbasis for $X$ and assume every cover by its members has a finite refinement.
theorems.statement: $X$ is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: A maximal open cover with no finite subcover exists by Zorn’s lemma if any such cover exists. Its subbasic members cannot cover. At a missed point choose a basic intersection inside one member of the cover. Adjoining each factor separately gives a finite subcover, and combining them yields a finite subcover from the original family.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Local compactness conventions in a Hausdorff space
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: A basis of quasi-compact neighbourhoods exists at each point exactly when each point has one quasi-compact neighbourhood.
theorems.proof: Inside a quasi-compact Hausdorff neighbourhood separate the point from the closed complement of any smaller prescribed open. The resulting closed quasi-compact neighbourhood lies inside that open.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Definition 5.11 and Lemma 5.12

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Closed shrinking of an open cover
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an indexed open cover of a quasi-compact Hausdorff space.
theorems.statement: There exists an open cover on the same index set such that the closure of each new open lies in its corresponding original open.
theorems.proof: Shrink a neighbourhood around each point inside one cover member using regularity. Choose finitely many that cover, and unite the chosen neighbourhoods for each original index.
refs: Stacks 09UV · existence of a common shrinking

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Refinement with prescribed intersections
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an indexed open cover of a quasi-compact Hausdorff space. Fix an integer $p\geq0$ and, for every ordered tuple of $p+1$ original indices (repetitions allowed), an open cover of the corresponding intersection. For an empty intersection use a cover containing the empty open, so that a member can be chosen even there. All conclusions concern one common refinement and one index map.
theorems.statement: There are an open cover and an assignment of each new index to an original index satisfying the closure and intersection conditions of the source simultaneously.
theorems.proof: Reduce to a finite cover. Induct on the tuple length, first treating repeated indices. For each remaining bad tuple, subdivide one member using a finite cover of the intersection of the closures. Refinement preserves earlier containments.
refs: Stacks 09UW · existence of common cover and index map

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Closures of the common refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an indexed open cover of a quasi-compact Hausdorff space. Fix an integer $p\geq0$ and, for every ordered tuple of $p+1$ original indices (repetitions allowed), an open cover of the corresponding intersection. For an empty intersection use a cover containing the empty open, so that a member can be chosen even there. All conclusions concern one common refinement and one index map.
theorems.statement: For the common refinement, the closure of every member is contained in its assigned original open.
theorems.proof: Reduce to a finite cover. Induct on the tuple length, first treating repeated indices. For each remaining bad tuple, subdivide one member using a finite cover of the intersection of the closures. Refinement preserves earlier containments.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Multiple intersections of the common refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an indexed open cover of a quasi-compact Hausdorff space. Fix an integer $p\geq0$ and, for every ordered tuple of $p+1$ original indices (repetitions allowed), an open cover of the corresponding intersection. For an empty intersection use a cover containing the empty open, so that a member can be chosen even there. All conclusions concern one common refinement and one index map.
theorems.statement: Each intersection of $p+1$ new members is contained in a single member of the given cover of the corresponding original intersection.
theorems.proof: Reduce to a finite cover. Induct on the tuple length, first treating repeated indices. For each remaining bad tuple, subdivide one member using a finite cover of the intersection of the closures. Refinement preserves earlier containments.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Coverage by lifted opens in the locally compact case
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be locally quasi-compact Hausdorff and $Z$ a quasi-compact subspace. Fix $p\geq0$, a family of ambient opens covering $Z$, and for every ordered $(p+1)$-tuple an open within the corresponding intersection with the same trace on $Z$. All conclusions refer to a single family of ambient opens indexed by the original family.
theorems.statement: There exists a common lifted family satisfying all the source conditions. Their union contains $Z$.
theorems.proof: Reduce to finitely many indices within a quasi-compact neighbourhood of the closed subset. Shrink the cover and induct on the tuple length, removing the closed bad loci disjoint from the subset.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closure control on lifted opens in the locally compact case
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be locally quasi-compact Hausdorff and $Z$ a quasi-compact subspace. Fix $p\geq0$, a family of ambient opens covering $Z$, and for every ordered $(p+1)$-tuple an open within the corresponding intersection with the same trace on $Z$. All conclusions refer to a single family of ambient opens indexed by the original family.
theorems.statement: There exists a common lifted family satisfying all the source conditions. The entire closure of each new open lies in its original open.
