theorems.proof: Reduce to finitely many indices within a quasi-compact neighbourhood of the closed subset. Shrink the cover and induct on the tuple length, removing the closed bad loci disjoint from the subset.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Tuple control for lifted opens in the locally compact case
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be locally quasi-compact Hausdorff and $Z$ a quasi-compact subspace. Fix $p\geq0$, a family of ambient opens covering $Z$, and for every ordered $(p+1)$-tuple an open within the corresponding intersection with the same trace on $Z$. All conclusions refer to a single family of ambient opens indexed by the original family.
theorems.statement: There exists a common lifted family satisfying all the source conditions. For every ordered tuple the intersection of its new opens lies in the designated open for that tuple.
theorems.proof: Reduce to finitely many indices within a quasi-compact neighbourhood of the closed subset. Shrink the cover and induct on the tuple length, removing the closed bad loci disjoint from the subset.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Coverage by lifted opens under separation along the subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be a quasi-compact subset of $X$ such that any two distinct points of $Z$ have disjoint neighbourhoods open in $X$. Fix $p\geq0$, a family of ambient opens covering $Z$, and for every ordered $(p+1)$-tuple an open within the corresponding intersection with the same trace on $Z$. All conclusions refer to a single family of ambient opens indexed by the original family.
theorems.statement: There exists a common lifted family satisfying all the source conditions. Their union contains $Z$.
theorems.proof: Ambient separation and compactness of the complement inside $Z$ give neighbourhoods whose closures have the required trace on $Z$. Take finitely many, then induct on tuple length, removing closures of bad intersections disjoint from $Z$.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Containment of lifted opens under separation along the subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be a quasi-compact subset of $X$ such that any two distinct points of $Z$ have disjoint neighbourhoods open in $X$. Fix $p\geq0$, a family of ambient opens covering $Z$, and for every ordered $(p+1)$-tuple an open within the corresponding intersection with the same trace on $Z$. All conclusions refer to a single family of ambient opens indexed by the original family.
theorems.statement: There exists a common lifted family satisfying all the source conditions. Each new open is contained in its corresponding original open.
theorems.proof: Ambient separation and compactness of the complement inside $Z$ give neighbourhoods whose closures have the required trace on $Z$. Take finitely many, then induct on tuple length, removing closures of bad intersections disjoint from $Z$.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closure control on lifted opens under separation along the subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be a quasi-compact subset of $X$ such that any two distinct points of $Z$ have disjoint neighbourhoods open in $X$. Fix $p\geq0$, a family of ambient opens covering $Z$, and for every ordered $(p+1)$-tuple an open within the corresponding intersection with the same trace on $Z$. All conclusions refer to a single family of ambient opens indexed by the original family.
theorems.statement: There exists a common lifted family satisfying all the source conditions. The trace on $Z$ of each closure lies in its original open.
theorems.proof: Ambient separation and compactness of the complement inside $Z$ give neighbourhoods whose closures have the required trace on $Z$. Take finitely many, then induct on tuple length, removing closures of bad intersections disjoint from $Z$.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Tuple control for lifted opens under separation along the subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be a quasi-compact subset of $X$ such that any two distinct points of $Z$ have disjoint neighbourhoods open in $X$. Fix $p\geq0$, a family of ambient opens covering $Z$, and for every ordered $(p+1)$-tuple an open within the corresponding intersection with the same trace on $Z$. All conclusions refer to a single family of ambient opens indexed by the original family.
theorems.statement: There exists a common lifted family satisfying all the source conditions. For every ordered tuple the intersection of its new opens lies in the designated open for that tuple.
theorems.proof: Ambient separation and compactness of the complement inside $Z$ give neighbourhoods whose closures have the required trace on $Z$. Take finitely many, then induct on tuple length, removing closures of bad intersections disjoint from $Z$.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Existence of limits of spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small diagram of spaces and continuous maps.
theorems.statement: The diagram admits a limit in topological spaces.
theorems.proof: The coherent tuples with their induced product topology represent all compatible cones, by the product universal property.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Underlying set of a topological limit
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small diagram of spaces and continuous maps.
theorems.statement: Forgetting topology sends the limiting cone to a limiting cone of sets.
theorems.proof: The underlying points are exactly the compatible tuples, and the projections are their coordinate maps.
refs: Stacks 08ZT · preservation by the forgetful functor

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Single-stage cylinders generate cofiltered limits
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small cofiltered diagram of spaces with limit $X$ and its canonical projections.
theorems.statement: Every open in $X$ is a union of inverse images of opens from individual stages, with at most one open needed per stage.
theorems.proof: A finite family of coordinate conditions can be pulled to a common stage and intersected there. At a repeated stage take the union of all opens used there.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Quasi-compact open descended from one stage
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small cofiltered diagram of spaces with limit $X$ and its canonical projections.
theorems.statement: Every quasi-compact open of $X$ is the inverse image of an open from one stage.
theorems.proof: Choose finitely many single-stage cylinders covering that open. Pull their representing opens to a common stage and take their union there.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Cofiltered limit recognition
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a space has as underlying set the limit of a small cofiltered diagram of spaces, and the inverse images of opens at individual stages form a basis of its topology.
theorems.statement: The indicated projections present this space as the limit in topological spaces.
theorems.proof: By the cylinder basis calculation, its topology is exactly the limit topology on the common underlying set.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Tychonoff theorem for arbitrary quasi-compact spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Take any set-indexed family of quasi-compact spaces, using the ordinary product topology and the axiom of choice.
theorems.statement: Its product is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Use Alexander’s theorem on the subbasis of single-coordinate cylinders. If a subbasic cover has no finite subcover, each coordinate’s cylinders miss a point in that factor. A tuple of these points contradicts coverage.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Theorem 5.8

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of limits of compact Hausdorff spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Assume every object of a small diagram is Hausdorff and quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: Its topological limit is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: The compatibility conditions are preimages of closed diagonals and cut out a closed subset of the quasi-compact product.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Lemma 1.13 and Theorem 5.8

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Nonempty cofiltered limit of compact Hausdorff spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small cofiltered diagram of nonempty quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces.
theorems.statement: Its limit has a point.
theorems.proof: Compatibility imposes closed conditions in the quasi-compact product. Finitely many constraints have a common solution by cofilteredness and a point of a common cone stage. The finite-intersection property then gives a coherent tuple.
refs: J. P. May, An outline summary of basic point set topology, Proposition 5.2 and Theorem 5.8
Stacks 0A2R · existence of a compatible family of points

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Finite unions of constructible sets
theorems.hypotheses: Work in any fixed space, using global constructibility.
theorems.statement: A finite union of constructible subsets is constructible.
theorems.proof: Concatenate their finite presentations by differences of retrocompact opens.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), 2.3.2–2.3.3

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Finite intersections of constructible sets
theorems.hypotheses: Work in any fixed space, using global constructibility.
theorems.statement: A finite intersection of constructible subsets is constructible.
theorems.proof: Distribute finite intersections over unions and use closure of retrocompact opens under finite unions and intersections.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), 2.3.2–2.3.3

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Complements of constructible sets
theorems.hypotheses: Work in any fixed space, using global constructibility.
theorems.statement: The complement of a constructible subset is constructible.
theorems.proof: The complement of one difference is the union of an open and the complement of an open. Distribute finite meets to get the required form.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), 2.3.2–2.3.3

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Trace of a constructible subset on an open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be constructible in $X$ and $U$ open in $X$.
theorems.statement: $E\cap U$ is constructible in $U$.
theorems.proof: A quasi-compact open in $U$ is quasi-compact open in $X$. Hence a retrocompact ambient open restricts to one in $U$.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.3.8(i)

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Ambient constructibility from a retrocompact open
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $U$ is retrocompact open in $X$ and $E$ constructible in $U$.
theorems.statement: $E$ is constructible in $X$.
theorems.proof: A retrocompact open in $U$ is open in $X$ and remains retrocompact there by first intersecting each quasi-compact test open with $U$. Apply this to the presentation of $E$.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Proposition 2.3.8(ii)

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructibility on a finite retrocompact open cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let finitely many retrocompact open subsets cover $X$.
theorems.statement: A subset is constructible exactly when each relative trace on a cover member is constructible.
theorems.proof: Open restriction proves necessity. Extend the traces along the retrocompact open inclusions and take their finite union.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), Corollary 2.3.9

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructible trace on a closed subset with quasi-compact complement
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be closed in $X$ with quasi-compact complement. Let $E$ be constructible in $X$.
theorems.statement: $E\cap Z$ is constructible in $Z$.
theorems.proof: Adjoin the whole complement of $Z$ to a quasi-compact open of $Z$ to obtain an ambient quasi-compact open. Intersecting it with an ambient retrocompact open and then with the closed $Z$ preserves quasi-compactness.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructible trace on a retrocompact subspace
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ has a basis of quasi-compact opens, $T$ is retrocompact in $X$, and $E$ is constructible in $X$.
theorems.statement: $E\cap T$ is constructible in $T$.
theorems.proof: Each quasi-compact open in $T$ is the trace of a finite union of ambient basic opens. Intersect the latter union with an ambient retrocompact open and then with $T$ to test retrocompactness in $T$.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructible extension across a closed inclusion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be closed in $X$ with retrocompact open complement, and $E$ constructible in $Z$.
theorems.statement: $E$ is constructible in $X$.
theorems.proof: Extend each retrocompact open of $Z$ by adjoining its ambient complement $X\setminus Z$. Each extended open is retrocompact by testing against quasi-compact opens. Differences of the two extensions give the original pieces.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Trace of a constructible subset on another constructible subspace
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ has a quasi-compact open basis, and $E,F$ are constructible in $X$.
theorems.statement: $E\cap F$ is constructible in $E$.
theorems.proof: The first constructible subset is retrocompact. Apply the retrocompact trace criterion.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Transitivity of constructibility over a quasi-compact open basis
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ has a quasi-compact open basis, $E$ is constructible in $X$, and $F$ is constructible in $E$.
theorems.statement: $F$ is constructible in $X$.
theorems.proof: Decompose $E$ into differences of retrocompact opens and restrict $F$ to each piece. Extend first across the closed inclusion in a retrocompact open and then across the open inclusion, then take the finite union.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructibility from a locally closed presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be quasi-compact, have a quasi-compact open basis and quasi-compact pairwise intersections of quasi-compact opens. Let $T$ be locally closed and quasi-compact with retrocompact complement.
theorems.statement: $T$ is constructible in $X$.
theorems.proof: Write $T$ as the intersection of its closure with one quasi-compact open $U$ by a finite basic covering. The complement of $T$ in $U$ is open and quasi-compact by retrocompactness. Both opens are retrocompact by the intersection hypothesis.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructibility on a finite constructible cover
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ has a quasi-compact open basis and a finite covering by constructible subspaces.
theorems.statement: A subset is constructible precisely when each of its traces is constructible in the respective cover member.
theorems.proof: Restriction and transitivity of constructibility apply on each member, and a finite union recovers the subset.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Dense constructible traces contain a dense open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be an irreducible subspace of $X$, and let $E$ be a finite union of locally closed subsets of $X$.
theorems.statement: The trace of $E$ is dense in $Z$ precisely when it contains a dense open of $Z$.
theorems.proof: Irreducibility forces one among finitely many locally closed pieces of a dense trace to be dense. A dense locally closed piece is open in the ambient subspace.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Testing a dense trace at a generic point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be an irreducible subspace of $X$, and let $E$ be a finite union of locally closed subsets of $X$. Assume $Z$ has a specified generic point.
theorems.statement: The trace of $E$ is dense in $Z$ precisely when $E$ contains that generic point.
theorems.proof: Every nonempty relative open contains the generic point. Conversely a subset containing the point has closure containing its whole point closure.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructibility and finite locally closed decompositions
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $X$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: A subset is constructible precisely when it is a finite union of locally closed subsets.
theorems.proof: Every ambient open is retrocompact since all subspaces are Noetherian and quasi-compact. Differences of opens are exactly the locally closed subsets.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Constructible inverse images between Noetherian spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous between Noetherian spaces and let $E$ be constructible in $Y$.
theorems.statement: The inverse image of $E$ is constructible in $X$.
theorems.proof: Use a finite locally closed presentation. Its preimages are locally closed by continuity and give constructibility in the Noetherian source.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructibility tested on irreducible closed subspaces
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is Noetherian and fix a subset $E$.
theorems.statement: $E$ is constructible exactly when for every irreducible closed $Z$, a dense trace on $Z$ contains a nonempty relatively open subset of $Z$.
theorems.proof: Necessity follows from the dense-trace test. Conversely, use Noetherian induction on closed subsets. Reduce a reducible closed subset to its finitely many components. For an irreducible one, remove an open contained in the trace or use the proper closure of a nondense trace.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Neighbourhood criterion on irreducible closed subspaces
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is Noetherian, $x$ is a point, and $E$ is constructible.
theorems.statement: $E$ contains a neighbourhood of $x$ exactly when it meets every irreducible closed subspace through $x$ in a dense subset.
theorems.proof: Forward use the density of nonempty opens in an irreducible space. For the converse a minimal closed subset where the neighbourhood criterion fails must be irreducible. Its dense constructible trace contains an open, and induction on the complement yields the desired neighbourhood.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Openness tested on irreducible closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be an arbitrary subset of a Noetherian space.
theorems.statement: $E$ is open exactly when its trace on each irreducible closed subset is either empty or contains a nonempty relatively open subset.
theorems.proof: The trace condition gives constructibility by the preceding generic test. At every point of $E$ all the relevant traces contain nonempty opens and are dense, giving the neighbourhood criterion.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Open product tube around two quasi-compact subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\subseteq X$ and $B\subseteq Y$ be quasi-compact and let $A\times B$ lie in an open $W\subseteq X\times Y$.
theorems.statement: There are opens containing $A$ and $B$ whose product lies in $W$.
theorems.proof: For each point of $A$, cover its slice over $B$ by finitely many basic rectangles and intersect their first factors. A second finite selection over $A$ and intersection in the second coordinate gives the required rectangle.
refs: Stacks 005N · existence of an open rectangle

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: A locally closed nonclosed point in a non-Jacobson space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Kolmogorov with a basis of quasi-compact opens, and suppose $X$ is not Jacobson.
theorems.statement: It has a point whose singleton is locally closed and is not closed.
theorems.proof: A nonempty locally closed set misses all ambient closed points. Shrink its open part to a quasi-compact basic open. The resulting nonempty locally closed subspace is quasi-compact and Kolmogorov and has a relatively closed point.
refs: Stacks 02I7 · existence of the nonclosed point

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Jacobson property on an open cover
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any open covering of $X$.
theorems.statement: $X$ is Jacobson exactly when each cover member is Jacobson.
theorems.proof: Criterion: every nonempty locally closed subset contains an ambient closed point. A relatively closed point on a Jacobson chart is globally closed once every chart is Jacobson: its singleton is locally closed and every chart meeting its closure forces the same point there.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Closed points on Jacobson charts
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any open covering of $X$.
theorems.statement: When these conditions hold the closed points of $X$ are exactly the union of the closed points of the cover members.
theorems.proof: A relatively closed point of an open chart has locally closed singleton in $X$. In a Jacobson space this singleton contains an ambient closed point, hence is closed. The reverse inclusion holds by restriction.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Jacobson inheritance for an open subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $T$ be an open subset of $X$.
theorems.statement: The subspace $T$ is Jacobson.
theorems.proof: Locally write $T$ as a union of locally closed pieces. Intersect any nonempty locally closed test subset of $T$ with a piece that it meets. This gives a nonempty locally closed subset in an open of $X$ and hence contains an ambient closed point.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closed points of an open subset in a Jacobson space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $T$ be an open subset of $X$.
theorems.statement: Every point closed in $T$ is closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Apply the same locally closed test to the singleton in $T$. It must contain an ambient closed point, necessarily itself.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Jacobson inheritance for a closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $T$ be a closed subset of $X$.
theorems.statement: The subspace $T$ is Jacobson.
theorems.proof: Locally write $T$ as a union of locally closed pieces. Intersect any nonempty locally closed test subset of $T$ with a piece that it meets. This gives a nonempty locally closed subset in an open of $X$ and hence contains an ambient closed point.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closed points of a closed subset in a Jacobson space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $T$ be a closed subset of $X$.
theorems.statement: Every point closed in $T$ is closed in $X$.
theorems.proof: Apply the same locally closed test to the singleton in $T$. It must contain an ambient closed point, necessarily itself.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Jacobson inheritance for a locally closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $T$ be a locally closed subset of $X$.
theorems.statement: The subspace $T$ is Jacobson.
theorems.proof: Locally write $T$ as a union of locally closed pieces. Intersect any nonempty locally closed test subset of $T$ with a piece that it meets. This gives a nonempty locally closed subset in an open of $X$ and hence contains an ambient closed point.

theorems.name: Closed points of a subset which locally on the ambient space is a union of locally closed subsets in a Jacobson space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $T$ be a subset which locally on the ambient space is a union of locally closed subsets of $X$.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Closed-point trace bijection for finite unions of locally closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $X_0$ be its subspace of closed points. Use the trace map $E\mapsto E\cap X_0$.
theorems.statement: Trace bijects finite unions of locally closed subsets of $X$ with those of $X_0$.
theorems.proof: Finite unions of locally closed subsets form a Boolean algebra. Every nonempty difference contains an ambient closed point by the Jacobson property, so distinct such sets have distinct traces. Lift open and closed subsets by the subspace topology and distribute intersections and unions to obtain surjectivity.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Order on closed-point traces for finite unions of locally closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $X_0$ be its subspace of closed points. Use the trace map $E\mapsto E\cap X_0$.
theorems.statement: The correspondence on finite unions of locally closed subsets preserves and reflects containment.
theorems.proof: Finite unions of locally closed subsets form a Boolean algebra. Every nonempty difference contains an ambient closed point by the Jacobson property, so distinct such sets have distinct traces. Lift open and closed subsets by the subspace topology and distribute intersections and unions to obtain surjectivity.

theorems.name: Closed-point traces of locally closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $X_0$ be its subspace of closed points. Use the trace map $E\mapsto E\cap X_0$.
theorems.statement: The bijection restricts to a bijection on locally closed subsets.
theorems.proof: Finite unions of locally closed subsets form a Boolean algebra. refs: Stacks 005Z · restriction to locally closed subsets

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Closed-point trace bijection for constructible subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Jacobson and let $X_0$ be its subspace of closed points. Use the trace map $E\mapsto E\cap X_0$.
theorems.statement: Trace bijects constructible subsets of $X$ with those of $X_0$.
theorems.proof: A family of ambient opens covers a Jacobson space if and only if it covers its closed points. Apply this inside each open Jacobson subspace to detect quasi-compactness of opens, then retrocompactness of opens; finite Boolean combinations give the constructible correspondence.
