theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Complement exchanges specialization and generalization stability
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any subset $T$ of a space.
theorems.statement: $T$ is stable under specialization precisely when its complement is stable under generalization.
theorems.proof: Taking the contrapositive for every ordered specialization pair gives the equivalence.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Composition preserves specialization lifting
theorems.hypotheses: Let two composable maps of spaces each lift specializations.
theorems.statement: Their composition also lifts specializations.
theorems.proof: Start with a source point and the specified relation in the final target. Lift first along the second map at the image of the source point, then along the first at the source point.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Image preserves specialization stability under lifting
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ lift specializations and let $T$ be a source subset stable under specialization.
theorems.statement: Its image is stable under specialization.
theorems.proof: Lift the given specialization starting from a chosen preimage in the stable subset. The lifted point still lies in that subset.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Composition preserves generalization lifting
theorems.hypotheses: Let two composable maps of spaces each lift generalizations.
theorems.statement: Their composition also lifts generalizations.
theorems.proof: Start with a source point and the specified relation in the final target. Lift first along the second map at the image of the source point, then along the first at the source point.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Image preserves generalization stability under lifting
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ lift generalizations and let $T$ be a source subset stable under generalization.
theorems.statement: Its image is stable under generalization.
theorems.proof: Lift the given generalization starting from a chosen preimage in the stable subset. The lifted point still lies in that subset.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Lifting generalizations along an open map
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $f:X\to Y$ is open and continuous, $X$ is Noetherian and quasi-sober, and $Y$ is Kolmogorov.
theorems.statement: Generalizations lift along $f$.
theorems.proof: Openness puts the chosen source point in the closure of the fibre over the generalization. This fibre has finitely many irreducible components. A generic point of the closure of a suitable component specializes to the chosen point and maps to the desired target point by the Kolmogorov property.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Kolmogorov quotient of a finite-fibre topological relation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $s,t:R\to U$ and $q:U\to X$ be continuous, with $q$ open, $U$ sober, $s,t$ each having finite fibres and each lifting generalizations. Assume the pairs $(t(r),s(r))$ form an equivalence relation and $q$ is its set quotient.
theorems.statement: The quotient space $X$ is Kolmogorov.
theorems.proof: Each class is finite. Generalization lifting makes the union of the point closures of a class saturated. If two classes specialize in both directions, alternately lift along them. Finiteness forces repetition and antisymmetry in the sober source identifies the classes.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Dimension bound under lifting of specializations
theorems.hypotheses: Let the map be surjective with sober target, and suppose specializations lift.
theorems.statement: Source Krull dimension is at least target Krull dimension.
theorems.proof: A chain of irreducible closed target subsets gives a chain of distinct generic points ordered by specialization. Starting at the appropriate endpoint, lift the chain. Continuity and the distinct images make the resulting chain of closures strict.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Dimension bound under lifting of generalizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let the map be surjective with sober target, and suppose generalizations lift.
theorems.statement: Source Krull dimension is at least target Krull dimension.
theorems.proof: A chain of irreducible closed target subsets gives a chain of distinct generic points ordered by specialization. Starting at the appropriate endpoint, lift the chain. Continuity and the distinct images make the resulting chain of closures strict.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructible subsets stable under specialization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a sober Noetherian space and $E$ a constructible subset stable under specialization.
theorems.statement: The subset is closed.
theorems.proof: Each component of the closure has dense constructible trace containing its generic point. Stability includes all its specializations.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Constructible subsets stable under generalization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a sober Noetherian space and $E$ a constructible subset stable under generalization.
theorems.statement: The subset is open.
theorems.proof: Apply the closed case to the constructible complement, which is stable under specialization.

theorems.subject: space-integer-function
theorems.name: Codimension read from a dimension function
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be sober with dimension function $d$. Suppose $x$ specializes to $y$.
theorems.statement: The codimension of the closure of $y$ in the closure of $x$ equals $d(x)-d(y)$.
theorems.proof: A maximal chain of irreducible closed subsets corresponds to successive immediate specializations, and the unit drops telescope.

theorems.subject: space-integer-function
theorems.name: Local constancy of the difference of two dimension functions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be locally Noetherian and sober and fix two dimension functions on $X$.
theorems.statement: Their difference is locally constant.
theorems.proof: In a Noetherian neighbourhood, discard the finitely many irreducible components missing the chosen point. On each remaining component the codimension formula makes the difference constant with its value at that point.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Local existence of dimension functions
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian, sober and catenary.
theorems.statement: Every point has an open neighbourhood admitting a dimension function.
theorems.proof: Shrink a Noetherian neighbourhood to remove components and components of pairwise intersections missing the chosen point. Normalize negative codimension on each remaining component to vanish there. Additivity makes the formulas agree on overlaps.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Obstruction class for a global dimension function
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian, sober and catenary. Use ordinary sheaf cohomology of its underlying space with the constant sheaf of integers.
theorems.statement: The obstruction to a dimension function is the class of its torsor in $H^1(X,\mathbb Z)$, and it vanishes exactly when a global dimension function exists.
theorems.proof: Local existence and locally constant differences make the sheaf of dimension functions a torsor under the sheaf of locally constant integer-valued functions. Its class is zero precisely when this torsor admits a section.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Finite unions of nowhere dense subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Take any finite family of nowhere dense subsets in a space.
theorems.statement: Their union is nowhere dense.
theorems.proof: Complements of their closures are open dense sets. A finite intersection of open dense sets meets each nonempty open, and is the complement of the closure of the union.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Nowhere dense subset of an open subspace
theorems.hypotheses: Let $U$ be open in $X$ and $T$ nowhere dense in $U$.
theorems.statement: $T$ is nowhere dense in $X$.
theorems.proof: Any nonempty ambient open in the closure of $T$ meets $T$, so its intersection with $U$ is a nonempty relative open in the relative closure, a contradiction.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Locality of nowhere denseness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an open cover of $X$ and assume that each trace of $T$ on a member is nowhere dense there.
theorems.statement: $T$ is nowhere dense in $X$.
theorems.proof: Relative closure on an open equals the trace of ambient closure. A nonempty open in the ambient closure would meet some cover member in a nonempty relative open in the trace closure.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Nowhere dense image along a closed embedding
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a homeomorphism onto a closed subspace and let $T$ be nowhere dense in its source.
theorems.statement: The image of $T$ is nowhere dense in the target.
theorems.proof: Its closure lies in the closed image. A nonempty ambient open contained in this closure pulls back to a nonempty source open in the closure of $T$.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closedness under open inverse image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be continuous and open and let $T$ be a subset of its target.
theorems.statement: If $T$ is closed nowhere dense, its inverse image is closed.
theorems.proof: Inverse images under continuous maps preserve closedness.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Nowhere denseness under open inverse image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be continuous and open and let $T$ be a subset of its target.
theorems.statement: If $T$ is closed nowhere dense, its inverse image is nowhere dense.
theorems.proof: A nonempty open in its closed inverse image would map to a nonempty open contained in $T$.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Closed nowhere dense sets detected by an open surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be continuous and open and let $T$ be a subset of its target.
theorems.statement: When $f$ is also surjective, $T$ is closed nowhere dense exactly when its inverse image is closed nowhere dense.
theorems.proof: The quotient criterion detects closedness. A nonempty open of the target in $T$ would pull back to a nonempty open by surjectivity.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Cofiltered presentation of a profinite space
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is profinite.
theorems.statement: It is a cofiltered limit of finite discrete spaces.
theorems.proof: Use the directed system of finite clopen partitions ordered by refinement. Clopens separate points and compactness supplies a point for every coherent choice of cells.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Arbitrary small limits of profinite spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of profinite spaces with continuous maps.
theorems.statement: Its limit is profinite.
theorems.proof: The limit is closed in the compact Hausdorff product and hence compact Hausdorff. Distinct coherent tuples differ in some factor, where a clopen separation pulls back to the limit.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Finite clopen partition refining an open cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be profinite and take any open cover.
theorems.statement: A finite partition by clopen subsets refines the cover.
theorems.proof: First choose a finite clopen cover refining it, using the clopen basis and compactness. Subtract earlier members to obtain pairwise disjoint clopens.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Profinite space of components
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and every connected component is the intersection of all clopens containing it.
theorems.statement: Its component space with the quotient topology is profinite.
theorems.proof: The quotient is quasi-compact and totally disconnected. Distinct components are separated by a clopen of $X$, necessarily saturated, so the quotient is Hausdorff.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Hausdorffness of the constructible topology
theorems.hypotheses: Take the constructible topology of a spectral space, generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements.
theorems.statement: The resulting space is Hausdorff.
theorems.proof: Quasi-compact opens distinguish points in the Kolmogorov space and become clopen in the new topology.
refs: M. Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, §2 (patch topology)

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Total disconnectedness of the constructible topology
theorems.hypotheses: Take the constructible topology of a spectral space, generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements.
theorems.statement: The resulting space is totally disconnected.
theorems.proof: The clopen separation of each pair rules out a connected subset containing distinct points.
refs: M. Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, §2 (patch topology)

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of the constructible topology
theorems.hypotheses: Take the constructible topology of a spectral space, generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements.
theorems.statement: The resulting space is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: The lattice of quasi-compact opens represents the space by prime filters. Compactness follows by the prime-filter extension property for consistent finite positive and negative membership constraints.
refs: M. Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, §2 (patch topology)

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Continuity on patch spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a spectral map between spectral spaces.
theorems.statement: The same function is continuous for the two constructible topologies.
theorems.proof: Pullbacks of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact open, and inverse image preserves complements.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Quasi-compact fibres of a spectral map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a spectral map between spectral spaces.
theorems.statement: Every fibre is quasi-compact in the original topology.
theorems.proof: A point is closed in the target patch topology. Its preimage is closed and compact in the source patch topology, which refines the original.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Patch-closed image of a spectral map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a spectral map between spectral spaces.
theorems.statement: The image is closed in the target constructible topology.
theorems.proof: Under the patch topologies this is a continuous image of a compact space in a Hausdorff space.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Spectrality detected by patch continuity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be continuous between spectral spaces with their original topologies.
theorems.statement: It is spectral exactly when it is also continuous for the patch topologies.
theorems.proof: The forward direction follows from the patch generators. Conversely the inverse image of a quasi-compact open is open in the original topology and clopen, hence compact, in the source patch topology.
refs: Stacks 0G1J · equivalence for a continuous map

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Spectral topology on a patch-closed subspace
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be patch-closed in a spectral space. This includes constructible subsets and subsets closed in the original topology.
theorems.statement: The subspace $E$ in the original topology is spectral.
theorems.proof: Trace of the quasi-compact open lattice is a basis stable under finite intersection and consists of patch-compact opens. Each irreducible closed subset of $E$ has its ambient generic point in $E$, since it meets every basic patch neighbourhood of that point.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closure by specializations from a patch-closed set
theorems.hypotheses: Work in a spectral space and distinguish the original topology from its patch topology.
theorems.statement: If $E$ is patch-closed and $x$ belongs to its original closure, some point of $E$ specializes to $x$.
theorems.proof: The quasi-compact opens through $x$ meet $E$ and have the finite-intersection property there in the patch topology. Their common point belongs to every original neighbourhood of $x$.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Closedness of specialization-stable patch-closed sets
theorems.hypotheses: Work in a spectral space and distinguish the original topology from its patch topology.
theorems.statement: A patch-closed specialization-stable subset is closed in the original topology.
theorems.proof: The preceding closure test places its closure in the subset.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Openness of generalization-stable patch-open sets
theorems.hypotheses: Work in a spectral space and distinguish the original topology from its patch topology.
theorems.statement: A patch-open generalization-stable subset is open in the original topology.
theorems.proof: Its complement is patch-closed and stable under specialization.

theorems.subject: space-point-pair
theorems.name: Separation or a common generalization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $x,y$ be points of a spectral space.
theorems.statement: Either a point specializes to both, or there are disjoint open neighbourhoods of $x$ and $y$. The common point is allowed to be $x$ or $y$.
theorems.proof: If every pair of basic neighbourhoods meets, the quasi-compact opens through either point satisfy the finite-intersection property in the compact patch space. A point in all of them specializes to both.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Profinite spectral spaces via trivial specialization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be spectral.
theorems.statement: $X$ is profinite exactly when no distinct points are related by specialization.
theorems.proof: Trivial specialization says that every singleton is closed. The spectral Hausdorff/profinite characterization then gives the equivalence.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Components of a spectral space form a profinite space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be spectral.
theorems.statement: Its quotient space of connected components is profinite.
theorems.proof: The quasi-compact basis and finite-intersection axioms identify each component with its quasicomponent. Apply the profinite component-space criterion.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Product of two spectral spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Take the ordinary product of two spectral spaces.
theorems.statement: The product is spectral.
theorems.proof: Products of quasi-compact basic opens are quasi-compact and form an intersection-stable basis. For an irreducible closed subset, its two projected closures have generic points. The pair is a generic point because its basic neighbourhoods meet the irreducible subset.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Homeomorphism under bijectivity and specialization lifting
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a bijective spectral map of spectral spaces lifting specializations.
theorems.statement: Its inverse is continuous, so it is a homeomorphism.
theorems.proof: In the patch topology the map is a continuous bijection from compact to Hausdorff and hence a homeomorphism. It takes closed sets to patch-closed sets stable under specialization, which are closed in the original topology.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Homeomorphism under bijectivity and generalization lifting
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a bijective spectral map of spectral spaces lifting generalizations.
theorems.statement: Its inverse is continuous, so it is a homeomorphism.
theorems.proof: In the patch topology the map is a continuous bijection from compact to Hausdorff and hence a homeomorphism. It takes open sets to patch-open sets stable under generalization, which are open in the original topology.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Directed inverse limit of finite sober spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let a directed inverse system have finite sober spaces at all stages.
theorems.statement: Its inverse limit is spectral.
theorems.proof: Finite spaces are quasi-compact and all their opens are quasi-compact. The finite-stage patch spaces are discrete. Patch compactness on the limit and the lattice of finite-stage cylinders give the spectral axioms.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Patch-closed representation in a power of the Sierpiński space
theorems.hypotheses: Use the Sierpiński space with two points and precisely one open singleton. Equip its powers with the product topology and then consider their patch topology.
theorems.statement: A space is spectral exactly when it is homeomorphic to a patch-closed subspace of such a power.
theorems.proof: Membership in quasi-compact opens embeds a spectral space in the Sierpiński power and its patch compactness gives closed image in the product of discrete two-point spaces. Conversely that power is an inverse limit of finite sober products and patch-closed subspaces are spectral.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness survives sobrification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X^s$ be the sobrification of $X$.
theorems.statement: If $X$ is quasi-compact, so is $X^s$.
theorems.proof: The frames of opens are isomorphic, hence covers and their finite subcovers correspond.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), 2.9.2.5, isomorphism on opens

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Spectral sobrification from compact opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X^s$ be the sobrification of $X$.
theorems.statement: If $X$ is quasi-compact with a quasi-compact open basis and quasi-compact binary intersections of quasi-compact opens, $X^s$ is spectral.
theorems.proof: The correspondence of opens preserves covering relations and hence quasi-compactness. Combine the transferred basis axioms with sobriety.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), 2.9.2.5, isomorphism on opens

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Noetherian sobrification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X^s$ be the sobrification of $X$.
theorems.statement: If $X$ is Noetherian, $X^s$ is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: The isomorphism on opens preserves the ascending chain condition.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), 2.9.2.5, isomorphism on opens

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Spectrality of a Noetherian sobrification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X^s$ be the sobrification of $X$.
theorems.statement: If $X$ is Noetherian, $X^s$ is spectral.
theorems.proof: All opens of a Noetherian space are quasi-compact, supplying the quasi-compact basis hypotheses.
refs: Grothendieck and Dieudonné, EGA I, 2nd ed., 0(I), 2.9.2.5, isomorphism on opens

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Quasi-compact limit of compatible patch-closed subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral.
theorems.statement: Given patch-closed subsets at every stage carried into one another by all transitions, their limit is quasi-compact in the original limit topology.
theorems.proof: Give the subsets their compact Hausdorff patch topologies. Their limit is compact and the map to the original limit is continuous and bijective.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness for an arbitrary spectral diagram
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral.
theorems.statement: The limit space is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Take all the given subsets equal to the whole stage spaces.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Compatible point in patch-closed stages
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: If the compatible patch-closed subsets are nonempty at every stage, their limit is nonempty.
theorems.proof: In their compact Hausdorff patch topologies a cofiltered limit of nonempty spaces is nonempty.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Nonempty limit of nonempty spectral stages
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: If all stage spaces are nonempty, so is their limit.
theorems.proof: Apply the preceding assertion to the entire stages.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Detecting patch containment at a finite stage
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered. At a stage $i$ choose patch-closed $E$ and patch-open $F$.
theorems.statement: Containment of the pullback of $E$ in that of $F$ on the limit is equivalent to this containment after pullback along some arrow to $i$.
theorems.proof: Take the compatible inverse images of the patch-closed difference in the cofiltered category over the stage. If all were nonempty, they would have a coherent point. The converse follows by pullback.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Descent of a constructible subset
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered. Let $E$ be constructible in the limit.
theorems.statement: Some constructible subset at a single stage pulls back to $E$.
theorems.proof: Quasi-compact opens of the limit are finite unions of cylinders from stage quasi-compact opens. Express the finite Boolean presentation at one common stage.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Open stage representative
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered. Let $E$ be constructible in the limit.
theorems.statement: When $E$ is open one can choose the stage representative open and constructible.
theorems.proof: An open constructible set is quasi-compact here; express it by a finite union of quasi-compact open cylinders at a common stage.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Closed stage representative
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered. Let $E$ be constructible in the limit.
theorems.statement: When $E$ is closed one can choose the stage representative closed and constructible.
theorems.proof: Apply the open choice to the constructible complement and take its complement at that stage.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Spectral cofiltered limit
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: The topological limit is spectral.
theorems.proof: Finite-stage quasi-compact open cylinders form an intersection-stable basis of quasi-compact opens. For an irreducible closed subset, the compatible generic points of its projected closures yield its unique generic point.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Spectral limit projections
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: Every projection is a spectral map.
theorems.proof: The inverse image of a stage quasi-compact open is quasi-compact by the patch-closed subset limit criterion on the cofiltered category over that stage.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Descent of quasi-compact opens
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: Every quasi-compact open in the limit is the pullback of a quasi-compact open at a single stage.
theorems.proof: A finite subcover by basic quasi-compact open cylinders suffices; pull these opens to a common stage.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Descent of inclusion between stages
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: If cylinder opens from stages $i,j$ satisfy containment in the limit, their quasi-compact open representatives satisfy containment after pullbacks along some arrows from a common stage.
theorems.proof: Pass to a common stage and apply the patch-closed versus patch-open containment criterion.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Descent of finite-union identities
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: For quasi-compact opens $U,U_1,\ldots,U_n$ at one stage, equality of the pullback of $U$ with the union of the pullbacks of the $U_j$ holds already after pullback to some stage mapping to it.
theorems.proof: The finite union is quasi-compact open. Descend the two containments and take a common refinement of their witnessing arrows.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Descent of finite-intersection identities
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of spectral spaces whose transition maps are spectral. Assume its indexing category is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: For quasi-compact opens $U,U_1,\ldots,U_n$ at one stage, equality of the pullback of $U$ with the intersection of the pullbacks of the $U_j$ holds already after pullback to some stage mapping to it.
theorems.proof: The finite intersection is quasi-compact open by spectrality. Descend equality by its two containments.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Spectral generization criterion 1
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W$ be a subset of a spectral space $X$.
theorems.statement: Being quasi-compact and stable under generalization is equivalent to the following condition. It is an intersection of constructible subsets and is stable under generalization.
theorems.proof: A patch-closed set is quasi-compact. If $W$ is quasi-compact and stable under generalization use $E=W$. The generalizations of a quasi-compact set are quasi-compact and can be separated from each exterior point closure by a quasi-compact open. Finite intersections make those opens filtered; intersections of quasi-compact opens are patch-closed and generalization-stable.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Spectral generization criterion 3
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W$ be a subset of a spectral space $X$.
theorems.statement: Being quasi-compact and stable under generalization is equivalent to the following condition. It consists of all points specializing to some point of a quasi-compact subset of $X$.
theorems.proof: A patch-closed set is quasi-compact. If $W$ is quasi-compact and stable under generalization use $E=W$. The generalizations of a quasi-compact set are quasi-compact and can be separated from each exterior point closure by a quasi-compact open. Finite intersections make those opens filtered; intersections of quasi-compact opens are patch-closed and generalization-stable.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Spectral generization criterion 4
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W$ be a subset of a spectral space $X$.
theorems.statement: Being quasi-compact and stable under generalization is equivalent to the following condition. It is an intersection of quasi-compact opens of $X$.
theorems.proof: A patch-closed set is quasi-compact. If $W$ is quasi-compact and stable under generalization use $E=W$. The generalizations of a quasi-compact set are quasi-compact and can be separated from each exterior point closure by a quasi-compact open. Finite intersections make those opens filtered; intersections of quasi-compact opens are patch-closed and generalization-stable.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Spectral generization criterion 5
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W$ be a subset of a spectral space $X$.
theorems.statement: Being quasi-compact and stable under generalization is equivalent to the following condition. It is the intersection of a nonempty family of quasi-compact opens directed downwards by inclusion.
theorems.proof: A patch-closed set is quasi-compact. If $W$ is quasi-compact and stable under generalization use $E=W$. The generalizations of a quasi-compact set are quasi-compact and can be separated from each exterior point closure by a quasi-compact open. Finite intersections make those opens filtered; intersections of quasi-compact opens are patch-closed and generalization-stable.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Spectrality of a filtered intersection of quasi-compact opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W$ be a subset of a spectral space $X$. Fix a nonempty downward-directed family of quasi-compact opens with intersection $W$.
theorems.statement: $W$ in its subspace topology is spectral.
theorems.proof: The inclusions of these quasi-compact opens are spectral, so their cofiltered limit is spectral.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Filtered-intersection limit presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W$ be a subset of a spectral space $X$. Fix a nonempty downward-directed family of quasi-compact opens with intersection $W$.
theorems.statement: $W$ is the topological inverse limit of the family of opens along inclusions.
theorems.proof: The compatible tuples identify with points of the intersection, and open traces from the stages give the subspace topology.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Cofinality among open neighbourhoods
theorems.hypotheses: Let $W$ be a subset of a spectral space $X$. Fix a nonempty downward-directed family of quasi-compact opens with intersection $W$.
theorems.statement: Each open containing $W$ contains some member of the chosen family.
theorems.proof: Otherwise the patch-closed intersections of members with the complement of that open would have the finite-intersection property and hence a point outside the open in $W$.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Removing a constructible subset from its generalizations
theorems.hypotheses: Take a constructible subset $E$ in a spectral space. Let $W$ be the set of all generalizations of points in $E$.
theorems.statement: $W\setminus E$ is spectral in its subspace topology.
theorems.proof: The generalization hull is spectral with spectral inclusion, so the trace of the complement of $E$ is patch-closed there and hence spectral.

theorems.subject: space-subset
theorems.name: Limit presentation of the difference
theorems.hypotheses: Take a constructible subset $E$ in a spectral space. Let $W$ be the set of all generalizations of points in $E$.
theorems.statement: For any nonempty downward-directed family of quasi-compact opens with intersection $W$, the inverse limit of their differences with $E$ is $W\setminus E$.
theorems.proof: All maps are subspace inclusions, so the underlying limit is the intersection and its topology is the induced topology.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Cardinality bound from a dense image
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $f:X\to Y$ is continuous, $Y$ Hausdorff and its image dense.
theorems.statement: The cardinality of $Y$ is at most that of the power set of the power set of $X$.
theorems.proof: Associate to each target point the filter of source subsets containing an inverse image of a neighbourhood. Disjoint neighbourhoods of distinct points, together with density, distinguish their filters.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Open embedding in the one-point compactification
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally quasi-compact and Hausdorff. Adjoin one point with the one-point compactification topology.
theorems.statement: $X$ embeds as an open subspace.
theorems.proof: The original opens are opens of the extended topology and induce exactly the original topology.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Hausdorffness of the one-point compactification
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally quasi-compact and Hausdorff. Adjoin one point with the one-point compactification topology.
theorems.statement: The extended space is Hausdorff.
theorems.proof: A quasi-compact neighbourhood inside $X$ supplies disjoint neighbourhoods of an original point and the added point.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Compactness of the one-point compactification
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally quasi-compact and Hausdorff. Adjoin one point with the one-point compactification topology.
theorems.statement: The extended space is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: One cover member contains the added point; its closed quasi-compact complement admits a finite subcover.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Remainder of the one-point compactification
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally quasi-compact and Hausdorff. Adjoin one point with the one-point compactification topology.
theorems.statement: The complement of the image consists of one point.
theorems.proof: Exactly one new point is adjoined to the original underlying set.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Locally compact Hausdorff spaces are open in their Stone–Čech reflection
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is locally quasi-compact and Hausdorff. Adjoin one point with the one-point compactification topology.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $X\to\beta X$ identifies $X$ with an open subspace.
theorems.proof: The map to the one-point extension factors through the reflection. The inverse image of the original open subspace is exactly the copy of $X$: compact neighbourhoods there have closed images in the reflection and its original image is dense.
refs: Stacks 090A · open embedding in the Stone–Čech reflection

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Open images for an irreducible surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $f:X\to Y$ is continuous and surjective with no proper closed subset mapping onto $Y$. Let $U$ be open in $X$.
theorems.statement: $f(U)\subseteq\overline{Y\setminus f(X\setminus U)}$.
theorems.proof: For any neighbourhood $V$ of a point of $f(U)$, the nonempty open $U\cap f^{-1}V$ has a proper closed complement. Some entire nonempty fibre lies inside that open, and its value is a witness in $V$.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Closures of disjoint opens in an extremally disconnected space
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is extremally disconnected and $U,V$ are disjoint opens.
theorems.statement: Their closures are disjoint.
theorems.proof: The closure of $U$ is disjoint from $V$ and is open. Its closed complement contains $V$ and hence the closure of $V$.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Irreducible surjection onto an extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an irreducible continuous surjection between quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces with $Y$ extremally disconnected.
theorems.statement: The map is a homeomorphism.
theorems.proof: Disjoint opens around two points in the same fibre give disjoint target opens obtained by omitting images of complements. The common image point would lie in both closures, contradicting extremal disconnectedness. A continuous compact-to-Hausdorff bijection is a homeomorphism.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Irreducible restriction of a compact Hausdorff surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous surjection between quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces.
theorems.statement: There is a quasi-compact $E\subseteq X$ still surjecting onto $Y$, with no proper closed subset of $E$ surjecting.
theorems.proof: For a descending chain of closed surjective subsets, compact fibres yield a common point of the chain over every target point. Apply Zorn’s lemma.
refs: Stacks 08YM · existence of an inclusion-minimal compact surjective restriction

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Splitting compact Hausdorff surjections onto an extremally disconnected space
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is quasi-compact Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: Extremal disconnectedness is equivalent to every compact Hausdorff surjection onto $X$ admitting a continuous section.
theorems.proof: Reduce the surjection to a minimal closed subdomain, which maps homeomorphically onto an extremally disconnected target. Conversely a section of the map from the disjoint sum of the closure of an open and the complement of the open pulls back the first clopen summand to the closure itself.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Projectivity in compact Hausdorff spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is quasi-compact Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: The section property is equivalent to lifting every map out of $X$ along every continuous surjection in the category of compact Hausdorff spaces.
theorems.proof: Pull the surjection back to $X$; the pullback is compact Hausdorff and surjects. A section gives a lift. Test the identity on $X$ for the converse.

theorems.subject: continuous-map
theorems.name: Rainwater’s proper closed subset for a selfmap
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is Hausdorff and $f:X\to X$ is continuous, surjective and different from the identity.
theorems.statement: There is a proper closed $E$ with $X=E\cup f(E)$.
theorems.proof: Choose a point moved by $f$, and disjoint opens around it and its image. The intersection of the first open with the preimage of the second is nonempty and disjoint from its own image. Its closed complement and its image cover $X$ by surjectivity.
refs: Stacks 090B · existence of proper closed subset

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Extremal disconnectedness of the Stone–Čech compactification of a discrete space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be discrete. Use its Stone–Čech compactification.
theorems.statement: Its compactification is extremally disconnected.
theorems.proof: For any compact Hausdorff surjection onto the compactification, choose lifts of the discrete subset and extend continuously by universality to obtain a section.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Total disconnectedness of the Stone–Čech compactification of a discrete space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be discrete. Use its Stone–Čech compactification.
theorems.statement: The compactification is totally disconnected.
theorems.proof: It is Hausdorff and extremally disconnected, hence disjoint neighbourhoods separate distinct points by disjoint clopen closures.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Profinite Stone–Čech compactification of a discrete space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be discrete. Use its Stone–Čech compactification.
theorems.statement: The compactification is profinite.
theorems.proof: It is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff cover
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is quasi-compact Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: There is a continuous surjection onto $X$ from a quasi-compact Hausdorff extremally disconnected space.
theorems.proof: Use the Stone–Čech compactification of the underlying discrete set. Its map induced by the identity onto $X$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Minimal extremally disconnected cover
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is quasi-compact Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: Such a cover can be chosen with no proper closed subset still surjecting.
theorems.proof: Take a minimal closed surjective restriction of the discrete Stone–Čech cover. Projectivity and the selfmap lemma yield a retraction onto this restriction, hence it is projective and extremally disconnected.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Uniqueness of a minimal extremally disconnected cover
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is quasi-compact Hausdorff.
theorems.statement: Any two such minimal covers are isomorphic over $X$.
theorems.proof: Projectivity gives a map over $X$ between them. Minimality makes it an irreducible surjection, which is an isomorphism over an extremally disconnected target.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Cardinality bound for the minimal extremally disconnected cover
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $X$ is quasi-compact Hausdorff. Fix an infinite cardinal $\kappa\geq |X|$.
theorems.statement: The minimal extremally disconnected cover has cardinality at most $2^{2^\kappa}$.
theorems.proof: Choose one lift per point of the base. Its closure still surjects and hence equals the whole cover by minimality. Apply the Hausdorff dense-image cardinality bound.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Local quasi-compactness from a quasi-compact open basis
theorems.hypotheses: Assume a space has a basis of quasi-compact opens and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The space is locally quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Basic quasi-compact open neighbourhoods form the required neighbourhood basis.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Retrocompactness of quasi-compact opens
theorems.hypotheses: Assume a space has a basis of quasi-compact opens and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: Each quasi-compact open is retrocompact.
theorems.proof: Its intersection with every quasi-compact test open is quasi-compact by assumption.

theorems.subject: space
theorems.name: Finite quasi-compact open refinements
theorems.hypotheses: Assume a space has a basis of quasi-compact opens and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: Every open cover of a quasi-compact open admits a finite refinement by quasi-compact opens with quasi-compact pairwise intersections.
theorems.proof: Refine pointwise by basic opens, pass to a finite subcover, and apply the intersection condition.

theorems.subject: ordered-space-family
theorems.name: Closed unions of strata below an index
theorems.hypotheses: Let an indexed stratification be locally finite and for each index $i$ let $Z_i$ be the union of all strata indexed below or equal to $i$.
theorems.statement: Each $Z_i$ is closed.
theorems.proof: The closure of a locally finite union lies in the union of the closures, and all these closures remain in the same downward union.

theorems.subject: ordered-space-family
theorems.name: Intersections of the closed unions
theorems.hypotheses: Let an indexed stratification be locally finite and for each index $i$ let $Z_i$ be the union of all strata indexed below or equal to $i$.
theorems.statement: $Z_i\cap Z_j$ is the union of all $Z_k$ for $k$ below both indices.
theorems.proof: A point lies in a unique stratum. Membership in each closed union expresses the order inequality on its index.

theorems.subject: ordered-space-family
theorems.name: Recovering a locally finite stratification
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a partially ordered family of closed sets $Z_i$ covers $X$, is locally finite, and every pairwise intersection equals the union of all $Z_k$ with $k$ below both indices.
theorems.statement: Removing from each $Z_i$ the union of the $Z_j$ strictly below it gives a locally finite stratification.
theorems.proof: Local finiteness makes the removed union closed. Each point is contained in finitely many members and the intersection formula gives a unique minimal index containing it. These differences are the resulting disjoint strata.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Finite stratified refinement of a partition
theorems.hypotheses: Start with a finite partition into locally closed subsets.
theorems.statement: It admits a finite stratification refining it.
theorems.proof: Close the finite collection of part closures and their boundaries under intersection, then take the successive differences of the resulting closed family ordered by inclusion.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Finite stratification adapted to constructible subsets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a finite union of prescribed constructible subsets. Use the common stratification furnished by the construction.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite stratification compatible with all the given subsets and with constructible strata.
theorems.proof: Present all subsets through finitely many retrocompact opens and use the finite family of closed complements and their intersections, stratified by membership.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Constructibility of each new stratum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a finite union of prescribed constructible subsets. Use the common stratification furnished by the construction.
theorems.statement: Each stratum of this stratification is constructible.
theorems.proof: Each membership cell is a finite Boolean combination of the retrocompact opens.

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Recovering each given constructible subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a finite union of prescribed constructible subsets. Use the common stratification furnished by the construction.
theorems.statement: Every prescribed constructible subset is a union of the chosen strata.
theorems.proof: Membership in all the generating opens is constant on each stratum.
refs: Stacks 09Y4 · each prescribed subset is a union

theorems.subject: space-subset-family
theorems.name: Good finite stratification over a Noetherian space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be Noetherian, with a finite partition into locally closed subsets.
theorems.statement: There is a finite good stratification refining the partition.
theorems.proof: Use Noetherian induction: remove a dense open piece in a chosen irreducible component where one given part is dense. Stratify the proper closed complement compatibly with the closure of that piece, then adjoin it.

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Existence of topological colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of topological spaces and continuous maps.
theorems.statement: The diagram has a colimit in spaces.
theorems.proof: The final topology on the set colimit makes maps out of it continuous exactly when all composites are continuous.
refs: Stacks 0B1X · existence of all small colimits

theorems.subject: space-diagram
theorems.name: Underlying set of a topological colimit
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of topological spaces and continuous maps.
theorems.statement: Forgetting topology preserves the colimit.
theorems.proof: Its underlying set is the usual set colimit by the explicit construction.
refs: Stacks 0B1X · preservation by the forgetful functor

theorems.subject: discrete-set
theorems.name: Continuous evaluation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be a discrete set, give its selfmaps the finite-agreement topology and its bijections the subspace topology.
theorems.statement: Evaluation of a selfmap at a point is continuous.
theorems.proof: Fix the input point using discreteness and prescribe just the value there.

theorems.subject: discrete-set
theorems.name: Continuity of the curried family
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be a discrete set, give its selfmaps the finite-agreement topology and its bijections the subspace topology.
theorems.statement: Every continuous map from $X\times E$ to $E$ gives a continuous map from $X$ to the selfmap space.
theorems.proof: On a finite test set take the intersection of the finitely many open evaluation conditions.

theorems.subject: discrete-set
theorems.name: Coarsest topology for evaluation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be a discrete set, give its selfmaps the finite-agreement topology and its bijections the subspace topology.
theorems.statement: The finite-agreement topology is the coarsest topology with continuous joint evaluation.
theorems.proof: Evaluation at each fixed point must be continuous, and finitely many such requirements form the basic neighbourhoods.

theorems.subject: discrete-set
theorems.name: Continuous composition of selfmaps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be a discrete set, give its selfmaps the finite-agreement topology and its bijections the subspace topology.
theorems.statement: Composition is continuous as a two-variable map.
theorems.proof: Fix the inner map on the finite test set and the outer map on the finite image of that set.

theorems.subject: discrete-set
theorems.name: Continuous inversion of permutations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be a discrete set, give its selfmaps the finite-agreement topology and its bijections the subspace topology.
theorems.statement: Inversion on the bijections is continuous.
theorems.proof: Prescribing an inverse on a finite set amounts to prescribing the forward map on its finite set of corresponding preimages.

theorems.subject: discrete-set
theorems.name: Topological permutation group
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E$ be a discrete set, give its selfmaps the finite-agreement topology and its bijections the subspace topology.
theorems.statement: The permutation group with this topology is a topological group.
theorems.proof: Both composition and inversion satisfy the required continuity conditions.

theorems.subject: topological-group-diagram
theorems.name: Limits of topological groups
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of topological groups.
theorems.statement: Every such diagram has a limit.
theorems.proof: Take the algebraic limit as the compatible tuples in the product, with the subspace topology. Operations act continuously coordinatewise.

theorems.subject: topological-group-diagram
theorems.name: Underlying space of a limit of topological groups
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of topological groups.
theorems.statement: The underlying topological space is the limit of the underlying spaces.
theorems.proof: The compatible tuples have exactly the subspace topology of the topological product.

theorems.subject: topological-group-diagram
theorems.name: Underlying algebraic limit of topological groups
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of topological groups.
theorems.statement: The algebraic forgetful functor preserves the limit.
theorems.proof: The underlying algebraic structure on the compatible tuples is the usual algebraic limit.

theorems.subject: topological-group-diagram
theorems.name: Colimits of topological groups
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of topological groups.
theorems.statement: Every such diagram has a colimit.
theorems.proof: Compatible maps into topological targets factor through the algebraic subobject generated by their images with the induced topology. This bounds a solution set, and the resulting limit-preserving cone functor is representable.

theorems.subject: topological-group-diagram
theorems.name: Underlying algebraic colimit of topological groups
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of topological groups.
theorems.statement: Forgetting the topology preserves the colimit in groups.
theorems.proof: The forgetful functor has a right adjoint assigning the indiscrete topology, so it preserves colimits.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-diagram
theorems.name: Limits of topological rings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of topological rings.
theorems.statement: Every such diagram has a limit.
theorems.proof: Take the algebraic limit as the compatible tuples in the product, with the subspace topology. Operations act continuously coordinatewise.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-diagram
