theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S.
theorems.statement: The functors $i_S^{-1}$ and $\pi_{S,*}$ both restrict a big sheaf to its values on the small objects over $S$.
theorems.proof: The functors $i_S^{-1}$ and $\pi_{S,*}$ both restrict a big sheaf to its values on the small objects over $S$.
refs: Stacks 021G · Direct and inverse image as restriction

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Factorization over the source (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Let f be a morphism from T to S in this site.
theorems.statement: $i_f=f_{\mathrm{big}}i_T$.
theorems.proof: $i_f=f_{\mathrm{big}}i_T$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Continuity of small base change (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Let f be a morphism from T to S in this site.
theorems.statement: Base change along f is continuous from the small site of S to the small site of T.
theorems.proof: Base change along f is continuous from the small site of S to the small site of T.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Small morphism of sites (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Let f be a morphism from T to S in this site.
theorems.statement: This functor defines a morphism from the small site of T to the small site of S.
theorems.proof: This functor defines a morphism from the small site of T to the small site of S.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Big and small projection square (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Let f be a morphism from T to S in this site.
theorems.statement: $f_{\mathrm{small}}\pi_T=\pi_S f_{\mathrm{big}}$.
theorems.proof: $f_{\mathrm{small}}\pi_T=\pi_S f_{\mathrm{big}}$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Factorization through the big topoi (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Let f be a morphism from T to S in this site.
theorems.statement: $f_{\mathrm{small}}=\pi_S f_{\mathrm{big}}i_T$.
theorems.proof: $f_{\mathrm{small}}=\pi_S f_{\mathrm{big}}i_T$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Factorization through the comparison morphism (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Let f be a morphism from T to S in this site.
theorems.statement: $f_{\mathrm{small}}=\pi_S i_f$.
theorems.proof: $f_{\mathrm{small}}=\pi_S i_f$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Direct image on the small site (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Let f be a morphism from T to S in this site.
theorems.statement: For a sheaf $F$ over $T$, the direct image at $U/S$ is $F((U\times_S T)/T)$.
theorems.proof: For a sheaf $F$ over $T$, the direct image at $U/S$ is $F((U\times_S T)/T)$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition on big sites (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Let f and g be composable morphisms in the chosen category.
theorems.statement: The morphism on big topoi for the composite is the composite of the induced morphisms, up to canonical identification.
theorems.proof: The morphism on big topoi for the composite is the composite of the induced morphisms, up to canonical identification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Cartesian base change with big target (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Use a cartesian square with f:T→S on the right, g:S′→S below, and projections f′:T′→S′ and g′:T′→T.
theorems.statement: $g_{\mathrm{big}}^{-1} f_{\mathrm{big},*} \cong f'_{\mathrm{big},*}(g'_{\mathrm{big}})^{-1}$.
theorems.proof: $g_{\mathrm{big}}^{-1} f_{\mathrm{big},*} \cong f'_{\mathrm{big},*}(g'_{\mathrm{big}})^{-1}$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition on small sites (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Let f and g be composable morphisms in the chosen category.
theorems.statement: The morphism on small topoi for the composite is the composite of the induced morphisms, up to canonical identification.
theorems.proof: The morphism on small topoi for the composite is the composite of the induced morphisms, up to canonical identification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Cartesian base change with small target (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Use a cartesian square with f:T→S on the right, g:S′→S below, and projections f′:T′→S′ and g′:T′→T.
theorems.statement: $i_g^{-1}f_{\mathrm{big},*}\cong f'_{\mathrm{small},*}i_{g'}^{-1}$.
theorems.proof: $i_g^{-1}f_{\mathrm{big},*}\cong f'_{\mathrm{small},*}i_{g'}^{-1}$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Description by small-site sheaves (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Consider sheaves of sets on the big slice over S.
theorems.statement: Giving a big sheaf is equivalent to giving a small-site sheaf on every T/S and a transition from its inverse image to the sheaf on T′ for each f:T′→T. These maps compose coherently and are invertible for étale morphisms.
theorems.proof: Giving a big sheaf is equivalent to giving a small-site sheaf on every T/S and a transition from its inverse image to the sheaf on T′ for each f:T′→T. These maps compose coherently and are invertible for étale morphisms.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sheaves on the fibres (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Consider sheaves of sets on the big slice over S.
theorems.statement: A big sheaf determines a small-site sheaf on each T/S.
theorems.proof: A big sheaf determines a small-site sheaf on each T/S.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Transition morphisms (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Consider sheaves of sets on the big slice over S.
theorems.statement: Each f:T′→T gives a transition from the small inverse image of the sheaf on T to the sheaf on T′.
theorems.proof: Each f:T′→T gives a transition from the small inverse image of the sheaf on T to the sheaf on T′.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition of transitions (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Consider sheaves of sets on the big slice over S.
theorems.statement: For each composable f,g the composite of the transition for g with the inverse image of the transition for f equals the transition for their composite.
theorems.proof: For each composable f,g the composite of the transition for g with the inverse image of the transition for f equals the transition for their composite.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Invertibility of transition maps (étale)
theorems.hypotheses: Choose a big étale site containing S. Consider sheaves of sets on the big slice over S.
theorems.statement: The transitions are isomorphisms for étale morphisms.
theorems.proof: The transitions are isomorphisms for étale morphisms.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition on big ph sites
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable arrows between objects in the big slice.
theorems.statement: The geometric morphism for the composite is canonically the composite of the two geometric morphisms.
theorems.proof: The geometric morphism for the composite is canonically the composite of the two geometric morphisms.
refs: Stacks 0DBS · Composition in the big site

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition on big fppf sites
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable arrows between objects in the big slice.
theorems.statement: The geometric morphism for the composite is canonically the composite of the two geometric morphisms.
theorems.proof: The geometric morphism for the composite is canonically the composite of the two geometric morphisms.
refs: Stacks 021X · Composition in the big site

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Base change of a standard ph covering
theorems.hypotheses: Take a standard covering and an arbitrary morphism between affine schemes to its target.
theorems.statement: The pullback is again a standard covering of the same type.
theorems.proof: The pullback is again a standard covering of the same type.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Base change of a standard V covering
theorems.hypotheses: Take a standard covering and an arbitrary morphism between affine schemes to its target.
theorems.statement: The pullback is again a standard covering of the same type.
theorems.proof: The pullback is again a standard covering of the same type.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Standard ph refinement of an affine open covering
theorems.hypotheses: The target is affine and the family is a Zariski open covering.
theorems.statement: There is a standard ph covering refining it.
theorems.proof: There is a standard ph covering refining it.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Refinement of a composite of standard ph coverings
theorems.hypotheses: Take a standard ph cover of an affine scheme and a standard ph cover of each domain.
theorems.statement: The composite family admits a standard ph refinement.
theorems.proof: The composite family admits a standard ph refinement.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A proper surjection gives a ph cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let a morphism of schemes be both proper and surjective.
theorems.statement: The singleton consisting of this morphism is a ph covering.
theorems.proof: The singleton consisting of this morphism is a ph covering.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Standard V coverings compose
theorems.hypotheses: Start with a standard V covering of an affine scheme and standard V coverings of each member.
theorems.statement: The composite family is a standard V covering.
theorems.proof: The composite family is a standard V covering.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: ph cover criterion by refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Every arrow of the given family is locally of finite type.
theorems.statement: The family is a ph covering if and only if some covering of the same type refines it.
theorems.proof: The family is a ph covering if and only if some covering of the same type refines it.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: ph cover criterion by coproduct
theorems.hypotheses: Every arrow of the given family is locally of finite type.
theorems.statement: The family is a ph covering if and only if the singleton formed by its coproduct is a covering of the same type.
theorems.proof: The family is a ph covering if and only if the singleton formed by its coproduct is a covering of the same type.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: V cover criterion by refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any family of morphisms of schemes to a common target.
theorems.statement: The family is a V covering if and only if some covering of the same type refines it.
theorems.proof: The family is a V covering if and only if some covering of the same type refines it.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: V cover criterion by coproduct
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any family of morphisms of schemes to a common target.
theorems.statement: The family is a V covering if and only if the singleton formed by its coproduct is a covering of the same type.
theorems.proof: The family is a V covering if and only if the singleton formed by its coproduct is a covering of the same type.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: standard V cover criterion by refinement
theorems.hypotheses: The target is affine, the given family is finite, and each domain is affine.
theorems.statement: The family is a standard V covering if and only if some covering of the same type refines it.
theorems.proof: The family is a standard V covering if and only if some covering of the same type refines it.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: standard V cover criterion by coproduct
theorems.hypotheses: The target is affine, the given family is finite, and each domain is affine.
theorems.statement: The family is a standard V covering if and only if the singleton formed by its coproduct is a covering of the same type.
theorems.proof: The family is a standard V covering if and only if the singleton formed by its coproduct is a covering of the same type.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Finite support over affine opens for fpqc families
theorems.hypotheses: For a family of scheme morphisms.
theorems.statement: The fpqc condition is equivalent to the following test: every arrow is flat and for each affine open U one can choose a quasi-compact open in each domain, only finitely many nonempty, whose images together equal U.
theorems.proof: The fpqc condition is equivalent to the following test: every arrow is flat and for each affine open U one can choose a quasi-compact open in each domain, only finitely many nonempty, whose images together equal U.
refs: Vistoli, §2.3.2, Proposition 2.33(i)–(ii), Definition 2.34 and the paragraph after Proposition 2.35, pp. 29–30

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: One affine covering of the target suffices for fpqc families
theorems.hypotheses: For a family of scheme morphisms.
theorems.statement: The fpqc condition is equivalent to the following test: all arrows are flat and the target has an affine open covering in which each open is the union of images of finitely many quasi-compact opens of domains.
theorems.proof: The fpqc condition is equivalent to the following test: all arrows are flat and the target has an affine open covering in which each open is the union of images of finitely many quasi-compact opens of domains.
refs: Vistoli, §2.3.2, Proposition 2.33(i)–(ii), Definition 2.34 and the paragraph after Proposition 2.35, pp. 29–30

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Pointwise neighbourhood test for fpqc families
theorems.hypotheses: When the target scheme is quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The fpqc condition is equivalent to the following test: all arrows are flat and every target point has a neighbourhood equal to the union of the images of finitely many quasi-compact opens in the domains; this union need not be open.
theorems.proof: The fpqc condition is equivalent to the following test: all arrows are flat and every target point has a neighbourhood equal to the union of the images of finitely many quasi-compact opens in the domains; this union need not be open.
refs: Vistoli, §2.3.2, Proposition 2.33(i)–(ii), Definition 2.34 and the paragraph after Proposition 2.35, pp. 29–30

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: fpqc families and their coproduct
theorems.hypotheses: Take an indexed family of scheme maps to T.
theorems.statement: The family is fpqc exactly when the singleton given by its coproduct over T is fpqc.
theorems.proof: The family is fpqc exactly when the singleton given by its coproduct over T is fpqc.
refs: Vistoli, §2.3.2, Proposition 2.33(i)–(ii), Definition 2.34 and the paragraph after Proposition 2.35, pp. 29–30

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Refinement test for flat families
theorems.hypotheses: All arrows of the family are flat. An fpqc covering refines the given family.
theorems.statement: The original family is an fpqc covering.
theorems.proof: The original family is an fpqc covering.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: fpqc-local test for a flat family
theorems.hypotheses: All arrows of the family are flat. There is an fpqc cover of the target such that the pulled-back family over each member is fpqc.
theorems.statement: The original family is an fpqc covering.
theorems.proof: The original family is an fpqc covering.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Affine test for a flat family
theorems.hypotheses: All arrows of the family are flat. After pullback along every morphism from an affine scheme the family admits a standard fpqc refinement.
theorems.statement: The original family is an fpqc covering.
theorems.proof: The original family is an fpqc covering.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: No cofinal set of fpqc covers of a nonempty affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a nonzero ring and consider all fpqc coverings of its spectrum.
theorems.statement: For every set of such covers, there is an fpqc cover admitting no refinement in the given set.
theorems.proof: For every set of such covers, there is an fpqc cover admitting no refinement in the given set.
refs: Stacks 0BBK · Failure of a set of cofinal refinements

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Tests for fpqc descent
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be a contravariant functor from schemes to sets.
theorems.statement: F is a sheaf for every fpqc covering precisely when it satisfies both Zariski descent and descent for every standard fpqc covering.
theorems.proof: F is a sheaf for every fpqc covering precisely when it satisfies both Zariski descent and descent for every standard fpqc covering.
refs: Stacks 022H · Main equivalence · conditions 1 and 2 taken together

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Singleton tests for fpqc descent
theorems.hypotheses: Assume F already satisfies Zariski descent.
theorems.statement: Descent for all standard fpqc coverings is equivalent to descent for faithfully flat arrows between affine schemes.
theorems.proof: Descent for all standard fpqc coverings is equivalent to descent for faithfully flat arrows between affine schemes.
refs: Stacks 022H · Moreover · conditions 2 and 2′ assuming condition 1

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Tests for V descent
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be a contravariant functor from schemes to sets.
theorems.statement: F is a sheaf for every V covering precisely when it satisfies both Zariski descent and descent for every standard V covering.
theorems.proof: F is a sheaf for every V covering precisely when it satisfies both Zariski descent and descent for every standard V covering.
refs: Stacks 0ETM · Main equivalence · conditions 1 and 2 taken together

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Singleton tests for V descent
theorems.hypotheses: Assume F already satisfies Zariski descent.
theorems.statement: Descent for all standard V coverings is equivalent to descent for singleton standard V coverings.
theorems.proof: Descent for all standard V coverings is equivalent to descent for singleton standard V coverings.
refs: Stacks 0ETM · Moreover · conditions 2 and 2′ assuming condition 1

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Testing ph descent
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be a presheaf of sets on the big ph site over S.
theorems.statement: F is a sheaf exactly when it satisfies Zariski descent and, for each proper surjection $V\to U$, the restriction from $F(U)$ identifies it with the equalizer of the two maps $F(V)\to F(V\times_U V)$.
theorems.proof: F is a sheaf exactly when it satisfies Zariski descent and, for each proper surjection $V\to U$, the restriction from $F(U)$ identifies it with the equalizer of the two maps $F(V)\to F(V\times_U V)$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Affine-target test for proper descent
theorems.hypotheses: On the big ph site over S, assume the presheaf already satisfies Zariski descent.
theorems.statement: The proper-surjective equalizer condition for all targets is equivalent to its restriction to affine targets.
theorems.proof: The proper-surjective equalizer condition for all targets is equivalent to its restriction to affine targets.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Valuative criterion for singleton V covers
theorems.hypotheses: The given morphism of schemes is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: Its singleton is a V covering if and only if the following condition holds. Every map from the spectrum of a valuation ring to the target lifts through the source after an injective local extension of valuation rings.
theorems.proof: Its singleton is a V covering if and only if the following condition holds. Every map from the spectrum of a valuation ring to the target lifts through the source after an injective local extension of valuation rings.
refs: Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology, Definition 1.1 (valuative criterion on qcqs schemes)

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Specialization criterion for singleton V covers
theorems.hypotheses: The given morphism of schemes is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: Its singleton is a V covering if and only if the following condition holds. After every base change, every specialization of two points in the new target lifts to a specialization in the new source.
theorems.proof: Its singleton is a V covering if and only if the following condition holds. After every base change, every specialization of two points in the new target lifts to a specialization in the new source.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Universal submersiveness of a V cover
theorems.hypotheses: Start with a V covering family and form its coproduct morphism to the common target.
theorems.statement: After every base change this morphism is surjective and gives the target the quotient topology.
theorems.proof: After every base change this morphism is surjective and gives the target the quotient topology.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Common enlargement of big Zariski sites
theorems.hypotheses: The given collection of big Zariski sites is a set.
theorems.statement: There is one big site of the same type containing each member.
theorems.proof: There is one big site of the same type containing each member.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Common enlargement of big étale sites
theorems.hypotheses: The given collection of big étale sites is a set.
theorems.statement: There is one big site of the same type containing each member.
theorems.proof: There is one big site of the same type containing each member.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Common enlargement of big fppf sites
theorems.hypotheses: The given collection of big fppf sites is a set.
theorems.statement: There is one big site of the same type containing each member.
theorems.proof: There is one big site of the same type containing each member.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Enlargement of big sites · inclusion criterion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. One chosen big site is contained in another in the sense of §34.12.
theorems.statement: The inclusion satisfies the hypotheses of the Stacks bigger-site comparison lemma.
theorems.proof: The inclusion satisfies the hypotheses of the Stacks bigger-site comparison lemma.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Enlargement of big sites · two geometric morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. One chosen big site is contained in another in the sense of §34.12.
theorems.statement: The inclusion induces a morphism g from the smaller sheaf topos to the larger and a morphism f in the other direction.
theorems.proof: The inclusion induces a morphism g from the smaller sheaf topos to the larger and a morphism f in the other direction.
refs: Stacks 022K · big sites · two geometric morphisms

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Enlargement of big sites · one-sided inverse
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. One chosen big site is contained in another in the sense of §34.12.
theorems.statement: The composite f after g is naturally isomorphic to the identity of the smaller topos.
theorems.proof: The composite f after g is naturally isomorphic to the identity of the smaller topos.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Enlargement of big slices over S · inclusion criterion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. One chosen big site is contained in another in the sense of §34.12. The base S belongs to the smaller one.
theorems.statement: The inclusion satisfies the hypotheses of the Stacks bigger-site comparison lemma.
theorems.proof: The inclusion satisfies the hypotheses of the Stacks bigger-site comparison lemma.
refs: Stacks 022K · big slices over S · inclusion criterion

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Enlargement of big slices over S · two geometric morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. One chosen big site is contained in another in the sense of §34.12. The base S belongs to the smaller one.
theorems.statement: The inclusion induces a morphism g from the smaller sheaf topos to the larger and a morphism f in the other direction.
theorems.proof: The inclusion induces a morphism g from the smaller sheaf topos to the larger and a morphism f in the other direction.
refs: Stacks 022K · big slices over S · two geometric morphisms

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Enlargement of big slices over S · one-sided inverse
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. One chosen big site is contained in another in the sense of §34.12. The base S belongs to the smaller one.
theorems.statement: The composite f after g is naturally isomorphic to the identity of the smaller topos.
theorems.proof: The composite f after g is naturally isomorphic to the identity of the smaller topos.
refs: Stacks 022K · big slices over S · one-sided inverse

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Extension of a limit-preserving presheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Let C be a full subcategory of schemes over S. Up to S-isomorphism, C contains each affine open of each of its objects and every affine scheme finitely presented over an affine open of S. Let F be a set-valued presheaf on C. Require Zariski gluing for covers in C, testing overlaps on affine open covers by objects of C, and require F to take directed inverse limits of affine S-schemes in C with limit in C to the colimit of their values.
theorems.statement: There is a presheaf on all S-schemes extending F that satisfies both Zariski descent and the directed affine-limit condition.
theorems.proof: There is a presheaf on all S-schemes extending F that satisfies both Zariski descent and the directed affine-limit condition.
refs: Stacks 0EUW · Extension of a limit-preserving presheaf

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Uniqueness of the extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let C be a full subcategory of schemes over S. Up to S-isomorphism, C contains each affine open of each of its objects and every affine scheme finitely presented over an affine open of S. Let F be a set-valued presheaf on C. Require Zariski gluing for covers in C, testing overlaps on affine open covers by objects of C, and require F to take directed inverse limits of affine S-schemes in C with limit in C to the colimit of their values.
theorems.statement: The extension with these two properties is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the identification on C.
theorems.proof: The extension with these two properties is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the identification on C.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Descending a standard covering
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. Present the target as a directed inverse limit of affine schemes. Start with a standard covering of the affine limit.
theorems.statement: At some index there is a standard covering with the same finite index set whose pullback is isomorphic to the given one.
theorems.proof: At some index there is a standard covering with the same finite index set whose pullback is isomorphic to the given one.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Descending a morphism of standard coverings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. Present the target as a directed inverse limit of affine schemes. Take two standard covers at one index and a morphism between their pullbacks to the limit.
theorems.statement: After passing to a later index a morphism of the pulled-back covers induces the specified morphism.
theorems.proof: After passing to a later index a morphism of the pulled-back covers induces the specified morphism.
refs: Stacks 049N · Descending a morphism of standard coverings

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Descending equality of morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. Present the target as a directed inverse limit of affine schemes. Take parallel morphisms of standard covers at one index that become equal at the limit.
theorems.statement: Their pullbacks are equal at some later index.
theorems.proof: Their pullbacks are equal at some later index.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Standard coverings at an affine inverse limit
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. Present the target as a directed inverse limit of affine schemes. Use the categories of standard coverings with their refinement morphisms as defined in the source.
theorems.statement: The category at the limit is the filtered colimit of the categories at the stages, up to equivalence.
theorems.proof: The category at the limit is the filtered colimit of the categories at the stages, up to equivalence.
refs: Stacks 049N · Standard coverings at an affine inverse limit

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Descent of the extended presheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. Let C be a full subcategory of schemes over S. Up to S-isomorphism, C contains each affine open of each of its objects and every affine scheme finitely presented over an affine open of S. Let F be a set-valued presheaf on C. Require Zariski gluing for covers in C, testing overlaps on affine open covers by objects of C, and require F to take directed inverse limits of affine S-schemes in C with limit in C to the colimit of their values. Also require descent for each standard cover of an affine V over S whose structure map factors through an affine open of S over which V is finitely presented.
theorems.statement: The unique extension satisfies the sheaf condition for every covering of the chosen type.
theorems.proof: The unique extension satisfies the sheaf condition for every covering of the chosen type.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Extending a sheaf beyond a chosen big site
theorems.hypotheses: Fix one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies. Let S belong to the chosen big site and F be a sheaf on its slice over S. On affine directed inverse limits in the slice it takes the limit to the colimit of its values.
theorems.statement: The extension from the chosen slice to all S-schemes satisfies descent for all coverings of the same type.
theorems.proof: The extension from the chosen slice to all S-schemes satisfies descent for all coverings of the same type.

theorems.statement: Their degreewise product in simplicial families over $X$ is a hypercover of $X$.
theorems.proof: Matching maps in a product are products of matching covers in the slice.

Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, Proposition 8.5, common refinements and simplicial homotopy

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Refinement through a specified covering of one degree
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in indexed families of objects over $X$. Fix $j\ge0$ and a covering $Z\to K_j$ of families over $X$.
theorems.statement: There exists a map of hypercovers $L\to K$ whose degree-$j$ map factors through $Z\to K_j$.
theorems.proof: The source constructs a relative matching cover and pulls it back over $K$. The conclusion specifies the map in degree $j$.
refs: Stacks 01GJ · numbered Stacks source and proof
Stacks 01GJ · factorization in one specified degree

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Refinement through a presheaf over one degree
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in indexed families of objects over $X$. Fix $j\ge0$ and $P\to F(K_j)$ epic after sheafification.
theorems.statement: There is a hypercover map $L\to K$ such that $F(L_j)\to F(K_j)$ factors through $P$.
theorems.proof: For each summand, lift its identity section locally, combine the lifts into a covering family, and refine in degree $j$.

Stacks 01GK · factorization through a locally surjective presheaf

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Extending across one simplex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in indexed families of objects over $X$. Let $U\subseteq V$ be simplicial sets with finite nonempty sets in each degree and with $U$ having only finitely many nondegenerate simplices. In degree $n\ge0$ adjoin exactly one simplex, with no changes below $n$ and only degenerate new simplices above $n$.
theorems.statement: The degree-zero cotensor restriction $\operatorname{Hom}(V,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(U,K)_0$ covers in the category of families over $X$.
theorems.proof: The map is a base change of the matching cover for the boundary of the newly attached simplex.
refs: Stacks 01GM · numbered Stacks source and proof
Stacks 01GM · extension by one nondegenerate simplex

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Extending across finitely many simplices
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in indexed families of objects over $X$. Let $U\subseteq V$ be simplicial sets with finite nonempty sets in each degree and with $U$ having only finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Suppose $V$ also has finitely many nondegenerate simplices.
theorems.statement: The degree-zero cotensor restriction $\operatorname{Hom}(V,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(U,K)_0$ covers in the category of families over $X$.
theorems.proof: Enumerate the new nondegenerate simplices in order of increasing dimension and compose the covering obtained at each attachment.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Every degree covers the augmentation target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in indexed families of objects over $X$.
theorems.statement: For every $n\ge0$, the family $K_n$ covers $X$.
theorems.proof: Use the degree-zero cover and the coverings induced by simplex inclusions.
refs: Stacks 0DEQ · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Covering faces of a hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in indexed families of objects over $X$.
theorems.statement: Each face $d_i:K_n\to K_{n-1}$ is a covering for $n\ge1$ and $0\le i\le n$.
theorems.proof: The inclusion of the corresponding face of the standard simplex induces this restriction on mapping families.
refs: Stacks 0DEQ · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Degree of the path cotensor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $L$ be any simplicial family over $X$, $n\ge0$, $D=\Delta[n+1]$, $B=\partial D$ and $I=\Delta[1]$. Write $[T,L]_0=\operatorname{Hom}(T,L)_0$.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{Hom}(I,L)_{n+1}=[I\times D,L]_0$.
theorems.proof: Cotensor adjunction identifies the terms, and a union along the common subcomplex turns into a fibre product of mapping objects.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Matching object of the path cotensor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $L$ be any simplicial family over $X$, $n\ge0$, $D=\Delta[n+1]$, $B=\partial D$ and $I=\Delta[1]$. Write $[T,L]_0=\operatorname{Hom}(T,L)_0$.
theorems.statement: The degree-$(n+1)$ matching object of $\operatorname{Hom}(I,L)$ is $[I\times B,L]_0$.
theorems.proof: Cotensor adjunction identifies the terms, and a union along the common subcomplex turns into a fibre product of mapping objects.

theorems.name: Degree of the endpoint pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $L$ be any simplicial family over $X$, $n\ge0$, $D=\Delta[n+1]$, $B=\partial D$ and $I=\Delta[1]$. Write $[T,L]_0=\operatorname{Hom}(T,L)_0$.
theorems.statement: $(L\times L)_{n+1}=[\partial I\times D,L]_0$.
theorems.proof: Cotensor adjunction identifies the terms, and a union along the common subcomplex turns into a fibre product of mapping objects.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Matching object of the endpoint pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $L$ be any simplicial family over $X$, $n\ge0$, $D=\Delta[n+1]$, $B=\partial D$ and $I=\Delta[1]$. Write $[T,L]_0=\operatorname{Hom}(T,L)_0$.
theorems.statement: The matching object for $L\times L$ in degree $n+1$ is $[\partial I\times B,L]_0$.
theorems.proof: Cotensor adjunction identifies the terms, and a union along the common subcomplex turns into a fibre product of mapping objects.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Restriction maps of the endpoint square
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $L$ be any simplicial family over $X$, $n\ge0$, $D=\Delta[n+1]$, $B=\partial D$ and $I=\Delta[1]$. Write $[T,L]_0=\operatorname{Hom}(T,L)_0$.
theorems.statement: The four arrows are restrictions induced by the inclusions $\partial I\subset I$ and $B\subset D$ on the two factors.
theorems.proof: Cotensor adjunction identifies the terms, and a union along the common subcomplex turns into a fibre product of mapping objects.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Relative matching object for endpoints
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $L$ be any simplicial family over $X$, $n\ge0$, $D=\Delta[n+1]$, $B=\partial D$ and $I=\Delta[1]$. Write $[T,L]_0=\operatorname{Hom}(T,L)_0$.
theorems.statement: The pullback of the lower and right-hand arrows is $[(\partial I\times D)\cup(I\times B),L]_0$ inside the indicated square.
theorems.proof: Cotensor adjunction identifies the terms, and a union along the common subcomplex turns into a fibre product of mapping objects.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Parallel maps become homotopic after refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in indexed families of objects over $X$. Let $L$ be a hypercover of $X$ and $a,b:K\to L$ two maps.
theorems.statement: Some hypercover map $c:K^\prime\to K$ makes $ac$ and $bc$ simplicially homotopic.
theorems.proof: Refine through the endpoint map of the path cotensor; the relevant matching cover comes from adjoining the finitely many simplices to the boundary prism.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Verdier’s hypercover comparison
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $A$ be an abelian sheaf and $i\ge0$.
theorems.statement: The directed colimit of $\check H^i(K,A)$ under refinements, indexed by the opposite homotopy category of hypercovers, is canonically $H^i(X,A)$, naturally in $A$.
theorems.proof: Products and homotopies after refinement give filteredness. The resulting cohomological functors agree in degree zero and are effaceable in positive degrees.

theorems.subject: site-presheaf-augmented-family
theorems.name: Representing a global class on a hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and binary products, $A$ an abelian sheaf, and $i\ge0$. Hypercovers here are of the terminal presheaf.
theorems.statement: For every $x\in H^i(C,A)$ there is a hypercover $K$ and a class in $\check H^i(K,A)$ mapping to $x$.
theorems.proof: Successive refinements lift cochains to represent a class in an injective resolution.
refs: Stacks 09VZ · numbered Stacks source and proof
SGA 4, Exposé V, Théorème 7.4.1, cohomology comparison under 7.3.0

theorems.subject: site-presheaf-augmented-family
theorems.name: Detecting equality of representatives after refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and binary products, $A$ an abelian sheaf, and $i\ge0$. Hypercovers here are of the terminal presheaf. Suppose $x_K,x_L$ on two hypercovers have the same global image.
theorems.statement: There is a common hypercover $M\to K,L$ on which the two pullbacks agree in $\check H^i(M,A)$.
theorems.proof: Pass to a common refinement, then refine again until the difference becomes a coboundary.
refs: Stacks 09VZ · numbered Stacks source and proof
SGA 4, Exposé V, Théorème 7.4.1, cohomology comparison under 7.3.0

theorems.subject: site-presheaf-augmented-family
theorems.name: The global hypercover colimit
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and binary products, $A$ an abelian sheaf, and $i\ge0$. Hypercovers here are of the terminal presheaf. Interpret the colimit in a universe in which the indexing system can be used.
theorems.statement: The colimit under refinements recovers $H^i(C,A)$.
theorems.proof: Representability of each class gives surjectivity and equality on a common refinement gives injectivity.

SGA 4, Exposé V, Théorème 7.4.1, cohomology comparison under 7.3.0

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: A hypercover by opens of a prescribed basis
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Let $\mathcal B$ be any basis.
theorems.statement: There exists a single hypercover of $X$ all of whose opens in every degree belong to $\mathcal B$.
theorems.proof: Inductively cover each matching intersection by basis opens and retain the degenerate simplices.
refs: Stacks 01H6 · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Basis components in a finite-degree hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Suppose $X$ is quasi-compact, every member of the chosen basis is a quasi-compact open, and the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: One can choose the same hypercover for all three conclusions of this lemma. All opens appearing in it are members of the specified basis.
theorems.proof: Use quasi-compactness to choose finite basis covers of the finite matching intersections at each degree.
refs: Stacks 01H7 · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Finitely many members in every degree
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Suppose $X$ is quasi-compact, every member of the chosen basis is a quasi-compact open, and the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: One can choose the same hypercover for all three conclusions of this lemma. Every indexing set $I_n$ is finite.
theorems.proof: Use quasi-compactness to choose finite basis covers of the finite matching intersections at each degree.
refs: Stacks 01H7 · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Finite covering families on matching intersections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Suppose $X$ is quasi-compact, every member of the chosen basis is a quasi-compact open, and the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: One can choose the same hypercover for all three conclusions of this lemma. The degree-zero cover, all double-intersection covers and all higher matching covers are finite.
theorems.proof: Use quasi-compactness to choose finite basis covers of the finite matching intersections at each degree.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Hypercover of an object by a specified collection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $\mathcal B$ be a subset of the objects of $C$. Every object has a cover with sources in $\mathcal B$, and appending one more map from a member of $\mathcal B$ to any such cover gives another cover.
theorems.statement: There exists a hypercover of $X$ all of whose component sources belong to $\mathcal B$.
theorems.proof: Construct matching covers by induction while retaining degenerate components; the enlargement axiom verifies that the resulting families cover.
refs: Stacks 0DAV · numbered Stacks source and proof
Stacks 0DAV · existence with all components in the specified subset

theorems.subject: site-presheaf-augmented-family
theorems.name: Hypercover of the terminal presheaf by a specified collection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with equalizers and fibre products. Suppose every object admits a cover from members of a fixed set $\mathcal B$ of objects.
theorems.statement: The terminal presheaf admits a hypercover with every component in $\mathcal B$.
theorems.proof: Start from all members of the given collection and lift successive matching objects locally, adjoining degeneracies. The construction only requires the matching maps to be locally surjective.
refs: Stacks 0DAX · numbered Stacks source and proof
Stacks 0DAX · site hypercover with prescribed components

theorems.subject: site-presheaf-augmented-family
theorems.name: Transporting a site hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:C\to D$ be a morphism of sites given by $u:D\to C$. Both sites have equalizers and fibre products and $u$ preserves these. Assume $K$ is a hypercover of the terminal presheaf on $D$.
theorems.statement: Applying $u$ to each component yields a hypercover of the terminal presheaf on $C$.
theorems.proof: The inverse-image functor on sheaves is left exact, preserves epimorphisms, and carries each sheafified representable to the sheafified representable associated to its image.
refs: Stacks 0DAY · numbered Stacks source and proof
Stacks 0DAY · preservation by inverse-image site functor

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Transporting an object hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:D\to C$ be continuous between sites with fibre products, and suppose $u$ preserves fibre products. Fix $Y\in D$ and an object hypercover $K\to Y$.
theorems.statement: The componentwise image $u(K)$ is a hypercover of $u(Y)$.
theorems.proof: The induced functor of slices preserves finite limits; thus it carries matching diagrams to matching diagrams, and continuity preserves their covering families.
refs: Stacks 0DAZ · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Basis sources in a degreewise finite site hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Every object has a finite covering with sources in a specified set $\mathcal B$. For each such finite covering, appending one more arrow from an object of $\mathcal B$ gives a covering.
theorems.statement: There exists a hypercover of $X$ with all sources in $\mathcal B$ and simultaneously finite component index sets in each degree.
theorems.proof: Choose finite basis coverings of the finitely many matching components in each induction step.
refs: Stacks 094K · numbered Stacks source and proof
Stacks 094K · basis membership of all components

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Finiteness of each degree in the prescribed basis construction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Every object has a finite covering with sources in a specified set $\mathcal B$. For each such finite covering, appending one more arrow from an object of $\mathcal B$ gives a covering.
theorems.statement: For the hypercover produced with sources in $\mathcal B$, $I_n$ is finite for every $n$.
theorems.proof: The finite matching diagram and the finite covers chosen at each stage involve only finitely many component indices.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Size convention for the collection of hypercovers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Use the specified sets of covering families in the Stacks definition of a site.
theorems.statement: The smallness assertion covers the entire collection formed with these choices.
theorems.proof: The induction on covers bounds all admissible extensions of a partial hypercover.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Level maps in a relative hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ have fibre products and let a class $P$ of morphisms contain isomorphisms and be stable under composition and base change. Let $U_\bullet\to X$ be augmented with $U_0\to X$, $U_1\to U_0\times_X U_0$ and all higher matching arrows in $P$.
theorems.statement: Every $U_n\to X$ belongs to $P$.
theorems.proof: Use the site with singleton covering arrows from $P$ and apply the all-degrees covering result.

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Face maps in a relative hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ have fibre products and let a class $P$ of morphisms contain isomorphisms and be stable under composition and base change. Let $U_\bullet\to X$ be augmented with $U_0\to X$, $U_1\to U_0\times_X U_0$ and all higher matching arrows in $P$.
theorems.statement: Every face map $U_n\to U_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$ belongs to $P$.
theorems.proof: In the singleton-cover site the relative hypercover gives an ordinary object hypercover, whose faces cover.
refs: Stacks 0DER · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Empty matching intersections and simplicial indices
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Let $(I,\{U_i\})$ be a hypercover in the fixed site of opens.
theorems.statement: Matching maps of the simplicial index set need not be onto. For example, cover the discrete two-point space by its two singletons; the intersection of distinct members can be covered by the empty family, so the corresponding edge can be absent.
theorems.proof: The site admits the empty covering of the empty open. The example has two disjoint contractible components in the index realization.
refs: Stacks 01H5 · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Refining away all empty opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Let $(I,\{U_i\})$ be a hypercover in the fixed site of opens.
theorems.statement: Retaining just the indices with nonempty open gives a simplicial subset, and the restricted families still form a hypercover.
theorems.proof: A nonempty open maps by inclusion to a nonempty open. Removing empty opens from the component coverings leaves the same union; use the covering conventions of the site of opens.
refs: Stacks 01H5 · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Simplicial space of an open hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Let $(I,\{U_i\})$ be a hypercover in the fixed site of opens.
theorems.statement: The coproduct of the indexed opens in each degree forms a simplicial space augmented to $X$.
theorems.proof: The index maps and the inclusions of opens induce the simplicial structure on the coproducts.
refs: Stacks 02N9 · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Cohomological descent on the simplicial space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Let $(I,\{U_i\})$ be a hypercover in the fixed site of opens. Write $p:U_\bullet\to X$ for the augmentation and let $A$ be an abelian sheaf on $X$.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison identifies $H^n(X,A)$ with $H^n(U_\bullet,p^*A)$ for every $n$.
theorems.proof: The augmentation supplied by the open hypercover has cohomological descent in the sense of SGA 4, V bis.
refs: Stacks 02N9 · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Levelwise cohomology of an open hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a topological space with its site of opens. Let $(I,\{U_i\})$ be a hypercover in the fixed site of opens. Let $p_j:U_j\to X$ be the maps from the coproducts of opens and let $A$ be an abelian sheaf.
theorems.statement: $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(U_p,p_p^*A)$ converges to $H^{p+q}(X,A)$.
theorems.proof: Take derived sections in each simplicial degree; the total complex computes the cohomology on the augmented simplicial space.

theorems.subject: site-semirepresentable
theorems.name: A family map induces a map of coproducts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(U_i)\to(V_j)$ be a map of families over a site $C$, and assume both indicated coproducts exist in $C$.
theorems.statement: The component from $U_i$ to $V_{a(i)}$ followed by its coproduct inclusion gives a unique induced arrow $\coprod U_i\to\coprod V_j$.
theorems.proof: This is exactly the universal property of the source coproduct.

theorems.subject: site-presheaf-augmented-family
theorems.name: Replacing a site hypercover by degreewise coproducts
theorems.hypotheses: Work on a site with equalizers and fibre products. For a site hypercover $K$, assume the coproduct $U_n$ of its components exists in every degree and $F(K_n)\to h_{U_n}$ is an isomorphism after sheafification.
theorems.statement: The singleton families $(U_n)$ give a hypercover of the terminal presheaf.
theorems.proof: Sheafification preserves finite limits, so relative matching maps agree after degreewise sheafification.
refs: Stacks 0DB1 · numbered Stacks source and proof

theorems.subject: site-object-augmented-family
theorems.name: Replacing an object hypercover by degreewise coproducts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $C$ be a site with fibre products and $X$ an object of $C$. Let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in indexed families of objects over $X$. Suppose the component coproducts $U_n$ exist. Assume pullbacks between existing family coproducts decompose as the coproduct of matching component pullbacks, and every family covering with existing source and target coproducts induces a singleton cover of coproducts.
theorems.statement: The singleton families $(U_n\to X)$ form an object hypercover.
theorems.proof: The assumed decomposition computes the matching objects on taking coproducts, and the covering hypothesis then gives all required matching covers.
refs: Stacks 0DB2 · numbered Stacks source and proof
Stacks 0DB2 · object hypercover after taking degreewise coproducts

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Products in the presheaf category
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a topological space and a small family of presheaves of sets.
theorems.statement: Their categorical product exists.
theorems.proof: The products of the values on each open carry componentwise restrictions and satisfy the universal property.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections of a product of presheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be presheaves of sets and $U$ an open of the common space.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G)(U)\to\mathcal F(U)\times\mathcal G(U)$ is bijective.
theorems.proof: Evaluation gives the pointwise construction of the product.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Abelian presheaf structure from addition, inverse and zero natural in the open set satisfying the abelian group diagrams internally
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a presheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$.
theorems.statement: Sectionwise abelian group structures making restrictions additive are naturally in bijection with addition, inverse and zero natural in the open set satisfying the abelian group diagrams internally.
theorems.proof: Products of presheaves are evaluated on each open. The group laws make the neutral element and inverse unique, and a map preserving addition between groups preserves both.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Abelian presheaf structure from natural addition, inverse and zero inducing an abelian group on sections over each open
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a presheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$.
theorems.statement: Sectionwise abelian group structures making restrictions additive are naturally in bijection with natural addition, inverse and zero inducing an abelian group on sections over each open.
theorems.proof: Products of presheaves are evaluated on each open. The group laws make the neutral element and inverse unique, and a map preserving addition between groups preserves both.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Abelian presheaf structure from a natural binary operation inducing an abelian group law on each set of sections
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a presheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$.
theorems.statement: Sectionwise abelian group structures making restrictions additive are naturally in bijection with a natural binary operation inducing an abelian group law on each set of sections.
theorems.proof: Products of presheaves are evaluated on each open. The group laws make the neutral element and inverse unique, and a map preserving addition between groups preserves both.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Change of rings for module presheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a map of ring presheaves on one space, $M$ an $A$-module presheaf and $N$ a $B$-module presheaf.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_{p,A}M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,N|_A)$.
theorems.proof: The tensor product is taken sectionwise. The usual extension–restriction bijections commute with restrictions.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Detecting the sheaf condition · underlying
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}$ be faithful, suppose $\mathcal C$ admits small limits, $F$ preserves them, and $F$ reflects isomorphisms. Fix a $\mathcal C$-valued presheaf on a space. The valued presheaf is a sheaf.
theorems.statement: Its underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf.
theorems.proof: Apply the forgetful functor to the comparison with the covering equalizer. It preserves the limiting diagram and reflects invertibility of the comparison.
refs: Stacks 0073 · The valued presheaf is a sheaf. implies Its underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Detecting the sheaf condition · reflect
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}$ be faithful, suppose $\mathcal C$ admits small limits, $F$ preserves them, and $F$ reflects isomorphisms. Fix a $\mathcal C$-valued presheaf on a space. The underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Abelian stalk · existence of a group law on the stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an abelian presheaf and a point of its base space.
theorems.statement: The stalk admits an abelian group law making every map from sections on a neighbourhood into the stalk additive.
theorems.proof: Represent finitely many germs on a common neighbourhood and add there. Compatibility with restrictions gives a well-defined group operation and the universal property.
refs: Stacks 007F · existence of a group law on the stalk

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Abelian stalk · uniqueness of the compatible group law
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an abelian presheaf and a point of its base space.
theorems.statement: Only one abelian group law has this compatibility with all neighbourhood maps.
theorems.proof: Represent finitely many germs on a common neighbourhood and add there. Compatibility with restrictions gives a well-defined group operation and the universal property.
refs: Stacks 007F · uniqueness of the compatible group law

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Abelian stalk · categorical colimit in abelian groups
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an abelian presheaf and a point of its base space.
theorems.statement: The stalk with its structure maps is the colimit of the neighbourhood diagram in abelian groups.
theorems.proof: Represent finitely many germs on a common neighbourhood and add there. Compatibility with restrictions gives a well-defined group operation and the universal property.
refs: Stacks 007F · categorical colimit in abelian groups

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Structured stalk · existence of structured stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a point, a $\mathcal C$-valued presheaf on its space, and a faithful $F:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}$ preserving the directed colimits which exist in $\mathcal C$ for all directed systems.
theorems.statement: The neighbourhood colimit exists in the value category.
theorems.proof: Neighbourhoods with reverse inclusion form a directed poset. Apply directed colimits and their functoriality.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Structured stalk · underlying set of the stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a point, a $\mathcal C$-valued presheaf on its space, and a faithful $F:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}$ preserving the directed colimits which exist in $\mathcal C$ for all directed systems.
theorems.statement: Applying the faithful functor to this colimit identifies its underlying set with the stalk of the underlying presheaf.
theorems.proof: Neighbourhoods with reverse inclusion form a directed poset. Apply directed colimits and their functoriality.
refs: Stacks 007H · underlying set of the stalk

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Structured stalk · functoriality in the presheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a point, a $\mathcal C$-valued presheaf on its space, and a faithful $F:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}$ preserving the directed colimits which exist in $\mathcal C$ for all directed systems.
theorems.statement: Taking the stalk defines a functor from the category of such presheaves to the value category.
theorems.proof: Neighbourhoods with reverse inclusion form a directed poset. Apply directed colimits and their functoriality.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Module structure on a stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a module presheaf over a ring presheaf and a point of the common base.
theorems.statement: The germ of the action gives a module structure on the stalk over the stalk of the ring presheaf.
theorems.proof: Represent the scalar and module germs on the same neighbourhood and apply the action there.
refs: Stacks 007J · module over the stalk of the ring presheaf

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Presheaf tensor extension on stalks
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $A\to B$ a map of ring presheaves, an $A$-module presheaf $M$, and a point $x$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $M_x\otimes_{A_x}B_x\to(M\otimes_{p,A}B)_x$ is an isomorphism of $B_x$-modules.
theorems.proof: Sectionwise scalar extension commutes with the directed colimit over neighbourhoods.
refs: Stacks 007K · extension of scalars commutes with the stalk

theorems.subject: concrete-category
theorems.name: Algebraic structure on pointed sets
theorems.hypotheses: Take the usual category of pointed sets with its forgetful functor to sets.
theorems.statement: This pair satisfies the axioms of a type of algebraic structure.
theorems.proof: Products and equalizers are formed on underlying sets. Finitary operations descend to filtered colimits. A bijective homomorphism has a structure-preserving inverse.

theorems.subject: concrete-category
theorems.name: Existence of the terminal object
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M.
theorems.statement: The terminal object exists in the category.
theorems.proof: Use the existence axiom of 007M for the specified diagram.

theorems.proof: Use preservation of the specified limit or filtered colimit.

theorems.subject: concrete-category
theorems.name: Existence of the pullback of any cospan

theorems.subject: concrete-category
theorems.name: (5) monomorphism implies injective function
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. The arrow is monic.
theorems.statement: Its underlying function is injective.
theorems.proof: Use faithfulness to test cancellation for functions. For the implication from monicity, use the diagonal criterion and preservation of fibre products.

theorems.subject: concrete-category
theorems.name: (5) injective function implies monomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. The underlying function is injective.

theorems.proof: Use faithfulness to test cancellation for functions. For the implication from monicity, use the diagonal criterion and preservation of fibre products.

theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. The underlying function is surjective.

theorems.proof: Use faithfulness to test cancellation for functions. For the implication from monicity, use the diagonal criterion and preservation of fibre products.

theorems.subject: concrete-category
theorems.name: Factorization detected by inclusion of images
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. Suppose $f:A\to B$ and $g:C\to B$ have $F(g)$ injective and $\operatorname{im} F(f)\subseteq\operatorname{im} F(g)$.
theorems.statement: There is $t:A\to C$ with $g t=f$.
theorems.proof: The projection of the pullback to the source of the first arrow is a bijection on underlying sets and therefore invertible.
refs: Stacks 007P · factorization through a structure map with injective underlying function

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Structured morphisms detected on stalks
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. Take a map between the underlying set sheaves of two structured sheaves and suppose every induced stalk map comes from a morphism in the value category.
theorems.statement: The given map underlies a morphism of structured sheaves.
theorems.proof: Embed sections into products of stalks and use the image factorization criterion 007P on each open.
refs: Stacks 007W · stalkwise compatibility implies a structured morphism

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Locally representable germs form a sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: For a presheaf of sets, assign to each open the families of stalk elements locally represented by a section.
theorems.statement: This presheaf satisfies the sheaf condition.
theorems.proof: Matching germ families glue pointwise, and local representability persists on the union.
refs: R. Vakil, The Rising Sea, Construction 2.4.6 and Exercise 2.4.H
Stacks 007Y · sheaf condition for the germ construction

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification preserves stalks
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a presheaf of sets and a point of its base.
theorems.statement: The unit of sheafification induces a bijection on the specified stalk.
theorems.proof: A locally represented germ has a presheaf representative at the point. Equality of germs is witnessed after shrinking a neighbourhood.
refs: R. Vakil, The Rising Sea, Exercise 2.4.L
Stacks 007Z · canonical bijection on each stalk

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Universal factorization through sheafification · exists
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a presheaf of sets, a sheaf of sets on the same space and a map from the presheaf to its underlying presheaf.
theorems.statement: The map factors through the unit into the sheafification.
theorems.proof: The images of local representatives agree on overlaps and glue uniquely in the target.
refs: R. Vakil, The Rising Sea, Definition 2.4.5 and Exercises 2.4.J–K

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Universal factorization through sheafification · unique
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a presheaf of sets, a sheaf of sets on the same space and a map from the presheaf to its underlying presheaf.
theorems.statement: The factor from the sheafification into the target sheaf is unique.
theorems.proof: The images of local representatives agree on overlaps and glue uniquely in the target.
refs: R. Vakil, The Rising Sea, Definition 2.4.5 and Exercises 2.4.J–K

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification preserves injective maps
theorems.hypotheses: Start with a sectionwise injective morphism of presheaves of sets.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism of sheaves is injective in the sheaf sense.
theorems.proof: The induced map on stalks has the asserted property. Use 007Z and 007T.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification preserves surjective maps
theorems.hypotheses: Start with a sectionwise surjective morphism of presheaves of sets.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism of sheaves is surjective in the sheaf sense.
theorems.proof: The induced map on stalks has the asserted property. Use 007Z and 007T.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: A pullback formula for the sections of a sheafification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a presheaf of sets, $U$ an open, and $P(V)=\prod_{x\in V}F_x$. Use the germ map $F\to P$.
theorems.statement: The set $F^\#(U)$ is the pullback of $P(U)\to\prod_{x\in U}P_x$ along $\prod_{x\in U}F_x\to\prod_{x\in U}P_x$. The former sends a family to its germs and the latter is induced by the germ map at each point.
theorems.proof: The pullback condition states that the chosen family is locally represented by presheaf sections.
refs: Stacks 0084 · canonical pullback square of germs

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of abelian presheaves · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an abelian presheaf on a space.
theorems.statement: Its underlying set sheafification admits an abelian sheaf structure for which the unit is additive.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of abelian presheaves · uniqueness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an abelian presheaf on a space.
theorems.statement: Only one such structure makes the unit additive.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of abelian presheaves · adjunction
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an abelian presheaf on a space.
theorems.statement: Maps from the abelian presheaf to an abelian sheaf correspond naturally and bijectively to maps from its abelian sheafification.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of valued presheaves · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. Fix a presheaf with values in that category.
theorems.statement: There is a structured sheafification with a structured unit map.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of valued presheaves · underlying sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. Fix a presheaf with values in that category.
theorems.statement: The unit identifies its underlying sheaf with the set-valued sheafification.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of valued presheaves · universal factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. Fix a presheaf with values in that category.
theorems.statement: Any structured map to a structured sheaf factors through this unit.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of valued presheaves · unique factor
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a type of algebraic structure $(\mathcal C,F)$ in the sense of Stacks 007M. Fix a presheaf with values in that category.
theorems.statement: The structured factor through the unit is unique.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of module presheaves · action
theorems.hypotheses: Take a presheaf of modules M over a ring presheaf A.
theorems.statement: There is a sheafified scalar multiplication agreeing with the original multiplication via the units.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of module presheaves · module structure
theorems.hypotheses: Take a presheaf of modules M over a ring presheaf A.
theorems.statement: This action makes the abelian sheafification of M a module over the ring sheafification of A.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of module presheaves · universal factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Take a presheaf of modules M over a ring presheaf A.
theorems.statement: Any A-linear map from M to the restriction of a module sheaf over the sheafification of A factors through the unit by a map linear over the sheafified ring.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheafification of module presheaves · unique factor
theorems.hypotheses: Take a presheaf of modules M over a ring presheaf A.
theorems.statement: For each such map, the factor linear over the sheafified ring is unique.
theorems.proof: The unit is an isomorphism on stalks. Local representatives determine the operations and compatible maps after sheafification.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Change of rings for sheaves of modules
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $A\to B$ a map of sheaves of rings, $M$ an $A$-module sheaf, and $N$ a $B$-module sheaf.
theorems.statement: The natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_A M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,N|_A)$ uses the sheaf tensor product.
theorems.proof: Sheafify the presheaf tensor product and apply its universal property followed by 006R.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sheaf tensor extension on stalks
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $A\to B$ a map of sheaves of rings, an $A$-module sheaf $M$, and a point $x$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $(M\otimes_A B)_x\cong M_x\otimes_{A_x}B_x$ over $B_x$.
theorems.proof: Apply 007K and use invariance of stalks under sheafification.
refs: Stacks 008B · stalk of extension of scalars

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Direct image takes sheaves to sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a sheaf on X.
theorems.statement: Its direct image is a sheaf on Y.
theorems.proof: Inverse image of opens preserves unions and intersections, so the sheaf axiom applies to the inverse-image covering.
refs: Stacks 008D · direct image satisfies the sheaf condition

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Composition of direct images of presheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be continuous maps.
theorems.statement: On presheaves of sets, $(g f)_*=g_* f_*$ as functors.
theorems.proof: The two inverse images of opens are literally equal.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Composition of inverse images of presheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be continuous maps.
theorems.statement: Taking the inverse image along the composite is canonically isomorphic to applying the two inverse images successively, on presheaves of sets.
theorems.proof: Both constructions are left adjoint to the same composite direct image.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Composition of direct images of sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be continuous maps.
theorems.statement: On sheaves of sets, $(g f)_*=g_* f_*$ as functors.
theorems.proof: The two inverse images of opens are literally equal.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Composition of inverse images of sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be continuous maps.
theorems.statement: Taking the inverse image along the composite is canonically isomorphic to applying the two inverse images successively, on sheaves of sets.
theorems.proof: Both constructions are left adjoint to the same composite direct image.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Presheaf inverse image · existence of the presheaf inverse-image functor
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a presheaf of sets on Y.
theorems.statement: The neighbourhood construction is functorial in the presheaf and defines a presheaf on X.
theorems.proof: Intersection gives a common smaller neighbourhood. The colimit universal property identifies compatible maps out of these sections with maps to the direct image.
refs: Stacks 008F · existence of the presheaf inverse-image functor

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Presheaf inverse image · left adjoint to direct image
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a presheaf of sets on Y.
theorems.statement: The presheaf inverse-image functor is left adjoint to presheaf direct image.
theorems.proof: Intersection gives a common smaller neighbourhood. The colimit universal property identifies compatible maps out of these sections with maps to the direct image.
refs: Stacks 008F · left adjoint to direct image

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Presheaf inverse image · neighbourhood colimit formula
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a presheaf of sets on Y.
theorems.statement: On $U\subseteq X$ open its sections are canonically $\operatorname{colim}_{V\supseteq f(U)}\mathcal G(V)$.
theorems.proof: Intersection gives a common smaller neighbourhood. The colimit universal property identifies compatible maps out of these sections with maps to the direct image.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Presheaf inverse image · directedness of the neighbourhood index
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a presheaf of sets on Y.
theorems.statement: Open neighbourhoods of the image are directed under reverse inclusion.
theorems.proof: Intersection gives a common smaller neighbourhood. The colimit universal property identifies compatible maps out of these sections with maps to the direct image.
refs: Stacks 008F · directedness of the neighbourhood index
