theorems.name: Stalk of an inverse image of a presheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix a point $x$ of $X$ and a presheaf on Y.
theorems.statement: Its inverse-image stalk at $x$ identifies canonically with its stalk at $f(x)$ as a set.
theorems.proof: Shrink neighbourhoods on the source and target in the colimit description. Sheafification preserves stalks, and addition of germs is computed on representatives.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Stalk of an inverse image of a sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix a point $x$ of $X$ and a sheaf on Y.
theorems.statement: Its inverse-image stalk at $x$ identifies canonically with its stalk at $f(x)$ as a set.
theorems.proof: Shrink neighbourhoods on the source and target in the colimit description. Sheafification preserves stalks, and addition of germs is computed on representatives.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Stalk of an inverse image of a abelian presheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix a point $x$ of $X$ and a abelian presheaf on Y.
theorems.statement: Its inverse-image stalk at $x$ identifies canonically with its stalk at $f(x)$ as an abelian group.
theorems.proof: Shrink neighbourhoods on the source and target in the colimit description. Sheafification preserves stalks, and addition of germs is computed on representatives.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Stalk of an inverse image of a abelian sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix a point $x$ of $X$ and a abelian sheaf on Y.
theorems.statement: Its inverse-image stalk at $x$ identifies canonically with its stalk at $f(x)$ as an abelian group.
theorems.proof: Shrink neighbourhoods on the source and target in the colimit description. Sheafification preserves stalks, and addition of germs is computed on representatives.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Representations of a map over a continuous map · push
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix sheaves of sets $G$ on $Y$ and $F$ on $X$.
theorems.statement: Maps over f are naturally in bijection with $\operatorname{Hom}(G,f_*F)$.
theorems.proof: Use adjunction or restrict from the whole inverse image of the target open. Evaluating on the whole inverse image recovers the original family.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Representations of a map over a continuous map · pull
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix sheaves of sets $G$ on $Y$ and $F$ on $X$.
theorems.statement: Maps over f are naturally in bijection with $\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}G,F)$.
theorems.proof: Use adjunction or restrict from the whole inverse image of the target open. Evaluating on the whole inverse image recovers the original family.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Representations of a map over a continuous map · pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix sheaves of sets $G$ on $Y$ and $F$ on $X$.
theorems.statement: Maps over f are naturally in bijection with restriction-compatible families $G(V)\to F(U)$ for all open pairs with $f(U)\subseteq V$.
theorems.proof: Use adjunction or restrict from the whole inverse image of the target open. Evaluating on the whole inverse image recovers the original family.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Stalk maps of a composite over continuous maps
theorems.hypotheses: For composable base maps $f,g$, matching sheaf maps $\varphi,\psi$ and a source point $x$,
theorems.statement: $(\varphi\circ\psi)_x=\varphi_x\circ\psi_{f(x)}$.
theorems.proof: Apply the composition formula to section representatives of a germ.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Lifting an underlying map of structured sheaves · exists
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix sheaves of sets $G$ on $Y$ and $F$ on $X$. Assume the sheaves carry structures of the same type and each component of the map over f is induced by a morphism of structures.
theorems.statement: There exists a structured map over f inducing the given map.
theorems.proof: Faithfulness gives uniqueness of the lifts and forces the restrictions to commute.
refs: Stacks 008Q · there exists a structured map over f inducing the given map

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Lifting an underlying map of structured sheaves · unique
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix sheaves of sets $G$ on $Y$ and $F$ on $X$. Assume the sheaves carry structures of the same type and each component of the map over f is induced by a morphism of structures.
theorems.statement: The structured lift of the given map is unique.
theorems.proof: Faithfulness gives uniqueness of the lifts and forces the restrictions to commute.
refs: Stacks 008Q · the structured lift of the given map is unique

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Module structure on the direct image
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix a ring presheaf on X and a presheaf of modules over it.
theorems.statement: The direct image of the module carries a natural action of the direct image of the rings making it a presheaf of modules.
theorems.proof: Direct image evaluates on inverse images of opens. For inverse image, finite products commute with the directed neighbourhood colimits, and sheafification preserves the induced operations.
refs: Stacks 008S · natural action and resulting module presheaf

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Functoriality of module direct image
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Fix a ring presheaf on X and a presheaf of modules over it.
theorems.statement: Applying the construction to linear maps defines a functor between the indicated module presheaf categories.
theorems.proof: The induced maps commute with the natural action.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Linear presheaf adjunction with rings on the target
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a ring presheaf $A$ on $Y$, an $A$-module presheaf $N$ and an $f_p A$-module presheaf $M$ on $X$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{f_pA}(f_p N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,f_*M)$. Scalars on $f_*M$ restrict along the unit.
theorems.proof: Use the set-level adjunction with linearity, and extension–restriction of scalars when the ring is specified on the source.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Linear presheaf adjunction with rings on the source
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a ring presheaf $B$ on $X$, a $B$-module presheaf $M$, and an $f_*B$-module presheaf $N$ on $Y$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_{f_pf_*B}f_p N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{f_*B}(N,f_*M)$. Scalar extension uses the counit and the tensor product in the indicated module presheaf category.
theorems.proof: Use the set-level adjunction with linearity, and extension–restriction of scalars when the ring is specified on the source.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Linear sheaf adjunction with rings on the target
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a ring sheaf $A$ on $Y$, an $A$-module sheaf $N$ and an $f^{-1} A$-module sheaf $M$ on $X$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{f^{-1}A}(f^{-1} N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,f_*M)$. Scalars on $f_*M$ restrict along the unit.
theorems.proof: Use the set-level adjunction with linearity, and extension–restriction of scalars when the ring is specified on the source.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Linear sheaf adjunction with rings on the source
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take a ring sheaf $B$ on $X$, a $B$-module sheaf $M$, and an $f_*B$-module sheaf $N$ on $Y$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_{f^{-1}f_*B}f^{-1} N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{f_*B}(N,f_*M)$. Scalar extension uses the counit and the tensor product in the indicated module sheaf category.
theorems.proof: Use the set-level adjunction with linearity, and extension–restriction of scalars when the ring is specified on the source.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Pullback is left adjoint to direct image of modules
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of ringed spaces. Take an $\mathcal O_X$-module $M$ and an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $N$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(f^*N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Y}(N,f_*M)$.
theorems.proof: Use extension–restriction on the source and the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction for modules.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Composition of push functors for module sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable morphisms of ringed spaces f and g.
theorems.proof: Direct images and their scalar restrictions compose. The left adjoints therefore compose up to canonical isomorphism.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Composition of pull functors for module sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable morphisms of ringed spaces f and g.
theorems.statement: $(gf)^*\cong f^*g^*$ canonically.
theorems.proof: Direct images and their scalar restrictions compose. The left adjoints therefore compose up to canonical isomorphism.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Module pullback on stalks
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of ringed spaces. Take an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $M$ and $x\in X$.
theorems.statement: $(f^*M)_x\cong M_{f(x)}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ canonically as $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules.
theorems.proof: Combine the stalk of the inverse image with commutation of the stalk with sheaf tensor products.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Stalk of a sets skyscraper inside the closure
theorems.hypotheses: Take its skyscraper at x with value A, and a point y with $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: Its stalk at y is canonically A.
theorems.proof: Every neighbourhood of a specialization contains x. Outside the closure one can take a neighbourhood missing x, where the sheaf has terminal sections.
refs: Stacks 009B · sets stalk inside the closure

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Stalk of a sets skyscraper outside the closure
theorems.hypotheses: Take its skyscraper at x with value A, and a point y with $y\notin\overline{\{x\}}$.
theorems.statement: Its stalk at y is the terminal object.
theorems.proof: Every neighbourhood of a specialization contains x. Outside the closure one can take a neighbourhood missing x, where the sheaf has terminal sections.
refs: Stacks 009B · sets stalk outside the closure

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Stalk–skyscraper adjunction for sets
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a point x, a sheaf F of sets and a set A.
theorems.statement: Morphisms from F to the skyscraper of A correspond naturally and bijectively to morphisms from the stalk of F at x to A, in the corresponding category.
theorems.proof: Apply inverse-image/direct-image adjunction to the inclusion of the point. For modules use the canonical ringed point with its stalk ring.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections of a directed colimit · mono
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a directed system $(F_i)$ of sheaves of sets on a space and an open $U$. Compare $\operatorname{colim}_i F_i(U)$ with $(\operatorname{colim}_i F_i)(U)$, where the latter colimit is a sheaf colimit. All transition morphisms are injective.
theorems.statement: The comparison is injective.
theorems.proof: Represent germs at stages. Quasi-compactness bounds finitely many local choices at a common stage. With quasi-compact overlaps equality of the finitely many restrictions can also be achieved at one stage.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections of a directed colimit · qc
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a directed system $(F_i)$ of sheaves of sets on a space and an open $U$. Compare $\operatorname{colim}_i F_i(U)$ with $(\operatorname{colim}_i F_i)(U)$, where the latter colimit is a sheaf colimit. The open U is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The comparison is injective.
theorems.proof: Represent germs at stages. Quasi-compactness bounds finitely many local choices at a common stage. With quasi-compact overlaps equality of the finitely many restrictions can also be achieved at one stage.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections of a directed colimit · qc-mono
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a directed system $(F_i)$ of sheaves of sets on a space and an open $U$. Compare $\operatorname{colim}_i F_i(U)$ with $(\operatorname{colim}_i F_i)(U)$, where the latter colimit is a sheaf colimit. The open U is quasi-compact and all transition morphisms are injective.
theorems.statement: The comparison is bijective.
theorems.proof: Represent germs at stages. Quasi-compactness bounds finitely many local choices at a common stage. With quasi-compact overlaps equality of the finitely many restrictions can also be achieved at one stage.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections of a directed colimit · finite-qc-overlaps
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a directed system $(F_i)$ of sheaves of sets on a space and an open $U$. Compare $\operatorname{colim}_i F_i(U)$ with $(\operatorname{colim}_i F_i)(U)$, where the latter colimit is a sheaf colimit. Every open cover of U admits a refining finite open cover with quasi-compact pairwise intersections, including the self-intersections.
theorems.statement: The comparison is bijective.
theorems.proof: Represent germs at stages. Quasi-compactness bounds finitely many local choices at a common stage. With quasi-compact overlaps equality of the finitely many restrictions can also be achieved at one stage.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections pulled back to a cofiltered limit of spectral spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $i\mapsto X_i$ be a small cofiltered diagram of spectral spaces and spectral maps $f_a:X_j\to X_i$ for $a:j\to i$. Put $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ with projections $p_i$. Fix $i$ and a quasi-compact open $U_i\subseteq X_i$. Fix a sheaf $G$ on $X_i$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{a:j\to i}(f_a^{-1}G)(f_a^{-1}U_i)\to(p_i^{-1}G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)$ is bijective.
theorems.proof: Quasi-compact opens of the limit descend to stages. Finite coverings and equalities on their quasi-compact overlaps can be realized after passing to a common stage.
refs: Stacks 0A32 · sections of the pullback as a colimit over arrows into i

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections of a compatible system over spectral spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $i\mapsto X_i$ be a small cofiltered diagram of spectral spaces and spectral maps $f_a:X_j\to X_i$ for $a:j\to i$. Put $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ with projections $p_i$. Fix $i$ and a quasi-compact open $U_i\subseteq X_i$. Take a sheaf $F_j$ at each stage with compatible $f_a$-maps, and set $F=\operatorname{colim}_j p_j^{-1}F_j$ in sheaves on $X$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical bijection $\operatorname{colim}_{a:j\to i}F_j(f_a^{-1}U_i)\cong F(p_i^{-1}U_i)$.
theorems.proof: Combine descent of quasi-compact opens, the pulled-back sheaf calculation at a single stage, and directed-colimit comparison on finite covers with quasi-compact intersections.
refs: Stacks 0A33 · sections of a compatible sheaf system on the limit

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Cofinal covers on a basis · necessary
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. For each basis element choose covering families by basis elements cofinal under refinement, so every basis cover admits one of the chosen families as a refinement. For every chosen cover fix a cover of each pairwise overlap by basis elements.
theorems.statement: A sheaf on the basis satisfies the test on the chosen covers with compatibility on the chosen overlap covers.
theorems.proof: Refine the given cover and the overlap comparisons by the chosen covers, use uniqueness to compare local gluings, and then glue back to the original open.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Cofinal covers on a basis · sufficient
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. For each basis element choose covering families by basis elements cofinal under refinement, so every basis cover admits one of the chosen families as a refinement. For every chosen cover fix a cover of each pairwise overlap by basis elements.
theorems.statement: A presheaf satisfying the test on the chosen covers with compatibility on the chosen overlap covers is a sheaf on the basis.
theorems.proof: Refine the given cover and the overlap comparisons by the chosen covers, use uniqueness to compare local gluings, and then glue back to the original open.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Cofinal covers on a basis · necessary
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. For each basis element choose covering families by basis elements cofinal under refinement, so every basis cover admits one of the chosen families as a refinement. Assume any two basis elements contained in a common basis element have intersection in the basis.
theorems.statement: A sheaf on the basis satisfies the test on the chosen covers with compatibility on the intersections themselves.
theorems.proof: Refine the given cover and the overlap comparisons by the chosen covers, use uniqueness to compare local gluings, and then glue back to the original open.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections on a basis and germs · injective
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Fix a sheaf of sets on the basis and a basis open U.
theorems.statement: The map from sections on U to the product of their stalks on U is injective.
theorems.proof: Local equality of germs gives equality after a basis refinement. Locally representing sections then glue uniquely by the basis sheaf condition.
refs: Stacks 009M · injectivity of the germ map

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Sections on a basis and germs · image
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Fix a sheaf of sets on the basis and a basis open U.
theorems.statement: Its image consists exactly of germ families such that around each point there is a basis neighbourhood inside U and one section on it representing all the germs there.
theorems.proof: Local equality of germs gives equality after a basis refinement. Locally representing sections then glue uniquely by the basis sheaf condition.
refs: Stacks 009M · image is exactly the locally representable families

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Extension of sets from a basis · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Take a sheaf of sets on the basis.
theorems.statement: It extends to a sheaf on the whole space with specified identifications on the basis commuting with restrictions.
theorems.proof: On arbitrary opens take locally representable families of germs. The sheaf axiom makes the local identifications unique.
refs: R. Vakil, The Rising Sea, Theorem 2.5.1

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Extension of sets from a basis · uniqueness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Take a sheaf of sets on the basis.
theorems.statement: An extension equipped with these identifications is unique up to the unique isomorphism respecting them.
theorems.proof: On arbitrary opens take locally representable families of germs. The sheaf axiom makes the local identifications unique.
refs: R. Vakil, The Rising Sea, Theorem 2.5.1

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Extension of structures from a basis · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Take a sheaf on the basis with values in a type of algebraic structure.
theorems.statement: It extends to a sheaf on the whole space with specified identifications on the basis commuting with restrictions.
theorems.proof: On arbitrary opens take locally representable families of germs. The sheaf axiom makes the local identifications unique.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Extension of structures from a basis · uniqueness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Take a sheaf on the basis with values in a type of algebraic structure.
theorems.statement: An extension equipped with these identifications is unique up to the unique isomorphism respecting them.
theorems.proof: On arbitrary opens take locally representable families of germs. The sheaf axiom makes the local identifications unique.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Equivalence of restriction to a basis for sets
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Use set-valued sheaves.
theorems.statement: Restriction to basis opens is an equivalence from the category on the whole space to the corresponding category of sheaves on the basis.
theorems.proof: Extension gives a quasi-inverse. Compatible maps on the basis extend uniquely.
refs: R. Vakil, The Rising Sea, Theorem 2.5.1 and §2.5, extension from a base

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Equivalence of restriction to a basis for structures
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Fix a type of algebraic structure and use sheaves with those values.
theorems.statement: Restriction to basis opens is an equivalence from the category on the whole space to the corresponding category of sheaves on the basis.
theorems.proof: Extension gives a quasi-inverse. Compatible maps on the basis extend uniquely.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Equivalence of restriction to a basis for modules
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Fix a sheaf of rings and use modules on the basis over its restriction.
theorems.statement: Restriction to basis opens is an equivalence from the category on the whole space to the corresponding category of sheaves on the basis.
theorems.proof: Extension gives a quasi-inverse. Compatible maps on the basis extend uniquely.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Extension of a basis module · action
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Fix a sheaf of rings and a sheaf of modules on the basis, and extend the ring and the underlying abelian sheaf to the whole space.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical action of the extended ring sheaf on the extended abelian sheaf agreeing with the given action on basis elements.
theorems.proof: Extend the multiplication using its compatibility on basis opens. Associativity and unity can be checked there.
refs: Stacks 009T · canonical action extending the basis action

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Extension of a basis module · module
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a basis of opens for the topology of a space X. Fix a sheaf of rings and a sheaf of modules on the basis, and extend the ring and the underlying abelian sheaf to the whole space.
theorems.statement: This action equips the extension of the abelian sheaf with a module structure over the extension of the ring sheaf.
theorems.proof: Extend the multiplication using its compatibility on basis opens. Associativity and unity can be checked there.
refs: Stacks 009T · module structure on the extension

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Map over f from a target basis · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take sheaves F on X and G on Y of the same type of algebraic structures. Fix a basis on Y and give maps from G(V) to F on the inverse image of V for every target basis open V. Require compatibility with all restrictions and that the components be arrows in the value category.
theorems.statement: There exists a map of the indicated sheaves over f inducing the prescribed components.
theorems.proof: Use the extension property of maps on a basis, gluing source components first when both bases are specified.
refs: Stacks 009V · existence of the map over f

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Map over f from a target basis · uniqueness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a continuous map $f:X\to Y$. Take sheaves F on X and G on Y of the same type of algebraic structures. Fix a basis on Y and give maps from G(V) to F on the inverse image of V for every target basis open V. Require compatibility with all restrictions and that the components be arrows in the value category.
theorems.statement: At most one map of the indicated sheaves over f induces all these components.
theorems.proof: Use the extension property of maps on a basis, gluing source components first when both bases are specified.
refs: Stacks 009V · uniqueness of the map over f

Require compatibility with all restrictions and linearity over the ring of sections on V via the structural maps.
theorems.statement: There exists a map of the indicated sheaves over f inducing the prescribed components.
theorems.proof: Use the extension property of maps on a basis, gluing source components first when both bases are specified.
refs: Stacks 009W · existence of the map over f

theorems.statement: The direct image along i is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: The counit restricts to an isomorphism on Z. Test the unit on stalks on both parts of the ambient space.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Open restriction for modules · presheaf formula
theorems.hypotheses: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ include an open subset. Fix a presheaf of rings on X, and use its restriction on U. Use modules as coefficients.
theorems.statement: The presheaf inverse image is evaluation on the opens contained in U.
theorems.proof: The opens in U are opens of X and restricting the direct-image sections evaluates on their intersection with U.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Gluing morphisms of sheaves · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an open cover $X=\bigcup_i U_i$. Take two sheaves of sets on X, and maps between their restrictions to the cover members agreeing on each overlap.
theorems.statement: The local maps extend to a global morphism.
theorems.proof: Apply gluing in the target sheaf to the images of restricted source sections.
refs: Stacks 04TN · existence of a glued morphism

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Gluing sheaves of sets
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an open cover $X=\bigcup_i U_i$. Use local sheaves of sets and overlap isomorphisms which are identities on self-overlaps and satisfy the cocycle condition on triple intersections.
theorems.statement: There is a sheaf on X with isomorphisms to the given sheaves over the cover members inducing exactly the specified transitions.
theorems.proof: Its sections are families of local sections matching under the transition isomorphisms. Operations on coefficients are applied componentwise.

theorems.subject: sheaf-operation
theorems.name: Descent equivalence for sheaves of sets
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an open cover $X=\bigcup_i U_i$. Use local sheaves of sets and overlap isomorphisms which are identities on self-overlaps and satisfy the cocycle condition on triple intersections.
theorems.statement: Restriction induces an equivalence from sheaves on X to the category of such gluing data, whose arrows are compatible tuples of local morphisms.
theorems.proof: Morphisms glue uniquely and every gluing datum is effective.

theorems.hypotheses: Let $\tau$ be one of fpqc, fppf, étale, smooth or syntomic. On affines the corresponding test maps are flat, flat of finite presentation, étale, smooth, or syntomic, respectively. Let $P$ be a morphism property Zariski local on the target and stable under base change by maps of the indicated type (locally of finite presentation in the fppf case). For all surjective affine test maps $S^\prime\to S$, require that $P$ on the pullback of any $X\to S$ implies $P$ on $X\to S$.
theorems.statement: Then $P$ is local on the target in the chosen topology.
theorems.proof: Then $P$ is local on the target in the chosen topology.
refs: Stacks 02KP · affine criterion for target locality

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Affine test for locality on the source
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\tau$ be one of fpqc, fppf, étale, smooth or syntomic. On affines the corresponding test maps are flat, flat of finite presentation, étale, smooth, or syntomic, respectively. Let $P$ be a morphism property Zariski local on both source and target. Assume precomposition with maps of the indicated type preserves it (locally of finite presentation for fppf). For every affine-to-affine $f:X\to Y$ require descent of $P$ from $f\circ a$ along any surjective affine test map $a:X^\prime\to X$.
theorems.statement: Then $P$ is local on the source in the chosen topology.
theorems.proof: Then $P$ is local on the source in the chosen topology.
refs: Stacks 036H · affine criterion for source locality

theorems.subject: descent-sheaf-data
theorems.name: Pulling back qc data
theorems.hypotheses: Fix families $(U_i\to S^\prime),(V_j\to S)$ and a compatible morphism between them over $h:S^\prime\to S$, consisting of an index map $a$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{a(i)}$.
theorems.statement: Pull the object on $V_{a(i)}$ back by $g_i$ and the overlap transition back by $g_i\times g_{i^\prime}$. This gives a datum on the source family $(U_i)$.
theorems.proof: Pull the object on $V_{a(i)}$ back by $g_i$ and the overlap transition back by $g_i\times g_{i^\prime}$. This gives a datum on the source family $(U_i)$.

theorems.statement: The two pullback functors are naturally isomorphic via the given transitions on the targets.
theorems.proof: The two pullback functors are naturally isomorphic via the given transitions on the targets.

theorems.proof: The augmented complex $0\to M\to A\otimes_R M\to A^{\otimes_R2}\otimes_R M\to\cdots$ with alternating coface differentials is exact.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Testing effectiveness by invariants
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings. Suppose $R\to A$ faithfully flat and let $(N,\varphi)$ be module descent data.
theorems.statement: Effectiveness is equivalent to invertibility of the natural $A$-linear map $A\otimes_R H^0(s(N_\bullet))\to N$.
theorems.proof: Effectiveness is equivalent to invertibility of the natural $A$-linear map $A\otimes_R H^0(s(N_\bullet))\to N$.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Testing all module descent data after base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings. Suppose both $R\to A$ and $R\to R^\prime$ faithfully flat. All module data for $R^\prime\to A\otimes_R R^\prime$ are effective.
theorems.statement: All module data for $R\to A$ are effective.
theorems.proof: All module data for $R\to A$ are effective.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Effectiveness for faithfully flat module data
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings. Suppose the map is faithfully flat.
theorems.statement: Every module descent datum is effective.
theorems.proof: Every module descent datum is effective.
refs: A. Vistoli, Notes on Grothendieck topologies, fibered categories and descent theory, Theorem 4.23

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Module descent equivalence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings. Suppose the map is faithfully flat.
theorems.statement: The functor sending an $R$-module to its canonical descent datum on scalar extension is an equivalence of categories.
theorems.proof: The functor sending an $R$-module to its canonical descent datum on scalar extension is an equivalence of categories.
refs: A. Vistoli, Notes on Grothendieck topologies, fibered categories and descent theory, Theorem 4.23

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Inverse to faithfully flat module descent
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings. Suppose the map is faithfully flat.
theorems.statement: The functor taking the degree-zero cohomology of the associated cochain complex is a quasi-inverse.
theorems.proof: The functor taking the degree-zero cohomology of the associated cochain complex is a quasi-inverse.
refs: A. Vistoli, Notes on Grothendieck topologies, fibered categories and descent theory, Theorem 4.23

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Character duality and exactness
theorems.hypotheses: Work with modules over any commutative ring. Write $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $(r\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$.
theorems.statement: It takes short exact sequences to short exact sequences in reverse order.
theorems.proof: It takes short exact sequences to short exact sequences in reverse order.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Character duality and reflection of injectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Work with modules over any commutative ring. Write $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $(r\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$.
theorems.statement: If $C(f)$ is surjective, $f$ is injective.
theorems.proof: If $C(f)$ is surjective, $f$ is injective.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Character duality and reflection of surjectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Work with modules over any commutative ring. Write $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $(r\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$.
theorems.statement: If $C(f)$ is injective, $f$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Testing module purity on the character dual
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:M\to N$ be a map of $R$-modules. Write $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $(r\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$.
theorems.statement: Tensoring $u$ with every $R$-module is injective exactly when $C(N)\to C(M)$ is a split epimorphism of $R$-modules.
theorems.proof: Tensoring $u$ with every $R$-module is injective exactly when $C(N)\to C(M)$ is a split epimorphism of $R$-modules.
refs: B. Mesablishvili, Pure morphisms of commutative rings are effective descent morphisms for modules, Theorem 4

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Split equalizer of the shifted descent diagram
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:R\to S$ be a commutative ring map and $(M,\theta)$ a module descent datum. Write $S_n=S^{\otimes_R n}$.
theorems.statement: The diagram over $S$ from $M$ to its twofold pullback and then its two parallel arrows to the threefold pullback, using $\theta$ in the first arrow of the pair, is the split equalizer displayed in Tag 08WZ.
theorems.proof: The diagram over $S$ from $M$ to its twofold pullback and then its two parallel arrows to the threefold pullback, using $\theta$ in the first arrow of the pair, is the split equalizer displayed in Tag 08WZ.
refs: Stacks 08WZ · split equalizer of the descent diagram

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Character dual of the split descent diagram
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:R\to S$ be a commutative ring map and $(M,\theta)$ a module descent datum. Write $S_n=S^{\otimes_R n}$.
theorems.statement: Applying the character functor reverses the split equalizer of Tag 08WZ to a split coequalizer.
theorems.proof: Applying the character functor reverses the split equalizer of Tag 08WZ to a split coequalizer.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Split equalizer in tensor powers of a ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:R\to S$ be any commutative ring map. Write $S_n=S^{\otimes_R n}$ with cofaces inserting the unit.
theorems.statement: The diagram $S\to S_2\rightrightarrows S_3$ of the indicated cofaces $\delta_1^1,\delta_2^2,\delta_1^2$ is a split equalizer.
theorems.proof: The diagram $S\to S_2\rightrightarrows S_3$ of the indicated cofaces $\delta_1^1,\delta_2^2,\delta_1^2$ is a split equalizer.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Preservation of the invariant equalizer under pure scalar extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:R\to S$ be a commutative ring map and $(M,\theta)$ a module descent datum. Write $S_n=S^{\otimes_R n}$. Assume $f$ universally injective as a module map.
theorems.statement: Tensoring the invariant equalizer with $S$ yields an equalizer of the shifted descent pair, as in the diagram of the source.
theorems.proof: Tensoring the invariant equalizer with $S$ yields an equalizer of the shifted descent pair, as in the diagram of the source.
refs: Stacks 08X7 · base extension of the invariant equalizer

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: A flat module has injective character module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a flat module over a commutative ring $R$. Write $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $(r\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$.
theorems.statement: The character module $C(M)$ is injective over $R$.
theorems.proof: The character module $C(M)$ is injective over $R$.

theorems.subject: descent-module-data
theorems.name: Pure descent for finitely generated modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be universally injective as a map of $R$-modules. Fix an $R$-module $N$.
theorems.statement: The $R$-module $N$ is finitely generated if and only if $N\otimes_R S$ is finitely generated over $S$.
theorems.proof: The $R$-module $N$ is finitely generated if and only if $N\otimes_R S$ is finitely generated over $S$.

theorems.proof: The $R$-module $N$ is finitely presented if and only if $N\otimes_R S$ is finitely presented over $S$.

theorems.name: Pure descent for flat modules

theorems.proof: The $R$-module $N$ is flat if and only if $N\otimes_R S$ is flat over $S$.

theorems.name: Pure descent for faithfully flat modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be universally injective as a map of $R$-modules. Fix an $R$-module $N$.

theorems.proof: The $R$-module $N$ is finite projective if and only if $N\otimes_R S$ is finite projective over $S$.

theorems.name: Pure descent for of finite type algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be universally injective as a map of $R$-modules. Fix an $R$-algebra $N$.
theorems.statement: The $R$-algebra $N$ is of finite type if and only if $N\otimes_R S$ is of finite type over $S$.

theorems.proof: The $R$-algebra $N$ is étale if and only if $N\otimes_R S$ is étale over $S$.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Replacing a family of scheme maps by its coproduct
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of scheme maps $(X_i\to S)$.
theorems.statement: Scheme descent data relative to the family are canonically equivalent to data for the single map $\coprod_i X_i\to S$.
theorems.proof: Scheme descent data relative to the family are canonically equivalent to data for the single map $\coprod_i X_i\to S$.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Pullback over a commuting square
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a commuting square of scheme maps with upper arrow $f:X^\prime\to X$ and lower arrow $h:S^\prime\to S$.
theorems.statement: Pullback of the underlying scheme and the transition defines a functor to descent data over $X^\prime\to S^\prime$.
theorems.proof: Pullback of the underlying scheme and the transition defines a functor to descent data over $X^\prime\to S^\prime$.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Independence of the upper map
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a commuting square of scheme maps with upper arrow $f:X^\prime\to X$ and lower arrow $h:S^\prime\to S$.  Suppose two upper arrows lie over the same $h$.
theorems.statement: Their pullback functors on descent data are canonically isomorphic.
theorems.proof: Their pullback functors on descent data are canonically isomorphic.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Flat surjections are epimorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to S$ be flat and surjective.
theorems.statement: It is an epimorphism in the category of schemes.
theorems.proof: It is an epimorphism in the category of schemes.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Faithfulness of flat surjective base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S^\prime\to S$ be flat and surjective.
theorems.statement: The base-change functor from schemes over $S$ to schemes over $S^\prime$ is faithful.
theorems.proof: The base-change functor from schemes over $S$ to schemes over $S^\prime$ is faithful.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Faithful pullback by a flat surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a commuting square of scheme maps with upper arrow $f:X^\prime\to X$ and lower arrow $h:S^\prime\to S$.  Suppose $f$ flat and surjective.
theorems.statement: Pullback on scheme descent data is faithful.
theorems.proof: Pullback on scheme descent data is faithful.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fully faithful pullback by an fpqc cover
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a commuting square of scheme maps with upper arrow $f:X^\prime\to X$ and lower arrow $h:S^\prime\to S$.  Take the same base and its identity as $h$, and suppose $(f)$ is an fpqc covering.
theorems.statement: Pullback on scheme descent data is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: Pullback on scheme descent data is fully faithful.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Self-maps act trivially on descent data
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to S$ be a scheme map and $f:X\to X$ any $S$-endomorphism.
theorems.statement: Pullback by $f$ on scheme descent data for $X/S$ is isomorphic to the identity functor.
theorems.proof: Pullback by $f$ on scheme descent data for $X/S$ is isomorphic to the identity functor.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: An arrow in the other direction gives equivalent descent categories
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X^\prime\to X$ be over $S$ and suppose some map $X\to X^\prime$ over $S$ exists. It need not be a section.
theorems.statement: Pullback by $f$ gives an equivalence between scheme descent data for $X/S$ and $X^\prime/S$.
theorems.proof: Pullback by $f$ gives an equivalence between scheme descent data for $X/S$ and $X^\prime/S$.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Faithful restriction using a cover of the base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to X^\prime$ be over $S$ and suppose the structure map $X\to S$ is flat and surjective.
theorems.statement: The pullback from data on $X^\prime/S$ to data on $X/S$ is faithful.
theorems.proof: The pullback from data on $X^\prime/S$ to data on $X/S$ is faithful.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fully faithful restriction using an fpqc base cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to X^\prime$ be over $S$ and assume $(X\to S)$ is an fpqc covering.
theorems.statement: The pullback from data on $X^\prime/S$ to data on $X/S$ is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: The pullback from data on $X^\prime/S$ to data on $X/S$ is fully faithful.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Full faithfulness of componentwise fpqc refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Fix families $(U_i\to S^\prime),(V_j\to S)$ and a compatible morphism between them over $h:S^\prime\to S$, consisting of an index map $a$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{a(i)}$.  Here $S^\prime=S$ and $h$ is its identity.  For every $j$, the family $(U_i\to V_j)_{a(i)=j}$ is fpqc covering.
theorems.statement: Family pullback on scheme descent data is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: Family pullback on scheme descent data is fully faithful.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Equivalence under componentwise Zariski refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Fix families $(U_i\to S^\prime),(V_j\to S)$ and a compatible morphism between them over $h:S^\prime\to S$, consisting of an index map $a$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{a(i)}$.  Here $S^\prime=S$ and $h$ is its identity.  For every $j$, the family $(U_i\to V_j)_{a(i)=j}$ is Zariski covering.
theorems.statement: Family pullback is an equivalence of scheme descent categories.
theorems.proof: Family pullback is an equivalence of scheme descent categories.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Zariski descent for schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of scheme maps $(X_i\to S)$. Suppose the family is a Zariski covering.
theorems.statement: The category of schemes over $S$ is equivalent to its category of scheme descent data.
theorems.proof: The category of schemes over $S$ is equivalent to its category of scheme descent data.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Full faithfulness between fpqc covering families
theorems.hypotheses: Fix families $(U_i\to S^\prime),(V_j\to S)$ and a compatible morphism between them over $h:S^\prime\to S$, consisting of an index map $a$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{a(i)}$.  Here $S^\prime=S$ and $h$ is its identity.  Both families are fpqc coverings of $S$, the first refining the second.
theorems.statement: Pullback along the refinement is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: Pullback along the refinement is fully faithful.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fpqc full faithfulness for schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of scheme maps $(X_i\to S)$. Suppose the family is an fpqc covering.
theorems.statement: The canonical functor identifies schemes over $S$ with a full subcategory of the scheme descent data.
theorems.proof: The canonical functor identifies schemes over $S$ with a full subcategory of the scheme descent data.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Effectiveness from invariant open neighbourhoods
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to S$ be surjective, flat and quasi-compact. Given descent data $(V,\varphi)$, suppose each $v\in V$ lies in an open $W$ such that $\varphi(W\times_S X)\subseteq X\times_S W$ and the restricted datum on $W$ is effective.
theorems.statement: Then the datum on $V$ is effective.
theorems.proof: Then the datum on $V$ is effective.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Affine test for effective descent of morphisms of fixed type
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\tau$ be one of fpqc, fppf, étale, smooth or syntomic. On affines the corresponding test maps are flat, flat of finite presentation, étale, smooth, or syntomic, respectively. Assume $P$ is stable under arbitrary base change, preserved by finite disjoint unions of source and target, and that for every surjective affine test map any scheme datum of type $P$ is effective.
theorems.statement: All scheme descent data of type $P$ are effective along coverings of the chosen topology.
theorems.proof: All scheme descent data of type $P$ are effective along coverings of the chosen topology.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fpqc effective descent for affine morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of scheme maps $(X_i\to S)$. Assume an fpqc covering and a scheme descent datum whose component structure maps are affine.
theorems.statement: The datum is effective.
theorems.proof: The datum is effective.
refs: A. Vistoli, ibid., Theorem 4.29 on quasi-coherent commutative algebras

theorems.statement: The datum is effective.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Descent data as locally representable sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a big scheme site for the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf topology, an object $S$ and a covering $(S_i\to S)$ in its slice site. Use schemes in the chosen site.
theorems.statement: Scheme data on the cover correspond equivalently to sheaves $F$ on the slice site such that each $h_{S_i}\times F$ is representable.
theorems.proof: Scheme data on the cover correspond equivalently to sheaves $F$ on the slice site such that each $h_{S_i}\times F$ is representable.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Local representatives of a sheaf of descent data
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a big scheme site for the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf topology, an object $S$ and a covering $(S_i\to S)$ in its slice site. Use schemes in the chosen site.
theorems.statement: The representatives of the products with $h_{S_i}$ are precisely the local schemes of the corresponding datum.
theorems.proof: The representatives of the products with $h_{S_i}$ are precisely the local schemes of the corresponding datum.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Representability and effectiveness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a big scheme site for the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf topology, an object $S$ and a covering $(S_i\to S)$ in its slice site. Use schemes in the chosen site.
theorems.statement: The sheaf is representable exactly when the corresponding scheme datum is effective.
theorems.proof: The sheaf is representable exactly when the corresponding scheme datum is effective.

theorems.subject: descent-sheaf-data
theorems.name: Galois descent for a field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k^\prime/k$ be a finite Galois extension with group $G$, $Y$ a $k$-scheme, $X=Y_{k^\prime}$ and $f_\sigma$ induced by the field automorphism $\sigma$.
theorems.statement: Quasi-coherent modules on $Y$ correspond to quasi-coherent $F$ on $X$ with isomorphisms $a_\sigma:F\to f_\sigma^*F$ satisfying $a_{\sigma\tau}=f_\sigma^*a_\tau\circ a_\sigma$ for all group elements.
theorems.proof: Quasi-coherent modules on $Y$ correspond to quasi-coherent $F$ on $X$ with isomorphisms $a_\sigma:F\to f_\sigma^*F$ satisfying $a_{\sigma\tau}=f_\sigma^*a_\tau\circ a_\sigma$ for all group elements.

theorems.subject: descent-sheaf-data
theorems.name: Fpqc descent of a quasi-coherent module locally projective
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of scheme maps $(X_i\to S)$. Suppose the family is fpqc covering and $F$ is a quasi-coherent module on $S$. On each covering scheme the pullback is locally projective.
theorems.statement: The module $F$ is locally projective on $S$.
theorems.proof: The module $F$ is locally projective on $S$.

theorems.subject: descent-sheaf-data
theorems.name: Finite type descends along an open flat surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of locally ringed spaces which is open, surjective and flat. For an arbitrary sheaf of modules $F$ on $Y$, assume $f^*F$ of finite type.
theorems.statement: The module $F$ is of finite type on $Y$.
theorems.proof: The module $F$ is of finite type on $Y$.
refs: Stacks 09UB · finiteness on locally ringed spaces

theorems.subject: descent-sheaf-data
theorems.name: Testing finite type by finite pushforward
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be finite and $F$ quasi-coherent on $X$.
theorems.statement: $F$ is of finite type as an $\mathcal O_X$-module if and only if $f_*F$ is of finite type over $\mathcal O_Y$.
theorems.proof: $F$ is of finite type as an $\mathcal O_X$-module if and only if $f_*F$ is of finite type over $\mathcal O_Y$.

theorems.subject: descent-sheaf-data
theorems.name: Testing finite presentation by finite pushforward
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be finite and of finite presentation and $F$ quasi-coherent on $X$.
theorems.statement: $F$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_X$-module if and only if $f_*F$ is of finite presentation over $\mathcal O_Y$.
theorems.proof: $F$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_X$-module if and only if $f_*F$ is of finite presentation over $\mathcal O_Y$.

theorems.hypotheses: Fix a scheme $S$ and the big scheme site over $S$ for the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf topology. The corresponding small-site assertions use only Zariski and étale. Fix an affine object $U$ and a standard finite affine covering $(U_i\to U)_{1\le i\le n}$ for the chosen topology.  For the literal singleton-cover formulation take étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf, or a Zariski family with pairwise disjoint images.
theorems.statement: The map $\coprod_iU_i\to U$ is a singleton cover.
theorems.proof: The map $\coprod_iU_i\to U$ is a singleton cover.

theorems.subject: descent-ringed-site
theorems.name: The coproduct arrow generates a covering Zariski sieve (editorial qualification)
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite family of open immersions cover an affine scheme $U$. Work on the big Zariski site containing their coproduct.
theorems.statement: Comparing Tag 03FI with the open-immersion definition in Tag 020O, the sieve generated by the coproduct arrow covers since the original family refines it. If two images overlap, this arrow is not an open immersion and is not a singleton covering family as defined in Tag 020O. On the small Zariski site the coproduct need not be an object.
theorems.proof: Comparing Tag 03FI with the open-immersion definition in Tag 020O, the sieve generated by the coproduct arrow covers since the original family refines it. If two images overlap, this arrow is not an open immersion and is not a singleton covering family as defined in Tag 020O. On the small Zariski site the coproduct need not be an object.
refs: Stacks 020O · definition of a Zariski covering family

theorems.subject: descent-ringed-site
theorems.name: Čech comparison for overlapping opens on the big site
theorems.hypotheses: Work on the big Zariski site with an abelian sheaf and a finite standard affine open cover. Form the coproduct arrow to the base.
theorems.statement: The summand inclusions give a covering refinement. All iterated fibre products of the coproduct decompose as disjoint unions of the multiple intersections, so the two Čech complexes agree even if the singleton is not an open cover.
theorems.proof: The summand inclusions give a covering refinement. All iterated fibre products of the coproduct decompose as disjoint unions of the multiple intersections, so the two Čech complexes agree even if the singleton is not an open cover.
refs: Stacks 03FI · (2),(3) overlapping opens in the big site

theorems.subject: descent-ringed-site
theorems.name: Čech and Amitsur complexes on standard affine covers
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a scheme $S$ and the big scheme site over $S$ for the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf topology. The corresponding small-site assertions use only Zariski and étale. Fix an affine object $U$ and a standard finite affine covering $(U_i\to U)_{1\le i\le n}$ for the chosen topology. For a quasi-coherent $F$ on $S$, the associated sheaf $F^a$ evaluates on $t:T\to S$ as $\Gamma(T,t^*F)$.
theorems.statement: Put $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)$, $A=\prod_i\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O)$ and $M=F^a(U)$. Then $R\to A$ is faithfully flat and the Čech complex identifies with the alternating complex of $A^{\otimes_R(\bullet+1)}\otimes_R M$.
theorems.proof: Put $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)$, $A=\prod_i\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O)$ and $M=F^a(U)$. Then $R\to A$ is faithfully flat and the Čech complex identifies with the alternating complex of $A^{\otimes_R(\bullet+1)}\otimes_R M$.

theorems.statement: For every $q\ge0$ the comparison identifies ordinary scheme cohomology $H^q(S,F)$ with the cohomology of $F^a$ on the specified site.
theorems.proof: For every $q\ge0$ the comparison identifies ordinary scheme cohomology $H^q(S,F)$ with the cohomology of $F^a$ on the specified site.
refs: SGA 4, Exposé VII, Proposition 4.3 (small étale–Zariski comparison)

theorems.subject: descent-ringed-site
theorems.name: Pullback of associated quasi-coherent sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a scheme $S$ and the big scheme site over $S$ for the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf topology. The corresponding small-site assertions use only Zariski and étale. Let $f:T\to S$ and take quasi-coherent $F$ on $S$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural identification $f^*(F^a)=(f^*F)^a$ under the corresponding equivalences.
theorems.proof: There is a natural identification $f^*(F^a)=(f^*F)^a$ under the corresponding equivalences.

theorems.subject: descent-ringed-site
theorems.name: Big-site pushforward can fail to correspond
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a scheme $S$ and the big scheme site over $S$ for the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic or fppf topology. Consider an arbitrary scheme morphism and its pushforward functor.
theorems.statement: The equivalence on quasi-coherent sheaves generally fails to intertwine scheme pushforward with big-site pushforward. In the punctured affine plane over a field, the pushforward of the structure sheaf from the complement of the origin is the structure sheaf, while the fibre of that open immersion over the origin is empty.
theorems.proof: The equivalence on quasi-coherent sheaves generally fails to intertwine scheme pushforward with big-site pushforward. In the punctured affine plane over a field, the pushforward of the structure sheaf from the complement of the origin is the structure sheaf, while the fibre of that open immersion over the origin is empty.

theorems.subject: descent-ringed-site
theorems.name: Small-site pushforward preserves quasi-coherence

theorems.statement: Scheme pushforward sends quasi-coherent modules to quasi-coherent modules, and so does the small-site pushforward.
theorems.proof: Scheme pushforward sends quasi-coherent modules to quasi-coherent modules, and so does the small-site pushforward.

theorems.subject: descent-ringed-site

theorems.statement: There is a canonical identification $f_{\rm small,*}(F^a)=(f_*F)^a$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical identification $f_{\rm small,*}(F^a)=(f_*F)^a$.

theorems.subject: descent-ringed-site
theorems.name: Comparison of higher direct images on the small site

theorems.proof: For all $i\ge0$, $R^if_{\rm small,*}(F^a)=(R^if_*F)^a$ canonically.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Testing universal effective epimorphisms on modules
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of scheme maps $(X_i\to S)$. All schemes are affine.
theorems.statement: Universal effectiveness in affine schemes is equivalent to exactness at the first two terms of $0\to\Gamma(S,F)\to\prod_i\Gamma(X_i,F_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{ij}\Gamma(X_i\times_S X_j,F_{ij})$ in the equalizer sense for every quasi-coherent $F$, using its indicated pullbacks.
theorems.proof: Universal effectiveness in affine schemes is equivalent to exactness at the first two terms of $0\to\Gamma(S,F)\to\prod_i\Gamma(X_i,F_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{ij}\Gamma(X_i\times_S X_j,F_{ij})$ in the equalizer sense for every quasi-coherent $F$, using its indicated pullbacks.
