theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Uniqueness of fpqc descent of an open subset
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of scheme maps $(X_i\to S)$. Suppose the family fpqc, and opens $W_i\subset X_i$ have equal two pullbacks to each pairwise overlap.
theorems.statement: At most one open $W\subset S$ has inverse images $W_i$ for all $i$.
theorems.proof: At most one open $W\subset S$ has inverse images $W_i$ for all $i$.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fpqc covers are universally effectively epimorphic
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a family of scheme maps $(X_i\to S)$. Assume the given family is an fpqc cover.
theorems.statement: The family is universally effectively epimorphic in schemes.
theorems.proof: The family is universally effectively epimorphic in schemes.
refs: A. Vistoli, Notes on Grothendieck topologies, fibered categories and descent theory, Theorem 2.55

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fpqc sheaf condition for representables
theorems.hypotheses: Work with schemes and fpqc covering families.
theorems.statement: Every scheme-representable presheaf satisfies the fpqc sheaf condition.
theorems.proof: Every scheme-representable presheaf satisfies the fpqc sheaf condition.
refs: A. Vistoli, Notes on Grothendieck topologies, fibered categories and descent theory, Theorem 2.55

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Descent of coequalizers from a cover and its overlaps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a,b:X\rightrightarrows Y$ and $c:Y\to Z$ satisfy $ca=cb$. Assume an fpqc cover $(Z_i\to Z)$ exists such that after base change to each $Z_i$ and to every $Z_i\times_Z Z_j$, the projection from the pullback of $Y$ is the coequalizer in schemes of the two pulled-back maps from $X$.
theorems.statement: Then $c$ is a coequalizer of $a,b$ in schemes.
theorems.proof: Then $c$ is a coequalizer of $a,b$ in schemes.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Postcomposition by an étale arrow
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be étale local on source and target, let $f:X\to Y$ have $P$, and let $g:Y\to Z$ be étale.
theorems.statement: $gf$ has $P$.
theorems.proof: $gf$ has $P$.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Cancellation of an étale arrow on the target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be étale local on source and target and let $g:Y\to Z$ be étale. Assume $gf$ has $P$.
theorems.statement: The original $f:X\to Y$ has $P$.
theorems.proof: The original $f:X\to Y$ has $P$.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Joint étale locality tested by pointed neighbourhoods
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on source and target and fix $f:X\to Y$. Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian.
theorems.statement: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. At every $x$ there is an étale map of germs $(U,u)\to(X,x)$, an étale $V\to Y$ and a map $U\to V$ with $P$ making the square commute on representatives.
theorems.proof: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. At every $x$ there is an étale map of germs $(U,u)\to(X,x)$, an étale $V\to Y$ and a map $U\to V$ with $P$ making the square commute on representatives.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Joint étale locality tested by all étale squares
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on source and target and fix $f:X\to Y$. Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian.
theorems.statement: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. In every commuting square with étale vertical arrows the top arrow has $P$.
theorems.proof: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. In every commuting square with étale vertical arrows the top arrow has $P$.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Joint étale locality tested by one surjective square
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on source and target and fix $f:X\to Y$. Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian.
theorems.statement: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. There is a commuting square as above with an étale surjective left arrow, an étale right arrow and top arrow with $P$.
theorems.proof: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. There is a commuting square as above with an étale surjective left arrow, an étale right arrow and top arrow with $P$.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Joint étale locality tested by a target cover
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on source and target and fix $f:X\to Y$. Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian.
theorems.statement: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. Some étale target cover makes all pullbacks of $f$ have $P$.
theorems.proof: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. Some étale target cover makes all pullbacks of $f$ have $P$.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Joint étale locality tested by a source cover
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on source and target and fix $f:X\to Y$. Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian.
theorems.statement: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. Some étale source cover makes all composites to $Y$ have $P$.
theorems.proof: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. Some étale source cover makes all composites to $Y$ have $P$.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Joint étale locality tested by successive target and source covers
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on source and target and fix $f:X\to Y$. Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian.
theorems.statement: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. There exists an étale target cover $(Y_i\to Y)$ and étale covers of $X\times_Y Y_i$ such that every resulting arrow to $Y_i$ has $P$.
theorems.proof: $P(f)$ is equivalent to the following condition. There exists an étale target cover $(Y_i\to Y)$ and étale covers of $X\times_Y Y_i$ such that every resulting arrow to $Y_i$ has $P$.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: From separate étale locality to joint locality
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on both the source and the target separately, and postcomposition with any open immersion preserves it.
theorems.statement: Then $P$ is étale local on source and target in the joint sense.
theorems.proof: Then $P$ is étale local on source and target in the joint sense.
refs: Stacks 04R2 · sufficient conditions for joint locality

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: The source locus in an étale square
theorems.hypotheses: Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian. Write $W(f)$ for the largest open in the source on which the restriction of $f$ has $P$. Assume joint étale locality of $P$. Let $a$ be étale at $u$ and $b$ étale at $h(u)$.
theorems.statement: Then $a(u)\in W(f)$ if and only if $u\in W(h)$.
theorems.proof: Then $a(u)\in W(f)$ if and only if $u\in W(h)$.

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Source loci in a smooth target square
theorems.hypotheses: Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian. Write $W(f)$ for the largest open in the source on which the restriction of $f$ has $P$. Assume $P$ étale local on the source, smooth local on the target and preserved by postcomposition with open immersions. Suppose $b$ smooth at $h(u)$ and $U\to X\times_YV$ étale at $u$.
theorems.statement: Then $a(u)\in W(f)$ exactly when $u\in W(h)$.
theorems.proof: Then $a(u)\in W(f)$ exactly when $u\in W(h)$.
refs: Stacks 0CF1 · smooth comparison of the source locus

theorems.subject: descent-locality
theorems.name: Invariant opens for polynomial shears
theorems.hypotheses: Take $n\ge2$, a field $k$ and a nonempty open $W\subset\mathbb A^n_k$. For every $i\ne j$ and $d\ge0$, require invariance under $x_i\mapsto x_i+x_j^d$, fixing the other coordinates.
theorems.statement: Either $W$ is the whole affine space, or $k$ has positive characteristic $p$ and its complement is a finite set of closed points whose coordinates are algebraic over $\mathbb F_p$.
theorems.proof: Either $W$ is the whole affine space, or $k$ has positive characteristic $p$ and its complement is a finite set of closed points whose coordinates are algebraic over $\mathbb F_p$.
refs: Stacks 0CF0 · invariant open or finite exceptional complement

theorems.subject: descent-germ
theorems.name: Induced property on germ morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on source and target and fix $f:X\to Y$. Define $Q$ on a map of germs by existence of a representative with $P$.
theorems.statement: Then $Q$ is étale local on source and target for germ morphisms.
theorems.proof: Then $Q$ is étale local on source and target for germ morphisms.
refs: Stacks 04R6 · locality of the extension to germs

theorems.subject: descent-germ
theorems.name: Recovering a global property from all source germs
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $P$ is étale local on source and target and fix $f:X\to Y$. Let $Q$ mean that some neighbourhood representative has $P$.
theorems.statement: $f$ has $P$ exactly when its germ at every $x\in X$ has $Q$.
theorems.proof: $f$ has $P$ exactly when its germ at every $x\in X$ has $Q$.

theorems.subject: descent-germ
theorems.name: Flatness at a marked point under étale changes of both germs
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a morphism of scheme germs $(X,x)\to(S,s)$.
theorems.statement: The condition flatness of $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is étale local on source and target.
theorems.proof: The condition flatness of $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is étale local on source and target.

theorems.subject: descent-germ
theorems.name: Local dimension of the fibre ring under étale changes of both germs
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a morphism of scheme germs $(X,x)\to(S,s)$. Fix $d\in\mathbb N\cup\{0,\infty\}$.
theorems.statement: The condition $\dim\mathcal O_{X_s,x}=d$ is étale local on source and target.
theorems.proof: The condition $\dim\mathcal O_{X_s,x}=d$ is étale local on source and target.

theorems.subject: descent-germ
theorems.name: Residue transcendence degree under étale changes of both germs
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a morphism of scheme germs $(X,x)\to(S,s)$. Fix $r\in\mathbb N\cup\{0,\infty\}$.
theorems.statement: The condition $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x)=r$ is étale local on source and target.
theorems.proof: The condition $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x)=r$ is étale local on source and target.

theorems.subject: descent-germ
theorems.name: Dimension of the fibre at the point under étale changes of both germs
theorems.hypotheses: Consider a morphism of scheme germs $(X,x)\to(S,s)$. Fix $d\in\mathbb N\cup\{0,\infty\}$.
theorems.statement: The condition $\dim_x(X_s)=d$ is étale local on source and target.
theorems.proof: The condition $\dim_x(X_s)=d$ is étale local on source and target.

theorems.subject: descent-germ
theorems.name: Étaleness of the map on fibres in a commuting square
theorems.hypotheses: Write a commuting square with horizontal $h:U\to V$, $f:X\to Y$ and vertical $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$; it need not be cartesian. Assume $a,b$ étale, choose $v\in V$, and put $y=b(v)$.
theorems.statement: The induced map $U_v\to X_y$ is étale.
theorems.proof: The induced map $U_v\to X_y$ is étale.
refs: Stacks 04NI · étaleness on the indicated fibres

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Testing unramified at a prime by its local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be finite type with $A$ Noetherian, and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ lie over $\mathfrak p\subset A$.
theorems.statement: The map is unramified at $\mathfrak q$ exactly when $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is unramified in the Noetherian local sense.
theorems.proof: This is the residue-field unramifiedness criterion on localizing, with local flatness added in the étale case.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there
Stacks 039G · criterion at the specified prime

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Testing étale at a prime by its local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be finite type with $A$ Noetherian, and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ lie over $\mathfrak p\subset A$.
theorems.statement: The map is étale at $\mathfrak q$ exactly when $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is étale in the Noetherian local sense.
theorems.proof: This is the residue-field unramifiedness criterion on localizing, with local flatness added in the étale case.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.6.1 and 17.6.3, local and completed étale criteria
Stacks 039L · criterion at the specified prime

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finiteness of the completed target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume the map is unramified in the local-ring sense of Tag 024M. Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: The completed target is a finite module over the completed source.
theorems.proof: The maximal-ideal and residue conditions control the completed algebra. For discrete valuation rings a uniformizer generates the maximal ideal.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Surjectivity after completion with equal residues
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume the map is unramified in the local-ring sense of Tag 024M. Suppose the residue field map is an isomorphism.Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: The map of completions is surjective.
theorems.proof: The maximal-ideal and residue conditions control the completed algebra. For discrete valuation rings a uniformizer generates the maximal ideal.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Surjectivity after completion with separably closed residue field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume the map is unramified in the local-ring sense of Tag 024M. Suppose the residue field of $A$ is separably closed.Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: The map of completions is surjective.
theorems.proof: The maximal-ideal and residue conditions control the completed algebra. For discrete valuation rings a uniformizer generates the maximal ideal.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Uniformizer test for complete discrete valuation rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume both rings are complete discrete valuation rings.Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: The local map is unramified exactly when a source uniformizer maps to a target uniformizer, the residue field extension is finite separable, and the target is essentially of finite type over the source.
theorems.proof: The maximal-ideal and residue conditions control the completed algebra. For discrete valuation rings a uniformizer generates the maximal ideal.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Completion criterion for unramified maps, local-ring formulation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume $B$ essentially of finite type over $A$. Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: The original local map is unramified in the local-ring sense if and only if the map on completions is unramified in the Noetherian local-ring sense.
theorems.proof: Completion preserves the residue fields and detects the maximal-ideal equality; faithful flatness of completion also detects flatness in the étale case.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Completion criterion for unramified maps, ring-map formulation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume $B$ essentially of finite type over $A$. Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: The original local map is unramified in the local-ring sense if and only if the map on completions is unramified as a ring map (in particular of finite type here).
theorems.proof: Completion preserves the residue fields and detects the maximal-ideal equality; faithful flatness of completion also detects flatness in the étale case.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Completion criterion for étale maps, local-ring formulation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume $B$ essentially of finite type over $A$. Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: The original local map is étale in the local-ring sense if and only if the map on completions is étale in the Noetherian local-ring sense.
theorems.proof: Completion preserves the residue fields and detects the maximal-ideal equality; faithful flatness of completion also detects flatness in the étale case.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.6.1 and 17.6.3, local and completed étale criteria

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Completion criterion for étale maps, ring-map formulation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume $B$ essentially of finite type over $A$. Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: The original local map is étale in the local-ring sense if and only if the map on completions is étale as a ring map (in particular of finite type here).
theorems.proof: Completion preserves the residue fields and detects the maximal-ideal equality; faithful flatness of completion also detects flatness in the étale case.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.6.1 and 17.6.3, local and completed étale criteria

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Completed étale local algebras are finite free
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume the map is étale in the local-ring sense of Tag 0258. Use completions for the respective maximal ideals.
theorems.statement: There is an isomorphism of completed-source modules $\widehat B\simeq(\widehat A)^{\oplus n}$ with $n\ge1$.
theorems.proof: The completed map is finite and flat, and its source is local.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.6.1 and 17.6.3, local and completed étale criteria

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Agreement of the local and general definitions of unramified
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian. Fix $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$.
theorems.statement: The stalk map satisfies the unramified local-ring definition precisely when $f$ is unramified at $x$ in the general scheme-theoretic sense.
theorems.proof: Choose affine charts and apply the local algebra criterion.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Agreement of the local and general definitions of étale
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian. Fix $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$.
theorems.statement: The stalk map satisfies the étale local-ring definition precisely when $f$ is étale at $x$ in the general scheme-theoretic sense.
theorems.proof: Choose affine charts and apply the local algebra criterion.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.6.1 and 17.6.3, local and completed étale criteria

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Differential criterion for unramifiedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian. Fix $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$.
theorems.statement: Unramifiedness at $x$ is equivalent to the following condition. $\Omega_{X/Y,x}=0$.
theorems.proof: The conormal exact sequence translates vanishing of differentials into the local presentation. The diagonal of an unramified map is an open immersion locally at the point.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Conormal criterion for unramifiedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian. Fix $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$.
theorems.statement: Unramifiedness at $x$ is equivalent to the following condition. There are open neighbourhoods of $x,y$ giving a closed immersion of the source neighbourhood into affine $n$-space over the target neighbourhood for some $n$, such that differentials of local elements of the defining ideal generate the ambient relative cotangent stalk at the image of $x$.
theorems.proof: The conormal exact sequence translates vanishing of differentials into the local presentation. The diagonal of an unramified map is an open immersion locally at the point.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Diagonal criterion for unramifiedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian. Fix $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$.
theorems.statement: Unramifiedness at $x$ is equivalent to the following condition. The relative diagonal is a local isomorphism at $x$.
theorems.proof: The conormal exact sequence translates vanishing of differentials into the local presentation. The diagonal of an unramified map is an open immersion locally at the point.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Unramified morphisms and uniqueness across infinitesimal thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The morphism is unramified if and only if it is formally unramified.
theorems.proof: The infinitesimal uniqueness property is equivalent to vanishing relative differentials; the assumed finite type supplies the finiteness part.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.1 and 17.4.4, under the finite presentation or Noetherian hypotheses there

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Sections are open immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $s$ be any section of a unramified morphism of schemes.
theorems.statement: The section is an open immersion.
theorems.proof: The section is obtained by base change of the relative diagonal. Apply the corresponding diagonal criterion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Sections are closed immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $s$ be any section of a separated morphism of schemes.
theorems.statement: The section is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: The section is obtained by base change of the relative diagonal. Apply the corresponding diagonal criterion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Sections are open and closed immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $s$ be any section of a unramified and separated morphism of schemes.
theorems.statement: The section is both an open and a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: The section is obtained by base change of the relative diagonal. Apply the corresponding diagonal criterion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Image of a section
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be unramified and separated, with $Y$ connected and nonempty.
theorems.statement: Each section is an isomorphism onto a connected component of $X$.
theorems.proof: The section image is connected, open and closed. On such a component the section is forced to be the inverse to $f$.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.9, sections of separated unramified morphisms over a connected base

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Components that carry sections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be unramified and separated, with $Y$ connected and nonempty.
theorems.statement: Taking the image bijects sections with components mapped isomorphically onto $Y$.
theorems.proof: The section image is connected, open and closed. On such a component the section is forced to be the inverse to $f$.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.9, sections of separated unramified morphisms over a connected base

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: At most one section through a point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be unramified and separated, with $Y$ connected and nonempty.
theorems.statement: For any point of $X$ at most one section has it in its image.
theorems.proof: The section image is connected, open and closed. On such a component the section is forced to be the inverse to $f$.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.9, sections of separated unramified morphisms over a connected base

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Uniqueness from a point and its residue map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to S$ be unramified and separated and let $Y$ be a connected $S$-scheme. Suppose $a,b:Y\to X$ over $S$ agree at a point $y$ and induce the same maps $\kappa(a(y))\to\kappa(y)$.
theorems.statement: The two scheme morphisms agree on $Y$.
theorems.proof: Their equalizer is open and closed by the diagonal criterion; the residue hypothesis puts $y$ in it.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA IV₄, 17.4.9, sections of separated unramified morphisms over a connected base

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Finiteness of a relative set of morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be Noetherian and $X\to S$ unramified and quasi-compact. Let $Y\to S$ have Noetherian source.
theorems.statement: The set of $S$-morphisms $Y\to X$ is finite.
theorems.proof: For separated targets the image of one point on each connected component and its residue-field map determine a lift. Their possibilities are finite. The general case uses a generically finite open and Noetherian induction on its closed complement.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flatness after killing a fibrewise nonzerodivisor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let $M$ be finite over $B$ and flat over $A$. Suppose $t\in\mathfrak m_B$ acts injectively on $M/\mathfrak m_AM$.
theorems.statement: Then $M/tM$ is flat as an $A$-module.
theorems.proof: Use the local flatness criterion for the quotient by the fibrewise nonzerodivisor.

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Openness of the sheaf flat locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian. Let $F$ be coherent on $X$.
theorems.statement: The locus where $F$ is flat relative to $Y$ is open in $X$.
theorems.proof: Apply openness of flatness for finitely presented coherent modules in the Noetherian finite-type setting.

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Openness of the map flat locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian. Use the structure sheaf.
theorems.statement: The flat locus of $f$ is open in $X$.
theorems.proof: Apply openness of flatness for finitely presented coherent modules in the Noetherian finite-type setting.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Flat locally finite type maps over a locally Noetherian base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be locally of finite type with $Y$ locally Noetherian. Suppose $f$ flat.
theorems.statement: The map $f$ is universally open, hence open.
theorems.proof: Over a locally Noetherian base the map is locally finitely presented. Flat locally finitely presented morphisms are universally open.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: A finite unramified map near a single radicial fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite morphism $f:X\to S$ and $s\in S$. Its set-theoretic fibre is the singleton $\{x\}$ and $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is purely inseparable. Assume $f$ is unramified.
theorems.statement: There exists an open neighbourhood of $s$ over which the entire morphism is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: The finite separable and purely inseparable residue extension is trivial. For a finite unramified algebra the residue criterion makes the map locally surjective on algebras; flatness in the étale case removes the defining ideal near the point.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: A finite étale map near a single radicial fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite morphism $f:X\to S$ and $s\in S$. Its set-theoretic fibre is the singleton $\{x\}$ and $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is purely inseparable. Assume $f$ is étale.
theorems.statement: There exists an open neighbourhood of $s$ over which the entire morphism is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The finite separable and purely inseparable residue extension is trivial. For a finite unramified algebra the residue criterion makes the map locally surjective on algebras; flatness in the étale case removes the defining ideal near the point.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Standard étale model for an étale local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume the map is étale in the local-ring sense of Tag 0258.
theorems.statement: There are polynomials $F,g\in A[t]$, with $F$ monic and $F^\prime$ a unit in $A[t,1/g]/(F)$, such that $B$ is the localization of this standard étale algebra at a prime.
theorems.proof: Use the local structure theorem and its unramified quotient formulation.

theorems.name: Standard étale model for an unramified local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume the map is unramified in the local-ring sense of Tag 024M.

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Étale coordinates over a prescribed affine target neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be étale at $x$, and fix any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $f(x)$.
theorems.statement: Some affine neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ factors over $V$ by an open immersion $U\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(R[t,1/F^\prime]/(F))$ for a monic polynomial $F\in R[t]$.
theorems.proof: Apply the standard presentation locally and shrink the source inside its standard étale model.

theorems.name: Smooth morphisms locally admit étale coordinates

theorems.proof: A standard smooth presentation with invertible Jacobian minor gives an étale map to affine space in the remaining coordinates.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Relative Frobenius of an étale morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme in characteristic $p>0$ for a prime $p$, and $U\to X$ étale.
theorems.statement: The relative Frobenius $U\to U\times_{X,F_X}X$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The relative Frobenius is a universal homeomorphism, and this map between étale $X$-schemes is étale.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Maps to an étale scheme lift across nil-immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S_0\hookrightarrow S$ be a closed immersion with the same underlying topological space. Its ideal need only be locally nil elementwise. Let $X$ be étale over $S$ and $Y$ any $S$-scheme.
theorems.statement: Restriction gives a bijection from $S$-maps $Y\to X$ to $S_0$-maps $Y_{S_0}\to X_{S_0}$.
theorems.proof: The étale lifting and finite-presentation conditions allow maps to lift uniquely locally through nil ideals, and uniqueness glues the lifts.
refs: D. Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms, Proposition A.4

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Full faithfulness after restriction to a nil-immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S_0\hookrightarrow S$ be a closed immersion with the same underlying topological space. Its ideal need only be locally nil elementwise.
theorems.statement: Restriction of étale schemes from $S$ to $S_0$ is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: Apply the unique lifting of maps between étale schemes.
refs: D. Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms, Proposition A.4

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Lifting étale schemes from a nil-immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S_0\hookrightarrow S$ be a closed immersion with the same underlying topological space. Its ideal need only be locally nil elementwise.
theorems.statement: Every étale $S_0$-scheme lifts to an étale $S$-scheme; with full faithfulness this gives an equivalence of the étale categories.
theorems.proof: Standard étale models lift on affine charts; full faithfulness lifts their overlap isomorphisms and permits gluing.

theorems.subject: morphism

theorems.hypotheses: By a pointed étale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$ we mean an étale map taking $u$ to $s$; its residue extension may be nontrivial. Let $X\to S$ be finite and unramified, with $s\in S$.
theorems.statement: There exists such a $U$ over which $X_U$ is a finite disjoint union of schemes whose maps to $U$ are closed immersions into $U$. The empty fibre can yield the empty union after shrinking.
theorems.proof: Finite maps are separated and closed. Apply the separated local picture to the whole fibre and shrink the base to remove the complementary part.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Faithfulness for étale objects over a surjective map
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, let $D_f$ take an étale $S$-scheme to the canonical descent datum on its pullback to $X$. Assume $f$ surjective.
theorems.statement: The functor $D_f$ is faithful.
theorems.proof: For maps between étale objects the equalizer is open; surjectivity detects when it is the entire source.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Descent of maps between étale objects along submersions
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, let $D_f$ take an étale $S$-scheme to the canonical descent datum on its pullback to $X$. Assume $f$ is submersive and remains submersive after every étale base change.
theorems.statement: The functor $D_f$ is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: A compatible map is encoded by its graph, an open subscheme in the relevant fibre product. Submersiveness after étale base change descends this graph.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fully faithful étale descent for surjective and universally closed maps
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, let $D_f$ take an étale $S$-scheme to the canonical descent datum on its pullback to $X$. Suppose $f$ is surjective and universally closed.
theorems.statement: The functor $D_f$ is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: In this class $f$ and its étale base changes induce the quotient topology, so the graph argument applies.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fully faithful étale descent for surjective and universally open maps
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, let $D_f$ take an étale $S$-scheme to the canonical descent datum on its pullback to $X$. Suppose $f$ is surjective and universally open.
theorems.statement: The functor $D_f$ is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: In this class $f$ and its étale base changes induce the quotient topology, so the graph argument applies.
refs: D. Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms, Theorems 5.17 and 5.19 (étale algebraic spaces in the paper)

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Fully faithful étale descent for surjective, quasi-compact and flat maps
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, let $D_f$ take an étale $S$-scheme to the canonical descent datum on its pullback to $X$. Suppose $f$ is surjective, quasi-compact and flat.
theorems.statement: The functor $D_f$ is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: In this class $f$ and its étale base changes induce the quotient topology, so the graph argument applies.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Local effectiveness of an étale descent datum
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, let $D_f$ take an étale $S$-scheme to the canonical descent datum on its pullback to $X$. Let $V\to X$ be étale with scheme descent datum for $X/S$. Choose an open cover $(S_i)$ of $S$. Assume the restricted data on $S_i$ are effective, the corresponding functors $D$ on pairwise overlaps are fully faithful, and those on triple overlaps are faithful.
theorems.statement: The given datum is effective.
theorems.proof: Full faithfulness gives unique gluing isomorphisms over pairwise overlaps; faithfulness over triples gives their cocycle identity. Glue the local realizations.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Henselian splitting of an étale scheme: decomposition
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair. Let $U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be quasi-compact, separated and étale, with its base change to $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ finite.
theorems.statement: There is a disjoint decomposition $U=U_{\rm fin}\amalg U_{\rm away}$ with the two stated properties simultaneously.
theorems.proof: A quasi-finite separated presentation embeds in a finite neighbourhood. Henselian lifting of the open-and-closed special-fibre piece produces the finite summand.

theorems.subject: descent-scheme-data
theorems.name: Effective descent of quasi-compact separated étale schemes
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, let $D_f$ take an étale $S$-scheme to the canonical descent datum on its pullback to $X$. Assume $f$ integral and surjective. Restrict to objects quasi-compact and separated over their respective bases.
theorems.statement: The functor $D_f$ is an equivalence from such étale $S$-schemes to compatible descent data on such étale $X$-schemes.
theorems.proof: Full faithfulness follows from universal closedness. The effectivity argument uses henselian neighbourhoods to descend the finite pieces and glues them; the separated quasi-finite descended objects are schemes.

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme
theorems.name: Smooth pullback of strict normal crossings divisors
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Suppose $D$ is a strict normal crossings divisor and $Y\to X$ is smooth.
theorems.statement: The pullback divisor on $Y$ has strict normal crossings.
theorems.proof: Flat pullback preserves the Cartier divisor. Smooth pullback preserves the regular parameter description; étale charts can first be pulled back for the étale-local case.

theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Suppose $D$ is a normal crossings divisor and $Y\to X$ is smooth.
theorems.statement: The pullback divisor on $Y$ has normal crossings.
theorems.proof: Flat pullback preserves the Cartier divisor. Smooth pullback preserves the regular parameter description; étale charts can first be pulled back for the étale-local case.

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme
theorems.name: Reducedness of a normal crossings divisor
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Assume $D$ is a normal crossings divisor. Write $N\to D$ for the normalization of $D_{\rm red}$ followed by the inclusion into $D$. For $n\ge1$ let $Z_n$ be the complement of the union of all pairwise diagonals in the $n$-fold fibre product of $N$ over $D$. These are relative diagonals of schemes, accounting for distinct branches after field extension.
theorems.statement: $D$ is reduced.
theorems.proof: Étale localization reduces the assertion to transverse intersections of distinct Cartier branches in the strict case.

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme
theorems.name: Unramified normalization of a normal crossings divisor
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Assume $D$ is a normal crossings divisor. Write $N\to D$ for the normalization of $D_{\rm red}$ followed by the inclusion into $D$. For $n\ge1$ let $Z_n$ be the complement of the union of all pairwise diagonals in the $n$-fold fibre product of $N$ over $D$. theorems.statement: $N\to D$ is unramified.
theorems.proof: Étale localization reduces the assertion to transverse intersections of distinct Cartier branches in the strict case.

theorems.name: Regularity of ordered branch strata of a normal crossings divisor
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Assume $D$ is a normal crossings divisor. Write $N\to D$ for the normalization of $D_{\rm red}$ followed by the inclusion into $D$. theorems.proof: Étale localization reduces the assertion to transverse intersections of distinct Cartier branches in the strict case.

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme
theorems.name: Local complete intersection branch maps of a normal crossings divisor
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Assume $D$ is a normal crossings divisor. theorems.statement: Each $Z_n\to X$ is a local complete intersection morphism.
theorems.proof: Étale localization reduces the assertion to transverse intersections of distinct Cartier branches in the strict case.

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme
theorems.name: Conormal rank of branch maps of a normal crossings divisor
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Assume $D$ is a normal crossings divisor. Write $N\to D$ for the normalization of $D_{\rm red}$ followed by the inclusion into $D$. For $n\ge1$ let $Z_n$ be the complement of the union of all pairwise diagonals in the $n$-fold fibre product of $N$ over $D$. These are relative diagonals of schemes, accounting for distinct branches after field extension.
theorems.statement: The conormal sheaf of $Z_n\to X$ is locally free of rank $n$.
theorems.proof: Étale localization reduces the assertion to transverse intersections of distinct Cartier branches in the strict case.

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme
theorems.name: Recognizing normal crossings from the normalization
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Write $N\to D$ for the normalization of $D_{\rm red}$ followed by the inclusion into $D$. For $n\ge1$ let $Z_n$ be the complement of the union of all pairwise diagonals in the $n$-fold fibre product of $N$ over $D$. These are relative diagonals of schemes, accounting for distinct branches after field extension. Assume $D$ reduced, its normalization unramified, and every $Z_n$ regular with $Z_n\to X$ a local complete intersection whose conormal sheaf is locally free of rank $n$.
theorems.statement: The closed subscheme $D$ is a normal crossings divisor.
theorems.proof: Étale locally the normalization splits into closed branches. The local complete intersection and conormal-rank conditions give regular branches of the asserted codimensions and hence a strict crossings chart.

theorems.subject: etale-closed-subscheme
theorems.name: Strict henselizations detect normal crossings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ and a closed subscheme $D\subseteq X$. Assume $X$ is J-2 or Nagata.
theorems.statement: The subscheme $D$ is a normal crossings divisor if and only if its pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,p}^{\rm sh}$ is a strict normal crossings divisor for every $p\in D$.
theorems.proof: A strict henselization splits étale branches. The additional finiteness and regular-locus hypotheses allow the local description to descend to an étale neighbourhood.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-compact unramified schemes over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and consider the structure map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Assume $X$ quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: It is unramified exactly when it is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $k$. In particular the structure map is then finite and affine. The empty union is allowed.
theorems.proof: Unramified schemes over a field are disjoint unions of these spectra. Quasi-compactness makes the union finite.
refs: Stacks 02G7 · Lemma (1), schemes unramified over a field
Stacks 024X · finite separable decomposition of the quasi-compact case

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Connected unramified schemes over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and consider the structure map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Assume $X$ nonempty and connected, with unramified structure map.
theorems.statement: It is the spectrum of one finite separable extension of $k$.
theorems.proof: Each component in the field decomposition is a single open-and-closed point.
refs: Stacks 02G7 · Lemma (1), schemes unramified over a field

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Étale and unramified coincide over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and consider the structure map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.
theorems.statement: The map is étale exactly when it is unramified.
theorems.proof: Every member of the disjoint field decomposition is finite étale over the field.
refs: Stacks 02G7 · Lemma (1), schemes unramified over a field

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Full column rank at a point of a zero scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R$, polynomials $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ in $n$ variables and a prime $\mathfrak q$ containing all of them. Let $x$ be the corresponding point of their common zero scheme $Z$. Assume their Jacobian matrix has rank $n$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.
theorems.statement: One has $m\ge n$ and $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is unramified at $x$.
theorems.proof: The Jacobian presents the relative differentials. Full rank makes them vanish near the given point.

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: An invertible square Jacobian at a point
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $R$, polynomials $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ in $n$ variables and a prime $\mathfrak q$ containing all of them. Let $x$ be the corresponding point of their common zero scheme $Z$. Assume their Jacobian matrix has rank $n$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Suppose $m=n$.
theorems.statement: The morphism is flat and étale at $x$.
theorems.proof: Inverting the determinant yields a standard smooth presentation of relative dimension zero.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: The different detects the source ramification locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be a finite extension of number fields with rings of integers $B/A$.
theorems.statement: The different ideal in $B$ is the annihilator of $\Omega_{B/A}$. Its vanishing locus consists of the ramified primes. Its open complement is étale over $\operatorname{Spec}A$.
theorems.proof: At nonzero primes the residue extensions are separable. Flatness follows from torsion-freeness over the Dedekind domain, and vanishing of the differentials detects unramifiedness.
refs: Stacks 024Z · different and ramification in the source

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: The discriminant detects ramification in the base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be a finite extension of number fields with rings of integers $B/A$.
theorems.statement: The norm of the different ideal is the discriminant ideal of the extension. Its vanishing locus is the set of base primes at which at least one prime of $B$ ramifies.
theorems.proof: The support of the norm consists of the base primes below the support of the different.
refs: Stacks 024Z · norm of the different and ramification in the target

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: A finite étale cover from a Galois extension of number fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/K$ be a finite extension of number fields with rings of integers $B/A$. Assume the extension Galois. Remove the zero locus of the different upstairs and that of the discriminant downstairs.
theorems.statement: The resulting map of open schemes is finite, surjective and étale.
theorems.proof: Transitivity of Galois conjugation on primes above a base prime makes the source open exactly the inverse image of the target open. Finite surjectivity survives the restriction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition of geometric morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Take geometric morphisms $g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ and $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$.
theorems.statement: The composite has inverse image $g^{-1}f^{-1}$ and direct image $f_*g_*$.
theorems.proof: Composition of the two adjunctions gives the required adjunction, and the composite of the inverse images preserves finite limits.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presheaf image · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Fix a map of presheaves of sets.
theorems.statement: There is a subpresheaf of the target through which the map factors by an objectwise surjective map.
theorems.proof: On each object the subset is forced to be the image. Naturality makes those subsets stable under restriction.
refs: Stacks 00V9 · existence of the image subpresheaf

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: All sieves on U form a set.
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Fix an object U.
theorems.statement: All sieves on U form a set.
theorems.proof: Each sieve is a subset of the set of arrows into U closed under precomposition. Unions and intersections preserve this closure; the intersection of all containing sieves generates the family.

theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:V\to U$ belong to a sieve $S$ on $U$.
theorems.statement: Then $f^*S=h_V$.
theorems.proof: Closure under precomposition places every arrow to V in the pullback.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A finite intersection of covering sieves on U covers U.
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Give $\mathcal C$ a Grothendieck topology $J$. Fix an object U.
theorems.statement: A finite intersection of covering sieves on U covers U.
theorems.proof: Apply transitivity and pullback stability. The empty intersection is the maximal sieve.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Lattice of topologies · meet
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Fix a set-indexed family of topologies on the same category.
theorems.statement: Objectwise intersection of the given topologies is a topology.
theorems.proof: Each axiom survives intersection. The topology of all sieves is an upper bound. Intersecting all upper bounds yields the least one.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Topology adapted to given presheaves · topology
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Fix a collection $(F_i)$ of presheaves. Declare $S$ over $U$ covering when every pullback $f^*S$ along $f:V\to U$ gives a bijection $F_i(V)\to\operatorname{Hom}(f^*S,F_i)$ for every $i$.
theorems.statement: This assignment of sieves defines a topology.
theorems.proof: The matching-family condition must be imposed universally after pullback. Descent along a covering sieve gives transitivity and taking the identity pullback gives the sheaf condition.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Topology adapted to given presheaves · sheaves

theorems.proof: The matching-family condition must be imposed universally after pullback. Descent along a covering sieve gives transitivity and taking the identity pullback gives the sheaf condition.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sieve plus construction · presheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Give $\mathcal C$ a Grothendieck topology $J$. Fix a presheaf of sets F, write LF for its plus construction over covering sieves, and let the unit take a section to its class on the maximal sieve.
theorems.statement: The assignments to objects and restriction maps define a presheaf LF.
theorems.proof: A representative is a natural transformation on one covering sieve. Pull back the sieve to restrict and pass to common refinements to compare representatives.

theorems.proof: Compare matching families on common covering refinements. Separation gives equality of local matches and the sheaf condition gives unique gluings.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Kan extension index · cospans
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories. For $V$ in $\mathcal D$ put $K=(V\downarrow u)^{\rm op}$. Assume the source category has fibre products and equalizers, both preserved by u.
theorems.statement: Every pair with common source in K completes to a commutative square.
theorems.proof: Use the preserved pullback to complete a span in the opposite comma category and the preserved equalizer to equalize the parallel arrows.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Kan extension index · parallel
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories. For $V$ in $\mathcal D$ put $K=(V\downarrow u)^{\rm op}$. Assume the source category has fibre products and equalizers, both preserved by u.
theorems.statement: Every parallel pair in K becomes equal after postcomposition with some arrow.
theorems.proof: Use the preserved pullback to complete a span in the opposite comma category and the preserved equalizer to equalize the parallel arrows.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered index for presheaf left Kan extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories. For $V$ in $\mathcal D$ put $K=(V\downarrow u)^{\rm op}$. Assume the source has a terminal object and fibre products, and u preserves both.
theorems.statement: The category K is filtered.
theorems.proof: The terminal object supplies an object of K. Products and equalizers in the source give common targets and coequalize parallel arrows in K.
refs: Stacks 00X3 · filteredness of the opposite comma categories

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Unit into a presheaf Kan extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories. Take a presheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C$.
theorems.statement: The identity at $u(U)$ yields a map $F(U)\to(u_pF)(uU)$ natural in $U$.
theorems.proof: Use the component in the colimit corresponding to the identity arrow.
refs: Stacks 00VD · canonical component compatible with restriction

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Left Kan extension and presheaf restriction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories. Take F on the source and G on the target, both presheaves of sets.
theorems.statement: There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(u_pF,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,u^pG)$.
theorems.proof: To give a map out of the colimit is to give the compatible maps indexed by the comma category.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Left Kan extension preserves represented objects
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories. Take $U\in\mathcal C$.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison $u_p h_U\cong h_{u(U)}$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Apply the adjunction followed by Yoneda.
refs: Stacks 04D2 · left Kan extension of a representable

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: combinatorial equivalence on indexed families
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Consider families with the same fixed target.
theorems.statement: The relation of combinatorial equivalence is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
theorems.proof: Identity matchings give reflexivity. Interchange the two directions, and compose the matching functions and their arrows for transitivity.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Tautologically equivalent families give equivalent sheaf tests
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Take two tautologically equivalent families over one target, assuming all pairwise fibre products within each family exist. Fix a presheaf of sets.
theorems.statement: The equalizer sheaf condition holds on one family if and only if it holds on the other.
theorems.proof: Transfer matching sections along the chosen isomorphisms and compare their pullbacks to overlaps.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Refining a family detects separatedness
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Let V refine U over a fixed target and let a presheaf be separated for the family V.
theorems.statement: The presheaf is separated for U.
theorems.proof: Restrict equality on all members of U along the refinement to all members of V.
refs: Stacks 0G1K · separation descends from a refinement

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Transferring the sheaf condition from a refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Let V refine U over a fixed target. Assume pairwise products over the target exist within U, within V and between U and V. A presheaf glues uniquely on V and on each member of U its sections inject into the product of sections on its pullbacks by all members of V.
theorems.statement: The presheaf satisfies the sheaf condition for U.
theorems.proof: Glue the induced matching sections on V and use the stated injections on the members of U to verify that the glued section has the original restrictions.
refs: Stacks 0G1L · descent of the sheaf condition from a refinement

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Compare covering presentations · 1 inclusion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Fix two site presentations on the same category. Every cover of the first is tautologically equivalent to some cover of the second.
theorems.statement: Every sheaf for the second presentation is a sheaf for the first.
theorems.proof: Compare the sheaf conditions on the two covering families and their pullbacks. Apply both inclusions for equality.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Compare covering presentations · 1 equality
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Fix two site presentations on the same category. Every cover of the first is tautologically equivalent to some cover of the second. Impose the same assumption with the presentations interchanged.
theorems.statement: The two full sheaf subcategories in the same presheaf category coincide.
theorems.proof: Compare the sheaf conditions on the two covering families and their pullbacks. Apply both inclusions for equality.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Compare covering presentations · 2 inclusion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Fix two site presentations on the same category. Every cover of the first is refined by some cover of the second.
theorems.statement: Every sheaf for the second presentation is a sheaf for the first.
theorems.proof: Compare the sheaf conditions on the two covering families and their pullbacks. Apply both inclusions for equality.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Compare covering presentations · 2 equality
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Fix two site presentations on the same category. Every cover of the first is refined by some cover of the second. Impose the same assumption with the presentations interchanged.
theorems.statement: The two full sheaf subcategories in the same presheaf category coincide.
theorems.proof: Compare the sheaf conditions on the two covering families and their pullbacks. Apply both inclusions for equality.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Independence of the small set of covering representatives
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. A proper class of covering families satisfies the three site axioms. Take two subsets defining sites, each containing a combinatorially equivalent representative of every original cover.
theorems.statement: The resulting full categories of sheaves in presheaves coincide.
theorems.proof: Both presentations have the same sheaf tests by passage to tautologically equivalent covers.
refs: Stacks 00VY · equality of the sheaf categories

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The topos of the site of group actions
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a group G and the small site of G-sets from Stacks 00W0, with jointly surjective covering families. It is full, contains the regular left action, computes fibre products as G-sets, represents invariant subsets up to isomorphism, and represents jointly surjective families up to combinatorial equivalence.
theorems.statement: Evaluation at the regular action and assignment of the equivariant Hom presheaf to a G-set are quasi-inverse equivalences between its sheaves and all left G-sets.
theorems.proof: Cover each action by maps from the regular orbit. Descent for those maps identifies sections with equivariant functions.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Its limit exists in sheaves.
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a small diagram of sheaves.
theorems.statement: Its limit exists in sheaves.
theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.

theorems.subject: site

theorems.statement: Matching families modulo common refinement form a presheaf F⁺.

theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The association F ↦ (F → F⁺) defines a functor.
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Vary the presheaf of sets F.
theorems.statement: The association F ↦ (F → F⁺) defines a functor.
theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.
refs: Stacks 00W5 · functoriality of the unit arrow

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: There is a third cover refining both.
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take two covers of the same target.
theorems.statement: There is a third cover refining both.
theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The two induced pullbacks from matching families on the target cover to matching families on the source cover are equal.
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take two morphisms of covering families inducing the same map on targets and a presheaf F.
theorems.statement: The two induced pullbacks from matching families on the target cover to matching families on the source cover are equal.
theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.
refs: Stacks 00W7 · independence of the cover map

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: On some covering of U all its restrictions come from original sections of F.
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take any section of F⁺ on U.
theorems.statement: On some covering of U all its restrictions come from original sections of F.
theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.
refs: Stacks 00W9 · local lift of a plus section

theorems.statement: Its plus presheaf is separated.
theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.

theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a separated presheaf F.
theorems.statement: Its plus presheaf is a sheaf.
theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.

theorems.statement: Its colimit exists in sheaves.
theorems.proof: Cover pullbacks and composites supply common refinements. Compute limits from the equalizer sheaf condition and colimits by the sheafification adjunction.
