theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sections of the associated sheaf · rep
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a presheaf of sets F and its associated sheaf aF. Fix a section of aF over U.
theorems.statement: There exist a covering and sections of F on its members representing its restrictions.
theorems.proof: Two applications of the plus construction give the stated local descriptions. Matching images glue uniquely in the associated sheaf.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sections of the associated sheaf · overlap
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a presheaf of sets F and its associated sheaf aF. Fix a section of aF over U and the local representatives from (1).
theorems.statement: On each pairwise overlap their restrictions in F agree after a suitable cover of that overlap.
theorems.proof: Two applications of the plus construction give the stated local descriptions. Matching images glue uniquely in the associated sheaf.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sections of the associated sheaf · exists
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a presheaf of sets F and its associated sheaf aF. Choose a cover and sections of F on its members agreeing locally on every pairwise overlap.
theorems.statement: Their images in aF are restrictions of a section of aF on the target.
theorems.proof: Two applications of the plus construction give the stated local descriptions. Matching images glue uniquely in the associated sheaf.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sections of the associated sheaf · unique
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a presheaf of sets F and its associated sheaf aF. Choose a cover and sections of F on its members agreeing locally on every pairwise overlap.
theorems.statement: At most one section of aF on the target induces those images.
theorems.proof: Two applications of the plus construction give the stated local descriptions. Matching images glue uniquely in the associated sheaf.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Bijections on covering objects suffice after sheafification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a map of presheaves which is bijective on a class of objects such that every object admits a covering by members of that class.
theorems.statement: The induced map on associated sheaves is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Use local representatives of sections and refine overlaps to test equality.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sheaf surjections coequalize their kernel pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a surjective morphism F → G of sheaves of sets.
theorems.statement: G is the coequalizer of the two projections from F ×_G F to F.
theorems.proof: Factor a map equal on the kernel pair by choosing local lifts and descending the resulting sections.
refs: Stacks 086K · coequalizer of the kernel pair

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Yoneda embedding into sheaves on a subcanonical site
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Assume the topology is subcanonical.
theorems.statement: Every representable is a sheaf, and Yoneda realizes the site category as a full subcategory of sheaves.
theorems.proof: Subcanonicity gives the sheaf condition and the Yoneda lemma identifies all Hom sets.
refs: Stacks 00WR · Yoneda is fully faithful into sheaves

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sheafified representables of a cover surject onto its target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a covering family (U_i → U).
theorems.statement: The canonical map from the presheaf coproduct of the h_{U_i} to h_U becomes surjective after sheafification.
theorems.proof: An arrow into U lifts locally to a source of the cover after base-changing the covering family.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presentation by sheafified representables · coequalizer
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a subset E of objects such that every object is covered by objects of E.
theorems.statement: Every sheaf is the coequalizer of a parallel pair F₁ ⇉ F₀.
theorems.proof: Use sections over E to obtain a surjection, and present its kernel pair similarly.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presentation by sheafified representables · terms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a subset E of objects such that every object is covered by objects of E.
theorems.statement: The two objects in this presentation can simultaneously be chosen as coproducts of sheafified representables from E.
theorems.proof: Use sections over E to obtain a surjection, and present its kernel pair similarly.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Colimit presentation by site objects · all
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH.
theorems.statement: Every sheaf is a colimit of a small diagram of sheafified representables induced by a diagram in the site.
theorems.proof: Use the diagram of local sections and refine their comparisons on covering objects.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Colimit presentation by site objects · subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Assume every object has a covering by members of a given subset E.
theorems.statement: For every sheaf such a presenting diagram can be chosen with all its objects in E.
theorems.proof: Use the diagram of local sections and refine their comparisons on covering objects.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: For every sheaf on the target category its precomposition with u is a sheaf on the source.
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites.
theorems.statement: For every sheaf on the target category its precomposition with u is a sheaf on the source.
theorems.proof: Use the sheaf condition on image covers, and the universal properties of left Kan extension and sheafification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sheafified left Kan extension on sheaves is left adjoint to precomposition on sheaves.
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites.
theorems.statement: Sheafified left Kan extension on sheaves is left adjoint to precomposition on sheaves.
theorems.proof: Use the sheaf condition on image covers, and the universal properties of left Kan extension and sheafification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: For every presheaf $G$ on the source, $(u_pG)^\#\cong(u_p(G^\#))^\#$ canonically.
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites.
theorems.statement: For every presheaf $G$ on the source, $(u_pG)^\#\cong(u_p(G^\#))^\#$ canonically.
theorems.proof: Use the sheaf condition on image covers, and the universal properties of left Kan extension and sheafification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: For each source object $U$, one has $u_s(h_U^\#)\cong h_{u(U)}^\#$ canonically.
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites.
theorems.statement: For each source object $U$, one has $u_s(h_U^\#)\cong h_{u(U)}^\#$ canonically.
theorems.proof: Use the sheaf condition on image covers, and the universal properties of left Kan extension and sheafification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition of morphisms of sites · continuous
theorems.hypotheses: Take two composable continuous functors, each defining a morphism of sites.
theorems.statement: Their composite functor is continuous.
theorems.proof: Continuity is stable under composition, and the composite inverse image is a composite of exact left adjoints.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition of morphisms of sites · morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take two composable continuous functors, each defining a morphism of sites.
theorems.statement: The composite functor defines the composite morphism of sites in the opposite direction.
theorems.proof: Continuity is stable under composition, and the composite inverse image is a composite of exact left adjoints.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Criterion for a morphism of sites · comma
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. For every target object V the opposite comma category (V ↓ u)ᵒᵖ is filtered.
theorems.statement: The sheafified left Kan extension is exact, so u defines a morphism from the target site to the source site.
theorems.proof: Filtered colimits of sets commute with finite limits. The finite-limit hypotheses imply filteredness of the comma categories, and sheafification preserves finite limits.
refs: Stacks 00X5 · exactness of the left adjoint and induced site morphism

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Criterion for a morphism of sites · finite-limits
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. The source has a terminal object and fibre products, and u preserves the terminal object and fibre products.
theorems.statement: The sheafified left Kan extension is exact, so u defines a morphism from the target site to the source site.
theorems.proof: Filtered colimits of sets commute with finite limits. The finite-limit hypotheses imply filteredness of the comma categories, and sheafification preserves finite limits.
refs: Stacks 00X6 · exactness of the left adjoint and induced site morphism

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A local image condition for site morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Take a functor u from C to D defining a morphism of sites D → C and an object V of D.
theorems.statement: There exists a cover of V each of whose members admits a map to u(U) for some source object U depending on that member.
theorems.proof: Use exactness of inverse image on the terminal object and the local description of its sheafification.
refs: Stacks 08H2 · cover by objects mapping into image objects

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: From a site morphism to a geometric morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take a morphism of sites D → C induced by u from C to D.
theorems.statement: The adjunction with inverse image the sheafified left extension and direct image precomposition is a geometric morphism Sh(D) → Sh(C).
theorems.proof: The inverse-image left adjoint is left exact by the defining hypothesis.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of a sheafified representable · forward
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a site object U. U is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: Its sheafified representable is quasi-compact in the topos.
theorems.proof: Translate covering families into epimorphisms of sheaves and use local lifts of sections of a coproduct.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of a sheafified representable · back
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a site object U. The sheafified representable of U is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: U is quasi-compact in the site.
theorems.proof: Translate covering families into epimorphisms of sheaves and use local lifts of sections of a coproduct.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness under an epimorphism · site
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let U → V induce an epimorphism of sheafified representables with U quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The site object V is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Pull the covering family back along the epimorphism, take the finite covering subfamily upstairs, then use surjectivity downstairs.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness under an epimorphism · sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let F → G be an epimorphism of sheaves with F quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The sheaf G is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Pull the covering family back along the epimorphism, take the finite covering subfamily upstairs, then use surjectivity downstairs.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of a finite coproduct
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a nonempty finite family of quasi-compact sheaves.
theorems.statement: Its coproduct is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Choose finitely many covering summands over each component and take the finite union of the choices.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered colimits and sections at U · 1
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets, and a site object U. Compare the colimit of sections at U with sections at U of the sheaf colimit. All transition maps are injective.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is injective.
theorems.proof: Represent the local sections at stages and use the stated finiteness or injectivity to compare them at a common stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered colimits and sections at U · 2
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets, and a site object U. Compare the colimit of sections at U with sections at U of the sheaf colimit. Assume U is a quasi-compact site object.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is injective.
theorems.proof: Represent the local sections at stages and use the stated finiteness or injectivity to compare them at a common stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered colimits and sections at U · 3
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets, and a site object U. Compare the colimit of sections at U with sections at U of the sheaf colimit. All transition maps are injective and U is a quasi-compact site object.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is bijective.
theorems.proof: Represent the local sections at stages and use the stated finiteness or injectivity to compare them at a common stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered colimits and sections at U · 4
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets, and a site object U. Compare the colimit of sections at U with sections at U of the sheaf colimit. Assume there is a cofinal system of finite covers of U such that all pairwise fibre products of members over U are quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is bijective.
theorems.proof: Represent the local sections at stages and use the stated finiteness or injectivity to compare them at a common stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered colimits and global sections · 1
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets. Compare the colimit of global sections with global sections of the sheaf colimit. All transition maps are injective.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is injective.
theorems.proof: Represent the local sections at stages and use the stated finiteness or injectivity to compare them at a common stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered colimits and global sections · 2
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets. Compare the colimit of global sections with global sections of the sheaf colimit. Assume the topos is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is injective.
theorems.proof: Represent the local sections at stages and use the stated finiteness or injectivity to compare them at a common stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered colimits and global sections · 3
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets. Compare the colimit of global sections with global sections of the sheaf colimit. All transition maps are injective and the topos is quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is bijective.
theorems.proof: Represent the local sections at stages and use the stated finiteness or injectivity to compare them at a common stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Filtered colimits and global sections · 4
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets. Compare the colimit of global sections with global sections of the sheaf colimit. Assume there is a set S of sheaves such that each epimorphism F → 1 receives a map K → F from a member K of S with K → 1 epic, and K × K is quasi-compact for every K in S.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is bijective.
theorems.proof: Represent the local sections at stages and use the stated finiteness or injectivity to compare them at a common stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Ordinal colimits with sufficiently large cofinality
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a diagram of sheaves of sets indexed by an ordinal of sufficiently large cofinality (relative to the small site).
theorems.statement: For every site object the colimit of its sections agrees with its sections in the sheaf colimit.
theorems.proof: The sizes of the covering families on the small site have a uniform bound. Cofinality large enough for all the families and their pairwise comparisons lets matching sections descend to one stage.
refs: Stacks 0GS0 · uniform comparison for all site objects

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Colimit presentation of a site · category
theorems.hypotheses: Use a small cofiltered diagram of sites, each of whose specified covering families has finite index set. A transition $a:j\to i$ gives a site morphism $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ represented by $u_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$, with strict composition as in 0A34.
theorems.statement: The colimit category of the underlying categories can be equipped with the stated site structure.
theorems.proof: Any finite diagram in the filtered colimit category can be realized at a stage. Finiteness of each covering index ensures the covering axioms descend to one stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Colimit presentation of a site · covers
theorems.hypotheses: Use a small cofiltered diagram of sites, each of whose specified covering families has finite index set. A transition $a:j\to i$ gives a site morphism $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ represented by $u_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$, with strict composition as in 0A34.
theorems.statement: Its coverings are the union of the images of the coverings from the stages.
theorems.proof: Any finite diagram in the filtered colimit category can be realized at a stage. Finiteness of each covering index ensures the covering axioms descend to one stage.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Pullback to the colimit site · morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Use a small cofiltered diagram of sites, each of whose specified covering families has finite index set. A transition $a:j\to i$ gives a site morphism $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ represented by $u_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$, with strict composition as in 0A34.
theorems.statement: Each canonical functor from a stage to the colimit category defines a site morphism from the colimit site back to that stage.
theorems.proof: Present the pullback by the indicated filtered colimit and verify the sheaf axiom using finite covers from the stages.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Pullback to the colimit site · sections
theorems.hypotheses: Use a small cofiltered diagram of sites, each of whose specified covering families has finite index set. A transition $a:j\to i$ gives a site morphism $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ represented by $u_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$, with strict composition as in 0A34.
theorems.statement: For $G$ a sheaf at stage $i$ and $U_i$ an object there, $(f_i^{-1}G)(u_i U_i)=\operatorname{colim}_{a:j\to i}(f_a^{-1}G)(u_a U_i)$ canonically.
theorems.proof: Present the pullback by the indicated filtered colimit and verify the sheaf axiom using finite covers from the stages.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sections of a compatible system of sheaves on a colimit site
theorems.hypotheses: Use a small cofiltered diagram of sites, each of whose specified covering families has finite index set. A transition $a:j\to i$ gives a site morphism $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ represented by $u_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$, with strict composition as in 0A34. Take sheaves $F_j$ at the stages with transition maps $f_a^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ satisfying the composition cocycle. Put $F=\operatorname{colim}_j f_j^{-1}F_j$.
theorems.statement: For $U_i$ at stage $i$, $\operatorname{colim}_{a:j\to i}F_j(u_a U_i)\cong F(u_i U_i)$.
theorems.proof: Apply the single-stage pullback formula and combine the filtered indexing categories.
refs: Stacks 09YN · section formula for a compatible system

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Recovery from the stages of a colimit site
theorems.hypotheses: Use a small cofiltered diagram of sites, each of whose specified covering families has finite index set. A transition $a:j\to i$ gives a site morphism $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ represented by $u_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$, with strict composition as in 0A34. Fix a sheaf F on the colimit site.
theorems.statement: The counits give $\operatorname{colim}_i f_i^{-1} f_{i,*} F\cong F$, with transitions from the adjunctions for the structural site morphisms.
theorems.proof: Apply the compatible-system formula to the pushforwards of F to the stages.
refs: Stacks 0EXJ · recovery of a sheaf from its stage pushforwards

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presheaf right extension · counit
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories.
theorems.statement: Evaluation at the identity on u(U) maps the right-extended sections there to F(U), compatibly with restrictions.
theorems.proof: Use the limit description of the right Kan extension and its universal property.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presheaf right extension · adjoint
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories.
theorems.statement: For presheaves F on C and G on D, maps from the precomposition of G to F are naturally in bijection with maps from G to the right extension of F.
theorems.proof: Use the limit description of the right Kan extension and its universal property.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presheaf functors for an adjoint pair · 1
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories. Let $v:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be right adjoint to $u$.
theorems.statement: $u^p h_V\cong h_{v(V)}$ for every $V$ in $\mathcal D$.
theorems.proof: The unit and counit give universal objects in the comma categories and evaluate the Kan extensions.

theorems.statement: For every $U$ the comma category $(U\downarrow v)$ has an initial object.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Cocontinuous direct image · sheaf condition
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be cocontinuous. Write $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its induced geometric morphism when referring to it.
theorems.statement: Right Kan extension of a sheaf on C is already a sheaf on D.
theorems.proof: Lift refinements of covers of image objects and apply descent in the source sheaf.

theorems.subject: site

theorems.statement: Sheafification after precomposition on sheaves of D is left adjoint to right Kan extension on sheaves of C.
theorems.proof: Precomposition preserves limits and colimits of presheaves. Use left exactness of sheafification and the adjunction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composing cocontinuous functors · cocontinuity
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable cocontinuous functors u and v between covering-family sites.
theorems.statement: Their composite is cocontinuous.
theorems.proof: Refine a cover twice. On inverse images use precomposition and its compatibility with sheafification.

theorems.statement: $g^{-1}G(U)=G(u(U))$ for every sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal D$.
theorems.proof: By continuity restriction is already a sheaf. It has adjoints on both sides.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Connected finite limits of lower shriek · fibre products
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be cocontinuous. Write $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its induced geometric morphism when referring to it. Assume u is also continuous. Assume C has fibre products and equalizers, all preserved by u.

theorems.proof: The comma indices are disjoint unions of filtered categories. Their colimits in sets commute with finite connected limits and sheafification is left exact.

theorems.proof: Fully faithful Kan extension followed by restriction recovers the original values; use the sheafification formulas.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A larger site with a retraction · reverse site morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be cocontinuous. Write $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its induced geometric morphism when referring to it. theorems.statement: There is a morphism of sites $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ represented by $u$.
theorems.proof: Left exactness gives the reverse site morphism, and the units and counits for the fully faithful functor identify the composite.

theorems.proof: The inverse image computed from v is the geometric inverse image from u, hence exact.

theorems.statement: The left adjoint u is cocontinuous.
theorems.proof: Pull an image cover across the continuous right adjoint and the adjunction unit, then apply 00XX and 00XY.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Representability criterion for lower shriek
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be geometric. Suppose every object of $\mathcal D$ is covered by objects of a set $E$, and for each $V\in E$ a sheaf $G_V$ on $\mathcal C$ represents the functor $F\mapsto(f^{-1}F)(V)$ naturally in $F$.
theorems.statement: The inverse-image functor has a left adjoint.
theorems.proof: Present each source sheaf as a colimit of sheafified representables from E, then use the representing objects and colimits.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Extension from a slice · presheaf formula
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$ and the localization $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Let G be a presheaf on C/U.
theorems.statement: $j_{U!}(G^\#)$ is the sheafification of $V\mapsto\coprod_{\phi:V\to U}G(V,\phi)$.
theorems.proof: Left Kan extension sums over the components labelled by arrows into U, then associated sheaf gives the left adjoint.

theorems.statement: For an arrow $X\to U$ one has $j_{U!}(h_{X/U}^\#)\cong h_X^\#$.
theorems.proof: Use the coproduct formula on representables and sheafify.

theorems.subject: site

theorems.statement: The functor carrying $G$ to $j_{U!}G\to h_U^\#$ is an equivalence with $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/h_U^\#$.
theorems.proof: Use the slice description of sections and restriction to recover the original slice sheaf.
refs: Stacks 00Y1 · equivalence with a topos slice

theorems.name: Extending the restriction to a slice · product formula
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$ and the localization $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$.
theorems.statement: For every sheaf $F$, $j_{U!}j_U^{-1}F\cong F\times h_U^\#$.
theorems.proof: Under the slice equivalence inverse image forms the product with the slicing object.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Iterated slice localization · commutative triangle
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$ and the localization $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Take an arrow $f:V\to U$ in $\mathcal C$. Write $j$ for postcomposition $\mathcal C/V\to\mathcal C/U$.
theorems.statement: Forgetting the map to U after postcomposition is forgetting the map to V.
theorems.proof: Composition of structure arrows identifies the two presentations of the slice, and the three adjoint functors compose accordingly.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Relocalization in the slice-topos presentation · (1) inverse image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$ and the localization $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Take an arrow $f:V\to U$ in $\mathcal C$. Write $j$ for postcomposition $\mathcal C/V\to\mathcal C/U$. Identify the two sheaf categories with slices over the corresponding sheafified representables.
theorems.statement: Pull back the object over the sheafified representable of U along the sheafified map represented by f.
theorems.proof: Apply the inverse-image and left-adjoint functors between slices.

theorems.statement: Postcompose the structural map to the sheafified representable of V with the sheafified map to that of U.
theorems.proof: Apply the inverse-image and left-adjoint functors between slices.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Descent for maps on a slice · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a covering family (U_i → U). Fix two sheaves on C. Maps between their restrictions on the slices by U_i agree on all slices by pairwise fibre products.
theorems.statement: The maps glue to a morphism on C/U.
theorems.proof: Use the sheaf condition in the target of the local maps.

theorems.subject: site

theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a covering family (U_i → U). Fix two sheaves on C. Maps between their restrictions on the slices by U_i agree on all slices by pairwise fibre products.
theorems.statement: At most one map on C/U has the prescribed restrictions.
theorems.proof: Use the sheaf condition in the target of the local maps.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Internal Hom adjunction · natural exponential adjunction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix sheaves F, G and H.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{Hom}(F\times G,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(G,H))$ naturally in all three arguments.
theorems.proof: A map on a slice is precisely a family of maps natural under base change into that slice.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Internal Hom from a sheafified representable · internal Hom formula
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$ and the localization $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$.
theorems.statement: $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(h_U^\#,F)\cong j_{U*}j_U^{-1}F$ for every sheaf $F$.
theorems.proof: Use the adjunctions of localization and the product formula for extension of a restriction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Effective descent for sheaves · existence with specified identifications
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a covering family (U_i → U). Fix gluing data on the covering.
theorems.statement: There is a sheaf on C/U with identifications of its restrictions with the given local sheaves.
theorems.proof: Define sections by compatible local sections using the overlap isomorphisms.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Effective descent for sheaves · compatibility with the given isomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a covering family (U_i → U). Fix gluing data on the covering.
theorems.statement: The identifications can simultaneously be chosen to induce exactly the prescribed transition maps on overlaps.
theorems.proof: Define sections by compatible local sections using the overlap isomorphisms.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Descent category on a slice · equivalence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a covering family (U_i → U).
theorems.statement: Restriction of a sheaf on C/U to the covering family, with its canonical transition maps, is an equivalence onto the category of gluing data.
theorems.proof: Maps glue uniquely and all descent data are effective.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Absolute descent data · equivalence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH.
theorems.statement: Sheaves on C are equivalent to families of sheaves on C/U for every object U with compatible pullback isomorphisms for every arrow V → U satisfying the composition cocycle. The equivalence takes restrictions on all slices.
theorems.proof: Recover sections on an object by evaluating its local sheaf at the identity and use transition isomorphisms for restriction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Extension on a subcanonical site · sectionwise coproduct
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$ and the localization $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Assume the topology subcanonical and G a sheaf on C/U.
theorems.statement: $(j_{U!}G)(V)=\coprod_{\phi:V\to U}G(V,\phi)$ with no further associated-sheaf operation required.
theorems.proof: The indexing representable already satisfies descent, so matching summands glue.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Right adjoint of slice restriction · (1) right adjoint
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$ and the localization $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Assume C has binary products.
theorems.statement: The slice forgetful functor has the right adjoint X ↦ (X × U → U).
theorems.proof: Apply the universal property of the product in the relevant slice and the formula for a cocontinuous functor with continuous right adjoint.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Restriction at a subterminal site object · unit isomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. theorems.statement: $F\to j_U^{-1}j_{U!}F$ is invertible.
theorems.proof: The slice forgetful functor is fully faithful under the stated assumption. Apply 00XT.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Square of slice localizations · commuting site functors
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a commutative square with rows $U'\to U$, $V'\to V$ and columns $U'\to V'$, $U\to V$.
theorems.statement: Postcomposition around the square yields a commutative square of continuous and cocontinuous slice functors.
theorems.proof: Postcompose the slice structure maps and use composition of localizations.

theorems.proof: The pullback identifies the two slice categories of factorizations used to compute the two sides.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localizing a site morphism · localized site morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take a site morphism $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ represented by $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Fix $V\in\mathcal D$. Set $U=u(V)$ and let $u'$ apply $u$ to arrows into $V$.
theorems.statement: The induced functor D/V → C/U determines a site morphism f′ in the opposite direction.
theorems.proof: Restriction to the slice is precomposition and the inverse image respects the sheafified representables and pullbacks.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localizing a finite-limit-preserving functor · commuting square of sites
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ have all finite limits and $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ is continuous and preserves finite limits. Fix $V$ and $U=u(V)$.
theorems.statement: The induced site morphism and its slice at V form a commutative square of site morphisms, with horizontal localizations represented by product with U or V.
theorems.proof: Products and all fibre products exist and are preserved, so the explicit continuous right adjoints present the horizontal arrows.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localizing a finite-limit-preserving functor · associated topos square
theorems.hypotheses: Assume $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ have all finite limits and $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ is continuous and preserves finite limits. Fix $V$ and $U=u(V)$.
theorems.statement: The induced topos square is the localization square of 03CF.
theorems.proof: Products and all fibre products exist and are preserved, so the explicit continuous right adjoints present the horizontal arrows.

theorems.hypotheses: Assume $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ have all finite limits and $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ is continuous and preserves finite limits. Fix $V$ and $U=u(V)$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization along a chosen structural arrow · localized square
theorems.hypotheses: Take a site morphism $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ represented by $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Fix $V\in\mathcal D$. Take $c:U\to u(V)$.
theorems.statement: There is a geometric morphism f_c from the U-slice to the V-slice fitting into the localization square over f.
theorems.proof: Compose the site localization of f with the slice pullback associated to the structural arrow.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization along a chosen structural arrow · factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Take a site morphism $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ represented by $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Fix $V\in\mathcal D$. Take $c:U\to u(V)$.
theorems.statement: It factors as localization along c followed by the localization of f at V.
theorems.proof: Compose the site localization of f with the slice pullback associated to the structural arrow.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization along a chosen structural arrow · inverse image formula
theorems.hypotheses: Take a site morphism $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ represented by $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Fix $V\in\mathcal D$. Take $c:U\to u(V)$.
theorems.statement: Pull a structural arrow $H\to h_V^\#$ back by $f^{-1}$ and then take its fibre product with $h_U^\#$ over $h_{u(V)}^\#$ along $c$.
theorems.proof: Compose the site localization of f with the slice pullback associated to the structural arrow.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization along a chosen structural arrow · compatibility for a commuting rectangle
theorems.hypotheses: Take a site morphism $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ represented by $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Fix $V\in\mathcal D$. Take $c:U\to u(V)$.
theorems.statement: For a:U′ → U, b:V′ → V and c′:U′ → u(V′) with c a = u(b)c′, the f_c′ and f_c commute with the intervening localizations.
theorems.proof: Compose the site localization of f with the slice pullback associated to the structural arrow.
refs: Stacks 04IN · compatibility for a commuting rectangle

theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be cocontinuous. Write $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its induced geometric morphism when referring to it. Fix U in C and V = u(U).
theorems.statement: Passing to slices by U and V commutes with forgetting the slice arrows.
theorems.proof: Lift target covering refinements on the sources of the structural slice arrows.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization on the target of a cocontinuous functor · (1) site
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be cocontinuous. Write $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its induced geometric morphism when referring to it. Fix $V$ in $\mathcal D$, put $K=(u\downarrow V)$, and give $K$ coverings detected by $j:K\to\mathcal C$ forgetting the arrow. Write $u':K\to\mathcal D/V$ for $(U,\psi)\mapsto(u(U),\psi)$.
theorems.statement: The induced covering families make K a site.
theorems.proof: Evaluate the Kan extension along the comma categories defining the direct images.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Comparison for a square of site functors · direct-image exchange
theorems.hypotheses: The square $v u'=u v'$ has vertical functors $u':C'\to D',u:C\to D$ and horizontal functors $v':C'\to C,v:D'\to D$. All four are cocontinuous. The two horizontal functors are also continuous. For each $V'\in D'$ the induced $(u'\downarrow V')\to(u\downarrow vV')$ is cofinal in the convention of Stacks 0FN1. Let $f',f,g',g$ be the respective induced geometric morphisms.
theorems.proof: Compute the direct-image exchange on sections using the stipulated square conditions. Pass to the adjoints for the second isomorphism.

theorems.name: Comparison for a square of site functors · direct-image exchange
theorems.hypotheses: Let $v':C'\to C$ and $v:D'\to D$ be both continuous and cocontinuous, inducing $g',g$ by cocontinuity. The continuous $u':D'\to C', u:D\to C$ define site morphisms $f',f$ in the opposite directions. Assume $uv=v'u'$.
theorems.proof: Compute the direct-image exchange on sections using the stipulated square conditions. Pass to the adjoints for the second isomorphism.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Slice of a special cocontinuous functor · commuting site square
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be cocontinuous. Write $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its induced geometric morphism when referring to it. Assume u special cocontinuous and take U in C.
theorems.statement: Applying u to arrows into U commutes with forgetting the arrow in each slice.
theorems.proof: The local fullness, local faithfulness and cover density tests pass to slices.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Slice of a special cocontinuous functor · specialness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be cocontinuous. Write $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its induced geometric morphism when referring to it. Assume u special cocontinuous and take U in C.
theorems.statement: The induced C/U → D/u(U) is special cocontinuous.
theorems.proof: The local fullness, local faithfulness and cover density tests pass to slices.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Slice of a special cocontinuous functor · equivalence on localized topoi
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be cocontinuous. Write $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its induced geometric morphism when referring to it. Assume u special cocontinuous and take U in C.
theorems.statement: The induced geometric localization square commutes and its two vertical arrows are equivalences.
theorems.proof: The local fullness, local faithfulness and cover density tests pass to slices.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presentation by a subcategory of sheaves · (3) specialness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let $\mathcal C'$ be a small full subcategory of its sheaves containing every $h_U^\#$ and closed under fibre products there. Use families with epic coproduct map, choosing a small set of covering representatives. Write $v(U)=h_U^\#$.
theorems.statement: The functor v is special cocontinuous. Let g denote its induced equivalence.
theorems.proof: Use full faithfulness of the presentation and Yoneda after sheafification.

theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. theorems.statement: For $G\in\mathcal C'$ its representable sheaf pulls back under the induced equivalence to $G$.

theorems.name: A subcanonical site adapted to prescribed sheaves · existence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a set of sheaves F_i on C. The following properties are achieved by one new site D and one special cocontinuous functor C → D inducing an equivalence g.
theorems.statement: Such an adapted equivalence exists.
theorems.proof: Enlarge the chosen small full subcategory of sheaves to contain the prescribed objects and be closed under the indicated limits and subobjects, then apply the comparison lemma.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presenting a geometric morphism by a site morphism · (1)
theorems.hypotheses: Given a geometric morphism $f:\operatorname{Sh}(C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(D)$, the following hold for one intermediate site $C'$ and functors $v:C\to C'$, $u:D\to C'$.
theorems.statement: The functor v is special cocontinuous.
theorems.proof: Enlarge the source presentation to contain the inverse images of sheafified representables of the target and apply the site comparison construction.

theorems.statement: The sections of the direct image of G → F over an object U are the right inverses of that arrow after restriction to C/U.
theorems.proof: Compute the right adjoint to product with F by its Hom sets.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site of elements of a sheaf · site structure
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C. Take the category of elements (U,s) with s a section of F at U and the coverings detected by forgetting s.
theorems.statement: The covering families make the category of elements a site.
theorems.proof: Fibres over a section form the corresponding sheaf on the category of elements. Taking their disjoint union recovers the sheaf over F.

theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C. Take the category of elements (U,s) with s a section of F at U and the coverings detected by forgetting s.
theorems.statement: This equivalence carries the induced morphism to the canonical slice projection.
theorems.proof: Fibres over a section form the corresponding sheaf on the category of elements. Taking their disjoint union recovers the sheaf over F.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Represented topos slices · agreement of localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C. Assume $F=h_U^\#$ for a site object $U$.
theorems.statement: The equivalence between sheaves on C/U and sheaves over F identifies the site-localization morphism with the topos-slice morphism.
theorems.proof: Both inverse images correspond to product with the same sheaf over itself.

theorems.name: Localizing twice · canonical localization triangle
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C. Fix a morphism s:G → F.
theorems.statement: The slice topos over G maps to the slice over F, over the common base topos.
theorems.proof: Identify the double slice with the slice over G.

theorems.name: Localizing twice · iterated localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C. Fix a morphism s:G → F.
theorems.statement: The intervening morphism is localization of the F-slice at G → F.
theorems.proof: Identify the double slice with the slice over G.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localizing twice · inverse image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C. Fix a morphism s:G → F.
theorems.statement: Its inverse image pulls a structural arrow to F back along s.
theorems.proof: Identify the double slice with the slice over G.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localizing twice · lower shriek
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C. Fix a morphism s:G → F.
theorems.statement: Its further left adjoint postcomposes a structural arrow to G with s.
theorems.proof: Identify the double slice with the slice over G.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Relocalizing along a site arrow · identification of triangles
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let V → U be a site arrow and take the induced morphism of sheafified representables.
theorems.statement: The triangle of slices over those sheaves identifies with the triangle of localizations of the presenting site at V and U.
theorems.proof: The functors over the represented slices have the same pullback formulas.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A geometric morphism on slices · commutative localization square
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a geometric morphism $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ of Grothendieck topoi and an object $G$ of $\mathcal D$. Let $F=f^{-1}G$.
theorems.statement: There is a morphism f′ from the F-slice to the G-slice fitting into a commuting square with f and the two projections.
theorems.proof: The left exact inverse image acts on structural arrows and their pullbacks.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A geometric morphism on slices · characterizing inverse image
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a geometric morphism $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ of Grothendieck topoi and an object $G$ of $\mathcal D$. Let $F=f^{-1}G$.
theorems.statement: It is characterized by taking the inverse image under f of the whole structural arrow.
theorems.proof: The left exact inverse image acts on structural arrows and their pullbacks.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A geometric morphism on slices · direct image after restriction
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a geometric morphism $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ of Grothendieck topoi and an object $G$ of $\mathcal D$. Let $F=f^{-1}G$.
theorems.proof: The left exact inverse image acts on structural arrows and their pullbacks.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site and topos localization of a morphism · identification of squares
theorems.hypotheses: Take a site morphism $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ represented by $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Fix $V\in\mathcal D$. Take $U=u(V)$.
theorems.statement: The site-localized square of 03CF is the sheafified-representable case of the geometric localization square of 04H1.
theorems.proof: Inverse image identifies the sheafified representable of V with the one for u(V).

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization along an arbitrary arrow into an inverse image · commuting square
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a geometric morphism $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ of Grothendieck topoi and an object $G$ of $\mathcal D$. Fix $s:F\to f^{-1}G$ in $\mathcal E$.
theorems.statement: There is a morphism f_s from the F-slice to the G-slice over f.
theorems.proof: Compose the canonical slice morphism with pullback along s. This places the target of f′ over G, as required by the diagram.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization along an arbitrary arrow into an inverse image · factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a geometric morphism $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ of Grothendieck topoi and an object $G$ of $\mathcal D$. Fix $s:F\to f^{-1}G$ in $\mathcal E$.
theorems.statement: It factors as localization along s followed by the canonical map from the slice over the inverse image of G to the slice over G.
theorems.proof: Compose the canonical slice morphism with pullback along s. This places the target of f′ over G, as required by the diagram.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization along an arbitrary arrow into an inverse image · inverse image formula
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a geometric morphism $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ of Grothendieck topoi and an object $G$ of $\mathcal D$. Fix $s:F\to f^{-1}G$ in $\mathcal E$.
theorems.statement: For $H\to G$, its inverse image is $f^{-1}H\times_{f^{-1}G}F\to F$.
theorems.proof: Compose the canonical slice morphism with pullback along s. This places the target of f′ over G, as required by the diagram.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization along an arbitrary arrow into an inverse image · naturality
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a geometric morphism $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ of Grothendieck topoi and an object $G$ of $\mathcal D$. Fix $s:F\to f^{-1}G$ in $\mathcal E$.
theorems.statement: For a:F′ → F, b:G′ → G and s′:F′ → f⁻¹G′ satisfying s a = (f⁻¹b)s′, the f_s′ and f_s commute with the relative localization morphisms.
theorems.proof: Compose the canonical slice morphism with pullback along s. This places the target of f′ over G, as required by the diagram.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site presentation of a topos localization along an arrow · identification of localized diagrams
theorems.hypotheses: Take a site morphism $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ represented by $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Fix $V\in\mathcal D$. Take $c:U\to u(V)$ and use $F=h_U^\#$, $G=h_V^\#$ and $f^{-1}G=h_{u(V)}^\#$. Use the arrow $F\to f^{-1}G$ induced by $c$.
theorems.statement: The site square of 04IN and the topos square of 04IV agree under the slice equivalences. The structural arrow to the inverse image is used even when it is not an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Apply the slice formulas to sheafified representables. In general the inverse image represents u(V), so identifying it with the sheafified representable of U without using c would be unjustified.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Stalk of a representable · natural identification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets.
theorems.statement: $(h_U)_p\cong u(U)$ naturally in $U$.
theorems.proof: Use representatives in the category of elements and evaluation.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Presheaf stalk adjunction · right adjoint on sets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets.
theorems.statement: The right adjoint of the stalk on presheaves sends $E$ to $U\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(u(U),E)$.
theorems.proof: Maps out of the colimit of sections are exactly the compatible functions represented by the stated presheaf.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Stalks under the covering tests · (1) sheaf condition
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Suppose the images of each cover jointly surject and, for each pair of its members, the comparison from the value on their fibre product to the fibre product of their values is surjective.
theorems.statement: For all sets E the presheaf U ↦ Map(u(U),E) is a sheaf.
theorems.proof: The two surjectivity conditions turn matching maps into an ordinary function on the value of the target. Apply the presheaf adjunction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Stalks under the covering tests · (2) adjunction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Suppose the images of each cover jointly surject and, for each pair of its members, the comparison from the value on their fibre product to the fibre product of their values is surjective.
theorems.statement: This functor on sets is right adjoint to the stalk on sheaves.
theorems.proof: The two surjectivity conditions turn matching maps into an ordinary function on the value of the target. Apply the presheaf adjunction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Stalks under the covering tests · (3) sheafification invariance
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Suppose the images of each cover jointly surject and, for each pair of its members, the comparison from the value on their fibre product to the fibre product of their values is surjective.
theorems.statement: The unit to sheafification induces a bijection on the stalk of every presheaf.
theorems.proof: The two surjectivity conditions turn matching maps into an ordinary function on the value of the target. Apply the presheaf adjunction.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site points and geometric points · (1) site point to topos point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH.
theorems.statement: For each site point, its stalk and skyscraper functors form a geometric point of the sheaf topos.
theorems.proof: The inverse image preserves finite limits and colimits, and sheafified representables generate the sheaf topos.
refs: Stacks 00YA · (1) site point to topos point

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site points and geometric points · (2) underlying site point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH.
theorems.statement: For each topos point $p$, $U\mapsto p^{-1}(h_U^\#)$ defines a site point.
theorems.proof: The inverse image preserves finite limits and colimits, and sheafified representables generate the sheaf topos.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site points and geometric points · (2) recovery of the geometric point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH.
theorems.statement: The geometric point associated to that site point recovers p up to canonical isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The inverse image preserves finite limits and colimits, and sheafified representables generate the sheaf topos.
refs: Stacks 00YA · (2) recovery of the geometric point

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A bounded site presenting the point · (1) point topos
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Assume u represents a point and every u(U) is a subset of a fixed infinite set S. Use the site of subsets of S with all functions and jointly surjective coverings, choosing bounded representatives as in the source.
theorems.statement: The sheaf category on this powerset site is equivalent to sets.
theorems.proof: Represent the required sets and their fibre products inside the powerset site, and identify evaluation at a singleton with the inverse equivalence.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A bounded site presenting the point · (2) site morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Assume u represents a point and every u(U) is a subset of a fixed infinite set S. Use the site of subsets of S with all functions and jointly surjective coverings, choosing bounded representatives as in the source.
theorems.statement: The functor u into the powerset site induces a site morphism from it to C.
theorems.proof: Represent the required sets and their fibre products inside the powerset site, and identify evaluation at a singleton with the inverse equivalence.

theorems.statement: The equivalence from sets followed by the induced geometric morphism is the original point.
theorems.proof: Represent the required sets and their fibre products inside the powerset site, and identify evaluation at a singleton with the inverse equivalence.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Stalk of its own skyscraper · canonical section
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ be a geometric point of a Grothendieck topos. Fix a set E.
theorems.statement: There is a natural map $E\to p^{-1}p_*E$.
theorems.proof: Use the maps determined by constant values and evaluate at the point.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Stalk of its own skyscraper · counit is a split surjection
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ be a geometric point of a Grothendieck topos. Fix a set E.
theorems.statement: Its composite with the adjunction counit $p^{-1}p_*E\to E$ is the identity.
theorems.proof: Use the maps determined by constant values and evaluate at the point.
refs: Stacks 05UX · counit is a split surjection

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Direct image of a point · all small limits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ be a geometric point of a Grothendieck topos. Consider the point direct image on sets.
theorems.statement: It preserves all small limits.
theorems.proof: The direct image is a right adjoint. Surjections of sets split in ZFC, and the naturally split counit of 05UX gives the reflection and faithfulness assertions.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Direct image of a point · left exactness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ be a geometric point of a Grothendieck topos. Consider the point direct image on sets.
theorems.statement: It preserves finite limits.
theorems.proof: The direct image is a right adjoint. Surjections of sets split in ZFC, and the naturally split counit of 05UX gives the reflection and faithfulness assertions.

theorems.name: Direct image of a point · faithfulness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ be a geometric point of a Grothendieck topos. Consider the point direct image on sets.

theorems.proof: The direct image is a right adjoint. Surjections of sets split in ZFC, and the naturally split counit of 05UX gives the reflection and faithfulness assertions.

theorems.name: Direct image of a point · preservation of surjections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ be a geometric point of a Grothendieck topos. Consider the point direct image on sets.
theorems.statement: It takes surjections of sets to epimorphisms of sheaves.
theorems.proof: The direct image is a right adjoint. Surjections of sets split in ZFC, and the naturally split counit of 05UX gives the reflection and faithfulness assertions.

theorems.name: Direct image of a point · reflection of injections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ be a geometric point of a Grothendieck topos. Consider the point direct image on sets.
theorems.statement: If the direct image of a function is monic, that function is injective.
theorems.proof: The direct image is a right adjoint. Surjections of sets split in ZFC, and the naturally split counit of 05UX gives the reflection and faithfulness assertions.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Direct image of a point · reflection of isomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ be a geometric point of a Grothendieck topos. Consider the point direct image on sets.
theorems.statement: If the direct image of a function is invertible, the function is bijective.
theorems.proof: The direct image is a right adjoint. Surjections of sets split in ZFC, and the naturally split counit of 05UX gives the reflection and faithfulness assertions.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Cofiltered neighbourhoods imply left exact stalks · left exactness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Suppose the category of pairs (U,x) with x in u(U) is cofiltered.
theorems.statement: The stalk on presheaves of sets preserves finite limits.
theorems.proof: It is a filtered colimit of evaluation functors into sets.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: From finite limits to cofiltered neighbourhoods · cofiltered neighbourhoods
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Assume the category has a terminal object and fibre products, u sends its terminal object to a singleton and preserves all fibre products.
theorems.statement: The category of neighbourhoods (U,x) is cofiltered.
theorems.proof: A preserved terminal object supplies a neighbourhood, and preserved finite limits provide cone and equalizer neighbourhoods.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: From finite limits to cofiltered neighbourhoods · finite-limit preservation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Assume the category has a terminal object and fibre products, u sends its terminal object to a singleton and preserves all fibre products.
theorems.statement: The stalk on sheaves preserves finite limits.
theorems.proof: A preserved terminal object supplies a neighbourhood, and preserved finite limits provide cone and equalizer neighbourhoods.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Point criterion on a finitely complete site · site point implies preservation of finite limits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Assume the site category has finite limits.
theorems.statement: Every site point preserves finite limits as a covariant functor to sets.
theorems.proof: A site point is the composite of Yoneda, sheafification and its stalk on sheaves. Conversely finite-limit preservation gives cofiltered neighbourhoods and the required pullback comparisons.
refs: Stacks 00YC · site point implies preservation of finite limits

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Point criterion on a finitely complete site · site point implies covering surjectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Assume the site category has finite limits.
theorems.statement: Every site point sends coverings to jointly surjective families.
theorems.proof: A site point is the composite of Yoneda, sheafification and its stalk on sheaves. Conversely finite-limit preservation gives cofiltered neighbourhoods and the required pullback comparisons.
refs: Stacks 00YC · site point implies covering surjectivity

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Point criterion on a finitely complete site · finite-limit preservation and covering surjectivity imply site point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let u be a covariant functor from the site category to sets. Assume the site category has finite limits.
theorems.statement: A functor preserving finite limits and sending covers to jointly surjective families defines a point.
theorems.proof: A site point is the composite of Yoneda, sheafification and its stalk on sheaves. Conversely finite-limit preservation gives cofiltered neighbourhoods and the required pullback comparisons.
refs: Stacks 00YC · finite-limit preservation and covering surjectivity imply site point

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Stalks and left Kan extension · canonical identification
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories. Take $v:\mathcal D\to\mathbf{Set}$ and put $w=vu$.
theorems.statement: $(u_pF)_v\cong F_w$ functorially for every presheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C$.
theorems.proof: Compare their right adjoints on sets or compose the index categories in the colimit.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition of a point and a morphism · point of the target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:D\to C$ be a site morphism represented by $u:C\to D$ and let $q$ be a site point of $D$ represented by $v$.
theorems.statement: The composite v u gives a site point p of C.
theorems.proof: Compose inverse-image functors. In the site presentation use invariance of stalks under sheafification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition of a point and a morphism · inverse image and stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:D\to C$ be a site morphism represented by $u:C\to D$ and let $q$ be a site point of $D$ represented by $v$.
theorems.statement: $(f^{-1}F)_q\cong F_p$ canonically for each sheaf $F$ on the target.
theorems.proof: Compose inverse-image functors. In the site presentation use invariance of stalks under sheafification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition of a point and a morphism · point of the target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a geometric morphism and $q$ a point of its source.
theorems.statement: The composite geometric morphism f q is a point p of its target.
theorems.proof: Compose inverse-image functors. In the site presentation use invariance of stalks under sheafification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Composition of a point and a morphism · inverse image and stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f$ be a geometric morphism and $q$ a point of its source.
theorems.statement: $(f^{-1}F)_q\cong F_p$ canonically for each sheaf $F$ on the target.
theorems.proof: Compose inverse-image functors. In the site presentation use invariance of stalks under sheafification.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localizing a point · point of the slice
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a site point represented by u and a site object U. Fix an element $x\in u(U)$.
theorems.statement: The functor assigning to $V\to U$ the fibre of $u(V)\to u(U)$ over $x$ is a site point $q_x$.
theorems.proof: Pull back the element along the category of neighbourhoods in the slice.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localizing a point · commutative triangle
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a site point represented by u and a site object U. Fix an element $x\in u(U)$.
theorems.statement: The associated geometric point composes with localization to the given point.
theorems.proof: Pull back the element along the category of neighbourhoods in the slice.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localizing a point · stalk comparison
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a site point represented by u and a site object U. Fix an element $x\in u(U)$.
theorems.statement: For each sheaf on C its stalk at p is the stalk of its restriction at q_x.
theorems.proof: Pull back the element along the category of neighbourhoods in the slice.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Points over a point · classification of lifts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a site point represented by u and a site object U.
theorems.statement: Points in the slice over the specified point, with their identification over it, correspond bijectively up to that identification to elements of u(U).
theorems.proof: The lift picks its element from the identity object in the slice. The fibre functor of 04H2 recovers it.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Stalk of extension from a slice · sum over lifts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a site point represented by u and a site object U. Take a sheaf G on the slice.
theorems.statement: $(j_{U!}G)_p\cong\coprod_{x\in u(U)}G_{q_x}$.
theorems.proof: Decompose the colimit computing the stalk according to the image element of u(U).

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Naturality of stalks for transformations of site functors · transformation of stalks
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a natural transformation $t:u'\to u$ of covariant functors to sets.
theorems.statement: There is a natural map $F_{u'}\to F_u$ on presheaves.
theorems.proof: Apply the map on categories of elements and its comparison of colimits.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Naturality of stalks for transformations of site functors · agreement on representables
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a natural transformation $t:u'\to u$ of covariant functors to sets.
theorems.statement: Under the Yoneda identifications its components on representables are the components of t.
theorems.proof: Apply the map on categories of elements and its comparison of colimits.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Criterion for a conservative family · conservativity implies separation of sections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a family of points represented by u_i.
theorems.statement: For every pair of distinct sections $s,t$ of any sheaf on any object $U$, some index $i$ and some $x\in u_i(U)$ give distinct germs represented by $(U,x,s)$ and $(U,x,t)$. This condition follows if the family is conservative.
theorems.proof: Detect equality of arrows from represented sheaves. Use this to test the diagonal and the codiagonal of a sheaf map.
refs: Stacks 00YM · conservativity implies separation of sections

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Criterion for a conservative family · separation of sections implies conservativity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a family of points represented by u_i.
theorems.statement: If the following test holds then the family is conservative. For every pair of distinct sections $s,t$ of any sheaf on any object $U$, some index $i$ and some $x\in u_i(U)$ give distinct germs represented by $(U,x,s)$ and $(U,x,t)$.
theorems.proof: Detect equality of arrows from represented sheaves. Use this to test the diagonal and the codiagonal of a sheaf map.
refs: Stacks 00YM · separation of sections implies conservativity

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Conservative points in a slice · conservative lifted family
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a site object U.
theorems.statement: For a conservative family (p_i,u_i), all the lifts indexed by i and x in u_i(U) form a conservative family on C/U.
theorems.proof: Test germs at the lifted points, or use extension from the slice and the coproduct formula on stalks.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Conservative points in a slice · enough points localize
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a site object U.
theorems.statement: If C has enough points then C/U has enough points.
theorems.proof: Test germs at the lifted points, or use extension from the slice and the coproduct formula on stalks.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Enough points from localizations · enough points globally
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take site objects U_i whose sheafified representables have coproduct surjecting onto the terminal sheaf. Assume C/U_i has enough points for every i.
theorems.statement: The site C has enough points.
theorems.proof: Compose conservative families on the slices with their projections. The jointly epimorphic family ensures that slice restrictions jointly detect isomorphisms.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Testing exactness of a site functor at points · site morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Take a conservative family of points on D such that each representing covariant functor composed with u defines a point on C.
theorems.statement: The functor u defines a site morphism D → C.
theorems.proof: The stalks of the proposed inverse image commute with finite limits since the composites are points. Conservativity reflects this exactness.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Refinement preserving distinguished germs · preservation of distinction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix an inverse system (V_j) over a directed poset J. Its functor u′ is the colimit of Hom(V_j,−), and its stalk on F is the colimit of F(V_j). Fix distinct elements in this stalk for one sheaf F. A refinement extends J as an induced ordered subsystem and agrees with all the original objects and arrows. Fix a finite cover (W_k → W) and an element in u′(W).
theorems.statement: There exists one refinement still separating the two chosen germs and satisfying the lifting conclusion of this result.
theorems.proof: At a finite cover at least one choice can preserve the distinguished inequality. For simultaneous lifting well-order the requirements and take unions at limit stages.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Refinement preserving distinguished germs · finite-cover lifting in the same refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix an inverse system (V_j) over a directed poset J. Its functor u′ is the colimit of Hom(V_j,−), and its stalk on F is the colimit of F(V_j). Fix distinct elements in this stalk for one sheaf F. A refinement extends J as an induced ordered subsystem and agrees with all the original objects and arrows. Fix a finite cover (W_k → W) and an element in u′(W).
theorems.statement: The chosen element maps into the image of u(W_k) for some k.
theorems.proof: At a finite cover at least one choice can preserve the distinguished inequality. For simultaneous lifting well-order the requirements and take unions at limit stages.
refs: Stacks 00YO · finite-cover lifting in the same refinement
