theorems.name: Refinement preserving distinguished germs · preservation of distinction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix an inverse system (V_j) over a directed poset J. Its functor u′ is the colimit of Hom(V_j,−), and its stalk on F is the colimit of F(V_j). Fix distinct elements in this stalk for one sheaf F. A refinement extends J as an induced ordered subsystem and agrees with all the original objects and arrows.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Refinement preserving distinguished germs · finite-cover lifting in the same refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix an inverse system (V_j) over a directed poset J. Its functor u′ is the colimit of Hom(V_j,−), and its stalk on F is the colimit of F(V_j). Fix distinct elements in this stalk for one sheaf F. A refinement extends J as an induced ordered subsystem and agrees with all the original objects and arrows.
theorems.statement: Simultaneously for every finite cover (W_k → W) and every original element of u′(W), its image comes from u(W_k) for some k.
theorems.proof: At a finite cover at least one choice can preserve the distinguished inequality. For simultaneous lifting well-order the requirements and take unions at limit stages.
refs: Stacks 00YP · finite-cover lifting in the same refinement

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Deligne’s sufficient condition for enough points · existence of a conservative family
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Suppose the site category has finite limits and every covering admits a refinement that is a finite covering.
theorems.statement: The site has enough points.
theorems.proof: Construct points separating each chosen pair of distinct local sections by iterating the finite-cover refinement procedure.
refs: P. Deligne, SGA 4, Exposé VI, Appendice, Proposition 9.0 (locally coherent topoi have enough points)
Stacks 00YQ · existence of a conservative family

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Enough points from finite-covering slices · existence of enough points
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Suppose the coproduct of sheafified representables of U_i surjects onto the terminal sheaf and each slice C/U_i has finite limits and every covering there admits a finite covering refinement.
theorems.statement: The site has enough points.
theorems.proof: Apply 00YQ in each slice and then use 06UL.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site criterion for preserving surjections · preservation of surjections
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a site morphism $D\to C$ represented by $u:C\to D$. For each $U$ in $C$ and each cover $(V_j\to u(U))$ suppose there is a cover $(U_i\to U)$ such that the map $\coprod h_{u(U_i)}^\#\to h_{u(U)}^\#$ factors through $\coprod h_{V_j}^\#\to h_{u(U)}^\#$.
theorems.statement: The direct image takes sheaf surjections to sheaf surjections.
theorems.proof: Choose local lifts on the target covering and use the sheaf-level factorization to obtain lifts on the source cover.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site criterion for reflecting injections and surjections · reflection of injections
theorems.hypotheses: Let a site morphism D → C be represented by u:C → D. Every object V of D admits a covering family of the form u(U_i) → V.
theorems.statement: A morphism is injective if its direct image is injective.
theorems.proof: The stated image objects cover the target, so the sectionwise and local tests can be performed there.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Site criterion for reflecting injections and surjections · reflection of surjections
theorems.hypotheses: Let a site morphism D → C be represented by u:C → D. Every object V of D admits a covering family of the form u(U_i) → V.
theorems.statement: A morphism is surjective if its direct image is surjective.
theorems.proof: The stated image objects cover the target, so the sectionwise and local tests can be performed there.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Pullback of emptiness · final assertion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Let U be sheaf-theoretically empty and take an arrow V → U.
theorems.statement: V is sheaf-theoretically empty.
theorems.proof: The empty covering is stable under base change.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sheafification under almost cocontinuity · natural comparison
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Assume u is almost cocontinuous. Fix a target presheaf G having singleton value on every sheaf-theoretically empty target object.
theorems.proof: The singleton condition controls the empty objects in the local lifting comparison.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Connected colimits under almost cocontinuity · pushouts
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Assume u is almost cocontinuous.
theorems.statement: Precomposition on sheaves preserves pushouts.
theorems.proof: The corresponding presheaf colimits have singleton values on empty objects when the diagram is connected and nonempty. Apply 04B8.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Connected colimits under almost cocontinuity · coequalizers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Assume u is almost cocontinuous.
theorems.statement: Precomposition on sheaves preserves coequalizers.
theorems.proof: The corresponding presheaf colimits have singleton values on empty objects when the diagram is connected and nonempty. Apply 04B8.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Connected colimits under almost cocontinuity · finite connected colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Assume u is almost cocontinuous.
theorems.statement: Precomposition on sheaves preserves finite connected colimits.
theorems.proof: The corresponding presheaf colimits have singleton values on empty objects when the diagram is connected and nonempty. Apply 04B8.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Connected colimits under almost cocontinuity · pushouts
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Assume u is almost cocontinuous. Assume u defines a morphism of sites in the opposite direction.
theorems.statement: Its geometric direct image preserves pushouts.
theorems.proof: The corresponding presheaf colimits have singleton values on empty objects when the diagram is connected and nonempty. Apply 04B8.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Connected colimits under almost cocontinuity · coequalizers
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Assume u is almost cocontinuous. Assume u defines a morphism of sites in the opposite direction.
theorems.statement: Its geometric direct image preserves coequalizers.
theorems.proof: The corresponding presheaf colimits have singleton values on empty objects when the diagram is connected and nonempty. Apply 04B8.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Connected colimits under almost cocontinuity · finite connected colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Assume u is almost cocontinuous. Assume u defines a morphism of sites in the opposite direction.
theorems.statement: Its geometric direct image preserves finite connected colimits.
theorems.proof: The corresponding presheaf colimits have singleton values on empty objects when the diagram is connected and nonempty. Apply 04B8.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Embedding criterion for a slice projection · (1) implies (2)
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C.
theorems.statement: If F is subterminal then the canonical slice projection is an embedding.
theorems.proof: Examine the counit for the canonical localization and its diagonal.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Embedding criterion for a slice projection · (2) implies (1)
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C.
theorems.statement: If the canonical slice projection presents its slice as a subtopos, F is subterminal.
theorems.proof: Examine the counit for the canonical localization and its diagonal.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Complementary closed subtopos · subtopos property
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Fix a sheaf F on C. Suppose F is a subobject of the terminal sheaf.
theorems.statement: The full subcategory of G for which F × G → F is invertible is a subtopos.
theorems.proof: Restriction over the open represented by F must be terminal. The inclusion of objects with this property has a left exact reflector.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Inverse image for presheaves of structures · adjunction for presheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Take a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between covering-family sites. Assume C has a terminal object and fibre products, with u preserving both. Fix a type of algebraic structure as in Stacks 007M.
theorems.statement: The inverse image and direct image extend to an adjunction on presheaves of those structures.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Computing global sections by a coequalizer presentation · equalizer formula
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site presented by covering families in the sense of Stacks 00VH. Take a sheaf $F$ and arrows $a,b:V\to U$ whose sheafified representables have coequalizer the terminal sheaf.
theorems.statement: $\Gamma(\mathcal C,F)$ identifies with the equalizer of $a^*,b^*:F(U)\rightrightarrows F(V)$.
theorems.proof: Apply Hom into F in the sheaf category and use sheafified Yoneda.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Existence of relative PD envelopes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided power (PD) ring, $B$ an $A$-algebra, and $J$ an ideal of $B$ containing $IB$.
theorems.statement: There exists a PD ring $D$ over $A$ with a morphism of pairs from $(B,J)$.
theorems.proof: Adjoin divided power variables for elements of the ideal, then quotient by the PD relations imposed by the map of pairs.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: PD envelope adjunction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided power (PD) ring, $B$ an $A$-algebra, and $J$ an ideal of $B$ containing $IB$.
theorems.statement: For every PD algebra $(E,K)$ over $A$, PD maps from $D$ to $E$ correspond naturally to $A$-maps $B\to E$ carrying $J$ into $K$.
theorems.proof: Adjoin divided power variables for elements of the ideal, then quotient by the PD relations imposed by the map of pairs.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: PD envelope of a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided power (PD) ring, $B$ an $A$-algebra, and $J$ an ideal of $B$ containing $IB$. Let $B^\prime\to B$ be a surjective $A$-algebra map with kernel $K$ and let $J^\prime$ be the inverse image of $J$.
theorems.statement: The envelope for $(B,J)$ is the envelope for $(B^\prime,J^\prime)$ modulo the ideal generated by the divided powers of positive order of the images of all elements of $K$. The PD ideal and its operations descend.
theorems.proof: Test the quotient against arbitrary PD targets. Vanishing on $K$ forces vanishing on all its divided powers.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Generators for a relative PD envelope
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(B,I,\gamma)$ be a PD ring and $J=I+(f_t)$. Form its relative envelope $D$ and the free PD polynomial algebra over $B$ on $x_t$.
theorems.statement: Sending $x_t$ to $f_t$ induces a surjection from the PD polynomial algebra to $D$.
theorems.proof: The generators impose the underlying substitutions, and closure under divided powers imposes the additional relations.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Relations for a relative PD envelope
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(B,I,\gamma)$ be a PD ring and $J=I+(f_t)$. Form its relative envelope $D$ and the free PD polynomial algebra over $B$ on $x_t$.
theorems.statement: The kernel is generated by the $x_t-f_t$ and the positive divided powers of $\sum r_tx_t-r_0$ for finite relations $\sum r_tf_t=r_0\in I$.
theorems.proof: The generators impose the underlying substitutions, and closure under divided powers imposes the additional relations.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Adjoining variables to a PD envelope
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided power (PD) ring, $B$ an $A$-algebra, and $J$ an ideal of $B$ containing $IB$. Adjoin arbitrary polynomial variables $x_i$ to $B$ and enlarge the ideal by all these variables.
theorems.statement: The enlarged envelope is the divided power polynomial algebra on the $x_i$ over the original envelope.
theorems.proof: Both algebras represent a lift of the original pair together with chosen elements of the target PD ideal.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Base change of PD envelopes over a fixed PD base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided power (PD) ring, $B$ an $A$-algebra, and $J$ an ideal of $B$ containing $IB$. Let $B\to B^\prime$ induce a flat map modulo $I$ and assume $\operatorname{Tor}_1^B(B^\prime,B/IB)=0$.
theorems.statement: The extension to $B^\prime$ of the envelope for $J$ is the relative envelope for $JB^\prime$ over the same PD base.
theorems.proof: Apply the relative envelope presentation. The stated hypotheses control the relations after base change.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Base change of PD envelopes along a map of PD bases
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(B,I,\gamma)\to(B^\prime,I^\prime,\gamma^\prime)$ be a PD map, $I\subset J$, with $B/I\to B^\prime/I^\prime$ flat and $J^\prime=JB^\prime+I^\prime$.
theorems.statement: The natural map from $D_{B,\gamma}(J)\otimes_BB^\prime$ to $D_{B^\prime,\gamma^\prime}(J^\prime)$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Apply the relative envelope presentation. The stated hypotheses control the relations after base change.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: PD structure on a square-zero extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a PD ring and $M$ an $A$-module. Give $B=A\oplus M$ the square-zero multiplication and put $J=I\oplus M$.
theorems.statement: For $(x,z)\in J$, set $\delta_n=(\gamma_n(x),\gamma_{n-1}(x)z)$ for $n\ge1$. These operations define divided powers on $J$.
theorems.proof: Expanding the PD identities in the displayed graded multiplication gives the asserted structure and its restriction to the base.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Compatibility of the square-zero extension with the base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a PD ring and $M$ an $A$-module. Give $B=A\oplus M$ the square-zero multiplication and put $J=I\oplus M$.
theorems.statement: For $(x,z)\in J$, set $\delta_n=(\gamma_n(x),\gamma_{n-1}(x)z)$ for $n\ge1$. The inclusion of $A$ into this extension preserves the given divided powers.
theorems.proof: Expanding the PD identities in the displayed graded multiplication gives the asserted structure and its restriction to the base.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: PD structure on a second-order extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a PD ring, $M,N$ modules and $q:M\times M\to N$ bilinear. In $B=A\oplus M\oplus N$ use $zz^\prime=q(z,z^\prime)+q(z^\prime,z)$ and annihilate $N$ by $M\oplus N$. Put $J=I\oplus M\oplus N$.
theorems.statement: Set $\delta_n(x,z,w)=(\gamma_n(x),\gamma_{n-1}(x)z,\gamma_{n-1}(x)w+\gamma_{n-2}(x)q(z,z))$ for $n\ge1$, interpreting negative-index terms as zero. These operations define divided powers on $J$.
theorems.proof: Expanding the PD identities in the displayed graded multiplication gives the asserted structure and its restriction to the base.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Compatibility of the second-order extension with the base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a PD ring, $M,N$ modules and $q:M\times M\to N$ bilinear. In $B=A\oplus M\oplus N$ use $zz^\prime=q(z,z^\prime)+q(z^\prime,z)$ and annihilate $N$ by $M\oplus N$. Put $J=I\oplus M\oplus N$.
theorems.statement: Set $\delta_n(x,z,w)=(\gamma_n(x),\gamma_{n-1}(x)z,\gamma_{n-1}(x)w+\gamma_{n-2}(x)q(z,z))$ for $n\ge1$, interpreting negative-index terms as zero. The inclusion of $A$ into this extension preserves the given divided powers.
theorems.proof: Expanding the PD identities in the displayed graded multiplication gives the asserted structure and its restriction to the base.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Finite products of big affine thickening rings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$.
theorems.statement: The big affine category has finite products.
theorems.proof: Finite products have a common nilpotence exponent. Coproducts and coequalizers are computed with their PD operations and their induced quotients.

theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$.

theorems.name: Finite nonempty colimits for small affine thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$.

theorems.proof: Finite products have a common nilpotence exponent. Coproducts and coequalizers are computed with their PD operations and their induced quotients.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Inclusion preserves small affine crystalline colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$.
theorems.statement: The inclusion of the small into the big affine category preserves these colimits.
theorems.proof: Finite products have a common nilpotence exponent. Coproducts and coequalizers are computed with their PD operations and their induced quotients.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: PD stability of sufficiently large powers of p
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ be an $A$-algebra presentation with kernel $J$. Let $E$ be its PD envelope and $\widehat E$ its $p$-adic completion. Let $E_e$ be the envelope of the image of $J$ in $P/p^eP$.
theorems.statement: For $e$ sufficiently large $p^eE$ and $p^e\widehat E$ lie in the respective PD ideals and are preserved by all positive divided powers.
theorems.proof: Since a power of $p$ vanishes on the given quotient, sufficiently high powers form PD-stable ideals. The envelope quotient formula identifies all the truncations.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Truncations of completed PD envelopes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ be an $A$-algebra presentation with kernel $J$. Let $E$ be its PD envelope and $\widehat E$ its $p$-adic completion. Let $E_e$ be the envelope of the image of $J$ in $P/p^eP$.
theorems.statement: For $e$ sufficiently large the natural identifications $\widehat E/p^e=E/p^e=E_e$ preserve divided powers.
theorems.proof: Since a power of $p$ vanishes on the given quotient, sufficiently high powers form PD-stable ideals. The envelope quotient formula identifies all the truncations.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Finite-level envelope as an affine thickening
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ be an $A$-algebra presentation with kernel $J$. Let $E$ be its PD envelope and $\widehat E$ its $p$-adic completion. Let $E_e$ be the envelope of the image of $J$ in $P/p^eP$.
theorems.statement: For sufficiently large $e$, $E_e\to C$ belongs to the small affine category.
theorems.proof: Since a power of $p$ vanishes on the given quotient, sufficiently high powers form PD-stable ideals. The envelope quotient formula identifies all the truncations.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Completed envelope as inverse limit
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ be an $A$-algebra presentation with kernel $J$. Let $E$ be its PD envelope and $\widehat E$ its $p$-adic completion. Let $E_e$ be the envelope of the image of $J$ in $P/p^eP$.
theorems.statement: The completed envelope with its PD ideal is the inverse limit of the finite-level envelopes.
theorems.proof: Since a power of $p$ vanishes on the given quotient, sufficiently high powers form PD-stable ideals. The envelope quotient formula identifies all the truncations.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Completed envelope as a completed thickening
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ be an $A$-algebra presentation with kernel $J$. Let $E$ be its PD envelope and $\widehat E$ its $p$-adic completion. Let $E_e$ be the envelope of the image of $J$ in $P/p^eP$.
theorems.statement: The map $\widehat E\to C$ is an object of the completed affine thickening category.
theorems.proof: Since a power of $p$ vanishes on the given quotient, sufficiently high powers form PD-stable ideals. The envelope quotient formula identifies all the truncations.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Weak initiality of the finite envelope system
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ be an $A$-algebra presentation with kernel $J$. Let $E$ be its PD envelope and $\widehat E$ its $p$-adic completion. Let $E_e$ be the envelope of the image of $J$ in $P/p^eP$. Assume $P$ a polynomial algebra. Fix an arbitrary big affine PD thickening $B$.
theorems.statement: For some $e$ there exists a morphism $E_e\to B$ in the big affine category.
theorems.proof: Lift the polynomial generators and apply the universal property of the PD envelope, followed by truncation or completion.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Weak initiality of the completed polynomial envelope
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ be an $A$-algebra presentation with kernel $J$. Let $E$ be its PD envelope and $\widehat E$ its $p$-adic completion. Let $E_e$ be the envelope of the image of $J$ in $P/p^eP$. Assume $P$ a polynomial algebra and let $B\to C$ be a completed affine PD thickening.
theorems.statement: There exists a morphism $\widehat E\to B$ in the completed affine category.
theorems.proof: Lift the polynomial generators and apply the universal property of the PD envelope, followed by truncation or completion.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: PD differentials of a polynomial algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with PD ideal $(J,\delta)$ in $B$.
theorems.statement: For $B[x]$ with extended PD ideal $JB[x]$, its module of PD differentials is the direct sum of the extended module of base PD differentials and $B[x]dx$.
theorems.proof: Use the universal property of divided power derivations on polynomial generators and on lifts through the quotient.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: PD differentials of a PD polynomial algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with PD ideal $(J,\delta)$ in $B$.
theorems.statement: For $B\langle x\rangle$ with the standard enlarged PD ideal, its module of PD differentials splits as the extended base module and one free generator $dx$.
theorems.proof: Use the universal property of divided power derivations on polynomial generators and on lifts through the quotient.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: PD differentials and quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with PD ideal $(J,\delta)$ in $B$.
theorems.statement: If $K\subset J$ is stable under positive divided powers, differentials on $B/K$ are the extended PD differentials on $B$ modulo the images of $dk$ for $k\in K$.
theorems.proof: Use the universal property of divided power derivations on polynomial generators and on lifts through the quotient.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Stability of the pd codiagonal ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)\to(B,J)$ be a map of PD rings. Take the PD-ring coproduct $B(1)$ of two copies of $B$ over $A$. Let $K$ be the kernel of its codiagonal to $B$ and write $J(1)$ for its PD ideal.
theorems.statement: $K\cap J(1)$ is preserved by the divided powers.
theorems.proof: The two inclusions determine a universal difference derivation modulo products and divided powers of order at least two.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: PD conormal formula for the pd codiagonal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)\to(B,J)$ be a map of PD rings. Take the PD-ring coproduct $B(1)$ of two copies of $B$ over $A$. Let $K$ be the kernel of its codiagonal to $B$ and write $J(1)$ for its PD ideal.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $\Omega^1_{B/A,\delta}=K/(K^2+(K\cap J(1))^{[2]})$.
theorems.proof: The two inclusions determine a universal difference derivation modulo products and divided powers of order at least two.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Stability of the affine codiagonal ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $(B,J)$ be a big affine thickening and take its self-coproduct $B(1)$ in the big affine category. Let $K$ be the kernel of its codiagonal to $B$ and write $J(1)$ for its PD ideal.

theorems.proof: The two inclusions determine a universal difference derivation modulo products and divided powers of order at least two.

theorems.name: PD conormal formula for the affine codiagonal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $(B,J)$ be a big affine thickening and take its self-coproduct $B(1)$ in the big affine category. Let $K$ be the kernel of its codiagonal to $B$ and write $J(1)$ for its PD ideal.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Differentials of the relative PD envelope
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided power (PD) ring, $B$ an $A$-algebra, and $J$ an ideal of $B$ containing $IB$. Write $E$ for the relative envelope.
theorems.statement: The PD differentials on $E$ over $A$ are canonically $E\otimes_B\Omega^1_{B/A}$, with ordinary differentials on $B$.
theorems.proof: Extending a derivation in a square-zero PD extension is the representing property of the envelope.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Comparing completed modules of PD differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with PD ideal $(J,\delta)$ in $B$. Assume $A$ is over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $p$ nilpotent in $B/J$. Write $B_e=B/p^eB$ for $e$ sufficiently large.
theorems.statement: The inverse limit of the PD differential modules of $B_e$ identifies with the $p$-adic completion of the PD differentials of $B$ and of the PD differentials of its $p$-adic completion.
theorems.proof: The high truncations inherit the divided powers and have the same modules of PD differentials modulo the corresponding powers of $p$.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Fibre products of PD schemes
theorems.hypotheses: For a diagram of PD schemes $T\to S\leftarrow T^\prime$, write a subscript $0$ for the closed subscheme cut out by the indicated PD ideal.
theorems.statement: The diagram admits a fibre product $W$ in PD schemes.
theorems.proof: Construct the PD pushout on affine opens and glue using its universal property.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: PD products map by closed immersions to ordinary products
theorems.hypotheses: For a diagram of PD schemes $T\to S\leftarrow T^\prime$, write a subscript $0$ for the closed subscheme cut out by the indicated PD ideal.
theorems.statement: The map from $W$ to the ordinary fibre product of schemes over $S$ is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: Construct the PD pushout on affine opens and glue using its universal property.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Special fibre of a product of PD schemes
theorems.hypotheses: For a diagram of PD schemes $T\to S\leftarrow T^\prime$, write a subscript $0$ for the closed subscheme cut out by the indicated PD ideal.
theorems.statement: The natural map $W_0\to T_0\times_{S_0}T_0^\prime$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Construct the PD pushout on affine opens and glue using its universal property.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Limits of relative crystalline thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent.
theorems.statement: The category of geometric relative PD thickenings has all finite nonempty limits, including binary products and pullbacks.
theorems.proof: The PD fibre product and the fibre product of closed parts give the representing diagram. The closed-part functor also has a left adjoint.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Underlying closed parts of crystalline limits
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent.
theorems.statement: The functor taking $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$ over $X$ preserves limits that exist.
theorems.proof: The PD fibre product and the fibre product of closed parts give the representing diagram. The closed-part functor also has a left adjoint.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Ordinary scheme pullback for a flat crystalline arrow
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Form the crystalline pullback of $T_1\to T\leftarrow T_2$ with their closed parts $U_i,U$. Suppose $T_2\to T$ flat and $U_2=U\times_T T_2$.
theorems.statement: The thickening scheme in the crystalline pullback is the ordinary scheme $T_1\times_T T_2$.
theorems.proof: Flat extension carries the defining PD ideal with its divided powers and the required quotient. The ordinary scheme pullback therefore represents the crystalline pullback.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Finite nonempty limits under crystalline inclusion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Write $j$ for the inclusion of the small into the big crystalline site.
theorems.statement: The inclusion preserves finite nonempty limits.
theorems.proof: A covering family of a small object is given by an open cover of its thickening scheme. The small closed parts are closed under finite nonempty limits over $X$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Full faithfulness of crystalline inclusion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Write $j$ for the inclusion of the small into the big crystalline site.
theorems.statement: The inclusion is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: A covering family of a small object is given by an open cover of its thickening scheme. The small closed parts are closed under finite nonempty limits over $X$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Continuity of crystalline inclusion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Write $j$ for the inclusion of the small into the big crystalline site.
theorems.statement: The inclusion is continuous.
theorems.proof: A covering family of a small object is given by an open cover of its thickening scheme. The small closed parts are closed under finite nonempty limits over $X$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Cocontinuity of crystalline inclusion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Write $j$ for the inclusion of the small into the big crystalline site.
theorems.statement: The inclusion is cocontinuous.
theorems.proof: A covering family of a small object is given by an open cover of its thickening scheme. The small closed parts are closed under finite nonempty limits over $X$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The small crystalline topos as a retract
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Write $j$ for the inclusion of the small into the big crystalline site.
theorems.statement: The inclusion induces $i$ from the small to the big crystalline topos. There is a morphism $\pi$ back with $\pi i$ canonically the identity.
theorems.proof: A covering family of a small object is given by an open cover of its thickening scheme. The small closed parts are closed under finite nonempty limits over $X$.
refs: Stacks 07IJ · two geometric morphisms and section

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Crystalline direct image as restriction
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Write $j$ for the inclusion of the small into the big crystalline site.
theorems.statement: $\pi_*=i^{-1}$ is restriction of sheaves from the big to the small site.
theorems.proof: A covering family of a small object is given by an open cover of its thickening scheme. The small closed parts are closed under finite nonempty limits over $X$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Crystalline inclusion of open pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Let $X^\prime\subset X$ and $S^\prime\subset S$ be opens, with $X^\prime$ mapping into $S^\prime$.
theorems.statement: The functor from the small site of $X^\prime/S^\prime$ to that of $X/S$ is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: Restriction to the open subobjects realizes the corresponding morphism over the Zariski topos as its localization.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Crystalline localization over a Zariski open
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Let $X^\prime\subset X$ and $S^\prime\subset S$ be opens, with $X^\prime$ mapping into $S^\prime$.
theorems.statement: The induced geometric morphism commutes with the maps to the Zariski topoi of $X^\prime$ and $X$.
theorems.proof: Restriction to the open subobjects realizes the corresponding morphism over the Zariski topos as its localization.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localization of the crystalline-to-Zariski morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Let $X^\prime\subset X$ and $S^\prime\subset S$ be opens, with $X^\prime$ mapping into $S^\prime$.
theorems.statement: This square identifies the first crystalline-to-Zariski map with localization of the second at $X^\prime$.
theorems.proof: Restriction to the open subobjects realizes the corresponding morphism over the Zariski topos as its localization.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Quasi-coherence of PD differentials on a scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(T,J,\delta)$ be a PD scheme with a scheme morphism $T\to S$. Impose the PD chain rule in $\Omega^1_{T/S}$.
theorems.statement: The resulting quotient sheaf $\Omega^1_{T/S,\delta}$ is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: The PD relation submodule is compatible with localization; affine calculations glue.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Affine sections of scheme PD differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(T,J,\delta)$ be a PD scheme with a scheme morphism $T\to S$. Impose the PD chain rule in $\Omega^1_{T/S}$.
theorems.statement: On each affine open $W\subset T$ mapping into an affine $V\subset S$, its sections are the PD differentials of $\mathcal O(W)$ relative to $\mathcal O(V)$.
theorems.proof: The PD relation submodule is compatible with localization; affine calculations glue.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Evaluating the crystalline differential sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Let $(U,T,\delta)$ be a small crystalline object.
theorems.statement: On $T$ the restriction of the crystalline differential sheaf is the sheaf of PD differentials of $T/S$.
theorems.proof: The universal derivations agree on every affine open chart and hence agree as sheaf maps.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Evaluating the universal crystalline derivation
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Let $(U,T,\delta)$ be a small crystalline object.
theorems.statement: Its universal derivation restricts to the universal PD derivation on $T/S$.
theorems.proof: The universal derivations agree on every affine open chart and hence agree as sheaf maps.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Affine crystalline sections of the differential sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Take an affine thickening $T$ in the small site mapping into an affine base open $V$.
theorems.statement: Sections over this object are the PD differentials of $\mathcal O(T)$ relative to $\mathcal O(V)$.
theorems.proof: Combine the sheaf restriction theorem with the affine description of PD differentials.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Diagonal ideal in the small crystalline site
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. For an object of the small site let $K$ denote the diagonal ideal in its crystalline self-product.
theorems.statement: $K$ lies in the PD ideal of the self-product and is preserved by the divided powers.
theorems.proof: Because the closed part is open in $X$, its self-product over $X$ is itself. The codiagonal formula becomes the PD conormal quotient.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Crystalline differentials from the PD diagonal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. For an object of the small site let $K$ denote the diagonal ideal in its crystalline self-product.
theorems.statement: The differential sheaf evaluated on the thickening identifies canonically with $K/K^{[2]}$ on it.
theorems.proof: Because the closed part is open in $X$, its self-product over $X$ is itself. The codiagonal formula becomes the PD conormal quotient.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Objectwise quasi-coherence of crystalline differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent.
theorems.statement: The differential sheaf on the small crystalline site is locally quasi-coherent in the objectwise sense.
theorems.proof: The local PD differential modules are quasi-coherent, and passage to a quotient ring gives a surjection on differentials.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Differential restriction along closed immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent.
theorems.statement: For an arrow whose map of thickening schemes is a closed immersion, the map from pulled-back target differentials to source differentials is surjective.
theorems.proof: The local PD differential modules are quasi-coherent, and passage to a quotient ring gives a surjection on differentials.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Canonical connection on a crystal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Let $E$ be a crystal of modules on the small site.
theorems.statement: The crystalline isomorphisms determine a canonical connection on $E$.
theorems.proof: The two sections of the first-order universal thickening give the connection. The crystal cocycle on the second-order thickening forces its curvature to vanish.
refs: Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on Crystalline Cohomology, §6, Definition 6.1

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Integrability of the crystalline connection
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Let $E$ be a crystal of modules on the small site.
theorems.statement: The canonical connection on $E$ has zero curvature.
theorems.proof: The two sections of the first-order universal thickening give the connection. The crystal cocycle on the second-order thickening forces its curvature to vanish.
refs: Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on Crystalline Cohomology, §6, Definition 6.1

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Cosimplicial homotopies under tensor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A_*$ be a cosimplicial ring and $u,v:K_*\to M_*$ homotopic maps of cosimplicial modules. Fix a cosimplicial $A_*$-module $L_*$.
theorems.statement: The maps obtained by tensoring with its identity are homotopic.
theorems.proof: Apply the indicated degreewise functor to the constituent operators of the cosimplicial homotopy.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Cosimplicial homotopies under exterior
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A_*$ be a cosimplicial ring and $u,v:K_*\to M_*$ homotopic maps of cosimplicial modules. Fix an exterior degree $i\ge0$.
theorems.statement: Taking the degree-$i$ exterior powers of the maps gives homotopic maps.
theorems.proof: Apply the indicated degreewise functor to the constituent operators of the cosimplicial homotopy.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Cosimplicial homotopies under base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A_*$ be a cosimplicial ring and $u,v:K_*\to M_*$ homotopic maps of cosimplicial modules. Fix a map of cosimplicial rings $A_*\to B_*$.
theorems.statement: After scalar extension the two maps are homotopic as cosimplicial $B_*$-module maps.
theorems.proof: Apply the indicated degreewise functor to the constituent operators of the cosimplicial homotopy.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Cosimplicial homotopies under completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A_*$ be a cosimplicial ring and $u,v:K_*\to M_*$ homotopic maps of cosimplicial modules. Fix a cosimplicial ideal of $A_*$.
theorems.statement: The maps induced on the respective degreewise ideal-adic completions are homotopic.
theorems.proof: Apply the indicated degreewise functor to the constituent operators of the cosimplicial homotopy.

theorems.subject: crystalline-pd-algebra
theorems.name: Coordinates for a completed crystalline self-product
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For $n\ge0$ let $D(n)$ be the completed PD envelope of the kernel of $P^{\otimes_A(n+1)}\to C$.
theorems.statement: Over its first factor $D$, the algebra $D(n)$ is the $p$-adically completed PD polynomial algebra on the differences between the first and the $(j+1)$st copy of each $x_i$, for $1\le j\le n$.
theorems.proof: The algebraic tensor presentation is polynomial in the coordinate differences. Complete the envelope after adjoining them as PD variables.
refs: Stacks 07L3 · coordinate description from the first tensor factor

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Completed envelope powers as crystalline thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For $n\ge0$ let $D(n)$ be the completed PD envelope of the kernel of $P^{\otimes_A(n+1)}\to C$.
theorems.statement: Both $D$ and the $D(n)$ are completed affine PD thickenings of $C$.
theorems.proof: Use the universal maps from the factors of the tensor algebra, first at each truncated level and then in the limit.

theorems.subject: crystalline-thickening
theorems.name: Coproducts of the completed presentation envelope
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For $n\ge0$ let $D(n)$ be the completed PD envelope of the kernel of $P^{\otimes_A(n+1)}\to C$.
theorems.statement: $D(n)$ represents the coproduct of $n+1$ copies of $D$ in the completed affine category.
theorems.proof: Use the universal maps from the factors of the tensor algebra, first at each truncated level and then in the limit.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: From affine crystals to modules with connection
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Take a crystal in quasi-coherent modules on the small site.
theorems.statement: Evaluation on the truncations of $D$ and inverse limit define a functor to modules with connection satisfying the four conditions. The module is classically $p$-adically complete, its connection takes values in the completed differential tensor product, has zero curvature, and in the given coordinates only finitely many positive iterates $\theta_i^k(m)$ are nonzero modulo $p$ for each section $m$.
theorems.proof: The evaluations on $D/p^e$ are compatible under reduction. Take their inverse limit and obtain the connection and convergence from crystalline transport over the completed self-products.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.8 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: p-adic completeness of the module after evaluating a crystal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Take a crystal in quasi-coherent modules on the small site.
theorems.statement: The natural map $M\to\varprojlim_e M/p^eM$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The evaluations on $D/p^e$ are compatible under reduction. Take their inverse limit and obtain the connection and convergence from crystalline transport over the completed self-products.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.8 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Connection with completed coefficients after evaluating a crystal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Take a crystal in quasi-coherent modules on the small site.
theorems.statement: $M$ has a connection with target $M\widehat\otimes_D\Omega_D^1$ satisfying the Leibniz rule.
theorems.proof: The evaluations on $D/p^e$ are compatible under reduction. Take their inverse limit and obtain the connection and convergence from crystalline transport over the completed self-products.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.8 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Integrability of a completed connection after evaluating a crystal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Take a crystal in quasi-coherent modules on the small site.
theorems.statement: The curvature vanishes in the completed module of two-forms.
theorems.proof: The evaluations on $D/p^e$ are compatible under reduction. Take their inverse limit and obtain the connection and convergence from crystalline transport over the completed self-products.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.8 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Topological quasi-nilpotence of a coordinate connection after evaluating a crystal
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Take a crystal in quasi-coherent modules on the small site.
theorems.statement: Write $\nabla m=\sum_i\theta_i(m)dx_i$. For each $m$ only finitely many pairs $(i,k)$ with $k\ge1$ satisfy $\theta_i^k(m)\notin pM$.
theorems.proof: The evaluations on $D/p^e$ are compatible under reduction. Take their inverse limit and obtain the connection and convergence from crystalline transport over the completed self-products.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.8 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Full faithfulness of completed crystalline evaluation
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Take module pairs on $D$ satisfying these hypotheses. The module is classically $p$-adically complete, its connection takes values in the completed differential tensor product, has zero curvature, and in the given coordinates only finitely many positive iterates $\theta_i^k(m)$ are nonzero modulo $p$ for each section $m$.
theorems.statement: Morphisms of crystals correspond bijectively to horizontal $D$-linear maps of pairs.
theorems.proof: The PD Taylor expansion built from the commuting operators converges by topological quasi-nilpotence. It identifies the pullbacks for all lifts and satisfies the cocycle identity.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.8 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Recognition of all affine crystalline modules with connection
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Take module pairs on $D$ satisfying these hypotheses. The module is classically $p$-adically complete, its connection takes values in the completed differential tensor product, has zero curvature, and in the given coordinates only finitely many positive iterates $\theta_i^k(m)$ are nonzero modulo $p$ for each section $m$.
theorems.statement: Every pair satisfying all four conditions comes from a crystal in quasi-coherent modules. Together with full faithfulness this gives an equivalence of categories.
theorems.proof: The PD Taylor expansion built from the commuting operators converges by topological quasi-nilpotence. It identifies the pullbacks for all lifts and satisfies the cocycle identity.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.8 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Retraction between smooth and polynomial envelopes
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P^\prime$ be smooth over $A$ and surject onto $C$. Write $D^\prime$ for the completed relative PD envelope of its kernel.
theorems.statement: A polynomial presentation can be chosen whose envelope $D$ admits PD maps $a:D\to D^\prime$ and $b:D^\prime\to D$ over $A$ and $C$, with $ab=1$.
theorems.proof: Use the strong lifting property of a smooth algebra, then use crystalline transport between the two lifts. Quasi-nilpotence over the smooth presentation is tested by pullback along the comparison map as in the proof.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Remark 2.9 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Independence of smooth presentation for crystalline pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P^\prime$ be smooth over $A$ and surject onto $C$. Write $D^\prime$ for the completed relative PD envelope of its kernel.
theorems.statement: These maps identify the categories of complete integrable, topologically quasi-nilpotent pairs. The criterion on the smooth presentation uses transport to a polynomial one.
theorems.proof: Use the strong lifting property of a smooth algebra, then use crystalline transport between the two lifts. Quasi-nilpotence over the smooth presentation is tested by pullback along the comparison map as in the proof.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Remark 2.9 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Crystalline evaluation on smooth presentations
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P^\prime$ be smooth over $A$ and surject onto $C$. Write $D^\prime$ for the completed relative PD envelope of its kernel.
theorems.statement: Crystals in quasi-coherent modules are therefore equivalent to the corresponding pairs over $D^\prime$.
theorems.proof: Use the strong lifting property of a smooth algebra, then use crystalline transport between the two lifts. Quasi-nilpotence over the smooth presentation is tested by pullback along the comparison map as in the proof.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Remark 2.9 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Acyclic affine objects for objectwise quasi-coherent coefficients
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Choose an object $(U,T,\delta)$ in the small site with $U$ or $T$ affine, and an objectwise quasi-coherent crystalline module $F$.
theorems.statement: $H^j((U,T,\delta),F)=0$ for every positive $j$.
theorems.proof: Covers on the slice are Zariski covers of $T$ and affine quasi-coherent sheaves have vanishing higher cohomology.
refs: Stacks 07JJ · vanishing in all positive degrees

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Computing affine crystalline cohomology on thickenings of the whole scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Assume $X,S$ affine and $F$ an objectwise quasi-coherent module. Give the full subcategory of thickenings with closed part all of $X$ the topology in which only maximal sieves cover.
theorems.statement: Restriction identifies the derived global sections of $F$ with those on this subcategory.
theorems.proof: The restriction comparison uses acyclicity on affine objects and the description of covers of each thickening.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Geometric morphism to completed crystalline thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Give the opposites of the small affine and completed affine thickening categories the topology in which only maximal sieves cover. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on the former and a completed object $B$, take $B_e=B/p^eB$ for large $e$.
theorems.statement: There is a morphism $g$ from the topos of ordinary affine thickenings to that of completed thickenings.
theorems.proof: The evaluations defining the direct image on a completed object are the inverse limit of a countable tower of evaluations on its truncations.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Degree-zero direct image on completed thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Give the opposites of the small affine and completed affine thickening categories the topology in which only maximal sieves cover. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on the former and a completed object $B$, take $B_e=B/p^eB$ for large $e$.
theorems.statement: The value of $g_*F$ on $B$ is $\varprojlim_e F(B_e)$.
theorems.proof: The evaluations defining the direct image on a completed object are the inverse limit of a countable tower of evaluations on its truncations.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Degree-one direct image on completed thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Give the opposites of the small affine and completed affine thickening categories the topology in which only maximal sieves cover. theorems.proof: The evaluations defining the direct image on a completed object are the inverse limit of a countable tower of evaluations on its truncations.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Higher direct images on completed thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Give the opposites of the small affine and completed affine thickening categories the topology in which only maximal sieves cover. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on the former and a completed object $B$, take $B_e=B/p^eB$ for large $e$.
theorems.statement: On $B$ all $R^jg_*F$ vanish for $j>1$.
theorems.proof: The evaluations defining the direct image on a completed object are the inverse limit of a countable tower of evaluations on its truncations.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A Čech complex from a weakly terminal object
theorems.hypotheses: Let a category with binary products have the topology in which only maximal sieves cover. Choose an object $W$ admitting a map from every object. Let $F$ be any abelian sheaf.
theorems.statement: Derived global sections are computed by the alternating cosimplicial complex whose term in degree $n$ is $F(W^{n+1})$.
theorems.proof: The presheaf represented by $W$ covers the final sheaf. The powers of $W$ are representable and evaluation in the presheaf category is exact.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Contractible cosimplicial module of ordered vertices
theorems.hypotheses: For a cosimplicial ring $A_*$ take the free module $N_n$ on the positions $0,\ldots,n$ in degree $n$, with structure maps sending basis vectors to their indicated positions.
theorems.statement: The identity of $N_*$ is cosimplicially homotopic to zero.
theorems.proof: At a simplex of the interval the homotopy retains the basis vectors on one side of the cut and sends the others to zero.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Contraction of crystalline one-forms
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For $n\ge0$ let $D(n)$ be the completed PD envelope of the kernel of $P^{\otimes_A(n+1)}\to C$.
theorems.statement: The cosimplicial module of completed PD one-forms on $D(n)$ is homotopic to zero.
theorems.proof: Contract the cosimplicial free module on the coordinate slots; the required degreewise operations preserve cosimplicial homotopies.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.15 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Contraction of higher crystalline forms with coefficients
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For $n\ge0$ let $D(n)$ be the completed PD envelope of the kernel of $P^{\otimes_A(n+1)}\to C$. Fix $i>0$ and any cosimplicial $D(*)$-module $M_*$.
theorems.statement: The completed tensors of $M_n$ with the completed exterior $i$-forms on $D(n)$ form a cosimplicial module homotopic to zero.
theorems.proof: Contract the cosimplicial free module on the coordinate slots; the required degreewise operations preserve cosimplicial homotopies.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.17 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Crystalline Poincaré lemma, absolute case
theorems.hypotheses: Take a PD polynomial algebra $P=A\langle x_i\rangle$ over any ring $A$.
theorems.statement: For every $A$-module $M$, its tensor with the PD de Rham complex of $P/A$, augmented by $M$, is exact.
theorems.proof: On PD monomials one integrates by increasing the divided power index. Tensoring the contraction and filtering by base degree give the relative statement; reductions give the completed variant.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.13 and its proof (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Completed crystalline Poincaré lemma, absolute case
theorems.hypotheses: Take a PD polynomial algebra $P=A\langle x_i\rangle$ over any ring $A$.
theorems.statement: For every classically $p$-adically complete $M$, the augmented complex using the completed algebra, completed forms and completed tensor products is exact.
theorems.proof: On PD monomials one integrates by increasing the divided power index. Tensoring the contraction and filtering by base degree give the relative statement; reductions give the completed variant.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.13 and its proof (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Crystalline Poincaré lemma, relative case
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with PD ideal $(J,\delta)$ in $B$. Let $P=B\langle x_i\rangle$ have the PD ideal generated by the base ideal and the variables.
theorems.statement: For a $B$-module with integrable connection the map from its PD de Rham complex to the de Rham complex of its scalar extension to $P$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: On PD monomials one integrates by increasing the divided power index. Tensoring the contraction and filtering by base degree give the relative statement; reductions give the completed variant.
refs: Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Lemma 2.13 and its proof (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Completed crystalline Poincaré lemma, relative case
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with PD ideal $(J,\delta)$ in $B$. Let $P=B\langle x_i\rangle$ have the PD ideal generated by the base ideal and the variables.
theorems.statement: For a complete module over the $p$-adic completion of $B$ with integrable connection into completed forms, the corresponding map of completed de Rham complexes after adjoining the variables is a quasi-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: On PD monomials one integrates by increasing the divided power index. Tensoring the contraction and filtering by base degree give the relative statement; reductions give the completed variant.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Affine crystalline cohomology from evaluated envelope powers
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For $n\ge0$ let $D(n)$ be the completed PD envelope of the kernel of $P^{\otimes_A(n+1)}\to C$. Assume $F$ is a module on the small crystalline site whose restrictions to all thickenings are quasi-coherent and whose comparison maps from pullback are surjective for arrows inducing closed immersions of thickening schemes. Write $M(n)$ for the inverse limit of its evaluations on the thickenings given by $D(n)/p^eD(n)$ for sufficiently large $e$.
theorems.statement: The alternating complex of the $M(n)$ represents $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Cris}(X/S),F)$.
theorems.proof: The completed envelope thickenings compute derived sections. The surjectivity hypothesis eliminates the first derived inverse limits.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Vanishing with positive-degree crystalline forms
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For $n\ge0$ let $D(n)$ be the completed PD envelope of the kernel of $P^{\otimes_A(n+1)}\to C$. Assume $F$ is a module on the small crystalline site whose restrictions to all thickenings are quasi-coherent and whose comparison maps from pullback are surjective for arrows inducing closed immersions of thickening schemes.
theorems.statement: $H^j(\operatorname{Cris}(X/S),F\otimes\Omega^i_{X/S})=0$ for every $i>0$ and $j\ge0$.
theorems.proof: After evaluation, positive exterior powers of the differential module give contractible cosimplicial modules, including after the completed tensor products.
refs: Stacks 07LF · all positive forms and nonnegative degrees

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Crystalline cohomology using a polynomial presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Choose a polynomial algebra $P=A[x_i]$ surjecting onto $C$ and let $D$ be the $p$-adic completion of the relative PD envelope of its kernel. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $F$ be a crystal in quasi-coherent modules and $(M,\nabla)$ the corresponding pair on the completed envelope $D$.
theorems.statement: The completed de Rham complex $M\widehat\otimes_{D}\Omega^\bullet_{D}$ computes $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Cris}(X/S),F)$. Its forms are the $p$-adic completions of the relative divided power differential forms over $A$, with $d\gamma_r(z)=\gamma_{r-1}(z)\,dz$ on the PD ideal for $r\geq1$. The connection induces the differential.
theorems.proof: Use the two directions of the crystalline Čech–de Rham double complex, the contraction for positive forms, and the relative PD Poincaré lemma.
refs: Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on Crystalline Cohomology, Theorem 7.1 (smooth embedding)
Bhatt–de Jong, Crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology, Theorem 2.12 (over the p-adic base in that paper)

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Crystalline cohomology using a smooth presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Let $P^\prime$ be smooth over $A$ and surject onto $C$. Write $D^\prime$ for the completed relative PD envelope of its kernel. theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The crystalline de Rham augmentation after direct image
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Take a crystal $F$ in quasi-coherent modules on the small site, and write $u$ for the canonical map to the Zariski topos of $X$.
theorems.statement: The projection of the de Rham complex of $F$ to $F[0]$ becomes a quasi-isomorphism under $Ru_*$.
theorems.proof: Compute on affine opens and apply vanishing for coefficients tensored with positive exterior powers of crystalline differentials.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Higher crystalline forms vanish under derived Zariski direct image
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Take a crystal $F$ in quasi-coherent modules on the small site, and write $u$ for the canonical map to the Zariski topos of $X$.
theorems.statement: For every $i>0$, $Ru_*(F\otimes\Omega^i_{X/S})=0$.
theorems.proof: Compute on affine opens and apply vanishing for coefficients tensored with positive exterior powers of crystalline differentials.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Reverse de Rham map for a split coordinate
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B\to B^\prime$ be a map with compatible relative differential calculi and fix an integrable module with connection on $B$. Choose $a\in B$, $z\in B^\prime$ and $\theta:B^\prime\to B^\prime$. $da=0$. $\Omega^\prime=(B^\prime\otimes_B\Omega)\oplus B^\prime dz$, giving $df=d_1f+\partial_z(f)dz$. $\theta$ is $B$-linear. $\partial_z\theta$ acts as multiplication by $a$. $B\to B^\prime$ stays injective after tensoring with every $B$-module. $af-\theta(\partial_z f)$ belongs to $B$ for every $f\in B^\prime$. For each $f\in B^\prime$, $(\theta\otimes1)d_1f-d_1(\theta f)$ belongs to the image of $\Omega$.
theorems.statement: There exists an opposite-direction chain map for the map to the base-changed de Rham complex.
theorems.proof: The integration operator on the additional coordinate gives a homotopy in the target; the resulting residual term descends to the base complex.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Source composite for a split coordinate
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B\to B^\prime$ be a map with compatible relative differential calculi and fix an integrable module with connection on $B$. Choose $a\in B$, $z\in B^\prime$ and $\theta:B^\prime\to B^\prime$. $da=0$. $\Omega^\prime=(B^\prime\otimes_B\Omega)\oplus B^\prime dz$, giving $df=d_1f+\partial_z(f)dz$. $\theta$ is $B$-linear. $\partial_z\theta$ acts as multiplication by $a$. $B\to B^\prime$ stays injective after tensoring with every $B$-module. $af-\theta(\partial_z f)$ belongs to $B$ for every $f\in B^\prime$. For each $f\in B^\prime$, $(\theta\otimes1)d_1f-d_1(\theta f)$ belongs to the image of $\Omega$.
theorems.statement: The reverse map composed after the map to the base-changed de Rham complex is chain homotopic to multiplication by $a$ on the source.
theorems.proof: The integration operator on the additional coordinate gives a homotopy in the target; the resulting residual term descends to the base complex.

For each $f\in B^\prime$, $(\theta\otimes1)d_1f-d_1(\theta f)$ belongs to the image of $\Omega$.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: Reverse de Rham map for a pth-root extension
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and an $A/I$-algebra $C$ with $p$ nilpotent in $C$. Fix $\lambda\in D$ and a pair satisfying the four crystalline conditions. For the completed algebra $D^\prime=(D[z]\langle\xi\rangle/(\xi-z^p+\lambda))^\wedge_p$ take its completed PD differentials.

theorems.subject: crystalline-connection
theorems.name: A primitive on a divided power polynomial algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $B^\prime=B\langle z\rangle$ be the free PD variable extension of a PD algebra $B$, with its enlarged PD ideal and the two PD differential calculi.
theorems.statement: Take $a=1$ and send $z^{[m]}$ to $z^{[m+1]}$ $B$-linearly. This satisfies the split-coordinate hypotheses and recovers the relative crystalline Poincaré lemma.
theorems.proof: Differentiation lowers the divided power index and integration raises it; their error on the other side is evaluation at zero.

theorems.subject: crystalline-frobenius
theorems.name: Sheafwise annihilator for purely inseparable crystalline pullback
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Assume $p\in\mathcal I$. Let $f:X^\prime\to X$ be an iterated alpha-p cover of constant degree $q$ and $E$ a quasi-coherent crystal on $X/S$ with crystalline pullback $E^\prime$.
theorems.statement: Each cohomology sheaf of the cone of $Ru_{X/S,*}E\to f_*Ru_{X^\prime/S,*}E^\prime$ is annihilated by $q$.
theorems.proof: Locally resolve each adjoining of a pth root by the completed PD calculation. Composing the isogenies multiplies their bounds.

theorems.subject: crystalline-frobenius
theorems.name: Kernel bound for pullback along the iterated cover
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Assume $p\in\mathcal I$. Let $f:X^\prime\to X$ be an iterated alpha-p cover of constant degree $q$ and $E$ a quasi-coherent crystal on $X/S$ with crystalline pullback $E^\prime$. Fix $i\ge0$.
theorems.statement: The kernel on degree-$i$ crystalline cohomology is killed by $q^{i+1}$.
theorems.proof: Use the cohomology-sheaf bound on the cone in the hypercohomology spectral sequence; its finite filtration gives the indicated power.

theorems.subject: crystalline-frobenius
theorems.name: Kernel bound for pullback along relative Frobenius
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Assume $p\in\mathcal I$. theorems.statement: The kernel on degree-$i$ crystalline cohomology is killed by $p^{d(i+1)}$.
theorems.proof: Use the cohomology-sheaf bound on the cone in the hypercohomology spectral sequence; its finite filtration gives the indicated power.

theorems.subject: crystalline-frobenius
theorems.name: Degree of Frobenius as an iterated alpha-p cover
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Assume $p\in\mathcal I$. Assume $X\to S_0$ is smooth of constant relative dimension $d$.

theorems.proof: Pass étale locally to affine space, where the relative Frobenius adjoins the coordinate roots one at a time.

theorems.subject: site

theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\to S^\prime$ be a morphism of PD schemes over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and $f:X\to Y$ a compatible morphism over the induced map of closed base schemes, with $p$ locally nilpotent on $X$ and $Y$. theorems.statement: The value of $Rf_{\rm cris,*}E$ on the thickening scheme $T^\prime$ is $R(T\to T^\prime)_*R\tau_{U/T,*}E_U$.

theorems.subject: site

theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\to S^\prime$ be a morphism of PD schemes over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and $f:X\to Y$ a compatible morphism over the induced map of closed base schemes, with $p$ locally nilpotent on $X$ and $Y$. Take a crystalline module $E$ on $X/S$ and a cover of $X$ by two opens $V,W$.
theorems.statement: The derived direct images for $X$, the direct sum for $V$ and $W$, and the direct image for $V\cap W$, in that order, form a distinguished triangle.
theorems.proof: This section of Stacks explicitly presents results with proof sketches. Localize the crystalline topos at the opens. The difference of the two restriction maps yields the Mayer–Vietoris triangle.
