theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. theorems.statement: In degree $n$ take the product over all ordered $(n+1)$-tuples of indices of the evaluated modules on the completed envelope of the corresponding intersection. Its alternating cochain complex computes crystalline derived sections.
theorems.proof: This section of Stacks explicitly presents results with proof sketches. Use the affine intersections of the chosen opens and the compatible PD envelopes of their tensor product presentations.

theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ and $X\to S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. theorems.statement: In bidegree $(n,m)$ take the direct sum over increasing tuples with $n+1$ indices of their evaluated crystal modules completed-tensored with degree-$m$ differential forms. The total complex with Čech and connection differentials computes crystalline cohomology.

theorems.proof: Use the defining values on the principal basis and their filtered colimits at a prime. Localization is functorial and exact, and exactness of sheaves is detected on stalks.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-map
theorems.name: Point image from global sections
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a locally ringed morphism f from X to an affine scheme Y and x in X.
theorems.statement: The prime of the coordinate ring of Y at f(x) is the inverse image of the maximal ideal of the source stalk under pullback of global functions followed by taking the germ at x.
theorems.proof: The stalk map is local, and evaluation at the point of an affine spectrum recovers its prime.
refs: Stacks 01HY · prime over the image point

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Open unit locus in a locally ringed space
theorems.hypotheses: Let f be a global section of the structure sheaf of a locally ringed space.
theorems.statement: The set D(f) of points at which the germ of f is a unit is open.
theorems.proof: A germwise inverse extends over a neighbourhood. The inverses agree on overlaps by uniqueness.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Inverting a section on its unit locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let f be a global section of the structure sheaf of a locally ringed space.
theorems.statement: The restriction of f to D(f) is an invertible global section there.
theorems.proof: A germwise inverse extends over a neighbourhood. The inverses agree on overlaps by uniqueness.
refs: Stacks 01HZ · global inverse on the locus

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: The unit locus on an affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $f\in R$.
theorems.statement: The locus where f has invertible germ is precisely the principal open of primes avoiding f.
theorems.proof: In the localization at a prime, the nonunits form its extended maximal ideal.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-map
theorems.name: Affine targets represent ring maps on global sections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a locally ringed space and $Y$ an affine scheme.
theorems.statement: Pullback of global functions identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm LRS}(X,Y)$ with ring maps $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$.
theorems.proof: The ring map determines the point image by the inverse image of a maximal ideal and its sheaf map on each principal open by localization.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine schemes and the opposite of rings
theorems.hypotheses: Consider affine schemes with their locally ringed morphisms and rings with unital homomorphisms.
theorems.statement: Global sections and Spec are contravariant quasi-inverse equivalences.
theorems.proof: The affine mapping property gives full faithfulness, and every affine scheme is a spectrum by definition.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Principal opens are affine schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $f\in R$.
theorems.statement: The open subspace on $D(f)$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(R_f)$.
theorems.proof: The map induced by localization identifies the underlying spaces and the local rings.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Finite products of affine schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Consider affine spectra and locally ringed test objects.
theorems.statement: Finite products exist among affine schemes, with terminal object Spec ℤ.
theorems.proof: Mapping a test space into each affine factor amounts to mapping its coordinate ring to global sections. The tensor-product adjunction then gives the universal property.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Pullbacks among affine schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Consider affine spectra and locally ringed test objects.
theorems.statement: Every pair of affine-scheme maps with common affine target has a fibre product in affine schemes.
theorems.proof: Mapping a test space into each affine factor amounts to mapping its coordinate ring to global sections. The tensor-product adjunction then gives the universal property.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Finite limits among affine schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Consider affine spectra and locally ringed test objects.
theorems.statement: Every finite diagram of affine schemes has a limit.
theorems.proof: Mapping a test space into each affine factor amounts to mapping its coordinate ring to global sections. The tensor-product adjunction then gives the universal property.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Product formula in locally ringed spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Consider affine spectra and locally ringed test objects.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{Spec}R\times\operatorname{Spec}S\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S)$ also in locally ringed spaces.
theorems.proof: Mapping a test space into each affine factor amounts to mapping its coordinate ring to global sections. The tensor-product adjunction then gives the universal property.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Tensor-product formula in locally ringed spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Consider affine spectra and locally ringed test objects.
theorems.statement: For $R$-algebras $A,B$ the spectrum of $A\otimes_R B$ is the fibre product of the two spectra over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ also in locally ringed spaces.
theorems.proof: Mapping a test space into each affine factor amounts to mapping its coordinate ring to global sections. The tensor-product adjunction then gives the universal property.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Disjoint union of two affine schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a locally ringed space is the disjoint union of two open subspaces Spec A and Spec B.
theorems.statement: It is affine and identifies with Spec of the product ring A × B.
theorems.proof: The two complementary idempotents in the product ring give these two open affine pieces.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Two constructions of an associated module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The localization sheaf $\widetilde M$ identifies canonically with the sheaf obtained from the module of global coefficients by extension of scalars to $\mathcal O_X$.
theorems.proof: Compute the natural comparison on stalks by localization. Extension of scalars from global coefficients is left adjoint to global sections.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Functorial comparison of associated modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: These canonical isomorphisms commute with all module homomorphisms.
theorems.proof: Compute the natural comparison on stalks by localization. Extension of scalars from global coefficients is left adjoint to global sections.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Associated modules are quasi-coherent
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: $\widetilde M$ is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Compute the natural comparison on stalks by localization. Extension of scalars from global coefficients is left adjoint to global sections.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Mapping property of an associated module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: For every sheaf of modules $F$, taking global sections identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\widetilde M,F)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\Gamma(X,F))$.
theorems.proof: Compute the natural comparison on stalks by localization. Extension of scalars from global coefficients is left adjoint to global sections.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Associated modules preserve tensor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let N be another module and let n be a nonnegative integer.
theorems.statement: $\widetilde{M\otimes_R N}\simeq\widetilde M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\widetilde N$.
theorems.proof: Tensor constructions and their defining quotients commute with localization, giving the canonical comparison on stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Associated modules preserve tensor power
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let N be another module and let n be a nonnegative integer.
theorems.statement: $\widetilde{T^n M}\simeq T^n(\widetilde M)$.
theorems.proof: Tensor constructions and their defining quotients commute with localization, giving the canonical comparison on stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Associated modules preserve symmetric power
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let N be another module and let n be a nonnegative integer.
theorems.statement: $\widetilde{\operatorname{Sym}^n M}\simeq\operatorname{Sym}^n(\widetilde M)$.
theorems.proof: Tensor constructions and their defining quotients commute with localization, giving the canonical comparison on stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Associated modules preserve exterior power
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let N be another module and let n be a nonnegative integer.
theorems.statement: $\widetilde{\bigwedge^n M}\simeq\bigwedge^n(\widetilde M)$.
theorems.proof: Tensor constructions and their defining quotients commute with localization, giving the canonical comparison on stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Internal Hom out of a finitely presented associated module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ commutative, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Assume M is finitely presented and take any R-module N.
theorems.statement: The internal sheaf Hom from $\widetilde M$ to $\widetilde N$ is canonically $\widetilde{\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)}$.
theorems.proof: A finite presentation computes Hom by a kernel of a map of finite products, which commutes with localization.

theorems.subject: affine-scheme-morphism
theorems.name: Affine pullback is extension of scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ correspond to a unital ring map $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: For an $R$-module $M$, pullback of $\widetilde M$ is naturally the sheaf of $S\otimes_R M$.
theorems.proof: For pullback use the extension-of-scalars adjunction. For direct image compute on principal opens of the target.

theorems.subject: affine-scheme-morphism
theorems.name: Affine direct image is restriction of scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ correspond to a unital ring map $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: For an $S$-module $N$, direct image of $\widetilde N$ is naturally the sheaf of $N$ viewed as an $R$-module.
theorems.proof: For pullback use the extension-of-scalars adjunction. For direct image compute on principal opens of the target.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine reconstruction of a quasi-coherent sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent module on $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: The canonical evaluation $\widetilde{\Gamma(X,F)}\to F$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: A presentation on a finite principal covering identifies restrictions with localizations of global sections.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-coherent modules on an affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: Global sections and association of a sheaf are quasi-inverse equivalences between $R$-modules and quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules.
theorems.proof: The unit of the adjunction is the principal-open calculation at 1 and the counit is affine reconstruction.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-coherence of a kernel
theorems.hypotheses: Take a map between two quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme.
theorems.statement: Its kernel in the ambient category of sheaves of modules is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Localization preserves kernels.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-coherence of a cokernel
theorems.hypotheses: Take a map between two quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme.
theorems.statement: Its cokernel in the ambient category of sheaves of modules is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Localization preserves cokernels.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-coherence of a direct sum
theorems.hypotheses: Take any set-indexed family of quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme.
theorems.statement: Its direct sum in the ambient category of sheaves of modules is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Localization commutes with arbitrary direct sums.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-coherence of a colimit
theorems.hypotheses: Take a small diagram of quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme.
theorems.statement: Its colimit in the ambient category of sheaves of modules is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Localization commutes with colimits, and the associated-sheaf functor is a left adjoint.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Two-out-of-three for quasi-coherence · term 3
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$ is exact in sheaves of modules on an affine scheme. Assume terms 1 and 2 are quasi-coherent.
theorems.statement: Term 3 is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Use the cokernel calculation for a map of quasi-coherent sheaves.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Two-out-of-three for quasi-coherence · term 1
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$ is exact in sheaves of modules on an affine scheme. Assume terms 2 and 3 are quasi-coherent.
theorems.statement: Term 1 is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Use the kernel calculation for a map of quasi-coherent sheaves.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Two-out-of-three for quasi-coherence · term 2
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$ is exact in sheaves of modules on an affine scheme. Assume terms 1 and 3 are quasi-coherent.
theorems.statement: Term 2 is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Local lifts of a global section of the quotient become compatible after clearing denominators on a finite principal cover. Exactness on global sections and the unit and counit identifications give the middle sheaf.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: A closed subspace of an affine spectrum is a quotient spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Take a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: There is an ideal $I$ with $Z\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.proof: On principal opens extend local generators of the kernel ideal. The resulting ideal sheaf is the localization of its global ideal, and its quotient gives the source.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: The ideal of a closed subspace is determined by its immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Take a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: Exactly one ideal $I\subset R$ gives this closed subscheme over $\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.proof: On principal opens extend local generators of the kernel ideal. The resulting ideal sheaf is the localization of its global ideal, and its quotient gives the source.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Scheme source of an open immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: For an open immersion of locally ringed spaces into X the source is a scheme.
theorems.proof: Around each point choose a principal open in an affine neighbourhood lying inside the specified open subset.
refs: Stacks 01IK · source of an open immersion

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Open subspaces of a scheme are schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: Every open subspace of X is a scheme.
theorems.proof: Around each point choose a principal open in an affine neighbourhood lying inside the specified open subset.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Scheme source of a closed immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Assume Z → X is a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces and X is a scheme.
theorems.statement: Z is a scheme.
theorems.proof: Restrict to an affine target chart and apply the quotient-spectrum description, where localization computes the kernel sheaf.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-coherent ideal of a closed immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Assume Z → X is a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces and X is a scheme.
theorems.statement: The kernel of the map from the target structure sheaf to the direct image of the source structure sheaf is a quasi-coherent ideal.
theorems.proof: Restrict to an affine target chart and apply the quotient-spectrum description, where localization computes the kernel sheaf.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed immersion on a target affine chart
theorems.hypotheses: Assume Z → X is a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces and X is a scheme.
theorems.statement: Over each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of X the map identifies with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ for an ideal $I$.
theorems.proof: Restrict to an affine target chart and apply the quotient-spectrum description, where localization computes the kernel sheaf.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Defining ideal on a target affine chart
theorems.hypotheses: Assume Z → X is a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces and X is a scheme.
theorems.statement: The restriction of the kernel to the chart is $\widetilde I$ for its defining ideal $I$.
theorems.proof: Restrict to an affine target chart and apply the quotient-spectrum description, where localization computes the kernel sheaf.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Local generation of ideal sheaves on schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be any scheme.
theorems.statement: An ideal sheaf is locally generated by sections exactly when it is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Use the previous affine description on an affine open cover. For the converse, a quasi-coherent ideal on an affine chart is generated by its global sections.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed subspaces of schemes are schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be any scheme.
theorems.statement: Every closed subspace of X associated to a locally generated ideal is a scheme.
theorems.proof: Use the previous affine description on an affine open cover. For the converse, a quasi-coherent ideal on an affine chart is generated by its global sections.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Generic point of an irreducible closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be any scheme with its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: Every nonempty irreducible closed subset has a generic point.
theorems.proof: Intersect an irreducible closed subset with an affine chart meeting it. There its prime defines a generic point. Density gives existence globally and the affine T₀ property gives uniqueness.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Uniqueness of a generic point
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be any scheme with its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: Each irreducible closed subset has at most one generic point.
theorems.proof: Intersect an irreducible closed subset with an affine chart meeting it. There its prime defines a generic point. Density gives existence globally and the affine T₀ property gives uniqueness.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Underlying spaces of schemes are sober
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be any scheme with its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: The underlying space is sober.
theorems.proof: Intersect an irreducible closed subset with an affine chart meeting it. There its prime defines a generic point. Density gives existence globally and the affine T₀ property gives uniqueness.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine opens form a basis
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any scheme X.
theorems.statement: For every open U and point x of U there is an affine open W with x in W and W contained in U.
theorems.proof: Intersect U with an affine chart and choose a principal open around x inside the intersection.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Local quasi-compactness of the underlying space
theorems.hypotheses: Fix any scheme X.
theorems.statement: Every point has a neighbourhood basis consisting of quasi-compact opens.
theorems.proof: Affine opens form a basis and every spectrum is quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Simultaneously principal affine neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $U,V$ be affine opens in a scheme and $x\in U\cap V$.
theorems.statement: There is an open neighbourhood of x that is principal in U and principal in V.
theorems.proof: First choose nested principal neighbourhoods around x in both charts. Clearing a power of a denominator expresses the smaller open as principal in the larger affine chart.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Simultaneously principal finite refinement
theorems.hypotheses: Choose an affine open cover of X and any affine open V.
theorems.statement: V admits a finite cover by opens which are principal in V and each principal in some member of the given cover.
theorems.proof: Choose simultaneous principal neighbourhoods pointwise, then extract a finite cover of V.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: An affine scheme is reduced exactly when its ring is reduced
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a ring $R$ and its spectrum.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is reduced precisely when $R$ is reduced.
theorems.proof: A reduced ring remains reduced on localization, and reducedness of a scheme applies in particular to its global functions.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Reduced closed subscheme on a closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let T be a closed subset of a scheme X.
theorems.statement: There exists a reduced closed subscheme whose underlying closed set is T.
theorems.proof: On affine charts take the radical ideal of the closed subset. These radical ideals are uniquely determined and agree on overlaps.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry I, Proposition 3.52, restricted to closed subsets

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Uniqueness of the reduced structure on closed support
theorems.hypotheses: Let T be a closed subset of a scheme X.
theorems.statement: There is exactly one such closed subscheme of X.
theorems.proof: On affine charts take the radical ideal of the closed subset. These radical ideals are uniquely determined and agree on overlaps.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry I, Proposition 3.52, restricted to closed subsets

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Factoring a map from a reduced source through a closed subscheme
theorems.hypotheses: Take a morphism f from a reduced scheme Y to a scheme X.
theorems.statement: For a closed subscheme Z of X, f factors through Z exactly when its set-theoretic image is contained in the underlying set of Z.
theorems.proof: Functions in the defining ideal pull back to sections vanishing in every residue field, hence to nilpotents on each affine chart of Y. Reducedness kills them.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Every map from a reduced source factors through the reduction
theorems.hypotheses: Take a morphism f from a reduced scheme Y to a scheme X.
theorems.statement: The map f factors through the closed immersion of the reduction of X.
theorems.proof: Functions in the defining ideal pull back to sections vanishing in every residue field, hence to nilpotents on each affine chart of Y. Reducedness kills them.
refs: M. Hoyois, Algebraic Geometry, Proposition 8.22, universal property of reduction

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Maps from a local spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be local and $X$ any scheme.
theorems.statement: Maps $\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ correspond to a point $x$ of $X$ and a local ring map $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to R$.
theorems.proof: The closed point determines x. Any affine neighbourhood of x pulls back to the entire source, and localization identifies the possible ring homomorphisms.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Image of a localization at a point
theorems.hypotheses: Fix points $x,x'$ in a scheme $X$.
theorems.statement: $x'$ generalizes $x$ precisely when it belongs to the image of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$.
theorems.proof: In an affine chart around x its generalizations correspond exactly to primes contained in the prime at x.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Underlying scheme points as equivalence classes of field-valued points
theorems.hypotheses: Field-valued morphisms to a scheme X are equivalent when they have a common refinement by a field-valued point. Domination means factorization over X.
theorems.statement: Taking the image point induces a bijection from the equivalence classes to points of X.
theorems.proof: A field-valued point is a point together with an embedding of its residue field. Any two such field extensions embed compatibly in a common field over that residue field.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Minimal field-valued representative of a point
theorems.hypotheses: Field-valued morphisms to a scheme X are equivalent when they have a common refinement by a field-valued point. Domination means factorization over X.
theorems.statement: The canonical $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ is a smallest representative under domination.
theorems.proof: A field-valued point is a point together with an embedding of its residue field. Any two such field extensions embed compatibly in a common field over that residue field.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Uniqueness of the minimal field-valued representative
theorems.hypotheses: Field-valued morphisms to a scheme X are equivalent when they have a common refinement by a field-valued point. Domination means factorization over X.
theorems.statement: The minimal representative is uniquely isomorphic to the residue-field representative over X.
theorems.proof: A field-valued point is a point together with an embedding of its residue field. Any two such field extensions embed compatibly in a common field over that residue field.
refs: Stacks 01J9 · uniqueness up to unique isomorphism

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Gluing locally ringed spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Take a set-indexed gluing datum on open subspaces of locally ringed spaces, with identity, overlap and cocycle conditions.
theorems.statement: There is a locally ringed space X with open embeddings of all pieces.
theorems.proof: Glue the topological spaces along the given identifications, then glue their sheaves of rings using the cocycle. The two mapping properties follow by restricting compatible sheaf maps to the charts.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Cover by the glued charts
theorems.hypotheses: Take a set-indexed gluing datum on open subspaces of locally ringed spaces, with identity, overlap and cocycle conditions.
theorems.statement: The images of the pieces cover X.
theorems.proof: Glue the topological spaces along the given identifications, then glue their sheaves of rings using the cocycle. The two mapping properties follow by restricting compatible sheaf maps to the charts.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Actual intersections of glued charts
theorems.hypotheses: Take a set-indexed gluing datum on open subspaces of locally ringed spaces, with identity, overlap and cocycle conditions.
theorems.statement: The image of the prescribed overlap in either chart is the intersection of the two charts in X.
theorems.proof: Glue the topological spaces along the given identifications, then glue their sheaves of rings using the cocycle. The two mapping properties follow by restricting compatible sheaf maps to the charts.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Transition identifications after gluing
theorems.hypotheses: Take a set-indexed gluing datum on open subspaces of locally ringed spaces, with identity, overlap and cocycle conditions.
theorems.statement: On each overlap, the composite of the first chart map with the inverse of the second chart map is the specified transition isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Glue the topological spaces along the given identifications, then glue their sheaves of rings using the cocycle. The two mapping properties follow by restricting compatible sheaf maps to the charts.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Maps out of a glued locally ringed space
theorems.hypotheses: Take a set-indexed gluing datum on open subspaces of locally ringed spaces, with identity, overlap and cocycle conditions.
theorems.statement: Morphisms X → Y are precisely families of morphisms on the pieces agreeing under all transitions.
theorems.proof: Glue the topological spaces along the given identifications, then glue their sheaves of rings using the cocycle. The two mapping properties follow by restricting compatible sheaf maps to the charts.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Maps into a glued locally ringed space
theorems.hypotheses: Take a set-indexed gluing datum on open subspaces of locally ringed spaces, with identity, overlap and cocycle conditions.
theorems.statement: Morphisms Y → X correspond to open covers indexed by the charts together with maps from the cover members to those charts. Each inverse image of a prescribed overlap must equal the corresponding intersection of cover members, and the maps must agree there via the transition.
theorems.proof: Glue the topological spaces along the given identifications, then glue their sheaves of rings using the cocycle. The two mapping properties follow by restricting compatible sheaf maps to the charts.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Gluing schemes along open subschemes
theorems.hypotheses: Take a set-indexed gluing datum on open subspaces of locally ringed spaces, with identity, overlap and cocycle conditions. Assume all pieces are schemes.
theorems.statement: The glued locally ringed space is a scheme.
theorems.proof: Every point lies in an open chart which itself has an affine neighbourhood at that point.

theorems.subject: scheme-presheaf
theorems.name: Representability from an open cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be a set-valued contravariant Zariski sheaf on schemes admitting a set-indexed cover by representable subfunctors whose inclusions are representable by open immersions.
theorems.statement: F is representable by a scheme.
theorems.proof: The pairwise intersections of the representing schemes are identified open subschemes satisfying the cocycle. Glue these schemes and use the sheaf axiom to identify their functor of points with F.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Terminal scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Work in the category of schemes.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ is terminal.
theorems.proof: Spec ℤ is terminal by the affine mapping property. The pullback functor is a Zariski sheaf covered by spectra of tensor products on compatible affine charts. A terminal object and pullbacks yield all finite limits.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Binary products in schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Work in the category of schemes.
theorems.statement: Any two schemes admit a product.
theorems.proof: Spec ℤ is terminal by the affine mapping property. The pullback functor is a Zariski sheaf covered by spectra of tensor products on compatible affine charts. A terminal object and pullbacks yield all finite limits.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Existence of scheme fibre products
theorems.hypotheses: Work in the category of schemes.
theorems.statement: Two scheme morphisms with a common target admit a fibre product.
theorems.proof: Spec ℤ is terminal by the affine mapping property. The pullback functor is a Zariski sheaf covered by spectra of tensor products on compatible affine charts. A terminal object and pullbacks yield all finite limits.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry I, Theorem 4.18, existence of scheme fibre products

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: All finite limits in schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Work in the category of schemes.
theorems.statement: Every finite diagram of schemes has a limit.
theorems.proof: Spec ℤ is terminal by the affine mapping property. The pullback functor is a Zariski sheaf covered by spectra of tensor products on compatible affine charts. A terminal object and pullbacks yield all finite limits.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Fibre product of affine schemes over an affine
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose both source schemes and the common target scheme are affine.
theorems.statement: Their fibre product is affine, with coordinate ring the tensor product over the coordinate ring of the base.
theorems.proof: Affine mapping duality identifies maps into that spectrum with pairs of maps agreeing over the base.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry I, Theorem 4.18, affine case

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Open chart in a fibre product
theorems.hypotheses: Given $X\to S\leftarrow Y$, take opens $U\subset S$, $V\subset X$, $W\subset Y$ such that both $V$ and $W$ map into $U$. Write $p,q$ for the projections.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $V\times_U W\to X\times_S Y$ is an open immersion.
theorems.proof: The two matching maps of a test scheme land in the indicated open intersection exactly when their projections factor through both open pieces.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Image of an open chart in a fibre product
theorems.hypotheses: Given $X\to S\leftarrow Y$, take opens $U\subset S$, $V\subset X$, $W\subset Y$ such that both $V$ and $W$ map into $U$. Write $p,q$ for the projections.
theorems.statement: Its image is $p^{-1}(V)\cap q^{-1}(W)$ with the open subscheme structure.
theorems.proof: The two matching maps of a test scheme land in the indicated open intersection exactly when their projections factor through both open pieces.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Assembling affine charts of a fibre product
theorems.hypotheses: Choose an affine open cover $(U_i)$ of $S$. Over each $U_i$ cover both inverse images in $X$ and $Y$ by affine opens $V_{ij},W_{ik}$.
theorems.statement: All $V_{ij}\times_{U_i}W_{ik}$ together form an affine open cover of $X\times_S Y$.
theorems.proof: Their images are intersections of inverse images of covering opens, and each tensor-product chart is affine.
refs: Görtz–Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry I, Theorem 4.18 and Corollary 4.19

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Points of a scheme fibre product
theorems.hypotheses: Fix morphisms $X\to S\leftarrow Y$ of schemes.
theorems.statement: Points above $(x,y)$ with common image $s$ are indexed by primes $\mathfrak p$ of $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y)$. These give all points.
theorems.proof: Field-valued points over a specified pair are represented by the spectrum of the tensor product of their residue fields.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Residue field of a point in a fibre product
theorems.hypotheses: Fix morphisms $X\to S\leftarrow Y$ of schemes.
theorems.statement: The residue field at the indexed point is canonically $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for the corresponding prime of the tensor product of residue fields.
theorems.proof: Field-valued points over a specified pair are represented by the spectrum of the tensor product of their residue fields.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Pullback of a closed immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Given $X\to S\leftarrow Y$, assume $X\to S$ is a closed immersion.
theorems.statement: The projection of the fibre product to Y is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: Pullbacks of open embeddings are open preimages and closed subspaces pull back by extending their ideals. Pull back a factorization for a general immersion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Pullback of a open immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Given $X\to S\leftarrow Y$, assume $X\to S$ is a open immersion.
theorems.statement: The projection of the fibre product to Y is a open immersion.
theorems.proof: Pullbacks of open embeddings are open preimages and closed subspaces pull back by extending their ideals. Pull back a factorization for a general immersion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Pullback of a immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Given $X\to S\leftarrow Y$, assume $X\to S$ is a immersion.
theorems.statement: The projection of the fibre product to Y is a immersion.
theorems.proof: Pullbacks of open embeddings are open preimages and closed subspaces pull back by extending their ideals. Pull back a factorization for a general immersion.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Ideal of a scheme-theoretic inverse image
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\hookrightarrow S$ be defined by a quasi-coherent ideal $I$ and $g:Y\to S$ any map of schemes.
theorems.statement: The ideal of $X\times_S Y$ in $Y$ is $\operatorname{im}(g^*I\to\mathcal O_Y)$.
theorems.proof: Affine locally this is the ideal generated by the image of the original ideal.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Base change over a common base preserves open immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be a open immersion over $S$ and let $S'\to S$ be any scheme morphism.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism $X_{S'}\to Y_{S'}$ is a open immersion.
theorems.proof: The relative base-change square is also the pullback square for the original morphism along the map of targets.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Base change over a common base preserves closed immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be a closed immersion over $S$ and let $S'\to S$ be any scheme morphism.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism $X_{S'}\to Y_{S'}$ is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: The relative base-change square is also the pullback square for the original morphism along the map of targets.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Base change over a common base preserves immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y$ be a immersion over $S$ and let $S'\to S$ be any scheme morphism.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism $X_{S'}\to Y_{S'}$ is a immersion.
theorems.proof: The relative base-change square is also the pullback square for the original morphism along the map of targets.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Topological pullback along the residue-field spectrum at s
theorems.hypotheses: Take a scheme morphism f from X to S, a point s in S, and its base change along the residue-field spectrum at s.
theorems.statement: The resulting square of underlying spaces is a pullback of topological spaces.
theorems.proof: Work on compatible affine charts and identify the prime spectra of the residue quotient or the localization.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Topological embedding along the residue-field spectrum at s
theorems.hypotheses: Take a scheme morphism f from X to S, a point s in S, and its base change along the residue-field spectrum at s.
theorems.statement: The projection into X is a homeomorphism onto the inverse image of the single point s with the subspace topology.
theorems.proof: The canonical lower map identifies its source homeomorphically with its image, and the topological square is Cartesian.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Topological pullback along the local-ring spectrum at s
theorems.hypotheses: Take a scheme morphism f from X to S, a point s in S, and its base change along the local-ring spectrum at s.
theorems.statement: The resulting square of underlying spaces is a pullback of topological spaces.
theorems.proof: Work on compatible affine charts and identify the prime spectra of the residue quotient or the localization.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Topological embedding along the local-ring spectrum at s
theorems.hypotheses: Take a scheme morphism f from X to S, a point s in S, and its base change along the local-ring spectrum at s.
theorems.statement: The projection into X is a homeomorphism onto the inverse image of the set of generalizations of s with the subspace topology.
theorems.proof: The canonical lower map identifies its source homeomorphically with its image, and the topological square is Cartesian.

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Local ring of a fibre as a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, take $x\in X$, set $s=f(x)$, and use the corresponding point of $X_s$.
theorems.statement: $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}\simeq\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{X,x}$.
theorems.proof: Use compatible affine charts, localize at x and quotient by the extended maximal ideal of the base stalk.

theorems.subject: scheme-morphism-point
theorems.name: Local ring of a fibre by residue-field extension
theorems.hypotheses: For $f:X\to S$, take $x\in X$, set $s=f(x)$, and use the corresponding point of $X_s$.
theorems.statement: $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}\simeq\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\kappa(s)$.
theorems.proof: Use compatible affine charts, localize at x and quotient by the extended maximal ideal of the base stalk.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Base change preserves quasi-compact scheme morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let f be a quasi-compact map of schemes over a base S and change the base by an arbitrary scheme morphism.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Over affine target charts choose finite affine covers of the source. The pulled-back charts give finite affine covers over compatible affine base charts.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Composition preserves quasi-compact scheme morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable quasi-compact scheme morphisms.
theorems.statement: Their composite is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Take the two inverse images of a quasi-compact open successively.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Realizing a specialization by a valuation ring
theorems.hypotheses: Take any specialization $s'\leadsto s$ in a scheme $S$.
theorems.statement: There is a map from a valuation spectrum sending its generic point to the first point of the specialization and its closed point to the second.
theorems.proof: Inside the chosen extension of $\kappa(s')$ take a valuation ring with that fraction field dominating the image of $\mathcal O_{S,s}$. The resulting local ring map realizes both points.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Realizing a specialization with prescribed generic residue extension
theorems.hypotheses: Take any specialization $s'\leadsto s$ in a scheme $S$.
theorems.statement: For any specified extension K of the residue field of the first point one can arrange that the generic residue extension is isomorphic to K over that residue field.
theorems.proof: Inside the chosen extension of $\kappa(s')$ take a valuation ring with that fraction field dominating the image of $\mathcal O_{S,s}$. The resulting local ring map realizes both points.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Diagonal of a morphism between affines
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a morphism of affine schemes.
theorems.statement: Its diagonal is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: Multiplication $B\otimes_A B\to B$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: The relative diagonal is an immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Take any map of schemes X → S.
theorems.statement: Its diagonal is an immersion.
theorems.proof: It factors as a closed immersion into the union of the affine chart squares U ×ᵥ U containing its image, followed by the open inclusion.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Largest locally closed agreement subscheme
theorems.hypotheses: Fix two parallel morphisms a,b from X to Y over a scheme S.
theorems.statement: There is a largest locally closed subscheme of X on which the two specified maps agree.
theorems.proof: Pull back the diagonal of Y over S along the pair (a,b). Its universal property gives the equalizer, and the diagonal is an immersion.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Universal property of the agreement subscheme
theorems.hypotheses: Fix two parallel morphisms a,b from X to Y over a scheme S.
theorems.statement: The agreement subscheme is the categorical equalizer of the two morphisms.
theorems.proof: Pull back the diagonal of Y over S along the pair (a,b). Its universal property gives the equalizer, and the diagonal is an immersion.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed equalizer for maps to a separated target
theorems.hypotheses: Take two morphisms from X to Y over S and assume Y is separated over S.
theorems.statement: Their equalizer is a closed subscheme of X.
theorems.proof: The equalizer is the base change of the closed diagonal of Y over S.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Affine intersections for a separated morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let f be separated, and let U and V be source affine opens mapping into one common affine open of its target.
theorems.statement: The intersection U ∩ V is affine.
theorems.proof: The overlap is the inverse image of the closed diagonal in an affine fibre-product chart. The absolute tensor ring surjects onto the relative tensor ring of that chart.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Tensor surjection on an affine overlap
theorems.hypotheses: Let f be separated, and let U and V be source affine opens mapping into one common affine open of its target.
theorems.statement: The map $\mathcal O_X(U)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U\cap V)$ taking a pure tensor to the product of the two restrictions is surjective.
theorems.proof: The overlap is the inverse image of the closed diagonal in an affine fibre-product chart. The absolute tensor ring surjects onto the relative tensor ring of that chart.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Chart criterion for separatedness
theorems.hypotheses: For every pair of source points over one target point choose affine neighbourhoods U and V mapping into one common target affine, whose intersection is affine and on which the tensor-product map of functions over ℤ onto the intersection is surjective.
theorems.statement: The morphism is separated.
theorems.proof: These products of neighbourhoods form an open cover of the relative square, and on each the diagonal is a closed immersion by the surjection onto the overlap ring.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Comparison of fibre products · an immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $X\to T\leftarrow Y$ and $T\to S$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $X\times_T Y\to X\times_S Y$ is an immersion.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Comparison of fibre products · a closed immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $X\to T\leftarrow Y$ and $T\to S$. Assume T → S is separated.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $X\times_T Y\to X\times_S Y$ is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Comparison of fibre products · quasi-compact
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $X\to T\leftarrow Y$ and $T\to S$. Assume T → S is quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $X\times_T Y\to X\times_S Y$ is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Graph of a morphism · an immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a morphism $X\to Y$ over $S$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $X\to X\times_S Y$ is an immersion.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Graph of a morphism · a closed immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a morphism $X\to Y$ over $S$. Assume Y → S is separated.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $X\to X\times_S Y$ is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Graph of a morphism · quasi-compact
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a morphism $X\to Y$ over $S$. Assume Y → S is quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $X\to X\times_S Y$ is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Section of a scheme morphism · an immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f:X\to S$ and a section $s:S\to X$ with $fs=\mathrm{id}_S$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $s:S\to X$ is an immersion.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Section of a scheme morphism · a closed immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f:X\to S$ and a section $s:S\to X$ with $fs=\mathrm{id}_S$. Assume X → S is separated.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $s:S\to X$ is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Section of a scheme morphism · quasi-compact
theorems.hypotheses: Fix $f:X\to S$ and a section $s:S\to X$ with $fs=\mathrm{id}_S$. Assume X → S is quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $s:S\to X$ is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Apply the appropriate property of the relative diagonal and its stability under pullback. The graph is the comparison with the identity of Y, and a section is the graph over its own source.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Separated morphisms under composition
theorems.hypotheses: Take two composable separated scheme morphisms.
theorems.statement: Their composite is separated.
theorems.proof: Factor its diagonal through the first diagonal followed by a pullback of the second.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Separated morphisms under base-change
theorems.hypotheses: Take a separated morphism over a base and any base change.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism is separated.
theorems.proof: The diagonal of the new morphism is a base change of the original diagonal.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Separated morphisms under product
theorems.hypotheses: Take two separated morphisms of schemes over a fixed base.
theorems.statement: The induced product morphism over the base is separated.
theorems.proof: Factor the product into two base changes and compose.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Cancellation of separatedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be composable and suppose $gf$ is separated.
theorems.statement: The first map f is separated.
theorems.proof: For separatedness restrict the closed diagonal of the composite to the relative square. For quasi-separatedness use affine neighbourhoods in Y mapped into a common target affine in Z and the affine-intersection criterion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-separated morphisms under composition
theorems.hypotheses: Take two composable quasi-separated scheme morphisms.
theorems.statement: Their composite is quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: Factor its diagonal through the first diagonal followed by a pullback of the second.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-separated morphisms under base-change
theorems.hypotheses: Take a quasi-separated morphism over a base and any base change.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism is quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: The diagonal of the new morphism is a base change of the original diagonal.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-separated morphisms under product
theorems.hypotheses: Take two quasi-separated morphisms of schemes over a fixed base.
theorems.statement: The induced product morphism over the base is quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: Factor the product into two base changes and compose.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Cancellation of quasi-separatedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be composable and suppose $gf$ is quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The first map f is quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: For separatedness restrict the closed diagonal of the composite to the relative square. For quasi-separatedness use affine neighbourhoods in Y mapped into a common target affine in Z and the affine-intersection criterion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-compact cancellation over a quasi-separated map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be scheme maps with $gf$ quasi-compact and $g$ quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The morphism f is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Factor f as its graph into the product over Z followed by projection to Y. The graph is quasi-compact by the quasi-separatedness of g and the projection is a pullback of gf.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Morphisms from an affine scheme are separated
theorems.hypotheses: Take any scheme morphism with affine source and arbitrary target.
theorems.statement: The morphism is separated.
theorems.proof: The composite structure morphism to Spec ℤ is separated, so cancellation gives separatedness of the first map.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine overlaps over a separated base
theorems.hypotheses: Assume X → S is separated, S is separated over Spec ℤ, and U,V are any two affine opens of X.
theorems.statement: The intersection U ∩ V is affine.
theorems.proof: X is separated over Spec ℤ by composition. Pull back its closed diagonal to the absolute product of the two affine opens.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed embedding of an overlap in the absolute product
theorems.hypotheses: Assume X → S is separated, S is separated over Spec ℤ, and U,V are any two affine opens of X.
theorems.statement: The natural map from U ∩ V into the product U × V over Spec ℤ is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: X is separated over Spec ℤ by composition. Pull back its closed diagonal to the absolute product of the two affine opens.
refs: Stacks 01KW · closed immersion into absolute product

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Composition of scheme monomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Take two composable monomorphisms of schemes.
theorems.statement: Their composite is a monomorphism.
theorems.proof: Postcomposition on test morphisms is the composite of two injections.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Base change of a scheme monomorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Take a monomorphism of schemes and an arbitrary base change.
theorems.statement: The induced morphism is a monomorphism.
theorems.proof: Its diagonal is the pullback of an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Locally closed subschemes of relatively separated schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let X → S be separated and let Z be a locally closed subscheme of X.
theorems.statement: The composite Z → S is separated.
theorems.proof: Its immersion into X is separated and separatedness is stable under composition.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Monomorphisms to a finite product of fields
theorems.hypotheses: Take a scheme monomorphism into the target Y described in each case.
theorems.statement: For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{i=1}^n k_i)$ with fields $k_i$, the source is the spectrum of the subproduct on a subset of the indices over $Y$.
theorems.proof: Work on the individual open-and-closed field components. A monomorphism to a field spectrum has at most one point. In the nonempty case its affine coordinate algebra has bijective multiplication on its tensor square and is the field itself.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Monomorphisms to disjoint unions of field spectra
theorems.hypotheses: Take a scheme monomorphism into the target Y described in each case.
theorems.statement: For $Y=\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ the source is the union of the components indexed by a subset, with the corresponding structures over $Y$.
theorems.proof: Work on the individual open-and-closed field components. A monomorphism to a field spectrum has at most one point. In the nonempty case its affine coordinate algebra has bijective multiplication on its tensor square and is the field itself.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Direct image of quasi-coherent modules along a qcqs morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.
theorems.statement: $f_*F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module.
theorems.proof: Over an affine target use a finite affine cover of the source and finite affine covers of their intersections. The sheaf equalizer is a kernel of a map between finite sums of affine direct images.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Composition of immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable morphisms of schemes, both of which are immersions.
theorems.statement: The composite is again a immersion.
theorems.proof: Open subspaces compose. For closed immersions use the closed-embedding and sheaf-surjectivity criterion, with exact direct image along the closed embedding. For general immersions restrict the target to suitable opens and compose the closed parts.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Composition of closed immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable morphisms of schemes, both of which are closed immersions.
theorems.statement: The composite is again a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: Open subspaces compose. For closed immersions use the closed-embedding and sheaf-surjectivity criterion, with exact direct image along the closed embedding. For general immersions restrict the target to suitable opens and compose the closed parts.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Composition of open immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Take composable morphisms of schemes, both of which are open immersions.
theorems.statement: The composite is again a open immersion.
theorems.proof: Open subspaces compose. For closed immersions use the closed-embedding and sheaf-surjectivity criterion, with exact direct image along the closed embedding. For general immersions restrict the target to suitable opens and compose the closed parts.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Stalks on an open subspace
theorems.hypotheses: Let U be an open subset of a locally ringed space X.
theorems.statement: The stalk at each point of the open subspace is canonically its stalk in the ambient space.
theorems.proof: Open neighbourhoods inside U are cofinal among neighbourhoods of its points in X.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Open restriction is locally ringed
theorems.hypotheses: Let U be an open subset of a locally ringed space X.
theorems.statement: The restricted structure sheaf has local stalks.
theorems.proof: Open neighbourhoods inside U are cofinal among neighbourhoods of its points in X.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Open subspace inclusion
theorems.hypotheses: Let U be an open subset of a locally ringed space X.
theorems.statement: The inclusion with the restricted sheaf is an open immersion.
theorems.proof: Open neighbourhoods inside U are cofinal among neighbourhoods of its points in X.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Closed support of a structure quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let I be a sheaf of ideals locally generated by sections on a locally ringed space X.
theorems.statement: The support Z of the quotient sheaf of rings by the ideal is a closed subset.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of the unit germ of a sheaf of rings is open. Restrict its quotient to the closed support and use the stalk description of direct image from a closed subspace.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: The structure sheaf on the support of a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let I be a sheaf of ideals locally generated by sections on a locally ringed space X.
theorems.statement: There is a unique sheaf of rings on Z, up to the canonical identification, whose direct image is the given quotient.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of the unit germ of a sheaf of rings is open. Restrict its quotient to the closed support and use the stalk description of direct image from a closed subspace.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Stalks of the induced closed structure
theorems.hypotheses: Let I be a sheaf of ideals locally generated by sections on a locally ringed space X.
theorems.statement: At a point of the support the stalk is the nonzero quotient of the ambient local ring by the stalk of the ideal, hence is local.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of the unit germ of a sheaf of rings is open. Restrict its quotient to the closed support and use the stalk description of direct image from a closed subspace.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Closed immersion defined by an ideal sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Let I be a sheaf of ideals locally generated by sections on a locally ringed space X.
theorems.statement: The resulting locally ringed morphism from Z into X is a closed immersion.
theorems.proof: Vanishing of the unit germ of a sheaf of rings is open. Restrict its quotient to the closed support and use the stalk description of direct image from a closed subspace.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Spectrum of a quotient as a closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a ring and I any ideal.
theorems.statement: The map $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a homeomorphism onto $V(I)$.
theorems.proof: Primes of the quotient correspond to primes containing I. Localizing the exact quotient sequence gives the description of stalks and ideals.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Stalk map from a quotient spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a ring and I any ideal.
theorems.statement: At $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ the stalk map is $R_{\mathfrak p}\to R_{\mathfrak p}/IR_{\mathfrak p}$.
theorems.proof: Primes of the quotient correspond to primes containing I. Localizing the exact quotient sequence gives the description of stalks and ideals.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed immersion from a quotient ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a ring and I any ideal.
theorems.statement: The quotient-spectrum map is a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces.
theorems.proof: Primes of the quotient correspond to primes containing I. Localizing the exact quotient sequence gives the description of stalks and ideals.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Associated ideal sheaf of a quotient spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a ring and I any ideal.
theorems.statement: It is the closed subspace associated to $\widetilde I$.
theorems.proof: Primes of the quotient correspond to primes containing I. Localizing the exact quotient sequence gives the description of stalks and ideals.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Two charts of the punctured plane
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $U=\mathbb A_k^2\setminus\{(x,y)\}$, where $(x,y)$ denotes the origin.
theorems.statement: $U=D(x)\cup D(y)$ with affine intersection $D(xy)$.
theorems.proof: Use the principal cover and its equalizer. Inside the fraction field a polynomial with only powers of x as denominators and only powers of y as denominators is already a polynomial.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Equalizer for functions on the punctured plane
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $U=\mathbb A_k^2\setminus\{(x,y)\}$, where $(x,y)$ denotes the origin.
theorems.statement: The functions on $U$ identify with pairs in $k[x,y]_x\times k[x,y]_y$ with equal images in $k[x,y]_{xy}$.
theorems.proof: Use the principal cover and its equalizer. Inside the fraction field a polynomial with only powers of x as denominators and only powers of y as denominators is already a polynomial.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Global functions on the punctured plane
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $U=\mathbb A_k^2\setminus\{(x,y)\}$, where $(x,y)$ denotes the origin.
theorems.statement: Restriction $k[x,y]\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Use the principal cover and its equalizer. Inside the fraction field a polynomial with only powers of x as denominators and only powers of y as denominators is already a polynomial.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Folding map for affine space with doubled origin
theorems.hypotheses: Over a field $k$, glue two copies of $\mathbb A^n_k$, $n\geq1$, along their punctured complements by the identity in coordinates.
theorems.statement: The coordinate identifications on the charts glue to a morphism to ordinary affine n-space.
theorems.proof: Since the two affine charts are identified on a dense open, their polynomial functions agree on the overlap exactly when the polynomials agree. The affinization map identifies the two origins.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Functions on affine space with doubled origin
theorems.hypotheses: Over a field $k$, glue two copies of $\mathbb A^n_k$, $n\geq1$, along their punctured complements by the identity in coordinates.
theorems.statement: Pullback along the folding map identifies the global functions with $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$.
theorems.proof: Since the two affine charts are identified on a dense open, their polynomial functions agree on the overlap exactly when the polynomials agree. The affinization map identifies the two origins.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: The two origins obstruct affineness
theorems.hypotheses: Over a field $k$, glue two copies of $\mathbb A^n_k$, $n\geq1$, along their punctured complements by the identity in coordinates.
theorems.statement: The glued scheme is nonaffine.
theorems.proof: Since the two affine charts are identified on a dense open, their polynomial functions agree on the overlap exactly when the polynomials agree. The affinization map identifies the two origins.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine opens with a nonaffine intersection
theorems.hypotheses: Over a field $k$, glue two copies of $\mathbb A^n_k$, $n\geq1$, along their punctured complements by the identity in coordinates. Assume n is at least two.
theorems.statement: The intersection of the two affine charts is nonaffine.
theorems.proof: Their overlap is punctured affine n-space. Computing functions on its standard cover gives the polynomial ring, and the canonical map to its spectrum omits the origin.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Irreducible closed subsets of doubled affine space
theorems.hypotheses: Over a field $k$, glue two copies of $\mathbb A^n_k$, $n\geq1$, along their punctured complements by the identity in coordinates. Assume n is at least two and take an irreducible closed subset different from either origin singleton.
theorems.statement: The subset contains one origin exactly when it contains both.
theorems.proof: Its generic point lies in the common complement of the two origins. Its closures in the two charts correspond under the coordinate identification.
refs: Stacks 01JD · origins in irreducible closed subsets

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: The projective line as a glued scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: The two affine lines are open charts of the resulting scheme with the specified transition.
theorems.proof: A polynomial in x that is a polynomial in its inverse is constant, and a spectrum of k has only one point. The change of projective coordinate s is fractional linear and sends 1 to infinity.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Global functions on the projective line
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: Its global regular functions are exactly k.
theorems.proof: A polynomial in x that is a polynomial in its inverse is constant, and a spectrum of k has only one point. The change of projective coordinate s is fractional linear and sends 1 to infinity.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: The projective line is nonaffine
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: The projective line is not affine.
theorems.proof: A polynomial in x that is a polynomial in its inverse is constant, and a spectrum of k has only one point. The change of projective coordinate s is fractional linear and sends 1 to infinity.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: A common affine neighbourhood of zero and infinity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: The complement of $x=1$ is affine, contains both $0$ and $\infty$, and has coordinate $s=1/(x-1)=y/(1-y)$.
theorems.proof: A polynomial in x that is a polynomial in its inverse is constant, and a spectrum of k has only one point. The change of projective coordinate s is fractional linear and sends 1 to infinity.
refs: Stacks 01JE · chart around zero and infinity

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Coordinate ring of the common neighbourhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: The complement of $1$ identifies with $\operatorname{Spec}k[s]$ via this coordinate; its section ring is $k[s]$.
theorems.proof: A polynomial in x that is a polynomial in its inverse is constant, and a spectrum of k has only one point. The change of projective coordinate s is fractional linear and sends 1 to infinity.

theorems.subject: scheme-presheaf
theorems.name: Global functions as a functor of test schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Take the functor assigning to a scheme the underlying set of its ring of global functions.
theorems.statement: Pullback of global functions defines a set-valued contravariant functor on schemes.
theorems.proof: Maps to an affine spectrum are ring maps into global sections. A map out of the polynomial ring is uniquely determined by the image of its variable.

theorems.subject: scheme-presheaf
theorems.name: The affine line represents global functions
theorems.hypotheses: Take the functor assigning to a scheme the underlying set of its ring of global functions.
theorems.statement: The spectrum of $\mathbb Z[x]$ represents the global-function functor.
theorems.proof: Maps to an affine spectrum are ring maps into global sections. A map out of the polynomial ring is uniquely determined by the image of its variable.

theorems.subject: scheme-presheaf
theorems.name: Universal regular function
theorems.hypotheses: Take the functor assigning to a scheme the underlying set of its ring of global functions.
theorems.statement: The universal section is the variable $x\in\mathbb Z[x]$.
theorems.proof: Maps to an affine spectrum are ring maps into global sections. A map out of the polynomial ring is uniquely determined by the image of its variable.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of the projective line over its field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: Its structure map is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Two affine charts give quasi-compactness. For the coordinate of a generic point in one chart, a valuation ring contains it or, when nonzero, its inverse. The chart so obtained gives a filler for the original square.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Valuative existence for the projective line
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: Its structure map satisfies valuative existence.
theorems.proof: Two affine charts give quasi-compactness. For the coordinate of a generic point in one chart, a valuation ring contains it or, when nonzero, its inverse. The chart so obtained gives a filler for the original square.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Universal closedness of the projective line
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: Its structure map is universally closed.
theorems.proof: Two affine charts give quasi-compactness. For the coordinate of a generic point in one chart, a valuation ring contains it or, when nonzero, its inverse. The chart so obtained gives a filler for the original square.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Failure of relative quasi-separatedness for doubled infinite-dimensional affine space
theorems.hypotheses: Over a field k, glue two copies of the spectrum of the polynomial ring in countably many variables along the complement of the origin.
theorems.statement: For the structure map to Spec k, the diagonal is not quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: The inverse image of the affine product of the two charts is their punctured intersection. The standard opens of the individual variables form a cover with no finite subcover.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Separatedness of the projective line
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and glue $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ along $D(x),D(y)$ by $xy=1$ to form $\mathbb P^1_k$.
theorems.statement: Its structure morphism to Spec k is separated.
theorems.proof: The intersection of its two charts is affine. Its Laurent polynomial coordinate ring is generated by the restrictions of functions from the two charts.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: An affine scheme surjecting onto the punctured plane
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $U=\mathbb A_k^2\setminus\{(x,y)\}$, where $(x,y)$ denotes the origin.
theorems.statement: The first-row map $\mathrm{GL}_{2,k}\to U$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: Every nonzero row over a residue field extends to an invertible matrix, and every projective field-valued point has a nonzero row representative. The punctured plane is nonaffine. Every map from the projective line to an affine factors through its global spectrum Spec k.
refs: Stacks 01KX · surjection onto the punctured plane

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: An affine source whose image fits in no affine target chart
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $U=\mathbb A_k^2\setminus\{(x,y)\}$, where $(x,y)$ denotes the origin.
theorems.statement: The image of the first-row map is contained in no affine open of U.
theorems.proof: Every nonzero row over a residue field extends to an invertible matrix, and every projective field-valued point has a nonzero row representative. The punctured plane is nonaffine. Every map from the projective line to an affine factors through its global spectrum Spec k.
refs: Stacks 01KX · image in no affine chart

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: An affine scheme surjecting onto the projective line
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $U=\mathbb A_k^2\setminus\{(x,y)\}$, where $(x,y)$ denotes the origin.
theorems.statement: The composite first-row and line map $\mathrm{GL}_{2,k}\to\mathbb P^1_k$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: Every nonzero row over a residue field extends to an invertible matrix, and every projective field-valued point has a nonzero row representative. The punctured plane is nonaffine. Every map from the projective line to an affine factors through its global spectrum Spec k.
refs: Stacks 01KX · surjection onto the projective line

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: No immersion of the projective line into an affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $U=\mathbb A_k^2\setminus\{(x,y)\}$, where $(x,y)$ denotes the origin.
theorems.statement: The projective line over k does not immerse into any affine scheme.
theorems.proof: Every nonzero row over a residue field extends to an invertible matrix, and every projective field-valued point has a nonzero row representative. The punctured plane is nonaffine. Every map from the projective line to an affine factors through its global spectrum Spec k.
refs: Stacks 01KX · no immersion into an affine

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Q\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ is monic
theorems.hypotheses: Use the canonical localization at the indicated point.
theorems.statement: The canonical inclusion of the rational generic point of Spec ℤ is a monomorphism.
theorems.proof: Localization is an epimorphism of rings because its tensor square over the original ring identifies with the localization. Work on an affine neighbourhood and compose with its open immersion.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Local scheme at a point maps monomorphically to the scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Use the canonical localization at the indicated point.
theorems.statement: For every scheme S and point s, the canonical map from the spectrum of its local ring at s to S is a monomorphism.
theorems.proof: Localization is an epimorphism of rings because its tensor square over the original ring identifies with the localization. Work on an affine neighbourhood and compose with its open immersion.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Representability on all locally ringed test objects
