theorems.hypotheses: Let F be a contravariant set-valued functor on all locally ringed spaces satisfying Zariski gluing there. Assume it has a set-indexed covering by subfunctors represented by schemes whose inclusions are representable by open immersions for every locally ringed test object.
theorems.statement: F is representable on locally ringed spaces.
theorems.proof: Glue the representing schemes along the open intersections specified by the subfunctors. The gluing property on all locally ringed test spaces proves representability there.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Scheme representing a functor on locally ringed spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be a contravariant set-valued functor on all locally ringed spaces satisfying Zariski gluing there. Assume it has a set-indexed covering by subfunctors represented by schemes whose inclusions are representable by open immersions for every locally ringed test object.
theorems.statement: The representing locally ringed space is a scheme.
theorems.proof: Glue the representing schemes along the open intersections specified by the subfunctors. The gluing property on all locally ringed test spaces proves representability there.

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Fibre product of schemes represents all locally ringed test objects
theorems.hypotheses: Take a diagram of schemes with two maps to a common scheme.
theorems.statement: A fibre product of the diagram exists in locally ringed spaces.
theorems.proof: Use the analogous representability test on locally ringed spaces, with tensor-product spectra for the affine open pieces.
refs: Stacks 01JN · existence in locally ringed spaces

theorems.subject: locally-ringed-space
theorems.name: Agreement of scheme and locally ringed fibre products
theorems.hypotheses: Take a diagram of schemes with two maps to a common scheme.
theorems.statement: The resulting locally ringed space is a scheme, giving the scheme fibre product.
theorems.proof: Use the analogous representability test on locally ringed spaces, with tensor-product spectra for the affine open pieces.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine schemes are quasi-separated
theorems.hypotheses: Take any affine scheme.
theorems.statement: It is quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: Every affine scheme is quasi-compact and its absolute diagonal is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Absolute and relative quasi-separated conditions over a fixed target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $Y$ quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The morphism f is quasi-separated exactly when X is quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: Apply composition with the structure morphism of Y in one direction and the appropriate cancellation theorem in the other.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Fibre products of quasi-separated schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y\leftarrow Z$ be two morphisms and suppose $X,Y,Z$ are all quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The fibre product over Y is quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: The projection is a base change of a relative morphism with the stated property. Compose with the structure morphism of the other factor.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine schemes are separated
theorems.hypotheses: Take any affine scheme.
theorems.statement: It is separated.
theorems.proof: Every affine scheme is quasi-compact and its absolute diagonal is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Absolute and relative separated conditions over a fixed target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $Y$ separated.
theorems.statement: The morphism f is separated exactly when X is separated.
theorems.proof: Apply composition with the structure morphism of Y in one direction and the appropriate cancellation theorem in the other.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Fibre products of separated schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y\leftarrow Z$ be two morphisms and suppose $X,Y,Z$ are all separated.
theorems.statement: The fibre product over Y is separated.
theorems.proof: The projection is a base change of a relative morphism with the stated property. Compose with the structure morphism of the other factor.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated
theorems.hypotheses: Take any affine scheme.
theorems.statement: It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: Every affine scheme is quasi-compact and its absolute diagonal is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Absolute and relative quasi-compact and quasi-separated conditions over a fixed target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The morphism f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated exactly when X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: Apply composition with the structure morphism of Y in one direction and the appropriate cancellation theorem in the other.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Fibre products of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y\leftarrow Z$ be two morphisms and suppose $X,Y,Z$ are all quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: The fibre product over Y is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
theorems.proof: The projection is a base change of a relative morphism with the stated property. Compose with the structure morphism of the other factor.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine schemes are quasi-compact and separated
theorems.hypotheses: Take any affine scheme.
theorems.statement: It is quasi-compact and separated.
theorems.proof: Every affine scheme is quasi-compact and its absolute diagonal is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: morphism
theorems.name: Absolute and relative quasi-compact and separated conditions over a fixed target
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $Y$ quasi-compact and separated.
theorems.statement: The morphism f is quasi-compact and separated exactly when X is quasi-compact and separated.
theorems.proof: Apply composition with the structure morphism of Y in one direction and the appropriate cancellation theorem in the other.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Fibre products of quasi-compact and separated schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X\to Y\leftarrow Z$ be two morphisms and suppose $X,Y,Z$ are all quasi-compact and separated.
theorems.statement: The fibre product over Y is quasi-compact and separated.
theorems.proof: The projection is a base change of a relative morphism with the stated property. Compose with the structure morphism of the other factor.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Kernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules on a scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Take an arbitrary scheme X and a morphism of quasi-coherent modules on X.
theorems.statement: The kernel in the category of sheaves of modules on X is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Restrict to every affine open chart and apply the affine kernel theorem. Quasi-coherence is local on the source.
refs: Stacks 01LB · kernel remark for arbitrary schemes

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Cokernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules on a scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Take an arbitrary scheme X and a morphism of quasi-coherent modules on X.
theorems.statement: The cokernel in the category of sheaves of modules on X is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: Open restriction preserves cokernels. On every affine chart the cokernel is the sheaf associated to the cokernel of the corresponding map of modules.

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: Testing local constructibility on affine opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let E be a subset of a scheme X.
theorems.statement: E is locally constructible precisely when its intersection with every affine open U is constructible in U.
theorems.proof: On an affine chart, constructibility can be checked on a finite cover by principal opens.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA I, second edition, Chapter 0, §2.3, constructible subsets

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: A generic point inside a constructible set
theorems.hypotheses: Let E be locally constructible in X and let ξ be the generic point of an irreducible component of X.
theorems.statement: If ξ belongs to E, some open neighbourhood of ξ is contained in E.
theorems.proof: Work on an affine neighbourhood and write a constructible set as a finite Boolean combination of quasi-compact opens. Apply the same argument to its complement.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA I, second edition, Chapter 0, §2.3, constructible subsets

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: A generic point outside a constructible set
theorems.hypotheses: Let E be locally constructible in X and let ξ be the generic point of an irreducible component of X.
theorems.statement: If ξ is outside E, some open neighbourhood of ξ misses E.
theorems.proof: Work on an affine neighbourhood and write a constructible set as a finite Boolean combination of quasi-compact opens. Apply the same argument to its complement.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA I, second edition, Chapter 0, §2.3, constructible subsets

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Intersection of quasi-compact opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme.
theorems.statement: The intersection of any two quasi-compact opens of X is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Pull back a product of quasi-compact opens by the quasi-compact diagonal.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Retrocompactness of quasi-compact opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme.
theorems.statement: Each quasi-compact open of X has quasi-compact intersection with every quasi-compact open of X.
theorems.proof: Pull back a product of quasi-compact opens by the quasi-compact diagonal.

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: Constructibility on a qcqs scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let E be locally constructible on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme X.
theorems.statement: E is constructible in X.
theorems.proof: Use a finite cover by retrocompact affine opens and glue constructibility.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA I, second edition, Chapter 0, §2.3, constructible subsets

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: Testing retrocompactness on affines
theorems.hypotheses: Let E be a subset of a scheme X.
theorems.statement: E is retrocompact precisely when its intersection with every affine open of X is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Every quasi-compact open is a finite union of affines.

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: Local finiteness of a retrocompact partition
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose the parts of a partition of a scheme X are retrocompact in X.
theorems.statement: The partition is locally finite precisely when each part is locally constructible.
theorems.proof: On an affine chart a locally finite partition is finite. In the converse use compactness in the constructible topology.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Reduced affine cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is reduced iff it admits an affine open cover with all section rings reduced.
theorems.proof: Nilpotence can be detected on stalks. On an affine open, stalks are the prime localizations of its section ring.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Reduced rings on every affine
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is reduced iff every affine open has reduced section ring.
theorems.proof: Nilpotence can be detected on stalks. On an affine open, stalks are the prime localizations of its section ring.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Reduced rings on every open
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is reduced iff all open subsets have reduced section rings.
theorems.proof: Nilpotence can be detected on stalks. On an affine open, stalks are the prime localizations of its section ring.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Overlapping irreducible affine charts
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is irreducible iff it has a nonempty affine covering by irreducible charts with every pair intersecting.
theorems.proof: Irreducibility means nonemptiness and intersection of any two nonempty opens. This criterion can be tested using an affine basis.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Irreducibility on every affine open
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is irreducible iff X is nonempty and each nonempty affine open of X is irreducible.
theorems.proof: Irreducibility means nonemptiness and intersection of any two nonempty opens. This criterion can be tested using an affine basis.

theorems.subject: scheme-ring-property
theorems.name: All affine charts for locally P
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a Zariski-local ring predicate P and a scheme X.
theorems.statement: X is locally P iff the coordinate ring of every affine open is a ring satisfying P.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme-ring-property
theorems.name: An affine covering for locally P
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a Zariski-local ring predicate P and a scheme X.
theorems.statement: X is locally P iff it has an affine open cover with all coordinate rings a ring satisfying P.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme-ring-property
theorems.name: Zariski descent of locally P
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a Zariski-local ring predicate P and a scheme X.
theorems.statement: X is locally P iff it has an open cover by locally P open subschemes.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme-ring-property
theorems.name: Open restriction of locally P
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a Zariski-local ring predicate P and a scheme X.
theorems.statement: If X is locally P, then each open subscheme is locally P.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Reducedness is affine-local
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is reduced precisely when each point has an affine neighbourhood whose ring is reduced.
theorems.proof: A reduced ring has reduced localizations and nilpotence is detected locally.

theorems.subject: ring-predicate
theorems.name: Locality of Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay rings
theorems.hypotheses: The ring predicate is evaluated on commutative rings.
theorems.statement: Being Noetherian and Cohen–Macaulay is a local property.
theorems.proof: Localizations preserve the property, and a finite principal cover permits descent.

theorems.subject: ring-predicate
theorems.name: Locality of Noetherian regular rings
theorems.hypotheses: The ring predicate is evaluated on commutative rings.
theorems.statement: Being Noetherian and regular is a local property.
theorems.proof: Localizations preserve the property, and a finite principal cover permits descent.

theorems.subject: ring-predicate
theorems.name: Locality of finite type over the integers
theorems.hypotheses: The ring predicate is evaluated on commutative rings.

theorems.proof: Localizations preserve the property, and a finite principal cover permits descent.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: All affine charts for locally Noetherian
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is locally Noetherian iff the coordinate ring of every affine open is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: An affine covering for locally Noetherian
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is locally Noetherian iff it has an affine open cover with all coordinate rings Noetherian.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Zariski descent of locally Noetherian
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is locally Noetherian iff it has an open cover by locally Noetherian open subschemes.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Open restriction of locally Noetherian
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: If X is locally Noetherian, then each open subscheme is locally Noetherian.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of immersions into locally Noetherian schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let Z → X be an immersion with X locally Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The immersion is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: In a Noetherian affine open of X every subspace is Noetherian and therefore quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Locally Noetherian underlying topology
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: The space of X is locally Noetherian.
theorems.proof: The affine charts of X can be taken to be spectra of Noetherian rings.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Inheritance of locally Noetherian by an immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Let Z be a locally closed subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme X.
theorems.statement: Z is locally Noetherian.
theorems.proof: A quotient of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, and in the global case the subspace is quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Inheritance of Noetherian by an immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Let Z be a locally closed subscheme of a Noetherian scheme X.
theorems.statement: Z is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: A quotient of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, and in the global case the subspace is quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Finiteness of irreducible components
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: X has finitely many irreducible components.
theorems.proof: Apply Noetherian induction to the underlying space.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Maps with Noetherian source are quasi-compact
theorems.hypotheses: Let X → Y be a scheme morphism with X Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The morphism is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: Each inverse image of an affine open of Y is an open in a Noetherian space.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed point in a nonempty scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: If X is nonempty, it contains a closed point.
theorems.proof: Specialize inside closed subsets. Nonempty locally Noetherian schemes have a closed point, as seen by using a Noetherian affine neighbourhood and minimal closed subsets.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed point in a nonempty closed subset
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: Every nonempty closed subset contains a point closed in X.
theorems.proof: Specialize inside closed subsets. Nonempty locally Noetherian schemes have a closed point, as seen by using a Noetherian affine neighbourhood and minimal closed subsets.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Specialization to a closed point
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: Every point specializes to a point closed in X.
theorems.proof: Specialize inside closed subsets. Nonempty locally Noetherian schemes have a closed point, as seen by using a Noetherian affine neighbourhood and minimal closed subsets.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Realizing a specialization by a trait
theorems.hypotheses: Let x′ specialize to x in a locally Noetherian scheme X.
theorems.statement: There is a map from the spectrum of a DVR with generic image x′ and closed image x.
theorems.proof: Use a DVR dominating the appropriate local domain in the closure of x′. In the nonconstant case use a DVR with the prescribed extension of fraction fields.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Prescribing the generic field of the trait
theorems.hypotheses: Let x′ specialize to x in a locally Noetherian scheme X.
theorems.statement: If x′ differs from x, any given finitely generated extension of κ(x′) may be realized as the induced extension at the generic point.
theorems.proof: Use a DVR dominating the appropriate local domain in the closure of x′. In the nonconstant case use a DVR with the prescribed extension of fraction fields.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Infinite antichains of points
theorems.hypotheses: Let T be an infinite subset of a Noetherian scheme S.
theorems.statement: T contains an infinite subset whose distinct points are incomparable under specialization.
theorems.proof: Stratify by successive maximal specializations. Finite chains at a fixed endpoint have length bounded by the dimension of its Noetherian local ring.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Incomparability of maximal generalizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let T be a subset of a Noetherian scheme S. Let M consist of points of T with no distinct generalization in T. The proof uses T here, correcting the undefined T′ in the printed statement.
theorems.statement: Distinct points of M are incomparable under specialization.
theorems.proof: A strict generalization decreases the finite dimension of the local ring. Minimize this dimension among generalizations in T.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Specialization from maximal generalizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let T be a subset of a Noetherian scheme S. Let M consist of points of T with no distinct generalization in T. The proof uses T here, correcting the undefined T′ in the printed statement.
theorems.statement: Each point of T specializes from a point of M.
theorems.proof: A strict generalization decreases the finite dimension of the local ring. Minimize this dimension among generalizations in T.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closure of maximal generalizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let T be a subset of a Noetherian scheme S. Let M consist of points of T with no distinct generalization in T. The proof uses T here, correcting the undefined T′ in the printed statement.
theorems.statement: M and T have the same closure.
theorems.proof: A strict generalization decreases the finite dimension of the local ring. Minimize this dimension among generalizations in T.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Countable dense subsets inside dense sets
theorems.hypotheses: Let T be an infinite dense subset of a Noetherian scheme S.
theorems.statement: There is a countable subset of T dense in S.
theorems.proof: Apply the maximal-generalizations lemma to closures of countable subsets and use finite irreducible decomposition.
refs: Stacks 0G2F · existence of a countable dense subset

theorems.proof: The Jacobson property of a space is local, and the affine criterion identifies it on spectra.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Jacobson property of Spec R minus its closed point
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose R is Noetherian local with closed point m.
theorems.statement: The scheme Spec R minus its closed point is Noetherian and Jacobson.
theorems.proof: Use the Jacobson property for the specified open of a Noetherian spectrum. In the Zariski-pair case I is contained in the Jacobson radical.

theorems.name: Normality on integral affine charts

theorems.statement: Normality is equivalent to integral closedness of the coordinate domain on every nonempty affine open.
theorems.proof: Normality of a domain is detected on its prime localizations.
refs: Stacks 033L · equivalence on nonempty affine opens

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Component decomposition of a normal scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose each quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components.
theorems.statement: X is normal iff it is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes.
theorems.proof: Normal local domains force distinct components to be disjoint. Local finiteness makes each component open, and Noetherianity gives global finiteness in the finite case.

theorems.hypotheses: Suppose X is Noetherian.

theorems.proof: Normal local domains force distinct components to be disjoint. Local finiteness makes each component open, and Noetherianity gives global finiteness in the finite case.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Connectedness detects integrality under local Noetherianity
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be nonempty, normal and locally Noetherian.
theorems.statement: X is integral iff X is connected.
theorems.proof: The normal integral components are open and closed. With nonemptiness, connectedness means precisely one component.
refs: Stacks 033O · first assertion (nonempty convention made explicit)

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Global functions on a normal integral scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be normal and integral.
theorems.statement: Its global section ring is a normal domain.
theorems.proof: Embed the ring in the function field as the intersection of the local rings. Each is an integrally closed domain.
refs: Stacks 0358 · normality and integrality of the ring of global sections

theorems.name: All stalks for Cohen–Macaulay
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is Cohen–Macaulay iff X is locally Noetherian and the local ring is Cohen–Macaulay at every point.
theorems.proof: In a locally Noetherian scheme every point specializes to a closed point. Localizing the closed-point condition gives the corresponding condition at any generalization.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Dimension from the local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: The dimension of X is the supremum of the Krull dimensions of its local rings.
theorems.proof: Chains of irreducible closed subsets through a chosen specialization correspond on an affine chart to chains of prime ideals in its local ring. Take suprema over all points.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Dimension from neighbourhood dimensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: The dimension of X is the supremum of the dimensions of X at its points.
theorems.proof: Chains of irreducible closed subsets through a chosen specialization correspond on an affine chart to chains of prime ideals in its local ring. Take suprema over all points.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Codimension at a generic point
theorems.hypotheses: Let Y be an irreducible closed subset of X with generic point ξ.
theorems.statement: The codimension of Y in X is the Krull dimension of the local ring at ξ.
theorems.proof: Chains of irreducible closed sets containing Y correspond to chains of primes in the local ring at ξ.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Generic points detected by dimension zero
theorems.hypotheses: Let x be a point of X.
theorems.statement: x is generic in an irreducible component iff its local ring has Krull dimension zero.
theorems.proof: Codimension zero means the closure of x is maximal among irreducible closed subsets.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Decomposition of locally Noetherian zero-dimensional schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be locally Noetherian of dimension zero.
theorems.statement: X is a disjoint union of spectra of Artinian local rings.
theorems.proof: Affine Noetherian rings of dimension zero are Artinian and decompose into local factors. Each singleton is open.
refs: Stacks 0AAX · disjoint union of local Artinian spectra

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Singleton components in dimension zero
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be zero-dimensional and quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: Every connected component is a point.
theorems.proof: Affine opens are closed. A quasi-compact open is a finite disjoint union of affine clopen pieces.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-compact opens in dimension zero
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be zero-dimensional and quasi-separated.
theorems.statement: Every quasi-compact open of X is affine.
theorems.proof: Affine opens are closed. A quasi-compact open is a finite disjoint union of affine clopen pieces.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Isolated points and neighbourhood dimension
theorems.hypotheses: Let x belong to a locally Noetherian scheme X.
theorems.statement: The dimension of X at x is zero iff x is isolated in X.
theorems.proof: A zero-dimensional Noetherian affine neighbourhood is a finite discrete space. Conversely use the singleton neighbourhood.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Open descent of catenarity
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is catenary iff X has an open covering by catenary schemes.
theorems.proof: Codimension chains can be studied in any open neighbourhood of the generic point of their smallest member. On affines they are chains of primes.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Local dimension functions on a catenary scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: X is catenary iff X admits a dimension function Zariski-locally.
theorems.proof: Use the correspondence between catenarity and local dimension functions on the underlying locally Noetherian sober space.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Catenarity detected by local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is catenary iff every local ring of X is catenary.
theorems.proof: Any interval of primes of an affine chart occurs in the local ring at its upper endpoint.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: All Serre R conditions characterize regular
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: X is regular iff it satisfies (Rₖ) for every integer k ≥ 0.
theorems.proof: Each Noetherian local ring has finite dimension. At each point take k equal to that dimension.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: All Serre S conditions characterize Cohen–Macaulay

theorems.statement: X is Cohen–Macaulay iff it satisfies (Sₖ) for every integer k ≥ 0.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Serre criterion for reduced schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: X is reduced iff it satisfies both (S₁) and (R₀).
theorems.proof: Apply the corresponding Serre criterion for Noetherian rings on affine opens.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Serre criterion for normal schemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: X is normal iff it satisfies both (S₂) and (R₁).
theorems.proof: Apply the corresponding Serre criterion for Noetherian rings on affine opens.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Normal schemes of dimension at most 1
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be normal, locally Noetherian and of dimension at most 1.
theorems.statement: X is regular.
theorems.proof: Normality gives (R₁) and (S₂). With the dimension bound the relevant condition holds up to the full dimension at each point.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Normal schemes of dimension at most 2
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be normal, locally Noetherian and of dimension at most 2.
theorems.statement: X is Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.proof: Normality gives (R₁) and (S₂). With the dimension bound the relevant condition holds up to the full dimension at each point.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Japanese stalks need not give a Japanese scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Consider the one-dimensional Noetherian domain cited in 033T, whose local rings are excellent and whose normalization is not finite.
theorems.statement: All its local rings are Japanese, whereas its spectrum is not Japanese.
theorems.proof: If this integral affine spectrum were Japanese then its coordinate domain would be Japanese and in particular its normalization would be finite.
refs: Stacks 033T · counterexample to the local-ring test

theorems.statement: Hoobler tests Japanese quotients by those associated primes. A different possible convention would test associated-prime quotients on all affine opens.
theorems.proof: The remark distinguishes the two conventions via the cited example of nonfinite normalization.
refs: Stacks 033T · terminology and proposed affine criterion
