theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Open restriction of Nagata
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: If X is Nagata, then each open subscheme is Nagata.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Testing the Nagata property on integral closed subschemes
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: X is Nagata iff each integral closed subscheme of X is Japanese.
theorems.proof: Use the criterion that all prime quotients of a Noetherian affine coordinate ring be Japanese.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: All stalks for a G-scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is a G-scheme iff X is locally Noetherian and the map from the local ring to its maximal-ideal completion is regular at every point.
theorems.proof: In a locally Noetherian scheme every point specializes to a closed point. Localizing the closed-point condition gives the corresponding condition at any generalization.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Closed-point test for a G-scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is a G-scheme iff X is locally Noetherian and the map from the local ring to its maximal-ideal completion is regular at every closed point.
theorems.proof: In a locally Noetherian scheme every point specializes to a closed point. Localizing the closed-point condition gives the corresponding condition at any generalization.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: All affine charts for a G-scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is a G-scheme iff the coordinate ring of every affine open is a G-ring.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: An affine covering for a G-scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is a G-scheme iff it has an affine open cover with all coordinate rings a G-ring.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Zariski descent of a G-scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is a G-scheme iff it has an open cover by a G-scheme open subschemes.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Open restriction of a G-scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: If X is a G-scheme, then each open subscheme is a G-scheme.
theorems.proof: The affine criterion follows by refinement with principal opens and descent of the stated ring property on finite principal covers.

theorems.subject: scheme-point
theorems.name: Branch sum over irreducible components
theorems.hypotheses: Fix x in X. Give each irreducible component through x its reduced induced structure.
theorems.statement: The branch count at x is the sum of the corresponding counts for these components.
theorems.proof: For finitely many minimal primes, normalize componentwise in the product of their fraction fields. Infinitely many components force an infinite count.

theorems.subject: scheme-point
theorems.name: A single branch
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a point x of a scheme X.
theorems.statement: The branch count is one iff X is unibranch at x.
theorems.proof: Apply the local-ring criterion to the henselization.

theorems.subject: scheme-point
theorems.name: Branch sum over irreducible components (geometric)
theorems.hypotheses: Fix x in X. Give each irreducible component through x its reduced induced structure.
theorems.statement: The geometric branch count at x is the sum of the corresponding counts for these components.
theorems.proof: For finitely many minimal primes, normalize componentwise in the product of their fraction fields. Infinitely many components force an infinite count.

theorems.subject: scheme-point
theorems.name: A single geometric branch
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a point x of a scheme X.
theorems.statement: The geometric branch count is one iff X is geometrically unibranch at x.
theorems.proof: Apply the local-ring criterion to the strict henselization.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Geometric unibranchness and punctured strict henselizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a Noetherian scheme.
theorems.statement: X is geometrically unibranch iff, at every point other than a generic point of an irreducible component, the punctured spectrum of the strict henselization is connected.
theorems.proof: Induct on local dimension. Distinct minimal primes would separate the punctured spectrum once its nonclosed stalks have unique minimal primes.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Finite generation on an affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X = Spec A, let M be an A-module and let F be its associated quasi-coherent sheaf.
theorems.statement: F is of finite type iff M is of finite type.
theorems.proof: Use principal affine trivializations and localization of M at a prime to compute its stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Finite presentation on an affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X = Spec A, let M be an A-module and let F be its associated quasi-coherent sheaf.
theorems.statement: F is of finite presentation iff M is of finite presentation.
theorems.proof: Use principal affine trivializations and localization of M at a prime to compute its stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Flatness on an affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X = Spec A, let M be an A-module and let F be its associated quasi-coherent sheaf.
theorems.statement: F is flat iff M is flat.
theorems.proof: Use principal affine trivializations and localization of M at a prime to compute its stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Local freeness on an affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X = Spec A, let M be an A-module and let F be its associated quasi-coherent sheaf.
theorems.statement: F is locally free iff M is locally free.
theorems.proof: Use principal affine trivializations and localization of M at a prime to compute its stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Finite local freeness on an affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X = Spec A, let M be an A-module and let F be its associated quasi-coherent sheaf.
theorems.statement: F is finite locally free iff M is finite locally free.
theorems.proof: Use principal affine trivializations and localization of M at a prime to compute its stalks.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Functions on a principal open
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be qcqs, let f be a global function and let X_f be its invertibility locus.
theorems.statement: The global function ring localized at f maps isomorphically to the ring of functions on X_f.
theorems.proof: Push forward to the affine spectrum of global functions. The pushforward is quasi-coherent and sections of a quasi-coherent sheaf on a principal affine open are obtained by localization.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Quasi-coherent sections on a principal open
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be qcqs, let f be a global function and let X_f be its invertibility locus.
theorems.statement: For every quasi-coherent F, localization of its module of global sections at f maps isomorphically to its sections over X_f.
theorems.proof: Push forward to the affine spectrum of global functions. The pushforward is quasi-coherent and sections of a quasi-coherent sheaf on a principal affine open are obtained by localization.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Injectivity after inverting a section
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, s a global section and X_s its nonvanishing open. Let F be quasi-coherent and localize its graded module of twisted global sections at s, taking the degree-zero part.
theorems.statement: If X is quasi-compact, the restriction map from the degree-zero localization to Γ(X_s,F) is injective.
theorems.proof: Trivialize L on affine charts. A finite cover gives a uniform exponent for annihilation. Quasi-separatedness permits a finite gluing argument on the overlaps.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA I, second edition, §6.8, localization by a section

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Recovering sections by inverting an invertible-sheaf section
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, s a global section and X_s its nonvanishing open. Let F be quasi-coherent and localize its graded module of twisted global sections at s, taking the degree-zero part.
theorems.statement: If X is qcqs, the same map is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Trivialize L on affine charts. A finite cover gives a uniform exponent for annihilation. Quasi-separatedness permits a finite gluing argument on the overlaps.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA I, second edition, §6.8, localization by a section

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Degree-zero localization of the section ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, s a global section and X_s its nonvanishing open. Let F be quasi-coherent and localize its graded module of twisted global sections at s, taking the degree-zero part.
theorems.statement: If X is qcqs, degree-zero localization of the section ring at s is the ring of functions on X_s.
theorems.proof: Trivialize L on affine charts. A finite cover gives a uniform exponent for annihilation. Quasi-separatedness permits a finite gluing argument on the overlaps.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA I, second edition, §6.8, localization by a section

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Injectivity for maps on a section open
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, s a global section and X_s its nonvanishing open. Let F,G be quasi-coherent. Form the degree-zero localization of the graded module of maps from F to G twisted by all powers of L.
theorems.statement: If X is quasi-compact and F is of finite type, restriction to Hom on X_s is injective.
theorems.proof: On an affine trivialization, finite generation gives a uniform annihilator exponent and finite presentation makes Hom commute with localization. Use a finite cover and finite overlap refinements where required.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Lifting maps on a section open
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, s a global section and X_s its nonvanishing open. Let F,G be quasi-coherent. Form the degree-zero localization of the graded module of maps from F to G twisted by all powers of L.
theorems.statement: If X is qcqs and F finitely presented, the map to Hom on X_s is bijective.
theorems.proof: On an affine trivialization, finite generation gives a uniform annihilator exponent and finite presentation makes Hom commute with localization. Use a finite cover and finite overlap refinements where required.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Sheaves from global sections on a quasi-affine open
theorems.hypotheses: Let U be quasi-compact open in Spec A, and F quasi-coherent on U.
theorems.statement: The A-module Γ(U,F) gives an associated sheaf whose restriction to U maps isomorphically to F.
theorems.proof: The open immersion is quasi-compact and separated, so the direct image is quasi-coherent.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine principal opens of the affinization
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be qcqs, f a global function and X_f affine.
theorems.statement: The map to the spectrum of global functions identifies X_f with D(f).
theorems.proof: Both opens are affine and have coordinate ring Γ(X,O_X) localized at f.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-affineness via affinization
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is quasi-affine iff the canonical morphism to the spectrum of its global functions is a quasi-compact open immersion.
theorems.proof: On principal affine opens of a quasi-affine presentation this map is an isomorphism onto a standard open.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Cartesian square of quasi-affine affinization maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let U → V be an open immersion of quasi-affine schemes.
theorems.statement: The inverse image of V under Spec Γ(U,O_U) → Spec Γ(V,O_V) is precisely U, with the canonical maps to both factors.
theorems.proof: Check on principal opens contained in V using the localization formula for global functions.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affine presentation with trivial affine-space pullbacks
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-affine.
theorems.statement: There exist n ≥ 0 and an affine scheme T over X such that for each affine X′ over X, its pullback is isomorphic over X′ to affine n-space.
theorems.proof: Choose finitely many principal opens covering X in an affine scheme. The unimodular-row construction of the proof becomes affine space after the specified affine pullback.
refs: Stacks 0F82 · existence with universal affine test

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Flat and finitely presented
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be quasi-coherent on a scheme X.
theorems.statement: Finite local freeness is equivalent to flatness together with finite presentation.
theorems.proof: On affine opens apply the finite projective module criteria and their rank function criterion.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Finite presentation and free stalks
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be quasi-coherent on a scheme X.
theorems.statement: Finite local freeness is equivalent to finite presentation together with freeness of every stalk.
theorems.proof: On affine opens apply the finite projective module criteria and their rank function criterion.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Locally free of finite type
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be quasi-coherent on a scheme X.
theorems.statement: Finite local freeness is equivalent to local freeness together with finite type.
theorems.proof: On affine opens apply the finite projective module criteria and their rank function criterion.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Finite generation with constant local rank
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be quasi-coherent on a scheme X.
theorems.statement: Finite local freeness is equivalent to finite type, freeness of every stalk, and local constancy of fibre dimension.
theorems.proof: On affine opens apply the finite projective module criteria and their rank function criterion.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Rank test over a reduced base
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be quasi-coherent on a scheme X. Assume X reduced.
theorems.statement: F is finite locally free iff it has finite type and its fibre dimension is locally constant.
theorems.proof: A presentation of the correct fibre rank is locally surjective. Over a reduced ring a relation vanishing at all primes vanishes.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Testing projectivity on an affine cover
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be quasi-coherent on a scheme X.
theorems.statement: F is locally projective iff its sections over each member of some affine open cover are projective over its coordinate ring.
theorems.proof: Projectivity descends along a finite principal cover and is stable under localization.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Locally projective sheaves on an affine
theorems.hypotheses: Let F be quasi-coherent on a scheme X.
theorems.statement: When X is affine, F is locally projective iff its module of global sections is projective.
theorems.proof: Projectivity descends along a finite principal cover and is stable under localization.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Pullback of locally projective modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let f be any scheme morphism X → Y and G a locally projective quasi-coherent module on Y.
theorems.statement: The pullback of G is locally projective on X.
theorems.proof: On affines, base change preserves a direct summand of a free module.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Extending a quasi-coherent sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Let j:U → X be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes.
theorems.statement: Each quasi-coherent module on U extends to one on X.
theorems.proof: The direct image along j preserves quasi-coherence. Pullbacks of modules along the unit F → j_*j^*F recover prescribed submodules and maps.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Extending a specified submodule
theorems.hypotheses: Let j:U → X be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes.
theorems.statement: For F quasi-coherent on X, each quasi-coherent submodule of F|U extends to a quasi-coherent submodule of F.
theorems.proof: The direct image along j preserves quasi-coherence. Pullbacks of modules along the unit F → j_*j^*F recover prescribed submodules and maps.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Extending a map into a given sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Let j:U → X be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes.
theorems.statement: For F quasi-coherent on X, any map from a quasi-coherent G on U to F|U extends to a map from a quasi-coherent extension of G into F.
theorems.proof: The direct image along j preserves quasi-coherence. Pullbacks of modules along the unit F → j_*j^*F recover prescribed submodules and maps.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Extending submodules of finite type
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let U be a quasi-compact open. Let F be quasi-coherent on X and let G be a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule of F|U.
theorems.statement: There is a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule of F restricting to G inside F|U.
theorems.proof: Extend from U one affine chart at a time using a finite affine cover of X. On the overlaps quasi-compactness gives finite generation data for the extension.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Directed union of finite-type submodules
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let F be quasi-coherent on a scheme X.
theorems.statement: F is the directed colimit of its finite-type quasi-coherent submodules.
theorems.proof: Extend finite submodules on an affine chart to X. Finite sums form a directed family.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Extension with finitely presented source
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let U be a quasi-compact open. Let F be quasi-coherent on X and G finitely presented on U, with a map G → F|U.
theorems.statement: There is a finitely presented module G′ on X and a map G′ → F restricting to the specified source and map.
theorems.proof: Extend from U one affine chart at a time using a finite affine cover of X. On the overlaps quasi-compactness gives finite generation data for the extension.
refs: Stacks 01PI · extension of a finitely presented source and its map

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Extending a module of finite type
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let U be a quasi-compact open. Let G be a module on U.
theorems.statement: If G is quasi-coherent of finite type, it has a finite-type quasi-coherent extension to X.
theorems.proof: Extend from U one affine chart at a time using a finite affine cover of X. On the overlaps quasi-compactness gives finite generation data for the extension.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Extending a finitely presented module
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let U be a quasi-compact open. Let G be a module on U.
theorems.statement: If G is finitely presented, it has a finitely presented extension to X.
theorems.proof: Extend from U one affine chart at a time using a finite affine cover of X. On the overlaps quasi-compactness gives finite generation data for the extension.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Presenting a quasi-coherent module over a filtered category
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Fix a quasi-coherent module F on X.
theorems.statement: There exists a diagram of finitely presented modules indexed by a filtered category and a compatible cocone to F whose induced colimit map is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Use the category of finitely presented modules equipped with maps to F and verify filteredness and the universal colimit map on affines.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Presenting a quasi-coherent module over a directed set
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Fix a quasi-coherent module F on X.
theorems.statement: There exists a diagram of finitely presented modules indexed by a directed set and a compatible cocone to F whose induced colimit map is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Choose a cofinal diagram indexed by a directed set in the filtered presentation.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Presenting a quasi-coherent algebra over a directed set
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Fix a quasi-coherent algebra F on X.
theorems.statement: There exists a diagram of finitely presented quasi-coherent algebras indexed by a directed set and a compatible cocone to F whose induced colimit map is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Approximate generators by finite presentation and impose finite systems of algebra relations on affine charts.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Surjective approximations to a finite-type module
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Fix a quasi-coherent finite-type module on X.
theorems.statement: It is a directed colimit of finitely presented modules with all transition maps surjective.
theorems.proof: Start with finite data mapping surjectively and approximate its relations by finite sets. In the algebra case impose relations making the approximants finite as modules.
refs: Stacks 086M · directed colimit with surjective transitions

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Surjective approximations to a finite algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Fix a quasi-coherent finite algebra on X.
theorems.statement: It is a directed colimit of finite quasi-coherent algebras of finite presentation with all transition maps surjective.
theorems.proof: Start with finite data mapping surjectively and approximate its relations by finite sets. In the algebra case impose relations making the approximants finite as modules.
refs: Stacks 086N · directed colimit with surjective transitions

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Approximation exact on a specified open
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let U be a quasi-compact open. Let F be finite type quasi-coherent and F|U finitely presented.
theorems.statement: There is a surjection G → F with G finitely presented and restriction to U an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: In a system of finitely presented approximations a sufficiently late term gives a surjection which can be made an isomorphism on U.
refs: Stacks 080V · (a)–(c), a single approximation with all three properties

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Directed union of finite-type subalgebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let A be a quasi-coherent algebra on X.
theorems.statement: A is the directed colimit of its finite-type quasi-coherent subalgebras.
theorems.proof: Generate subalgebras by finite-type quasi-coherent submodules and take their directed union.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Integral algebras as unions of finite subalgebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let A be an integral quasi-coherent algebra.
theorems.statement: A is the directed colimit of its finite quasi-coherent subalgebras.
theorems.proof: Finite-type subalgebras of an integral algebra are finite. Then approximate each finite algebra by finite algebras of finite presentation.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Finite presented approximations to integral algebras
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let A be an integral quasi-coherent algebra.
theorems.statement: A is a directed colimit of quasi-coherent algebras which are finite as modules and finitely presented as algebras.
theorems.proof: Finite-type subalgebras of an integral algebra are finite. Then approximate each finite algebra by finite algebras of finite presentation.

theorems.subject: ringed-space-module
theorems.name: A set of representatives for bounded modules
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a ringed space and a cardinal κ in the stated generator bound.
theorems.statement: There is a set of κ-generated modules containing a representative of every isomorphism class of such modules.
theorems.proof: Bound the choices of open cover, generators and relations by sets.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Uniform cardinal bound for quasi-coherent approximation
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: There exists a cardinal κ depending on X such that each quasi-coherent module is the directed union of its κ-generated quasi-coherent submodules.
theorems.proof: Choose a bound for the affine covering data and close generating subsets under the required restrictions and gluings.
refs: Stacks 077N · uniform cardinal then directed colimit

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: The category of quasi-coherent modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: The category of quasi-coherent modules on X is Grothendieck abelian.
theorems.proof: The bounded approximation theorem supplies a generator. Filtered colimits are exact and the inclusion preserves colimits. Apply the Grothendieck category and adjoint functor criteria used in the proof.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Enough injectives for quasi-coherent modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: The category of quasi-coherent modules has enough injectives.
theorems.proof: The bounded approximation theorem supplies a generator. Filtered colimits are exact and the inclusion preserves colimits. Apply the Grothendieck category and adjoint functor criteria used in the proof.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Limits of quasi-coherent modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: The category of quasi-coherent modules admits all small limits.
theorems.proof: The bounded approximation theorem supplies a generator. Filtered colimits are exact and the inclusion preserves colimits. Apply the Grothendieck category and adjoint functor criteria used in the proof.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: The coherator
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: Inclusion into all modules has a right adjoint Q.
theorems.proof: The bounded approximation theorem supplies a generator. Filtered colimits are exact and the inclusion preserves colimits. Apply the Grothendieck category and adjoint functor criteria used in the proof.
refs: Stacks 077P · (2), existence of the right adjoint

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: The coherator on quasi-coherent modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: The counit Q(F) → F is an isomorphism for quasi-coherent F.
theorems.proof: The bounded approximation theorem supplies a generator. Filtered colimits are exact and the inclusion preserves colimits. Apply the Grothendieck category and adjoint functor criteria used in the proof.

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: Retrocompact and quasi-compact opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let U be an open subscheme.
theorems.statement: U is retrocompact in X iff U is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: A quasi-compact open is a finite union of affines, hence retrocompact on a quasi-separated scheme. Extend an ideal cutting out its complement using finite-type approximation.

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: Finite union of affine opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let U be an open subscheme.
theorems.statement: U is quasi-compact iff U is a finite union of affine opens.
theorems.proof: A quasi-compact open is a finite union of affines, hence retrocompact on a quasi-separated scheme. Extend an ideal cutting out its complement using finite-type approximation.

theorems.subject: scheme-subset
theorems.name: Complement cut out by a finite-type ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let U be an open subscheme.
theorems.statement: U is quasi-compact iff its complement is the set-theoretic vanishing locus of a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal of X.
theorems.proof: A quasi-compact open is a finite union of affines, hence retrocompact on a quasi-separated scheme. Extend an ideal cutting out its complement using finite-type approximation.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Quasi-coherence of the annihilator
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal I on X and a quasi-coherent F. Let H be the subsheaf annihilated by I.
theorems.statement: H is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: On an affine choose finitely many generators for I. The annihilator is an intersection of finitely many kernels, which commutes with localization.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Annihilator sections on affines
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal I on X and a quasi-coherent F. Let H be the subsheaf annihilated by I.
theorems.statement: Its sections on an affine open U are exactly the elements of F(U) annihilated by I(U).
theorems.proof: On an affine choose finitely many generators for I. The annihilator is an intersection of finitely many kernels, which commutes with localization.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Annihilator on a stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal I on X and a quasi-coherent F. Let H be the subsheaf annihilated by I.
theorems.statement: At each point the stalk of H is the submodule of the stalk of F annihilated by the stalk of I.
theorems.proof: On an affine choose finitely many generators for I. The annihilator is an intersection of finitely many kernels, which commutes with localization.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Pushforward of an annihilator subsheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Let f:X → Y be qcqs, I a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal on Y and F quasi-coherent on X.
theorems.statement: Pushing forward the subsheaf of F annihilated by the extended ideal gives exactly the subsheaf of f_*F annihilated by I.
theorems.proof: Act on sections on inverse images using local generators of I.
refs: Stacks 07ZN · equality of subsheaves after pushforward

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Affine equations for the support
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a closed subset Z of X with retrocompact open complement and a quasi-coherent module F. Let H be its subsheaf supported on Z.
theorems.statement: On each affine open U, the trace of Z is cut out set-theoretically by a finitely generated ideal I.
theorems.proof: In an affine chart the complement is a finite union of principal opens. Vanishing after localization at their generators amounts to annihilation by some power of the ideal.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Affine supported sections as power torsion
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a closed subset Z of X with retrocompact open complement and a quasi-coherent module F. Let H be its subsheaf supported on Z.
theorems.statement: For U and I as above, H(U) consists of sections killed by some power of I.
theorems.proof: In an affine chart the complement is a finite union of principal opens. Vanishing after localization at their generators amounts to annihilation by some power of the ideal.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Quasi-coherence with prescribed support
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a closed subset Z of X with retrocompact open complement and a quasi-coherent module F. Let H be its subsheaf supported on Z.
theorems.statement: H is quasi-coherent.
theorems.proof: In an affine chart the complement is a finite union of principal opens. Vanishing after localization at their generators amounts to annihilation by some power of the ideal.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Pushforward of a subsheaf with prescribed support
theorems.hypotheses: Let f:X → Y be qcqs. Let F be quasi-coherent on X and Z closed in Y with retrocompact complement.
theorems.statement: The pushforward of the subsheaf supported on the inverse image of Z is the subsheaf of f_*F supported on Z.
theorems.proof: In both descriptions, a section restricts to zero on the inverse image of the complement of Z.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Injectivity from powers of an ideal
theorems.hypotheses: For a ring A, a finitely generated ideal I and an A-module M, let U = Spec A minus V(I). Restriction gives a map from the colimit of Hom(Iⁿ,M) to the sections of the associated sheaf on U.
theorems.statement: The indicated restriction map is always injective.
theorems.proof: Represent a section on a finite principal cover of U and clear denominators. Differences on the overlaps can be killed by a suitable ideal power.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Surjectivity without annihilated elements
theorems.hypotheses: For a ring A, a finitely generated ideal I and an A-module M, let U = Spec A minus V(I). Restriction gives a map from the colimit of Hom(Iⁿ,M) to the sections of the associated sheaf on U.
theorems.statement: If I·m = 0 implies m = 0 in M, the restriction map is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Represent a section on a finite principal cover of U and clear denominators. Differences on the overlaps can be killed by a suitable ideal power.
refs: Stacks 01PM · first displayed map, torsion hypothesis

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Sections via successive annihilator quotients
theorems.hypotheses: For a ring A, a finitely generated ideal I and an A-module M, let U = Spec A minus V(I). Restriction gives a map from the colimit of Hom(Iⁿ,M) to the sections of the associated sheaf on U.
theorems.statement: For Mₙ the elements killed by Iⁿ, the colimit of Hom(Iⁿ,M/Mₙ) maps isomorphically to the sections on U.
theorems.proof: Represent a section on a finite principal cover of U and clear denominators. Differences on the overlaps can be killed by a suitable ideal power.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Injectivity of the ideal-power map for a scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact, I a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, F quasi-coherent, and U the complement of V(I).
theorems.statement: The canonical map from the colimit of Hom(Iⁿ,F) to Γ(U,F) is injective.
theorems.proof: Apply the affine ideal-power formula on a finite affine cover. Quasi-separatedness gives finite overlap data for the gluing step.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Sections on U via annihilator quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact, I a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, F quasi-coherent, and U the complement of V(I).
theorems.statement: If X is also quasi-separated and Fₙ is the subsheaf killed by Iⁿ, the colimit of Hom(Iⁿ,F/Fₙ) maps isomorphically to Γ(U,F).
theorems.proof: Apply the affine ideal-power formula on a finite affine cover. Quasi-separatedness gives finite overlap data for the gluing step.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Positive tensor powers preserve and detect ampleness
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Fix n ≥ 1.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff its n-th tensor power is ample.
theorems.proof: Taking powers of sections does not alter the corresponding nonvanishing open.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Restriction of ampleness to a closed subscheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Assume L ample and Z a closed subscheme of X.
theorems.statement: L restricted to Z is ample.
theorems.proof: Intersections of affine nonvanishing opens with Z are closed in affine schemes.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Section opens inside an affine chart
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, s a global section and X_s its nonvanishing open. Let U be an affine open of X.
theorems.statement: The intersection of U and X_s is affine.
theorems.proof: On an affine an invertible sheaf corresponds to an invertible module and the nonvanishing locus of its section is affine by the affine-local argument of the proof.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Tensoring with a sheaf generated locally by nonvanishing powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Let L be ample and M invertible. Assume the nonvanishing loci of sections of strictly positive powers of M cover X.
theorems.statement: The tensor product of L and M is ample.
theorems.proof: Choose common powers of sections near a point and multiply. Intersect with an affine section open for L.
refs: Grothendieck–Dieudonné, EGA II, Proposition 4.5.6(ii), globally generated case

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Affine refinement of a basis of section opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Suppose nonvanishing opens of sections of positive powers form a topological basis.
theorems.statement: Those nonvanishing opens that are affine still form a basis.
theorems.proof: Refine a neighbourhood inside an affine open, then apply the affine-intersection lemma.
refs: Stacks 01PX · affine section opens form a basis

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Affine section covers force separatedness
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Assume affine nonvanishing opens of positive powers cover X.
theorems.statement: X is separated.
theorems.proof: First use affineness of chart intersections to get quasi-separatedness. In the valuative criterion, equalize the degrees of two chosen sections. Comparing the two line lattices over the valuation ring puts both maps inside one separated affine chart.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: An ample invertible sheaf forces separatedness
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose a scheme X admits an ample invertible sheaf.
theorems.statement: X is separated.
theorems.proof: An ample sheaf provides the affine section-open cover in 01PY.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: The section-ring morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume the nonvanishing opens X_s for positive-degree homogeneous sections cover X.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical morphism f:X → Y.
theorems.proof: Construct ring maps on the standard opens D₊(s) using degree-zero fractions. Glue the maps and check the twisting maps on the same opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Inverse images of standard opens
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume the nonvanishing opens X_s for positive-degree homogeneous sections cover X.
theorems.statement: The inverse image of D₊(s) is X_s for each positive-degree homogeneous s.
theorems.proof: Construct ring maps on the standard opens D₊(s) using degree-zero fractions. Glue the maps and check the twisting maps on the same opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Multiplicative comparison of twists
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume the nonvanishing opens X_s for positive-degree homogeneous sections cover X.
theorems.statement: There are maps from the pullbacks of O_Y(n) to Lⁿ compatible with multiplication.
theorems.proof: Construct ring maps on the standard opens D₊(s) using degree-zero fractions. Glue the maps and check the twisting maps on the same opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Recovery of sections in degree n
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume the nonvanishing opens X_s for positive-degree homogeneous sections cover X.
theorems.statement: The composite from Sₙ through Γ(Y,O_Y(n)) back to the twisted sections on X is the identity in each degree of S.
theorems.proof: Construct ring maps on the standard opens D₊(s) using degree-zero fractions. Glue the maps and check the twisting maps on the same opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Local isomorphisms along multiples of a degree
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume the nonvanishing opens X_s for positive-degree homogeneous sections cover X.
theorems.statement: Every x has a neighbourhood and d ≥ 1 on which the twisting comparison is an isomorphism in all degrees dn for integers n.
theorems.proof: Construct ring maps on the standard opens D₊(s) using degree-zero fractions. Glue the maps and check the twisting maps on the same opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Quasi-compact section-ring morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume the nonvanishing opens X_s for positive-degree homogeneous sections cover X. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The canonical morphism X → Y is quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: A finite collection of homogeneous sections covers X. Localize on standard opens and use the defining section ring.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Density in the section-ring Proj
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume the nonvanishing opens X_s for positive-degree homogeneous sections cover X. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: The canonical morphism X → Y has dense image.
theorems.proof: A finite collection of homogeneous sections covers X. Localize on standard opens and use the defining section ring.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Embedding from an ample invertible sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume L ample and let f:X → Y be the canonical map.
theorems.statement: The canonical f is an open immersion.
theorems.proof: On affine section opens, localization identifies their rings with the degree-zero parts of the localized section ring. Density follows from 01Q0.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Density of the ample embedding
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume L ample and let f:X → Y be the canonical map.
theorems.statement: The image of f is dense in Y.
theorems.proof: On affine section opens, localization identifies their rings with the degree-zero parts of the localized section ring. Density follows from 01Q0.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: An ample twist on a quasi-compact open of Proj
theorems.hypotheses: Let j:X → Proj S be an open immersion for a graded ring S, with X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: Some strictly positive d makes the pullback of O(d) both invertible and ample.
theorems.proof: Choose a finite cover by standard opens and take a common multiple of their degrees.
refs: Stacks 01Q2 · existence of a common invertible ample twist

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Ampleness criterion for the Proj morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff the positive-degree section opens cover X and the resulting morphism to the section-ring Proj is an open immersion.
theorems.proof: Use the cycle of implications of Proposition 01Q3: localization on affine section opens produces twisted generators, and the ideal tests produce a basis of section opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Ampleness criterion for a section-open basis
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff the positive-degree section opens form a basis.
theorems.proof: Use the cycle of implications of Proposition 01Q3: localization on affine section opens produces twisted generators, and the ideal tests produce a basis of section opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Ampleness criterion for an affine section-open basis
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff the affine positive-degree section opens form a basis.
theorems.proof: Use the cycle of implications of Proposition 01Q3: localization on affine section opens produces twisted generators, and the ideal tests produce a basis of section opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Ampleness criterion for twisted generation
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff for every quasi-coherent F, the images of the evaluation maps Γ(X,F ⊗ Lⁿ) ⊗ℤ L⁻ⁿ → F for all n ≥ 1 sum to F.
theorems.proof: Use the cycle of implications of Proposition 01Q3: localization on affine section opens produces twisted generators, and the ideal tests produce a basis of section opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Ampleness criterion for generation of ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff the same sum of evaluation images equals I for each quasi-coherent ideal I, using Γ(X,I ⊗ Lⁿ) for n ≥ 1.
theorems.proof: Use the cycle of implications of Proposition 01Q3: localization on affine section opens produces twisted generators, and the ideal tests produce a basis of section opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Ampleness criterion for large twists
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff X is quasi-separated and for every finite-type quasi-coherent F all twists F ⊗ Lⁿ are globally generated for sufficiently large n.
theorems.proof: Use the cycle of implications of Proposition 01Q3: localization on affine section opens produces twisted generators, and the ideal tests produce a basis of section opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Ampleness criterion for negative-power quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff X is quasi-separated and every finite-type quasi-coherent F is a quotient of a finite sum of copies of a single negative power L⁻ⁿ for some n > 0.
theorems.proof: Use the cycle of implications of Proposition 01Q3: localization on affine section opens produces twisted generators, and the ideal tests produce a basis of section opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Ampleness criterion for negative-power quotients of ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume X quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: L is ample iff X is quasi-separated and every finite-type quasi-coherent ideal is a quotient of a finite sum of copies of a single negative power L⁻ⁿ for some n > 0.
theorems.proof: Use the cycle of implications of Proposition 01Q3: localization on affine section opens produces twisted generators, and the ideal tests produce a basis of section opens.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Pullback of ampleness under i is a quasi-compact immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Let L be ample and i:X′ → X a morphism. Suppose i is a quasi-compact immersion.
theorems.statement: The pullback of L is ample on X′.
theorems.proof: In these circumstances X′ is quasi-compact and the inverse images of section opens form a basis. Apply the section-open criterion.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Pullback of ampleness under X′ is quasi-compact and i is an immersion
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Let L be ample and i:X′ → X a morphism. Suppose X′ is quasi-compact and i is an immersion.
theorems.statement: The pullback of L is ample on X′.
theorems.proof: In these circumstances X′ is quasi-compact and the inverse images of section opens form a basis. Apply the section-open criterion.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Pullback of ampleness under i is quasi-compact and is a homeomorphism onto its image
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Let L be ample and i:X′ → X a morphism. Suppose i is quasi-compact and is a homeomorphism onto its image.
theorems.statement: The pullback of L is ample on X′.
theorems.proof: In these circumstances X′ is quasi-compact and the inverse images of section opens form a basis. Apply the section-open criterion.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Pullback of ampleness under X′ is quasi-compact and i is a homeomorphism onto its image
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Let L be ample and i:X′ → X a morphism. Suppose X′ is quasi-compact and i is a homeomorphism onto its image.
theorems.statement: The pullback of L is ample on X′.
theorems.proof: In these circumstances X′ is quasi-compact and the inverse images of section opens form a basis. Apply the section-open criterion.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Exterior products of ample invertible sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Let S be quasi-separated, X and Y schemes over S, with ample invertible sheaves L and N respectively.
theorems.statement: On X ×_S Y the tensor product of the two respective pullbacks of L and N is ample.
theorems.proof: Choose affine nonvanishing opens refined over common affine opens in S. Quasi-separatedness of S gives quasi-compactness of the product.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Trivial bundle criterion for quasi-affineness
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be a scheme.
theorems.statement: X is quasi-affine iff its structure sheaf is ample.
theorems.proof: The section-open criterion for the trivial bundle is exactly the existence of a finite cover by affine principal opens from global functions.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Quasi-affine subschemes under quasi-compact immersions
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-affine and i:X′ → X a quasi-compact immersion.
theorems.statement: X′ is quasi-affine.
theorems.proof: The trivial sheaf of X is ample and its pullback remains ample.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Affineness from a unit ideal of global functions
theorems.hypotheses: Let finitely many global functions generate the unit ideal in Γ(X,O_X), and assume each corresponding principal open of X is affine.
theorems.statement: X is affine.
theorems.proof: The principal opens cover, and the local identifications with the corresponding standard opens in the affinization glue to an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Image in the invertible twisting locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume L ample and let f:X → Y be the canonical map.
theorems.statement: The image lies where O_Y(1) is invertible and all products O_Y(n) ⊗ O_Y(m) → O_Y(n+m) are isomorphisms.
theorems.proof: At every image point the nonvanishing degrees have greatest common divisor one. Localize on homogeneous section opens and use the universal twisting maps.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: All twists recover powers of L
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume L ample and let f:X → Y be the canonical map.
theorems.statement: For every integer n, the map from the pullback of O_Y(n) to Lⁿ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: At every image point the nonvanishing degrees have greatest common divisor one. Localize on homogeneous section opens and use the universal twisting maps.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Reconstruction from twisted global sections
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume L ample and let f:X → Y be the canonical map. Take a quasi-coherent F and let M be its graded module of twisted global sections.
theorems.statement: The pullback of the sheaf associated to M on Proj S is naturally isomorphic to F.
theorems.proof: On each affine section open the comparison is the degree-zero localization map from 01PW. These maps are natural and agree on overlaps.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Degree-zero normalization of reconstruction
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume L ample and let f:X → Y be the canonical map. Take a quasi-coherent F and let M be its graded module of twisted global sections.
theorems.statement: The composite from M₀ to sections of its associated sheaf on Proj S and then to Γ(X,F) is the identity.
theorems.proof: On each affine section open the comparison is the degree-zero localization map from 01PW. These maps are natural and agree on overlaps.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Reconstruction for powers of L
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume L ample and let f:X → Y be the canonical map. Write θ_F for the functorial reconstruction map of 01QJ and M for the graded module belonging to F.
theorems.statement: The twisting isomorphism in degree n is θ for F = Lⁿ.
theorems.proof: The identifications come from multiplication of homogeneous sections under localization. The remark states the compatibility and omits its proof.
refs: Stacks 01QK · identification of the twisting isomorphism

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Reconstruction commutes with homogeneous multiplication
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be invertible on X, S its nonnegative graded section ring and Y = Proj S. Assume L ample and let f:X → Y be the canonical map. Write θ_F for the functorial reconstruction map of 01QJ and M for the graded module belonging to F.
theorems.statement: Under the identification of M shifted by n with the module of twisted sections of F ⊗ Lⁿ, the pullback of multiplication by O_Y(n) commutes with θ_F and θ for Lⁿ.
theorems.proof: The identifications come from multiplication of homogeneous sections under localization. The remark states the compatibility and omits its proof.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Reconstructing modules on quasi-compact Proj
theorems.hypotheses: Let X = Proj S be quasi-compact for a graded ring S. Let F be quasi-coherent and M the graded direct sum of the global sections of F(n) in all integer degrees.
theorems.statement: The canonical map from the associated sheaf of M to F is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Check on standard opens. If such a cover has degree-one defining sections, the twist identifications also give the stated normalization degree by degree.

theorems.subject: scheme-sheaf-pair
theorems.name: Degreewise normalization on Proj
theorems.hypotheses: Let X = Proj S be quasi-compact for a graded ring S. Let F be quasi-coherent and M the graded direct sum of the global sections of F(n) in all integer degrees.
theorems.statement: If standard opens defined in degree one cover X, the induced maps from each Mₙ to Γ(X,F(n)) are identities.
theorems.proof: Check on standard opens. If such a cover has degree-one defining sections, the twist identifications also give the stated normalization degree by degree.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Disjoint affine neighbourhoods of generic points
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-separated and select a finite list of distinct irreducible components with generic points ηᵢ.
theorems.statement: There are pairwise disjoint affine opens Uᵢ, each containing the corresponding ηᵢ.
theorems.proof: Separate the chosen generic points in affine neighbourhoods using constructibility and quasi-separatedness. A finite disjoint union of affines is affine.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: One affine neighbourhood of generic points
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-separated and select a finite list of distinct irreducible components with generic points ηᵢ.
theorems.statement: The union of these opens is an affine open containing all the selected generic points.
theorems.proof: Separate the chosen generic points in affine neighbourhoods using constructibility and quasi-separatedness. A finite disjoint union of affines is affine.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: A dense separated open of a quasi-compact scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-compact.
theorems.statement: There is a dense open subscheme of X which is separated.
theorems.proof: Take a finite affine cover and successively remove the closures of the earlier charts from later charts to obtain disjoint separated opens with dense union.
refs: Stacks 03J1 · existence of a dense separated open

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: An affine neighbourhood for one point and finitely many component generic points
theorems.hypotheses: Let X be quasi-separated, x any point and ηᵢ the generic points of finitely many distinct irreducible components.
theorems.statement: One affine open contains x and all the ηᵢ.
theorems.proof: Start with an affine neighbourhood of x and use the disjoint-neighbourhood construction for generic points outside it.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Common affine neighbourhood assuming X is quasi-affine
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose X is quasi-affine. Let E be a finite subset of X.
theorems.statement: There is an affine open of X containing E.
theorems.proof: Reduce to a locally closed immersion in Proj, then apply homogeneous prime avoidance to find one standard open on which the subscheme is closed.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Common affine neighbourhood assuming X is isomorphic to a locally closed subscheme of an affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose X is isomorphic to a locally closed subscheme of an affine scheme. Let E be a finite subset of X.
theorems.statement: There is an affine open of X containing E.
theorems.proof: Reduce to a locally closed immersion in Proj, then apply homogeneous prime avoidance to find one standard open on which the subscheme is closed.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Common affine neighbourhood assuming X admits an ample invertible sheaf
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose X admits an ample invertible sheaf. Let E be a finite subset of X.
theorems.statement: There is an affine open of X containing E.
theorems.proof: Reduce to a locally closed immersion in Proj, then apply homogeneous prime avoidance to find one standard open on which the subscheme is closed.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Common affine neighbourhood assuming X is isomorphic to a locally closed subscheme of Proj of a graded ring
theorems.hypotheses: Suppose X is isomorphic to a locally closed subscheme of Proj of a graded ring. Let E be a finite subset of X.
theorems.statement: There is an affine open of X containing E.
theorems.proof: Reduce to a locally closed immersion in Proj, then apply homogeneous prime avoidance to find one standard open on which the subscheme is closed.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: Affine section open separating a finite set from a closed set
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Assume L ample and E finite contained in an open W of X.
theorems.statement: A section of some positive power of L has an affine nonvanishing locus containing E and contained in W.
theorems.proof: Apply the finite-set affine-neighbourhood lemma and the section-open criterion within that neighbourhood.

theorems.subject: scheme-line-bundle
theorems.name: A degree-one section near a finite set on a quasi-affine scheme
theorems.hypotheses: Let L be an invertible sheaf on a scheme X. Assume X quasi-affine and E finite contained in an open W.
theorems.statement: A section of L itself has an affine nonvanishing locus containing E and contained in W.
theorems.proof: On the quasi-affine scheme use global functions to adjust sections generating L near the finite set.
refs: Stacks 0F20 · section of the original invertible sheaf

theorems.subject: scheme-point
theorems.name: An affine chart embedding into the stalk when X is integral
theorems.hypotheses: Let x be a point of a scheme X. Suppose X is integral.
theorems.statement: There is an affine neighbourhood U of x such that the map from the coordinate ring of U into the local ring at x is injective.
theorems.proof: Coordinate rings of nonempty affine opens are domains, so localization at a prime is injective.

theorems.subject: scheme-point
theorems.name: An affine chart embedding into the stalk when X is locally Noetherian
theorems.hypotheses: Let x be a point of a scheme X. Suppose X is locally Noetherian.
theorems.statement: There is an affine neighbourhood U of x such that the map from the coordinate ring of U into the local ring at x is injective.
theorems.proof: Choose a Noetherian affine chart and remove the support of the finitely generated kernel of its map to the stalk.

theorems.subject: scheme-point
theorems.name: An affine chart embedding into the stalk when X is reduced with finitely many irreducible components
theorems.hypotheses: Let x be a point of a scheme X. Suppose X is reduced with finitely many irreducible components.
theorems.statement: There is an affine neighbourhood U of x such that the map from the coordinate ring of U into the local ring at x is injective.
theorems.proof: Shrink away the components not through x. A reduced ring embeds in the product of the function fields of its components.

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Simultaneous standard-open neighbourhoods
theorems.hypotheses: Let W have open immersions into affine schemes U and V, and let w belong to W.
theorems.statement: There is an affine open containing w in W whose images are principal opens of both U and V.
theorems.proof: Refine first by principal opens from the two affine bases, then clear the denominator of one defining function on the previously chosen principal open.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Compatible choice of the big Zariski site
theorems.hypotheses: Start with schemes $X,Y,S$, choose $\mathit{Sch}_\alpha$ by Tag 000J containing them, and choose the set $\mathrm{Cov}_{\rm fppf}$ of fppf coverings as in Tag 000X.
theorems.statement: Keep this same category of schemes. Select exactly the Zariski covering families among the chosen fppf covers. With this collection it is a big Zariski site.
theorems.proof: Every covering of the specified type is an fppf covering. Selection by type is invariant under replacement by isomorphic arrows over the target and preserves the site axioms for the chosen covers.
refs: Stacks 03FF · compatible sites on one category
Stacks 000X · choice of a set of covering families
